The Sixteen Great Chapters

1. Katthapaññattivāro

1. The Section on Where It Was Enacted

1. Pārājikakaṇḍaṃ

1. The Chapter on the Pārājika Offenses

1. Yaṃ [T 0.0001][P 5.0001][M 0.0001][V 0.0001] tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena paṭhamaṃ pārājikaṃ kattha paññattaṃ, kaṃ ārabbha, kismiṃ vatthusmiṃ? Atthi tattha paññatti, anupaññatti, anuppannapaññatti? Sabbatthapaññatti, padesapaññatti? Sādhāraṇapaññatti, asādhāraṇapaññatti? Ekatopaññatti, ubhatopaññatti? Pañcannaṃ pātimokkhuddesānaṃ katthogadhaṃ kattha pariyāpannaṃ? Katamena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchati? Catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ katamā vipatti? Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ [V 0.0002] katamo āpattikkhandho? Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ? Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammati? Ko tattha vinayo, ko tattha abhivinayo? Kiṃ tattha pātimokkhaṃ, kiṃ tattha adhipātimokkhaṃ? Kā vipatti? Kā sampatti? Kā paṭipatti? Kati atthavase paṭicca bhagavatā paṭhamaṃ pārājikaṃ paññattaṃ? Ke sikkhanti? Ke sikkhitasikkhā? Kattha ṭhitaṃ? Ke dhārenti? Kassa vacanaṃ? Kenābhatanti?

1. That first pārājika which was enacted by that Blessed One—the knowing one, the seeing one, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—where was it enacted? Concerning whom? In what matter? Is there an original enactment, a subsequent enactment, an enactment for a non-arisen matter? Is it a universal enactment or a local enactment? A common enactment or an uncommon enactment? A one-sided enactment or a two-sided enactment? Among the five recitations of the Pātimokkha, in which is it included, in which is it comprised? By which recitation is it recited? Among the four failures, which failure is it? Among the seven groups of offenses, which group of offenses is it? Among the six origins of offenses, by how many origins does it arise? Among the four legal issues, which legal issue is it? Among the seven settlements, by how many settlements is it settled? What there is the Vinaya, what there is the Abhivinaya? What there is the Pātimokkha, what there is the Adhipātimokkha? What is failure? What is accomplishment? What is the practice? In consideration of how many benefits was the first pārājika enacted by the Blessed One? Who train? Who have completed the training? In whom is it established? Who bear it? Whose word is it? By whom was it brought?

2. Yaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena paṭhamaṃ [T 0.0002] pārājikaṃ kattha paññattanti? Vesāliyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sudinnaṃ kalandaputtaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sudinno kalandaputto purāṇadutiyikāya methunaṃ [P 5.0002] dhammaṃ paṭisevi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Atthi tattha paññatti, anupaññatti, anuppannapaññattīti? Ekā paññatti, dve anupaññattiyo. Anuppannapaññatti [M 0.0002] tasmiṃ natthi. Sabbatthapaññatti, padesapaññattīti? Sabbatthapaññatti. Sādhāraṇapaññatti, asādhāraṇapaññattīti? Sādhāraṇapaññatti. Ekatopaññatti, ubhatopaññattīti? Ubhatopaññatti. Pañcannaṃ pātimokkhuddesānaṃ katthogadhaṃ kattha pariyāpannanti? Nidānogadhaṃ, nidānapariyāpannaṃ. Katamena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchatīti? Dutiyena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchati. Catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ katamā vipattīti? Sīlavipatti. Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katamo āpattikkhandhoti? Pārājikāpattikkhandho. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhātīti? Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato. Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇanti? Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammatīti? Dvīhi samathehi sammati – sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca. Ko tattha vinayo, ko tattha abhivinayoti? Paññatti vinayo, vibhatti abhivinayo. Kiṃ tattha pātimokkhaṃ, kiṃ tattha adhipātimokkhanti? Paññatti pātimokkhaṃ, vibhatti adhipātimokkhaṃ. Kā vipattīti? Asaṃvaro vipatti. Kā [T 0.0003] sampattīti? Saṃvaro sampatti. Kā paṭipattīti? Na evarūpaṃ karissāmīti yāvajīvaṃ āpāṇakoṭikaṃ samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu. a. ni. 10.31 Kati atthavase paṭicca bhagavatā paṭhamaṃ pārājikaṃ paññattanti? Dasa atthavase paṭicca bhagavatā paṭhamaṃ pārājikaṃ paññattaṃ – saṅghasuṭṭhutāya, saṅghaphāsutāya, dummaṅkūnaṃ puggalānaṃ niggahāya, pesalānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ phāsuvihārāya, diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ āsavānaṃ saṃvarāya, samparāyikānaṃ āsavānaṃ paṭighātāya, appasannānaṃ pasādāya, pasannānaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya, saddhammaṭṭhitiyā, vinayānuggahāya. Ke sikkhantīti? Sekkhā ca puthujjanakalyāṇakā ca sikkhanti. Ke sikkhitasikkhāti? Arahanto sikkhitasikkhā[V 0.0003]. Kattha ṭhitanti? Sikkhākāmesu ṭhitaṃ. Ke dhārentīti? Yesaṃ vattati te dhārenti. Kassa vacananti? Bhagavato vacanaṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassa. Kenābhatanti? Paramparābhataṃ –

2. That first pārājika which was enacted by that Blessed One—the knowing one, the seeing one, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—where was it enacted? It was enacted in Vesālī. Concerning whom? Concerning Sudinna, the son of Kalandaka. In what matter? Sudinna, the son of Kalandaka, engaged in sexual intercourse with his former wife; in that matter. Is there an original enactment, a subsequent enactment, an enactment for a non-arisen matter? There is one original enactment and two subsequent enactments. There is no enactment for a non-arisen matter in this case. Is it a universal enactment or a local enactment? It is a universal enactment. A common enactment or an uncommon enactment? It is a common enactment. A one-sided enactment or a two-sided enactment? It is a two-sided enactment. Among the five recitations of the Pātimokkha, in which is it included, in which is it comprised? It is included in the introduction, comprised in the introduction. By which recitation is it recited? It is recited by the second recitation. Among the four failures, which failure is it? It is the failure of morality. Among the seven groups of offenses, which group of offenses is it? It is the group of pārājika offenses. Among the six origins of offenses, by how many origins does it arise? It arises from one origin: it arises from the body and from the mind, not from speech. Among the four legal issues, which legal issue is it? It is a legal issue concerning an offense. Among the seven settlements, by how many settlements is it settled? It is settled by two settlements: by the settlement of proceeding in the presence and by the settlement of acting on an admission. What there is the Vinaya, what there is the Abhivinaya? The enactment is the Vinaya, the analysis is the Abhivinaya. What there is the Pātimokkha, what there is the Adhipātimokkha? The enactment is the Pātimokkha, the analysis is the Adhipātimokkha. What is failure? Non-restraint is failure. What is accomplishment? Restraint is accomplishment. What is the practice? Having undertaken for as long as life lasts, until the end of life, one trains in the training rules, thinking, “I will not do such a thing.” In consideration of how many benefits was the first pārājika enacted by the Blessed One? In consideration of ten benefits was the first pārājika enacted by the Blessed One: for the excellence of the Saṅgha, for the comfort of the Saṅgha, for the suppression of ill-behaved persons, for the comfortable living of well-behaved bhikkhus, for the restraint of the taints in the present life, for the warding off of the taints in a future life, for inspiring confidence in the faithless, for the increase of confidence in the faithful, for the stability of the True Dhamma, and for the support of the Vinaya. Who train? Learners and virtuous worldlings train. Who have completed the training? Arahants have completed the training. In whom is it established? It is established in those who desire the training. Who bear it? Those who study it bear it. Whose word is it? It is the word of the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. By whom was it brought? It was brought by the succession of teachers—

3.

3.

Upāli dāsako ceva, soṇako siggavo tathā;

Moggaliputtena moggalīputtena (syā.) pañcamā, ete jambusirivhaye jambusarivhaye (sārattha).

Upāli and Dāsaka, Soṇaka and likewise Siggava, with Moggaliputta as the fifth; these taught the Vinaya in Jambusirivhaya.

Tato [P 5.0003] mahindo iṭṭiyo iṭṭhiyo (sī.), uttiyo sambalo uṭṭiyo sampalo (itipi) tathā;

Bhaddanāmo ca paṇḍito.

Then Mahinda, Iṭṭiya, Uttiya, and likewise Sambala, and the wise Bhaddanāma.

Ete [M 0.0003] nāgā mahāpaññā, jambudīpā idhāgatā;

Vinayaṃ te vācayiṃsu, piṭakaṃ tambapaṇṇiyā.

These Nāgas of great wisdom came here from Jambudīpa; they taught the Vinaya Piṭaka in Tambapaṇṇi.

Nikāye [T 0.0004] pañca vācesuṃ, satta ceva pakaraṇe;

Tato ariṭṭho medhāvī, tissadatto ca paṇḍito.

They taught the five Nikāyas and the seven treatises; then the insightful Ariṭṭha, and the wise Tissadatta.

Visārado kāḷasumano, thero ca dīghanāmako;

Dīghasumano ca paṇḍito.

The confident Kāḷasumana, and the Elder named Dīgha; and the wise Dīghasumana.

Punadeva punareva (syā.) kāḷasumano, nāgatthero ca buddharakkhito;

Tissatthero ca medhāvī, devatthero revatthero (itipi) ca paṇḍito.

And again Kāḷasumana, the Elder Nāga, and Buddharakkhita; the insightful Elder Tissa, and the wise Elder Deva.

Punadeva [V 0.0004] sumano medhāvī, vinaye ca visārado;

Bahussuto cūḷanāgo, gajova duppadhaṃsiyo.

And again, the insightful Sumana, confident in the Vinaya; and the very learned Cūḷanāga, like an elephant difficult to assail.

Dhammapālitanāmo ca, rohaṇe rohaṇo (sī.) sādhupūjito;

Tassa sisso mahāpañño khemanāmo tipeṭako.

And the one named Dhammapālita, honored by the virtuous in Rohaṇa; his disciple, of great wisdom, named Khema, was a bearer of the Tipiṭaka.

Dīpe tārakarājāva paññāya atirocatha;

Upatisso ca medhāvī, phussadevo mahākathī.

Like the king of stars in the island, he shone exceedingly with wisdom; and the insightful Upatissa, and Phussadeva, the great preacher.

Punadeva sumano medhāvī, pupphanāmo bahussuto;

Mahākathī mahāsivo, piṭake sabbattha kovido.

Again, the wise Sumana and the learned Mahāpaduma; the great preacher Mahāsiva, skilled in all the Piṭakas.

Punadeva upāli medhāvī, vinaye ca visārado;

Mahānāgo mahāpañño, saddhammavaṃsakovido.

Again, the wise Upāli, confident in the Vinaya; and Mahānāga of great wisdom, skilled in the lineage of the true Dhamma.

Punadeva abhayo medhāvī, piṭake sabbattha kovido;

Tissatthero ca medhāvī, vinaye ca visārado.

Again, the wise Abhaya, skilled in all the Piṭakas; and the wise Elder Tissa, confident in the Vinaya.

Tassa sisso mahāpañño, pupphanāmo bahussuto;

Sāsanaṃ [T 0.0005] anurakkhanto, jambudīpe patiṭṭhito.

His disciple of great wisdom and learned, named Sumana, who remained in Jambudīpa protecting the Teaching.

Cūḷābhayo ca medhāvī, vinaye ca visārado;

Tissatthero ca medhāvī, saddhammavaṃsakovido.

The wise Cūḷābhaya, confident in the Vinaya; and the wise Elder Tissa, skilled in the lineage of the true Dhamma.

Cūḷadevo phussadevo (sī.) ca medhāvī, vinaye ca visārado;

Sivatthero ca medhāvī, vinaye sabbattha kovido.

The wise Cūḷadeva, confident in the Vinaya; and the wise Elder Siva, skilled in all aspects of the Vinaya.

Ete [M 0.0004] nāgā mahāpaññā, vinayaññū maggakovidā;

Vinayaṃ dīpe pakāsesuṃ, piṭakaṃ tambapaṇṇiyāti.

These noble ones of great wisdom, knowers of the Vinaya and skilled in the path, expounded the Vinaya Piṭaka in the island of Tambapaṇṇi.

4. Yaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena dutiyaṃ pārājikaṃ kattha paññattanti? Rājagahe paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Dhaniyaṃ kumbhakāraputtaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Dhaniyo kumbhakāraputto rañño dārūni adinnaṃ ādiyi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhātīti? Tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti[P 5.0004], na vācato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

4. The second Pārājika, which was laid down by that Blessed One, the one who knows and sees, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—where was it laid down? It was laid down at Rājagaha. Concerning whom? Concerning Dhaniya, the potter's son. In what matter? Dhaniya, the potter’s son, took the king's timber that was not given; it was in that matter. There is one original regulation and one supplementary regulation. Among the six origins of an offense, from how many origins does it arise? It arises from three origins: it may arise from body and mind, but not from speech; it may arise from speech and mind, but not from body; it may arise from body, speech, and mind... and so on.

5. Tatiyaṃ pārājikaṃ kattha paññattanti? Vesāliyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule [V 0.0005] bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū aññamaññaṃ jīvitā voropesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ [T 0.0006] āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhātīti? Tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

5. Where was the third Pārājika laid down? It was laid down at Vesālī. Concerning whom? Concerning many bhikkhus. In what matter? Many bhikkhus deprived one another of life; it was in that matter. There is one original regulation and one supplementary regulation. Among the six origins of an offense, from how many origins does it arise? It arises from three origins: it may arise from body and mind, but not from speech; it may arise from speech and mind, but not from body; it may arise from body, speech, and mind... and so on.

6. Catutthaṃ pārājikaṃ kattha paññattanti? Vesāliyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Vaggumudātīriye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Vaggumudātīriyā bhikkhū gihīnaṃ aññamaññassa uttarimanussadhammassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhātīti? Tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

6. Where was the fourth Pārājika laid down? It was laid down at Vesālī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhus on the bank of the Vaggumudā River. In what matter? The bhikkhus on the bank of the Vaggumudā River spoke to the laity in praise of one another's superhuman states; it was in that matter. There is one original regulation and one supplementary regulation. Among the six origins of an offense, from how many origins does it arise? It arises from three origins: it may arise from body and mind, but not from speech; it may arise from speech and mind, but not from body; it may arise from body, speech, and mind... and so on.

Cattāro pārājikā niṭṭhitā.

The four Pārājikas are concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Methunādinnādānañca[M 0.0005], manussaviggahuttari;

Pārājikāni cattāri, chejjavatthū asaṃsayāti.

Sexual intercourse, taking what is not given, a human being, and superhuman states; these four Pārājikas are, without doubt, grounds for expulsion.

2. Saṅghādisesakaṇḍaṃ

2. The Section on Saṅghādisesa

7. Yaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena upakkamitvā asuciṃ mocentassa saṅghādiseso kattha paññatto? Kaṃ ārabbha? Kismiṃ vatthusmiṃ? Atthi tattha paññatti, anupaññatti[T 0.0007], anuppannapaññatti? Sabbatthapaññatti, padesapaññatti? Sādhāraṇapaññatti, asādhāraṇapaññatti? Ekatopaññatti, ubhatopaññatti? Pañcannaṃ pātimokkhuddesānaṃ katthogadhaṃ kattha pariyāpannaṃ? Katamena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchati? Catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ katamā vipatti? Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katamo āpattikkhandho? Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ? Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammati? Ko tattha vinayo, ko tattha abhivinayo? Kiṃ tattha pātimokkhaṃ, kiṃ tattha adhipātimokkhaṃ[V 0.0006]? Kā vipatti, kā sampatti, kā paṭipatti? Kati atthavase paṭicca bhagavatā upakkamitvā asuciṃ mocentassa saṅghādiseso paññatto? Ke sikkhanti, ke sikkhitasikkhā? Kattha ṭhitaṃ? Ke dhārenti? Kassa vacanaṃ? Kenābhatanti?

7. That Saṅghādisesa which was laid down by that Blessed One—the knowing, the seeing, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—for one who, having made an effort, emits impurity: where was it laid down? Concerning whom? In what matter? Is there in that case an original formulation, a supplementary formulation, or a formulation for what has not yet arisen? Is it a universal formulation or a local formulation? A general formulation or a specific formulation? A formulation for one party or for both parties? Among the five recitations of the Pātimokkha, in which is it included, in which is it encompassed? By which recitation does it come to be recited? Among the four kinds of failure, which failure is it? Among the seven groups of offenses, which group of offenses is it? Among the six origins of offenses, from how many origins does it arise? Among the four kinds of legal issues, which legal issue is it? Among the seven means of settlement, by how many means of settlement is it settled? What in that case is the discipline, what is the higher discipline? What in that case is the Pātimokkha, what is the higher Pātimokkha? What is the failure, what is the attainment, what is the practice? Depending on how many benefits did the Blessed One lay down the Saṅghādisesa for one who, having made an effort, emits impurity? Who trains? Who are those with the training completed? In whom is it established? Who maintains it? Whose word is it? By whom was it transmitted?

8. Yaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena upakkamitvā asuciṃ mocentassa saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ seyyasakaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā seyyasako hatthena upakkamitvā asuciṃ mocesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Atthi tattha paññatti, anupaññatti, anuppannapaññattīti? Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Anuppannapaññatti tasmiṃ natthi. Sabbattha paññatti, padesapaññattīti? Sabbatthapaññatti. Sādhāraṇapaññatti, asādhāraṇapaññattīti[T 0.0008]? Asādhāraṇapaññatti. Ekatopaññatti, ubhatopaññattīti? Ekatopaññatti. Pañcannaṃ pātimokkhuddesānaṃ katthogadhaṃ kattha pariyāpannanti? Nidānogadhaṃ nidānapariyāpannaṃ. Katamena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchatīti? Tatiye [M 0.0006] uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchati[P 5.0005]. Catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ katamā vipattīti? Sīlavipatti. Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katamo āpattikkhandhoti? Saṅghādiseso āpattikkhandho. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhātīti? Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato. Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇanti? Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammatīti? Dvīhi samathehi sammati – sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca. Ko tattha vinayo, ko tattha abhivinayoti? Paññatti vinayo, vibhatti abhivinayo. Kiṃ tattha pātimokkhaṃ, kiṃ tattha adhipātimokkhanti? Paññatti pātimokkhaṃ, vibhatti adhipātimokkhaṃ. Kā vipattīti? Asaṃvaro vipatti. Kā sampattīti? Saṃvaro sampatti. Kā paṭipattīti? Na evarūpaṃ karissāmīti yāvajīvaṃ āpāṇakoṭikaṃ samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu. a. ni. 10.31 Kati atthavase paṭicca bhagavatā upakkamitvā asuciṃ mocentassa saṅghādiseso paññattoti? Dasa atthavase paṭicca bhagavatā upakkamitvā asuciṃ mocentassa saṅghādiseso paññatto – saṅghasuṭṭhutāya, saṅghaphāsutāya, dummaṅkūnaṃ puggalānaṃ niggahāya, pesalānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ phāsuvihārāya, diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ āsavānaṃ saṃvarāya, samparāyikānaṃ āsavānaṃ [T 0.0009] paṭighātāya, appasannānaṃ pasādāya, pasannānaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya, saddhammaṭṭhitiyā, vinayānuggahāya. Ke sikkhantīti? Sekkhā ca puthujjanakalyāṇakā ca sikkhanti. Ke sikkhitasikkhāti? Arahanto sikkhitasikkhā. Kattha ṭhitanti? Sikkhākāmesu ṭhitaṃ. Ke dhārentīti? Yesaṃ vattati[V 0.0007], te dhārenti. Kassa vacananti? Bhagavato vacanaṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassa. Kenābhatanti? Paramparābhataṃ –

8. Where was the Saṅghādisesa offense for one who, through effort, emits semen, laid down by that Blessed One—the knowing, the seeing, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Seyyasaka. On what matter? The Venerable Seyyasaka, through effort with his hand, emitted semen; on that matter. In that case, is there an original formulation, a supplementary formulation, or a formulation for what has not yet arisen? There is one original formulation and one supplementary formulation; there is no formulation for what has not yet arisen. Is it a universal formulation or a local formulation? It is a universal formulation. Is it a common formulation or a specific formulation? It is a specific formulation. Is it a formulation for one party or for both parties? It is a formulation for one party. Among the five recitations of the Pātimokkha, where is it included, where is it encompassed? It is included in the introduction, it is encompassed in the introduction. By which recitation does it come into the recitation? It comes into the recitation by the third recitation. Among the four kinds of failure, which failure is it? It is a failure in virtue. Among the seven groups of offenses, which group of offenses is it? It is the Saṅghādisesa group of offenses. Among the six origins of offenses, by how many origins does it arise? It arises by one origin: it arises from the body and the mind, not from speech. Among the four kinds of legal issues, which legal issue is it? It is a legal issue concerning an offense. Among the seven means of settlement, by how many means of settlement is it settled? It is settled by two means of settlement: by a verdict in the presence and by acting after acknowledgement. In that case, what is the discipline, what is the higher discipline? The original formulation is the discipline, the analysis is the higher discipline. In that case, what is the Pātimokkha, what is the higher Pātimokkha? The original formulation is the Pātimokkha, the analysis is the higher Pātimokkha. What is the failure? Non-restraint is the failure. What is the attainment? Restraint is the attainment. What is the practice? Having undertaken for as long as life lasts, until the very end of life, saying, 'I will not do such a thing,' one trains in the training rules; this is the practice. Depending on how many benefits did the Blessed One lay down the Saṅghādisesa offense for one who, through effort, emits semen? It was laid down depending on ten benefits: for the excellence of the Saṅgha, for the comfort of the Saṅgha, for the restraint of shameless persons, for the ease of virtuous monks, for the protection against taints in the present life, for the warding off of taints in the future life, for the confidence of those without confidence, for the increase of those with confidence, for the stability of the True Dhamma, and for the support of the discipline. Who trains? Learners and virtuous worldlings train. Who have completed the training? Arahants have completed the training. In whom is it established? It is established in those who desire the training. Who maintain it? Those who practice it maintain it. Whose word is it? It is the word of the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. By whom was it transmitted? It was transmitted by a succession of teachers:

Upāli dāsako ceva, soṇako siggavo tathā;

Moggaliputtena pañcamā, ete jambusirivhaye.

Upāli, and also Dāsaka, Soṇaka, and likewise Siggava; with Moggaliputta as the fifth, these recited the Vinaya in Jambudīpa.

Tato mahindo iṭṭiyo, uttiyo sambalo tathā;

Bhaddanāmo ca paṇḍito.

Then Mahinda, Iṭṭiya, Uttiya, and likewise Sambala, and the wise Bhaddanāma.

Ete nāgā mahāpaññā, jambudīpā idhāgatā;

Vinayaṃ te vācayiṃsu, piṭakaṃ tambapaṇṇiyā.

These great beings of great wisdom, came here from Jambudīpa; they recited the Vinaya Piṭaka in Tambapaṇṇi.

Nikāye pañca vācesuṃ, satta ceva pakaraṇe;

Tato ariṭṭho medhāvī, tissadatto ca paṇḍito.

They recited the five Nikāyas and also the seven treatises; then Ariṭṭha the sagacious, and Tissadatta the wise.

Visārado [M 0.0007] kāḷasumano, thero ca dīghanāmako;

Dīghasumano ca paṇḍito.

Kāḷasumana the confident, and the elder named Dīgha; and Dīghasumana the wise.

Punadeva kāḷasumano, nāgatthero ca buddharakkhito;

Tissatthero ca medhāvī, devatthero ca paṇḍito.

And again Kāḷasumana, the elder Nāga, and Buddharakkhita; and the elder Tissa the sagacious, and the elder Deva the wise.

Punadeva sumano medhāvī, vinaye ca visārado;

Bahussuto cūḷanāgo, gajova duppadhaṃsiyo.

And again Sumana the sagacious, and confident in the Vinaya; Cūḷanāga of great learning, difficult to assail like an elephant.

Dhammapālitanāmo ca, rohaṇe sādhupūjito;

Tassa sisso mahāpañño, khemanāmo tipeṭako.

And one named Dhammapālita, honored by the good in Rohaṇa; his disciple of great wisdom, named Khema, a master of the Tipiṭaka.

Dīpe tārakarājāva, paññāya atirocatha;

Upatisso ca medhāvī, phussadevo mahākathī.

He shone exceedingly in the island with wisdom, like the king of stars; and Upatissa the sagacious, and Phussadeva the great expounder.

Punadeva [V 0.0008] sumano medhāvī, pupphanāmo bahussuto;

Mahākathī mahāsivo, piṭake sabbattha kovido.

Again, the wise Sumana, and the widely learned Pupphanāma; the great preacher Mahāsiva, skilled in all the Piṭakas.

Punadeva upāli medhāvī, vinaye ca visārado;

Mahānāgo mahāpañño, saddhammavaṃsakovido.

Again, the wise Upāli, skilled also in the Vinaya; and Mahānāga, of great wisdom, skilled in the lineage of the good Dhamma.

Punadeva abhayo medhāvī, piṭake sabbattha kovido;

Tissatthero ca medhāvī, vinaye ca visārado.

Again, the wise Abhaya, skilled in all the Piṭakas; and the elder Tissa, wise and skilled in the Vinaya.

Tassa sisso mahāpañño, pupphanāmo bahussuto;

Sāsanaṃ anurakkhanto, jambudīpe patiṭṭhito.

His disciple, of great wisdom, named Puppha, widely learned, while protecting the Dispensation, was established in Jambudīpa.

Cūḷābhayo ca medhāvī, vinaye ca visārado;

Tissatthero ca medhāvī, saddhammavaṃsakovido.

And Cūḷābhaya, wise and skilled in the Vinaya; and the elder Tissa, wise and skilled in the lineage of the good Dhamma.

Cūḷadevo ca medhāvī, vinaye ca visārado;

Sivatthero ca medhāvī, vinaye sabbattha kovido.

And Cūḷadeva, wise and skilled in the Vinaya; and the elder Siva, wise and skilled in all aspects of the Vinaya.

Ete nāgā mahāpaññā, vinayaññū maggakovido;

Vinayaṃ dīpe pakāsesuṃ, piṭakaṃ tambapaṇṇiyāti.

These great beings, of great wisdom, knowers of the Vinaya, skilled in the path, proclaimed the Vinaya Piṭaka on the island of Tambapaṇṇi.

9. Yaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena mātugāmena saddhiṃ kāyasaṃsaggaṃ samāpajjantassa saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ ārabbha[M 0.0008]. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā udāyī mātugāmena [T 0.0010] saddhiṃ kāyasaṃsaggaṃ samāpajji, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

9. The Saṅghādisesa offense for a monk who engages in bodily contact with a woman, which was laid down by the Blessed One, the knowing one, the seeing one, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—where was it laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the venerable Udāyī. In what matter? The venerable Udāyī engaged in bodily contact with a woman; in that matter it was laid down. There is one promulgation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech... etc.

10. Mātugāmaṃ duṭṭhullāhi vācāhi obhāsantassa saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā [V 0.0009] udāyī mātugāmaṃ duṭṭhullāhi vācāhi obhāsi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

10. The Saṅghādisesa offense for a monk who addresses a woman with coarse words—where was it laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the venerable Udāyī. In what matter? The venerable Udāyī addressed a woman with coarse words; in that matter it was laid down. There is one promulgation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins: it may arise from body and from mind, not from speech; it may arise from speech and from mind, not from body; it may arise from body, from speech, and from mind... etc.

11. Mātugāmassa santike attakāmapāricariyāya vaṇṇaṃ bhāsantassa saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā [T 0.0011] udāyī mātugāmassa santike attakāmapāricariyāya vaṇṇaṃ abhāsi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

11. The Saṅghādisesa offense for a monk who, in the presence of a woman, speaks in praise of being served with sensual pleasures for his own benefit—where was it laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the venerable Udāyī. In what matter? The venerable Udāyī, in the presence of a woman, spoke in praise of being served with sensual pleasures for his own benefit; in that matter it was laid down. There is one promulgation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins: it may arise from body and from mind, not from speech; it may arise from speech and from mind, not from body; it may arise from body, from speech, and from mind... etc.

12. Sañcarittaṃ samāpajjantassa saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā udāyī sañcarittaṃ samāpajji, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato samuṭṭhāti, na vācato na cittato; siyā vācato samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato na cittato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca samuṭṭhāti, na cittato; siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato[P 5.0006]; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

12. The Saṅghādisesa offense for a monk who engages in matchmaking—where was it laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the venerable Udāyī. In what matter? The venerable Udāyī engaged in matchmaking; in that matter it was laid down. There is one original promulgation and one supplementary promulgation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins: it may arise from body, not from speech, not from mind; it may arise from speech, not from body, not from mind; it may arise from body and from speech, not from mind; it may arise from body and from mind, not from speech; it may arise from speech and from mind, not from body; it may arise from body, from speech, and from mind... etc.

13. Saññācikā [M 0.0009] kuṭiṃ kārāpentassa saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Āḷaviyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āḷavake bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āḷavakā bhikkhū saññācikāya kuṭiyo kārāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

13. The Saṅghādisesa offense for a monk who has a hut built for himself by asking for it—where was it laid down? It was laid down in Āḷavī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the monks of Āḷavī. In what matter? The monks of Āḷavī had huts built for themselves by asking for them; in that matter it was laid down. There is one promulgation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins... etc.

14. Mahallakaṃ vihāraṃ kārāpentassa saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Kosambiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ channaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā channo vihāravatthuṃ sodhento aññataraṃ cetiyarukkhaṃ chedāpesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

14. The Saṅghādisesa offense for a monk who has a large dwelling built—where was it laid down? It was laid down in Kosambī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the venerable Channa. In what matter? The venerable Channa, while clearing a dwelling site, had a certain shrine-tree cut down; in that matter it was laid down. There is one promulgation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins... etc.

15. Bhikkhuṃ [V 0.0010] amūlakena pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṃsentassa saṅghādiseso [T 0.0012] kattha paññattoti? Rājagahe paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Mettiyabhūmajake bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ amūlakena pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṃsesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

15. The Saṅghādisesa offense for a monk who accuses another monk of a groundless Pārājika offense—where was it laid down? It was laid down in Rājagaha. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the Mettiyabhūmajaka monks. In what matter? The Mettiyabhūmajaka monks accused the venerable Dabba Mallaputta of a groundless Pārājika offense; in that matter it was laid down. There is one promulgation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins... etc.

16. Bhikkhuṃ aññabhāgiyassa adhikaraṇassa kiñci desaṃ lesamattaṃ upādāya pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṃsentassa saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Rājagahe paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Mettiyabhūmajake bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ aññabhāgiyassa adhikaraṇassa kiñci desaṃ lesamattaṃ upādāya pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṃsesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

16. The Saṅghādisesa offense for a monk who, taking as a pretext a mere trifle of some point in a legal issue belonging to another matter, accuses another monk of a Pārājika offense—where was it laid down? It was laid down in Rājagaha. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the Mettiyabhūmajaka monks. In what matter? The Mettiyabhūmajaka monks, taking as a pretext a mere trifle of some point in a legal issue belonging to another matter, accused the venerable Dabba Mallaputta of a Pārājika offense; in that matter it was laid down. There is one promulgation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins... etc.

17. Saṅghabhedakassa bhikkhuno yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjantassa saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Rājagahe paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Devadattaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Devadatto samaggassa saṅghassa bhedāya parakkami, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

17. The Saṅghādisesa offense for a schismatic monk who does not abandon his view after being admonished up to the third time—where was it laid down? It was laid down in Rājagaha. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning Devadatta. In what matter? Devadatta strove for the splitting of the united Saṅgha; in that matter it was laid down. There is one promulgation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body, and from speech, and from mind... etc.

18. Bhedānuvattakānaṃ [M 0.0010] bhikkhūnaṃ yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjantānaṃ saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Rājagahe paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū devadattassa saṅghabhedāya parakkamantassa [T 0.0013] anuvattakā ahesuṃ vaggavādakā, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

18. Where was the Saṅghādisesa laid down for bhikkhus who are followers of a schismatic and who do not abandon their view after being admonished up to the third time? It was laid down in Rājagaha. Concerning whom? Concerning many bhikkhus. In what matter? Many bhikkhus were followers of Devadatta, who was striving for schism in the Saṅgha, and were proponents of division; in that matter. There is one original laying down. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body, and from speech, and from mind... and so on.

19. Dubbacassa bhikkhuno yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanā [P 5.0007] na paṭinissajjantassa saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Kosambiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ channaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā channo bhikkhūhi sahadhammikaṃ vuccamāno attānaṃ avacanīyaṃ akāsi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

19. Where was the Saṅghādisesa laid down for a bhikkhu who is difficult to correct and who does not abandon his view after being admonished up to the third time? It was laid down in Kosambī. Concerning whom? Concerning the venerable Channa. In what matter? The venerable Channa, when spoken to by the bhikkhus in accordance with the Dhamma, made himself unamenable to correction; in that matter. There is one original laying down. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body, and from speech, and from mind... and so on.

20. Kuladūsakassa [V 0.0011] bhikkhuno yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjantassa saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Assajipunabbasuke bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Assajipunabbasukā bhikkhū saṅghena pabbājanīyakammakatā bhikkhū chandagāmitā dosagāmitā mohagāmitā bhayagāmitā pāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

20. Where was the Saṅghādisesa laid down for a bhikkhu who corrupts families and who does not abandon his ways after being admonished up to the third time? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasuka. In what matter? The bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasuka, upon whom the Saṅgha had carried out an act of banishment, caused the bhikkhus to fall into wrong courses through desire, hatred, delusion, and fear; in that matter. There is one original laying down. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body, and from speech, and from mind... and so on.

Terasa saṅghādisesā niṭṭhitā.

The thirteen Saṅghādisesa training rules are concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Vissaṭṭhi [T 0.0014] kāyasaṃsaggaṃ, duṭṭhullaṃ attakāmañca;

Sañcarittaṃ kuṭī ceva, vihāro ca amūlakaṃ.

Emission of semen, bodily contact, lewd speech, and serving one's own desires; acting as a go-between, and a hut, and a dwelling, and a baseless charge.

Kiñcidesañca bhedo ca, tasseva tatheva (ka.) anuvattakā;

Dubbacaṃ kuladūsañca, saṅghādisesā terasāti.

And a charge based on a trifle, and creating schism, and the followers of that very one; and being difficult to correct, and corrupting families; thus are the thirteen Saṅghādisesa rules.

3. Aniyatakaṇḍaṃ

3. The Chapter on the Indeterminate Rules

21. Yaṃ [M 0.0011] tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena paṭhamo aniṃyato kattha paññatto? Kaṃ ārabbha? Kismiṃ vatthusmiṃ? Atthi tattha paññatti, anupaññatti, anuppannapaññatti, sabbatthapaññatti padesapaññatti, sādhāraṇapaññatti asādhāraṇapaññatti, ekatopaññatti ubhatopaññatti, pañcannaṃ pātimokkhuddesānaṃ katthogadhaṃ kattha pariyāpannaṃ, katamena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchati, catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ katamā vipatti, sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katamo āpattikkhandho, channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti, catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ, sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammati, ko tattha vinayo, ko tattha abhivinayo, kiṃ tattha pātimokkhaṃ, kiṃ tattha adhipātimokkhaṃ, kā vipatti, kā sampatti, kā paṭipatti, kati atthavase paṭicca bhagavatā paṭhamo aniyato paññatto, ke [T 0.0015] sikkhanti, ke sikkhitasikkhā, kattha ṭhitaṃ, ke dhārenti, kassa vacanaṃ kenābhatanti.

21. The first indeterminate rule formulated by that Blessed One—the one who knows, the one who sees, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—where was it formulated? Concerning whom? In what matter? Is there an original formulation there, a subsequent formulation, a non-arisen formulation? Is it a formulation for all places or a formulation for a specific region? A common formulation or an uncommon formulation? A formulation for one side or a formulation for both sides? Among the five recitations of the Pātimokkha, in which is it included? In which is it comprised? By which recitation does it come to be recited? Among the four failures, which failure is it? Among the seven groups of offenses, which group of offenses is it? Among the six origins of offenses, from how many origins does it arise? Among the four legal issues, which legal issue is it? Among the seven settlements, by how many settlements is it settled? What is the Vinaya there? What is the Abhivinaya there? What is the Pātimokkha there? What is the Adhipātimokkha there? What is failure? What is accomplishment? What is the practice? For the sake of how many benefits did the Blessed One formulate the first indeterminate rule? Who trains in it? Who are those with training completed? Where is it established? Who upholds it? Whose word is it? By whom was it transmitted?

22. Yaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena paṭhamo aniyato kattha [V 0.0012] paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā udāyī mātugāmena saddhiṃ eko ekāya raho paṭicchanne āsane alaṅkammaniye nisajjaṃ kappesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Atthi tattha paññatti, anupaññatti, anuppannapaññattīti? Ekā paññatti. Anupaññatti anuppannapaññatti tasmiṃ natthi. Sabbatthapaññatti, padesapaññattīti? Sabbatthapaññatti. Sādhāraṇapaññatti, asādhāraṇapaññattīti? Asādhāraṇapaññatti. Ekatopaññatti, ubhatopaññattīti? Ekatopaññatti. Pañcannaṃ pātimokkhuddesānaṃ katthogadhaṃ kattha pariyāpannanti? Nidānogadhaṃ nidānapariyāpannaṃ. Katamena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchatīti? Catutthena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchati. Catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ katamā vipattīti? Siyā sīlavipatti siyā ācāravipatti. Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katamo āpattikkhandhoti? Siyā pārājikāpattikkhandho siyā saṅghādisesāpattikkhandho siyā pācittiyāpattikkhandho. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhātīti? Eke [M 0.0012] samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca [T 0.0016] cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato. Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇanti? Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammatīti? Tīhi samathehi sammati – siyā sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca, siyā sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca. Ko tattha vinayo, ko tattha abhivinayoti? Paññatti vinayo, vibhatti abhivinayo. Kiṃ tattha pātimokkhaṃ, kiṃ tattha adhipātimokkhanti? Paññatti pātimokkhaṃ, vibhatti adhipātimokkhaṃ. Kā vipattīti? Asaṃvaro vipatti. Kā sampattīti? Saṃvaro sampatti. Kā paṭipattīti? Na evarūpaṃ karissāmīti yāvajīvaṃ āpāṇakoṭikaṃ samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu. a. ni. 10.31 Kati atthavase paṭicca bhagavatā paṭhamo aniyato paññattoti[P 5.0008]? Dasa atthavase paṭicca bhagavatā paṭhamo aniyato paññatto – saṅghasuṭṭhutāya, saṅghaphāsutāya, dummaṅkūnaṃ puggalānaṃ niggahāya, pesalānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ phāsuvihārāya, diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ āsavānaṃ saṃvarāya, samparāyikānaṃ āsavānaṃ paṭighātāya, appasannānaṃ pasādāya, pasannānaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya, saddhammaṭṭhitiyā, vinayānuggahāya. Ke sikkhantīti? Sekkhā ca puthujjanakalyāṇakā ca sikkhanti. Ke sikkhitasikkhāti? Arahanto sikkhitasikkhā. Kattha ṭhitanti? Sikkhākāmesu ṭhitaṃ. Ke dhārentīti? Yesaṃ vattati te dhārenti. Kassa vacananti? Bhagavato vacanaṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassa. Kenābhatanti? Paramparābhataṃ –

22. Where was the first indeterminate rule formulated by that Blessed One—the one who knows, the one who sees, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One? It was formulated in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Udāyī. In what matter? The Venerable Udāyī sat together with a woman, one-on-one, in a secluded, screened place, on a seat suitable for sexual intercourse; in that matter. Is there an original formulation, a subsequent formulation, a non-arisen formulation? There is one original formulation. In this case, there is no subsequent formulation or non-arisen formulation. Is it a formulation for all places or a formulation for a specific region? A formulation for all places. A common formulation or an uncommon formulation? An uncommon formulation. A formulation for one side or a formulation for both sides? A formulation for one side. Among the five recitations of the Pātimokkha, in which is it included, in which is it comprised? It is included in the Introduction, comprised in the Introduction. By which recitation does it come to be recited? It comes to be recited with the fourth recitation. Among the four failures, which failure is it? It may be a failure in virtue; it may be a failure in conduct. Among the seven groups of offenses, which group of offenses is it? It may be the group of Pārājika offenses; it may be the group of Saṅghādisesa offenses; it may be the group of Pācittiya offenses. Among the six origins of offenses, from how many origins does it arise? It arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech. Among the four legal issues, which legal issue is it? A legal issue concerning an offense. Among the seven settlements, by how many settlements is it settled? It is settled by three settlements: sometimes by the procedure in the presence and by acting on an admission; sometimes by the procedure in the presence and by the covering over with grass. What is the Vinaya there? What is the Abhivinaya there? The formulation is the Vinaya; the analysis is the Abhivinaya. What is the Pātimokkha there? What is the Adhipātimokkha there? The formulation is the Pātimokkha; the analysis is the Adhipātimokkha. What is failure? Non-restraint is failure. What is accomplishment? Restraint is accomplishment. What is the practice? One trains in the training rules, having undertaken for as long as life lasts, until the end of life, the resolve: ‘I will not do such a thing.’ For the sake of how many benefits did the Blessed One formulate the first indeterminate rule? The Blessed One formulated the first indeterminate rule for the sake of ten benefits: for the excellence of the Saṅgha, for the comfort of the Saṅgha, for the restraint of ill-behaved persons, for the comfortable living of well-behaved bhikkhus, for the guarding against taints in the present life, for the warding off of taints in a future life, for inspiring faith in the faithless, for the increase of faith in the faithful, for the stability of the true Dhamma, and for the support of the Vinaya. Who trains in it? Learners and virtuous worldlings train in it. Who are those with training completed? Arahants are those with training completed. Where is it established? It is established in those who desire the training. Who upholds it? Those who are versed in it uphold it. Whose word is it? It is the word of the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. By whom was it transmitted? It was transmitted by succession—

Upāli [T 0.0017] dāsako ceva, soṇako siggavo tathā;

Moggaliputtena pañcamā, ete jambusirivhaye.

Upāli and also Dāsaka, Soṇaka, and likewise Siggava; with Moggaliputta as the fifth, these were in the Isle of Jambu.

Tato [V 0.0013] mahindo iṭṭiyo, uttiyo sambalo tathā;

Bhaddanāmo ca paṇḍito.

Then Mahinda, Iṭṭiya, Uttiya, and Sambala likewise; and the wise Bhaddanāma.

Ete nāgā mahāpaññā, jambudīpā idhāgatā;

Vinayaṃ te vācayiṃsu, piṭakaṃ tambapaṇṇiyā.

These Nāgas of great wisdom came here from Jambudīpa; they recited the Vinaya Piṭaka in Tambapaṇṇi.

Nikāye pañca vācesuṃ, satta ceva pakaraṇe;

Tato ariṭṭho medhāvī, tissadatto ca paṇḍito.

They recited the five Nikāyas and the seven treatises. After that, there was Ariṭṭha the discerningly wise, and Tissadatta the wise.

Visārado kāḷasumano, thero ca dīghanāmako;

Dīghasumano ca paṇḍito.

The skilled Kāḷasumana, and the Elder named Dīgha; and Dīghasumana the wise.

Punadeva [M 0.0013] kāḷasumano, nāgatthero ca buddharakkhito;

Tissatthero ca medhāvī, devatthero ca paṇḍito.

And again, Kāḷasumana, the Elder Nāga, and Buddharakkhita; the discerningly wise Elder Tissa, and the wise Elder Deva.

Punadeva sumano medhāvī, vinaye ca visārado;

Bahussuto cūḷanāgo, gajova duppadhaṃsiyo.

And again, Sumana the discerningly wise and skilled in the Vinaya; and Cūḷanāga, of great learning, like an elephant difficult to assail.

Dhammapālitanāmo ca, rohaṇe sādhupūjito;

Tassa sisso mahāpañño, khemanāmo tipeṭako.

And the one named Dhammapālita, honored by the virtuous in Rohaṇa; his disciple, named Khema, of great wisdom, a master of the Tipiṭaka.

Dīpe tārakarājāva paññāya atirocatha;

Upatisso ca medhāvī, phussadevo mahākathī.

On the island, he shone exceedingly with wisdom like the king of stars; and Upatissa the discerningly wise, and Phussadeva the great preacher.

Punadeva sumano medhāvī, pupphanāmo bahussuto;

Mahākathī mahāsivo, piṭake sabbattha kovido.

Again, the wise Sumana, the greatly learned Pupphanāma, and the great preacher Mahāsiva, skilled in the entire Piṭaka.

Punadeva upāli medhāvī, vinaye ca visārado;

Mahānāgo mahāpañño, saddhammavaṃsakovido.

Again, the wise Upāli, skilled in the Vinaya; and the greatly wise Mahānāga, skilled in the lineage of the true Dhamma.

Punadeva [V 0.0014] abhayo medhāvī, piṭake sabbattha kovido;

Tissatthero ca medhāvī, vinaye ca visārado.

Again, the wise Abhaya, skilled in the entire Piṭaka; and the wise Elder Tissa, skilled in the Vinaya.

Tassa sisso mahāpañño, pupphanāmo bahussuto;

Sāsanaṃ anurakkhanto, jambudīpe patiṭṭhito.

His disciple, Pupphanāma, greatly wise and greatly learned, while protecting the Dispensation, was established in Jambudīpa.

Cūḷābhayo ca medhāvī, vinaye ca visārado;

Tissatthero ca medhāvī, saddhammavaṃsakovido.

And the wise Cūḷābhaya, skilled in the Vinaya; and the wise Elder Tissa, skilled in the lineage of the true Dhamma.

Cūḷadevo ca medhāvī, vinaye ca visārado;

Sivatthero ca medhāvī, vinaye sabbattha kovido.

And the wise Cūḷadeva, skilled in the Vinaya; and the wise Elder Siva, skilled in the entire Vinaya.

Ete nāgā mahāpaññā, vinayaññū maggakovidā;

Vinayaṃ dīpe pakāsesuṃ, piṭakaṃ tambapaṇṇiyāti.

These Nāgas, of great wisdom, knowers of the Vinaya, skilled in the Path, proclaimed the Vinaya Piṭaka on the island of Tambapaṇṇi.

23. Yaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena dutiyo aniyato kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā udāyī mātugāmena saddhiṃ eko ekāya raho nisajjaṃ kappesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Atthi tattha paññatti, anupaññatti anuppannapaññattīti? Ekā paññatti. Anupaññatti [M 0.0014] anuppannapaññatti tasmiṃ natthi. Sabbatthapaññatti, padesapaññattīti? Sabbatthapaññatti. Sādhāraṇapaññatti asādhāraṇapaññattīti? Asādhāraṇapaññatti. Ekatopaññatti ubhatopaññattīti? Ekatopaññatti. Pañcannaṃ pātimokkhuddesānaṃ katthogadhaṃ kattha pariyāpannanti? Nidānogadhaṃ nidānapariyāpannaṃ. Katamena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchatīti? Catutthena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchati. Catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ katamā vipattīti? Siyā sīlavipatti, siyā ācāravipatti. Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katamo āpattikkhandhoti? Siyā [T 0.0018] saṅghādisesāpattikkhandho, siyā pācittiyāpattikkhandho. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhātīti? Tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti. Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇanti? Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammatīti? Tīhi samathehi sammati – siyā [V 0.0015] sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca, siyā sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca…pe….

23. Where was the second undetermined rule laid down by that Blessed One, the Knowing One, the Seeing One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One? — It was laid down at Sāvatthī. — Concerning whom was it laid down? — Concerning the Venerable Udāyī. — In what matter? — The Venerable Udāyī arranged a secluded sitting, one on one, with a woman; in that matter. — Is there an original rule, a supplementary rule, or a rule for a case that has not yet arisen? — There is one original rule. There is no supplementary rule or rule for a case that has not yet arisen in this case. — Is it a universal rule or a limited rule? — A universal rule. — Is it a common rule or a rule not common? — A rule not common. — Is it a rule for one side or for both sides? — A rule for one side. — Among the five recitations of the Pātimokkha, where is it included, where is it comprised? — It is included in the Introduction, comprised in the Introduction. — By which recitation does it come up for recitation? — It comes up for recitation with the fourth recitation. — Of the four failures, which failure is it? — It may be a failure in virtue; it may be a failure in conduct. — Of the seven classes of offenses, which class of offense is it? — It may be the class of Saṅghādisesa offenses; it may be the class of Pācittiya offenses. — Of the six origins of offenses, from how many origins does it arise? — It arises from three origins: it may arise from body and mind, not from speech; it may arise from speech and mind, not from body; it may arise from body, speech, and mind. — Of the four legal questions, which legal question is it? — A legal question concerning an offense. — Of the seven settlements, by how many settlements is it settled? — It is settled by three settlements: it may be by proceeding in the presence of and by acting on an admission; it may be by proceeding in the presence of and by the covering over with grass… etc.

Dve aniyatā niṭṭhitā.

The two undetermined rules are concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Alaṅkammaniyañceva, tatheva ca na heva kho;

Aniyatā supaññattā, buddhaseṭṭhena tādināti.

The 'Alaṅkammaniya' rule, and likewise the 'Na heva kho' rule; these two undetermined rules were well laid down by the supreme Buddha, the Such a One.

4. Nissaggiyakaṇḍaṃ

4. The Chapter on Forfeiture

1. Kathinavaggo

1. The Section on the Kathina

24. Yaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena atirekacīvaraṃ dasāhaṃ atikkāmentassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Vesāliyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū atirekacīvaraṃ dhāresuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi [M 0.0015] samuṭṭhāti [T 0.0019] – siyā kāyato ca vācato ca samuṭṭhāti, na cittato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

24. Where was the pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture for a monk who lets an extra robe pass beyond ten days laid down by that Blessed One, the Knowing One, the Seeing One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One? — It was laid down in Vesālī. — Concerning whom? — Concerning the group-of-six monks. — In what matter? — The group-of-six monks kept an extra robe; in that matter. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins: it may arise from body and speech, not from mind; or it may arise from body, speech, and mind… and so on.

25. Ekarattaṃ ticīvarena vippavasantassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū bhikkhūnaṃ hatthe cīvaraṃ nikkhipitvā santaruttarena janapadacārikaṃ pakkamiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca vācato ca samuṭṭhāti, na cittato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

25. Where was the pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture for spending one night apart from the three robes laid down? — It was laid down in Sāvatthī. — Concerning whom? — Concerning many monks. — In what matter? — Many monks, having placed a robe in the hands of other monks, went on a journey in the country with their lower and upper robes; in that matter. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins: it may arise from body and speech, not from mind; or it may arise from body, speech, and mind… and so on.

26. Akālacīvaraṃ paṭiggahetvā māsaṃ atikkāmentassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū akālacīvaraṃ paṭiggahetvā māsaṃ atikkāmesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti[V 0.0016], ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca vācato ca samuṭṭhāti, na cittato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

26. Where was the pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture for a monk who, having accepted an out-of-season robe, lets it pass beyond a month, laid down? — It was laid down in Sāvatthī. — Concerning whom? — Concerning many monks. — In what matter? — Many monks, having accepted an out-of-season robe, let it pass beyond a month; in that matter. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins: it may arise from body and speech, not from mind; or it may arise from body, speech, and mind… and so on.

27. Aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā purāṇacīvaraṃ dhovāpentassa [P 5.0009] nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā [T 0.0020] udāyī aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā purāṇacīvaraṃ dhovāpesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

27. Where was the pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture for a monk who causes an old robe to be washed by an unrelated bhikkhunī laid down? — It was laid down in Sāvatthī. — Concerning whom? — Concerning the Venerable Udāyī. — In what matter? — The Venerable Udāyī caused an old robe to be washed by an unrelated bhikkhunī; in that matter. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins… and so on.

28. Aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā hatthato cīvaraṃ paṭiggaṇhantassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Rājagahe paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā udāyī aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā hatthato cīvaraṃ paṭiggahesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

28. Where was the pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture for a monk who receives a robe from the hand of an unrelated bhikkhunī laid down? — It was laid down in Rājagaha. — Concerning whom? — Concerning the Venerable Udāyī. — In what matter? — The Venerable Udāyī received a robe from the hand of an unrelated bhikkhunī; in that matter. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins… and so on.

29. Aññātakaṃ [M 0.0016] gahapatiṃ vā gahapatāniṃ vā cīvaraṃ viññāpentassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā upanando sakyaputto aññātakaṃ seṭṭhiputtaṃ cīvaraṃ viññāpesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

29. Where was the pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture for a monk who solicits a robe from an unrelated householder or householder's wife laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan. In what matter? The Venerable Upananda the Sakyan solicited a robe from the unrelated son of a wealthy man; in that matter. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins... and so on.

30. Aññātakaṃ gahapatiṃ vā gahapatāniṃ vā tatuttari cīvaraṃ viññāpentassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū na mattaṃ jānitvā bahuṃ cīvaraṃ [T 0.0021] viññāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

30. Where was the pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture for a monk who solicits a robe in excess from an unrelated householder or householder's wife laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what matter? The group-of-six monks, not knowing the proper measure, solicited many robes; in that matter. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins... and so on.

31. Pubbe appavāritassa aññātakaṃ gahapatikaṃ upasaṅkamitvā cīvare vikappaṃ āpajjantassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā upanando [V 0.0017] sakyaputto pubbe appavārito aññātakaṃ gahapatikaṃ upasaṅkamitvā cīvare vikappaṃ āpajji, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

31. Where was the pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture for a monk who, not having been previously invited, approaches an unrelated householder and makes a specification regarding a robe, laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan. In what matter? The Venerable Upananda the Sakyan, not having been previously invited, approached an unrelated householder and made a specification regarding a robe; in that matter. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins... and so on.

32. Pubbe appavāritassa aññātake gahapatike upasaṅkamitvā cīvare vikappaṃ āpajjantassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā upanando sakyaputto pubbe appavārito aññātake gahapatike upasaṅkamitvā cīvare vikappaṃ āpajji, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

32. Where was the pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture for a monk who, not having been previously invited, approaches unrelated householders and makes a specification regarding a robe, laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan. In what matter? The Venerable Upananda the Sakyan, not having been previously invited, approached unrelated householders and made a specification regarding a robe; in that matter. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins... and so on.

33. Atirekatikkhattuṃ codanāya atirekachakkhattuṃ ṭhānena cīvaraṃ abhinipphādentassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ [T 0.0022][P 5.0010] paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā upanando sakyaputto upāsakena – “ajjaṇho, bhante, āgamehī”ti [M 0.0017] vuccamāno nāgamesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

33. Where was the pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture laid down for one who has a robe completed by prompting more than three times and by standing for it more than six times? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan. In what matter? The Venerable Upananda the Sakyan, being told by a lay follower, 'Venerable sir, please wait today,' did not wait; in that matter. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins... and so on.

Kathinavaggo paṭhamo.

The First Kathina Chapter is finished.

2. Kosiyavaggo

2. 2. The Kosiya Chapter

34. Kosiyamissakaṃ santhataṃ kārāpentassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Āḷaviyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kosiyakārake upasaṅkamitvā evamāhaṃsu “bahū, āvuso, kosakārake pacatha. Amhākampi dassatha. Mayampi icchāma kosiyamissakaṃ santhataṃ kātu”nti, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

34. Where was the pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture laid down for one who has a rug made mixed with silk? It was laid down in Āḷavī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what matter? The group-of-six monks, having approached the silk-makers, spoke thus: 'Friends, you boil many silk-producing worms. Give to us also. We too wish to make a rug mixed with silk'; in that matter. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins... and so on.

35. Suddhakāḷakānaṃ eḷakalomānaṃ santhataṃ kārāpentassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Vesāliyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti[T 0.0023]? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū suddhakāḷakānaṃ eḷakalomānaṃ santhataṃ kārāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

35. Where was the pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture laid down for one who has a rug made of purely black sheep's wool? It was laid down in Vesālī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what matter? The group-of-six monks had a rug made of purely black sheep's wool; in that matter. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins... and so on.

36. Anādiyitvā [V 0.0018] tulaṃ odātānaṃ tulaṃ gocariyānaṃ navaṃ santhataṃ kārāpentassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū thokaññeva odātaṃ ante odātānaṃ ante ante (sī.), odātānaṃ ante (syā.) ādiyitvā tatheva suddhakāḷakānaṃ eḷakalomānaṃ santhataṃ kārāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

36. Where was the pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture laid down for one who, without taking a measure of white wool and a measure of brown wool, has a new rug made? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what matter? The group-of-six monks, having taken only a little white wool for the border, had a rug made otherwise of purely black sheep's wool, just as before; in that matter. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins... and so on.

37. Anuvassaṃ santhataṃ kārāpentassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū anuvassaṃ santhataṃ kārāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ[M 0.0018]. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

37. Where was the pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture laid down for one who has a rug made annually? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning many monks. In what matter? Many monks had a rug made annually; in that matter. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins... and so on.

38. Anādiyitvā purāṇasanthatassa sāmantā sugatavidatthiṃ navaṃ nisīdanasanthataṃ kārāpentassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha[T 0.0024]. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū santhatāni ujjhitvā āraññikaṅgaṃ piṇḍapātikaṅgaṃ paṃsukūlikaṅgaṃ samādiyiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

38. Where was the pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture laid down for one who has a new sitting-rug made without taking a Sugata-span from the border of an old rug? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning many monks. In what matter? Many monks, having discarded their rugs, undertook the ascetic practice of a forest-dweller, the ascetic practice of an alms-food-eater, and the ascetic practice of a rag-robe-wearer; in that matter. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins... and so on.

39. Eḷakalomāni paṭiggahetvā tiyojanaṃ atikkāmentassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Aññataro bhikkhu eḷakalomāni paṭiggahetvā tiyojanaṃ atikkāmesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi [P 5.0011] samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato samuṭṭhāti, na vācato na cittato; siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

39. Where was the Nissaggiya Pācittiya offense for one who, having accepted sheep's wool, carries it beyond three yojanas laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning a certain monk. In what matter? A certain monk, having accepted sheep's wool, carried it beyond three yojanas; in that matter. There is one promulgation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins: sometimes it arises from the body, not from speech, not from mind; sometimes it arises from the body and from the mind, not from speech... and so on.

40. Aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā eḷakalomāni dhovāpentassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sakkesu paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū aññātikāhi bhikkhunīhi eḷakalomāni dhovāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

40. Where was the Nissaggiya Pācittiya offense for one who has sheep's wool washed by a bhikkhunī who is not a relative laid down? It was laid down in the land of the Sakyans. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what matter? The group-of-six monks had sheep's wool washed by bhikkhunīs who were not their relatives; in that matter. There is one promulgation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from all six origins... and so on.

41. Rūpiyaṃ paṭiggaṇhantassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Rājagahe paññattaṃ[V 0.0019]. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ [T 0.0025] sakyaputtaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā upanando sakyaputto rūpiyaṃ paṭiggahesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

41. Where was the Nissaggiya Pācittiya offense for one who accepts gold and silver laid down? It was laid down in Rājagaha. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan. In what matter? The Venerable Upananda the Sakyan accepted gold and silver; in that matter. There is one promulgation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from all six origins... and so on.

42. Nānappakārakaṃ rūpiyasaṃvohāraṃ samāpajjantassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū [M 0.0019] ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū nānappakārakaṃ rūpiyasaṃvohāraṃ samāpajjiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

42. Where was the Nissaggiya Pācittiya offense for one who engages in various kinds of transactions involving gold and silver laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what matter? The group-of-six monks engaged in various kinds of transactions involving gold and silver; in that matter. There is one promulgation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from all six origins... and so on.

43. Nānappakārakaṃ kayavikkayaṃ samāpajjantassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā upanando sakyaputto paribbājakena saddhiṃ kayavikkayaṃ samāpajji, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

43. Where was the Nissaggiya Pācittiya offense for one who engages in various kinds of buying and selling laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan. In what matter? The Venerable Upananda the Sakyan engaged in buying and selling with a wanderer; in that matter. There is one promulgation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from all six origins... and so on.

Kosiyavaggo dutiyo.

The Second Chapter on Silk is finished.

3. Pattavaggo

3. 3. The Chapter on the Bowl

44. Atirekapattaṃ [T 0.0026] dasāhaṃ atikkāmentassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū atirekapattaṃ dhāresuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca vācato ca samuṭṭhāti, na cittato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

44. Where was the Nissaggiya Pācittiya offense for one who keeps an extra bowl for more than ten days laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what matter? The group-of-six monks kept an extra bowl; in that matter. There is one promulgation and one supplementary promulgation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins: sometimes it arises from the body and speech, not from the mind; sometimes it arises from the body, speech, and mind... and so on.

45. Ūnapañcabandhanena pattena aññaṃ navaṃ pattaṃ cetāpentassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sakkesu paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū appamattakenapi bhinnena appamattakenapi khaṇḍena vilikhitamattenapi bahū patte viññāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

45. Where was the Nissaggiya Pācittiya offense for one who, having a bowl with fewer than five mends, asks for another new bowl laid down? It was laid down in the land of the Sakyans. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what matter? The group-of-six monks had many bowls requested even for a slight crack, a slight chip, or a mere scratch; in that matter. There is one promulgation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from all six origins... and so on.

46. Bhesajjāni [V 0.0020] paṭiggahetvā sattāhaṃ atikkāmentassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū [P 5.0012] ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū bhesajjāni paṭiggahetvā sattāhaṃ atikkāmesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti kathinake…pe….

46. Where was the Nissaggiya Pācittiya offense for one who, having accepted medicines, keeps them for more than seven days laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning many monks. In what matter? Many monks, having accepted medicines, kept them for more than seven days; in that matter. There is one promulgation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins; it is a Kathina-related offense... and so on.

47. Atirekamāse [T 0.0027][M 0.0020] sese gimhāne vassikasāṭikacīvaraṃ pariyesantassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū atirekamāse sese gimhāne vassikasāṭikacīvaraṃ pariyesiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

47. Where was the Nissaggiya Pācittiya offense for one who seeks a rains-bathing cloth when more than a month of the hot season remains laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what matter? The group-of-six monks sought a rains-bathing cloth when more than a month of the hot season remained; in that matter. There is one promulgation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from all six origins... and so on.

48. Bhikkhussa sāmaṃ cīvaraṃ datvā kupitena anattamanena acchindantassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā upanando sakyaputto bhikkhussa sāmaṃ cīvaraṃ datvā kupito anattamano acchindi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

48. Where was the Nissaggiya Pācittiya offense for one who, having himself given a robe to a monk, snatches it back out of anger and displeasure laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan. In what matter? The Venerable Upananda the Sakyan, having himself given a robe to a monk, snatched it back out of anger and displeasure; in that matter. There is one promulgation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins... and so on.

49. Sāmaṃ suttaṃ viññāpetvā tantavāyehi cīvaraṃ vāyāpentassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Rājagahe paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sāmaṃ suttaṃ viññāpetvā tantavāyehi cīvaraṃ vāyāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

49. Where was the Nissaggiya Pācittiya training rule laid down for a monk who, having himself asked for thread, has a robe woven by weavers? It was laid down in Rājagaha. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the monks of the group of six. In what matter was it laid down? The monks of the group of six, having themselves asked for thread, had a robe woven by weavers; in that matter, it was laid down. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins... and so on.

50. Pubbe appavāritassa aññātakassa gahapatikassa tantavāye upasaṅkamitvā [T 0.0028] cīvare vikappaṃ āpajjantassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā upanando sakyaputto pubbe appavārito aññātakassa gahapatikassa tantavāye upasaṅkamitvā cīvare vikappaṃ āpajji, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

50. Where was the Nissaggiya Pācittiya training rule laid down for a monk who, not having been invited beforehand, approaches the weavers of a householder who is not a relative and makes a special arrangement concerning a robe? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan. In what matter was it laid down? The Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan, not having been invited beforehand, approached the weavers of a householder who was not a relative and made a special arrangement concerning a robe; in that matter, it was laid down. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins... and so on.

51. Accekacīvaraṃ [V 0.0021] paṭiggahetvā cīvarakālasamayaṃ atikkāmentassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū accekacīvaraṃ paṭiggahetvā cīvarakālasamayaṃ atikkāmesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti.
