Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti kathinake…pe….

51. Where was the Nissaggiya Pācittiya training rule laid down for a monk who, having accepted an urgent robe, lets the robe season pass by? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning many monks. In what matter was it laid down? Many monks, having accepted an urgent robe, let the robe season pass by; in that matter, it was laid down. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins. It has the Kathina origin... and so on.

52. Tiṇṇaṃ [M 0.0021] cīvarānaṃ aññataraṃ cīvaraṃ antaraghare nikkhipitvā atirekachārattaṃ vippavasantassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū tiṇṇaṃ cīvarānaṃ aññataraṃ cīvaraṃ antaraghare nikkhipitvā atirekachārattaṃ vippavasiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā [P 5.0013] paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti kathinake…pe….

52. Where was the Nissaggiya Pācittiya training rule laid down for a monk who, having left one of the three robes in an inhabited area, dwells apart from it for more than six nights? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning many monks. In what matter was it laid down? Many monks, having left one of the three robes in an inhabited area, dwelt apart from it for more than six nights; in that matter, it was laid down. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins. It has the Kathina origin... and so on.

53. Jānaṃ [T 0.0029] saṅghikaṃ lābhaṃ pariṇataṃ attano pariṇāmentassa nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū jānaṃ saṅghikaṃ lābhaṃ pariṇataṃ attano pariṇāmesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

53. Where was the Nissaggiya Pācittiya training rule laid down for a monk who, knowing, causes a gain that has been allotted to the Sangha to be allotted to himself? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the monks of the group of six. In what matter was it laid down? The monks of the group of six, knowing, caused a gain that had been allotted to the Sangha to be allotted to themselves; in that matter, it was laid down. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins... and so on.

Pattavaggo tatiyo.

The third Bowl Chapter is finished.

Tiṃsa nissaggiyā pācittiyā niṭṭhitā.

The thirty Nissaggiya Pācittiya training rules are finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse thereof is as follows:

Dasekarattimāso ca, dhovanañca paṭiggaho;

Aññātaṃ tañca aññātakañca (ka.) uddissa, ubhinnaṃ dūtakena ca.

Ten, one night, and a month; and washing, and acceptance; from an unrelated person, and that, designated, of both, and by a messenger.

Kosiyā suddhadvebhāgā, chabbassāni nisīdanaṃ;

Dve ca lomāni uggaṇhe, ubho nānappakārakā.

Silk; pure black and two parts; six years, a sitting-cloth; and two (rules on) wool, accepting (gold and silver); both of various kinds.

Dve ca pattāni bhesajjaṃ, vassikā dānapañcamaṃ;

Sāmaṃ vāyāpanacceko, sāsaṅkaṃ saṅghikena cāti.

And two (rules on) bowls, medicine, a rains-cloth, the fifth is taking back; (requesting thread) oneself, having it woven, an urgent (robe); in a dangerous place, and with what is for the Sangha. Thus ends the summary verse.

5. Pācittiyakaṇḍaṃ

5. The Pācittiya Section

1. Musāvādavaggo

1. The Chapter on False Speech

54. Yaṃ [V 0.0022] tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sampajānamusāvāde pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti[M 0.0022]? Hatthakaṃ sakyaputtaṃ ārabbha[T 0.0030]. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā hatthako sakyaputto titthiyehi saddhiṃ sallapanto avajānitvā paṭijāni, paṭijānitvā avajāni, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

54. Where was the Pācittiya training rule concerning deliberate false speech laid down by that Blessed One, the knowing one, the seeing one, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning Hatthaka the Sakyan. In what matter was it laid down? The Venerable Hatthaka the Sakyan, while conversing with sectarians, having denied, then admitted; having admitted, then denied; in that matter, it was laid down. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins: sometimes it arises from body and from mind, not from speech; sometimes it arises from speech and from mind, not from body; sometimes it arises from body, and from speech, and from mind... and so on.

55. Omasavāde pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū pesalehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ bhaṇḍantā bhaṇḍentā (ka.) pesale bhikkhū omasiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

55. Where was the Pācittiya training rule concerning insulting speech laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the monks of the group of six. In what matter was it laid down? The monks of the group of six, while quarreling with monks of amiable virtue, insulted the monks of amiable virtue; in that matter, it was laid down. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins... and so on.

56. Bhikkhupesuññe pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhūnaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ pesuññaṃ upasaṃhariṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

56. Where was the Pācittiya training rule concerning slander against monks laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the monks of the group of six. In what matter was it laid down? The monks of the group of six brought slanderous speech to monks who had become quarrelsome, become contentious, and had fallen into dispute; in that matter, it was laid down. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins... and so on.

57. Anupasampannaṃ padaso dhammaṃ vācentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū [T 0.0031] ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū upāsake padaso dhammaṃ vācesuṃ[P 5.0014], tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā vācato samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato na cittato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato…pe….

57. Where was the Pācittiya training rule laid down for a monk who makes an unordained person recite the Dhamma phrase by phrase? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the monks of the group of six. In what matter was it laid down? The monks of the group of six made lay male followers recite the Dhamma phrase by phrase; in that matter, it was laid down. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins: sometimes it arises from speech, not from body, not from mind; sometimes it arises from speech and from mind, not from body... and so on.

58. Anupasampannena uttaridirattatirattaṃ sahaseyyaṃ kappentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Āḷaviyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū anupasampannena sahaseyyaṃ kappesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti[V 0.0023], ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ [M 0.0023] āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato samuṭṭhāti, na vācato na cittato; siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

58. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for a monk who lies down together with an unordained person for more than two or three nights? It was laid down in Āḷavī. Concerning whom was it laid down? Concerning many monks. In what matter? Many monks lay down together with an unordained person; in that matter. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins: sometimes it arises from the body, not from speech, not from mind; sometimes it arises from the body and mind, not from speech... and so on.

59. Mātugāmena sahaseyyaṃ kappentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā anuruddho mātugāmena sahaseyyaṃ kappesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti eḷakalomake…pe….

59. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for a monk who lies down together with a woman? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? Concerning the Venerable Anuruddha. In what matter? The Venerable Anuruddha lay down together with a woman; in that matter. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins, as in the Eḷakalomaka case... and so on.

60. Mātugāmassa uttarichappañcavācāhi dhammaṃ desentassa pācittiyaṃ [T 0.0032] kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā udāyī mātugāmassa dhammaṃ desesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, dve anupaññattiyo. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti padasodhamme…pe….

60. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for a monk who teaches the Dhamma to a woman in more than five or six phrases? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? Concerning the Venerable Udāyī. In what matter? The Venerable Udāyī taught the Dhamma to a woman; in that matter. There is one original enactment and two supplementary enactments. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins, as in the Padasodhamma case... and so on.

61. Anupasampannassa uttarimanussadhammaṃ bhūtaṃ ārocentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Vesāliyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Vaggumudātīriye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Vaggumudātīriyā bhikkhū gihīnaṃ aññamaññassa uttarimanussadhammassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato samuṭṭhāti, na vācato na cittato; siyā vācato samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato na cittato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca samuṭṭhāti, na cittato…pe….

61. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for a monk who reports an actual superior human state to an unordained person? It was laid down in Vesālī. Concerning whom was it laid down? Concerning the monks on the bank of the Vaggumudā river. In what matter? The monks on the bank of the Vaggumudā river spoke to householders in praise of one another's superior human state; in that matter. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins: sometimes it arises from the body, not from speech, not from mind; sometimes it arises from speech, not from the body, not from mind; sometimes it arises from the body and from speech, not from mind... and so on.

62. Bhikkhussa duṭṭhullāpattiṃ anupasampannassa ārocentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhussa duṭṭhullāpattiṃ anupasampannassa ārocesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

62. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for a monk who reports another monk's grave offense to an unordained person? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what matter? The group-of-six monks reported a monk's grave offense to an unordained person; in that matter. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins... and so on.

63. Pathaviṃ [T 0.0033] khaṇantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Āḷaviyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āḷavake bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āḷavakā [M 0.0024] bhikkhū pathaviṃ khaṇiṃsu[V 0.0024], tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

63. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for a monk who digs the earth? It was laid down in Āḷavī. Concerning whom was it laid down? Concerning the monks of Āḷavī. In what matter? The monks of Āḷavī dug the earth; in that matter. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins... and so on.

Musāvādavaggo paṭhamo.

The first chapter, the Chapter on False Speech, is finished.

2. Bhūtagāmavaggo

2. The Chapter on Plant Life

64. Bhūtagāmapātabyatā [P 5.0015] pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Āḷaviyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āḷavake bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āḷavakā bhikkhū rukkhaṃ chindiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

64. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for destroying plant life? It was laid down in Āḷavī. Concerning whom was it laid down? Concerning the monks of Āḷavī. In what matter? The monks of Āḷavī cut down a tree; in that matter. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins... and so on.

65. Aññavādake vihesake pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Kosambiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ channaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā channo saṅghamajjhe āpattiyā anuyuñjiyamāno aññenaññaṃ paṭicari, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ [T 0.0034] tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

65. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for speaking evasively and for causing vexation? It was laid down in Kosambī. Concerning whom was it laid down? Concerning the Venerable Channa. In what matter? The Venerable Channa, when being questioned about an offense in the midst of the Saṅgha, evaded the question with another topic; in that matter. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins... and so on.

66. Ujjhāpanake khiyyanake pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Rājagahe paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Mettiyabhūmajake bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ bhikkhū ujjhāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

66. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for criticizing and for disparaging? It was laid down in Rājagaha. Concerning whom was it laid down? Concerning the Mettiya-Bhūmajaka monks. In what matter? The Mettiya-Bhūmajaka monks incited other monks to criticize the Venerable Dabba Mallaputta; in that matter. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins... and so on.

67. Saṅghikaṃ mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā bhisiṃ vā kocchaṃ vā ajjhokāse santharitvā anuddharitvā anāpucchā pakkamantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū saṅghikaṃ senāsanaṃ ajjhokāse santharitvā anuddharitvā anāpucchā pakkamiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti kathinake…pe….

67. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for a monk who, having spread out a bed, bench, mattress, or cushion belonging to the Saṅgha in an open space, departs without putting it away and without asking leave? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? Concerning many monks. In what matter? Many monks, having spread out lodging belonging to the Saṅgha in an open space, departed without putting it away and without asking leave; in that matter. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins, as in the Kathina case... and so on.

68. Saṅghike [M 0.0025] vihāre seyyaṃ santharitvā anuddharitvā anāpucchā pakkamantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sattarasavaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sattarasavaggiyā bhikkhū saṅghike vihāre seyyaṃ santharitvā anuddharitvā [V 0.0025] anāpucchā pakkamiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti[T 0.0035]. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti kathinake…pe….

68. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for a monk who, having spread out bedding in a monastery belonging to the Saṅgha, departs without putting it away and without asking leave? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? Concerning the group-of-seventeen monks. In what matter? The group-of-seventeen monks, having spread out bedding in a monastery belonging to the Saṅgha, departed without putting it away and without asking leave; in that matter. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins, as in the Kathina case... and so on.

69. Saṅghike vihāre jānaṃ pubbupagataṃ bhikkhuṃ anupakhajja seyyaṃ kappentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū there bhikkhū anupakhajja seyyaṃ kappesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

69. Where was the pācittiya regulation enacted for a bhikkhu who, in a monastery belonging to the Saṅgha, knowingly prepares bedding by encroaching upon a bhikkhu who was previously established there? It was enacted at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it enacted? Concerning the group-of-six bhikkhus. In which case was it enacted? The group-of-six bhikkhus prepared bedding by encroaching upon elder bhikkhus; in that case. There is one initial regulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, but not from speech... etc.

70. Bhikkhuṃ kupitena anattamanena saṅghikā vihārā nikkaḍḍhantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kupitā anattamanā bhikkhū saṅghikā vihārā nikkaḍḍhiṃsu[P 5.0016], tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

70. Where was the pācittiya regulation enacted for a bhikkhu who, being angry and displeased, evicts another bhikkhu from a monastery belonging to the Saṅgha? It was enacted at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it enacted? Concerning the group-of-six bhikkhus. In which case was it enacted? The group-of-six bhikkhus, being angry and displeased, evicted bhikkhus from a monastery belonging to the Saṅgha; in that case. There is one initial regulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins... etc.

71. Saṅghike vihāre uparivehāsakuṭiyā āhaccapādakaṃ mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā abhinisīdantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Aññataro bhikkhu saṅghike vihāre uparivehāsakuṭiyā āhaccapādakaṃ mañcaṃ sahasā abhinisīdi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā [T 0.0036] paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato samuṭṭhāti, na vācato na cittato; siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

71. Where was the pācittiya regulation enacted for a bhikkhu who sits down forcefully on a bed or a bench with removable legs in an upper-story cell in a monastery belonging to the Saṅgha? It was enacted at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it enacted? Concerning a certain bhikkhu. In which case was it enacted? A certain bhikkhu sat down suddenly on a bed with removable legs in an upper-story cell in a monastery belonging to the Saṅgha; in that case. There is one initial regulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins: sometimes it arises from the body, not from speech and not from mind; sometimes it arises from body and mind, not from speech... etc.

72. Dvattipariyāye adhiṭṭhahitvā tatuttari adhiṭṭhahantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Kosambiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ channaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā channo katapariyositaṃ vihāraṃ punappunaṃ chādāpesi, punappunaṃ limpāpesi, atibhāriko vihāro paripati[M 0.0026], tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

72. Where was the pācittiya regulation enacted for a bhikkhu who, having supervised two or three layers of roofing, supervises more than that? It was enacted at Kosambī. Concerning whom was it enacted? Concerning the Venerable Channa. In which case was it enacted? The Venerable Channa repeatedly had a completed monastery re-roofed and re-plastered; the monastery became excessively heavy and collapsed; in that case. There is one initial regulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from all six origins... etc.

73. Jānaṃ sappāṇakaṃ udakaṃ tiṇaṃ vā mattikaṃ vā siñcantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Āḷaviyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āḷavake bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti[V 0.0026]? Āḷavakā bhikkhū jānaṃ sappāṇakaṃ udakaṃ tiṇampi mattikampi siñciṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

73. Where was the pācittiya regulation enacted for a bhikkhu who knowingly sprinkles grass or clay with water containing living beings? It was enacted at Āḷavī. Concerning whom was it enacted? Concerning the bhikkhus of Āḷavī. In which case was it enacted? The bhikkhus of Āḷavī knowingly sprinkled both grass and clay with water containing living beings; in that case. There is one initial regulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins... etc.

Bhūtagāmavaggo dutiyo.

End of the Second Chapter: On Plant Life.

3. Ovādavaggo

3. The Third Chapter: On Admonition

74. Asammatena [T 0.0037] bhikkhuniyo ovadantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū asammatā bhikkhuniyo ovadiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Atthi tattha paññatti, anupaññatti, anuppannapaññattīti? Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Anuppannapaññatti tasmiṃ natthi. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā vācato samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato na cittato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato…pe….

74. Where was the pācittiya regulation enacted for a bhikkhu who, not having been authorized, admonishes bhikkhunīs? It was enacted at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it enacted? Concerning the group-of-six bhikkhus. In which case was it enacted? The group-of-six bhikkhus, not having been authorized, admonished bhikkhunīs; in that case. Is there an initial regulation, a supplementary regulation, or an unenacted regulation in this case? There is one initial regulation and one supplementary regulation. There is no unenacted regulation in this case. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins: sometimes it arises from speech, not from body and not from mind; sometimes it arises from speech and mind, not from body... etc.

75. Atthaṅgate sūriye bhikkhuniyo ovadantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ cūḷapanthakaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā cūḷapanthako atthaṅgate sūriye bhikkhuniyo ovadi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti padasodhamme…pe….

75. Where was the pācittiya regulation enacted for a bhikkhu who admonishes bhikkhunīs after the sun has set? It was enacted at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it enacted? Concerning the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka. In which case was it enacted? The Venerable Cūḷapanthaka admonished bhikkhunīs after the sun had set; in that case. There is one initial regulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins; it is of the padasodhamma type... etc.

76. Bhikkhunupassayaṃ upasaṅkamitvā bhikkhuniyo ovadantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sakkesu paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū [T 0.0038] ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhunupassayaṃ [P 5.0017] upasaṅkamitvā bhikkhuniyo ovadiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti kathinake…pe….

76. Where was the pācittiya regulation enacted for a bhikkhu who, having approached a bhikkhunīs' residence, admonishes bhikkhunīs? It was enacted among the Sakyans. Concerning whom was it enacted? Concerning the group-of-six bhikkhus. In which case was it enacted? The group-of-six bhikkhus, having approached a bhikkhunīs' residence, admonished the bhikkhunīs; in that case. There is one initial regulation and one supplementary regulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins; it is of the kaṭhina type... etc.

77. “Āmisahetu [M 0.0027] bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo ovadantī”ti bhaṇantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū “āmisahetu bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo ovadantī”ti bhaṇiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

77. Where was the pācittiya regulation enacted for a bhikkhu who says, 'Bhikkhus admonish bhikkhunīs for the sake of material gain'? It was enacted at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it enacted? Concerning the group-of-six bhikkhus. In which case was it enacted? The group-of-six bhikkhus said, 'Bhikkhus admonish bhikkhunīs for the sake of material gain'; in that case. There is one initial regulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins... etc.

78. Aññātikāya [V 0.0027] bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ dentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Aññataro bhikkhu aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ adāsi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

78. Where was the pācittiya regulation enacted for a bhikkhu who gives a robe to a bhikkhunī who is not a relative? It was enacted at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it enacted? Concerning a certain bhikkhu. In which case was it enacted? A certain bhikkhu gave a robe to a bhikkhunī who was not a relative; in that case. There is one initial regulation and one supplementary regulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from all six origins... etc.

79. Aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ sibbentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā udāyī aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ sibbesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti [T 0.0039] …pe….

79. Where was the pācittiya offense laid down for a monk who sews a robe for a bhikkhunī who is not a relative? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Udāyī. In what matter? The Venerable Udāyī sewed a robe for a bhikkhunī who was not a relative. In that matter. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins... etc.

80. Bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ catūhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato samuṭṭhāti, na vācato na cittato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca samuṭṭhāti, na cittato; siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

80. Where was the pācittiya offense laid down for a monk who travels on the same long journey together with a bhikkhunī by arrangement? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what matter? The group-of-six monks traveled on the same long journey together with bhikkhunīs by arrangement. In that matter. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from four origins: sometimes it arises from the body, not from speech, not from mind; sometimes it arises from the body and speech, not from mind; sometimes it arises from the body and mind, not from speech; sometimes it arises from the body, speech, and mind... etc.

81. Bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaṃ nāvaṃ abhiruhantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaṃ nāvaṃ abhiruhiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ catūhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

81. Where was the pācittiya offense laid down for a monk who boards the same boat together with a bhikkhunī by arrangement? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what matter? The group-of-six monks boarded the same boat together with bhikkhunīs by arrangement. In that matter. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from four origins... etc.

82. Jānaṃ [M 0.0028] bhikkhuniparipācitaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Rājagahe paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Devadattaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Devadatto jānaṃ bhikkhuniparipācitaṃ [T 0.0040] piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñji, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

82. Where was the pācittiya offense laid down for a monk who knowingly eats almsfood prepared by a bhikkhunī? It was laid down in Rājagaha. Concerning whom? Concerning Devadatta. In what matter? Devadatta knowingly ate almsfood prepared by a bhikkhunī. In that matter. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from the body and from the mind, not from speech... etc.

83. Bhikkhuniyā [P 5.0018][V 0.0028] saddhiṃ eko ekāya raho nisajjaṃ kappentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā udāyī bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ eko ekāya raho nisajjaṃ kappesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

83. Where was the pācittiya offense laid down for a monk who sits one-on-one with a bhikkhunī in a secluded place? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Udāyī. In what matter? The Venerable Udāyī sat one-on-one with a bhikkhunī in a secluded place. In that matter. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from the body and from the mind, not from speech... etc.

Ovādavaggo tatiyo.

The Third Chapter, the Chapter on Admonition, is concluded.

4. Bhojanavaggo

4. The Fourth Chapter: On Meals

84. Tatuttari āvasathapiṇḍaṃ bhuñjantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū [T 0.0041] ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū anuvasitvā anuvasitvā āvasathapiṇḍaṃ bhuñjiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti eḷakalomake…pe….

84. Where was the pācittiya offense laid down for a monk who eats almsfood from a public rest house more than once? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what matter? The group-of-six monks, having stayed day after day, ate the almsfood from the public rest house. In that matter. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins, as in the Eḷakalomaka case... etc.

85. Gaṇabhojane pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Rājagahe paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Devadattaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Devadatto sapariso kulesu viññāpetvā viññāpetvā bhuñji, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, satta anupaññattiyo. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti eḷakalomake…pe….

85. Where was the pācittiya offense for a group meal laid down? It was laid down in Rājagaha. Concerning whom? Concerning Devadatta. In what matter? Devadatta, together with his company, having requested again and again at the houses of supporters, ate. In that matter. There is one original enactment and seven supplementary enactments. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins, as in the Eḷakalomaka case... etc.

86. Paramparabhojane pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Vesāliyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū [M 0.0029] aññatra nimantitā aññatra bhuñjiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, catasso anupaññattiyo. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti kathinake…pe….

86. Where was the pācittiya offense for eating successive meals laid down? It was laid down in Vesālī. Concerning whom? Concerning many monks. In what matter? Many monks, having been invited to one place, ate in another. In that matter. There is one original enactment and four supplementary enactments. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins, as in the Kathina case... etc.

87. Dvattipattapūre pūve paṭiggahetvā tatuttari paṭiggaṇhantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū na mattaṃ jānitvā paṭiggahesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā [T 0.0042] paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

87. Where was the pācittiya offense laid down for one who, having accepted two or three bowlfuls of cakes, accepts more than that? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning many monks. In what matter? Many monks accepted without knowing the proper measure. In that matter. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from all six origins... etc.

88. Bhuttāvinā [V 0.0029] pavāritena anatirittaṃ khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā bhuñjantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū bhuttāvī pavāritā aññatra bhuñjiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti kathinake…pe….

88. Where was the pācittiya offense laid down for one who, having eaten and declined more food, eats hard or soft food that has not been made a leftover? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning many monks. In what matter? Many monks, having eaten and declined more food, ate elsewhere. In that matter. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins, as in the Kathina case... etc.

89. Bhikkhuṃ bhuttāviṃ pavāritaṃ anatirittena khādanīyena vā bhojanīyena vā abhihaṭṭhuṃ pavārentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Aññataro bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ bhuttāviṃ pavāritaṃ anatirittena bhojanīyena abhihaṭṭhuṃ pavāresi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

89. Regarding the pācittiya training rule for one who invites a bhikkhu—who has eaten and declined more food—by bringing forward hard or soft food that has not been made a leftover, where was it laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning a certain bhikkhu. In what matter was it laid down? A certain bhikkhu invited a bhikkhu—who has eaten and declined more food—by bringing forward soft food that had not been made a leftover; in that matter, it was laid down. There is one original laying down. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins... etc.

90. Vikāle [P 5.0019] khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā bhuñjantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Rājagahe paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sattarasavaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sattarasavaggiyā bhikkhū vikāle bhojanaṃ bhuñjiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti eḷakalomake…pe….

90. Regarding the pācittiya training rule for eating hard or soft food at the wrong time, where was it laid down? It was laid down in Rājagaha. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the Group of Seventeen bhikkhus. In what matter was it laid down? The Group of Seventeen bhikkhus ate food at the wrong time; in that matter, it was laid down. There is one original laying down. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins, as in the Eḷakalomaka case... etc.

91. Sannidhikārakaṃ khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā bhuñjantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ belaṭṭhasīsaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā belaṭṭhasīso sannidhikārakaṃ bhojanaṃ [M 0.0030] bhuñji, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti eḷakalomake…pe….

91. Regarding the pācittiya training rule for eating hard or soft food that has been stored, where was it laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the Venerable Belaṭṭhasīsa. In what matter was it laid down? The Venerable Belaṭṭhasīsa ate food that had been stored; in that matter, it was laid down. There is one original laying down. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins, as in the Eḷakalomaka case... etc.

92. Paṇītabhojanāni attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū paṇītabhojanāni attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ catūhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

92. Regarding the pācittiya training rule for one who, for their own sake, requests and eats choice foods, where was it laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the Group of Six bhikkhus. In what matter was it laid down? The Group of Six bhikkhus, for their own sake, requested and ate choice foods; in that matter, it was laid down. There is one original laying down and one supplementary laying down. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from four origins... etc.

93. Adinnaṃ mukhadvāraṃ āhāraṃ āharantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Vesāliyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Aññataro bhikkhu [V 0.0030] adinnaṃ mukhadvāraṃ [T 0.0044] āhāraṃ āhari, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti eḷakalomake…pe….

93. Regarding the pācittiya training rule for one who brings unoffered food to the entrance of the mouth, where was it laid down? It was laid down at Vesālī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning a certain bhikkhu. In what matter was it laid down? A certain bhikkhu brought unoffered food to the entrance of his mouth; in that matter, it was laid down. There is one original laying down and one supplementary laying down. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins, as in the Eḷakalomaka case... etc.

Bhojanavaggo catuttho.

The Fourth Chapter on Food.

5. Acelakavaggo

5. The Chapter on Naked Ascetics

94. Acelakassa vā paribbājakassa vā paribbājikāya vā sahatthā khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā dentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Vesāliyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā ānando aññatarissā paribbājikāya ekaṃ maññamāno dve pūve adāsi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti eḷakalomake…pe….

94. Regarding the pācittiya training rule for one who gives hard or soft food with one's own hand to a naked ascetic, a male wanderer, or a female wanderer, where was it laid down? It was laid down at Vesālī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the Venerable Ānanda. In what matter was it laid down? The Venerable Ānanda gave two cakes to a certain female wanderer, thinking it was one cake; in that matter, it was laid down. There is one original laying down. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins, as in the Eḷakalomaka case... etc.

95. Bhikkhuṃ “ehāvuso, gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā piṇḍāya pavisissāmā”ti tassa dāpetvā vā adāpetvā vā uyyojentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti[T 0.0045]? Āyasmā upanando sakyaputto bhikkhuṃ “ehāvuso, gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pavisissāmā”ti, tassa adāpetvā uyyojesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

95. Regarding the pācittiya training rule for one who dismisses a bhikkhu—whether having had something given to him or not—after inviting him with the words, 'Come, friend, let us enter a village or a town for alms,' where was it laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan son. In what matter was it laid down? The Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan son, invited a bhikkhu saying, 'Come, friend, let us enter the village for alms,' and then dismissed him without having had anything given to him; in that matter, it was laid down. There is one original laying down. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins... etc.

96. Sabhojane [M 0.0031] kule anupakhajja nisajjaṃ kappentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā upanando sakyaputto sabhojane kule anupakhajja nisajjaṃ kappesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti[P 5.0020]. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

96. Regarding the pācittiya training rule for one who sits down, having intruded upon a family at mealtime, where was it laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan son. In what matter was it laid down? The Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan son, sat down, having intruded upon a family at mealtime; in that matter, it was laid down. There is one original laying down. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body and mind, not from speech... etc.

97. Mātugāmena saddhiṃ raho paṭicchanne āsane nisajjaṃ kappentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā upanando sakyaputto mātugāmena saddhiṃ raho paṭicchanne āsane nisajjaṃ kappesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

97. Regarding the pācittiya training rule for one who sits together with a woman on a concealed seat in a secluded place, where was it laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan son. In what matter was it laid down? The Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan son, sat together with a woman on a concealed seat in a secluded place; in that matter, it was laid down. There is one original laying down. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body and mind, not from speech... etc.

98. Mātugāmena [V 0.0031] saddhiṃ eko ekāya raho nisajjaṃ kappentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā upanando sakyaputto mātugāmena saddhiṃ eko ekāya raho nisajjaṃ kappesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

98. Regarding the pācittiya training rule for one who sits alone with a woman in a secluded place, where was it laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan son. In what matter was it laid down? The Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan son, sat alone with a woman in a secluded place; in that matter, it was laid down. There is one original laying down. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body and mind, not from speech... etc.

99. Nimantitena sabhattena santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā purebhattaṃ pacchābhattaṃ kulesu cārittaṃ āpajjantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Rājagahe paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā upanando sakyaputto nimantito sabhatto samāno purebhattaṃ pacchābhattaṃ kulesu cārittaṃ āpajji, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, catasso anupaññattiyo. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti kathinake…pe….

99. Where was the Pācittiya rule laid down for a monk who, having been invited to a meal, wanders among families either before the meal or after the meal without having asked permission from a monk who is present? It was laid down at Rājagaha. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan son. In what case? The Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan son, having been invited to a meal, wandered among families before the meal and after the meal; in that case. There is one original enactment and four supplementary enactments. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins, as in the Kathinaka case... etc.

100. Tatuttari bhesajjaṃ viññāpentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sakkesu paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū mahānāmena sakkena “ajjaṇho, bhante, āgamethā”ti [M 0.0032] vuccamānā nāgamesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

100. Where was the Pācittiya rule laid down for a monk who requests medicine beyond the specified time? It was laid down among the Sakyans. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what case? The group-of-six monks, though being told by Mahānāma the Sakyan, 'Venerable sirs, please wait today,' did not wait; in that case. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from all six origins... etc.

101. Uyyuttaṃ senaṃ dassanāya gacchantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti[T 0.0047]? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uyyuttaṃ senaṃ dassanāya agamaṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti eḷakalomake…pe….

101. Where was the Pācittiya rule laid down for a monk who goes to see a deployed army? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what case? The group-of-six monks went to see a deployed army; in that case. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins, as in the Eḷakalomaka case... etc.

102. Atirekatirattaṃ senāya vasantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū atirekatirattaṃ senāya vasiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti eḷakalomake…pe….

102. Where was the Pācittiya rule laid down for a monk who stays with an army for more than three nights? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what case? The group-of-six monks stayed with an army for more than three nights; in that case. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins, as in the Eḷakalomaka case... etc.

103. Uyyodhikaṃ gacchantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ[P 5.0021]. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uyyodhikaṃ [V 0.0032] agamaṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti eḷakalomake…pe….

103. Where was the Pācittiya rule laid down for a monk going to a battlefield? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what case? The group-of-six monks went to a battlefield; in that case. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins, as in the Eḷakalomaka case... etc.

Acelakavaggo pañcamo.

The Fifth Chapter on Naked Ascetics.

6. Surāpānavaggo

6. 6. The Chapter on Drinking Liquor

104. Surāmerayapāne [T 0.0048] pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Kosambiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ sāgataṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā sāgato majjaṃ pivi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato samuṭṭhāti, na vācato na cittato; siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

104. Where was the Pācittiya rule laid down for drinking fermented and distilled liquor? It was laid down at Kosambī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Sāgata. In what case? The Venerable Sāgata drank an intoxicant; in that case. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins: sometimes it arises from the body, not from speech, not from mind; sometimes it arises from the body and from the mind, not from speech... etc.

105. Aṅgulipatodake pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā [M 0.0033] bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ aṅgulipatodakena hāsesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

105. Where was the Pācittiya rule laid down for tickling with the finger? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what case? The group-of-six monks made another monk laugh by tickling with the finger; in that case. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from the body and from the mind, not from speech... etc.

106. Udake hasadhamme hassadhamme (sī. syā.) pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sattarasavaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sattarasavaggiyā bhikkhū aciravatiyā nadiyā udake kīḷiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato [T 0.0049] ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

106. Where was the Pācittiya rule laid down for sporting in the water? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-seventeen monks. In what case? The group-of-seventeen monks were playing in the water of the river Aciravatī; in that case. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from the body and from the mind, not from speech... etc.

107. Anādariye pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Kosambiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ channaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā channo anādariyaṃ akāsi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

107. Where was the Pācittiya rule laid down for disrespect? It was laid down at Kosambī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Channa. In what case? The Venerable Channa acted with disrespect; in that case. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins... etc.

108. Bhikkhuṃ bhiṃsāpentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ bhiṃsāpesuṃ[V 0.0033], tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

108. Where was the Pācittiya rule laid down for a monk who frightens another monk? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what case? The group-of-six monks frightened a monk; in that case. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins... etc.

109. Jotiṃ samādahitvā visibbentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Bhaggesu paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū jotiṃ samādahitvā visibbesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, dve anupaññattiyo. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

109. Where was the Pācittiya rule laid down for a monk who, having kindled a fire, warms himself? It was laid down among the Bhaggas. Concerning whom? Concerning many monks. In what case? Many monks, having kindled a fire, warmed themselves; in that case. There is one original enactment and two supplementary enactments. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from all six origins... etc.

110. Orenaddhamāsaṃ nahāyantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Rājagahe paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū rājānampi passitvā na [T 0.0050] mattaṃ jānitvā nahāyiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, cha anupaññattiyo. Sabbatthapaññatti, padesapaññattīti? Padesapaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti eḷakalomake…pe….

110. Regarding the pācittiya for a bhikkhu bathing within half a month, where was it laid down? It was laid down at Rājagaha. Concerning whom? Concerning many bhikkhus. In what matter? Many bhikkhus, having seen the king, bathed without knowing the proper measure; in that matter. There is one original enactment and six supplementary enactments. Is it a universal enactment or a local enactment? It is a local enactment. Of the six origins of an offense, it arises from two origins, as in the Eḷakalomaka case... and so on...

111. Anādiyitvā [P 5.0022][M 0.0034] tiṇṇaṃ dubbaṇṇakaraṇānaṃ aññataraṃ dubbaṇṇakaraṇaṃ navaṃ cīvaraṃ paribhuñjantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū attano cīvaraṃ na sañjāniṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti eḷakalomake…pe….

111. Regarding the pācittiya for a bhikkhu who uses a new robe without applying one of the three means of discoloration, where was it laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning many bhikkhus. In what matter? Many bhikkhus did not recognize their own robes; in that matter. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of an offense, it arises from two origins, as in the Eḷakalomaka case... and so on...

112. Bhikkhussa vā bhikkhuniyā vā sikkhamānāya vā sāmaṇerassa vā sāmaṇeriyā vā sāmaṃ cīvaraṃ vikappetvā appaccuddhāraṇaṃ paribhuñjantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā upanando sakyaputto bhikkhussa sāmaṃ cīvaraṃ vikappetvā appaccuddhāraṇaṃ paribhuñji, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti kathinake…pe….

112. Regarding the pācittiya for a bhikkhu who, having personally made a formal determination of a robe for a bhikkhu, or a bhikkhunī, or a female probationer, or a male novice, or a female novice, then uses it without having rescinded that determination, where was it laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan. In what matter? The Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan, having personally made a formal determination of a robe for a bhikkhu, used it without having rescinded that determination; in that matter. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of an offense, it arises from two origins, as in the Kathina case... and so on...

113. Bhikkhussa pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā nisīdanaṃ vā sūcigharaṃ vā kāyabandhanaṃ vā apanidhentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ [T 0.0051] paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhūnaṃ pattampi cīvarampi apanidhesuṃ[V 0.0034], tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

113. Regarding the pācittiya for a bhikkhu who hides another bhikkhu's bowl, or robe, or sitting-cloth, or needle-case, or girdle, where was it laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhus of the group-of-six. In what matter? The bhikkhus of the group-of-six hid the bowls and robes of bhikkhus; in that matter. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of an offense, it arises from three origins... and so on...

Surāmerayavaggo chaṭṭho.

The Surāmeraya Chapter is the sixth.

7. Sappāṇakavaggo

7. The Chapter on Living Beings

114. Sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā udāyī sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

114. Regarding the pācittiya for one who intentionally deprives a living being of life, where was it laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Udāyī. In what matter? The Venerable Udāyī intentionally deprived a living being of life; in that matter. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of an offense, it arises from three origins... and so on...

115. Jānaṃ sappāṇakaṃ udakaṃ paribhuñjantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti[M 0.0035]? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū jānaṃ sappāṇakaṃ [T 0.0052] udakaṃ paribhuñjiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

115. Regarding the pācittiya for one who knowingly uses water containing living beings, where was it laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six bhikkhus. In what matter? The group-of-six bhikkhus knowingly used water containing living beings; in that matter. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of an offense, it arises from three origins... and so on...

116. Jānaṃ yathādhammaṃ nihatādhikaraṇaṃ puna kammāya ukkoṭentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū jānaṃ yathādhammaṃ nihatādhikaraṇaṃ puna kammāya ukkoṭesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

116. Regarding the pācittiya for one who, knowing that a legal issue has been settled according to the Dhamma, reopens it for a formal act, where was it laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six bhikkhus. In what matter? The group-of-six bhikkhus, knowing that a legal issue had been settled according to the Dhamma, reopened it for a formal act; in that matter. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of an offense, it arises from three origins... and so on...

117. Bhikkhussa jānaṃ duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ paṭicchādentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ [P 5.0023] ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Aññataro bhikkhu bhikkhussa jānaṃ duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ paṭicchādesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

117. Regarding the pācittiya for one who knowingly conceals a bhikkhu's serious offense, where was it laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning a certain bhikkhu. In what matter? A certain bhikkhu knowingly concealed a bhikkhu's serious offense; in that matter. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of an offense, it arises from one origin—it arises from body, and from speech, and from mind... and so on...

118. Jānaṃ ūnavīsativassaṃ puggalaṃ upasampādentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Rājagahe paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule [V 0.0035] bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū jānaṃ ūnavīsativassaṃ puggalaṃ upasampādesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

118. Regarding the pācittiya for one who knowingly gives the higher ordination to a person under twenty years of age, where was it laid down? It was laid down at Rājagaha. Concerning whom? Concerning many bhikkhus. In what matter? Many bhikkhus knowingly gave the higher ordination to a person under twenty years of age; in that matter. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of an offense, it arises from three origins... and so on...

119. Jānaṃ [T 0.0053] theyyasatthena saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Aññataro bhikkhu jānaṃ theyyasatthena saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajji, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

119. Regarding the pācittiya for one who, knowing, travels along a long road in the same direction with a caravan of thieves, having made an agreement, where was it laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning a certain bhikkhu. In what matter? A certain bhikkhu, knowing, traveled along a long road in the same direction with a caravan of thieves, having made an agreement; in that matter. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of an offense, it arises from two origins: sometimes it arises from body and mind, but not from speech; sometimes it arises from body, and from speech, and from mind... and so on...

120. Mātugāmena saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ [M 0.0036] vatthusminti? Aññataro bhikkhu mātugāmena saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajji, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ catūhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

120. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for one who, having made an arrangement with a woman, travels along the same long road? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning a certain bhikkhu. In what case? A certain bhikkhu, having made an arrangement with a woman, traveled along the same long road; in that case. There is one promulgation. It arises from four of the six origins of offenses.

121. Pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Ariṭṭho bhikkhu gaddhabādhipubbo pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajji, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti. Kāyato ca vācato [T 0.0054] ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

121. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for one who does not relinquish a wicked view when being formally admonished up to the third time? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, who was formerly a vulture-killer. In what case? The bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, who was formerly a vulture-killer, did not relinquish a wicked view when being formally admonished up to the third time; in that case. There is one promulgation. It arises from one of the six origins of offenses. It arises from body, speech, and mind.

122. Jānaṃ tathāvādinā bhikkhunā ariṭṭhena bhikkhunā (ka.) akaṭānudhammena taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissaṭṭhena saddhiṃ sambhuñjantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū jānaṃ tathāvādinā ariṭṭhena bhikkhunā akaṭānudhammena taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissaṭṭhena saddhiṃ sambhuñjiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

122. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for one who knowingly partakes in communion with a bhikkhu who speaks thus, for whom the proper procedure has not been carried out, and who has not relinquished that view? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six bhikkhus. In what case? The group-of-six bhikkhus knowingly partook in communion with the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, who spoke thus, for whom the proper procedure had not been carried out, and who had not relinquished that view; in that case. There is one promulgation. It arises from three of the six origins of offenses.

123. Jānaṃ tathānāsitaṃ samaṇuddesaṃ upalāpentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā [V 0.0036] bhikkhū jānaṃ tathānāsitaṃ kaṇṭakaṃ [P 5.0024] samaṇuddesaṃ upalāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

123. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for one who knowingly persuades a novice who has been thus expelled? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six bhikkhus. In what case? The group-of-six bhikkhus knowingly persuaded the novice Kaṇṭaka, who had been thus expelled; in that case. There is one promulgation. It arises from three of the six origins of offenses.

Sappāṇakavaggo sattamo.

The Seventh Chapter, on Beings with Breath, is concluded.

8. Sahadhammikavaggo

8. The Chapter on What is in Accordance with the Dhamma

124. Bhikkhūhi [T 0.0055] sahadhammikaṃ vuccamānena “na tāvāhaṃ, āvuso, etasmiṃ sikkhāpade sikkhissāmi yāva na aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ byattaṃ vinayadharaṃ paripucchissāmī”ti [M 0.0037] bhaṇantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Kosambiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ channaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā channo bhikkhūhi sahadhammikaṃ vuccamāno “na tāvāhaṃ, āvuso, etasmiṃ sikkhāpade sikkhissāmi yāva na aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ byattaṃ vinayadharaṃ paripucchissāmī”ti bhaṇi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

124. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for a bhikkhu who, when being spoken to by the bhikkhus in accordance with the Dhamma, says, ‘Venerable Sirs, I will not train in this training rule until I have questioned another bhikkhu who is skilled and a master of the Vinaya’? It was laid down at Kosambī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Channa. In what case? The Venerable Channa, when being spoken to by the bhikkhus in accordance with the Dhamma, said, ‘Venerable Sirs, I will not train in this training rule until I have questioned another bhikkhu who is skilled and a master of the Vinaya’; in that case. There is one promulgation. It arises from three of the six origins of offenses.

125. Vinayaṃ vivaṇṇentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū vinayaṃ vivaṇṇesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

125. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for one who disparages the Vinaya? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six bhikkhus. In what case? The group-of-six bhikkhus disparaged the Vinaya; in that case. There is one promulgation. It arises from three of the six origins of offenses.

126. Mohanake pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū mohesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

126. Where was the Pācittiya offense for feigning ignorance laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six bhikkhus. In what case? The group-of-six bhikkhus feigned ignorance; in that case. There is one promulgation. It arises from three of the six origins of offenses.

127. Bhikkhussa kupitena anattamanena pahāraṃ dentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha [T 0.0056] paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kupitā anattamanā bhikkhūnaṃ pahāraṃ adaṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

127. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for one who, being angry and displeased, gives a blow to a bhikkhu? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six bhikkhus. In what case? The group-of-six bhikkhus, being angry and displeased, gave a blow to bhikkhus; in that case. There is one promulgation. It arises from one of the six origins of offenses—it arises from body and mind, not from speech.

128. Bhikkhussa kupitena anattamanena talasattikaṃ uggirantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti[V 0.0037]? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū kupitā anattamanā bhikkhūnaṃ talasattikaṃ uggiriṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

128. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for one who, being angry and displeased, raises his palm against a bhikkhu? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six bhikkhus. In what case? The group-of-six bhikkhus, being angry and displeased, raised their palms against bhikkhus; in that case. There is one promulgation. It arises from one of the six origins of offenses—it arises from body and mind, not from speech.

129. Bhikkhuṃ amūlakena saṅghādisesena anuddhaṃsentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha[M 0.0038]. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ amūlakena saṅghādisesena anuddhaṃsesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

129. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for one who accuses a bhikkhu of a groundless Saṅghādisesa offense? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six bhikkhus. In what case? The group-of-six bhikkhus accused a bhikkhu of a groundless Saṅghādisesa offense; in that case. There is one promulgation. It arises from three of the six origins of offenses.

130. Bhikkhussa sañcicca kukkuccaṃ upadahantassa uppādentassa (syā.) pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye [T 0.0057] bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhūnaṃ sañcicca kukkuccaṃ upadahiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

130. Where was the Pācittiya offense promulgated for a monk who intentionally causes worry to another monk? It was promulgated at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. On what occasion? The group-of-six monks intentionally caused worry to other monks. On that occasion. There is one promulgation. It arises from three of the six origins of offenses…and so on.

131. Bhikkhūnaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ [P 5.0025] upassutiṃ upassuti (?) tiṭṭhantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhūnaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ upassutiṃ tiṭṭhahiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

131. Where was the Pācittiya offense promulgated for a monk who stands eavesdropping on monks who are engaged in arguments, quarrels, or contentions? It was promulgated at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. On what occasion? The group-of-six monks stood eavesdropping on monks who were engaged in arguments, quarrels, or contentions. On that occasion. There is one promulgation. It arises from two of the six origins of offenses—it may arise from body and mind, not from speech; it may arise from body, speech, and mind…and so on.

132. Dhammikānaṃ kammānaṃ chandaṃ datvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṃ khiyyadhammaṃ (ka.) āpajjantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū dhammikānaṃ kammānaṃ chandaṃ datvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṃ āpajjiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

132. Where was the Pācittiya offense promulgated for a monk who, having given consent for lawful formal acts, afterwards engages in criticism? It was promulgated at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. On what occasion? The group-of-six monks, having given consent for lawful formal acts, afterwards engaged in criticism. On that occasion. There is one promulgation. It arises from three of the six origins of offenses…and so on.

133. Saṅghe vinicchayakathāya vattamānāya chandaṃ adatvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ[T 0.0058]. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ ārabbha[V 0.0038]. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Aññataro bhikkhu saṅghe vinicchayakathāya vattamānāya chandaṃ adatvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

133. Where was the Pācittiya offense promulgated for a monk who, while a discussion for a decision is proceeding in the Saṅgha, departs after rising from his seat without having given consent? It was promulgated at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning a certain monk. On what occasion? A certain monk, while a discussion for a decision was proceeding in the Saṅgha, departed after rising from his seat without having given consent. On that occasion. There is one promulgation. It arises from one of the six origins of offenses—it arises from body, speech, and mind…and so on.

134. Samagge [M 0.0039] saṅghena cīvaraṃ datvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṃ āpajjantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Rājagahe paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū samaggena saṅghena cīvaraṃ datvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṃ āpajjiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

134. Where was the Pācittiya offense promulgated for a monk who, having given a robe with the united Saṅgha, afterwards engages in criticism? It was promulgated at Rājagaha. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. On what occasion? The group-of-six monks, having given a robe with the united Saṅgha, afterwards engaged in criticism. On that occasion. There is one promulgation. It arises from three of the six origins of offenses…and so on.

135. Jānaṃ saṅghikaṃ lābhaṃ pariṇataṃ puggalassa pariṇāmentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū jānaṃ saṅghikaṃ lābhaṃ pariṇataṃ puggalassa pariṇāmesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

135. Where was the Pācittiya offense promulgated for a monk who knowingly diverts a designated gain belonging to the Saṅgha to an individual? It was promulgated at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. On what occasion? The group-of-six monks knowingly diverted a designated gain belonging to the Saṅgha to an individual. On that occasion. There is one promulgation. It arises from three of the six origins of offenses…and so on.

Sahadhammikavaggo aṭṭhamo.

The Sahadhammikavagga, the eighth.

9. Rājavaggo

9. 9. The Rājavagga

136. Pubbe [T 0.0059] appaṭisaṃviditena rañño antepuraṃ pavisantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā ānando pubbe appaṭisaṃvidito rañño antepuraṃ pāvisi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti kathinake…pe….

136. Where was the Pācittiya offense promulgated for a monk who enters the king's inner palace unannounced beforehand? It was promulgated at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Ānanda. On what occasion? The Venerable Ānanda entered the king's inner palace unannounced beforehand. On that occasion. There is one promulgation. It arises from two of the six origins of offenses…and so on.

137. Ratanaṃ uggaṇhantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ[P 5.0026]. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Aññataro bhikkhu ratanaṃ uggahesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, dve anupaññattiyo. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

137. Where was the Pācittiya offense promulgated for a monk who picks up a jewel? It was promulgated at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning a certain monk. On what occasion? A certain monk picked up a jewel. On that occasion. There is one promulgation and two supplementary promulgations. It arises from the six origins of offenses…and so on.

138. Santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā vikāle gāmaṃ pavisantassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti[V 0.0039]? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū vikāle gāmaṃ pavisiṃsu, tasmiṃ [T 0.0060] vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, tisso anupaññattiyo. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti kathinake…pe….

138. Where was the Pācittiya offense promulgated for a monk who enters a village at the wrong time without asking an available monk? It was promulgated at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six monks. On what occasion? The group-of-six monks entered a village at the wrong time. On that occasion. There is one promulgation and three supplementary promulgations. It arises from two of the six origins of offenses…and so on.

139. Aṭṭhimayaṃ [M 0.0040] vā dantamayaṃ vā visāṇamayaṃ vā sūcigharaṃ kārāpentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sakkesu paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū na mattaṃ jānitvā bahū sūcighare viññāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

139. Where was the Pācittiya offense promulgated for a monk who has a needle-case made of bone, ivory, or horn? It was promulgated among the Sakyans. Concerning whom? Concerning numerous monks.
