On what occasion? Numerous monks, not knowing the proper measure, requested many needle-cases. On that occasion. There is one promulgation. It arises from the six origins of offenses…and so on.

140. Pamāṇātikkantaṃ mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā kārāpentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā upanando sakyaputto ucce mañce sayi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

140. Where was the Pācittiya offense promulgated for a monk who has a bed or a bench made that exceeds the standard measurement? It was promulgated at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan son. On what occasion? The Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan son, lay on a high bed. On that occasion. There is one promulgation. It arises from the six origins of offenses…and so on.

141. Mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā tūlonaddhaṃ kārāpentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā tūlonaddhaṃ kārāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

141. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for a monk who has a bed or a bench stuffed with cotton made? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what matter? The group-of-six monks had a bed or a bench stuffed with cotton made. In that matter. There is one original formulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins... and so on.

142. Pamāṇātikkantaṃ [T 0.0061] nisīdanaṃ kārāpentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū appamāṇikāni nisīdanāni dhāresuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

142. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for a monk who has a sitting-cloth made that exceeds the standard measurement? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what matter? The group-of-six monks used sitting-cloths of no standard measurement. In that matter. There is one original formulation and one supplementary formulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins... and so on.

143. Pamāṇātikkantaṃ kaṇḍuppaṭicchādiṃ kārāpentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū appamāṇikāyo kaṇḍuppaṭicchādiyo dhāresuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

143. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for a monk who has a scab-covering cloth made that exceeds the standard measurement? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what matter? The group-of-six monks used scab-covering cloths of no standard measurement. In that matter. There is one original formulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins... and so on.

144. Pamāṇātikkantaṃ [V 0.0040] vassikasāṭikaṃ kārāpentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha[M 0.0041]. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū appamāṇikāyo vassikasāṭikāyo dhāresuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

144. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for a monk who has a rains-bathing cloth made that exceeds the standard measurement? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what matter? The group-of-six monks used rains-bathing cloths of no standard measurement. In that matter. There is one original formulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins... and so on.

145. Sugatacīvarappamāṇaṃ [P 5.0027] cīvaraṃ kārāpentassa pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ nandaṃ [T 0.0062] ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā nando sugatacīvarappamāṇaṃ cīvaraṃ dhāresi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

145. Where was the Pācittiya offense laid down for a monk who has a robe made to the measurement of the Sugata's robe? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? Concerning the Venerable Nanda. In what matter? The Venerable Nanda wore a robe of the measurement of the Sugata's robe. In that matter. There is one original formulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins... and so on.

Rājavaggo navamo.

The Rājavagga, the ninth.

Dvenavuti pācittiyā niṭṭhitā.

The ninety-two Pācittiya training rules are concluded.

Khuddakaṃ samattaṃ.

The Khuddaka is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of that is:

Musā omasapesuññaṃ, padaseyyā ca itthiyā;

Aññatra viññunā bhūtā desanārocanā ceva (sī. syā.), duṭṭhullāpatti khaṇanā.

The training rule on false speech, the training rule on contemptuous speech, the training rule on slander, the Padasodhamma training rule, the first Sahaseyya training rule, the second Sahaseyya training rule concerning a woman, the Dhammadassanā training rule known as 'Aññatra viññunā', the Bhūtārocana training rule, the Duṭṭhullārocana training rule, and the Pathavīkhaṇana training rule.

Bhūtaṃ aññāya ujjhāyi bhūtaññavādaujjhāyi (sī.), mañco seyyo ca vuccati;

Pubbe nikkaḍḍhanāhacca, dvāraṃ sappāṇakena ca.

The Bhūtagāma training rule, the Aññavādaka training rule, the Ujjhāpanaka training rule, the first Senāsana training rule and the second Senāsana training rule are spoken of; the Anupakhajja training rule marked by 'pubbe', the Nikkaḍḍhana training rule, the Āhaccapādaka training rule, the Mahallakavihāra training rule marked by the word 'dvāra', and the Sappāṇaka training rule.

Asammatā atthaṅgate, upassayāmisena ca;

Dade sibbe vidhānena, nāvā bhuñjeyya ekato.

The Ovāda training rule, the Atthaṅgata training rule, the Bhikkhunupassaya training rule, and the Āmisa training rule; the Cīvaradāna training rule, the Cīvarasibbana training rule, the Saṃvidhāna training rule, the Nāvābhiruhana training rule, the Bhikkhunīparipācita training rule, and the Rahonisajja training rule.

Piṇḍaṃ gaṇaṃ paraṃ pūvaṃ, pavārito pavāritaṃ;

Vikālaṃ sannidhi khīraṃ, dantaponena te dasa.

The Āvasathapiṇḍa training rule, the Gaṇabhojana training rule, the Paramparabhojana training rule, the Kāṇamātā training rule marked by 'pūva', the first Pavāraṇā training rule, the second Pavāraṇā training rule, the Vikālabhojana training rule, the Sannidhikāraka training rule, the Paṇītabhojana training rule, and the Dantapona training rule; these are the ten.

Acelakaṃ uyyokhajja acelakānupakhajja (ka.), paṭicchannaṃ rahena ca;

Nimantito paccayehi, senāvasanuyyodhikaṃ.

The Acelaka training rule, the Uyyojana training rule, the Sabhojana training rule, the Rahopaṭicchanna training rule, and the Rahonisajja training rule; the Cāritta training rule, the Mahānāma training rule, the Uyyuttasenā training rule, the Senāvasana training rule, and the Uyyodhika training rule.

Surā [V 0.0041] aṅguli hāso ca, anādariyañca bhiṃsanaṃ;

Joti nahāna dubbaṇṇaṃ, sāmaṃ apanidhena ca.

The Surāpāna training rule, the Aṅgulipatodaka training rule, and the Hasadhamma training rule; and the Anādariya training rule, the Bhiṃsāpana training rule, the Joti training rule, the Nahāna training rule, the Dubbaṇṇakaraṇa training rule, the Vikappanā training rule, and the Cīvara-apanidhāna training rule.

Sañciccudakakammā [M 0.0042] ca, duṭṭhullaṃ ūnavīsati;

Theyyaitthiavadesaṃ ariṭṭhakaṃ (vibhaṅge), saṃvāse nāsitena ca.

The Sañciccapāṇa training rule, the Sappāṇaka training rule, and the Ukkoṭana training rule; the Duṭṭhulla training rule, the Ūnavīsativassa training rule, the Theyyasattha training rule, the Saṃvidhāna training rule concerning a woman, the Ariṭṭha training rule concerning a wrong view, the Ukkhittaka-sambhoga training rule, and the Kaṇḍaka training rule.

Sahadhammikavilekhā, moho pahārenuggire;

Amūlakañca sañcicca, sossāmi khiyyapakkame.

The Sahadhammika training rule, the Vilekhana training rule, the Mohana training rule, the Pahāra training rule, the Talasattika training rule; and the Amūlaka training rule, the Sañcicca training rule, the Upassuti training rule, the Kammapaṭibāhana training rule, and the Chandaṃ-adatvā-gamana training rule.

Saṅghena cīvaraṃ datvā, pariṇāmeyya puggale;

Raññañca ratanaṃ santaṃ, sūci mañco ca tūlikā;

Nisīdanaṃ kaṇḍucchādi, vassikā sugatena cāti.

The Dubbala training rule known as 'Saṅghena cīvaraṃ datvā', the Pariṇāmana training rule, and the Antepura training rule marked by 'rañña'; the Ratana training rule, the Vikālagāmappavesana training rule, the Sūcighara training rule, the Mañca training rule, and the Tūlonaddha training rule; the Nisīdana training rule, the Kaṇḍuppaṭicchādana training rule, the Vassikasāṭika training rule, and the Nandatthera training rule. Thus ends the summary of the training rules.

Tesaṃ vaggānaṃ uddānaṃ –

The summary of those chapters is:

Musā bhūtā ca ovādo, bhojanācelakena ca;

Surā sappāṇakā dhammo, rājavaggena te navāti.

The Musāvādavagga, and the Bhūtagāmavagga, the Ovādavagga, the Bhojanavagga, and the Acelakavagga; the Surāmerayavagga, the Sappāṇakavagga, the Sahadhammikavagga, together with the Rājavagga; these are the nine. Thus ends the summary.

6. Pāṭidesanīyakaṇḍaṃ

6. The Section on Offenses to be Acknowledged

146. Yaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā antaragharaṃ paviṭṭhāya hatthato khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā bhuñjantassa pāṭidesanīyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Aññataraṃ [T 0.0063] bhikkhuṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Aññataro bhikkhu aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā antaragharaṃ paviṭṭhāya hatthato āmisaṃ paṭiggahesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi [P 5.0028] samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato samuṭṭhāti, na vācato na cittato; siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

146. The Pāṭidesanīya training rule that was laid down by that Blessed One—the Knowing One, the Seeing One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—for a monk who, having received with his own hand either hard food or soft food from the hand of an unrelated bhikkhunī who has entered a house, then eats it: where was it laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning a certain monk. In what matter was it laid down? A certain monk received almsfood from the hand of an unrelated bhikkhunī who had entered a house; it was laid down in that matter. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins: sometimes it arises from the body, not from speech, not from mind; sometimes it arises from the body and from the mind, not from speech... and so on.

147. Bhikkhuniyā vosāsantiyā na nivāretvā bhuñjantassa pāṭidesanīyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Rājagahe paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo vosāsantiyo na nivāresuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā [V 0.0042] paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca vācato ca samuṭṭhāti, na cittato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

147. The Pāṭidesanīya training rule for a monk who eats without stopping a bhikkhunī who is directing the meal: where was it laid down? It was laid down in Rājagaha. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the group-of-six monks. In what matter was it laid down? The group-of-six monks did not stop the bhikkhunīs who were directing the meal; it was laid down in that matter. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins: sometimes it arises from the body and from speech, not from mind; sometimes it arises from the body, from speech, and from the mind... and so on.

148. Sekkhasammatesu [M 0.0043] kulesu khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā bhuñjantassa pāṭidesanīyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū na mattaṃ jānitvā paṭiggahesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, dve anupaññattiyo. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato samuṭṭhāti, na vācato na cittato; siyā kāyato ca cittato [T 0.0064] ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

148. The Pāṭidesanīya training rule for a monk who, in families designated as 'learners', having received with his own hand either hard food or soft food, then eats it: where was it laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning many monks. In what matter was it laid down? Many monks received without knowing the proper measure; it was laid down in that matter. There is one enactment and two supplementary enactments. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins: sometimes it arises from the body, not from speech, not from mind; sometimes it arises from the body and from the mind, not from speech... etc.

149. Āraññakesu senāsanesu pubbe appaṭisaṃviditaṃ khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā ajjhārāme sahatthā paṭiggahetvā bhuñjantassa pāṭidesanīyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sakkesu paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti. Sambahulā bhikkhū ārāme core paṭivasante nārocesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca vācato ca samuṭṭhāti, na cittato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

149. The Pāṭidesanīya training rule for a monk who, in forest lodgings not previously announced as dangerous, having received with his own hand either hard food or soft food within the monastery grounds, then eats it: where was it laid down? It was laid down among the Sakyans. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning many monks. In what matter was it laid down? Many monks did not inform about the thieves residing in the monastery; it was laid down in that matter. There is one enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins: sometimes it arises from the body and from speech, not from mind; sometimes it arises from the body, from speech, and from the mind... etc.

Cattāro pāṭidesanīyā niṭṭhitā.

The four Pāṭidesanīya training rules are concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of that is:

Aññātikāya vosāsaṃ, sekkhaāraññakena ca;

Pāṭidesanīyā cattāro, sambuddhena pakāsitāti.

The first Pāṭidesanīya rule concerning an unrelated bhikkhunī, the second concerning directing a meal, the third concerning learners, and the fourth concerning a forest dwelling; these four Pāṭidesanīya training rules were declared by the Perfectly Enlightened One. Thus ends the summary.

7. Sekhiyakaṇḍaṃ

7. The Section on Training

1. Parimaṇḍalavaggo

1. The Chapter on Wearing Evenly

150. Yaṃ [V 0.0043] tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena anādariyaṃ paṭicca purato vā pacchato vā olambentena nivāsentassa dukkaṭaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū puratopi pacchatopi olambentā nivāsesuṃ, tasmiṃ [T 0.0065] vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ [M 0.0044] ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

150. Where was the offence of wrong-doing laid down by that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, who knows and sees, for one who, on account of disrespect, wears the lower robe allowing it to hang down in front or behind? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the monks of the group of six. In what matter? The monks of the group of six wore their lower robes allowing them to hang down both in front and behind; in that matter. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offences, it arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech… etc.

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca purato vā pacchato vā olambentena pārupantassa dukkaṭaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū puratopi pacchatopi olambentā pārupiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

Where was the offence of wrong-doing laid down for one who, on account of disrespect, wears the upper robe allowing it to hang down in front or behind? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the monks of the group of six. In what matter? The monks of the group of six wore their upper robes allowing them to hang down both in front and behind; in that matter. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offences, it arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech… etc.

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca kāyaṃ vivaritvā antaraghare gacchantassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti. Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

The offence of wrong-doing for one who, on account of disrespect, walks within an inhabited area with the body uncovered… etc. There is one enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech… etc.

Anādariyaṃ [P 5.0029] paṭicca kāyaṃ vivaritvā antaraghare nisīdantassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti. Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

The offence of wrong-doing for one who, on account of disrespect, sits within an inhabited area with the body uncovered… etc. There is one enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech… etc.

2. Ujjagghikavaggo

2. The Chapter on Loud Laughter

151. Anādariyaṃ paṭicca ujjagghikāya antaraghare gacchantassa dukkaṭaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū mahāhasitaṃ hasantā antaraghare gacchiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

151. Where was the offence of wrong-doing laid down for a monk who, on account of disrespect, goes in an inhabited area laughing loudly? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the monks of the group of six. In what matter was it laid down? The monks of the group of six went in an inhabited area laughing a great laugh; in that matter, it was laid down. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body, and from speech, and from mind... etc.

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca ujjagghikāya antaraghare nisīdantassa dukkaṭaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? The monks of the group of six sat in an inhabited area laughing a great laugh; in that case, it was laid down. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body, and from speech, and from mind... and so on.

For a monk who, on account of disrespect, goes in an inhabited area swaying his body, there is an offense of wrong-doing... and so on. There is one original enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, but not from speech... and so on.

153. Anādariyaṃ [V 0.0048] paṭicca asakkaccaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjantassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti. Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

Due to disrespect, for one who eats almsfood while looking here and there, there is an offense of wrong-doing... and so on... There is one enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech... and so on...

Anādariyaṃ [T 0.0071] paṭicca tahaṃ tahaṃ omasitvā piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjantassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti. Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

Due to disrespect, for one who eats almsfood while inspecting it here and there, there is an offense of wrong-doing... and so on... There is one enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech... and so on...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca sūpaññeva bahuṃ bhuñjantassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti. Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

Due to disrespect, for one who eats much curry only, there is an offense of wrong-doing... and so on... There is one enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech... and so on...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca thūpakato omadditvā piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjantassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti. Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

Due to disrespect, for one who eats almsfood by pressing down from the top of the mound, there is an offense of wrong-doing... and so on... There is one enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech... and so on...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca sūpaṃ vā byañjanaṃ vā odanena paṭicchādentassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti. Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

Due to disrespect, for one who conceals either curry or relish with rice, there is an offense of wrong-doing... and so on... There is one enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech... and so on...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca sūpaṃ vā odanaṃ vā agilāno attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjantassa dukkaṭaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sūpampi odanampi attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā [M 0.0049] paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Due to disrespect, for one who, not being ill, eats after having requested either curry or rice for one's own sake, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Where was it enacted? It was enacted in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it enacted? It was enacted concerning the group-of-six monks. In what matter was it enacted? The group-of-six monks ate after having requested both curry and rice for their own sake; in that matter it was enacted. There is one enactment; there is one supplementary enactment. Among the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins: sometimes it arises from body and from mind, not from speech; sometimes it arises from body, from speech, and from mind... and so on...

Anādariyaṃ [T 0.0072][V 0.0049] paṭicca ujjhānasaññinā paresaṃ pattaṃ olokentassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti. Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

Due to disrespect, for one who looks at another's bowl with the perception of finding fault, there is an offense of wrong-doing... and so on... There is one enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech... and so on...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca mahantaṃ kabaḷaṃ karontassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti. Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

Due to disrespect, for one who makes a large mouthful, there is an offense of wrong-doing... and so on... There is one enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech... and so on...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca dīghaṃ ālopaṃ karontassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti. Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

Due to disrespect, for one who makes a long mouthful, there is an offense of wrong-doing... and so on... There is one enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech... and so on...

Piṇḍapātavaggo catuttho.

The Fourth Chapter on Almsfood is concluded.

154. Due to disrespect, for one who opens the mouth before the morsel is brought to it, there is an offense of wrong-doing... and so on... There is one enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech... and so on...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca bhuñjamānena sabbaṃ hatthaṃ mukhe pakkhipantassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti. Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

Due to disrespect, for one who, while eating, puts the whole hand into the mouth, there is an offense of wrong-doing... and so on... There is one enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech... and so on...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca sakabaḷena mukhena byāharantassa dukkaṭaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha[P 5.0031]. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sakabaḷena mukhena byāhariṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Due to disrespect, for one who speaks with a mouth full of food, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Where was it enacted? It was enacted in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it enacted? It was enacted concerning the group-of-six monks. In what matter was it enacted? The group-of-six monks spoke with their mouths full of food; in that matter it was enacted. There is one enactment. Among the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body, from speech, and from mind... and so on...

Anādariyaṃ [M 0.0050] paṭicca piṇḍukkhepakaṃ bhuñjantassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā [T 0.0073] paññatti. Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

Due to disrespect, for one who eats by tossing up morsels of food, there is an offense of wrong-doing... and so on... There is one enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech... and so on...

Anādariyaṃ [V 0.0050] paṭicca kabaḷāvacchedakaṃ bhuñjantassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti. Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

Due to disrespect, for one who eats by biting off from a morsel, there is an offense of wrong-doing... and so on... There is one enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech... and so on...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca avagaṇḍakārakaṃ bhuñjantassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti. Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

Due to disrespect, for one who eats while stuffing the cheeks, there is an offense of wrong-doing... and so on... There is one enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech... and so on...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca hatthaniddhunakaṃ bhuñjantassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti. Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

Due to disrespect, for one who eats while shaking the hand, there is an offense of wrong-doing... and so on... There is one enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech... and so on...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca sitthāvakārakaṃ bhuñjantassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti. Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

Due to disrespect, for one who eats while scattering grains of rice, there is an offense of wrong-doing... and so on... There is one enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech... and so on...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca jivhānicchārakaṃ bhuñjantassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti. Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

Due to disrespect, for one who eats while sticking out the tongue, there is an offense of wrong-doing... and so on... There is one enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech... and so on...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca capucapukārakaṃ bhuñjantassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti. Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

On account of disrespect, for one who eats making a 'capu capu' sound, there is an offense of wrong-doing... There is one original enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from the body and from the mind, not from speech...

Kabaḷavaggo pañcamo.

The Chapter on Morsels, the Fifth.

6. Surusuruvaggo

6. The Surusuru Chapter

155. Anādariyaṃ [T 0.0074] paṭicca surusurukārakaṃ bhuñjantassa dukkaṭaṃ kattha paññattanti? Kosambiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū surusurukārakaṃ khīraṃ piviṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ[M 0.0051]. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

155. The offense of wrong-doing for one who eats making a 'suru suru' sound on account of disrespect—where was it laid down? It was laid down in Kosambī. Concerning whom was it laid down? Concerning many monks. In what instance? Many monks drank milk making a 'suru suru' sound; in that instance. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from the body and from the mind, not from speech...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca hatthanillehakaṃ bhuñjantassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti. Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

On account of disrespect, for one who eats licking the hand, there is an offense of wrong-doing... There is one enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from the body and from the mind, not from speech...

Anādariyaṃ [V 0.0051] paṭicca pattanillehakaṃ bhuñjantassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti. Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

On account of disrespect, for one who eats scraping the bowl, there is an offense of wrong-doing... There is one enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from the body and from the mind, not from speech...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca oṭṭhanillehakaṃ bhuñjantassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti. Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

On account of disrespect, for one who eats licking the lips, there is an offense of wrong-doing... There is one enactment. It arises from one origin: it arises from the body and from the mind, not from speech...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca sāmisena hatthena pānīyathālakaṃ paṭiggaṇhantassa dukkaṭaṃ kattha paññattanti? Bhaggesu paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū sāmisena hatthena pānīyathālakaṃ paṭiggahesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena [T 0.0075] samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

The offense of wrong-doing for one who receives a drinking-water vessel with a hand soiled with food on account of disrespect—where was it laid down? It was laid down among the Bhaggas. Concerning whom was it laid down? Concerning many monks. In what instance? Many monks received a drinking-water vessel with a hand soiled with food; in that instance. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from the body and from the mind, not from speech...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca sasitthakaṃ pattadhovanaṃ antaraghare chaḍḍentassa dukkaṭaṃ kattha paññattanti? Bhaggesu paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū sasitthakaṃ pattadhovanaṃ antaraghare chaḍḍesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

The offense of wrong-doing for one who discards bowl-washing water containing lumps of rice within an inhabited area on account of disrespect—where was it laid down? It was laid down among the Bhaggas. Concerning whom was it laid down? Concerning many monks. In what instance? Many monks discarded bowl-washing water containing lumps of rice within an inhabited area; in that instance. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from the body and from the mind, not from speech...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca chattapāṇissa dhammaṃ desentassa dukkaṭaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū chattapāṇissa dhammaṃ desesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato…pe….

The offense of wrong-doing for one who teaches the Dhamma to a person with an umbrella in hand on account of disrespect—where was it laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? Concerning the group-of-six monks. In what instance? The group-of-six monks taught the Dhamma to a person with an umbrella in hand; in that instance. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from speech and from the mind, not from the body...

Anādariyaṃ [M 0.0052] paṭicca daṇḍapāṇissa dhammaṃ desentassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato…pe….

On account of disrespect, for one who teaches the Dhamma to a person with a staff in hand, there is an offense of wrong-doing... There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from speech and from the mind, not from the body...

Anādariyaṃ [T 0.0076] paṭicca satthapāṇissa dhammaṃ desentassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti, ekā [V 0.0052] anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato…pe….

On account of disrespect, for one who teaches the Dhamma to a person with a sword in hand, there is an offense of wrong-doing... There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from speech and from the mind, not from the body...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca āvudhapāṇissa dhammaṃ desentassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato…pe….

On account of disrespect, for one who teaches the Dhamma to a person with a weapon in hand, there is an offense of wrong-doing... There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from speech and from the mind, not from the body...

Surusuruvaggo chaṭṭho.

The Surusuru Chapter, the Sixth.

7. The Chapter on Footwear

156. Anādariyaṃ paṭicca pādukāruḷhassa dhammaṃ desentassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato…pe….

156. On account of disrespect, for one who teaches the Dhamma to a person wearing sandals, there is an offense of wrong-doing... There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from speech and from the mind, not from the body...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca upāhanāruḷhassa dhammaṃ desentassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato…pe….
