Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from speech and from the mind, not from the body...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca yānagatassa dhammaṃ desentassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti[T 0.0077], na kāyato…pe….

On account of disrespect, for one who teaches the Dhamma to a person in a vehicle, there is an offense of wrong-doing... There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from speech and from the mind, not from the body...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca sayanagatassa dhammaṃ desentassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato…pe….

On account of disrespect, for one who teaches the Dhamma to a person who is lying down, there is an offense of wrong-doing... There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from speech and from the mind, not from the body...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca pallatthikāya nisinnassa dhammaṃ desentassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhāne [M 0.0053] samuṭṭhāti – vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato…pe….

On account of disrespect, for one who teaches the Dhamma to a person sitting with a supporting strap, there is an offense of wrong-doing... There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from speech and from the mind, not from the body...

Anādariyaṃ [V 0.0053] paṭicca veṭhitasīsassa [P 5.0032] dhammaṃ desentassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato…pe….

On account of disrespect, for a bhikkhu teaching the Dhamma to a person with a wrapped head, there is a dukkaṭa offense... There is one original formulation, one supplementary formulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from speech and from mind, not from body...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca oguṇṭhitasīsassa dhammaṃ desentassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato…pe….

On account of disrespect, for a bhikkhu teaching the Dhamma to a person with a covered head, there is a dukkaṭa offense... There is one original formulation, one supplementary formulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from speech and from mind, not from body...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca chamāyaṃ nisīditvā āsane nisinnassa dhammaṃ desentassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti [T 0.0078] – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

On account of disrespect, for a bhikkhu who, sitting on the ground, teaches the Dhamma to a person sitting on a seat, there is a dukkaṭa offense... There is one original formulation, one supplementary formulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body, from speech, and from mind...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca nīce āsane nisīditvā ucce āsane nisinnassa dhammaṃ desentassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

On account of disrespect, for a bhikkhu who, sitting on a low seat, teaches the Dhamma to a person sitting on a high seat, there is a dukkaṭa offense... There is one original formulation, one supplementary formulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body, from speech, and from mind...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca ṭhitena nisinnassa dhammaṃ desentassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

On account of disrespect, for a bhikkhu who, while standing, teaches the Dhamma to a person who is sitting, there is a dukkaṭa offense... There is one original formulation, one supplementary formulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body, from speech, and from mind...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca pacchato gacchantena purato gacchantassa dhammaṃ desentassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

On account of disrespect, for a bhikkhu who, while walking behind, teaches the Dhamma to a person walking in front, there is a dukkaṭa offense... There is one original formulation, one supplementary formulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body, from speech, and from mind...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca uppathena gacchantena pathena gacchantassa dhammaṃ desentassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

On account of disrespect, for a bhikkhu who, while walking off the path, teaches the Dhamma to a person walking on the path, there is a dukkaṭa offense... There is one original formulation, one supplementary formulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body, from speech, and from mind...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca ṭhitena uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā karontassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti[V 0.0054], ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhāne [M 0.0054] samuṭṭhāti – kāyato [T 0.0079] ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

On account of disrespect, for a bhikkhu who defecates or urinates while standing, there is a dukkaṭa offense... There is one original formulation, one supplementary formulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca harite uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karontassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

On account of disrespect, for a bhikkhu who defecates, urinates, or spits on greenery, there is a dukkaṭa offense... There is one original formulation, one supplementary formulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech...

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karontassa dukkaṭaṃ…pe… kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū udake uccārampi passāvampi kheḷampi akaṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

On account of disrespect, for a bhikkhu who defecates, urinates, or spits in water, there is a dukkaṭa offense... Where was it laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six bhikkhus. In what matter? In the matter of the group-of-six bhikkhus who defecated, urinated, and spat in water. There is one original formulation, one supplementary formulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech...

Pādukavaggo sattamo.

The seventh chapter on footwear.

Pañcasattati sekhiyā niṭṭhitā.

The seventy-five training rules are concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Parimaṇḍalaṃ paṭicchannaṃ, susaṃvutokkhittacakkhu;

Ukkhittojjagghikā saddo, tayo ceva pacālanā.

Dressing all around, being well-covered, well-restrained, with downcast eyes; not hitching up the robe, loud laughter, little sound, and the three kinds of swaying.

Khambhaṃ oguṇṭhito cevukkuṭipallatthikāya ca;

Sakkaccaṃ [T 0.0080] pattasaññī ca, samasūpaṃ samatittikaṃ samatitthikaṃ (ka.).

With arms akimbo, and with head covered; squatting, and sitting cross-legged; receiving respectfully, with mind on the bowl, with level curry, and level to the brim.

Sakkaccaṃ pattasaññī ca, sapadānaṃ samasūpakaṃ;

Thūpakato paṭicchannaṃ, viññattujjhānasaññinā.

Respectfully, and with mind on the bowl; in sequence, with level curry; making a heap, covering, asking, and looking with annoyance.

Na mahantaṃ maṇḍalaṃ dvāraṃ, sabbaṃ hatthaṃ na byāhare;

Ukkhepo chedanā gaṇḍo, dhunaṃ sitthāvakārakaṃ.

Not too large, round, opening the mouth; the whole hand, not speaking; tossing, nibbling, stuffing the cheeks; shaking, and scattering rice.

Jivhānicchārakañceva[V 0.0055], capucapu surusuru;

Hattho [P 5.0033] patto ca oṭṭho ca, sāmisaṃ sitthakena ca.

Sticking out the tongue; smacking, slurping; licking the hand, the bowl, and the lips; with a soiled hand, and with rice grains.

Chattapāṇissa [M 0.0055] saddhammaṃ, na desenti tathāgatā;

Evameva daṇḍapāṇissa, satthaāvudhapāṇinaṃ.

The Tathāgatas do not teach the good Dhamma to one holding a parasol; just so, to one holding a staff, a knife, or a weapon.

Pādukā upāhanā ceva, yānaseyyāgatassa ca;

Pallatthikā nisinnassa, veṭhitoguṇṭhitassa ca.

To one wearing wooden sandals and other footwear; and to one who is in a vehicle or on a bed; to one sitting cross-legged; and to one whose head is wrapped or covered.

Chamā nīcāsane ṭhāne, pacchato uppathena ca;

Ṭhitakena na kātabbaṃ, harite udakamhi cāti.

On the ground; on a low seat; while standing; from behind; and from off the path. It should not be done by one who is standing, nor on greenery, nor in water.

Tesaṃ vaggānamuddānaṃ –

The summary of those chapters:

Parimaṇḍalaujjagghi, khambhaṃ piṇḍaṃ tatheva ca;

Kabaḷā surusuru ca, pādukena ca sattamāti.

The Parimaṇḍala, Ujjagghika, Khambhaka, and Piṇḍapāta chapters; the Kabaḷa and Surusuru chapters, and the Pāduka chapter as the seventh.

Mahāvibhaṅge katthapaññattivāro niṭṭhito.

In the Great Analysis, the section on where it was laid down is concluded.

2. Katāpattivāro

2. The Section on Committed Offenses

1. Pārājikakaṇḍaṃ

1. The Chapter on the Pārājikas

157. Methunaṃ [V 0.0056] dhammaṃ paṭisevanto kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevanto tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Akkhāyite sarīre methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevati, āpatti pārājikassa; yebhuyyena khāyite [T 0.0081] sarīre methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevati, āpatti thullaccayassa; vaṭṭakate vivaṭakate (syā.) mukhe acchupantaṃ aṅgajātaṃ paveseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa – methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevanto imā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati.

157. How many offenses does one who engages in sexual intercourse incur? One who engages in sexual intercourse incurs three offenses. If one engages in sexual intercourse with a body that has not been eaten, it is an offense entailing expulsion. If one engages in sexual intercourse with a body that has been mostly eaten, it is a grave offense. If one inserts the sexual organ into a wide-open mouth without it touching, it is an offense of wrong-doing. One who engages in sexual intercourse incurs these three offenses.

158. Adinnaṃ ādiyanto kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Adinnaṃ ādiyanto tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Pañcamāsakaṃ vā atirekapañcamāsakaṃ vā agghanakaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyati, āpatti pārājikassa; atirekamāsakaṃ vā ūnapañcamāsakaṃ vā agghanakaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyati, āpatti thullaccayassa; māsakaṃ vā ūnamāsakaṃ vā agghanakaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyati, āpatti dukkaṭassa – adinnaṃ ādiyanto imā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati.

158. How many offenses does a bhikkhu who takes what is not given incur? A bhikkhu who takes what is not given incurs three offenses. If, with the intention of theft, one takes what is not given that is of the value of five māsakas or more than five māsakas, it is an offense of pārājika. If, with the intention of theft, one takes what is not given that is of the value of more than one māsaka but less than five māsakas, it is an offense of thullaccaya. If, with the intention of theft, one takes what is not given that is of the value of one māsaka or less than one māsaka, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. A bhikkhu who takes what is not given incurs these three offenses.

159. Sañcicca [M 0.0056] manussaviggahaṃ jīvitā voropento kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Sañcicca manussaviggahaṃ jīvitā voropento tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Manussaṃ odissa opātaṃ khaṇati “papatitvā marissatī”ti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; papatite dukkhā vedanā uppajjati, āpatti thullaccayassa; marati, āpatti pārājikassa – sañcicca manussaviggahaṃ jīvitā voropento imā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati.

159. How many offenses does a bhikkhu who intentionally deprives a human being of life incur? A bhikkhu who intentionally deprives a human being of life incurs three offenses. If one digs a pit with a human in mind, thinking, ‘Having fallen, he will die,’ it is an offense of dukkaṭa. When he has fallen and a painful feeling arises, it is an offense of thullaccaya. If he dies, it is an offense of pārājika. A bhikkhu who intentionally deprives a human being of life incurs these three offenses.

160. Asantaṃ abhūtaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ ullapanto kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Asantaṃ [V 0.0057] abhūtaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ ullapanto tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Pāpiccho icchāpakato asantaṃ abhūtaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ ullapati, āpatti pārājikassa; “yo te vihāre [T 0.0082] vasati, so bhikkhu arahā”ti bhaṇati, paṭivijānantassa āpatti thullaccayassa; na paṭivijānantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa – asantaṃ abhūtaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ ullapanto imā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati.

160. How many offenses does a bhikkhu who claims a non-existent, untrue superhuman state incur? A bhikkhu who claims a non-existent, untrue superhuman state incurs three offenses. If, having evil wishes and being overcome by desire, one claims a non-existent, untrue superhuman state, it is an offense of pārājika. If one says, ‘The bhikkhu who lives in your monastery is an Arahant,’ it is an offense of thullaccaya if the listener understands, and an offense of dukkaṭa if the listener does not understand. A bhikkhu who claims a non-existent, untrue superhuman state incurs these three offenses.

Cattāro pārājikā niṭṭhitā.

The four Pārājikas are concluded.

2. Saṅghādisesakaṇḍaṃ

2. The Chapter on the Saṅghādisesas

161. Upakkamitvā asuciṃ mocento tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Ceteti upakkamati [P 5.0034] muccati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa; ceteti upakkamati na muccati, āpatti thullaccayassa; payoge dukkaṭaṃ.

161. A bhikkhu who, having made an effort, emits semen incurs three offenses. If he intends, makes an effort, and it is emitted, it is an offense of saṅghādisesa; if he intends, makes an effort, but it is not emitted, it is an offense of thullaccaya; in the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Mātugāmena saddhiṃ kāyasaṃsaggaṃ samāpajjanto tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Kāyena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa; kāyena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti thullaccayassa; kāyapaṭibaddhena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

A bhikkhu engaging in bodily contact with a woman incurs three offenses. If he touches body with body, it is an offense of saṅghādisesa; if he touches with his body something connected to her body, it is an offense of thullaccaya; if he touches with something connected to his body something connected to her body, it is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Mātugāmaṃ duṭṭhullāhi vācāhi obhāsento tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Vaccamaggaṃ passāvamaggaṃ ādissa vaṇṇampi bhaṇati, avaṇṇampi bhaṇati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa; vaccamaggaṃ passāvamaggaṃ ṭhapetvā adhakkhakaṃ ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalaṃ ādissa vaṇṇampi bhaṇati avaṇṇampi bhaṇati, āpatti thullaccayassa; kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ ādissa vaṇṇampi bhaṇati avaṇṇampi bhaṇati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

A bhikkhu who addresses a woman with coarse words incurs three offenses. If, referring to the passages for feces or urine, he speaks in praise or in dispraise, it is an offense of saṅghādisesa; if, setting aside the passages for feces and urine, he speaks in praise or in dispraise referring to the area below the collarbones and above the knees, it is an offense of thullaccaya; if he speaks in praise or in dispraise referring to something connected to the body, it is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Attakāmapāricariyā [M 0.0057] vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanto tisso āpattiyo āpajjati[T 0.0083]. Mātugāmassa santike attakāmapāricariyāya vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa; paṇḍakassa santike attakāmapāricariyāya vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, āpatti thullaccayassa; tiracchānagatassa santike attakāmapāricariyāya vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

A bhikkhu who speaks in praise of service for one's own sensual pleasure incurs three offenses. If he speaks in praise of service for one's own sensual pleasure in the presence of a woman, it is an offense of saṅghādisesa; if he does so in the presence of a paṇḍaka, it is an offense of thullaccaya; if he does so in the presence of an animal, it is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Sañcarittaṃ samāpajjanto tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Paṭiggaṇhāti vīmaṃsati paccāharati[V 0.0058], āpatti saṅghādisesassa; paṭiggaṇhāti vīmaṃsati na paccāharati, āpatti thullaccayassa; paṭiggaṇhāti na vīmaṃsati na paccāharati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

A bhikkhu who engages in matchmaking incurs three offenses. If he accepts, investigates, and reports back, it is an offense of saṅghādisesa; if he accepts and investigates but does not report back, it is an offense of thullaccaya; if he accepts but does not investigate and does not report back, it is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Saññācikāya kuṭiṃ kārāpento tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Kārāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; ekaṃ piṇḍaṃ anāgate, āpatti thullaccayassa; tasmiṃ piṇḍe āgate, āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

A bhikkhu who has a hut built by means of solicitation incurs three offenses. In having it built, there is an offense of dukkaṭa in the effort; before one clod of earth arrives, it is an offense of thullaccaya; when that clod of earth has arrived, it is an offense of saṅghādisesa.

Mahallakaṃ vihāraṃ kārāpento tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Kārāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; ekaṃ piṇḍaṃ anāgate, āpatti thullaccayassa; tasmiṃ piṇḍe āgate, āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

A bhikkhu who has a large monastery built incurs three offenses. In having it built, there is an offense of dukkaṭa in the effort; before one clod of earth arrives, it is an offense of thullaccaya; when that clod of earth has arrived, it is an offense of saṅghādisesa.

Bhikkhuṃ amūlakena pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṃsento tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Anokāsaṃ kārāpetvā cāvanādhippāyo vadeti, āpatti saṅghādisesena dukkaṭassa; okāsaṃ kārāpetvā akkosādhippāyo vadeti, āpatti omasavādassa.

A bhikkhu who groundlessly accuses another bhikkhu of a pārājika offense incurs three offenses. If, having created an improper occasion, he speaks with the intention of expulsion, it is an offense of dukkaṭa along with an offense of saṅghādisesa; if, having created a proper occasion, he speaks with the intention of reviling, it is an offense of omasavāda.

Bhikkhuṃ aññabhāgiyassa adhikaraṇassa kiñci desaṃ lesamattaṃ upādāya pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṃsento tisso āpattiyo āpajjati[T 0.0084]. Anokāsaṃ kārāpetvā cāvanādhippāyo vadeti, āpatti saṅghādisesena dukkaṭassa; okāsaṃ kārāpetvā akkosādhippāyo vadeti, āpatti omasavādassa.

A bhikkhu who, taking up a mere pretext concerning some point of a different matter, accuses another bhikkhu of a pārājika offense incurs three offenses. If, having created an improper occasion, he speaks with the intention of expulsion, it is an offense of dukkaṭa along with an offense of saṅghādisesa; if, having created a proper occasion, he speaks with the intention of reviling, it is an offense of omasavāda.

Saṅghabhedako bhikkhu yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanto tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

A schismatic bhikkhu who does not relinquish his view when admonished for the third time incurs three offenses. With the motion, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; with the two formal announcements, there are offenses of thullaccaya; at the conclusion of the formal announcements, there is an offense of saṅghādisesa.

Bhedakānuvattakā [P 5.0035] bhikkhū yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya samanubhāsiyamānā (syā.) na paṭinissajjantā tisso āpattiyo āpajjanti. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; dvīhi kammavācāhi [M 0.0058] thullaccayā; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

Bhikkhus who are followers of a schismatic and do not relinquish their view when admonished for the third time incur three offenses. With the motion, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; with the two formal announcements, there are offenses of thullaccaya; at the conclusion of the formal announcements, there is an offense of saṅghādisesa.

Dubbaco bhikkhu yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya samanubhāsiyamāno (syā.) na paṭinissajjanto tisso āpattiyo āpajjati[V 0.0059]. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

A bhikkhu who is difficult to admonish and does not relinquish his view when admonished for the third time incurs three offenses. With the motion, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; with the two formal announcements, there are offenses of thullaccaya; at the conclusion of the formal announcements, there is an offense of saṅghādisesa.

Kuladūsako bhikkhu yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanto tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

A bhikkhu who is a corrupter of families, not relinquishing his view when admonished up to the third time, incurs three offenses. With the motion (ñatti), there is an offense of dukkaṭa; with the two formal acts (kammavācā), there are offenses of thullaccaya; at the conclusion of the formal act, there is an offense of saṅghādisesa.

Terasa saṅghādisesā niṭṭhitā.

The thirteen saṅghādisesa offenses are concluded.

3. Nissaggiyakaṇḍaṃ

3. The Nissaggiya Section

1. Kathinavaggo

1. The Chapter on the Kathina

162. Atirekacīvaraṃ [T 0.0085] dasāhaṃ atikkāmento ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

162. A monk who allows an extra robe to be kept for more than ten days incurs one offense: a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Ekarattaṃ ticīvarena vippavasanto ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who dwells apart from the three robes for one night incurs one offense: a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Akālacīvaraṃ paṭiggahetvā māsaṃ atikkāmento ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who, having received an out-of-season robe, allows a month to pass, incurs one offense: a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā purāṇacīvaraṃ dhovāpento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Dhovāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; dhovāpite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who has an old robe washed by an unrelated bhikkhunī incurs two offenses. In the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been washed, there is a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā hatthato cīvaraṃ paṭiggaṇhanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Gaṇhāti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; gahite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who receives a robe from the hand of an unrelated bhikkhunī incurs two offenses. In the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been received, there is a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Aññātakaṃ [V 0.0060] gahapatiṃ vā gahapatāniṃ vā cīvaraṃ viññāpento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Viññāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; viññāpite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who asks an unrelated male householder or female householder for a robe incurs two offenses. In the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been asked for, there is a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Aññātakaṃ [M 0.0059] gahapatiṃ vā gahapatāniṃ vā tatuttari cīvaraṃ viññāpento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Viññāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; viññāpite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who asks an unrelated male householder or female householder for a further robe incurs two offenses. In the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been asked for, there is a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Pubbe appavārito aññātakaṃ gahapatikaṃ upasaṅkamitvā cīvare vikappaṃ āpajjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vikappaṃ āpajjati[T 0.0086], payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vikappaṃ āpanne nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who, not having been previously invited, approaches an unrelated male householder and makes a specification regarding a robe, incurs two offenses. In the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when the specification has been made, there is a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Pubbe appavārito aññātake gahapatike upasaṅkamitvā cīvare vikappaṃ āpajjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vikappaṃ āpajjati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vikappaṃ āpanne nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who, not having been previously invited, approaches unrelated male householders and makes a specification regarding a robe, incurs two offenses. In the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when the specification has been made, there is a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Atirekatikkhattuṃ codanāya atirekachakkhattuṃ ṭhānena cīvaraṃ abhinipphādento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Abhinipphādeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; abhinipphādite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who has a robe completed by prompting more than three times and by standing more than six times incurs two offenses. In the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been completed, there is a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Kathinavaggo paṭhamo.

The first chapter, the Kathinavagga, is concluded.

2. Kosiyavaggo

2. The Chapter on Silk

163. Kosiyamissakaṃ santhataṃ kārāpento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Kārāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; kārāpite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

163. A monk who has a felt rug mixed with silk made incurs two offenses. In the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been made, there is a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Suddhakāḷakānaṃ eḷakalomānaṃ santhataṃ kārāpento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Kārāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; kārāpite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who has a felt rug made of pure black sheep's wool incurs two offenses. In the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been made, there is a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Anādiyitvā [P 5.0036] tulaṃ odātānaṃ tulaṃ gocariyānaṃ navaṃ santhataṃ kārāpento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Kārāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; kārāpite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who has a new felt rug made without including one part of white wool and one part of tawny wool incurs two offenses. In the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been made, there is a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Anuvassaṃ santhataṃ kārāpento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Kārāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; kārāpite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who has a felt rug made every year incurs two offenses. In the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been made, there is a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Anādiyitvā [T 0.0087][V 0.0061] purāṇasanthatassa sāmantā sugatavidatthiṃ navaṃ nisīdanasanthataṃ kārāpento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Kārāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; kārāpite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who has a new sitting-rug made without taking a Sugata-span from the border of an old felt rug incurs two offenses. In the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been made, there is a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Eḷakalomāni [M 0.0060] paṭiggahetvā tiyojanaṃ atikkāmento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paṭhamaṃ pādaṃ tiyojanaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; dutiyaṃ pādaṃ atikkāmeti, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who, having received sheep's wool, travels beyond three yojanas, incurs two offenses. When the first footstep crosses the three-yojana boundary, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when the second footstep crosses, there is a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā eḷakalomāni dhovāpento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Dhovāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; dhovāpite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who has sheep's wool washed by an unrelated bhikkhunī incurs two offenses. In the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been washed, there is a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Rūpiyaṃ paṭiggaṇhanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Gaṇhāti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; gahite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who accepts gold and silver incurs two offenses. In the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been accepted, there is a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Nānappakārakaṃ rūpiyasaṃvohāraṃ samāpajjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Samāpajjati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; samāpanne nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who engages in various kinds of exchange involving gold and silver incurs two offenses. In the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when he has engaged in it, there is a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Nānappakārakaṃ kayavikkayaṃ samāpajjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Samāpajjati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; samāpanne nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who engages in various kinds of buying and selling incurs two offenses. In the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when he has engaged in it, there is a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Kosiyavaggo dutiyo.

The second chapter, the Kosiyavagga, is concluded.

3. Pattavaggo

3. The Chapter on the Bowl

164. Atirekapattaṃ dasāhaṃ atikkāmento ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

164. A monk who allows an extra bowl—one that has not been determined or shared—to exceed ten days, incurs one offense: a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Ūnapañcabandhanena [T 0.0088] pattena aññaṃ navaṃ pattaṃ cetāpento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Cetāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; cetāpite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who, while having a bowl with fewer than five bindings, asks for another new bowl, incurs two offenses. In the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been obtained, there is a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Bhesajjāni paṭiggahetvā sattāhaṃ atikkāmento ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who, having received medicines, allows seven days to pass, incurs one offense: a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Atirekamāse [V 0.0062] sese gimhāne vassikasāṭikacīvaraṃ pariyesanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Pariyesati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; pariyiṭṭhe nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who seeks a rains-bathing cloth when more than a month of the hot season remains incurs two offenses. In the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been obtained, there is a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Bhikkhussa sāmaṃ cīvaraṃ datvā kupito anattamano acchindanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Acchindati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; acchinne nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who, having himself given a robe to another monk, then, being angry and displeased, snatches it back, incurs two offenses. In the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been snatched back, there is a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Sāmaṃ [M 0.0061] suttaṃ viññāpetvā tantavāyehi cīvaraṃ vāyāpento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vāyāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vāyāpite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who, having himself asked for thread, has a robe woven by weavers, incurs two offenses. In the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been woven, there is a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Pubbe appavārito aññātakassa gahapatikassa tantavāye upasaṅkamitvā cīvare vikappaṃ āpajjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vikappaṃ āpajjati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vikappaṃ āpanne nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A monk who, not having been previously invited, approaches the weavers of an unrelated householder and makes a specification concerning a robe, incurs two offenses. In the effort, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when the specification has been made, there is a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Accekacīvaraṃ [P 5.0037] paṭiggahetvā cīvarakālasamayaṃ atikkāmento ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhu who, having accepted an urgent robe, allows the robe season to pass, falls into one offense: a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Tiṇṇaṃ [T 0.0089] cīvarānaṃ aññataraṃ cīvaraṃ antaraghare nikkhipitvā atirekachārattaṃ vippavasanto ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhu who, having placed one of the three robes in an inhabited area, dwells apart from it for more than six nights, falls into one offense: a pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Jānaṃ saṅghikaṃ lābhaṃ pariṇataṃ attano pariṇāmento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Pariṇāmeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; pariṇāmite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhu who knowingly diverts to himself a gain belonging to the Sangha that had been dedicated to it, falls into two offenses. If he diverts it, there is an offense of dukkaṭa in the effort; when it has been diverted, he falls into an offense of pācittiya that entails forfeiture.

Pattavaggo tatiyo.

The Third Chapter on the Bowl is finished.

Tiṃsa nissaggiyā pācittiyā niṭṭhitā.

The thirty pācittiyas that entail forfeiture are finished.

4. Pācittiyakaṇḍaṃ

4. The Section on Pācittiya Offenses

1. Musāvādavaggo

1. The Chapter on False Speech

165. Sampajānamusāvādaṃ bhāsanto kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Sampajānamusāvādaṃ bhāsanto pañca āpattiyo āpajjati. Pāpiccho icchāpakato asantaṃ abhūtaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ [V 0.0063] ullapati, āpatti pārājikassa; bhikkhuṃ amūlakena pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṃseti, āpatti saṅghādisesassa; “yo te vihāre vasati, so bhikkhu arahā”ti bhaṇati, paṭivijānantassa āpatti thullaccayassa; na paṭivijānantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa; sampajānamusāvāde pācittiyaṃ – sampajānamusāvādaṃ bhāsanto imā pañca āpattiyo āpajjati.

165. How many offenses does a bhikkhu who speaks a deliberate falsehood fall into? A bhikkhu who speaks a deliberate falsehood falls into five offenses. If, having evil wishes and being overcome by desire, he boasts of a non-existent, untrue state superior to human states, it is an offense of pārājika. If he accuses a bhikkhu of a groundless pārājika offense, it is an offense of saṅghādisesa. If he says, ‘The bhikkhu who lives in your monastery is an arahant,’ it is an offense of thullaccaya for one who understands, and an offense of dukkaṭa for one who does not understand. For a deliberate falsehood, there is an offense of pācittiya. Thus, a bhikkhu who speaks a deliberate falsehood falls into these five offenses.

Omasanto [M 0.0062] dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Upasampannaṃ omasati, āpatti pācittiyassa; anupasampannaṃ omasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

A bhikkhu who scorns others falls into two offenses. If he scorns one who is fully ordained, it is an offense of pācittiya; if he scorns one who is not fully ordained, it is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Pesuññaṃ upasaṃharanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Upasampannassa [T 0.0090] pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati, āpatti pācittiyassa; anupasampannassa pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

A bhikkhu who engages in slander falls into two offenses. If he directs slander towards one who is fully ordained, it is an offense of pācittiya; if he directs slander towards one who is not fully ordained, it is an offense of dukkaṭa.

Anupasampannaṃ padaso dhammaṃ vācento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vāceti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; pade pade āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who teaches the Dhamma word-for-word to one who is not fully ordained falls into two offenses. If he teaches, there is an offense of dukkaṭa in the effort; for each and every word, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Anupasampannena uttaridirattatirattaṃ sahaseyyaṃ kappento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Nipajjati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; nipanne āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who arranges to sleep in the same lodging with one who is not fully ordained for more than two or three nights falls into two offenses. If he lies down, there is an offense of dukkaṭa in the effort; when he has lain down, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Mātugāmena sahaseyyaṃ kappento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Nipajjati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; nipanne āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who arranges to sleep in the same lodging with a woman falls into two offenses. If he lies down, there is an offense of dukkaṭa in the effort; when he has lain down, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Mātugāmassa uttarichappañcavācāhi dhammaṃ desento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Deseti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; pade pade āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who teaches the Dhamma to a woman with more than five or six words falls into two offenses. If he teaches, there is an offense of dukkaṭa in the effort; for each and every word, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Anupasampannassa uttarimanussadhammaṃ bhūtaṃ ārocento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Āroceti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; ārocite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who announces a true state superior to human states to one who is not fully ordained falls into two offenses. If he announces it, there is an offense of dukkaṭa in the effort; when it has been announced, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Bhikkhussa duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ anupasampannassa ārocento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Āroceti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; ārocite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who announces a bhikkhu’s gross offense to one who is not fully ordained falls into two offenses. If he announces it, there is an offense of dukkaṭa in the effort; when it has been announced, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Pathaviṃ [T 0.0091][V 0.0064] khaṇanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Khaṇati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; pahāre pahāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who digs the earth falls into two offenses. If he digs, there is an offense of dukkaṭa in the effort; for each and every strike, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Musāvādavaggo paṭhamo.

The First Chapter on False Speech is finished.

2. Bhūtagāmavaggo

2. The Chapter on Plant Life

166. Bhūtagāmaṃ [P 5.0038] pātento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Pāteti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; pahāre pahāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

166. One who destroys plant life falls into two offenses. If he destroys it, there is an offense of dukkaṭa in the effort; for each and every blow, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Aññenaññaṃ [M 0.0063] paṭicaranto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Anāropite aññavādake aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati, āpatti dukkaṭassa; āropite aññavādake aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

One who speaks evasively falls into two offenses. Before the formal act concerning evasiveness has been imposed, if he speaks evasively, it is an offense of dukkaṭa; after the formal act concerning evasiveness has been imposed, if he speaks evasively, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Bhikkhuṃ ujjhāpento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Ujjhāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; ujjhāpite āpatti pācittiyassa.

One who disparages a bhikkhu falls into two offenses. If he disparages, there is an offense of dukkaṭa in the effort; when he has disparaged, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Saṅghikaṃ mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā bhisiṃ vā kocchaṃ vā ajjhokāse santharitvā anuddharitvā anāpucchā pakkamanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paṭhamaṃ pādaṃ leḍḍupātaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; dutiyaṃ pādaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

One who spreads out a bed, a chair, a mattress, or a cushion belonging to the Sangha in the open air and departs without putting it away or taking leave falls into two offenses. When he takes the first step beyond a stone's throw, it is an offense of dukkaṭa; when he takes the second step beyond, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Saṅghike vihāre seyyaṃ santharitvā anuddharitvā anāpucchā pakkamanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paṭhamaṃ pādaṃ parikkhepaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; dutiyaṃ pādaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

One who spreads out bedding in a dwelling belonging to the Sangha and departs without putting it away or taking leave falls into two offenses. When he takes the first step beyond the boundary, it is an offense of dukkaṭa; when he takes the second step beyond, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Saṅghike vihāre jānaṃ pubbupagataṃ bhikkhuṃ anupakhajja seyyaṃ [T 0.0092] kappento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Nipajjati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; nipanne āpatti pācittiyassa.

One who, knowing that a bhikkhu has arrived earlier, prepares a sleeping place by encroaching upon him in a dwelling belonging to the Sangha, falls into two offenses. If he lies down, there is an offense of dukkaṭa in the effort; when he has lain down, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Bhikkhuṃ kupito anattamano saṅghikā vihārā nikkaḍḍhento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Nikkaḍḍhati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; nikkaḍḍhite āpatti pācittiyassa.

One who, being angry and displeased, forcibly removes a bhikkhu from a dwelling belonging to the Sangha falls into two offenses. If he forcibly removes him, there is an offense of dukkaṭa in the effort; when he has been forcibly removed, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Saṅghike [V 0.0065] vihāre uparivehāsakuṭiyā āhaccapādakaṃ mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā abhinisīdanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Abhinisīdati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; abhinisinne āpatti pācittiyassa.

One who sits down heavily on a bed or a chair with removable legs in an upper-story room of a dwelling belonging to the Sangha falls into two offenses. If he sits down heavily, there is an offense of dukkaṭa in the effort; when he has sat down heavily, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Dvattipariyāye adhiṭṭhahitvā tatuttari adhiṭṭhahanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Adhiṭṭheti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; adhiṭṭhite āpatti pācittiyassa.

One who, having supervised the roofing of a dwelling with two or three layers, supervises beyond that, falls into two offenses. If he supervises, there is an offense of dukkaṭa in the effort; when it has been supervised, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Jānaṃ sappāṇakaṃ udakaṃ tiṇaṃ vā mattikaṃ vā siñcanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Siñcati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; siñcite āpatti pācittiyassa.

One who, knowing that water contains living beings, waters grass or clay falls into two offenses. If he waters, there is an offense of dukkaṭa in the effort; when he has watered, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Bhūtagāmavaggo dutiyo.

The Second Chapter on Plant Life is finished.

3. Ovādavaggo

3. The Chapter on Admonition

167. Asammato [M 0.0064] bhikkhuniyo ovadanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Ovadati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; ovadite āpatti pācittiyassa.

167. One who, not being authorized, admonishes nuns falls into two offenses. If he admonishes, there is an offense of dukkaṭa in the effort; when he has admonished, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Atthaṅgate sūriye bhikkhuniyo ovadanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Ovadati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; ovadite āpatti pācittiyassa.

One who admonishes nuns after the sun has set falls into two offenses. If he admonishes, there is an offense of dukkaṭa in the effort; when he has admonished, it is an offense of pācittiya.

Bhikkhunupassayaṃ [T 0.0093] upasaṅkamitvā bhikkhuniyo ovadanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Ovadati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; ovadite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who, having approached a nunnery, admonishes the bhikkhunīs, incurs two offenses. In the effort to admonish, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when the admonition is completed, there is an offense requiring expiation.

“Āmisahetu bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo ovadantī”ti bhaṇanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhaṇati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; bhaṇite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who says, 'Bhikkhus admonish bhikkhunīs for the sake of material gain,' incurs two offenses. In the effort of speaking, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when it has been said, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ dento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Deti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; dinne āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who gives a robe to a bhikkhunī who is not a relative incurs two offenses. In the effort of giving, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when it has been given, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Aññātikā [P 5.0039] bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ sibbento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Sibbeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; ārāpathe ārāpathe āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who sews a robe for a bhikkhunī who is not a relative incurs two offenses. In the effort of sewing, there is an offense of wrong-doing; for each stitch, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Bhikkhuniyā [V 0.0066] saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paṭipajjati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; paṭipanne āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who, having made an arrangement with a bhikkhunī, travels along the same long road, incurs two offenses. In the effort of traveling, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when the journey has been undertaken, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaṃ nāvaṃ abhiruhanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Abhiruhati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; abhiruḷhe āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who, having made an arrangement with a bhikkhunī, boards the same boat, incurs two offenses. In the effort of boarding, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when he has boarded, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Jānaṃ bhikkhuniparipācitaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuñjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. “Bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who knowingly eats almsfood arranged by a bhikkhunī incurs two offenses. When he accepts it thinking, 'I will eat,' there is an offense of wrong-doing; for each mouthful, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Bhikkhuniyā [T 0.0094] saddhiṃ eko ekāya raho nisajjaṃ kappento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Nisīdati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; nisinne āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who arranges to sit down alone with a bhikkhunī in a secluded place incurs two offenses. In the effort of sitting, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when he is seated, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Ovādavaggo tatiyo.

The Chapter on Admonition, the third.

4. Bhojanavaggo

4. The Chapter on Food

168. Tatuttari [M 0.0065] āvasathapiṇḍaṃ bhuñjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

168. A bhikkhu who eats almsfood from a public rest-house on a subsequent occasion incurs two offenses. If he accepts it with the thought, 'I will eat,' there is an offense of wrong-doing; for every mouthful, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Gaṇabhojanaṃ bhuñjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who eats a group meal incurs two offenses. If he accepts it with the thought, 'I will eat,' there is an offense of wrong-doing; for every mouthful, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Paramparabhojanaṃ bhuñjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who eats a successive meal incurs two offenses. If he accepts it with the thought, 'I will eat,' there is an offense of wrong-doing; for every mouthful, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Dvattipattapūre pūve paṭiggahetvā tatuttari paṭiggaṇhanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Gaṇhāti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; gahite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who, having accepted two or three bowlfuls of cakes, accepts more than that, incurs two offenses. In the effort of accepting, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when it has been accepted, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Bhuttāvī pavārito anatirittaṃ khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā bhuñjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati[V 0.0067]. Bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who, having eaten and indicated he is satisfied, eats hard or soft food that has not been designated as a leftover, incurs two offenses. If he accepts it with the thought, 'I will eat,' there is an offense of wrong-doing; for every mouthful, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Bhikkhuṃ bhuttāviṃ pavāritaṃ anatirittena khādanīyena vā bhojanīyena [T 0.0095] vā abhihaṭṭhuṃ pavārento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Tassa vacanena khādissāmi bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; bhojanapariyosāne āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who invites another bhikkhu—who has already eaten and indicated he is satisfied—to eat hard or soft food that has not been designated as a leftover, incurs two offenses. If the other bhikkhu accepts it at his word, thinking, 'I will eat' or 'I will consume,' there is an offense of wrong-doing; at the conclusion of the eating, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Vikāle khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā bhuñjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Khādissāmi bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who eats hard or soft food at the wrong time incurs two offenses. If he accepts it with the thought, 'I will eat' or 'I will consume,' there is an offense of wrong-doing; for every mouthful, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Sannidhikārakaṃ khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā bhuñjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Khādissāmi bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who eats stored hard or soft food incurs two offenses. If he accepts it with the thought, 'I will eat' or 'I will consume,' there is an offense of wrong-doing; for every mouthful, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Paṇītabhojanāni attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who, having requested excellent foods for his own benefit, eats them, incurs two offenses. When he accepts it with the thought, 'I will eat,' there is an offense of wrong-doing; for every mouthful, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Adinnaṃ [M 0.0066] mukhadvāraṃ āhāraṃ āharanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who brings unoffered food to the entrance of his mouth incurs two offenses. When he accepts it with the thought, 'I will eat,' there is an offense of wrong-doing; for every mouthful, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Bhojanavaggo catuttho.

The Chapter on Food, the fourth.

5. Acelakavaggo

5. The Chapter on the Naked Ascetic.

169. Acelakassa, vā paribbājakassa vā paribbājikāya vā sahatthā khādanīyaṃ [P 5.0040] vā bhojanīyaṃ vā dento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Deti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; dinne āpatti pācittiyassa.

169. A bhikkhu who gives hard or soft food with his own hand to a naked ascetic, a male wanderer, or a female wanderer, incurs two offenses. In the effort of giving, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when it has been given, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Bhikkhuṃ – “ehāvuso, gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā piṇḍāya pavisissāmā”ti [T 0.0096] tassa dāpetvā vā [V 0.0068] adāpetvā vā uyyojento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Uyyojeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; uyyojite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who, after saying to another bhikkhu, 'Come, friend, let us enter a village or a town for alms,' dismisses him—whether having caused something to be given to him or not—incurs two offenses. In the effort of dismissing, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when he has been dismissed, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Sabhojane kule anupakhajja nisajjaṃ kappento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Nisīdati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; nisinne āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who intrudes and arranges to sit down in a household where a couple is present incurs two offenses. In the effort of sitting down, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when he has sat down, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Mātugāmena saddhiṃ raho paṭicchanne āsane nisajjaṃ kappento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Nisīdati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; nisinne āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who arranges to sit down together with a woman on a secluded and concealed seat incurs two offenses. In the effort of sitting down, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when he has sat down, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Mātugāmena saddhiṃ eko ekāya raho nisajjaṃ kappento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Nisīdati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; nisinne āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who arranges to sit down alone with a woman in a secluded place incurs two offenses. In the effort of sitting down, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when he has sat down, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Nimantito sabhatto samāno purebhattaṃ pacchābhattaṃ kulesu cārittaṃ āpajjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paṭhamaṃ pādaṃ ummāraṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; dutiyaṃ pādaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who, being invited and having a meal engagement, wanders among families either before or after the meal, incurs two offenses. When he makes the first footstep cross the threshold, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when he makes the second footstep cross it, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Tatuttari bhesajjaṃ viññāpento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Viññāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; viññāpite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who requests medicine beyond that invitation period incurs two offenses. In the effort of requesting, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when it has been requested, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Uyyuttaṃ [M 0.0067] senaṃ dassanāya gacchanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati[T 0.0097]. Gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa; yattha ṭhito passati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who goes to see a deployed army incurs two offenses. In the act of going, there is an offense of wrong-doing; at the place where he stands and sees it, there is an offense requiring expiation.

Atirekatirattaṃ senāya vasanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vasati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vasite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who stays with an army for more than three nights incurs two offenses. In the effort to stay, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when he has stayed, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Uyyodhikaṃ gacchanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa; yattha ṭhito passati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who goes to a battlefield incurs two offenses. When he goes, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; where he stands and sees, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Acelakavaggo pañcamo.

The Fifth Chapter on the Naked Ascetic is concluded.

6. Surāmerayavaggo

6. The Sixth Chapter: On Intoxicating Drink

170. Majjaṃ [V 0.0069] pivanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. “Pivissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

170. A bhikkhu who drinks an intoxicant incurs two offenses. When he accepts it with the thought, 'I will drink,' there is an offense of dukkaṭa; for every swallow, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Bhikkhuṃ aṅgulipatodakena hāsento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Hāseti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; hasite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who makes another bhikkhu laugh by poking with a finger incurs two offenses. In the effort to make him laugh, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when he has been made to laugh, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Udake kīḷanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Heṭṭhāgopphake udake kīḷati, āpatti dukkaṭassa; uparigopphake kīḷati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who plays in the water incurs two offenses. If he plays in water below the ankles, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; if he plays in water above the ankles, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Anādariyaṃ karonto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Karoti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; kate āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who acts with disrespect incurs two offenses. In the effort to do so, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been done, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Bhikkhuṃ bhiṃsāpento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhiṃsāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; bhiṃsāpite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who frightens another bhikkhu incurs two offenses. In the effort to frighten, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when he has been frightened, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Jotiṃ samādahitvā visibbento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Samādahati[T 0.0098], payoge dukkaṭaṃ; samādahite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who, having kindled a fire, warms himself incurs two offenses. In the effort to kindle it, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been kindled, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Orenaddhamāsaṃ nahāyanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Nahāyati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; nahānapariyosāne āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who bathes within half a month incurs two offenses. In the effort to bathe, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; at the conclusion of bathing, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Anādiyitvā [P 5.0041] tiṇṇaṃ dubbaṇṇakaraṇānaṃ aññataraṃ dubbaṇṇakaraṇaṃ navaṃ cīvaraṃ paribhuñjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paribhuñjati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; paribhutte āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who uses a new robe without applying one of the three means of discoloration incurs two offenses. In the effort to use it, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been used, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Bhikkhussa [M 0.0068] vā bhikkhuniyā vā sikkhamānāya vā sāmaṇerassa vā sāmaṇeriyā vā sāmaṃ cīvaraṃ vikappetvā appaccuddhāraṇaṃ paribhuñjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paribhuñjati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; paribhutte āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who, having made his own robe shared property with a bhikkhu, a bhikkhunī, a female probationer, a male novice, or a female novice, then uses that robe without it having been returned, incurs two offenses. In the effort to use it, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been used, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Bhikkhussa [V 0.0070] pattaṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā nisīdanaṃ vā sūcigharaṃ vā kāyabandhanaṃ vā apanidhento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Apanidheti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; apanidhite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who hides another bhikkhu's bowl, robe, sitting cloth, needle case, or belt incurs two offenses. In the effort to hide it, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been hidden, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Surāmerayavaggo chaṭṭho.

The Sixth Chapter, on Intoxicating Drink, is concluded.

7. Sappāṇakavaggo

7. The Seventh Chapter: On Living Beings

171. Sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropento kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropento catasso āpattiyo āpajjati. Anodissa opātaṃ khaṇati – “yo koci papatitvā marissatī”ti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; manusso tasmiṃ papatitvā marati, āpatti pārājikassa; yakkho vā peto vā tiracchānagatamanussaviggaho vā tasmiṃ [T 0.0099] papatitvā marati, āpatti thullaccayassa; tiracchānagato tasmiṃ papatitvā marati, āpatti pācittiyassa – sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropento imā catasso āpattiyo āpajjati.

171. How many offenses does a bhikkhu who intentionally deprives a living being of life incur? A bhikkhu who intentionally deprives a living being of life incurs four offenses. If he digs a pitfall without specifying anyone, thinking, “Whoever falls into it will die,” there is an offense of dukkaṭa. If a human being falls into it and dies, there is an offense of pārājika. If a yakkha, a peta, or an animal in human form falls into it and dies, there is an offense of thullaccaya. If an animal falls into it and dies, there is an offense of pācittiya. Thus, a bhikkhu who intentionally deprives a living being of life incurs these four offenses.

Jānaṃ sappāṇakaṃ udakaṃ paribhuñjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paribhuñjati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; paribhutte āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who knowingly uses water containing living beings incurs two offenses. In the effort to use it, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been used, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Jānaṃ yathādhammaṃ nihatādhikaraṇaṃ punakammāya ukkoṭento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Ukkoṭeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; ukkoṭite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who, knowing, reopens for a formal act a legal issue that has been settled in accordance with the Dhamma incurs two offenses. In the effort to reopen it, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when it has been reopened, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Bhikkhussa jānaṃ duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ paṭicchādento ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhu who knowingly conceals another bhikkhu’s grave offense incurs one offense: an offense of pācittiya.

Jānaṃ ūnavīsativassaṃ puggalaṃ upasampādento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Upasampādeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; upasampādite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who knowingly gives the higher ordination to a person under twenty years of age incurs two offenses. In the effort to give the higher ordination, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when the person has been given the higher ordination, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Jānaṃ [M 0.0069] theyyasatthena saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paṭipajjati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; paṭipanne āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who, knowing, having made an arrangement with a caravan of thieves, travels along the same long road incurs two offenses. In the effort to travel, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when he has traveled, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Mātugāmena saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paṭipajjati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; paṭipanne āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who, having made an arrangement with a woman, travels along the same long road incurs two offenses. In the effort to travel, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when he has traveled, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Pāpikāya [V 0.0071] diṭṭhiyā yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanto [T 0.0100] dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who does not relinquish a wrong view when being admonished up to the third time by a motion and formal act incurs two offenses. For the motion, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; at the conclusion of the formal act, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Jānaṃ tathāvādinā bhikkhunā akaṭānudhammena taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissaṭṭhena saddhiṃ sambhuñjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Sambhuñjati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; sambhutte āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who knowingly associates with a bhikkhu who speaks thus, for whom the act of rehabilitation has not been done, and who has not relinquished that view, incurs two offenses. In the effort to associate, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when he has associated, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Jānaṃ [P 5.0042] tathānāsitaṃ samaṇuddesaṃ upalāpento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Upalāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; upalāpite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who, knowing, entices a novice who has been expelled in such a way incurs two offenses. In the effort to entice him, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when he has been enticed, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Sappāṇakavaggo sattamo.

The Seventh Chapter, on Living Beings, is concluded.

8. Sahadhammikavaggo

8. The Eighth Chapter: On Matters in Accordance with the Dhamma

172. Bhikkhūhi sahadhammikaṃ vuccamāno – “na tāvāhaṃ, āvuso, etasmiṃ sikkhāpade sikkhissāmi yāva na aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ byattaṃ vinayadharaṃ paripucchissāmī”ti bhaṇanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhaṇati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; bhaṇite āpatti pācittiyassa.

172. A bhikkhu who, when being spoken to by other bhikkhus in accordance with the training rule, says, 'Venerables, I will not train in this training rule until I have asked another bhikkhu who is competent and a Vinaya-holder,' incurs two offenses. In the effort to speak, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when he has spoken, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Vinayaṃ vivaṇṇento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vivaṇṇeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vivaṇṇite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who disparages the Vinaya incurs two offenses. In the effort to disparage it, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when he has disparaged it, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Mohento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Anāropite mohe moheti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; āropite mohe moheti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhu who feigns ignorance incurs two offenses. If he feigns ignorance before the formal act of charging with bewilderment has been imposed, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; if he feigns ignorance after it has been imposed, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Bhikkhussa [M 0.0070] kupito anattamano pahāraṃ dento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paharati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; pahate āpatti pācittiyassa[T 0.0101].

A bhikkhu who, being angry and displeased, strikes another bhikkhu incurs two offenses. In the effort to strike, there is an offense of dukkaṭa; when he has been struck, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Bhikkhussa kupito anattamano talasattikaṃ uggiranto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Uggirati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; uggirite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A monk who, being angry and displeased with another monk, raises the palm of his hand, incurs two offenses. In the effort to raise it, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when it has been raised, there is an offense entailing confession.

Bhikkhuṃ [V 0.0072] amūlakena saṅghādisesena anuddhaṃsento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Anuddhaṃseti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; anuddhaṃsite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A monk who groundlessly accuses another monk of a saṅghādisesa offense incurs two offenses. In the effort to accuse, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when he has accused him, there is an offense entailing confession.

Bhikkhussa sañcicca kukkuccaṃ upadahanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Upadahati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; upadahite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A monk who intentionally causes remorse for another monk incurs two offenses. In the effort to cause it, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when he has caused it, there is an offense entailing confession.

Bhikkhūnaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ upassutiṃ tiṭṭhanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. “Sossāmī”ti gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa; yattha ṭhito suṇāti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A monk who stands eavesdropping on monks who have become quarrelsome, contentious, and have fallen into dispute incurs two offenses. If he goes with the thought, ‘I will listen,’ there is an offense of wrong-doing; where he stands and listens, there is an offense entailing confession.

Dhammikānaṃ kammānaṃ chandaṃ datvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṃ āpajjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Khiyyati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; khiyyite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A monk who, having given his consent for lawful formal acts, afterwards falls into a state of criticism, incurs two offenses. In the effort to criticize, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when he has criticized, there is an offense entailing confession.

Saṅghe vinicchayakathāya vattamānāya chandaṃ adatvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Parisāya hatthapāsaṃ vijahantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa; vijahite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A monk who, while a discussion for a decision is in progress in the Sangha, rises from his seat and departs without giving his consent, incurs two offenses. As he is leaving the hand's reach of the assembly, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when he has left it, there is an offense entailing confession.

Samaggena [T 0.0102] saṅghena cīvaraṃ datvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṃ āpajjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Khiyyati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; khiyyite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A monk who, having given a robe together with a united Sangha, afterwards falls into a state of criticism, incurs two offenses. In the effort to criticize, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when he has criticized, there is an offense entailing confession.

Jānaṃ saṅghikaṃ lābhaṃ pariṇataṃ puggalassa pariṇāmento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Pariṇāmeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; pariṇāmite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A monk who knowingly diverts to an individual a gain belonging to the Sangha that has been designated for it, incurs two offenses. In the effort to divert it, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when he has diverted it, there is an offense entailing confession.

Sahadhammikavaggo aṭṭhamo.

The Eighth Chapter on Companions in the Dhamma.

9. Rājavaggo

9. The Chapter on Kings

173. Pubbe [M 0.0071] appaṭisaṃvidito rañño antepuraṃ pavisanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paṭhamaṃ pādaṃ ummāraṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; dutiyaṃ pādaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

173. A monk who enters the king's inner palace without prior announcement incurs two offenses. When he crosses the threshold with the first foot, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when he crosses with the second foot, there is an offense entailing confession.

Ratanaṃ [P 5.0043][V 0.0073] uggaṇhanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Gaṇhāti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; gahite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A monk who picks up a jewel incurs two offenses. In the effort to pick it up, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when it has been picked up, there is an offense entailing confession.

Santaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpucchā vikāle gāmaṃ pavisanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paṭhamaṃ pādaṃ parikkhepaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; dutiyaṃ pādaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A monk who enters a village at an improper time without asking leave of a resident monk incurs two offenses. When he crosses the boundary with his first foot, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when he crosses with his second foot, there is an offense entailing confession.

Aṭṭhimayaṃ vā dantamayaṃ vā visāṇamayaṃ vā sūcigharaṃ kārāpento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Kārāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; kārāpite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A monk who has a needle case made of bone, ivory, or horn, incurs two offenses. In the effort to have it made, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when it has been made, there is an offense entailing confession.

Pamāṇātikkantaṃ mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā kārāpento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Kārāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; kārāpite [T 0.0103] āpatti pācittiyassa.

A monk who has a bed or a bench made that exceeds the standard measurement incurs two offenses. In the effort to have it made, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when it has been made, there is an offense entailing confession.

Mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā tūlonaddhaṃ kārāpento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Kārāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; kārāpite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A monk who has a bed or a bench stuffed with cotton made incurs two offenses. In the effort to have it made, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when it has been made, there is an offense entailing confession.

Pamāṇātikkantaṃ nisīdanaṃ kārāpento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Kārāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; kārāpite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A monk who has a sitting-cloth made that exceeds the standard measurement incurs two offenses. In the effort to have it made, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when it has been made, there is an offense entailing confession.

Pamāṇātikkantaṃ kaṇḍuppaṭicchādiṃ kārāpento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Kārāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; kārāpite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A monk who has a cloth for covering itches made that exceeds the standard measurement incurs two offenses. In the effort to have it made, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when it has been made, there is an offense entailing confession.

Pamāṇātikkantaṃ vassikasāṭikaṃ kārāpento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Kārāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; kārāpite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A monk who has a rains-cloth made that exceeds the standard measurement incurs two offenses. In the effort to have it made, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when it has been made, there is an offense entailing confession.

Cīvaraṃ kārāpento kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Sugatacīvarappamāṇaṃ cīvaraṃ kārāpento dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Kārāpeti[M 0.0072], payoge dukkaṭaṃ; kārāpite āpatti pācittiyassa – sugatacīvarappamāṇaṃ cīvaraṃ kārāpento imā dve āpattiyo āpajjati.

A monk having a robe made—how many offenses does he incur? A monk who has a robe made to the measurement of the Sugata's robe incurs two offenses. In the effort to have it made, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when it has been made, there is an offense entailing confession. A monk who has a robe made to the measurement of the Sugata's robe incurs these two offenses.

Rājavaggo navamo. Khuddakā niṭṭhitā.

The Ninth, the Chapter on Kings, is finished. The Minor Rules are concluded.

5. Pāṭidesanīyakaṇḍaṃ

5. The Section on Offenses to be Acknowledged

174. Aññātikāya [T 0.0104][V 0.0074] bhikkhuniyā antaragharaṃ paviṭṭhāya hatthato khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā bhuñjanto kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā antaragharaṃ paviṭṭhāya hatthato khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā bhuñjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa – aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā antaragharaṃ paviṭṭhāya hatthato khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā bhuñjanto imā dve āpattiyo āpajjati.

174. When an unrelated bhikkhunī has entered a village, a monk who receives hard food or soft food from her hand with his own hand and eats it—how many offenses does he incur? When an unrelated bhikkhunī has entered a village, a monk who receives hard food or soft food from her hand with his own hand and eats it incurs two offenses. If he receives it with the intention, ‘I will eat,’ there is an offense of wrong-doing; for every mouthful, there is an offense to be acknowledged. A monk who receives hard food or soft food from the hand of an unrelated bhikkhunī who has entered a village and eats it with his own hand incurs these two offenses.

Bhikkhuniyā vosāsantiyā na nivāretvā bhuñjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa.

A monk who eats without having stopped a bhikkhunī who is directing the meal incurs two offenses. If he receives the food with the intention, ‘I will eat,’ there is an offense of wrong-doing; for every mouthful, there is an offense to be acknowledged.

Sekkhasammatesu kulesu khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā bhuñjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa.

A monk who receives hard food or soft food with his own hand in families designated as ‘in training’ and eats it, incurs two offenses. If he receives it with the intention, ‘I will eat,’ there is an offense of wrong-doing; for every mouthful, there is an offense to be acknowledged.

Āraññakesu senāsanesu pubbe appaṭisaṃviditaṃ khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā ajjhārāme sahatthā paṭiggahetvā bhuñjanto kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Āraññakesu senāsanesu pubbe appaṭisaṃviditaṃ khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā ajjhārāme sahatthā paṭiggahetvā [T 0.0105] bhuñjanto dve āpattiyo āpajjati[P 5.0044]. Bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre [M 0.0073] ajjhohāre āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa – āraññakesu senāsanesu pubbe appaṭisaṃviditaṃ khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā ajjhārāme sahatthā paṭiggahetvā bhuñjanto imā dve āpattiyo āpajjati.

In forest lodgings, a monk who receives with his own hand within the monastery grounds and eats hard or soft food, without having been previously informed of its danger—how many offenses does he incur? In forest lodgings, a monk who receives with his own hand within the monastery grounds and eats hard or soft food, without having been previously informed of its danger, incurs two offenses. If he receives it intending, 'I will eat,' he incurs an offense of wrong-doing; for every mouthful, he incurs an offense to be acknowledged. Thus, in forest lodgings, a monk who receives with his own hand within the monastery grounds and eats hard or soft food, without having been previously informed of its danger, incurs these two offenses.

Cattāro pāṭidesanīyā niṭṭhitā.

The four Pāṭidesanīya rules are concluded.

6. Sekhiyakaṇḍaṃ

6. The Section on the Trainings

1. Parimaṇḍalavaggo

1. The Chapter on Proper Attire

175. Anādariyaṃ [V 0.0075] paṭicca purato vā pacchato vā olambento nivāsento kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Anādariyaṃ paṭicca purato vā pacchato vā olambento nivāsento ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ – anādariyaṃ paṭicca purato vā pacchato vā olambento nivāsento imaṃ ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati.

175. How many offenses does a monk incur who, on account of disrespect, wears the lower robe letting it hang down in front or behind? A monk who, on account of disrespect, wears the lower robe letting it hang down in front or behind incurs one offense. A monk who, on account of disrespect, wears the lower robe letting it hang down in front or behind incurs this one offense: an offense of wrong-doing.

…Anādariyaṃ paṭicca purato vā pacchato vā olambento pārupanto ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, a monk who wears the upper robe letting it hang down in front or behind incurs one offense: an offense of wrong-doing.

…Anādariyaṃ paṭicca kāyaṃ vivaritvā antaraghare gacchanto ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, a monk who goes within an inhabited area with his body uncovered incurs one offense: an offense of wrong-doing.

…Anādariyaṃ paṭicca kāyaṃ vivaritvā antaraghare nisīdanto ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, a monk who sits within an inhabited area with his body uncovered incurs one offense: an offense of wrong-doing.

…Anādariyaṃ paṭicca hatthaṃ vā pādaṃ vā kīḷāpento antaraghare gacchanto ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, a monk who goes within an inhabited area playing with his hands or feet incurs one offense: an offense of wrong-doing.

…Anādariyaṃ [T 0.0106] paṭicca hatthaṃ vā pādaṃ vā kīḷāpento antaraghare nisīdanto ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, a monk who sits within an inhabited area playing with his hands or feet incurs one offense: an offense of wrong-doing.

…Anādariyaṃ paṭicca tahaṃ tahaṃ olokento antaraghare gacchanto ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, a monk who goes within an inhabited area looking here and there incurs one offense: an offense of wrong-doing.

…Anādariyaṃ paṭicca tahaṃ tahaṃ olokento antaraghare nisīdanto ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, a monk who sits within an inhabited area looking here and there incurs one offense: an offense of wrong-doing.

…Anādariyaṃ [M 0.0074][V 0.0076] paṭicca ukkhittakāya antaraghare gacchanto ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, a monk who goes within an inhabited area with his robe hitched up incurs one offense: an offense of wrong-doing.

…Anādariyaṃ paṭicca ukkhittakāya antaraghare nisīdanto ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, a monk who sits within an inhabited area with his robe hitched up incurs one offense: an offense of wrong-doing.

Parimaṇḍalavaggo paṭhamo.

The First Chapter on Proper Attire.

176. On account of disrespect, a monk who goes within an inhabited area laughing boisterously incurs one offense: an offense of wrong-doing.

…Anādariyaṃ paṭicca ujjagghikāya antaraghare nisīdanto ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, a monk who sits within an inhabited area laughing boisterously incurs one offense: an offense of wrong-doing.

On account of disrespect, a monk who goes within an inhabited area making a loud noise, a great noise, incurs one offense: an offense of wrong-doing.

…Anādariyaṃ paṭicca uccāsaddaṃ mahāsaddaṃ karonto antaraghare nisīdanto ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

…Anādariyaṃ paṭicca kāyappacālakaṃ antaraghare gacchanto ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, a monk who sits within an inhabited area swaying his body incurs one offense: an offense of wrong-doing.

…Anādariyaṃ paṭicca bāhuppacālakaṃ antaraghare gacchanto ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, a monk who goes within an inhabited area swinging his arms incurs one offense: an offense of wrong-doing.

On account of disrespect, a monk who sits within an inhabited area swinging his arms incurs one offense: an offense of wrong-doing.

On account of disrespect, a monk who goes within an inhabited area swaying his head incurs one offense: an offense of wrong-doing.

…Anādariyaṃ paṭicca sīsappacālakaṃ antaraghare nisīdanto ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, a monk who sits within an inhabited area swaying his head incurs one offense: an offense of wrong-doing.

Ujjagghikavaggo dutiyo.

On account of disrespect, a monk who receives almsfood while looking here and there incurs one offense: an offense of wrong-doing.

On account of disrespect, a monk who receives much curry only incurs one offense: an offense of wrong-doing.

On account of disrespect, a bhikkhu who teaches the Dhamma to a person in a vehicle incurs one offense of dukkaṭa.

…Anādariyaṃ paṭicca sayanagatassa dhammaṃ desento ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, a bhikkhu who teaches the Dhamma to a person who is lying down incurs one offense of dukkaṭa.
