…Anādariyaṃ paṭicca pallatthikāya nisinnassa dhammaṃ desento ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, teaching the Dhamma to one sitting with a supporting strap, one incurs one offense of wrong conduct.

…Anādariyaṃ paṭicca veṭhitasīsassa dhammaṃ desento ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, teaching the Dhamma to one wearing a head-wrap, one incurs one offense of wrong conduct.

…Anādariyaṃ paṭicca oguṇṭhitasīsassa dhammaṃ desento ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, teaching the Dhamma to one with a covered head, one incurs one offense of wrong conduct.

…Anādariyaṃ [M 0.0079] paṭicca chamāyaṃ nisīditvā āsane nisinnassa dhammaṃ desento ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, teaching the Dhamma while sitting on the ground to one sitting on a seat, one incurs one offense of wrong conduct.

…Anādariyaṃ paṭicca nīce āsane nisīditvā ucce āsane nisinnassa dhammaṃ desento ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, teaching the Dhamma while sitting on a low seat to one sitting on a high seat, one incurs one offense of wrong conduct.

…Anādariyaṃ paṭicca ṭhito nisinnassa dhammaṃ desento ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, teaching the Dhamma while standing to one who is sitting, one incurs one offense of wrong conduct.

…Anādariyaṃ paṭicca pacchato gacchanto purato gacchantassa dhammaṃ desento ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, teaching the Dhamma while walking behind to one walking in front, one incurs one offense of wrong conduct.

…Anādariyaṃ [V 0.0082] paṭicca uppathena gacchanto pathena gacchantassa dhammaṃ [T 0.0113] desento ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, teaching the Dhamma while walking off the path to one walking on the path, one incurs one offense of wrong conduct.

…Anādariyaṃ paṭicca ṭhito uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā karonto ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, defecating or urinating while standing, one incurs one offense of wrong conduct.

…Anādariyaṃ paṭicca harite uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karonto ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ….

On account of disrespect, defecating, urinating, or spitting on greenery, one incurs one offense of wrong conduct.

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karonto kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karonto ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ – anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karonto imaṃ ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati.

On account of disrespect, when one defecates, urinates, or spits in water, how many offenses are incurred? On account of disrespect, when one defecates, urinates, or spits in water, one offense of wrong conduct is incurred. On account of disrespect, when one defecates, urinates, or spits in water, one incurs this one offense.

Pādukavaggo sattamo.

The Chapter on Footwear, the seventh.

Sekhiyā niṭṭhitā.

The Sekhiya training rules are concluded.

Katāpattivāro niṭṭhito dutiyo.

The second Section on Incurred Offenses is concluded.

3. Vipattivāro

3. The Section on Failures

182. Methunaṃ [V 0.0083] dhammaṃ paṭisevantassa āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ kati vipattiyo bhajanti? Methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevantassa āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ dve vipattiyo bhajanti – siyā sīlavipattiṃ, siyā ācāravipattiṃ…pe….

182. The offenses of one who engages in sexual intercourse, to how many of the four failures do they pertain? The offenses of one who engages in sexual intercourse pertain to two of the four failures: sometimes a failure in virtue, and sometimes a failure in conduct... and so on.

Anādariyaṃ [M 0.0080] paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karontassa āpatti catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ kati vipattiyo bhajati? Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ [T 0.0114] vā karontassa āpatti catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ ekaṃ vipattiṃ bhajati – ācāravipattiṃ.

The offense of one who, on account of disrespect, passes feces, or urine, or sputum in water, to how many of the four failures does it pertain? The offense of one who, on account of disrespect, passes feces, or urine, or sputum in water, pertains to one of the four failures: a failure in conduct.

Vipattivāro niṭṭhito tatiyo.

The third Section on Failures is concluded.

4. Saṅgahitavāro

4. The Section on Inclusion

183. Methunaṃ [V 0.0084] dhammaṃ paṭisevantassa āpattiyo sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katihi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā? Methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevantassa āpattiyo sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ tīhi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā – siyā pārājikāpattikkhandhena, siyā thullaccayāpattikkhandhena, siyā dukkaṭāpattikkhandhena…pe….

183. The offenses of one who engages in sexual intercourse, by how many of the seven aggregates of offenses are they included? The offenses of one who engages in sexual intercourse are included by three of the seven aggregates of offenses: sometimes by the aggregate of Pārājika offenses, sometimes by the aggregate of Thullaccaya offenses, and sometimes by the aggregate of Dukkaṭa offenses... and so on.

Anādariyaṃ [P 5.0047] paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karontassa āpatti sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katihi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā? Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karontassa āpatti sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ ekena āpattikkhandhena saṅgahitā – dukkaṭāpattikkhandhena.

The offense of one who, on account of disrespect, passes feces, or urine, or sputum in water, by how many of the seven aggregates of offenses is it included? The offense of one who, on account of disrespect, passes feces, or urine, or sputum in water, is included by one of the seven aggregates of offenses: by the aggregate of Dukkaṭa offenses.

Saṅgahitavāro niṭṭhito catuttho.

The fourth Section on Inclusion is concluded.

5. Samuṭṭhānavāro

5. The Section on Arising

184. Methunaṃ [V 0.0085] dhammaṃ paṭisevantassa āpattiyo channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti samuṭṭhahanti (sī. syā.)? Methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevantassa āpattiyo channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhanti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti, na vācato…pe….

184. The offenses of one who engages in sexual intercourse, from how many of the six origins of offenses do they arise? The offenses of one who engages in sexual intercourse arise from one of the six origins of offenses: they arise from body and from mind, not from speech... and so on.

Anādariyaṃ [M 0.0081] paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karontassa āpatti channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi [T 0.0115] samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karontassa āpatti channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato.

The offense of one who, on account of disrespect, passes feces, or urine, or sputum in water, from how many of the six origins of offenses does it arise? The offense of one who, on account of disrespect, passes feces, or urine, or sputum in water, arises from one of the six origins of offenses: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech.

Samuṭṭhānavāro niṭṭhito pañcamo.

The fifth Section on Arising is concluded.

6. Adhikaraṇavāro

6. The Section on Legal Issues

185. Methunaṃ [V 0.0086] dhammaṃ paṭisevantassa āpattiyo catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ? Methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevantassa āpattiyo catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ āpattādhikaraṇaṃ…pe….

185. The offenses of one who engages in sexual intercourse: which of the four legal issues are they? The offenses of one who engages in sexual intercourse are the legal issue of an offense... and so on.

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karontassa āpatti catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ? Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karontassa āpatti catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ āpattādhikaraṇaṃ.

The offense of one who, out of disrespect, defecates, urinates, or spits in water: which of the four legal issues is it? The offense of one who, out of disrespect, defecates, urinates, or spits in water is the legal issue of an offense.

Adhikaraṇavāro niṭṭhito chaṭṭho.

The sixth Section on Legal Issues is concluded.

7. Samathavāro

7. The Section on Settlements

186. Methunaṃ [V 0.0087] dhammaṃ paṭisevantassa āpattiyo sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammanti? Methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevantassa āpattiyo sattannaṃ samathānaṃ tīhi samathehi sammanti – siyā sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca, siyā sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca…pe….

186. By how many of the seven settlements are the offenses of one who engages in sexual intercourse settled? The offenses of one who engages in sexual intercourse are settled by three of the seven settlements: sometimes by the Procedure in the Presence and by Acknowledgment, and sometimes by the Procedure in the Presence and by Covering Over with Grass… and so on.

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karontassa āpatti sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammati? Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ [T 0.0116] vā karontassa āpatti sattannaṃ samathānaṃ tīhi samathehi sammati – siyā sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca, siyā sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca.

By how many of the seven settlements is the offense of one who, out of disrespect, defecates, urinates, or spits in water settled? The offense of one who, out of disrespect, defecates, urinates, or spits in water is settled by three of the seven settlements: sometimes by the Procedure in the Presence and by Acknowledgment, and sometimes by the Procedure in the Presence and by Covering Over with Grass.

Samathavāro niṭṭhito sattamo.

The seventh section on settlements is concluded.

8. Samuccayavāro

8. The Section on Compilation

187. Methunaṃ [M 0.0082][V 0.0088] dhammaṃ paṭisevanto kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevanto tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Akkhāyite sarīre methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevati, āpatti pārājikassa; yebhuyyena khāyite sarīre methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevati, āpatti thullaccayassa; vaṭṭakate mukhe acchupantaṃ [P 5.0048] aṅgajātaṃ paveseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa – methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevanto imā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati.

187. How many offenses does one who engages in sexual intercourse incur? One who engages in sexual intercourse incurs three offenses. If one engages in sexual intercourse with a corpse that has not been eaten, one incurs an offense of pārājika; if one engages in sexual intercourse with a corpse that has been mostly eaten, one incurs a grave offense; if one inserts the genital organ into an open mouth without it touching, one incurs an offense of wrong-doing. One who engages in sexual intercourse incurs these three offenses.

Tā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ kati vipattiyo bhajanti, sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katihi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā, channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti, catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ, sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammanti? Tā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ dve vipattiyo bhajanti – siyā sīlavipattiṃ, siyā ācāravipattiṃ. Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ tīhi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā – siyā pārājikāpattikkhandhena, siyā thullaccayāpattikkhandhena, siyā dukkaṭāpattikkhandhena. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhanti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti, na vācato. Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ, āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Sattannaṃ [T 0.0117] samathānaṃ tīhi samathehi sammanti – siyā sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca, siyā sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca…pe….

To how many of the four failures do these offenses pertain? By how many of the seven groups of offenses are they included? From how many of the six origins of offenses do they arise? Which of the four legal issues are they? By how many of the seven settlements are they settled? These offenses pertain to two of the four failures: sometimes to a failure in morality, and sometimes to a failure in conduct. They are included by three of the seven groups of offenses: sometimes by the group of offenses entailing expulsion, sometimes by the group of grave offenses, and sometimes by the group of offenses of wrong-doing. They arise from one of the six origins of offenses: they arise from body and from mind, not from speech. Among the four legal issues, they are the legal issue of an offense. They are settled by three of the seven settlements: sometimes by the Procedure in the Presence and by Acknowledgment, and sometimes by the Procedure in the Presence and by Covering Over with Grass…and so on.

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karonto kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karonto ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ – anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karonto imaṃ ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati.

How many offenses does one who, out of disrespect, defecates, urinates, or spits in water incur? One who, out of disrespect, defecates, urinates, or spits in water incurs one offense: an offense of wrong-doing. One who, out of disrespect, defecates, urinates, or spits in water incurs this one offense.

Sā [V 0.0089] āpatti catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ kati vipattiyo bhajati, sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katihi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā, channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti, catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ, sattannaṃ, samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammati? Sā āpatti catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ ekaṃ vipattiṃ bhajati – ācāravipattiṃ. Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ ekena āpattikkhandhena saṅgahitā – dukkaṭāpattikkhandhena. Channaṃ [M 0.0083] āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato. Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ, āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ tīhi samathehi sammati – siyā sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca, siyā sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca.

To how many of the four failures does this offense pertain? By how many of the seven groups of offenses is it included? From how many of the six origins of offenses does it arise? Which of the four legal issues is it? By how many of the seven settlements is it settled? This offense pertains to one of the four failures: a failure in conduct. It is included by one of the seven groups of offenses: by the group of offenses of wrong-doing. It arises from one of the six origins of offenses: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech. Among the four legal issues, it is the legal issue of an offense. It is settled by three of the seven settlements: sometimes by the Procedure in the Presence and by Acknowledgment, and sometimes by the Procedure in the Presence and by Covering Over with Grass.

Samuccayavāro niṭṭhito aṭṭhamo.

The eighth section on compilation is concluded.

Ime aṭṭha vārā sajjhāyamaggena likhitā.

These eight sections are written according to the method of recitation.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse:

Katthapaññatti [T 0.0118] kati ca, vipattisaṅgahena ca;

Samuṭṭhānādhikaraṇā samatho, samuccayena cāti.

Where Designated and How Many; Failures and Inclusion; Origins and Legal Issues, Settlements, and Compilation.

1. Katthapaññattivāro

1. The Section on the Place of Enactment

1. Pārājikakaṇḍaṃ

1. The Chapter on the Pārājika Offenses

188. Yaṃ [V 0.0090] tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevanapaccayā pārājikaṃ kattha paññattaṃ, kaṃ ārabbha, kismiṃ vatthusmiṃ…pe… kenābhatanti?

188. Where was the pārājika rule concerning engaging in sexual intercourse laid down by that Blessed One, the knowing one, the seeing one, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One? Concerning whom was it laid down? On what occasion was it laid down? … By whom was it brought?

Yaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevanapaccayā pārājikaṃ [P 5.0049] kattha paññattanti? Vesāliyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sudinnaṃ kalandaputtaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sudinno kalandaputto purāṇadutiyikāya methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Atthi tattha paññatti, anupaññatti, anuppannapaññattīti? Ekā paññatti, dve anupaññattiyo. Anuppannapaññatti tasmiṃ natthi. Sabbattha paññatti, padesapaññattīti? Sabbatthapaññatti. Sādhāraṇapaññatti, asādhāraṇapaññattīti? Sādhāraṇapaññatti. Ekatopaññatti, ubhatopaññattīti? Ubhatopaññatti. Pañcannaṃ pātimokkhuddesānaṃ katthogadhaṃ kattha pariyāpannanti? Nidānogadhaṃ nidānapariyāpannaṃ. Katamena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchatīti? Dutiyena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchati. Catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ katamā vipattīti? Sīlavipatti. Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katamo [T 0.0119] āpattikkhandhoti? Pārājikāpattikkhandho. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhātīti? Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato [M 0.0084] ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe… kenābhatanti? Paramparābhataṃ –

Where was the pārājika rule concerning engaging in sexual intercourse laid down by that Blessed One, the knowing one, the seeing one, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One? It was laid down at Vesālī. Concerning whom? Concerning Sudinna Kalandaputta. On what occasion? Sudinna Kalandaputta engaged in sexual intercourse with his former wife. On that occasion. Is there an original enactment, a supplementary enactment, or an unarisen enactment in this case? There is one original enactment and two supplementary enactments. There is no unarisen enactment in this case. Is it a universal enactment or a partial enactment? It is a universal enactment. Is it a common enactment or an uncommon enactment? It is a common enactment. Is it an enactment for one side or for both sides? It is an enactment for both sides. In which of the five recitations of the Pātimokkha is it included, where is it comprised? It is included in the introduction, comprised in the introduction. By which recitation does it come to be recited? It comes to be recited by the second recitation. Which of the four failures is it? It is a failure of virtue. Which of the seven groups of offenses is it? It is the group of pārājika offenses. From how many of the six origins of offenses does it arise? It arises from one origin—it arises from body and mind, not from speech… By whom was it brought? It was brought by a succession of teachers.

Upāli dāsako ceva, soṇako siggavo tathā;

Moggaliputtena pañcamā, ete jambusirivhaye. …pe…;

Upāli and Dāsaka, Soṇaka and Siggava likewise; with Moggaliputta as the fifth, these taught the Vinaya in Jambudīpa...

Ete [V 0.0091] nāgā mahāpaññā, vinayaññū maggakovidā;

Vinayaṃ dīpe pakāsesuṃ, piṭakaṃ tambapaṇṇiyāti.

These great beings, of great wisdom, knowers of the Vinaya, skilled in the path, proclaimed the Vinaya Piṭaka on the island of Tambapaṇṇi.

189. Yaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena adinnaṃ ādiyanapaccayā pārājikaṃ kattha paññattanti? Rājagahe paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Dhaniyaṃ kumbhakāraputtaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Dhaniyo kumbhakāraputto rañño dārūni adinnaṃ ādiyi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

189. Where was the pārājika rule concerning taking what is not given laid down by that Blessed One, the knowing one, the seeing one, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One? It was laid down at Rājagaha. Concerning whom? Concerning Dhaniya, the potter's son. On what occasion? Dhaniya, the potter's son, took the king’s wood that was not given. On that occasion. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins: it may arise from body and mind, not from speech; it may arise from speech and mind, not from body; it may arise from body, speech, and mind...

190. Sañcicca manussaviggahaṃ jīvitā voropanapaccayā pārājikaṃ [T 0.0120] kattha paññattanti? Vesāliyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū aññamaññaṃ jīvitā voropesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

190. Where was the pārājika rule concerning the intentional deprivation of a human being of life laid down? It was laid down at Vesālī. Concerning whom? Concerning numerous bhikkhus. On what occasion? Numerous bhikkhus deprived one another of life. On that occasion. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins: it may arise from body and mind, not from speech; it may arise from speech and mind, not from body; it may arise from body, speech, and mind...

191. Asantaṃ abhūtaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ ullapanapaccayā pārājikaṃ kattha paññattanti? Vesāliyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Vaggumudātīriye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Vaggumudātīriyā bhikkhū gihīnaṃ aññamaññassa uttarimanussadhammassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

191. Where was the pārājika rule concerning boasting of a non-existent, untrue, superhuman state laid down? It was laid down at Vesālī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhus on the bank of the Vaggumudā river. On what occasion? The bhikkhus on the bank of the Vaggumudā river spoke to householders in praise of one another’s superhuman states. On that occasion. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins: it may arise from body and mind, not from speech; it may arise from speech and mind, not from body; it may arise from body, speech, and mind...

Cattāro pārājikā niṭṭhitā.

The four pārājikas are concluded.

2. Saṅghādisesakaṇḍādi

2. 2. The Chapter on Saṅghādisesa Offenses, and So Forth

192. Yaṃ [M 0.0085] tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena upakkamitvāasuciṃ mocanapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññatto, kaṃ ārabbha, kismiṃ vatthusmiṃ…pe… kenābhatanti?

192. The Saṅghādisesa offense, laid down by the Blessed One—the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—on account of intentionally emitting semen: where was it laid down? Concerning whom was it laid down? In what matter was it laid down? …and so on… By whom was it handed down?

Yaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena upakkamitvā asuciṃ mocanapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ [T 0.0121] paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ seyyasakaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā seyyasako upakkamitvā asuciṃ mocesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Atthi tattha paññatti, anupaññatti, anuppannapaññattīti? Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Anuppannapaññatti tasmiṃ natthi. Sabbatthapaññatti, padesapaññattīti? Sabbatthapaññatti. Sādhāraṇapaññatti, asādhāraṇapaññattīti? Asādhāraṇapaññatti. Ekatopaññatti, ubhatopaññattīti? Ekatopaññatti. Pañcannaṃ pātimokkhuddesānaṃ katthogadhaṃ kattha pariyāpannanti? Nidānogadhaṃ nidānapariyāpannaṃ. Katamena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchatīti? Tatiyena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchati. Catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ katamā vipattīti? Sīlavipatti. Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katamo āpattikkhandhoti? Saṅghādisesāpattikkhandho. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhātīti? Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe… kenābhatanti? Paramparābhataṃ –

Where was the Saṅghādisesa offense laid down by the Blessed One, the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, on account of intentionally emitting semen? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Seyyasaka. In what matter? The Venerable Seyyasaka intentionally emitted semen; in that matter. Is there a primary rule, a supplementary rule, or an unformulated matter in this case? There is one primary rule and one supplementary rule. There is no unformulated matter in this case. Is it a universal rule or a limited rule? It is a universal rule. Is it a common rule or an uncommon rule? It is an uncommon rule. Is it a one-sided rule or a two-sided rule? It is a one-sided rule. Into which of the five Pātimokkha recitations is it included, and to which does it belong? It is included in the introduction and belongs to the introduction. By which recitation does it come up for recitation? It comes up for recitation with the third recitation. Which of the four failures is it? It is a failure in virtue. Which of the seven classes of offenses is it? It is the Saṅghādisesa class of offenses. By how many of the six origins of offenses does it arise? It arises from one origin—it arises from body and mind, not from speech…and so on… By whom was it handed down? It was handed down by a succession of teachers—

Upāli dāsako ceva, soṇako siggavo tathā;

Moggaliputtena pañcamā, ete jambusirivhaye. …pe…;

Upāli and Dāsaka, Soṇaka and Siggava likewise; with Moggaliputta as the fifth, these taught the Vinaya in the Isle of Jambu. …and so on…

Ete nāgā mahāpaññā, vinayaññū maggakovidā;

Vinayaṃ [T 0.0122] dīpe pakāsesuṃ, piṭakaṃ tambapaṇṇiyāti.

These nāgas, of great wisdom, knowers of the Vinaya, skilled in the path, proclaimed the Vinaya Piṭaka on the island of Tambapaṇṇi.

Mātugāmena saddhiṃ kāyasaṃsaggaṃ samāpajjanapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā udāyī mātugāmena saddhiṃ kāyasaṃsaggaṃ samāpajji, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

The Saṅghādisesa offense on account of entering into bodily contact with a woman: where was it laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Udāyī. In what matter? The Venerable Udāyī entered into bodily contact with a woman; in that matter. There is one primary rule. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin—it arises from body and mind, not from speech…and so on…

Mātugāmaṃ [M 0.0086] duṭṭhullāhi vācāhi obhāsanapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ [V 0.0093] paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā udāyī mātugāmaṃ duṭṭhullāhi vācāhi obhāsi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

The Saṅghādisesa offense on account of addressing a woman with coarse words: where was it laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Udāyī. In what matter? The Venerable Udāyī addressed a woman with coarse words; in that matter. There is one primary rule. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins: sometimes it arises from body and mind, not from speech; sometimes it arises from speech and mind, not from body; sometimes it arises from body, speech, and mind. …and so on…

Mātugāmassa santike attakāmapāricariyāya vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā udāyī mātugāmassa santike attakāmapāricariyāya vaṇṇaṃ bhāsi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ [T 0.0123] āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

The Saṅghādisesa offense on account of speaking in a woman's presence in praise of service for one's own sensual enjoyment: where was it laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Udāyī. In what matter? The Venerable Udāyī spoke in a woman's presence in praise of service for his own sensual enjoyment; in that matter. There is one primary rule. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins. …and so on…

Sañcarittaṃ samāpajjanapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā udāyī sañcarittaṃ samāpajji, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato samuṭṭhāti, na vācato na cittato; siyā vācato samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato na cittato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca samuṭṭhāti, na cittato; siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

The Saṅghādisesa offense on account of undertaking matchmaking: where was it laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Udāyī. In what matter? The Venerable Udāyī undertook matchmaking; in that matter. There is one primary rule and one supplementary rule. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins: sometimes it arises from body, not from speech or mind; sometimes it arises from speech, not from body or mind; sometimes it arises from body and speech, not from mind; sometimes it arises from body and mind, not from speech; sometimes it arises from speech and mind, not from body; sometimes it arises from body, speech, and mind. …and so on…

Saññācikāya kuṭiṃ kārāpanapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti[P 5.0050]? Āḷaviyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āḷavake bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āḷavakā bhikkhū saññācikāya kuṭiyo kārāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

The Saṅghādisesa offense on account of having a hut built by personal solicitation: where was it laid down? It was laid down at Āḷavī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhus of Āḷavī. In what matter? The bhikkhus of Āḷavī had huts built by personal solicitation; in that matter. There is one primary rule. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins. …and so on…

Mahallakaṃ [M 0.0087] vihāraṃ kārāpanapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Kosambiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ channaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā channo vihāravatthuṃ sodhento aññataraṃ cetiyarukkhaṃ chedāpesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā [T 0.0124] paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

The Saṅghādisesa offense on account of having a large monastery built: where was it laid down? It was laid down at Kosambī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Channa. In what matter? The Venerable Channa, while clearing a site for a monastery, had a certain tree designated as a shrine cut down; in that matter. There is one primary rule. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from six origins. …and so on…

Bhikkhuṃ [V 0.0094] amūlakena pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṃsanapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Rājagahe paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Mettiyabhūmajake bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ amūlakena pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṃsesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

The Saṅghādisesa offense on account of groundlessly accusing a bhikkhu of a pārājika offense: where was it laid down? It was laid down at Rājagaha. Concerning whom? Concerning the Mettiyabhūmajaka bhikkhus. In what matter? The Mettiyabhūmajaka bhikkhus groundlessly accused the Venerable Dabba Mallaputta of a pārājika offense; in that matter. There is one primary rule. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins. …and so on…

Bhikkhuṃ aññabhāgiyassa adhikaraṇassa kiñcidesaṃ lesamattaṃ upādāya pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṃsanapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Rājagahe paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Mettiyabhūmajake bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ dabbaṃ mallaputtaṃ aññabhāgiyassa adhikaraṇassa kiñci desaṃ lesamattaṃ upādāya pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṃsesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

The Saṅghādisesa offense on account of accusing a bhikkhu of a pārājika offense by seizing upon some trifling detail of an unrelated issue: where was it laid down? It was laid down at Rājagaha. Concerning whom? Concerning the Mettiyabhūmajaka bhikkhus. In what matter? The Mettiyabhūmajaka bhikkhus accused the Venerable Dabba Mallaputta of a pārājika offense by seizing upon some trifling detail of an unrelated issue; in that matter. There is one primary rule. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins. …and so on…

Saṅghabhedakassa bhikkhuno yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Rājagahe paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Devadattaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Devadatto samaggassa saṅghassa bhedāya parakkami, tasmiṃ [T 0.0125] vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

The Saṅghādisesa offense on account of a schismatic bhikkhu not relinquishing his view after being formally admonished up to the third time: where was it laid down? It was laid down at Rājagaha. Concerning whom? Concerning Devadatta. In what matter? Devadatta strove to split the united Saṅgha; in that matter. There is one primary rule. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body, speech, and mind. …and so on…

Bhedakānuvattakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Rājagahe paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhū devadattassa saṅghabhedāya parakkamantassa anuvattakā ahesuṃ vaggavādakā, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ eke [M 0.0088] samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

The Saṅghādisesa offense on account of bhikkhus who are followers of a schismatic not relinquishing their view after being formally admonished up to the third time: where was it laid down? It was laid down at Rājagaha. Concerning whom? Concerning many bhikkhus. In what matter? Many bhikkhus were followers and factional speakers for Devadatta, who was striving to split the Saṅgha; in that matter. There is one primary rule. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body, speech, and mind. …and so on…

Dubbacassa bhikkhuno yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Kosambiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Āyasmantaṃ channaṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Āyasmā channo bhikkhūhi sahadhammikaṃ vuccamāno attānaṃ avacanīyaṃ akāsi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

The Saṅghādisesa offense on account of a bhikkhu who is difficult to admonish not relinquishing his view after being formally admonished up to the third time: where was it laid down? It was laid down at Kosambī. Concerning whom? Concerning the Venerable Channa. In what matter? The Venerable Channa, when being spoken to by the bhikkhus in accordance with the Dhamma, made himself unadmonishable; in that matter. There is one primary rule. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body, speech, and mind. …and so on…

Kuladūsakassa [V 0.0095] bhikkhuno yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Assajipunabbasuke bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ [T 0.0126] vatthusminti? Assajipunabbasukā bhikkhū saṅghena pabbājanīyakammakatā bhikkhū chandagāmitā dosagāmitā mohagāmitā bhayagāmitā pāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Where was the Saṅghādisesa offence laid down for a bhikkhu who corrupts families, on account of not relinquishing his view after being formally admonished up to the third time? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu. In what matter? The bhikkhus Assaji and Punabbasu, upon whom the Saṅgha had performed the act of banishment, caused the bhikkhus who had performed the act to fall into courses of desire, hatred, delusion, and fear; in that matter. There is one original formulation. Of the six origins of offences, it arises from one origin: it arises from body, speech, and mind… etc.

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karaṇapaccayā dukkaṭaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiye bhikkhū ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū udake uccārampi passāvampi kheḷampi akaṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

Where was the dukkaṭa offence laid down for defecating, urinating, or spitting in water out of disrespect? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six bhikkhus. In what matter? The group-of-six bhikkhus defecated, urinated, and spat in water; in that matter. There is one original formulation and one supplementary formulation. Of the six origins of offences, it arises from one origin: it arises from body and mind, but not from speech… etc.

Katthapaññattivāro niṭṭhito paṭhamo.

The first section on where the rules were laid down is finished.

2. Katāpattivāro

2. The Section on Committed Offences

1. Pārājikakaṇḍaṃ

1. The Division on Pārājika Offences

193. Methunaṃ [V 0.0096] dhammaṃ paṭisevanapaccayā kati āpattiyo āpajjati[P 5.0051]? Methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevanapaccayā catasso āpattiyo āpajjati – akkhāyite sarīre methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevati, āpatti pārājikassa; yebhuyyena khāyite sarīre methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevati, āpatti thullaccayassa[M 0.0089]; vaṭṭakate mukhe acchupantaṃ aṅgajātaṃ paveseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; jatumaṭṭhake pācittiyaṃ – methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevanapaccayā imā [T 0.0127] catasso āpattiyo āpajjati.

193. How many offences does one incur on account of engaging in sexual intercourse? On account of engaging in sexual intercourse, one incurs four offences: if one engages in sexual intercourse with a corpse that has not been eaten by animals, an offence of pārājika is incurred; if one engages in sexual intercourse with a corpse that has been mostly eaten by animals, an offence of thullaccaya is incurred; if one inserts the genital organ into an open mouth without it touching, an offence of dukkaṭa is incurred; for a lacquered figure, an offence of pācittiya is incurred. On account of engaging in sexual intercourse, one incurs these four offences.

Adinnaṃ ādiyanapaccayā kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Adinnaṃ ādiyanapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Pañcamāsakaṃ vā atirekapañcamāsakaṃ vā agghanakaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyati, āpatti pārājikassa; atirekamāsakaṃ vā ūnapañcamāsakaṃ vā agghanakaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyati, āpatti thullaccayassa; māsakaṃ vā ūnamāsakaṃ vā agghanakaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyati, āpatti dukkaṭassa – adinnaṃ ādiyanapaccayā imā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati.

How many offences does one incur on account of taking what is not given? On account of taking what is not given, one incurs three offences. If one takes what is not given, reckoned as theft, of the value of five māsakas or more than five māsakas, an offence of pārājika is incurred; if one takes what is not given, reckoned as theft, of the value of more than one māsaka but less than five māsakas, an offence of thullaccaya is incurred; if one takes what is not given, reckoned as theft, of the value of one māsaka or less than one māsaka, an offence of dukkaṭa is incurred. On account of taking what is not given, one incurs these three offences.

Sañcicca manussaviggahaṃ jīvitā voropanapaccayā kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Sañcicca manussaviggahaṃ jīvitā voropanapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Manussaṃ odissa opātaṃ khaṇati “papatitvā marissatī”ti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; papatite dukkhā vedanā uppajjati, āpatti thullaccayassa; marati, āpatti pārājikassa – sañcicca manussaviggahaṃ jīvitā voropanapaccayā imā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati.

How many offences does one incur on account of intentionally depriving a human being of life? On account of intentionally depriving a human being of life, one incurs three offences. If one digs a pitfall with reference to a person, thinking, 'Having fallen, they will die,' an offence of dukkaṭa is incurred. If, upon their having fallen, a painful feeling arises, an offence of thullaccaya is incurred. If they die, an offence of pārājika is incurred. On account of intentionally depriving a human being of life, one incurs these three offences.

Asantaṃ abhūtaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ ullapanapaccayā kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Asantaṃ [V 0.0097] abhūtaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ ullapanapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati – pāpiccho icchāpakato asantaṃ abhūtaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ ullapati, āpatti pārājikassa, “yo [T 0.0128] te vihāre vasati so bhikkhu arahā”ti bhaṇati, paṭivijānantassa āpatti thullaccayassa; na paṭivijānantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa – asantaṃ abhūtaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ ullapanapaccayā imā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati.

How many offences does one incur on account of proclaiming a non-existent, untrue superhuman state? On account of proclaiming a non-existent, untrue superhuman state, one incurs three offences: if, being of evil desires and overcome by desire, one proclaims a non-existent, untrue superhuman state, an offence of pārājika is incurred; if one says, 'The monk who lives in your monastery is an arahant,' and the listener understands, an offence of thullaccaya is incurred; if the listener does not understand, an offence of dukkaṭa is incurred. On account of proclaiming a non-existent, untrue superhuman state, one incurs these three offences.

Cattāro pārājikā niṭṭhitā.

The four pārājikas are concluded.

2. Saṅghādisesakaṇḍādi

2. The Chapter on Saṅghādisesa, and so forth

194. Upakkamitvā asuciṃ mocanapaccayā kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Upakkamitvā asucimocanapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati – ceteti upakkamati muccati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa; ceteti [M 0.0090] upakkamati na muccati, āpatti thullaccayassa; payoge dukkaṭaṃ – upakkamitvā asucimocanapaccayā imā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati.

194. On account of making an effort to discharge semen, how many offences does one incur? On account of making an effort to discharge semen, one incurs three offences: if one intends, makes an effort, and it is discharged, an offence of saṅghādisesa is incurred; if one intends, makes an effort, but it is not discharged, an offence of thullaccaya is incurred; for the effort, a dukkaṭa is incurred. On account of making an effort to discharge semen, one incurs these three offences.

Kāyasaṃsaggaṃ samāpajjanapaccayā kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Kāyasaṃsaggaṃ samāpajjanapaccayā pañca āpattiyo āpajjati – avassutā bhikkhunī avassutassa purisapuggalassa adhakkhakaṃ ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalaṃ gahaṇaṃ sādiyati, āpatti pārājikassa; bhikkhu kāyena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa; kāyena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti thullaccayassa; kāyapaṭibaddhena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa; aṅgulipatodake pācittiyaṃ – kāyasaṃsaggaṃ samāpajjanapaccayā imā pañca āpattiyo āpajjati.

On account of engaging in physical contact, how many offences does one incur? On account of engaging in physical contact, one incurs five offences: if a lustful bhikkhunī consents to a lustful male person grasping the area below the collarbone and above the kneecap, an offence of pārājika is incurred; if a bhikkhu touches body with body, an offence of saṅghādisesa is incurred; if with the body he touches what is connected to the body, an offence of thullaccaya is incurred; if with what is connected to the body he touches what is connected to the body, an offence of dukkaṭa is incurred; for poking with a finger, a pācittiya is incurred. On account of engaging in physical contact, one incurs these five offences.

Mātugāmaṃ duṭṭhullāhi vācāhi obhāsanapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati – vaccamaggaṃ passāvamaggaṃ ādissa vaṇṇampi bhaṇati avaṇṇampi bhaṇati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa; vaccamaggaṃ passāvamaggaṃ ṭhapetvā adhakkhakaṃ ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalaṃ ādissa vaṇṇampi bhaṇati [T 0.0129] avaṇṇampi bhaṇati, āpatti thullaccayassa; kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ ādissa vaṇṇampi bhaṇati avaṇṇampi bhaṇati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

On account of addressing a woman with coarse words, one incurs three offences: if one speaks praise or dispraise referring to the passage for feces or the passage for urine, an offence of saṅghādisesa is incurred; if, excluding the passage for feces and the passage for urine, one speaks praise or dispraise referring to the area below the collarbone and above the kneecap, an offence of thullaccaya is incurred; if one speaks praise or dispraise referring to what is connected to the body, an offence of dukkaṭa is incurred.

Attakāmapāricariyāya vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati – mātugāmassa santike attakāmapāricariyāya vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa; paṇḍakassa [V 0.0098] santike attakāmapāricariyāya vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, āpatti thullaccayassa; tiracchānagatassa santike attakāmapāricariyāya vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

On account of speaking in praise of service for one's own sensual pleasure, one incurs three offenses: if one speaks in praise of service for one's own sensual pleasure in the presence of a woman, an offense of Saṅghādisesa is incurred; if one speaks in praise of service for one's own sensual pleasure in the presence of a eunuch, an offense of Thullaccaya is incurred; if one speaks in praise of service for one's own sensual pleasure in the presence of an animal, an offense of Dukkaṭa is incurred.

Sañcarittaṃ samāpajjanapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati – paṭiggaṇhāti vīmaṃsati paccāharati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa; paṭiggaṇhāti vīmaṃsati na paccāharati, āpatti thullaccayassa; paṭiggaṇhāti na vīmaṃsati na paccāharati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

On account of undertaking the work of a go-between, one incurs three offenses: if one accepts, investigates, and reports back, an offense of Saṅghādisesa is incurred; if one accepts and investigates but does not report back, an offense of Thullaccaya is incurred; if one accepts but does not investigate and does not report back, an offense of Dukkaṭa is incurred.

Saññācikāya kuṭiṃ kārāpanapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati – kārāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; ekaṃ piṇḍaṃ ekapiṇḍe (syā.) anāgate āpatti thullaccayassa; tasmiṃ piṇḍe āgate āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

On account of having a hut built by personal solicitation, one incurs three offenses: when one has it built, for the effort, a Dukkaṭa is incurred; before the final lump of clay arrives, an offense of Thullaccaya is incurred; when that final lump of clay has arrived, an offense of Saṅghādisesa is incurred.

Mahallakaṃ [M 0.0091] vihāraṃ kārāpanapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati – kārāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; ekaṃ piṇḍaṃ anāgate, āpatti thullaccayassa; tasmiṃ piṇḍe āgate āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

On account of having a large dwelling built, one incurs three offenses: when one has it built, for the effort, a Dukkaṭa is incurred; before the final lump of clay arrives, an offense of Thullaccaya is incurred; when that final lump of clay has arrived, an offense of Saṅghādisesa is incurred.

Bhikkhuṃ amūlakena pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṃsanapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati – anokāsaṃ kārāpetvā cāvanādhippāyo [T 0.0130] vadeti, āpatti saṅghādisesena dukkaṭassa; okāsaṃ kārāpetvā akkosādhippāyo vadeti, āpatti omasavādassa.

On account of groundlessly accusing a bhikkhu of a Pārājika offense, one incurs three offenses: if, without having an opportunity made, one speaks with the intention of disrobing him, an offense of Dukkaṭa together with Saṅghādisesa is incurred; if, having had an opportunity made, one speaks with the intention of reviling, an offense of Omasavāda is incurred.

Bhikkhuṃ aññabhāgiyassa adhikaraṇassa kiñci desaṃ lesamattaṃ upādāya pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṃsanapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati – anokāsaṃ kārāpetvā cāvanādhippāyo vadeti, āpatti saṅghādisesena dukkaṭassa; okāsaṃ kārāpetvā akkosādhippāyo vadeti, āpatti omasavādassa.

On account of accusing a bhikkhu of a Pārājika offense by taking up a mere pretext concerning some point of a matter belonging to another party, one incurs three offenses: if, without having an opportunity made, one speaks with the intention of disrobing him, an offense of Dukkaṭa together with Saṅghādisesa is incurred; if, having had an opportunity made, one speaks with the intention of reviling, an offense of Omasavāda is incurred.

Saṅghabhedako bhikkhu yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati – ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

On account of a bhikkhu who is a splitter of the Saṅgha not desisting when being admonished up to the third time, three offenses are incurred: for the motion, a Dukkaṭa is incurred; for the two formal announcements, Thullaccayas are incurred; at the conclusion of the formal announcements, an offense of Saṅghādisesa is incurred.

Bhedakānuvattakā bhikkhū yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanapaccayā tisso āpattiyo [V 0.0099] āpajjati – ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

On account of bhikkhus who are followers of a splitter not desisting when being admonished up to the third time, three offenses are incurred: for the motion, a Dukkaṭa is incurred; for the two formal announcements, Thullaccayas are incurred; at the conclusion of the formal announcements, an offense of Saṅghādisesa is incurred.

Dubbaco bhikkhu yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati – ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

On account of a bhikkhu who is difficult to admonish not desisting when being admonished up to the third time, three offenses are incurred: for the motion, a Dukkaṭa is incurred; for the two formal announcements, Thullaccayas are incurred; at the conclusion of the formal announcements, an offense of Saṅghādisesa is incurred.

Kuladūsako bhikkhu yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati – ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa…pe….

On account of a bhikkhu who is a corrupter of families not desisting when being admonished up to the third time, three offenses are incurred: for the motion, a Dukkaṭa is incurred; for the two formal announcements, Thullaccayas are incurred; at the conclusion of the formal announcements, an offense of Saṅghādisesa is incurred… and so on.

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā [P 5.0052] karaṇapaccayā kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ [M 0.0092] vā kheḷaṃ vā karaṇapaccayā ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ – anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karaṇapaccayā imaṃ ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati.

On account of disrespect, how many offenses are incurred for defecating, urinating, or spitting in water? On account of disrespect, for defecating, urinating, or spitting in water, one incurs one offense, a Dukkaṭa. Thus, on account of disrespect, for defecating, urinating, or spitting in water, one incurs this one offense.

Katāpattivāro niṭṭhito dutiyo.

The second section on incurred offenses is concluded.

3. Vipattivāro

3. 3. The Section on Failures

195. Methunaṃ [V 0.0100] dhammaṃ paṭisevanapaccayā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ kati vipattiyo bhajanti? Methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevanapaccayā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ dve vipattiyo bhajanti – siyā sīlavipattiṃ siyā ācāravipattiṃ…pe….

195. Under how many of the four kinds of failures do the offenses due to engaging in sexual intercourse fall? The offenses due to engaging in sexual intercourse fall under two of the four kinds of failures—possibly a failure in virtue, possibly a failure in conduct… and so on.

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karaṇapaccayā āpatti catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ kati vipattiyo bhajati? Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karaṇapaccayā āpatti catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ ekaṃ vipattiṃ bhajati – ācāravipattiṃ.

Due to disrespect, under how many of the four kinds of failures does the offense of defecating, urinating, or spitting in water fall? Due to disrespect, the offense of defecating, urinating, or spitting in water falls under one of the four kinds of failures—a failure in conduct.

Vipattivāro niṭṭhito tatiyo.

The Third Section on Failures is concluded.

4. Saṅgahitavāro

4. 4. The Section on Inclusion

196. Methunaṃ [V 0.0101] dhammaṃ paṭisevanapaccayā āpattiyo sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katihi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā? Methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevanapaccayā [T 0.0132] āpattiyo sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ catūhi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā – siyā pārājikāpattikkhandhena, siyā thullaccayāpattikkhandhena, siyā pācittiyāpattikkhandhena, siyā dukkaṭāpattikkhandhena…pe….

196. Under how many of the seven aggregates of offenses are the offenses due to engaging in sexual intercourse included? The offenses due to engaging in sexual intercourse are included under four of the seven aggregates of offenses—possibly the Pārājika aggregate, possibly the Thullaccaya aggregate, possibly the Pācittiya aggregate, or possibly the Dukkaṭa aggregate… and so on.

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karaṇapaccayā āpatti sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katihi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā? Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karaṇapaccayā āpatti sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ ekena āpattikkhandhena saṅgahitā – dukkaṭāpattikkhandhena.

Due to disrespect, under how many of the seven aggregates of offenses is the offense of defecating, urinating, or spitting in water included? Due to disrespect, the offense of defecating, urinating, or spitting in water is included under one of the seven aggregates of offenses—the Dukkaṭa aggregate.

Saṅgahitavāro niṭṭhito catuttho.

The Fourth Section on Inclusion is concluded.

5. Samuṭṭhānavāro

5. 5. The Section on Origination

197. Methunaṃ [M 0.0093][V 0.0102] dhammaṃ paṭisevanapaccayā āpattiyo channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti? Methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevanapaccayā āpattiyo channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhanti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti, na vācato…pe….

197. From how many of the six sources of origination of offenses do the offenses due to engaging in sexual intercourse originate? The offenses due to engaging in sexual intercourse originate from one of the six sources of origination of offenses—they originate from body and mind, not from speech… and so on.

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karaṇapaccayā āpatti channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karaṇapaccayā āpatti channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

Due to disrespect, from how many of the six origins of offenses does the offense of defecating, urinating, or spitting in water originate? Due to disrespect, the offense of defecating, urinating, or spitting in water originates from one of the six origins of offenses—it originates from body and mind, not from speech… and so on.

Samuṭṭhānavāro niṭṭhito pañcamo.

The Fifth Section on Origination is concluded.

6. Adhikaraṇavāro

6. The Section on Legal Issues

198. Methunaṃ [T 0.0133][V 0.0103] dhammaṃ paṭisevanapaccayā āpattiyo catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ? Methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevanapaccayā āpattiyo catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ āpattādhikaraṇaṃ…pe….

198. The offenses due to engaging in sexual intercourse, to which of the four legal issues do they belong? The offenses due to engaging in sexual intercourse belong to the legal issue of offenses… and so on.

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karaṇapaccayā āpatti catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ? Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karaṇapaccayā āpatti catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ āpattādhikaraṇaṃ.

The offense of defecating, urinating, or spitting in water out of disrespect, to which of the four legal issues does it belong? The offense of defecating, urinating, or spitting in water out of disrespect belongs to the legal issue of offenses.

Adhikaraṇavāro niṭṭhito chaṭṭho.

The sixth Section on Legal Issues is concluded.

7. Samathavāro

7. The Section on Settlements

199. Methunaṃ [V 0.0104] dhammaṃ paṭisevanapaccayā āpattiyo sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammanti? Methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevanapaccayā āpattiyo sattannaṃ samathānaṃ tīhi samathehi sammanti – siyā sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca; siyā sammukhāvinayena tiṇavatthārakena ca…pe….

199. The offenses due to engaging in sexual intercourse, by how many of the seven settlements are they settled? The offenses due to engaging in sexual intercourse are settled by three of the seven settlements: sometimes by the procedure in the presence and by acting after acknowledgement; and sometimes by the procedure in the presence and by the covering over with grass… and so on.

Anādariyaṃ [M 0.0094] paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karaṇapaccayā āpatti sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammati? Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karaṇapaccayā āpatti sattannaṃ samathānaṃ tīhi samathehi sammati – siyā sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca, siyā sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena cāti.

The offense of defecating, urinating, or spitting in water out of disrespect, by how many of the seven settlements is it settled? The offense of defecating, urinating, or spitting in water out of disrespect is settled by three of the seven settlements: sometimes by the procedure in the presence and by acting after acknowledgement, and sometimes by the procedure in the presence and by the covering over with grass.

Samathavāro niṭṭhito sattamo.

The seventh Section on Settlements is concluded.

8. Samuccayavāro

8. The Section on Compilation

200. Methunaṃ [T 0.0134][V 0.0105] dhammaṃ paṭisevanapaccayā kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevanapaccayā catasso āpattiyo [P 5.0053] āpajjati. Akkhāyite sarīre methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevati, āpatti pārājikassa; yebhuyyena khāyite sarīre methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevati, āpatti thullaccayassa; vaṭṭakate mukhe acchupantaṃ aṅgajātaṃ paveseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; jatumaṭṭhake pācittiyaṃ – methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevanapaccayā imā catasso āpattiyo āpajjati. Tā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ kati vipattiyo bhajanti? Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katihi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā? Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti? Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ? Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammanti? Tā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ dve vipattiyo bhajanti – siyā sīlavipattiṃ siyā ācāravipattiṃ. Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ catūhi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā – siyā pārājikāpattikkhandhena, siyā thullaccayāpattikkhandhena, siyā pācittiyāpattikkhandhena, siyā dukkaṭāpattikkhandhena. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhanti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti, na vācato. Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ, āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ, tīhi samathehi sammanti – siyā sammukhāvinayena ca, paṭiññātakaraṇena ca, siyā sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca…pe….

200. How many offenses are incurred due to engaging in sexual intercourse? Due to engaging in sexual intercourse, four offenses are incurred. If one engages in sexual intercourse with a corpse not yet eaten by dogs or jackals, an offense entailing expulsion is incurred; if one engages in sexual intercourse with a corpse that has been mostly eaten, a serious offense is incurred; if one inserts the male organ into a wide-open mouth without it touching, an offense of wrong-doing is incurred; for piercing with a stick of lac, an offense entailing expiation is incurred—due to engaging in sexual intercourse, these four offenses are incurred. Those offenses, how many of the four failures do they partake in? By how many of the seven aggregates of offenses are they included? From how many of the six origins of offenses do they arise? Which of the four legal issues is it? By how many of the seven settlements are they settled? Those offenses partake in two of the four failures: sometimes failure in virtue, and sometimes failure in conduct. They are included in four of the seven aggregates of offenses: sometimes the aggregate of offenses entailing expulsion, sometimes the aggregate of serious offenses, sometimes the aggregate of offenses entailing expiation, and sometimes the aggregate of offenses of wrong-doing. They arise from one of the six origins of offenses: they arise from body and from mind, not from speech. Among the four legal issues, it is the legal issue of offenses. Among the seven settlements, they are settled by three settlements: sometimes by the procedure in the presence and by acting after acknowledgement; and sometimes by the procedure in the presence and by the covering over with grass… and so on.

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca [T 0.0135] udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karaṇapaccayā kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karaṇapaccayā ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Dukkaṭaṃ – anādariyaṃ paṭicca [M 0.0095] udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karaṇapaccayā imaṃ ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Sā āpatti catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ kati vipattiyo bhajati? Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katihi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā? Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ [V 0.0106] adhikaraṇaṃ? Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammati? Sā āpatti catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ ekaṃ vipattiṃ bhajati – ācāravipattiṃ. Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ ekena āpattikkhandhena saṅgahitā – dukkaṭāpattikkhandhena. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato. Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ, āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ tīhi samathehi sammati – siyā sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca, siyā sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena cāti.

Due to disrespect, how many offenses are incurred by defecating, urinating, or spitting in water? Due to disrespect, one offense is incurred by defecating, urinating, or spitting in water: an offense of wrong-doing. Due to disrespect, one incurs this single offense by defecating, urinating, or spitting in water. That offense, how many of the four failures does it partake in? By how many of the seven aggregates of offenses is it included? From how many of the six origins of offenses does it arise? Which of the four legal issues is it? By how many of the seven settlements is it settled? That offense partakes in one of the four failures: failure in conduct. It is included in one of the seven aggregates of offenses: the aggregate of offenses of wrong-doing. It arises from one of the six origins of offenses: it arises from body and from mind, not from speech. Among the four legal issues, it is the legal issue of offenses. It is settled by three of the seven settlements: sometimes by the procedure in the presence and by acting after acknowledgement, and sometimes by the procedure in the presence and by the covering over with grass.

Samuccayavāro niṭṭhito aṭṭhamo.

The eighth Section on Compilation is concluded.

Aṭṭhapaccayavārā niṭṭhitā.

The eight sections on conditions are concluded.

Mahāvibhaṅge soḷasamahāvārā niṭṭhitā.

The sixteen great sections in the Great Analysis are concluded.

Bhikkhuvibhaṅgamahāvāro niṭṭhito.

The Great Section of the Analysis of Monks is concluded.

Bhikkhunīvibhaṅgo

The Analysis of the Bhikkhunīs' Rules

1. Katthapaññattivāro

1. The Section on Where the Rules Were Laid Down

1. Pārājikakaṇḍaṃ

1. The Chapter on the Pārājika Offenses

201. Yaṃ [T 0.0136][P 5.0054][M 0.0096][V 0.0107] tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena bhikkhunīnaṃ pañcamaṃ pārājikaṃ kattha paññattaṃ? Kaṃ ārabbha? Kismiṃ vatthusmiṃ? Atthi tattha paññatti, anupaññatti, anuppannapaññatti? Sabbatthapaññatti, padesapaññatti? Sādhāraṇapaññatti, asādhāraṇapaññatti? Ekatopaññatti, ubhatopaññatti? Catunnaṃ pātimokkhuddesānaṃ katthogadhaṃ kattha pariyāpannaṃ? Katamena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchati? Catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ katamā vipatti? Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katamo āpattikkhandho? Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ? Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammati? Ko tattha vinayo? Ko tattha abhivinayo? Kiṃ tattha pātimokkhaṃ? Kiṃ tattha adhipātimokkhaṃ? Kā vipatti? Kā sampatti? Kā paṭipatti? Kati atthavase paṭicca bhagavatā bhikkhunīnaṃ pañcamaṃ pārājikaṃ paññattaṃ? Kā sikkhanti? Kā sikkhitasikkhā? Kattha ṭhitaṃ? Kā dhārenti? Kassa vacanaṃ? Kenābhatanti?

201. That fifth pārājika for bhikkhunīs which was laid down by the Blessed One—the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One—where was it laid down? Concerning whom was it laid down? In what matter was it laid down? Is there in this case an original enactment, a subsequent enactment, or an unenacted enactment? Is it a universal enactment or a local enactment? Is it a shared enactment or an unshared enactment? Is it a one-sided enactment or a two-sided enactment? Among the four recitations of the Pātimokkha, in which is it included, in which is it comprised? By which recitation is it recited? Among the four failures, which failure is it? Among the seven groups of offenses, which group of offenses is it? Among the six origins of offenses, from how many origins does it arise? Among the four legal issues, which legal issue is it? Among the seven methods for settling legal issues, by how many is it settled? What is the Vinaya in this case? What is the Abhivinaya in this case? What is the Pātimokkha in this case? What is the Adhipātimokkha in this case? What is failure? What is accomplishment? What is the practice? On account of how many benefits was the fifth pārājika for bhikkhunīs laid down by the Blessed One? Who are the ones training? Who are the ones who have completed the training? In whom is it established? Who maintains it? Whose word is it? By whom was it handed down?

202. Yaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena bhikkhunīnaṃ pañcamaṃ pārājikaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sundarīnandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ [T 0.0137] vatthusminti? Sundarīnandā bhikkhunī avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Atthi tattha paññatti anupaññatti anuppannapaññattīti? Ekā paññatti. Anupaññatti anuppannapaññatti tasmiṃ natthi. Sabbatthapaññatti[V 0.0108], padesapaññattīti? Sabbatthapaññatti. Sādhāraṇapaññatti, asādhāraṇapaññattīti? Asādhāraṇapaññatti. Ekatopaññatti, ubhatopaññattīti? Ekatopaññatti. Catunnaṃ pātimokkhuddesānaṃ katthogadhaṃ kattha pariyāpannanti? Nidānogadhaṃ nidānapariyāpannaṃ. Katamena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchatīti? Dutiyena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchati. Catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ katamā vipattīti? Sīlavipatti. Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katamo āpattikkhandhoti? Pārājikāpattikkhandho. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhātīti? Ekena samuṭṭhāne [M 0.0097] samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato. Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇanti? Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ? Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammatīti? Dvīhi samathehi sammati – sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca. Ko tattha vinayo, ko tattha abhivinayoti? Paññatti vinayo, vibhatti abhivinayo. Kiṃ tattha pātimokkhaṃ, kiṃ tattha adhipātimokkhanti? Paññatti pātimokkhaṃ, vibhatti adhipātimokkhaṃ. Kā vipattīti? Asaṃvaro vipatti. Kā sampattīti[T 0.0138]? Saṃvaro sampatti. Kā paṭipattīti? Na evarūpaṃ karissāmīti yāvajīvaṃ āpāṇakoṭikaṃ samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu. a. ni. 10.31 Kati atthavase paṭicca bhagavatā bhikkhunīnaṃ pañcamaṃ pārājikaṃ paññattanti? Dasa atthavase paṭicca bhagavatā bhikkhunīnaṃ pañcamaṃ pārājikaṃ paññattaṃ – saṅghasuṭṭhutāya, saṅghaphāsutāya, dummaṅkūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ niggahāya, pesalānaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ phāsuvihārāya, diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ āsavānaṃ saṃvarāya, samparāyikānaṃ āsavānaṃ paṭighātāya, appasannānaṃ pasādāya, pasannānaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya, saddhammaṭṭhitiyā, vinayānuggahāya. Kā sikkhantīti? Sekkhā ca puthujjanakalyāṇikā ca sikkhanti. Kā sikkhitasikkhāti? Arahantiyo arahantā (ka.) sikkhitasikkhā. Kattha ṭhitanti? Sikkhākāmāsu ṭhitaṃ. Kā dhārentīti? Yāsaṃ vattati tā dhārenti. Kassa vacananti? Bhagavato vacanaṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassa. Kenābhatanti? Paramparābhataṃ –

202. That fifth pārājika for bhikkhunīs which was laid down by the Blessed One—the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One—where was it laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā. In what matter? The bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā, being impassioned, consented to physical contact with an impassioned man; in that matter. Is there in this case an original enactment, a subsequent enactment, or an unenacted enactment? There is one original enactment. There is no subsequent enactment or unenacted enactment in this case. Is it a universal enactment or a local enactment? It is a universal enactment. Is it a shared enactment or an unshared enactment? It is an unshared enactment. Is it a one-sided enactment or a two-sided enactment? It is a one-sided enactment. Among the four recitations of the Pātimokkha, in which is it included, in which is it comprised? It is included in the introduction, comprised in the introduction. By which recitation is it recited? It is recited by the second recitation. Among the four failures, which failure is it? It is a failure in virtue. Among the seven groups of offenses, which group of offenses is it? It is the group of pārājika offenses. Among the six origins of offenses, from how many origins does it arise? It arises from one origin: it arises from body and mind, not from speech. Among the four legal issues, which legal issue is it? It is a legal issue concerning an offense. Among the seven methods for settling legal issues, by how many is it settled? It is settled by two methods: by the procedure in the presence of and by acting according to acknowledgement. What is the Vinaya in this case? What is the Abhivinaya in this case? The rule-matrix is the Vinaya; the analysis is the Abhivinaya. What is the Pātimokkha in this case? What is the Adhipātimokkha in this case? The rule-matrix is the Pātimokkha; the analysis is the Adhipātimokkha. What is failure? Non-restraint is failure. What is accomplishment? Restraint is accomplishment. What is the practice? The practice is this: one trains in the training rules, having undertaken for as long as life lasts, until life's very end, the resolve: 'I will not do such a thing.' On account of how many benefits was the fifth pārājika for bhikkhunīs laid down by the Blessed One? On account of ten benefits was the fifth pārājika for bhikkhunīs laid down by the Blessed One: for the excellence of the Saṅgha, for the comfort of the Saṅgha, for the restraint of ill-behaved bhikkhunīs, for the comfortable living of bhikkhunīs of lovely virtue, for the restraint of taints in the present life, for the dispelling of taints in future lives, for inspiring confidence in the unconfident, for the increase of confidence in the confident, for the stability of the true Dhamma, and for the support of the Vinaya. Who are the ones training? Learners and virtuous worldlings are the ones training. Who are the ones who have completed the training? Female Arahants have completed the training. In whom is it established? It is established in those who desire the training. Who maintains it? Those who study it maintain it. Whose word is it? It is the word of the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One. By whom was it handed down? It was handed down by a succession of teachers:

Upāli dāsako ceva, soṇako siggavo tathā;

Moggaliputtena pañcamā, ete jambusirivhaye.

Upāli and Dāsaka, Soṇaka and likewise Siggava; with Moggaliputta as the fifth, these in Jambusirivhaya recited the Vinaya.

Tato mahindo iṭṭiyo, uttiyo sambalo tathā;

Bhaddanāmo ca paṇḍito.

Then Mahinda, Iṭṭiya, Uttiya, and likewise Sambala, and the wise Bhaddanāma.

Ete [V 0.0109] nāgā mahāpaññā, jambudīpā idhāgatā;

Vinayaṃ te vācayiṃsu, piṭakaṃ tambapaṇṇiyā.

These Nāgas of great wisdom came here from Jambudīpa; they recited the Vinaya Piṭaka in Tambapaṇṇi.

Nikāye pañca vācesuṃ, satta ceva pakaraṇe;

Tato ariṭṭho medhāvī, tissadatto ca paṇḍito.

They recited the five Nikāyas and the seven treatises; then the insightful Ariṭṭha, and the wise Tissadatta.

Visārado kāḷasumano, thero ca dīghanāmako;

Dīghasumano ca paṇḍito.

The confident Kāḷasumana, the elder named Dīgha, and the wise Dīghasumana.

Punadeva [M 0.0098] kāḷasumano, nāgatthero ca buddharakkhito;

Tissatthero ca medhāvī, devatthero ca paṇḍito.

And again, Kāḷasumana, the elder Nāga, and Buddharakkhita; and the insightful elder Tissa, and the wise elder Deva.

Punadeva sumano medhāvī, vinaye ca visārado;

Bahussuto cūḷanāgo, gajova duppadhaṃsiyo.

And again, the insightful Sumana, confident in the Vinaya; the very learned Cūḷanāga, hard to assail like an elephant.

Dhammapālitanāmo ca, rohaṇe sādhupūjito;

Tassa sisso mahāpañño, khemanāmo tipeṭako.

And the one named Dhammapālita, honored by the virtuous in Rohaṇa; his disciple of great wisdom, named Khema, a master of the Tipiṭaka.

Dīpe tārakarājāva paññāya atirocatha;

Upatisso ca medhāvī, phussadevo mahākathī.

In the island, he shone forth with wisdom like the king of stars; and the insightful Upatissa, and Phussadeva, the great preacher.

Punadeva sumano medhāvī, pupphanāmo bahussuto;

Mahākathī mahāsivo, piṭake sabbattha kovido.

Again, the insightful Sumana, the widely learned Pupphanāma, the great preacher Mahāsiva, skilled in all the Piṭakas.

Punadeva upāli medhāvī, vinaye ca visārado;

Mahānāgo mahāpañño, saddhammavaṃsakovido.

Again, the wise Upāli, skilled in the Vinaya; and Mahānāga of great wisdom, skilled in the lineage of the true Dhamma.

Punadeva abhayo medhāvī, piṭake sabbattha kovido;

Tissatthero ca medhāvī, vinaye ca visārado.

Again, the wise Abhaya, skilled in all the Piṭakas; and the elder Tissa, wise and skilled in the Vinaya.

Tassa [V 0.0110] sisso mahāpañño, pupphanāmo bahussuto;

Sāsanaṃ anurakkhanto, jambudīpe patiṭṭhito.

His disciple, of great wisdom, named Puppha, widely learned, protecting the Dispensation, was established in Jambudīpa.

Cūḷābhayo ca medhāvī, vinaye ca visārado;

Tissatthero ca medhāvī, saddhammavaṃsakovido.

And the wise Cūḷābhaya, skilled in the Vinaya; and the elder Tissa, wise and versed in the lineage of the true Dhamma.

Cūḷadevo ca medhāvī, vinaye ca visārado;

Sivatthero ca medhāvī, vinaye sabbattha kovido.

And the wise Cūḷadeva, skilled in the Vinaya; and the elder Siva, wise and expert in all aspects of the Vinaya.

Ete nāgā mahāpaññā, vinayaññū maggakovidā;

Vinayaṃ [P 5.0055] dīpe pakāsesuṃ, piṭakaṃ tambapaṇṇiyāti.

These noble ones of great wisdom, knowers of the Vinaya, skilled in the Path, illuminated the Vinaya Piṭaka in the island of Tambapaṇṇi.

203. Yaṃ [T 0.0139] tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena bhikkhunīnaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ pārājikaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Thullanandā bhikkhunī jānaṃ pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpannaṃ bhikkhuniṃ nevattanā paṭicodesi [M 0.0099] gaṇassa ārocesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

203. Where was the sixth pārājika for bhikkhunīs enacted by that Blessed One, the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One? It was enacted at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. In what matter? The bhikkhunī Thullanandā, knowing a bhikkhunī had committed a pārājika offense, neither reproved her herself nor reported it to the group. In that matter. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: it arises from body, from speech, and from mind...

204. Bhikkhunīnaṃ sattamaṃ pārājikaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Thullanandā bhikkhunī samaggena saṅghena ukkhittaṃ ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ anuvatti, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – dhuranikkhepe…pe….

204. Where was the seventh pārājika for bhikkhunīs enacted? It was enacted at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. In what matter? The bhikkhunī Thullanandā followed the bhikkhu Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture trainer, who had been suspended by a united Saṅgha. In that matter. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: from the laying down of the burden...

205. Bhikkhunīnaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ pārājikaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo aṭṭhamaṃ vatthuṃ paripūresuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – dhuranikkhepe…pe….

205. Where was the eighth pārājika for bhikkhunīs enacted? It was enacted at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunīs of the group of six. In what matter? The bhikkhunīs of the group of six fulfilled the eighth item. In that matter. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: from the laying down of the burden...

Aṭṭha pārājikā niṭṭhitā.

The eight pārājikas are concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Methunādinnādānañca[T 0.0140][V 0.0111], manussaviggahuttari;

Kāyasaṃsaggaṃ chādeti, ukkhittā aṭṭha vatthukā;

Paññāpesi mahāvīro, chejjavatthū asaṃsayāti.

Sexual intercourse, taking what is not given, killing a human being, and claiming superior human attainments; bodily contact, concealing an offense, following a suspended monk, and the rule of eight items. The Great Hero laid down these grounds for expulsion without a doubt.

2. Saṅghādisesakaṇḍaṃ

2. 2. The Section on Saṅghādisesa

206. Yaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena ussayavādikāya bhikkhuniyā aḍḍaṃ karontiyā saṅghādiseso kattha paññatto? Kaṃ ārabbha? Kismiṃ vatthusmiṃ…pe… kenābhatanti?

206. That Saṅghādisesa training rule which was laid down by the Blessed One—the one who knows, the one who sees, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—for a bhikkhunī who disputes contentiously and creates a legal issue: where was it laid down? Concerning whom was it laid down? In what matter was it laid down? ... By whom was it brought?

207. Yaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena ussayavādikāya bhikkhuniyā aḍḍaṃ karontiyā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Thullanandā bhikkhunī ussayavādikā vihari, tasmiṃ [M 0.0100] vatthusmiṃ. Atthi tattha paññatti, anupaññatti, anuppannapaññattīti? Ekā paññatti. Anupaññatti anuppannapaññatti tasmiṃ natthi. Sabbatthapaññatti, padesapaññattīti? Sabbatthapaññatti. Sādhāraṇapaññatti, asādhāraṇapaññattīti? Asādhāraṇapaññatti. Ekatopaññatti, ubhatopaññattīti? Ekatopaññatti. Catunnaṃ pātimokkhuddesānaṃ katthogadhaṃ kattha pariyāpannanti? Nidānogadhaṃ nidānapariyāpannaṃ[T 0.0141]. Katamena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchatīti? Tatiyena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchati.
