Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Where was the pācittiya offense for giving the higher ordination to a married probationer who is fully twelve years old but has not completed her two-year training in the six rules laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning many bhikkhunīs. On what occasion? On the occasion when many bhikkhunīs gave the higher ordination to a married probationer who is fully twelve years old but has not completed her two-year training in the six rules. There is one original enactment. It arises from three of the six origins of offenses... etc.

Paripuṇṇadvādasavassaṃ gihigataṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ saṅghena asammataṃ vuṭṭhāpentiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇadvādasavassaṃ gihigataṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ saṅghena asammataṃ vuṭṭhāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Where was the pācittiya offense for giving the higher ordination to a married probationer who is fully twelve years old and has completed her two-year training in the six rules, but has not been approved by the Saṅgha laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning many bhikkhunīs. On what occasion? On the occasion when many bhikkhunīs gave the higher ordination to a married probationer who is fully twelve years old and has completed her two-year training in the six rules, but has not been approved by the Saṅgha. There is one original enactment. It arises from three of the six origins of offenses... etc.

Sahajīviniṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā dve vassāni neva anuggaṇhantiyā na anuggaṇhāpentiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Thullanandā bhikkhunī sahajīviniṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā dve vassāni neva anuggahesi na anuggaṇhāpesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – dhuranikkhepe…pe….

Where was the pācittiya offense for a bhikkhunī who, after giving the higher ordination to her co-resident disciple, for two years neither supports her nor has her supported laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. On what occasion? On the occasion when the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, after giving the higher ordination to her co-resident disciple, for two years neither supported her nor had her supported. There is one original enactment. It arises from one of the six origins of offenses: through neglect of duty... etc.

Vuṭṭhāpitaṃ [T 0.0170] pavattiniṃ dve vassāni nānubandhantiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ [V 0.0130] paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo vuṭṭhāpitaṃ pavattiniṃ dve vassāni nānubandhiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – paṭhamapārājike…pe….

Where was the pācittiya offense for a bhikkhunī who for two years does not attend upon the preceptor who gave her the higher ordination laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning many bhikkhunīs. On what occasion? On the occasion when many bhikkhunīs for two years did not attend upon the preceptors who gave them the higher ordination. There is one original enactment. It arises from one of the six origins of offenses—that of the first pārājika... etc.

Sahajīviniṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā neva vūpakāsentiyā na vūpakāsāpentiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Thullanandā bhikkhunī sahajīviniṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā neva vūpakāsesi na vūpakāsāpesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – dhuranikkhepe…pe….

Where was the pācittiya offense for a bhikkhunī who, after giving the higher ordination to her co-resident disciple, neither takes her away nor has her taken away laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. On what occasion? On the occasion when the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, after giving the higher ordination to her co-resident disciple, neither took her away nor had her taken away. There is one original enactment. It arises from one of the six origins of offenses: through neglect of duty... etc.

Gabbhinivaggo sattamo.

The Chapter on Pregnant Women, the Seventh.

8. Kumārībhūtavaggo

8. The Chapter on the Maiden.

225. Ūnavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ vuṭṭhāpentiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha[M 0.0119]. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo ūnavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ vuṭṭhāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

225. Where was the pācittiya offense for giving the higher ordination to a maiden who is under twenty years of age laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning many bhikkhunīs. On what occasion? On the occasion when many bhikkhunīs gave the higher ordination to a maiden who was under twenty years of age. There is one original enactment. It arises from three of the six origins of offenses... etc.

Paripuṇṇavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṃ vuṭṭhāpentiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ [T 0.0171] paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṃ vuṭṭhāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Where was the pācittiya offense for giving the higher ordination to a probationer who, being a maiden who has completed twenty years of age, has not trained for two years in the six rules laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning many bhikkhunīs. On what occasion? On the occasion when many bhikkhunīs gave the higher ordination to a probationer who, being a maiden who had completed twenty years of age, had not trained for two years in the six rules. There is one original enactment. It arises from three of the six origins of offenses... etc.

Paripuṇṇavīsativassaṃ [P 5.0068] kumāribhūtaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ saṅghena asammataṃ vuṭṭhāpentiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ saṅghena asammataṃ vuṭṭhāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Where was the pācittiya offense for giving the higher ordination to a probationer who, being a maiden who has completed twenty years of age and has trained for two years in the six rules, has not been approved by the Saṅgha laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning many bhikkhunīs. On what occasion? On the occasion when many bhikkhunīs gave the higher ordination to a probationer who, being a maiden who had completed twenty years of age and had trained for two years in the six rules, had not been approved by the Saṅgha. There is one original enactment. It arises from three of the six origins of offenses... etc.

Ūnadvādasavassāya [V 0.0131] vuṭṭhāpentiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo ūnadvādasavassā vuṭṭhāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Where was the pācittiya offense laid down for a bhikkhunī who ordains one who is under twelve years of age? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning many bhikkhunīs. In regard to what matter? Many bhikkhunīs ordained those who were under twelve years of age; in regard to that matter. There is one enactment. It arises from three of the six origins of offenses... and so on.

Paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya saṅghena asammatāya vuṭṭhāpentiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā [T 0.0172] bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇadvādasavassā saṅghena asammatā vuṭṭhāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – dutiyapārājike…pe….

Where was the pācittiya offense laid down for a bhikkhunī who ordains one who, having completed twelve years of age, has not been authorized by the Saṅgha? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning many bhikkhunīs. In regard to what matter? Many bhikkhunīs ordained those who, having completed twelve years of age, had not been authorized by the Saṅgha; in regard to that matter. There is one enactment. It arises from three of the six origins of offenses—as in the second pārājika... and so on.

“Alaṃ tāva te, ayye, vuṭṭhāpitenā”ti vuccamānāya “sādhū”ti paṭissuṇitvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṃ āpajjantiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Caṇḍakāḷiṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī “alaṃ tāva te, ayye, vuṭṭhāpitenā”ti vuccamānā [M 0.0120] “sādhū”ti paṭissuṇitvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṃ āpajji, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Where was the pācittiya offense laid down for a bhikkhunī who, when told, 'Venerable lady, let there be enough of your giving ordination for now,' having agreed by saying, 'Very well,' later falls into a state of criticism? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī. In regard to what matter? The bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī, when told, 'Venerable lady, let there be enough of your giving ordination for now,' having agreed by saying, 'Very well,' later fell into a state of criticism; in regard to that matter. There is one enactment. It arises from three of the six origins of offenses... and so on.

Sikkhamānaṃ – “sace me tvaṃ, ayye, cīvaraṃ dassasi, evāhaṃ taṃ vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti vatvā neva vuṭṭhāpentiyā na vuṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ karontiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Thullanandā bhikkhunī sikkhamānaṃ – “sace me tvaṃ, ayye, cīvaraṃ dassasi, evāhaṃ taṃ vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti vatvā neva vuṭṭhāpesi na vuṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ akāsi[V 0.0132], tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – dhuranikkhepe…pe….

Where was the pācittiya offense laid down for a bhikkhunī who, having said to a probationer, 'Venerable lady, if you give me a robe, then I will ordain you,' neither ordains her herself nor makes an effort for her ordination? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. In regard to what matter? The bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having said to a probationer, 'Venerable lady, if you give me a robe, then I will ordain you,' neither ordained her herself nor made an effort for her ordination; in regard to that matter. There is one enactment. It arises from one of the six origins of offenses—from laying down the burden... and so on.

Sikkhamānaṃ – “sace maṃ tvaṃ, ayye, dve vassāni anubandhissasi, evāhaṃ taṃ vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti vatvā neva vuṭṭhāpentiyā na vuṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ [T 0.0173] karontiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Thullanandā bhikkhunī sikkhamānaṃ – “sace maṃ tvaṃ, ayye, dve vassāni anubandhissasi, evāhaṃ taṃ vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti vatvā neva vuṭṭhāpesi na vuṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ akāsi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – dhuranikkhepe…pe….

Where was the pācittiya offense laid down for a bhikkhunī who, having said to a probationer, 'Venerable lady, if you attend on me for two years, then I will ordain you,' neither ordains her herself nor makes an effort for her ordination? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. In regard to what matter? The bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having said to a probationer, 'Venerable lady, if you attend on me for two years, then I will ordain you,' neither ordained her herself nor made an effort for her ordination; in regard to that matter. There is one enactment. It arises from one of the six origins of offenses—from laying down the burden... and so on.

Purisasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ kumārakasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ caṇḍiṃ sokāvāsaṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpentiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Thullanandā bhikkhunī purisasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ kumārakasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ caṇḍiṃ sokāvāsaṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Where was the pācittiya offense laid down for a bhikkhunī who ordains a probationer who associates with men, associates with young men, is harsh, and causes grief to men? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. In regard to what matter? The bhikkhunī Thullanandā ordained a probationer who associated with men, associated with young men, was harsh, and caused grief to men; in regard to that matter. There is one enactment. It arises from three of the six origins of offenses... and so on.

Mātāpitūhi vā sāmikena vā ananuññātaṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpentiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Thullanandā bhikkhunī mātāpitūhipi sāmikenāpi ananuññātaṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpesi[P 5.0069], tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ catūhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā vācato samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato na cittato; siyā kāyato ca vācato [M 0.0121] ca samuṭṭhāti, na cittato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na [T 0.0174] kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Where was the pācittiya offense laid down for a bhikkhunī who ordains a probationer not permitted by her parents or husband? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. In regard to what matter? The bhikkhunī Thullanandā ordained a probationer not permitted by her parents and also by her husband; in regard to that matter. There is one enactment. It arises from four of the six origins of offenses: it may arise from speech, not from body, not from mind; it may arise from body and speech, not from mind; it may arise from speech and mind, not from body; it may arise from body, speech, and mind... and so on.

Pārivāsikachandadānena sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpentiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Rājagahe paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Thullanandā bhikkhunī pārivāsikachandadānena sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Where was the pācittiya offense laid down for a bhikkhunī who ordains a probationer with an invalid declaration of consent? It was laid down at Rājagaha. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. In regard to what matter? The bhikkhunī Thullanandā ordained a probationer with an invalid declaration of consent; in regard to that matter. There is one enactment. It arises from three of the six origins of offenses... and so on.

Anuvassaṃ vuṭṭhāpentiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo anuvassaṃ vuṭṭhāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Where was the pācittiya offense laid down for a bhikkhunī who ordains every year? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning many bhikkhunīs. In regard to what matter? Many bhikkhunīs ordained every year; in regard to that matter. There is one enactment. It arises from three of the six origins of offenses... and so on.

Ekaṃ vassaṃ dve vuṭṭhāpentiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo ekaṃ [V 0.0133] vassaṃ dve vuṭṭhāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Where was the pācittiya laid down for a bhikkhunī who ordains two probationers in one year? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning many bhikkhunīs. In what case? Many bhikkhunīs ordained two probationers in one year; in that case. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins... and so on.

Kumārībhūtavaggo aṭṭhamo.

The Eighth Chapter on the Maiden is concluded.

9. Chattupāhanavaggo

9. The Chapter on Umbrellas and Footwear

226. Chattupāhanaṃ dhārentiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ [T 0.0175] paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo chattupāhanaṃ dhāresuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – eḷakalomake…pe….

226. Where was the pācittiya laid down for a bhikkhunī using an umbrella and footwear? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six bhikkhunīs. In what case? The group-of-six bhikkhunīs used an umbrella and footwear; in that case. There is one enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins—as in the Eḷakalomaka case…and so on.

Yānena yāyantiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo yānena yāyiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – eḷakalomake…pe….

Where was the pācittiya laid down for a bhikkhunī traveling by vehicle? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six bhikkhunīs. In what case? The group-of-six bhikkhunīs traveled by vehicle; in that case. There is one enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins—as in the Eḷakalomaka case…and so on.

Saṅghāṇiṃ [M 0.0122] dhārentiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Aññataraṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Aññatarā bhikkhunī saṅghāṇiṃ dhāresi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – eḷakalomake…pe….

Where was the pācittiya laid down for a bhikkhunī wearing a girdle? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning a certain bhikkhunī. In what case? A certain bhikkhunī wore a girdle; in that case. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins—as in the Eḷakalomaka case…and so on.

Itthālaṅkāraṃ dhārentiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo itthālaṅkāraṃ dhāresuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ [T 0.0176] dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – eḷakalomake…pe….

Where was the pācittiya laid down for a bhikkhunī wearing a woman’s adornment? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six bhikkhunīs. In what case? The group-of-six bhikkhunīs wore a woman’s adornment; in that case. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins—as in the Eḷakalomaka case…and so on.

Gandhavaṇṇakena nahāyantiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo gandhavaṇṇakena nahāyiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – eḷakalomake…pe….

Where was the pācittiya laid down for a bhikkhunī bathing with scented cosmetic paste? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six bhikkhunīs. In what case? The group-of-six bhikkhunīs bathed with scented cosmetic paste; in that case. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins—as in the Eḷakalomaka case…and so on.

Vāsitakena [V 0.0134] piññākena nahāyantiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo vāsitakena piññākena nahāyiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – eḷakalomake…pe….

Where was the pācittiya laid down for a bhikkhunī bathing with scented sesame flour? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six bhikkhunīs. In what case? The group-of-six bhikkhunīs bathed with scented sesame flour; in that case. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins—as in the Eḷakalomaka case…and so on.

Bhikkhuniyā ummaddāpentiyā parimaddāpentiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo bhikkhuniyā ummaddāpesuṃ parimaddāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – eḷakalomake…pe….

Where was the pācittiya laid down for a bhikkhunī who has another bhikkhunī rub or knead her? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning many bhikkhunīs. In what case? Many bhikkhunīs had another bhikkhunī rub and knead them; in that case. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins—as in the Eḷakalomaka case…and so on.

Sikkhamānā [P 5.0070] ummaddāpentiyā parimaddāpentiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahulā [T 0.0177] bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo sikkhamānāya ummaddāpesuṃ parimaddāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – eḷakalomake…pe….

Where was the pācittiya laid down for a bhikkhunī who has a female probationer rub or knead her? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning many bhikkhunīs. In what case? Many bhikkhunīs had a female probationer rub and knead them; in that case. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins—as in the Eḷakalomaka case…and so on.

Sāmaṇeriyā ummaddāpentiyā parimaddāpentiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha[M 0.0123]. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo sāmaṇeriyā ummaddāpesuṃ parimaddāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – eḷakalomake…pe….

Where was the pācittiya laid down for a bhikkhunī who has a female novice rub or knead her? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning many bhikkhunīs. In what case? Many bhikkhunīs had a female novice rub and knead them; in that case. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins—as in the Eḷakalomaka case…and so on.

Gihiniyā ummaddāpentiyā parimaddāpentiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo gihiniyā ummaddāpesuṃ parimaddāpesuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – eḷakalomake…pe….

Where was the pācittiya laid down for a bhikkhunī who has a laywoman rub or knead her? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning many bhikkhunīs. In what case? Many bhikkhunīs had a laywoman rub and knead them; in that case. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins—as in the Eḷakalomaka case…and so on.

Bhikkhussa purato anāpucchā āsane nisīdantiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo bhikkhussa purato anāpucchā āsane nisīdiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ[T 0.0178]. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – kathinake…pe….

Where was the pācittiya laid down for a bhikkhunī sitting on a seat in front of a bhikkhu without asking permission? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning many bhikkhunīs. In what case? Many bhikkhunīs sat on a seat in front of a bhikkhu without asking permission; in that case. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins—as in the Kathinaka case…and so on.

Anokāsakataṃ [V 0.0135] bhikkhuṃ pañhaṃ pucchantiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo anokāsakataṃ bhikkhuṃ pañhaṃ pucchiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – padasodhamme…pe….

Where was the pācittiya offense for a bhikkhunī who asks a question of a bhikkhu who has not given permission laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning many bhikkhunīs. In what matter was it laid down? Many bhikkhunīs asked a question of a bhikkhu who had not given permission; in that matter, it was laid down. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins: it is a padasodhamma offense... and so on.

Asaṅkaccikāya asaṅkacchikāya (syā.) gāmaṃ pavisantiyā pācittiyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Aññataraṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Aññatarā bhikkhunī asaṅkaccikā gāmaṃ pāvisi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato samuṭṭhāti, na vācato na cittato; siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe….

Regarding the pācittiya offense for a bhikkhunī entering a village without a breast-cloth, where was it laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning a certain bhikkhunī. In what case was it laid down? A certain bhikkhunī entered a village without a breast-cloth; in that case, it was laid down. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins: sometimes it arises from the body, not from speech, not from mind; sometimes it arises from the body and from the mind, not from speech... and so on.

Chattupāhanavaggo navamo.

The ninth, the Chapter on the Umbrella and Footwear.

Navavaggakhuddakā niṭṭhitā.

The nine minor chapters are concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof is:

Lasuṇaṃ [M 0.0124] saṃhare lomaṃ, talamaṭṭhañca suddhikaṃ;

Bhuñjantāmakadhaññānaṃ, dve vighāsena dassanā.

The Lasuṇa rule, the Lomasaṃharaṇa rule, the Talaghātaka and Jatumaddhaka rules, the Udakasuddhi rule, the Bhuñjanta and Āmakadhañña rules, the two Vighāsa rules, and the Giraggasamajja rule marked by 'dassanā'.

Andhakāre [T 0.0179] paṭicchanne, ajjhokāse rathikāya ca;

Pure pacchā vikāle ca, duggahi niraye vadhi.

The Rattandhakāra rule, the Paṭicchanna rule, the Ajjhokāsa rule, and the Rathika rule; the Purebhatta, Pacchābhatta, and Vikāla rules; the Paraṃujjhāpana rule marked by 'duggahita', the Abhisapana rule marked by 'nirayena', and the Vadhitvā Rodana rule.

Naggodakā visibbetvā, pañcāhikaṃ saṅkamanīyaṃ;

Gaṇaṃ vibhaṅgasamaṇaṃ, dubbalaṃ kathinena ca.

The Nagga and Udakasāṭika rules, the Cīvarasibbana rule marked by 'visibbetvā', the Pañcāhika rule, the Cīvarasaṅkamanīya rule, the Gaṇacīvaralābha rule, the Cīvaravibhaṅga rule, the Samaṇacīvaradāna rule, the Dubbalacīvarapaccāsā rule, and the Kathinuddhāra rule.

Ekamañcattharaṇena, sañcicca sahajīvinī;

Datvā saṃsaṭṭhaanto ca, tirovassaṃ na pakkame.

The first and second Tuvaṭṭa rules, the Aphāsukaraṇa rule marked by 'sañcicca', the Dukkhitasahajīvinī rule, the Upassayadāna rule marked by 'datvā', the Saṃsaṭṭha rule, the Antoraṭṭha rule, the Tiroraṭṭha rule, the Antovassa rule, and the Na Pakkama rule.

Rājā āsandi suttañca, gihi vūpasamena ca;

Dade cīvarāvasathaṃ, pariyāpuṇañca vācaye.

The Cittāgāra rule marked by 'rāja', the Āsandī rule, the Suttakantana rule, the Gihiveyyāvacca rule, the Na Vūpasamana rule, the Āgārika rule marked by 'dade', the first and second Āvasatha rules, the Pariyāpuṇana rule, and the Vācana rule.

Ārāmakkosacaṇḍī [V 0.0136] ca, bhuñjeyya kulamaccharī;

Vāse pavāraṇovādaṃ, dve dhammā pasākhena ca.

The Ārāma rule, the Akkosana rule, the Caṇḍīkata rule, the Aññatrabhunjana rule, the Kulamaccharī rule, the Abhikkhukavāsa rule, the Na Pavāraṇa rule, the Ovāda rule, the Dvedhamma rule, and the Pasākha rule.

Gabbhī pāyantī cha dhamme, asammatūnadvādasa;

Paripuṇṇañca [P 5.0071] saṅghena, saha vuṭṭhā cha pañca ca.

The Gabbhinī rule, the Pāyantī rule, the Dvevassa rule, the Saṅghena Asammata rule, the first Gihigata rule, the second Gihigata rule, the third Gihigata rule, the first Sahajīvinī rule, the Vuṭṭhāpita rule, and the Cha Pañca Yojana rule.

Kumārī dve ca saṅghena, dvādasa sammatena ca;

Alaṃ sace ca dvevassaṃ, saṃsaṭṭhā sāmikena ca.

The two Kumārībhūta rules, the third Kumārībhūta rule, the Ūnadvādasavassa rule, the Paripuṇṇadvādasavassa rule, the Alaṃ Tāva rule, the Cīvara rule, the Dvevassa rule, the Purisasaṃsaṭṭha rule, and the Ananujñāta rule.

Pārivāsikānuvassaṃ, duve vuṭṭhāpanena ca;

Chattayānena saṅghāṇi, itthālaṅkāravaṇṇake.

The Pārivāsika Chandadāna rule, the Anuvassavuṭṭhāpana rule, the Dve Vuṭṭhāpana rule, the Chattupāhana rule, the Yāna rule, the Saṅghāṇi rule, the Itthālaṅkāra rule, and the Gandhavannaka rule.

Piññākabhikkhunī ceva, sikkhā ca sāmaṇerikā;

Gihi bhikkhussa purato, anokāsaṃ saṅkaccikāti.

The Vāsitapiññāka rule, the Bhikkhunī-ummaddana rule, the Sikkhamāna-ummaddana rule, the Sāmaṇerī-ummaddana rule, the Gihī-ummaddana rule, the Bhikkhussapurato rule, the Anokāsakatapañha rule, and the Asaṅkaccika rule. This is the summary of the training rules.

Tesaṃ vaggānaṃ uddānaṃ –

The summary of those chapters is:

Lasuṇandhakārā nhānā, tuvaṭṭā cittagārakā;

Ārāmaṃ [T 0.0180] gabbhinī ceva, kumārī chattupāhanāti.

The Lasuṇa Chapter, the Rattandhakāra Chapter, the Nahāna Chapter, the Tuvaṭṭa Chapter, the Cittagāra Chapter, the Ārāma Chapter, the Gabbhinī Chapter, the Kumārībhūta Chapter, and the Chattupāhana Chapter. This is the conclusion of the summary of chapters.

5. Pāṭidesanīyakaṇḍaṃ

5. 5. The Section on Offenses to be Confessed

227. Sappiṃ [M 0.0125] viññāpetvā bhuñjantiyā pāṭidesanīyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo sappiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ catūhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

227. Regarding the offense to be confessed for a bhikkhunī who, having requested ghee, eats it, where was it laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the bhikkhunīs of the group of six. In what case was it laid down? The bhikkhunīs of the group of six, having requested ghee, ate it; in that case, it was laid down. There is one original enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from four origins... and so on.

Telaṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantiyā pāṭidesanīyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo telaṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ catūhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Regarding the offense to be confessed for a bhikkhunī who, having requested oil, eats it, where was it laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the bhikkhunīs of the group of six. In what case was it laid down? The bhikkhunīs of the group of six, having requested oil, ate it; in that case, it was laid down. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from four origins... and so on.

Madhuṃ [V 0.0137] viññāpetvā bhuñjantiyā pāṭidesanīyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo madhuṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ catūhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Regarding the offense to be confessed for a bhikkhunī who, having requested honey, eats it, where was it laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the bhikkhunīs of the group of six. In what case was it laid down? The bhikkhunīs of the group of six, having requested honey, ate it; in that case, it was laid down. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from four origins... and so on.

Phāṇitaṃ [T 0.0181] viññāpetvā bhuñjantiyā pāṭidesanīyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo phāṇitaṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ catūhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Regarding the offense to be confessed for a bhikkhunī who, having requested molasses, eats it, where was it laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the bhikkhunīs of the group of six. In what case was it laid down? The bhikkhunīs of the group of six, having requested molasses, ate it; in that case, it was laid down. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from four origins... and so on.

Macchaṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantiyā pāṭidesanīyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo macchaṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ catūhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Regarding the offense to be confessed for a bhikkhunī who, having requested fish, eats it, where was it laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the bhikkhunīs of the group of six. In what case was it laid down? The bhikkhunīs of the group of six, having requested fish, ate it; in that case, it was laid down. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from four origins... and so on.

Maṃsaṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantiyā pāṭidesanīyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo. Maṃsaṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ catūhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Regarding the offense to be confessed for a bhikkhunī who, having requested meat, eats it, where was it laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the bhikkhunīs of the group of six. In what case was it laid down? The bhikkhunīs of the group of six, having requested meat, ate it; in that case, it was laid down. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from four origins... and so on.

Khīraṃ [M 0.0126] viññāpetvā bhuñjantiyā pāṭidesanīyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo [T 0.0182] ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo khīraṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ catūhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Regarding the Pāṭidesanīya for a bhikkhunī who, having requested milk, eats it, where was it laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the bhikkhunīs of the group of six. In what case was it laid down? The bhikkhunīs of the group of six, having requested milk, ate it; in that case, it was laid down. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from four origins... and so on.

Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantiyā pāṭidesanīyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ catūhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato samuṭṭhāti, na vācato na cittato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca samuṭṭhāti, na cittato; siyā [V 0.0138] kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Regarding the Pāṭidesanīya for a bhikkhunī who, having requested curds, eats them, where was it laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom was it laid down? It was laid down concerning the bhikkhunīs of the group of six. In what case was it laid down? The bhikkhunīs of the group of six, having requested curds, ate them; in that case, it was laid down. There is one original enactment and one supplementary enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from four origins: sometimes it arises from the body, not from speech, not from the mind; sometimes it arises from the body and from speech, not from the mind; sometimes it arises from the body and from the mind, not from speech; sometimes it arises from the body, from speech, and from the mind…and so on.

Aṭṭha pāṭidesanīyā niṭṭhitā.

The eight Pāṭidesanīya offenses are concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Sappiṃ telaṃ madhuñceva, phāṇitaṃ macchameva ca;

Maṃsaṃ khīraṃ dadhiñcāpi, viññāpetvāna bhikkhunī;

Pāṭidesanīyā aṭṭha, sayaṃ buddhena desitāti.

Ghee, oil, and honey, molasses, and fish as well; meat, milk, and also curds—for a bhikkhunī having requested these, the eight Pāṭidesanīya rules were taught by the Buddha himself.

Ye sikkhāpadā bhikkhuvibhaṅge vitthāritā te saṃkhittā

The training rules that were detailed in the Bhikkhuvibhaṅga are summarized

Bhikkhunivibhaṅge.

in the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga.

Katthapaññattivāro niṭṭhito paṭhamo.

The first section on where the rules were laid down is concluded.

2. Katāpattivāro

2. 2. The Section on Committed Offenses

1. Pārājikakaṇḍaṃ

1. 1. The Pārājika Chapter

228. Avassutā [T 0.0183][V 0.0139] bhikkhunī avassutassa purisapuggalassa kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyantī kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Avassutā bhikkhunī avassutassa purisapuggalassa kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyantī [P 5.0072] tisso āpattiyo āpajjati[M 0.0127]. Adhakkhakaṃ ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalaṃ gahaṇaṃ sādiyati, āpatti pārājikassa; ubbhakkhakaṃ adhojāṇumaṇḍalaṃ gahaṇaṃ sādiyati, āpatti thullaccayassa; kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ gahaṇaṃ sādiyati, āpatti dukkaṭassa – avassutā bhikkhunī avassutassa purisapuggalassa kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyantī imā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati.

228. A bhikkhunī who is sullied by lust, consenting to physical contact with a male person who is sullied by lust—how many offenses does she fall into? A bhikkhunī who is sullied by lust, consenting to physical contact with a male person who is sullied by lust, falls into three offenses. If she consents to being grasped below the collarbones and above the kneecaps, she falls into an offense of Pārājika; if she consents to being grasped above the collarbones and below the kneecaps, she falls into an offense of Thullaccaya; if she consents to the grasping of what is connected to the body, she falls into an offense of Dukkaṭa. A bhikkhunī who is sullied by lust, consenting to physical contact with a male person who is sullied by lust, falls into these three offenses.

Vajjappaṭicchādikā bhikkhunī vajjaṃ paṭicchādentī kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Vajjappaṭicchādikā bhikkhunī vajjaṃ paṭicchādentī tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Jānaṃ pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicchādeti, āpatti pārājikassa; vematikā paṭicchādeti, āpatti thullaccayassa; ācāravipattiṃ paṭicchādeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa – vajjappaṭicchādikā bhikkhunī vajjaṃ paṭicchādentī imā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati.

A bhikkhunī who conceals a fault, by concealing a fault—how many offenses does she fall into? A bhikkhunī who conceals a fault, by concealing a fault, falls into three offenses. If, knowing, she conceals a Pārājika offense, she falls into an offense of Pārājika; if, being in doubt, she conceals it, she falls into an offense of Thullaccaya; if she conceals a failure in conduct, she falls into an offense of Dukkaṭa. A bhikkhunī who conceals a fault, by concealing a fault, falls into these three offenses.

Ukkhittānuvattikā bhikkhunī yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjantī kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Ukkhittānuvattikā bhikkhunī yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjantī tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā; kammavācāpariyosāne [T 0.0184] āpatti pārājikassa – ukkhittānuvattikā bhikkhunī yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjantī imā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati.

A bhikkhunī who follows one who has been suspended, not relinquishing that view when being admonished up to the third time—how many offenses does she fall into? A bhikkhunī who follows one who has been suspended, not relinquishing that view when being admonished up to the third time, falls into three offenses. By the motion, she falls into an offense of Dukkaṭa; by the two formal acts, offenses of Thullaccaya; at the conclusion of the formal act, she falls into an offense of Pārājika. A bhikkhunī who follows one who has been suspended, not relinquishing that view when being admonished up to the third time, falls into these three offenses.

Aṭṭhamaṃ vatthuṃ paripūrentī kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Aṭṭhamaṃ vatthuṃ paripūrentī tisso āpattiyo [V 0.0140] āpajjati. Purisena – “itthannāmaṃ okāsaṃ itthannāmaṃ gahanaṃ (sī.), itthannāmaṃ gabbhaṃ (syā.) āgacchā”ti vuttā gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa; purisassa hatthapāsaṃ okkantamatte āpatti thullaccayassa; aṭṭhamaṃ vatthuṃ paripūreti, āpatti pārājikassa – aṭṭhamaṃ vatthuṃ paripūrentī imā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati.

A bhikkhunī who is fulfilling the eighth matter, into how many offenses does she fall? A bhikkhunī who is fulfilling the eighth matter falls into three offenses. When, having been told by a man, 'Come to such and such a place,' she goes, she falls into an offense of Dukkaṭa. Merely upon entering the arm's reach of the man, she falls into an offense of Thullaccaya. When she fulfills the eighth matter, she falls into an offense of Pārājika. A bhikkhunī who is fulfilling the eighth matter falls into these three offenses.

Pārājikā niṭṭhitā.

The Pārājikas are concluded.

2. Saṅghādisesakaṇḍaṃ

2. 2. The Saṅghādisesa Section

229. Ussayavādikā bhikkhunī aḍḍaṃ karontī tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekassa āroceti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; dutiyassa āroceti, [M 0.0128] āpatti thullaccayassa; aḍḍapariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

229. A contentious bhikkhunī, while making a legal case, falls into three offenses. If she informs one person, she falls into an offense of Dukkaṭa; if she informs a second person, she falls into an offense of Thullaccaya; at the conclusion of the legal case, she falls into an offense of Saṅghādisesa.

Coriṃ vuṭṭhāpentī tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

A bhikkhunī who ordains a female thief falls into three offenses. By the motion, she falls into an offense of Dukkaṭa; by the two formal acts, offenses of Thullaccaya; at the conclusion of the formal act, she falls into an offense of Saṅghādisesa.

Ekā gāmantaraṃ gacchantī tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa; paṭhamaṃ pādaṃ parikkhepaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti thullaccayassa; dutiyaṃ pādaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti saṅghādisesassa[T 0.0185].

A bhikkhunī who goes alone to another village falls into three offenses. If she goes, she falls into an offense of Dukkaṭa; if she crosses the boundary with the first foot, she falls into an offense of Thullaccaya; if she crosses with the second foot, she falls into an offense of Saṅghādisesa.

Samaggena saṅghena ukkhittaṃ bhikkhuniṃ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena anapaloketvā kārakasaṅghaṃ anaññāya gaṇassa chandaṃ osārentī tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

A bhikkhunī who, without consulting the acting Saṅgha and without knowing the assembly's consent, reinstates a bhikkhunī who has been expelled by a unanimous Saṅgha in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction, falls into three offenses. By the motion, she falls into an offense of Dukkaṭa; by the two formal acts, offenses of Thullaccaya; at the conclusion of the formal act, she falls into an offense of Saṅghādisesa.

Avassutā bhikkhunī avassutassa purisapuggalassa hatthato khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā bhuñjantī [P 5.0073] tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. “Khādissāmi bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti thullaccayassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti saṅghādisesassa; udakadantaponaṃ paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

A lustful bhikkhunī who, with her own hand, receives and eats chewable or edible food from the hand of a lustful man, falls into three offenses. If she receives it thinking, “I will chew, I will eat,” she falls into an offense of Thullaccaya; with every swallow, she falls into an offense of Saṅghādisesa; if she receives water and a tooth-stick, she falls into an offense of Dukkaṭa.

“Kiṃ te, ayye, eso purisapuggalo karissati avassuto vā anavassuto vā, yato tvaṃ [V 0.0141] anavassutā! Iṅgha, ayye, yaṃ te eso purisapuggalo deti khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā, taṃ tvaṃ sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khāda vā bhuñja vā”ti uyyojentī tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Tassā vacanena khādissāmi bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti thullaccayassa; bhojanapariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

A bhikkhunī who encourages another by saying, “Venerable lady, what can this man do to you, whether he is lustful or not, since you are not lustful? Come now, venerable lady, whatever chewable or staple food this man gives you, receive it with your own hand and chew or eat it,” incurs three offenses. If, by her words, the other bhikkhunī receives it with the intention, “I will chew, I will eat,” it is a dukkaṭa offense; with every swallow, it is a thullaccaya offense; at the conclusion of eating, it is a saṅghādisesa offense.

Kupitā bhikkhunī yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjantī tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā[T 0.0186]; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

An angry bhikkhunī who does not abandon her view when admonished up to the third time incurs three offenses. By the motion, a dukkaṭa offense; by the two formal acts, thullaccaya offenses; at the conclusion of the formal act, a saṅghādisesa offense.

Kismiñcideva adhikaraṇe paccākatā bhikkhunī yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjantī tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; [M 0.0129] dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

A bhikkhunī who has been defeated in some legal issue and does not abandon her view when admonished up to the third time incurs three offenses. By the motion, a dukkaṭa offense; by the two formal acts, thullaccaya offenses; at the conclusion of the formal act, a saṅghādisesa offense.

Saṃsaṭṭhā bhikkhuniyo yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjantiyo tisso āpattiyo āpajjanti. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

Bhikkhunīs who associate with laypeople and do not abandon their view when admonished up to the third time incur three offenses. By the motion, a dukkaṭa offense; by the two formal acts, thullaccaya offenses; at the conclusion of the formal act, a saṅghādisesa offense.

“Saṃsaṭṭhāva, ayye, tumhe viharatha. Mā tumhe nānā viharitthā”ti uyyojentī yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjantī tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

A bhikkhunī who encourages others by saying, “Venerable ladies, you should dwell associating with laypeople. Do not dwell separately,” and does not abandon her view when admonished up to the third time, incurs three offenses. By the motion, a dukkaṭa offense; by the two formal acts, thullaccaya offenses; at the conclusion of the formal act, a saṅghādisesa offense.

Saṅghādisesā niṭṭhitā.

The Saṅghādisesa rules are concluded.

3. Nissaggiyakaṇḍaṃ

3. The Chapter on Forfeiture

230. Pattasannicayaṃ karontī ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

230. A bhikkhunī who accumulates bowls incurs one offense: a pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture.

Akālacīvaraṃ “kālacīvara”nti adhiṭṭhahitvā bhājāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhājāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; bhājāpite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhunī who, having determined an out-of-season robe to be an 'in-season robe,' has it distributed, incurs two offenses. In the effort of having it distributed, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been distributed, there is a pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture.

Bhikkhuniyā [V 0.0142] saddhiṃ cīvaraṃ parivattetvā acchindantī dve āpattiyo [T 0.0187] āpajjati. Acchindati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; acchinne nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhunī who, having exchanged a robe with another bhikkhunī, takes it away by force, incurs two offenses. In the effort of taking it away, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been taken away, there is a pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture.

Aññaṃ viññāpetvā aññaṃ viññāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Viññāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; viññāpite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhunī who, having requested one thing, then requests another, incurs two offenses. In the effort of requesting, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been requested, there is a pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture.

Aññaṃ cetāpetvā aññaṃ cetāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Cetāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; cetāpite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhunī who, having had one thing procured, then has another procured, incurs two offenses. In the effort of having it procured, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been procured, there is a pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture.

Aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena saṅghikena aññaṃ cetāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Cetāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; cetāpite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhunī who has something else procured with a requisite belonging to the Saṅgha that was intended for a different purpose, incurs two offenses. In the effort of having it procured, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been procured, there is a pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture.

Aññadatthike [M 0.0130] parikkhārena aññuddisikena saṅghikena saṃyācikena aññaṃ cetāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Cetāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; cetāpite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhunī who has something else procured with a requisite belonging to the Saṅgha, obtained by request, that was intended for a different purpose, incurs two offenses. In the effort of having it procured, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been procured, there is a pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture.

Aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena mahājanikena aññaṃ cetāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Cetāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; cetāpite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhunī who has something else procured with a requisite belonging to a group that was intended for a different purpose, incurs two offenses. In the effort of having it procured, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been procured, there is a pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture.

Aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena mahājanikena saṃyācikena aññaṃ cetāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Cetāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; cetāpite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhunī who has something else procured with a requisite belonging to a group, obtained by request, that was intended for a different purpose, incurs two offenses. In the effort of having it procured, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been procured, there is a pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture.

Aññadatthikena [T 0.0188] parikkhārena aññuddisike [P 5.0074] puggalikena saṃyācikena aññaṃ cetāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Cetāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; cetāpite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhunī who has something else procured with a personal requisite, obtained by request, that was intended for a different purpose, incurs two offenses. In the effort of having it procured, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been procured, there is a pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture.

Atirekacatukkaṃsaparamaṃ garupāvuraṇaṃ cetāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Cetāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; cetāpite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhunī who has a heavy cloak procured for a price exceeding the maximum of four kaṃsas, incurs two offenses. In the effort of having it procured, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been procured, there is a pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture.

Atirekaaḍḍhateyyakaṃsaparamaṃ lahupāvuraṇaṃ cetāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Cetāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; cetāpite nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhunī who has a light cloak procured for a price exceeding the maximum of two and a half kaṃsas, incurs two offenses. In the effort of having it procured, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been procured, there is a pācittiya offense requiring forfeiture.

Nissaggiyā pācittiyā niṭṭhitā.

The pācittiya offenses requiring forfeiture are concluded.

4. Pācittiyakaṇḍaṃ

4. The Section on Offenses Entailing Expiation

1. Lasuṇavaggo

1. The Chapter on Garlic

231. Lasuṇaṃ [V 0.0143] khādantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Khādissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

231. A bhikkhunī who eats garlic incurs two offenses. If she accepts it thinking, 'I will eat it,' there is an offense of wrong conduct; for every mouthful she swallows, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Sambādhe lomaṃ saṃharāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Saṃharāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; saṃharāpite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who has hair removed in a private area incurs two offenses. In the effort of having it removed, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been removed, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Talaghātakaṃ [M 0.0131] karontī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Karoti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; kate āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who strikes her urinary passage incurs two offenses. In the effort of doing so, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been done, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Jatumaṭṭhakaṃ ādiyantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Ādiyati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ, ādinne āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who uses a lacquered stick incurs two offenses. In the effort of using it, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been used, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Atirekadvaṅgulapabbaparamaṃ udakasuddhikaṃ ādiyantī dve āpattiyo [T 0.0189] āpajjati. Ādiyati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; ādinne āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who performs a water-cleansing to a depth of more than two finger-joints incurs two offenses. In the effort of doing so, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been done, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Bhikkhussa bhuñjantassa pānīyena vā vidhūpanena vā upatiṭṭhantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Hatthapāse tiṭṭhati, āpatti pācittiyassa; hatthapāsaṃ vijahitvā tiṭṭhati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

A bhikkhunī who attends to a bhikkhu while he is eating, with drinking water or a fan, incurs two offenses. If she stands within arm's reach, there is an offense entailing expiation; if she stands beyond arm's reach, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

Āmakadhaññaṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who, having requested raw grain, eats it, incurs two offenses. If she accepts it thinking, 'I will eat it,' there is an offense of wrong conduct; for every mouthful she swallows, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā saṅkāraṃ vā vighāsaṃ vā tirokuṭṭe vā tiropākāre vā chaḍḍentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Chaḍḍeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; chaḍḍite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who disposes of feces, urine, refuse, or leftover food on the other side of a wall or a fence incurs two offenses. In the effort of disposing, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been disposed of, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā saṅkāraṃ vā vighāsaṃ vā harite chaḍḍentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Chaḍḍeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; chaḍḍite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who disposes of feces, urine, refuse, or leftover food on green vegetation incurs two offenses. In the effort of disposing, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been disposed of, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Naccaṃ [V 0.0144] vā gītaṃ vā vāditaṃ vā dassanāya gacchantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa; yattha ṭhitā passati vā suṇāti vā, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who goes to see dancing, singing, or instrumental music incurs two offenses. For going, there is an offense of wrong conduct; wherever she stands and sees or hears it, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Lasuṇavaggo paṭhamo.

The first chapter, on garlic, is concluded.

2. Rattandhakāravaggo

2. The Chapter on Darkness at Night

232. Rattandhakāre appadīpe purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭhantī [T 0.0190] dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Hatthapāse tiṭṭhati, āpatti pācittiyassa; hatthapāsaṃ vijahitvā tiṭṭhati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

232. A bhikkhunī who stands one-on-one with a man in the darkness of night where there is no lamp incurs two offenses. If she stands within arm's reach, there is an offense entailing expiation; if she stands beyond arm's reach, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

Paṭicchanne [M 0.0132] okāse purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭhantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Hatthapāse tiṭṭhati, āpatti pācittiyassa; hatthapāsaṃ vijahitvā tiṭṭhati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

A bhikkhunī who stands one-on-one with a man in a concealed place incurs two offenses. If she stands within arm's reach, there is an offense entailing expiation; if she stands beyond arm's reach, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

Ajjhokāse [P 5.0075] purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭhantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Hatthapāse tiṭṭhati, āpatti pācittiyassa; hatthapāsaṃ vijahitvā tiṭṭhati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

A bhikkhunī who stands one-on-one with a man in an open space incurs two offenses. If she stands within arm's reach, there is an offense entailing expiation; if she stands beyond arm's reach, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

Rathikāya vā byūhe vā siṅghāṭake vā purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā santiṭṭhantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Hatthapāse tiṭṭhati, āpatti pācittiyassa; hatthapāsaṃ vijahitvā tiṭṭhati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

A bhikkhunī who stands one-on-one with a man on a main road, a side road, or at a crossroads incurs two offenses. If she stands within arm's reach, there is an offense entailing expiation; if she stands beyond arm's reach, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

Purebhattaṃ kulāni upasaṅkamitvā āsane nisīditvā sāmike anāpucchā pakkamantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paṭhamaṃ pādaṃ anovassakaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; dutiyaṃ pādaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who, having approached families before the meal and sat on a seat, departs without taking leave of the owners, incurs two offenses. When she moves the first foot beyond the area covered by the eaves, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when she moves the second foot beyond, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Pacchābhattaṃ kulāni upasaṅkamitvā sāmike anāpucchā āsane nisīdantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Nisīdati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; nisinne āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who, having approached families after the meal, sits on a seat without taking leave of the owners, incurs two offenses. In the effort of sitting, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when she is seated, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Vikāle [T 0.0191] kulāni upasaṅkamitvā sāmike anāpucchā seyyaṃ santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā abhinisīdantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Abhinisīdati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; abhinisinne āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who, having approached families at the wrong time and without taking leave of the owners, either prepares a lodging or has one prepared, and then sits or lies down, incurs two offenses. In the effort of sitting or lying down, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when she has sat or lain down, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Duggahitena [V 0.0145] dūpadhāritena paraṃ ujjhāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Ujjhāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; ujjhāpite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who criticizes another on the basis of something poorly grasped or poorly remembered incurs two offenses. In the effort of criticizing, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when the criticism has been made, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Attānaṃ vā paraṃ vā nirayena vā brahmacariyena vā abhisapantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Abhisapati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; abhisapite āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who curses herself or another with hell or with the holy life incurs two offenses. In the effort of cursing, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when the curse has been made, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Attānaṃ vadhitvā vadhitvā rodantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vadhati rodati, āpatti pācittiyassa; vadhati na rodati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

A bhikkhunī who, striking herself repeatedly, weeps, incurs two offenses. If she strikes herself and weeps, there is an offense entailing expiation; if she strikes herself but does not weep, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

Rattandhakāravaggo dutiyo.

The second chapter, on darkness at night, is concluded.

3. Nahānavaggo

3. The Chapter on Bathing

233. Naggā [M 0.0133] nahāyantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Nahāyati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; nahānapariyosāne āpatti pācittiyassa.

233. A bhikkhunī who bathes naked incurs two offenses. In the effort of bathing, there is an offense of wrong conduct; at the conclusion of bathing, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Pamāṇātikkantaṃ udakasāṭikaṃ kārāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Kārāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; kārāpite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who has a bathing cloth that exceeds the standard measurement made incurs two offenses. In the effort of having it made, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been made, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ visibbetvā vā visibbāpetvā vā neva [T 0.0192] sibbentī na sibbāpanāya ussukkaṃ karontī ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhunī who, having unstitched another bhikkhunī's robe herself or having had it unstitched, neither sews it again nor makes an effort to have it sewn, incurs a single offense entailing expiation.

Pañcāhikaṃ saṅghāṭicāraṃ atikkāmentī ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Pācittiyaṃ. Cīvarasaṅkamanīyaṃ dhārentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Dhāreti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; dhārite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who is separated from her set of robes for more than five days incurs a single offense entailing expiation. A bhikkhunī who wears a robe belonging to another without permission incurs two offenses. In the effort of wearing it, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been worn, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Gaṇassa cīvaralābhaṃ antarāyaṃ karontī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Karoti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; kate, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who creates an obstacle to the community's gain of robes incurs two offenses. In the effort of doing so, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been done, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Dhammikaṃ [V 0.0146] cīvaravibhaṅgaṃ paṭibāhantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paṭibāhati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; paṭibāhite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who obstructs a lawful distribution of robes incurs two offenses. In the effort of obstructing, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been obstructed, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Agārikassa vā paribbājakassa vā paribbājikāya vā samaṇacīvaraṃ dentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Deti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; dinne, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who gives a recluse's robe to a householder, a male wanderer, or a female wanderer incurs two offenses. In the effort of giving, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been given, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Dubbalacīvarapaccāsā [P 5.0076] cīvarakālasamayaṃ atikkāmentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Atikkāmeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; atikkāmite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who, hoping for a better robe, lets the robe-making season pass incurs two offenses. In the effort of letting it pass, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has passed, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Dhammikaṃ kathinuddhāraṃ paṭibāhantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paṭibāhati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; paṭibāhite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who obstructs a lawful withdrawal of the kathina privilege incurs two offenses. In the effort of obstructing, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been obstructed, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Nahānavaggo tatiyo.

The third chapter, on bathing, is concluded.

4. Tuvaṭṭavaggo

4. The Chapter on Lying Down Together

234. Dve [T 0.0193][M 0.0134] bhikkhuniyo ekamañce tuvaṭṭentiyo dve āpattiyo āpajjanti. Nipajjanti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; nipanne, āpatti pācittiyassa.

234. Two bhikkhunīs who lie down together on one bed incur two offenses. In the effort of lying down, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when they have lain down, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Dve bhikkhuniyo ekattharaṇapāvuraṇā tuvaṭṭentiyo dve āpattiyo āpajjanti. Nipajjanti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; nipanne, āpatti pācittiyassa.

Two bhikkhunīs who lie down together with a single ground-sheet and covering incur two offenses. In the effort of lying down, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when they have lain down, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Bhikkhuniyā sañcicca aphāsuṃ karontī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Karoti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; kate, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who intentionally causes discomfort to another bhikkhunī incurs two offenses. In the effort of causing it, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when it has been caused, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Dukkhitaṃ sahajīviniṃ neva upaṭṭhentī na upaṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ karontī ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhunī who neither attends to an afflicted co-resident pupil herself, nor makes an effort to have her attended to, incurs a single offense entailing expiation.

Bhikkhuniyā upassayaṃ datvā kupitā anattamanā nikkaḍḍhantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Nikkaḍḍhati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; nikkaḍḍhite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who, having given a dwelling to another bhikkhunī, becomes angry and displeased and evicts her, incurs two offenses. In the effort of evicting her, there is an offense of wrong conduct; when she has been evicted, there is an offense entailing expiation.

Saṃsaṭṭhā [V 0.0147] bhikkhunī yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who associates with laypeople and does not relinquish this after being admonished up to the third time incurs two offenses. At the end of the motion, there is an offense of wrong-doing; at the conclusion of the formal act, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Antoraṭṭhe sāsaṅkasammate sappaṭibhaye asatthikā cārikaṃ carantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paṭipajjati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; paṭipanne, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who travels on a journey without a companion in a region within the country acknowledged as dangerous and perilous incurs two offenses. Should she set out, in the effort, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when she has set out, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Tiroraṭṭhe [T 0.0194] sāsaṅkasammate sappaṭibhaye asatthikā cārikaṃ carantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paṭipajjati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; paṭipanne, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who travels on a journey without a companion in a region outside the country acknowledged as dangerous and perilous incurs two offenses. Should she set out, in the effort, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when she has set out, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Antovassaṃ cārikaṃ carantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paṭipajjati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; paṭipanne, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who travels on a journey during the rains-residence incurs two offenses. Should she set out, in the effort, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when she has set out, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Vassaṃvuṭṭhā bhikkhunī cārikaṃ na pakkamantī ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhunī who has completed the rains-residence but does not set out on a journey incurs one offense: a pācittiya.

Tuvaṭṭavaggo catuttho.

The Fourth Chapter: The Tuvaṭṭa Chapter.

5. Cittāgāravaggo

5. The Chapter on the Painted Rest House.

235. Rājāgāraṃ [M 0.0135] vā cittāgāraṃ vā ārāmaṃ vā uyyānaṃ vā pokkharaṇiṃ vā dassanāya gacchantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa; yattha ṭhitā passati, āpatti pācittiyassa.

235. A bhikkhunī who goes for the purpose of seeing a king's recreational house, or a recreational painted rest house, or a recreational park, or a recreational garden, or a recreational pond, incurs two offenses. As she goes, there is an offense of wrong-doing; where she stands and looks, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āsandiṃ vā pallaṅkaṃ vā paribhuñjantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paribhuñjati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; paribhutte, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who uses a couch with long legs or a throne with legs shaped like animal figures incurs two offenses. In the effort of using it, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when it has been used, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Suttaṃ kantantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Kantati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; ujjavujjave, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who spins thread incurs two offenses. In the effort of spinning, there is an offense of wrong-doing; at each winding on the spindle, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Gihiveyyāvaccaṃ karontī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Karoti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; kate, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who performs services for laypeople incurs two offenses. In the effort of doing so, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when it has been done, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Bhikkhuniyā [P 5.0077][V 0.0148] – “ehāyye imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamehī”ti vuccamānā – “sādhū”ti [T 0.0195] paṭissuṇitvā neva vūpasamentī na vūpasamāya ussukkaṃ karontī ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhunī who, being told, 'Come, venerable one, settle this dispute,' and having agreed, saying 'Good,' neither settles it herself nor makes an effort for its settlement, incurs one offense: a pācittiya.

Agārikassa vā paribbājakassa vā paribbājikāya vā sahatthā khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā dentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Deti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; dinne, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who gives hard food or soft food with her own hand to a householder, or a male wanderer, or a female wanderer incurs two offenses. In the effort of giving, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when it has been given, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āvasathacīvaraṃ anissajjitvā paribhuñjantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paribhuñjati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; paribhutte, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who uses a seasonal robe without having relinquished it incurs two offenses. In the effort of using it, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when it has been used, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Āvasathaṃ anissajjitvā cārikaṃ pakkamantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paṭhamaṃ pādaṃ parikkhepaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; dutiyaṃ pādaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who departs on a journey without having relinquished a dwelling with an enclosure incurs two offenses. As she causes the first footstep to cross the boundary, there is an offense of wrong-doing; as she causes the second footstep to cross, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Tiracchānavijjaṃ pariyāpuṇantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Pariyāpuṇāti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; pade pade āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who learns worldly knowledge incurs two offenses. In the effort of learning, there is an offense of wrong-doing; at every word, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Tiracchānavijjaṃ vācentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vāceti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; pade pade āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who teaches worldly knowledge incurs two offenses. In the effort of teaching, there is an offense of wrong-doing; at every word, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Cittāgāravaggo pañcamo.

The Fifth Chapter, the Cittāgāra Chapter, is concluded.

6. Ārāmavaggo

6. The Chapter on the Monastery.

236. Jānaṃ [M 0.0136] sabhikkhukaṃ ārāmaṃ anāpucchā pavisantī dve āpattiyo [T 0.0196] āpajjati. Paṭhamaṃ pādaṃ parikkhepaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; dutiyaṃ pādaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

236. A bhikkhunī who, knowing it to be a monastery where there is a bhikkhu, enters without asking permission, incurs two offenses. As she causes the first footstep to cross the boundary, there is an offense of wrong-doing; as she causes the second footstep to cross, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Bhikkhuṃ akkosantī paribhāsantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Akkosati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; akkosite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who insults or reviles a bhikkhu incurs two offenses. In the effort of insulting, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when the insult is complete, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Caṇḍīkatā [V 0.0149] gaṇaṃ paribhāsantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paribhāsati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; paribhāsite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who, being harsh, reviles a group of bhikkhunīs incurs two offenses. In the effort of reviling, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when the reviling is complete, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Nimantitā vā pavāritā vā khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā bhuñjantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. “Khādissāmi bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who, having been invited or having been offered with pavāraṇā, eats hard food or soft food incurs two offenses. As she accepts it thinking, 'I will eat,' there is an offense of wrong-doing; at every swallow, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Kulaṃ maccharāyantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Maccharāyati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; maccharite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who is possessive of a family incurs two offenses. In the effort of being possessive, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when the possessiveness is complete, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Abhikkhuke āvāse vassaṃ vasantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. “Vassaṃ vasissāmī”ti senāsanaṃ paññapeti pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhapeti pariveṇaṃ sammajjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa; saha aruṇuggamanā āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who spends the rains-residence in a residence where there is no bhikkhu incurs two offenses. As she prepares the lodging, sets out drinking water and water for use, or sweeps the surrounding area, thinking, 'I will spend the rains-residence,' there is an offense of wrong-doing; at the break of dawn, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Vassaṃvuṭṭhā bhikkhunī ubhatosaṅghe tīhi ṭhānehi na pavārentī ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhunī who has completed the rains-residence and does not invite criticism in both Sanghas on three grounds incurs one offense: a pācittiya.

Ovādāya vā saṃvāsāya vā na gacchantī ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhunī who does not go for admonition or for communion incurs one offense: a pācittiya.

Uposathampi [T 0.0197] na pucchantī ovādampi na yācantī ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhunī who neither asks about the Uposatha nor requests the admonition incurs one offense: a pācittiya.

Pasākhe jātaṃ gaṇḍaṃ vā rudhitaṃ vā anapaloketvā saṅghaṃ vā gaṇaṃ vā purisena saddhiṃ ekenekā bhedāpentī dve [P 5.0078] āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhedāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; bhinne, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who, without having informed the Sangha or a group, has a boil or a wound that has arisen on the fork of the body lanced by a man, one-on-one, incurs two offenses. In the effort of having it lanced, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when it has been lanced, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Ārāmavaggo chaṭṭho.

The Sixth Chapter, the Ārāma Chapter, is concluded.

7. Gabbhinīvaggo

7. The Chapter on the Pregnant Woman.

237. Gabbhiniṃ [M 0.0137] vuṭṭhāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vuṭṭhāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vuṭṭhāpite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

237. A bhikkhunī who ordains a pregnant woman incurs two offenses. In the effort of ordaining, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when she has been ordained, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Pāyantiṃ [V 0.0150] vuṭṭhāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vuṭṭhāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vuṭṭhāpite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who ordains a breastfeeding woman incurs two offenses. In the effort of ordaining, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when she has been ordained, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vuṭṭhāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vuṭṭhāpite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who ordains a probationer who has not trained for two years in the six rules incurs two offenses. In the effort of ordaining, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when she has been ordained, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ sikkhamānaṃ saṅghena asammataṃ vuṭṭhāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vuṭṭhāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vuṭṭhāpite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who ordains a probationer who has trained for two years in the six rules but has not been authorized by the Saṅgha incurs two offenses. In the effort of ordaining, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when she has been ordained, there is an offense of pācittiya.

Ūnadvādasavassaṃ gihigataṃ vuṭṭhāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vuṭṭhāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vuṭṭhāpite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who ordains a formerly married woman who is less than twelve years old incurs two offenses. If she ordains, there is an offense of wrong-doing in the effort; when she has been ordained, there is an offense of expiation.

Paripuṇṇadvādasavassaṃ gihigataṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu [T 0.0198] asikkhitasikkhaṃ vuṭṭhāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vuṭṭhāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vuṭṭhāpite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who ordains a formerly married woman who is fully twelve years old but has not trained for two years in the six rules incurs two offenses. If she ordains, there is an offense of wrong-doing in the effort; when she has been ordained, there is an offense of expiation.

Paripuṇṇadvādasavassaṃ gihigataṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ saṅghena asammataṃ vuṭṭhāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vuṭṭhāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vuṭṭhāpite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who ordains a formerly married woman who is fully twelve years old, has trained for two years in the six rules, but has not been authorized by the Saṅgha incurs two offenses. If she ordains, there is an offense of wrong-doing in the effort; when she has been ordained, there is an offense of expiation.
