Sahajīviniṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā dve vassāni neva anuggaṇhantī nānuggaṇhāpentī ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Pācittiyaṃ.

Having ordained a co-resident, a bhikkhunī who for two years neither supports her nor has her supported incurs one offense: an offense of expiation.

Vuṭṭhāpitaṃ pavattiniṃ dve vassāni nānubandhantī ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhunī who for two years does not attend upon the preceptor who ordained her incurs one offense: an offense of expiation.

Sahajīviniṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā neva vūpakāsentī na vūpakāsāpentī ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Pācittiyaṃ.

Having ordained a co-resident, a bhikkhunī who neither leads her away nor has her led away incurs one offense: an offense of expiation.

Gabbhinīvaggo sattamo.

The seventh, the Chapter on the Pregnant Woman.

8. Kumārībhūtavaggo

8. The Chapter on the Maiden

238. Ūnavīsativassaṃ [M 0.0138][V 0.0151] kumāribhūtaṃ vuṭṭhāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vuṭṭhāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vuṭṭhāpite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

238. A bhikkhunī who ordains a maiden who is less than twenty years old incurs two offenses. If she ordains, there is an offense of wrong-doing in the effort; when she has been ordained, there is an offense of expiation.

Paripuṇṇavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṃ vuṭṭhāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vuṭṭhāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vuṭṭhāpite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who ordains a maiden who is fully twenty years old but has not trained for two years in the six rules incurs two offenses. If she ordains, there is an offense of wrong-doing in the effort; when she has been ordained, there is an offense of expiation.

Paripuṇṇavīsativassaṃ kumāribhūtaṃ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṃ saṅghena asammataṃ vuṭṭhāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati[T 0.0199]. Vuṭṭhāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vuṭṭhāpite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who ordains a maiden who is fully twenty years old, has trained for two years in the six rules, but has not been authorized by the Saṅgha incurs two offenses. If she ordains, there is an offense of wrong-doing in the effort; when she has been ordained, there is an offense of expiation.

Ūnadvādasavassā vuṭṭhāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vuṭṭhāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vuṭṭhāpite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who is less than twelve years in seniority and ordains another incurs two offenses. If she ordains, there is an offense of wrong-doing in the effort; when she has been ordained, there is an offense of expiation.

Paripuṇṇadvādasavassā saṅghena asammatā vuṭṭhāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vuṭṭhāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vuṭṭhāpite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who is fully twelve years in seniority but has not been authorized by the Saṅgha and ordains another incurs two offenses. If she ordains, there is an offense of wrong-doing in the effort; when she has been ordained, there is an offense of expiation.

“Alaṃ tāva te, ayye, vuṭṭhāpitenā”ti vuccamānā “sādhū”ti paṭissuṇitvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṃ āpajjantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Khiyyati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; khiyyite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who, on being told, 'Venerable lady, that is enough of your ordaining for now,' agrees, saying, 'Good,' but afterwards falls into a state of complaining, incurs two offenses. If she complains, there is an offense of wrong-doing in the effort; when she has complained, there is an offense of expiation.

Sikkhamānaṃ – “sace me tvaṃ, ayye, cīvaraṃ dassasi, evāhaṃ taṃ vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti vatvā neva vuṭṭhāpentī na vuṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ karontī ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhunī who, having said to a probationer, 'Venerable lady, if you give me a robe, then I will ordain you,' neither ordains her herself nor makes an effort to have her ordained, incurs one offense: an offense of expiation.

Sikkhamānaṃ [P 5.0079] – “sace maṃ tvaṃ, ayye, dve vassāni anubandhissasi, evāhaṃ taṃ vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti vatvā neva vuṭṭhāpentī na vuṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṃ karontī ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati. Pācittiyaṃ.

A bhikkhunī who, having said to a probationer, 'Venerable lady, if you attend upon me for two years, then I will ordain you,' neither ordains her herself nor makes an effort to have her ordained, incurs one offense: an offense of expiation.

Purisasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ [V 0.0152] kumārakasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ caṇḍiṃ sokāvāsaṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vuṭṭhāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vuṭṭhāpite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who ordains a probationer who associates with men, associates with boys, is harsh, or is prone to grief incurs two offenses. If she ordains, there is an offense of wrong-doing in the effort; when she has been ordained, there is an offense of expiation.

Mātāpitūhi vā sāmikena vā ananuññātaṃ sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpentī [T 0.0200] dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vuṭṭhāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vuṭṭhāpite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who ordains a probationer who has not been permitted by her mother and father or by her husband incurs two offenses. If she ordains, there is an offense of wrong-doing in the effort; when she has been ordained, there is an offense of expiation.

Pārivāsikachandadāne [M 0.0139] sikkhamānaṃ vuṭṭhāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vuṭṭhāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vuṭṭhāpite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who ordains a probationer by means of an invalid granting of consent incurs two offenses. If she ordains, there is an offense of wrong-doing in the effort; when she has been ordained, there is an offense of expiation.

Anuvassaṃ vuṭṭhāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vuṭṭhāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vuṭṭhāpite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who ordains a probationer every year incurs two offenses. If she ordains, there is an offense of wrong-doing in the effort; when she has been ordained, there is an offense of expiation.

Ekaṃ vassaṃ dve vuṭṭhāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Vuṭṭhāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; vuṭṭhāpite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who ordains two probationers in one year incurs two offenses. If she ordains, there is an offense of wrong-doing in the effort; when she has been ordained, there is an offense of expiation.

Kumārībhūtavaggo aṭṭhamo.

The eighth, the Chapter on the Maiden.

9. Chattupāhanavaggo

9. The Chapter on Umbrellas and Footwear

239. Chattupāhanaṃ dhārentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Dhāreti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; dhārite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

239. A bhikkhunī who uses an umbrella or footwear incurs two offenses. While using, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when it has been used, there is an offense of expiation.

Yānena yāyantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Yāyati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; yāyite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who travels by vehicle incurs two offenses. While traveling, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when she has traveled, there is an offense of expiation.

Saṅghāṇiṃ dhārentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Dhāreti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; dhārite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who wears a girdle incurs two offenses. While wearing, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when it has been worn, there is an offense of expiation.

Itthālaṅkāraṃ dhārentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Dhāreti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; dhārite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who wears women's ornaments incurs two offenses. While wearing, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when they have been worn, there is an offense of expiation.

Gandhavaṇṇakena [V 0.0153] nahāyantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Nahāyati[T 0.0201], payoge dukkaṭaṃ; nahānapariyosāne, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who bathes with scented paste incurs two offenses. While bathing, there is an offense of wrong-doing; at the conclusion of bathing, there is an offense of expiation.

Vāsitakena piññākena nahāyantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Nahāyati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; nahānapariyosāne, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who bathes with scented sesame flour incurs two offenses. While bathing, there is an offense of wrong-doing; at the conclusion of bathing, there is an offense of expiation.

Bhikkhuniyā ummaddāpentī parimaddāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Ummaddāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; ummaddite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who has another bhikkhunī rub or massage her incurs two offenses. While having her rubbed, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when she has been rubbed, there is an offense of expiation.

Sikkhamānāya ummaddāpentī parimaddāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Ummaddāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; ummaddite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who has a female probationer rub or massage her incurs two offenses. While having her rubbed, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when she has been rubbed, there is an offense of expiation.

Sāmaṇeriyā [M 0.0140] ummaddāpentī parimaddāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Ummaddāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; ummaddite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who has a female novice rub or massage her incurs two offenses. While having her rubbed, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when she has been rubbed, there is an offense of expiation.

Gihiniyā ummaddāpentī parimaddāpentī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Ummaddāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; ummaddite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who has a laywoman rub or massage her incurs two offenses. While having her rubbed, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when she has been rubbed, there is an offense of expiation.

Bhikkhussa purato anāpucchā āsane nisīdantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Nisīdati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; nisinne, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who, without asking, sits on a seat in front of a bhikkhu incurs two offenses. In the effort of sitting, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when she has sat down, there is an offense of expiation.

Anokāsakataṃ bhikkhuṃ pañhaṃ pucchantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Pucchati, payoge dukkaṭaṃ; pucchite, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who asks a question of a bhikkhu without having been granted leave incurs two offenses. In the effort of asking, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when she has asked, there is an offense of expiation.

Asaṅkaccikā gāmaṃ pavisantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Paṭhamaṃ [T 0.0202] pādaṃ parikkhepaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; dutiyaṃ pādaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti pācittiyassa.

A bhikkhunī who enters a village without her breast-cloth incurs two offenses. When she crosses the boundary with the first foot, there is an offense of wrong-doing; when she crosses with the second foot, there is an offense of expiation.

Chattupāhanavaggo navamo.

The Chapter on Umbrellas and Footwear is the ninth.

Khuddakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Minor Section is concluded.

5. Pāṭidesanīyakaṇḍaṃ

5. 5. The Section on Offenses to be Confessed

240. Sappiṃ [V 0.0154] viññāpetvā bhuñjantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa.

240. A bhikkhunī who, having requested ghee, eats it, incurs two offenses. When she accepts it with the thought, ‘I will eat,’ there is an offense of wrong-doing; for every mouthful, there is an offense to be confessed.

Telaṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa.

A bhikkhunī who, having requested oil, eats it, incurs two offenses. When she accepts it with the thought, ‘I will eat,’ there is an offense of wrong-doing; for every mouthful, there is an offense to be confessed.

Madhuṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa.

A bhikkhunī who, having requested honey, eats it, incurs two offenses. When she accepts it with the thought, ‘I will eat,’ there is an offense of wrong-doing; for every mouthful, there is an offense to be confessed.

Phāṇitaṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa.

A bhikkhunī who, having requested molasses, eats it, incurs two offenses. When she accepts it with the thought, ‘I will eat,’ there is an offense of wrong-doing; for every mouthful, there is an offense to be confessed.

Macchaṃ [M 0.0141] viññāpetvā bhuñjantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa.

A bhikkhunī who, having requested fish, eats it, incurs two offenses. When she accepts it with the thought, ‘I will eat,’ there is an offense of wrong-doing; for every mouthful, there is an offense to be confessed.

Maṃsaṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhuñjissāmīti [T 0.0203] paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa.

A bhikkhunī who, having requested meat, eats it, incurs two offenses. When she accepts it with the thought, ‘I will eat,’ there is an offense of wrong-doing; for every mouthful, there is an offense to be confessed.

Khīraṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa.

A bhikkhunī who, having requested milk, eats it, incurs two offenses. When she accepts it with the thought, ‘I will eat,’ there is an offense of wrong-doing; for every mouthful, there is an offense to be confessed.

Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa.

A bhikkhunī who, having requested curd, eats it, incurs two offenses. When she accepts it with the thought, ‘I will eat,’ there is an offense of wrong-doing; for every mouthful, there is an offense to be confessed.

Aṭṭha pāṭidesanīyā niṭṭhitā.

The eight offenses to be confessed are concluded.

Katāpattivāro niṭṭhito dutiyo.

The second section on committed offenses is concluded.

3. Vipattivāro

3. 3. The Section on Failures

241. Avassutā [P 5.0080][V 0.0155] bhikkhuniyā avassutassa purisapuggalassa kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyantiyā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ kati vipattiyo bhajanti? Avassutāya bhikkhuniyā avassutassa purisapuggalassa kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyantiyā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ dve vipattiyo bhajanti – siyā sīlavipattiṃ, siyā ācāravipattiṃ…pe….

241. When a bhikkhunī overcome by lust consents to physical contact with a man overcome by lust, to how many of the four failures do the offenses pertain? When a bhikkhunī overcome by lust consents to physical contact with a man overcome by lust, the offenses pertain to two of the four failures: it may be a failure in virtue, or it may be a failure in conduct…and so on.

Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantiyā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ kati vipattiyo bhajanti? Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantiyā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ ekaṃ vipattiṃ bhajanti – ācāravipattiṃ.

When a bhikkhunī eats after requesting curd, to how many of the four failures do the offenses pertain? When a bhikkhunī eats after requesting curd, the offenses pertain to one of the four failures: the failure in conduct.

Vipattivāro niṭṭhito tatiyo.

The third section on failures is concluded.

4. Saṅgahavāro

4. 4. The Section on Inclusion

242. Avassutā [M 0.0142][V 0.0156] bhikkhuniyā avassutassa purisapuggalassa kāyasaṃsaggaṃ [T 0.0204] sādiyantiyā āpattiyo sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katihi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā? Avassutāya bhikkhuniyā avassutassa purisapuggalassa kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyantiyā āpattiyo sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ tīhi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā – siyā pārājikāpattikkhandhena, siyā thullaccayāpattikkhandhena, siyā dukkaṭāpattikkhandhena…pe….

242. When a bhikkhunī who is overcome by lust consents to physical contact with a man who is overcome by lust, by how many of the seven groups of offenses are the offenses comprised? When a bhikkhunī who is overcome by lust consents to physical contact with a man who is overcome by lust, the offenses are comprised by three of the seven groups of offenses: possibly by the group of pārājika offenses, possibly by the group of thullaccaya offenses, or possibly by the group of dukkaṭa offenses… and so on.

Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantiyā āpattiyo sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katihi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā? Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantiyā āpattiyo sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ dvīhi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā – siyā pāṭidesanīyāpattikkhandhena, siyā dukkaṭāpattikkhandhena.

When a bhikkhunī eats after requesting curd, by how many of the seven groups of offenses are the offenses comprised? When a bhikkhunī eats after requesting curd, the offenses are comprised by two of the seven groups of offenses: possibly by the group of pāṭidesanīya offenses, or possibly by the group of dukkaṭa offenses.

Saṅgahavāro niṭṭhito catuttho.

The fourth section on inclusion is concluded.

5. Samuṭṭhānavāro

5. 5. The Section on Origination

243. Avassutāya [V 0.0157] bhikkhuniyā avassutassa purisapuggalassa kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyantiyā āpattiyo channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti? Avassutāya bhikkhuniyā avassutassa purisapuggalassa kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyantiyā āpattiyo channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhanti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti, na vācato…pe….

243. When a bhikkhunī who is overcome by lust consents to physical contact with a man who is overcome by lust, from how many of the six origins of offenses do the offenses arise? When a bhikkhunī who is overcome by lust consents to physical contact with a man who is overcome by lust, the offenses arise from one of the six origins: they arise from body and mind, but not from speech… and so on.

Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantiyā āpattiyo channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti? Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā [T 0.0205] bhuñjantiyā āpattiyo channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ catūhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti – siyā kāyato samuṭṭhanti, na vācato na cittato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca samuṭṭhanti, na cittato; siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti, na vācato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti.

When a bhikkhunī eats after having requested curd, from how many of the six origins of offenses do the offenses arise? When a bhikkhunī eats after having requested curd, the offenses arise from four of the six origins: they may arise from the body, but not from speech or mind; they may arise from body and speech, but not from mind; they may arise from body and mind, but not from speech; or they may arise from body, speech, and mind.

Samuṭṭhānavāro niṭṭhito pañcamo.

The fifth section on origination is concluded.

6. Adhikaraṇavāro

6. 6. The Section on Legal Questions

244. Avassutā [M 0.0143][V 0.0158] bhikkhuniyā avassutassa purisapuggalassa kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyantiyā āpattiyo catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ? Avassutāya bhikkhuniyā avassutassa purisapuggalassa kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyantiyā āpattiyo catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ – āpattādhikaraṇaṃ…pe….

244. When a bhikkhunī who is overcome by lust consents to physical contact with a man who is overcome by lust, which of the four legal questions are the offenses? When a bhikkhunī who is overcome by lust consents to physical contact with a man who is overcome by lust, the offenses are a legal question concerning an offense… and so on.

Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantiyā āpattiyo catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ? Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantiyā āpattiyo catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ – āpattādhikaraṇaṃ.

The offenses of a bhikkhunī who eats after having requested curd: of the four legal questions, which legal question are they? The offenses of a bhikkhunī who eats after having requested curd are, of the four legal questions, a legal question concerning an offense.

Adhikaraṇavāro niṭṭhito chaṭṭho.

The sixth section on legal questions is concluded.

7. Samathavāro

7. The Section on Settlements

245. Avassutāya [V 0.0159] bhikkhuniyā avassutassa purisapuggalassa kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyantiyā āpattiyo sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammanti? Avassutāya bhikkhuniyā avassutassa purisapuggalassa kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyantiyā āpattiyo sattannaṃ samathānaṃ tīhi samathehi sammanti – siyā sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca, siyā sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca…pe….

245. The offenses of a lustful bhikkhunī who consents to physical contact with a lustful man, by how many of the seven settlements are they settled? The offenses of a lustful bhikkhunī who consents to physical contact with a lustful man are settled by three of the seven settlements: it may be by the procedure in the presence and by acting according to acknowledgement, or it may be by the procedure in the presence and by covering over with grass… and so on.

Dadhiṃ [T 0.0206][P 5.0081] viññāpetvā bhuñjantiyā āpattiyo sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammanti? Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantiyā āpattiyo sattannaṃ samathānaṃ tīhi samathehi sammanti – siyā sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca, siyā sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca.

The offenses of a bhikkhunī who eats after having requested curd, by how many of the seven settlements are they settled? The offenses of a bhikkhunī who eats after having requested curd are settled by three of the seven settlements: it may be by the procedure in the presence and by acting according to acknowledgement, or it may be by the procedure in the presence and by covering over with grass.

Samathavāro niṭṭhito sattamo.

The seventh Section on Settlements is concluded.

8. Samuccayavāro

8. The Section on Combinations

246. Avassutā [V 0.0160] bhikkhunī avassutassa purisapuggalassa kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyantī kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Avassutā bhikkhunī avassutassa purisapuggalassa [M 0.0144] kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyantī tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Adhakkhakaṃ ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalaṃ gahaṇaṃ sādiyati, āpatti pārājikassa; ubbhakkhakaṃ adhojāṇumaṇḍalaṃ gahaṇaṃ sādiyati, āpatti thullaccayassa; kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ gahaṇaṃ sādiyati, āpatti dukkaṭassa – avassutā bhikkhunī avassutassa purisapuggalassa kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyantī imā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati.

246. A lustful bhikkhunī, consenting to physical contact with a lustful man, incurs how many offenses? A lustful bhikkhunī, consenting to physical contact with a lustful man, incurs three offenses. If she consents to being grasped below the collarbone and above the knee, it is a pārājika offense; if she consents to being grasped above the collarbone and below the knee, it is a thullaccaya offense; if she consents to being grasped on an object connected to the body, it is a dukkaṭa offense. A lustful bhikkhunī, consenting to physical contact with a lustful man, incurs these three offenses.

Tā [V 0.0161] āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ kati vipattiyo bhajanti? Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katihi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā? Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti? Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ? Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammanti? Tā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ dve vipattiyo bhajanti – siyā sīlavipattiṃ, siyā ācāravipattiṃ. Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ tīhi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā – siyā [T 0.0207] pārājikāpattikkhandhena, siyā thullaccayāpattikkhandhena, siyā dukkaṭāpattikkhandhena. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhanti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti, na vācato. Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ tīhi samathehi sammanti – siyā sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca, siyā sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca…pe….

To how many of the four failures do these offenses pertain? By how many of the seven groups of offenses are they included? From how many of the six origins of offenses do they originate? Which of the four legal questions is it? By how many of the seven settlements are they settled? These offenses pertain to two of the four failures—it may be a failure in virtue, or it may be a failure in conduct. They are included by three of the seven groups of offenses—it may be by the group of pārājika offenses, by the group of thullaccaya offenses, or by the group of dukkaṭa offenses. They originate from one of the six origins of offenses—they originate from body and mind, but not from speech. It is a legal question concerning an offense. They are settled by three of the seven settlements—it may be by the procedure in the presence and by acting according to acknowledgement, or it may be by the procedure in the presence and by covering over with grass… and so on.

Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantī kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantī dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa – dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantī imā dve āpattiyo āpajjati.

A bhikkhunī who eats after having requested curd, how many offenses does she incur? A bhikkhunī who eats after having requested curd incurs two offenses. If she receives it with the thought, 'I will eat,' it is a dukkaṭa offense; with every swallow, it is a pāṭidesanīya offense. A bhikkhunī who eats after having requested curd incurs these two offenses.

Tā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ kati vipattiyo bhajanti? Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katihi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā? Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti? Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ? Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammanti? Tā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ ekaṃ vipattiṃ bhajanti – ācāravipattiṃ. Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ dvīhi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā – siyā pāṭidesanīyāpattikkhandhena, siyā dukkaṭāpattikkhandhena. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ catūhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti – siyā kāyato samuṭṭhanti na vācato na cittato, siyā kāyato ca vācato ca samuṭṭhanti na cittato, siyā [M 0.0145] kāyato [T 0.0208] ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti na vācato, siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti. Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ – āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ tīhi samathehi sammanti – siyā sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca, siyā sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca.

To how many of the four failures do these offenses pertain? By how many of the seven groups of offenses are they included? From how many of the six origins of offenses do they originate? Which of the four legal questions is it? By how many of the seven settlements are they settled? These offenses pertain to one of the four failures—the failure in conduct. They are included by two of the seven groups of offenses—it may be by the group of pāṭidesanīya offenses, or by the group of dukkaṭa offenses. They originate from four of the six origins of offenses—they may originate from the body, but not from speech or mind; they may originate from the body and speech, but not from the mind; they may originate from the body and mind, but not from speech; or they may originate from the body, speech, and mind. It is a legal question concerning an offense. They are settled by three of the seven settlements—it may be by the procedure in the presence and by acting according to acknowledgement, or it may be by the procedure in the presence and by covering over with grass.

Samuccayavāro niṭṭhito aṭṭhamo.

The eighth Section on Combinations is concluded.

1. Katthapaññattivāro

1. The Section on Where it was Laid Down

1. Pārājikakaṇḍaṃ

1. The Chapter on the Pārājikas

247. Yaṃ [V 0.0162] tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyanapaccayā pārājikaṃ kattha paññattaṃ? Kaṃ ārabbha? Kismiṃ vatthusmiṃ…pe… kenābhatanti?

247. That Pārājika which was laid down by that Blessed One—who knows, who sees, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One—on account of delighting in bodily contact: where was it laid down? Concerning whom? In what matter? … By whom was it brought?

Yaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyanapaccayā pārājikaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sundarīnandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sundarīnandā bhikkhunī avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Atthi tattha paññatti, anupaññatti, anuppannapaññattīti? Ekā paññatti. Anupaññatti anuppannapaññatti tasmiṃ natthi. Sabbatthapaññatti, padesapaññattīti? Sabbatthapaññatti. Sādhāraṇapaññatti, asādhāraṇapaññattīti? Asādhāraṇapaññatti. Ekatopaññatti, ubhatopaññattīti? Ekatopaññatti. Catunnaṃ pātimokkhuddesānaṃ katthogadhaṃ kattha pariyāpannanti? Nidānogadhaṃ nidānapariyāpannaṃ? Katamena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchatīti? Dutiyena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchati. Catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ katamā vipattīti? Sīlavipatti. Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katamo āpattikkhandhoti[T 0.0209]? Pārājikāpattikkhandho. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhātīti? Ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato…pe… kenābhatanti? Paramparābhataṃ –

That Pārājika which was laid down by that Blessed One—who knows, who sees, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—on account of delighting in bodily contact: where was it laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā. In what matter? The bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā, being lustful, delighted in bodily contact with a lustful man; in that matter. Is there an enactment, a supplementary enactment, an unpromulgated enactment therein? There is one enactment. There is no supplementary enactment or unpromulgated enactment therein. Is it a universal enactment or a partial enactment? A universal enactment. Is it a common enactment or an uncommon enactment? An uncommon enactment. Is it a one-sided enactment or a two-sided enactment? A one-sided enactment. Of the four recitations of the Pātimokkha, where is it included, where is it comprised? It is included in the introduction, comprised in the introduction. By which recitation does it come to be recited? It comes to be recited by the second recitation. Of the four failures, which failure is it? A failure in virtue. Of the seven groups of offenses, which group of offenses is it? The group of Pārājika offenses. Of the six origins of offenses, by how many origins does it arise? It arises from one origin: it arises from body and mind, not from speech... By whom was it brought? It was brought by a succession of teachers—

Upāli [M 0.0146] dāsako ceva, soṇako siggavo tathā;

Moggaliputtena pañcamā, ete jambusirivhaye. …pe…;

Upāli and Dāsaka, Soṇaka and Siggava too; these, with Moggaliputta as the fifth, recited the Vinaya in Jambudīpa...

Ete [V 0.0163] nāgā mahāpaññā, vinayaññū maggakovidā;

Vinayaṃ dīpe pakāsesuṃ, piṭakaṃ tambapaṇṇiyāti.

These great beings, of great wisdom, knowers of the Vinaya, skilled in the path, proclaimed the Vinaya Piṭaka on the island of Tambapaṇṇi.

Vajjappaṭicchādanapaccayā [P 5.0082] pārājikaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Thullanandā bhikkhunī jānaṃ pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpannaṃ bhikkhuniṃ nevattanā paṭicodesi na gaṇassa ārocesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – dhuranikkhepe…pe….

The Pārājika on account of concealing an offense: where was it laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. In what matter? The bhikkhunī Thullanandā, knowing a bhikkhunī had fallen into a Pārājika offense, neither admonished her herself nor informed the group; in that matter. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: from abandoning the training...

Yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanapaccayā pārājikaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Thullanandā bhikkhunī samaggena saṅghena ukkhittaṃ ariṭṭhaṃ bhikkhuṃ gaddhabādhipubbaṃ anuvatti, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – dhuranikkhepe…pe….

The Pārājika on account of not relinquishing after being admonished up to the third time: where was it laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. In what matter? The bhikkhunī Thullanandā followed the monk Ariṭṭha, who had formerly been a vulture-killer and had been suspended by a unified Sangha; in that matter. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: from abandoning the training...

Aṭṭhamaṃ vatthuṃ paripūraṇapaccayā pārājikaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo aṭṭhamaṃ vatthuṃ paripūresuṃ, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ [T 0.0210] ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – dhuranikkhepe…pe….

The Pārājika on account of fulfilling the eighth matter: where was it laid down? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunīs of the group of six. In what matter? The bhikkhunīs of the group of six fulfilled the eighth matter; in that matter. There is one enactment. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: from abandoning the training...

Pārājikā niṭṭhitā.

The Pārājikas are concluded.

2. Saṅghādisesakaṇḍādi

2. The Chapter on Saṅghādisesa, and So Forth

248. Yaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena ussayavādikāya bhikkhuniyā aḍḍaṃ karaṇapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññatto? Kaṃ ārabbha? Kismiṃ vatthusmiṃ…pe… kenābhatanti?

248. Where was the Saṅghādisesa laid down by that Blessed One—the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—on account of a contentious bhikkhunī instituting a legal issue? Concerning whom? In what matter? … By whom was it brought?

Yaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena ussayavādikāya bhikkhuniyā aḍḍaṃ karaṇapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti[M 0.0147]? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti[V 0.0164]? Thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Thullanandā bhikkhunī ussayavādikā vihari, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Atthi tattha paññatti, anupaññatti, anuppannapaññattīti? Ekā paññatti. Anupaññatti anuppannapaññatti tasmiṃ natthi. Sabbatthapaññatti, padesapaññattīti? Sabbatthapaññatti. Sādhāraṇapaññatti, asādhāraṇapaññattīti? Asādhāraṇapaññatti. Ekatopaññatti, ubhatopaññattīti? Ekatopaññatti. Catunnaṃ pātimokkhuddesānaṃ katthogadhaṃ kattha pariyāpannanti? Nidānogadhaṃ nidānapariyāpannaṃ. Katamena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchatīti? Tatiyena uddesena uddesaṃ āgacchati. Catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ katamā vipattīti? Sīlavipatti. Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katamo āpattikkhandhoti? Saṅghādisesāpattikkhandho. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhātīti? Dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca vācato ca samuṭṭhāti, na cittato; siyā kāyato ca vācato cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe… kenābhatanti? Paramparābhataṃ –

Where was the Saṅghādisesa laid down by that Blessed One—the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—on account of a contentious bhikkhunī instituting a legal issue? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. In what matter? The bhikkhunī Thullanandā lived contentiously; in that matter. Is there an enactment, a supplementary enactment, or an unpromulgated enactment therein? There is one enactment. There is no supplementary enactment or unpromulgated enactment therein. Is it a universal enactment or a partial enactment? It is a universal enactment. Is it a common enactment or an uncommon enactment? It is an uncommon enactment. Is it a one-sided enactment or a two-sided enactment? It is a one-sided enactment. Among the four recitations of the Pātimokkha, where is it included, where is it comprised? It is included in the introduction, comprised in the introduction. By which recitation does it come up for recitation? It comes up for recitation by the third recitation. Among the four kinds of failures, which failure is it? It is a failure in virtue. Among the seven groups of offenses, which group of offenses is it? It is the Saṅghādisesa group of offenses. From how many of the six origins of offenses does it arise? It arises from two origins: sometimes it arises from body and speech, not from mind; sometimes it arises from body, speech, and mind. … By whom was it brought? It was brought by a succession of teachers—

Upāli dāsako ceva, soṇako siggavo tathā;

Moggaliputtena pañcamā, ete jambusirivhaye. …pe…;

Upāli and Dāsaka, Soṇaka and Siggava likewise; these, with Moggaliputta as the fifth, recited the Vinaya in Jambudīpa… etc.

Ete nāgā mahāpaññā, vinayaññū maggakovidā;

Vinayaṃ dīpe pakāsesuṃ, piṭakaṃ tambapaṇṇiyāti.

These great beings, of great wisdom, knowers of the Vinaya, skilled in the path, proclaimed the Vinaya Piṭaka on the island of Tambapaṇṇi.

Coriṃ [T 0.0211] vuṭṭhāpanapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Thullanandā bhikkhunī coriṃ vuṭṭhāpesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ dvīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Where was the Saṅghādisesa laid down on account of giving ordination to a female thief? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. On what occasion? The bhikkhunī Thullanandā gave ordination to a female thief. That was the occasion. There is one original rule. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from two origins: it may arise from speech and mind, not from body; or it may arise from body, speech, and mind… etc.

Ekā gāmantaraṃ gamanapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Aññataraṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Aññatarā bhikkhunī ekā gāmantaraṃ gacchi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, tisso anupaññattiyo. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – paṭhamapārājike…pe….

Where was the Saṅghādisesa laid down on account of going to another village alone? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning a certain bhikkhunī. On what occasion? A certain bhikkhunī went to another village alone. That was the occasion. There is one original rule and three supplementary rules. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin, that of the first Pārājika… etc.

Samaggena [M 0.0148] saṅghena ukkhittaṃ bhikkhuniṃ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena anapaloketvā kārakasaṅghaṃ [V 0.0165] anaññāya gaṇassa chandaṃ osāraṇapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Thullanandā bhikkhunī samaggena saṅghena ukkhittaṃ bhikkhuniṃ [T 0.0212] dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena anapaloketvā kārakasaṅghaṃ anaññāya gaṇassa chandaṃ osāresi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – dhuranikkhepe…pe….

Where was the Saṅghādisesa laid down on account of reinstating a bhikkhunī who had been suspended by a united Saṅgha in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction, without asking permission of the Saṅgha that performed the act and without knowing the consent of the group? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. On what occasion? The bhikkhunī Thullanandā reinstated a bhikkhunī who had been suspended by a united Saṅgha in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction, without asking permission of the Saṅgha that performed the act and without knowing the consent of the group. That was the occasion. There is one original rule. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: that of abandoning the training… etc.

Avassutāya bhikkhuniyā avassutassa purisapuggalassa hatthato khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā bhuñjanapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sundarīnandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sundarīnandā bhikkhunī avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa hatthato āmisaṃ paṭiggahesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – paṭhamapārājike…pe….

Where was the Saṅghādisesa laid down on account of a lustful bhikkhunī, having received hard food or soft food from the hand of a lustful man with her own hand, eating it? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā. On what occasion? The bhikkhunī Sundarīnandā, being lustful, received almsfood from the hand of a lustful man. That was the occasion. There is one original rule. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin, that of the first Pārājika… etc.

“Kiṃ te, ayye, eso purisapuggalo karissati avassuto vā anavassuto vā, yato tvaṃ anavassutā! Iṅgha, ayye, yaṃ te eso purisapuggalo deti khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā taṃ tvaṃ sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khāda vā bhuñja vā”ti uyyojanapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Aññataraṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Aññatarā bhikkhunī – “kiṃ te, ayye, eso purisapuggalo karissati avassuto vā anavassuto vā, yato tvaṃ anavassutā! Iṅgha, ayye, yaṃ te eso purisapuggalo deti khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā taṃ tvaṃ sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khāda vā bhuñja vā”ti uyyojesi, tasmiṃ [T 0.0213] vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

Where was the Saṅghādisesa laid down on account of inciting another, saying: “Venerable lady, what will this man do to you, whether he is lustful or not, since you are not lustful? Come, venerable lady, whatever hard food or soft food this man gives you, having received it with your own hand, eat it or consume it”? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning a certain bhikkhunī. On what occasion? A certain bhikkhunī incited another, saying: “Venerable lady, what will this man do to you, whether he is lustful or not, since you are not lustful? Come, venerable lady, whatever hard food or soft food this man gives you, having received it with your own hand, eat it or consume it.” That was the occasion. There is one original rule. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from three origins… etc.

Kupitāya anattamanāya bhikkhuniyā yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Caṇḍakāḷiṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī kupitā anattamanā evaṃ avaca – “buddhaṃ paccācikkhāmi, dhammaṃ paccācikkhāmi, saṅghaṃ paccācikkhāmi, sikkhaṃ paccācikkhāmī”ti, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ[M 0.0149]. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – dhuranikkhepe…pe….

Where was the Saṅghādisesa laid down on account of an angry and displeased bhikkhunī not relinquishing her view after being admonished up to the third time? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī. On what occasion? The bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī, being angry and displeased, said thus: 'I renounce the Buddha, I renounce the Dhamma, I renounce the Saṅgha, I renounce the training.' That was the occasion. There is one original rule. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: that of abandoning the training… etc.

Kismiñcideva [V 0.0166] adhikaraṇe paccākatāya bhikkhuniyā yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Caṇḍakāḷiṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī kismiñcideva adhikaraṇe paccākatā kupitā anattamanā evaṃ avaca – “chandagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo, dosagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo, mohagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo, bhayagāminiyo ca bhikkhuniyo”ti, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – dhuranikkhepe…pe….

Where was the Saṅghādisesa laid down on account of a bhikkhunī who, having been defeated in some dispute, does not relinquish her view after being admonished up to the third time? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī. On what occasion? The bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī, having been defeated in some dispute, being angry and displeased, spoke thus: ‘The bhikkhunīs are biased by desire, the bhikkhunīs are biased by hatred, the bhikkhunīs are biased by delusion, and the bhikkhunīs are biased by fear.’ That was the occasion. There is one original rule. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: that of abandoning the training… etc.

Saṃsaṭṭhānaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanapaccayā [T 0.0214] saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo saṃsaṭṭhā vihariṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – dhuranikkhepe…pe….

Where was the Saṅghādisesa laid down on account of bhikkhunīs who associate with laypeople not relinquishing that practice after being admonished up to the third time? It was laid down at Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning many bhikkhunīs. On what occasion? Many bhikkhunīs dwelt associating with laypeople. That was the occasion. There is one original rule. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from one origin: that of abandoning the training… etc.

“Saṃsaṭṭhā[P 5.0083], ayye, tumhe viharatha. Mā tumhe nānā viharitthā”ti uyyojentiyā yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanapaccayā saṅghādiseso kattha paññattoti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññatto. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Thullanandaṃ bhikkhuniṃ ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Thullanandā bhikkhunī – “saṃsaṭṭhāva ayye, tumhe viharatha. Mā tamhe nānā viharitthā”ti uyyojesi, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – dhuranikkhepe…pe….

Where was the Saṅghādisesa training rule laid down on account of a bhikkhunī who encourages others, saying, ‘Venerable ladies, you should dwell associating with laypeople. Do not dwell separately,’ and does not relinquish that view after being admonished up to the third time? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the bhikkhunī Thullanandā. In what matter? The bhikkhunī Thullanandā encouraged others, saying, ‘Venerable ladies, you should dwell associating with laypeople. Do not dwell separately.’ It was in that matter. There is one formulation. It arises from one of the six origins of offenses: through abandoning the training... and so on.

Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjanapaccayā pāṭidesanīyaṃ kattha paññattanti? Sāvatthiyaṃ paññattaṃ. Kaṃ ārabbhāti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo ārabbha. Kismiṃ vatthusminti? Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjiṃsu, tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Ekā paññatti, ekā anupaññatti. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ catūhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe…[T 0.0215].

Where was the Pāṭidesanīya training rule concerning eating after having requested curd laid down? It was laid down in Sāvatthī. Concerning whom? Concerning the group-of-six bhikkhunīs. In what matter? The group-of-six bhikkhunīs, having requested curd, ate it; in that matter. There is one original formulation and one subsequent formulation. Of the six origins of offenses, it arises from four origins... and so on.

Katthapaññattivāro niṭṭhito paṭhamo.

The first section on where it was laid down is finished.

2. Katāpattivāro

2. The Section on Incurred Offenses

1. Pārājikakaṇḍaṃ

1. The Section on Pārājika Offenses

249. Kāyasaṃsaggaṃ [M 0.0150][V 0.0167] sādiyanapaccayā kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyanapaccayā pañca āpattiyo āpajjati. Avassutā bhikkhunī avassutassa purisapuggalassa adhakkhakaṃ ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalaṃ gahaṇaṃ sādiyati, āpatti pārājikassa; bhikkhu kāyena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa; kāyena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti thullaccayassa; kāyapaṭibaddhena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa; aṅgulipatodake pācittiyaṃ – kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyanapaccayā imā pañca āpattiyo āpajjati.

249. How many offenses does one incur on account of taking pleasure in physical contact? On account of taking pleasure in physical contact, one incurs five offenses. If a lustful bhikkhunī takes pleasure in a lustful man's grasping below the collarbone and above the knees, an offense of pārājika is incurred. If a bhikkhu touches body with body, an offense of saṅghādisesa is incurred. If he touches with the body what is connected to the body, an offense of thullaccaya is incurred. If he touches with what is connected to the body what is connected to the body, an offense of dukkaṭa is incurred. For poking with a finger, a pācittiya offense is incurred. On account of taking pleasure in physical contact, one incurs these five offenses.

Vajjappaṭicchādanapaccayā kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Vajjappaṭicchādanapaccayā catasso āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhikkhunī jānaṃ pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpannaṃ (syā.) paṭicchādeti, āpatti pārājikassa; vematikā paṭicchādeti, āpatti thullaccayassa; bhikkhu saṅghādisesaṃ paṭicchādeti, āpatti pācittiyassa; ācāravipattiṃ paṭicchādeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa – vajjappaṭicchādanapaccayā imā catasso āpattiyo āpajjati.

How many offenses does one incur on account of concealing a fault? On account of concealing a fault, one incurs four offenses. If a bhikkhunī knowingly conceals a pārājika offense, an offense of pārājika is incurred. If, being doubtful, she conceals it, an offense of thullaccaya is incurred. If a bhikkhu conceals a saṅghādisesa offense, an offense of pācittiya is incurred. If one conceals a failure in conduct, an offense of dukkaṭa is incurred. On account of concealing a fault, one incurs these four offenses.

Yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanapaccayā kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanapaccayā pañca āpattiyo āpajjati. Ukkhittānuvattikā bhikkhunī yāvatatiyaṃ [T 0.0216] samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjati, ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti pārājikassa; bhedakānuvattikā bhikkhunī yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa; pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjati, āpatti pācittiyassa [V 0.0168] – yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanapaccayā imā pañca āpattiyo āpajjati.

How many offenses does one incur on account of not relinquishing after the third formal act of admonition? On account of not relinquishing after the third formal act of admonition, one incurs five offenses. If a bhikkhunī who follows one who is living under suspension does not relinquish that association after the third formal act of admonition, a dukkaṭa offense is incurred at the motion, thullaccaya offenses with the two formal acts, and at the conclusion of the formal act, an offense of pārājika is incurred. If a bhikkhunī who follows a schismatic does not relinquish that association after the third formal act of admonition, an offense of saṅghādisesa is incurred. If one does not relinquish a bad view after the third formal act of admonition, an offense of pācittiya is incurred. On account of not relinquishing after the third formal act of admonition, one incurs these five offenses.

Aṭṭhamaṃ vatthuṃ paripūraṇapaccayā kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Aṭṭhamaṃ vatthuṃ paripūraṇapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Purisena – “itthannāmaṃ okāsaṃ āgacchā”ti vuttā gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa; purisassa [M 0.0151] hatthapāsaṃ okkantamatte āpatti thullaccayassa; aṭṭhamaṃ vatthuṃ paripūreti, āpatti pārājikassa – aṭṭhamaṃ vatthuṃ paripūraṇapaccayā imā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati.

How many offenses does one incur on account of the fulfillment of the eighth ground? On account of the fulfillment of the eighth ground, one incurs three offenses. When, being told by a man, 'Come to such and such a place,' she goes, an offense of dukkaṭa is incurred; when she steps within arm's reach of the man, an offense of thullaccaya is incurred; when she fulfills the eighth ground, an offense of pārājika is incurred. On account of the fulfillment of the eighth ground, one incurs these three offenses.

Pārājikā niṭṭhitā.

The Pārājikas are concluded.

2. Saṅghādisesakaṇḍādi

2. The Chapter on Saṅghādisesa, and So Forth

250. Ussayavādikā bhikkhunī aḍḍaṃ karaṇapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Ekassa āroceti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; dutiyassa āroceti, āpatti thullaccayassa; aḍḍapariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

250. A contentious bhikkhunī, on account of bringing a legal case, incurs three offenses. If she informs one person, an offense of dukkaṭa is incurred; if she informs a second person, an offense of thullaccaya is incurred; at the conclusion of the legal case, an offense of saṅghādisesa is incurred.

Coriṃ vuṭṭhāpanapaccayā [P 5.0084] tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā; kammavācāpariyosāne [T 0.0217] āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

On account of giving ordination to a female thief, one incurs three offenses. With the motion, a dukkaṭa offense is incurred; with the two formal acts, thullaccaya offenses are incurred; at the conclusion of the formal act, an offense of saṅghādisesa is incurred.

Ekā gāmantaraṃ gamanapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Gacchati, āpatti dukkaṭassa; paṭhamaṃ pādaṃ parikkhepaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti thullaccayassa; dutiyaṃ pādaṃ atikkāmeti, āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

On account of going alone to another village, one incurs three offenses. When she goes, an offense of dukkaṭa is incurred; when she crosses the boundary with the first foot, an offense of thullaccaya is incurred; when she crosses with the second foot, an offense of saṅghādisesa is incurred.

Samaggena saṅghena ukkhittaṃ bhikkhuniṃ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena anapaloketvā kārakasaṅghaṃ anaññāya gaṇassa chandaṃ osāraṇapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

On account of reinstating a bhikkhunī who was expelled by a united Saṅgha in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction—without informing the Saṅgha that performed the act and without ascertaining the consent of the group—one incurs three offenses. With the motion, a dukkaṭa offense is incurred; with the two formal acts, thullaccaya offenses are incurred; at the conclusion of the formal act, an offense of saṅghādisesa is incurred.

Avassutā bhikkhunī avassutassa purisapuggalassa hatthato khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sahatthā [V 0.0169] paṭiggahetvā bhuñjanapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. “Khādissāmi bhuñjissāmī”ti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti thullaccayassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti saṅghādisesassa; udakadantaponaṃ paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

A lustful bhikkhunī, on account of receiving with her own hand hard or soft food from the hand of a lustful man and eating it, incurs three offenses. If she receives it thinking, 'I will eat, I will consume,' an offense of thullaccaya is incurred; with every swallow, an offense of saṅghādisesa is incurred; if she receives water and a tooth-cleaner, an offense of dukkaṭa is incurred.

“Kiṃ te, ayye, eso purisapuggalo karissati avassuto vā anavassuto vā, yato tvaṃ anavassutā! Iṅgha, ayye, yaṃ te eso purisapuggalo [M 0.0152] deti khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā taṃ tvaṃ sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khāda vā bhuñja vā”ti, uyyojanapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Tassā vacanena khādissāmi bhuñjissāmīti [T 0.0218] paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti thullaccayassa; bhojanapariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

On account of urging another, saying, 'Venerable, what will this man do to you, whether he is lustful or not, since you are not lustful? Come, venerable, whatever food, hard or soft, this man gives you, receive it with your own hand and eat or consume it,' one incurs three offenses. If, by her word, one accepts it thinking, 'I will eat, I will consume,' it is an offense of dukkaṭa; with every swallow, it is an offense of thullaccaya; at the conclusion of the meal, it is an offense of saṅghādisesa.

Kupitā bhikkhunī yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

An angry bhikkhunī, on account of not relinquishing her view after being formally admonished up to the third time, incurs three offenses. With the motion, it is a dukkaṭa offense; with the two formal acts, they are thullaccaya offenses; at the conclusion of the formal act, it is an offense of saṅghādisesa.

Kismiñcideva adhikaraṇe paccākatā bhikkhunī yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

A bhikkhunī who has been defeated in some legal issue, on account of not relinquishing her view after being formally admonished up to the third time, incurs three offenses. With the motion, it is a dukkaṭa offense; with the two formal acts, they are thullaccaya offenses; at the conclusion of the formal act, it is an offense of saṅghādisesa.

Saṃsaṭṭhā bhikkhunī yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

A bhikkhunī who associates with laypeople, on account of not relinquishing this after being formally admonished up to the third time, incurs three offenses. With the motion, it is a dukkaṭa offense; with the two formal acts, they are thullaccaya offenses; at the conclusion of the formal act, it is an offense of saṅghādisesa.

“Saṃsaṭṭhāva, ayye, tumhe viharatha, mā tumhe nānā viharitthā”ti uyyojentī yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanapaccayā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati. Ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti saṅghādisesassa.

A bhikkhunī who urges others, saying, 'Venerables, you should live in association with laypeople; do not live separately,' on account of not relinquishing this after being formally admonished up to the third time, incurs three offenses. With the motion, it is a dukkaṭa offense; with the two formal acts, they are thullaccaya offenses; at the conclusion of the formal act, it is an offense of saṅghādisesa.

Dasa saṅghādisesā niṭṭhitā…pe….

The ten saṅghādisesa offenses are concluded… and so forth….

(Yathā heṭṭhā tathā vitthāretabbā paccayameva nānākaraṇaṃ)

(This should be elaborated in the same way as that below; only the cause is different.)

Dadhiṃ [T 0.0219][V 0.0170] viññāpetvā bhuñjanapaccayā kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjanapaccayā dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre ajjhohāre āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa – dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjanapaccayā imā dve āpattiyo āpajjati.

On account of requesting curd and eating it, how many offenses does one incur? On account of requesting curd and eating it, one incurs two offenses. If one receives it thinking, 'I will eat,' it is an offense of dukkaṭa; with every swallow, it is an offense of pāṭidesanīya. Thus, on account of requesting curd and eating it, one incurs these two offenses.

Katāpattivāro niṭṭhito dutiyo.

The second Section on Offenses Committed is concluded.

3. Vipattivāro

3. The Section on Failures

251. Kāyasaṃsaggaṃ [M 0.0153][V 0.0171] sādiyanapaccayā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ kati vipattiyo bhajanti? Kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyanapaccayā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ dve vipattiyo bhajanti – siyā sīlavipattiṃ, siyā ācāravipattiṃ…pe… dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjanapaccayā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ kati vipattiyo bhajanti? Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjanapaccayā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ ekaṃ vipattiṃ bhajanti – ācāravipattiṃ.

251. To how many of the four failures do the offenses due to taking pleasure in bodily contact pertain? The offenses due to taking pleasure in bodily contact pertain to two of the four failures: sometimes the failure of virtue, and sometimes the failure of conduct... and so on. To how many of the four failures do the offenses due to eating after having requested curd pertain? The offenses due to eating after having requested curd pertain to one of the four failures: the failure of conduct.

Vipattivāro niṭṭhito tatiyo.

The third Section on Failures is concluded.

4. Saṅgahavāro

4. The Section on Inclusion

252. Kāyasaṃsaggaṃ [V 0.0172] sādiyanapaccayā āpattiyo sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ [P 5.0085] katihi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā? Kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyanapaccayā āpattiyo sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ pañcahi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā – siyā pārājikāpattikkhandhena, siyā saṅghādisesāpattikkhandhena, siyā thullaccayāpattikkhandhena, siyā pācittiyāpattikkhandhena, siyā dukkaṭāpattikkhandhena…pe….

252. By how many of the seven groups of offenses are the offenses due to taking pleasure in bodily contact included? The offenses due to taking pleasure in bodily contact are included by five of the seven groups of offenses: sometimes by the group of Pārājika offenses, sometimes by the group of Saṅghādisesa offenses, sometimes by the group of Thullaccaya offenses, sometimes by the group of Pācittiya offenses, and sometimes by the group of Dukkaṭa offenses... and so on.

Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā [T 0.0220] bhuñjanapaccayā āpattiyo sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katihi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā? Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjanapaccayā āpattiyo sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ dvīhi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā – siyā pāṭidesanīyāpattikkhandhena, siyā dukkaṭāpattikkhandhena.

By how many of the seven groups of offenses are the offenses due to eating after having requested curd included? The offenses due to eating after having requested curd are included by two of the seven groups of offenses: sometimes by the group of Pāṭidesanīya offenses, and sometimes by the group of Dukkaṭa offenses.

Saṅgahavāro niṭṭhito catuttho.

The fourth Section on Inclusion is concluded.

5. Samuṭṭhānavāro

5. The Section on Origination

253. Kāyasaṃsaggaṃ [V 0.0173] sādiyanapaccayā āpattiyo channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti? Kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyanapaccayā āpattiyo channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhanti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti, na vācato…pe….

253. From how many of the six origins of offenses do the offenses due to taking pleasure in bodily contact arise? The offenses due to taking pleasure in bodily contact arise from one of the six origins of offenses: they arise from body and mind, not from speech... and so on.

Dadhiṃ [M 0.0154] viññāpetvā bhuñjanapaccayā āpattiyo channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti? Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjanapaccayā āpattiyo channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ catūhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti – siyā kāyato samuṭṭhanti, na vācato na cittato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca samuṭṭhanti, na cittato; siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti, na vācato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti.

From how many of the six origins of offenses do the offenses due to eating after requesting curd arise? The offenses due to eating after requesting curd arise from four of the six origins of offenses: they may arise from the body, not from speech or mind; they may arise from body and speech, not from mind; they may arise from body and mind, not from speech; and they may arise from body, speech, and mind.

Samuṭṭhānavāro niṭṭhito pañcamo.

The fifth Section on Origination is concluded.

6. Adhikaraṇavāro

6. The Section on Legal Questions

254. Kāyasaṃsaggaṃ [V 0.0174] sādiyanapaccayā āpattiyo catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ? Kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyanapaccayā āpattiyo catunnaṃ [T 0.0221] adhikaraṇānaṃ, āpattādhikaraṇaṃ…pe….

254. Which of the four legal questions are the offenses due to taking pleasure in bodily contact? Of the four legal questions, the offenses due to taking pleasure in bodily contact are a legal question concerning offenses... and so on.

Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjanapaccayā āpattiyo catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ? Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjanapaccayā āpattiyo catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ – āpattādhikaraṇaṃ.

Which of the four legal questions are the offenses due to eating after having requested curd? Of the four legal questions, the offenses due to eating after having requested curd are a legal question concerning offenses.

Adhikaraṇavāro niṭṭhito chaṭṭho.

The sixth Section on Legal Questions is concluded.

7. Samathavāro

7. The Section on Settlements

255. Kāyasaṃsaggaṃ [V 0.0175] sādiyanapaccayā āpattiyo sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammanti? Kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyanapaccayā āpattiyo sattannaṃ samathānaṃ tīhi samathehi sammanti – siyā sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca, siyā sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca…pe….

255. The offenses due to consenting to bodily contact, by how many of the seven settlements are they settled? The offenses due to consenting to bodily contact are settled by three of the seven settlements: sometimes by the procedure in the presence and by acting on an admission, or sometimes by the procedure in the presence and by covering over with grass… and so on.

Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjanapaccayā āpattiyo sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammanti? Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjanapaccayā āpattiyo sattannaṃ samathānaṃ tīhi samathehi sammanti – siyā sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca, siyā sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca.

The offenses due to eating after having requested curd, by how many of the seven settlements are they settled? The offenses due to eating after having requested curd are settled by three of the seven settlements: sometimes by the procedure in the presence and by acting on an admission, or sometimes by the procedure in the presence and by covering over with grass.

Samathavāro niṭṭhito sattamo.

The seventh Section on Settlements is concluded.

8. Samuccayavāro

8. 8. The Compendium Section

256. Kāyasaṃsaggaṃ [M 0.0155][V 0.0176] sādiyanapaccayā kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyanapaccayā pañca āpattiyo āpajjati. Avassutā bhikkhunī avassutassa purisapuggalassa adhakkhakaṃ ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalaṃ gahaṇaṃ sādiyati, āpatti pārājikassa; bhikkhu kāyena kāyaṃ āmasati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa; kāyena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti thullaccayassa[T 0.0222]; kāyapaṭibaddhena kāyapaṭibaddhaṃ āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa; aṅgulipatodake pācittiyaṃ – kāyasaṃsaggaṃ sādiyanapaccayā imā pañca āpattiyo āpajjati.

256. Due to consenting to physical contact, how many offenses does one fall into? Due to consenting to physical contact, one falls into five offenses. A lustful bhikkhunī consents to a lustful man’s grasping below the collarbone and above the circle of the knees: an offense of Pārājika. A bhikkhu touches body with body: an offense of Saṅghādisesa. With the body he touches what is connected to the body: an offense of Thullaccaya. With what is connected to the body he touches what is connected to the body: an offense of Dukkaṭa. For tickling with the fingers: an offense of Pācittiya. Due to consenting to physical contact, one falls into these five offenses.

Tā [V 0.0177] āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ kati vipattiyo bhajanti? Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katihi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā? Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti? Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ? Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammanti? Tā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ dve vipattiyo bhajanti – siyā sīlavipattiṃ, siyā ācāravipattiṃ. Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ pañcahi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā – siyā pārājikāpattikkhandhena, siyā saṅghādisesāpattikkhandhena, siyā thullaccayāpattikkhandhena, siyā pācittiyāpattikkhandhena, siyā dukkaṭāpattikkhandhena. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhanti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti, na vācato. Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ tīhi samathehi sammanti – siyā sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca, siyā sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca…pe….

Those offenses, how many of the four failures do they partake of? By how many of the seven groups of offenses are they included? From how many of the six origins of offenses do they arise? Which of the four legal questions is it? By how many of the seven settlements are they settled? Those offenses partake of two of the four failures: sometimes failure in virtue, and sometimes failure in conduct. They are included by five of the seven groups of offenses: sometimes by the group of Pārājika offenses, sometimes by the group of Saṅghādisesa offenses, sometimes by the group of Thullaccaya offenses, sometimes by the group of Pācittiya offenses, and sometimes by the group of Dukkaṭa offenses. From the six origins of offenses, they arise from one type of origin: from body and from mind, not from speech. Of the four legal questions, it is a legal question concerning offenses. They are settled by three of the seven settlements: sometimes by the procedure in the presence and by acting on an admission, or sometimes by the procedure in the presence and by covering over with grass… and so on.

Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjanapaccayā kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjanapaccayā dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhuñjissāmīti paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa; ajjhohāre [T 0.0223] ajjhohāre āpatti pāṭidesanīyassa – dadhiṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjanapaccayā imā dve āpattiyo āpajjati.

Due to eating after having requested curd, how many offenses does one fall into? Due to eating after having requested curd, one falls into two offenses. When one receives it thinking, 'I will eat,' it is an offense of wrong-doing; with every swallow, it is an offense requiring confession. Due to eating after having requested curd, one falls into these two offenses.

Tā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ kati vipattiyo bhajanti? Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katihi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā? Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti? Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ[M 0.0156]? Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katihi samathehi sammanti? Tā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ ekaṃ vipattiṃ bhajanti – ācāravipattiṃ. Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ dvīhi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā – siyā pāṭidesanīyāpattikkhandhena, siyā dukkaṭāpattikkhandhena. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ catūhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti – siyā kāyato samuṭṭhanti, na vācato na cittato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca samuṭṭhanti, na cittato; siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti na vācato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti. Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ, āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ tīhi samathehi sammanti – siyā sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca, siyā sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena cāti.

Those offenses, how many of the four kinds of failures do they partake of? By how many of the seven groups of offenses are they included? From how many of the six origins of offenses do they arise? Which of the four legal questions is it? By how many of the seven settlements are they settled? Those offenses partake of one of the four kinds of failures—failure in conduct. They are included by two of the seven groups of offenses—sometimes by the group of offenses requiring confession, and sometimes by the group of offenses of wrong-doing. They arise from four of the six origins of offenses—sometimes they arise from the body, not from speech nor from mind; sometimes they arise from body and speech, not from mind; sometimes they arise from body and mind, not from speech; sometimes they arise from body, speech, and mind. Of the four legal questions, it is a legal question concerning offenses. They are settled by three of the seven settlements—sometimes by the procedure in the presence and by acting on an admission, or sometimes by the procedure in the presence and by covering over with grass.

Samuccayavāro niṭṭhito aṭṭhamo. imassānantaraṃ porāṇasīhaḷapotthake evampi§dissati –§“tesamuddānaṃ –§kativāro ca vipattivāro ca, saṅgahavāro ca samuṭṭhānavāro. adhikaraṇavāro ca samathavāro ca, samuccayavāro ca ime satta vārā. ādito paññattivārena saha aṭṭhavārāti”iti.

The eighth Compendium Section is concluded.

Aṭṭha paccayavārā niṭṭhitā.

The eight Sections on Conditions are concluded.

Bhikkhunīvibhaṅge soḷasa mahāvārā niṭṭhitā.

The Sixteen Great Chapters in the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga are concluded.

Samuṭṭhānasīsasaṅkhepo

A Concise Account of the Headings of Origin

Samuṭṭhānassuddānaṃ

The Index of Origins

257.

257.

Aniccā [T 0.0224][P 5.0086][M 0.0157][V 0.0178] sabbe saṅkhārā, dukkhānattā ca saṅkhatā;

Nibbānañceva paññatti, anattā iti nicchayā.

All formations are impermanent; all conditioned things are suffering and also not-self. Nibbāna and concepts are determined to be not-self.

Buddhacande anuppanne, buddhādicce anuggate;

Tesaṃ sabhāgadhammānaṃ, nāmamattaṃ na nāyati.

When the Buddha-moon has not arisen, when the Buddha-sun has not risen, not even the mere name of those phenomena of a similar nature is known.

Dukkaraṃ vividhaṃ katvā, pūrayitvāna pāramī;

Uppajjanti mahāvīrā, cakkhubhūtā sabrahmake.

Having performed various difficult deeds and having fulfilled the perfections, the great heroes arise, having become the eye in the world with its Brahmās.

Te desayanti saddhammaṃ, dukkhahāniṃ sukhāvahaṃ;

Aṅgīraso sakyamuni, sabbabhūtānukampako.

They teach the good Dhamma, which ends suffering and brings happiness; the Radiant One, the Sage of the Sakyans, compassionate towards all beings,

Sabbasattuttamo sīho, piṭake tīṇi desayi;

Suttantamabhidhammañca, vinayañca mahāguṇaṃ.

the Lion, supreme among all beings, taught the three Piṭakas: the Suttanta, the Abhidhamma, and the Vinaya of great virtue.

Evaṃ nīyati saddhammo, vinayo yadi tiṭṭhati;

Ubhato ca vibhaṅgāni, khandhakā yā ca mātikā.

If the Vinaya endures, thus the good Dhamma also endures. There are the two Vibhaṅgas, the Khandhakas, and the Mātikā.

Mālā suttaguṇeneva, parivārena ganthitā;

Tasseva parivārassa, samuṭṭhānaṃ niyato kataṃ.

Just as a garland is strung together by a thread, so are these bound together by the Parivāra. In that same Parivāra, the fixed origin is established.

Sambhedaṃ [V 0.0179] nidānaṃ caññaṃ, sutte dissanti upari;

Tasmā sikkhe parivāraṃ, dhammakāmo supesaloti.

The combined origin, the source, and others are seen in the text above. Therefore, one who desires the Dhamma, being virtuous, should train in the Parivāra.

Terasasamuṭṭhānaṃ

The Thirteen Origins

Vibhaṅge dvīsu paññattaṃ, uddisanti uposathe;

Pavakkhāmi samuṭṭhānaṃ, yathāñāyaṃ suṇātha me.

Of the training rules laid down in the two Vibhaṅgas, which are recited on the Uposatha day, I shall declare their origin according to the proper method. Listen to me.

Pārājikaṃ [T 0.0225] yaṃ paṭhamaṃ, dutiyañca tato paraṃ;

Sañcarittānubhāsanañca, atirekañca cīvaraṃ.

The first Pārājika origin, and the second which follows; then the Sañcaritta origin, the Samanubhāsana origin, and the origin of the extra robe.

Lomāni padasodhammo, bhūtaṃ saṃvidhānena ca;

Theyyadesanacorī ca, ananuññātāya terasa.

The Eḷakalomā origin, the Padasodhamma origin, the Bhūtarocana origin, and the Saṃvidhāna origin; the Theyyasattha, Dhammadesanā, and Corīvuṭṭhāpana origins; together with the Ananuññāta origin, these are the thirteen.

Terasete samuṭṭhāna nayā, viññūhi cintitā.

Ekekasmiṃ samuṭṭhāne, sadisā idha dissare.

These thirteen methods of origin have been considered by the wise. In each single origin, similar cases are seen herein.

1. Paṭhamapārājikasamuṭṭhānaṃ

1. The First Pārājika Origin

258.

258.

Methunaṃ [M 0.0158] sukkasaṃsaggo, aniyatā paṭhamikā;

Pubbūpaparipācitā, raho bhikkhuniyā saha.

The training rules on: sexual intercourse, emission of semen, bodily contact; the first undetermined rule; approaching a man beforehand, ripening almsfood for a bhikkhunī; and sitting in a secluded place together with a bhikkhunī.

Sabhojane raho dve ca, aṅguli udake hasaṃ;

Pahāre [P 5.0087] uggire ceva, tepaññāsā ca sekhiyā.

The training rules on: intruding on a family at mealtime, the two rules on seclusion, poking with a finger, playing in the water, giving a blow, and raising a hand-weapon; and the fifty-three Sekhiya rules.

Adhakkhagāmāvassutā, talamaṭṭhañca suddhikā;

Vassaṃvuṭṭhā ca ovādaṃ, nānubandhe pavattiniṃ.

The training rules on: one with testicles, going to another village, and accepting food from a lustful person; on striking with the palm and applying lacquer; on accepting water purification; on having spent the rains retreat; on going for an exhortation; and on not following the preceptor.

Chasattati ime sikkhā, kāyamānasikā katā;

Sabbe ekasamuṭṭhānā, paṭhamaṃ pārājikaṃ yathā.

These seventy-six training rules are established as arising from body and mind. All have a single origin, just as the first Pārājika.

Paṭhamapārājikasamuṭṭhānaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

Here ends the section on the First Pārājika Origin.

2. Dutiyapārājikasamuṭṭhānaṃ

2. The Second Pārājika Origin

259.

259.

Adinnaṃ [V 0.0180] viggahuttari, duṭṭhullā attakāminaṃ;

Amūlā aññabhāgiyā, aniyatā dutiyikā.

The training rules on: taking what is not given; on killing a human being and on superhuman states; on coarse speech; on serving one's own desires; on a baseless accusation; on partaking of what is another's share; and the second undetermined rule.

Acchinde pariṇāmane, musā omasapesuṇā;

Duṭṭhullā pathavīkhaṇe, bhūtaṃ aññāya ujjhāpe.

The training rules on: snatching away a given robe; on diverting something to oneself; on false speech; on contemptuous speech and on slandering a bhikkhu; on reporting a coarse offense; on digging the earth; on destroying plant life; on prevarication; and on causing vexation.

Nikkaḍḍhanaṃ [T 0.0226] siñcanañca, āmisahetu bhuttāvī;

Ehi anādari bhiṃsā, apanidhe ca jīvitaṃ.

The training rules on: expelling from a monastery; sprinkling with water; for the sake of a material gain; the second rule on being formally refused; dismissing; disrespect; frightening a bhikkhu; hiding something away; and intentionally taking life.

Jānaṃ sappāṇakaṃ kammaṃ, ūnasaṃvāsanāsanā;

Sahadhammikavilekhā, moho amūlakena ca.

The training rules on: knowingly using water with living beings; on obstructing a formal act; on one under twenty years of age, on co-residing with an expelled one, and on associating with a novice who has been expelled; on being spoken to according to the Dhamma and on reviling; the Pācittiya rule on causing confusion; and on a baseless accusation of a subsequent offense.

Kukkuccaṃ dhammikaṃ cīvaraṃ, datvā kukkuccaṃ dhammikaṃ cīvaraṃ (sī.), kukkuccaṃ dhammikaṃ datvā (syā.) pariṇāmeyya puggale;

Kiṃ te akālaṃ acchinde, duggahī nirayena ca.

The training rules on: causing remorse; on complaining after giving consent; on complaining after giving a robe; on diverting something to an individual; the second rule on being under the influence of passion; on distributing robes out of season; on snatching away a robe after an exchange; on causing another to be vexed by a poorly grasped point; and on cursing.

Gaṇaṃ vibhaṅgaṃ dubbalaṃ, kathināphāsupassayaṃ;

Akkosacaṇḍī maccharī, gabbhinī ca pāyantiyā.

The training rules on: receiving a group robe; on distributing robes; on hoping for a robe for a weak person; on withdrawing the Kathina, on causing discomfort, and on a lodging; on abuse, on being fierce, and on being stingy with a family; on a pregnant woman; and on a nursing mother.

Dvevassaṃ [M 0.0159] sikkhā saṅghena, tayo ceva gihīgatā;

Kumāribhūtā tisso ca, ūnadvādasasammatā.

The training rule on training for two years; the training rule on not being appointed by the Saṅgha; the three training rules on one who was formerly married; the three training rules on one who was a maiden; and the training rules on ordaining one under twelve years of age and on ordaining one who has completed twelve years of age with the Saṅgha's approval.

Alaṃ tāva sokāvāsaṃ, chandā anuvassā ca dve;

Sikkhāpadā sattatime, samuṭṭhānā tikā katā.

The training rules on: 'that is enough'; on a dwelling of sorrow; on giving consent for a probationer; on ordaining every year; and the two rules on ordination. These seventy training rules are established as having a threefold origin.

Kāyacittena na vācā, vācācittaṃ na kāyikaṃ;

Tīhi dvārehi jāyanti, pārājikaṃ dutiyaṃ yathā.

They arise from body and mind, not from speech; from speech and mind, not from body; and from the three doors, just as the second Pārājika.

Dutiyapārājikasamuṭṭhānaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

Here ends the section on the Second Pārājika Origin.

3. Sañcarittasamuṭṭhānaṃ

3. The Sañcaritta Origin

260.

260.

Sañcarī [V 0.0181] kuṭi vihāro, dhovanañca paṭiggaho;
