The eighteenth section on ‘Are Settled’ and ‘Are Not Settled’ is concluded.

19. Samathādhikaraṇavāro

19. 19. The Section on Settlements and Legal Questions

309. Samathā [M 0.0200] samathehi sammanti? Samathā adhikaraṇehi sammanti? Adhikaraṇā samathehi sammanti? Adhikaraṇā adhikaraṇehi sammanti?

309. Are settlements settled by settlements? Are settlements settled by legal questions? Are legal questions settled by settlements? Are legal questions settled by legal questions?

Siyā [P 5.0110] samathā samathehi sammanti, siyā samathā samathehi na sammanti. Siyā samathā adhikaraṇehi sammanti, siyā samathā adhikaraṇehi na sammanti. Siyā adhikaraṇā samathehi sammanti, siyā adhikaraṇā samathehi na sammanti. Siyā adhikaraṇā adhikaraṇehi sammanti, siyā adhikaraṇā adhikaraṇehi na sammanti.

Some settlements are settled by settlements; some settlements are not settled by settlements. Some settlements are settled by legal questions; some settlements are not settled by legal questions. Some legal questions are settled by settlements; some legal questions are not settled by settlements. Some legal questions are settled by legal questions; some legal questions are not settled by legal questions.

310. Kathaṃ siyā samathā samathehi sammanti, kathaṃ siyā samathā samathehi na sammanti? Yebhuyyasikā sammukhāvinayena sammati; sativinayena na sammati, amūḷhavinayena na sammati, paṭiññātakaraṇena na sammati, tassapāpiyasikāya na sammati, tiṇavatthārakena na sammati.

310. How is it that some settlements are settled by settlements, and how is it that some settlements are not settled by settlements? The settlement by majority is settled by the settlement in the presence; it is not settled by the settlement by mindfulness, not by the settlement for one who is no longer insane, not by the settlement by acknowledgment, not by the settlement for one of bad character, not by the settlement by covering over as with grass.

Sativinayo sammukhāvinayena sammati; amūḷhavinayena na sammati, paṭiññātakaraṇena na [V 0.0223] sammāti, tassapāpiyasikāya na sammati, tiṇavatthārakena na sammati, yebhuyyasikāya na sammati.

The settlement by mindfulness is settled by the settlement in the presence; it is not settled by the settlement for one who is no longer insane, not by the settlement by acknowledgment, not by the settlement for one of bad character, not by the settlement by covering over as with grass, not by the settlement by majority.

Amūḷhavinayo sammukhāvinayena sammati; paṭiññātakaraṇena na sammati, tassapāpiyasikāya [T 0.0281] na sammati, tiṇavatthārakena na sammati, yebhuyyasikāya na sammati, sativinayena na sammati.

The settlement for one who is no longer insane is settled by the settlement in the presence; it is not settled by the settlement by acknowledgment, not by the settlement for one of bad character, not by the settlement by covering over as with grass, not by the settlement by majority, not by the settlement by mindfulness.

Paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ sammukhāvinayena sammati; tassapāpiyasikāya na sammati, tiṇavatthārakena na sammati, yebhuyyasikāya na sammati, sativinayena na sammati, amūḷhavinayena na sammati.

The settlement by acknowledgment is settled by the settlement in the presence; it is not settled by the settlement for one of bad character, not by the settlement by majority, not by the settlement by mindfulness, not by the settlement for one who is no longer insane.

Tassapāpiyasikā sammukhāvinayena sammati; tiṇavatthārakena na sammati, yebhuyyasikāya na sammati, sativinayena na sammati, amūḷhavinayena na sammati, paṭiññātakaraṇena na sammati.

The settlement for one of bad character is settled by the settlement in the presence; it is not settled by the settlement by covering over as with grass, not by the settlement by majority, not by the settlement by mindfulness, not by the settlement for one who is no longer insane, not by the settlement by acknowledgment.

Tiṇavatthārako sammukhāvinayena sammati; yebhuyyasikāya na sammati, sativinayena na sammati, amūḷhavinayena na sammati, paṭiññātakaraṇena na sammati, tassapāpiyasikāya na sammati. Evaṃ siyā samathā samathehi sammanti. Evaṃ siyā samathā samathehi na sammanti.

The settlement by covering over as with grass is settled by the settlement in the presence; it is not settled by the settlement by majority, not by the settlement by mindfulness, not by the settlement for one who is no longer insane, not by the settlement by acknowledgment, not by the settlement for one of bad character. Thus, in some cases, settlements are settled by settlements. Thus, in some cases, settlements are not settled by settlements.

311. Kathaṃ [M 0.0201] siyā samathā adhikaraṇehi sammanti, kathaṃ siyā samathā adhikaraṇehi na sammanti? Sammukhāvinayo vivādādhikaraṇena na sammati, anuvādādhikaraṇena na sammati, āpattādhikaraṇena na sammati; kiccādhikaraṇena sammati.

311. How is it that some settlements are settled by legal questions, and how is it that some settlements are not settled by legal questions? The settlement in the presence is not settled by a legal question of dispute, not by a legal question of accusation, not by a legal question of offense; it is settled by a legal question of duties.

Yebhuyyasikā vivādādhikaraṇena na sammati, anuvādādhikaraṇena na sammati, āpattādhikaraṇena na sammati; kiccādhikaraṇena sammati.

The settlement by majority is not settled by a legal question of dispute, not by a legal question of accusation, not by a legal question of offense; it is settled by a legal question of duties.

Sativinayo vivādādhikaraṇena na sammati, anuvādādhikaraṇena na sammati, āpattādhikaraṇena na sammati; kiccādhikaraṇena sammati.

The settlement by mindfulness is not settled by a legal question of dispute, not by a legal question of accusation, not by a legal question of offense; it is settled by a legal question of duties.

Amūḷhavinayo [T 0.0282][V 0.0224] vivādādhikaraṇena na sammati, anuvādādhikaraṇena na sammati, āpattādhikaraṇena na sammati; kiccādhikaraṇena sammati.

The settlement for one who is no longer insane is not settled by a legal question of dispute, not by a legal question of accusation, not by a legal question of offense; it is settled by a legal question of duties.

Paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ vivādādhikaraṇena na sammati, anuvādādhikaraṇena na sammati, āpattādhikaraṇena na sammati; kiccādhikaraṇena sammati.

The settlement by acknowledgment is not settled by a legal question of dispute, not by a legal question of accusation, not by a legal question of offense; it is settled by a legal question of duties.

Tassapāpiyasikā vivādādhikaraṇena na sammati, anuvādādhikaraṇena na sammati, āpattādhikaraṇena na sammati; kiccādhikaraṇena sammati.

The settlement for one of bad character is not settled by a legal question of dispute, not by a legal question of accusation, not by a legal question of offense; it is settled by a legal question of duties.

Tiṇavatthārako vivādādhikaraṇena na sammati, anuvādādhikaraṇena na sammati, āpattādhikaraṇena na sammati; kiccādhikaraṇena sammati. Evaṃ siyā samathā adhikaraṇehi sammanti. Evaṃ siyā samathā adhikaraṇehi na sammanti.

The settlement by covering over as with grass is not settled by a legal question of dispute, not by a legal question of accusation, not by a legal question of offense; it is settled by a legal question of duties. Thus, in some cases, settlements are settled by legal questions. Thus, in some cases, settlements are not settled by legal questions.

312. Kathaṃ siyā adhikaraṇā samathehi sammanti, kathaṃ siyā adhikaraṇā samathehi na sammanti? Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ sammukhāvinayena ca yebhuyyasikāya ca sammati; sativinayena ca amūḷhavinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca tassapāpiyasikāya ca tiṇavatthārakena ca na sammati.

312. How is it that some legal questions are settled by settlements, and how is it that some legal questions are not settled by settlements? A legal question of dispute is settled by the settlement in the presence and by the settlement by majority; it is not settled by the settlement by mindfulness, by the settlement for one who is no longer insane, by the settlement by acknowledgment, by the settlement for one of bad character, and by the settlement by covering over as with grass.

Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ sammukhāvinayena ca sativinayena ca amūḷhavinayena ca tassapāpiyasikāya ca sammati; yebhuyyasikāya ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca na sammati.

A legal question of accusation is settled by the settlement in the presence, by the settlement by mindfulness, by the settlement for one who is no longer insane, and by the settlement for one of bad character; it is not settled by the settlement by majority, by the settlement by acknowledgment, and by the settlement by covering over as with grass.

Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca sammati; yebhuyyasikāya ca sativinayena ca amūḷhavinayena ca tassapāpiyasikāya ca na sammati.

A legal question of offense is settled by the settlement in the presence, by the settlement by acknowledgment, and by the settlement by covering over as with grass; it is not settled by the settlement by majority, by the settlement by mindfulness, by the settlement for one who is no longer insane, and by the settlement for one of bad character.

Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ [M 0.0202] sammukhāvinayena sammati[T 0.0283]; yebhuyyasikāya ca sativinayena ca amūḷhavinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca tassapāpiyasikāya [P 5.0111] tiṇavatthārakena ca na sammati. Evaṃ siyā adhikaraṇā samathehi sammanti. Evaṃ siyā adhikaraṇā samathehi na sammanti.

An issue of duties is settled by the procedure for settlement 'in the presence'; it is not settled by the procedure for settlement 'by a majority', by the procedure for settlement 'of mindfulness', by the procedure for settlement for one who is not of unsound mind, by the procedure for settlement of 'acting on an admission', by the procedure for settlement for one's bad character, nor by the procedure for settlement of 'covering with grass'. Thus, some issues are settled by procedures for settlement. Thus, some issues are not settled by procedures for settlement.

313. Kathaṃ [V 0.0225] siyā adhikaraṇā adhikaraṇehi sammanti? Kathaṃ siyā adhikaraṇā adhikaraṇehi na sammanti? Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ vivādādhikaraṇena na sammati, anuvādādhikaraṇena na sammati, āpattādhikaraṇena na sammati; kiccādhikaraṇena sammati.

313. How is it that some issues are settled by issues? How is it that some issues are not settled by issues? An issue of dispute is not settled by an issue of dispute, not by an issue of accusation, not by an issue of an offense; it is settled by an issue of duties.

Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ vivādādhikaraṇena na sammati, anuvādādhikaraṇena na sammati, āpattādhikaraṇena na sammati; kiccādhikaraṇena sammati.

An issue of accusation is not settled by an issue of dispute, not by an issue of accusation, not by an issue of an offense; it is settled by an issue of duties.

Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ vivādādhikaraṇena na sammati, anuvādādhikaraṇena na sammati, āpattādhikaraṇena na sammati; kiccādhikaraṇena sammati.

An issue of an offense is not settled by an issue of dispute, not by an issue of accusation, not by an issue of an offense; it is settled by an issue of duties.

Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ vivādādhikaraṇena na sammati, anuvādādhikaraṇena na sammati, āpattādhikaraṇena na sammati; kiccādhikaraṇena sammati. Evaṃ siyā adhikaraṇā adhikaraṇehi sammanti. Evaṃ siyā adhikaraṇā adhikaraṇehi na sammanti.

An issue of duties is not settled by an issue of dispute, not by an issue of accusation, not by an issue of an offense; it is settled by an issue of duties. Thus, some issues are settled by issues. Thus, some issues are not settled by issues.

Chāpi samathā cattāropi adhikaraṇā sammukhāvinayena sammanti; sammukhāvinayo na kenaci sammati.

The six procedures for settlement and the four issues are settled by the procedure of 'in the presence'; the procedure of 'in the presence' is not settled by any issue or any procedure for settlement.

Samathādhikaraṇavāro niṭṭhito ekūnavīsatimo.

The nineteenth Section on Procedures for Settlement and Issues is finished.

20. Samuṭṭhāpanavāro

20. 20. The Section on Origination

314. Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ [T 0.0284] catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ samuṭṭhāpeti? Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ na katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ samuṭṭhāpeti; apica, vivādādhikaraṇapaccayā cattāro adhikaraṇā jāyanti. Yathā kathaṃ viya? cūḷava. 215; pari. 348 ādayo Idha bhikkhū vivadanti – “dhammoti vā, adhammoti vā, vinayoti vā, avinayoti vā, abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatenāti vā, bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatenāti vā, anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti vā, āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti [M 0.0203] vā, apaññattaṃ tathāgatenāti vā, paññattaṃ tathāgatenāti vā, āpattīti vā, anāpattīti vā, lahukā āpattīti vā, garukā āpattīti vā, sāvasesā āpattīti vā, anavasesā āpattīti vā, duṭṭhullā āpattīti vā aduṭṭhullā āpattīti vā”. Yaṃ tattha bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo nānāvādo aññathāvādo vipaccatāya vohāro medhakaṃ medhagaṃ (ka.), idaṃ vuccati vivādādhikaraṇaṃ. Vivādādhikaraṇe saṅgho vivadati. Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ [V 0.0226] vivadamāno anuvadati. Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ anuvadamāno āpattiṃ āpajjati āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Tāya āpattiyā saṅgho kammaṃ karoti kiccādhikaraṇaṃ. Evaṃ vivādādhikaraṇapaccayā cattāro adhikaraṇā jāyanti.

314. An issue of dispute, among the four issues, which issue does it cause to arise? An issue of dispute, among the four issues, does not cause any issue to arise; but rather, due to an issue of dispute as a condition, the four issues arise. How so? Herein, monks dispute: 'This is Dhamma,' or 'This is not Dhamma'; 'This is Vinaya,' or 'This is not Vinaya'; 'This was not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata,' or 'This was spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata'; 'This was not practiced by the Tathāgata,' or 'This was practiced by the Tathāgata'; 'This was not laid down by the Tathāgata,' or 'This was laid down by the Tathāgata'; 'This is an offense,' or 'This is not an offense'; 'This is a light offense,' or 'This is a grave offense'; 'This is an offense with a remainder,' or 'This is an offense without a remainder'; 'This is a gross offense,' or 'This is not a gross offense.' Whatever quarreling, contention, strife, dispute, differing opinions, opposing views, verbal conflict for the sake of mental distress, or wrangling there is in that, this is called an issue of dispute. When there is an issue of dispute, the Saṅgha disputes, which is an issue of dispute. While disputing, one makes an accusation, which is an issue of accusation. While making an accusation, one commits an offense, which is an issue of an offense. On account of that offense, the Saṅgha performs a formal act, which is an issue of duties. Thus, due to an issue of dispute as a condition, the four issues arise.

315. Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ samuṭṭhāpeti? Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ na katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ samuṭṭhāpeti; apica, anuvādādhikaraṇapaccayā cattāro adhikaraṇā [T 0.0285] jāyanti. Yathā kathaṃ viya? cūḷava. 215; pari. 348 ādayo Idha bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ anuvadanti sīlavipattiyā vā ācāravipattiyā vā diṭṭhivipattiyā vā ājīvavipattiyā vā. Yo tattha anuvādo anuvadanā anullapanā anubhaṇanā anusampavaṅkatā abbhussahanatā anubalappadānaṃ, idaṃ vuccati anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ. Anuvādādhikaraṇe saṅgho vivadati. Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ vivadamāno anuvadati. Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ anuvadamāno āpattiṃ āpajjati āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Tāya āpattiyā saṅgho kammaṃ karoti kiccādhikaraṇaṃ. Evaṃ anuvādādhikaraṇapaccayā cattāro adhikaraṇā jāyanti.

315. An issue of accusation, among the four issues, which issue does it cause to arise? An issue of accusation, among the four issues, does not cause any issue to arise; but rather, due to an issue of accusation as a condition, the four issues arise. How so? Herein, monks accuse a monk of a corruption of virtue, a corruption of conduct, a corruption of view, or a corruption of livelihood. Therein, whatever accusation, act of accusing, speaking, stating, persistent insinuation, exertion, or giving of support there is, this is called an issue of accusation. When there is an issue of accusation, the Saṅgha disputes, which is an issue of dispute. While disputing, one makes an accusation, which is an issue of accusation. While making an accusation, one commits an offense, which is an issue of an offense. On account of that offense, the Saṅgha performs a formal act, which is an issue of duties. Thus, due to an issue of accusation as a condition, the four issues arise.

316. Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ samuṭṭhāpeti? Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ na katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ samuṭṭhāpeti; apica, āpattādhikaraṇapaccayā cattāro adhikaraṇā jāyanti. Yathā kathaṃ viya? Pañcapi āpattikkhandhā āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, sattapi āpattikkhandhā āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, idaṃ vuccati āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Āpattādhikaraṇe saṅgho vivadati. Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ vivadamāno [P 5.0112] anuvadati. Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ anuvadamāno āpattiṃ āpajjati āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Tāya [M 0.0204] āpattiyā saṅgho kammaṃ karoti kiccādhikaraṇaṃ. Evaṃ āpattādhikaraṇapaccayā cattāro adhikaraṇā jāyanti.

316. An issue of an offense, among the four issues, which issue does it cause to arise? An issue of an offense, among the four issues, does not cause any issue to arise; but rather, due to an issue of an offense as a condition, the four issues arise. How so? The five groups of offenses are an issue of an offense; the seven groups of offenses are also an issue of an offense. This is called an issue of an offense. When there is an issue of an offense, the Saṅgha disputes, which is an issue of dispute. While disputing, one makes an accusation, which is an issue of accusation. While making an accusation, one commits an offense, which is an issue of an offense. On account of that offense, the Saṅgha performs a formal act, which is an issue of duties. Thus, due to an issue of an offense as a condition, the four issues arise.

317. Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ samuṭṭhāpeti[T 0.0286]? Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ na katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ samuṭṭhāpeti, apica kiccādhikaraṇapaccayā cattāro adhikaraṇā jāyanti. Yathā kathaṃ viya? Yā saṅghassa kiccayatā karaṇīyatā apalokanakammaṃ ñattikammaṃ ñattidutiyakammaṃ ñatticatutthakammaṃ, idaṃ vuccati kiccādhikaraṇaṃ. Kiccādhikaraṇe saṅgho vivadati. Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ vivadamāno anuvadati. Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ anuvadamāno āpattiṃ āpajjati āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Tāya āpattiyā [V 0.0227] saṅgho kammaṃ karoti kiccādhikaraṇaṃ. Evaṃ kiccādhikaraṇapaccayā cattāro adhikaraṇā jāyanti.

317. A legal issue concerning duties—among the four legal issues, which legal issue does it give rise to? A legal issue concerning duties—among the four legal issues, it does not give rise to any legal issue. But in fact, due to a legal issue concerning duties as a cause, the four legal issues arise. How so? Whatever is the Sangha's duty, what should be done, an act of announcement, an act of a motion, an act of a motion with one announcement, or an act of a motion with three announcements—this is called a legal issue concerning duties. Regarding a legal issue concerning duties, the Sangha disputes; this is a legal issue arising from disputes. While disputing, one accuses; this is a legal issue arising from accusations. While accusing, one commits an offense; this is a legal issue arising from offenses. On account of that offense, the Sangha performs an act; this is a legal issue concerning duties. Thus, due to a legal issue concerning duties as a cause, the four legal issues arise.

Samuṭṭhāpanavāro niṭṭhito vīsatimo.

The twentieth section on origination is finished.

21. Bhajativāro

21. 21. The Section on Association

318. Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ bhajati? Katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ upanissitaṃ? Katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ pariyāpannaṃ? Katamena adhikaraṇena saṅgahitaṃ?

318. A legal issue arising from disputes—among the four legal issues, to which legal issue does it belong? Which legal issue is it dependent on? In which legal issue is it included? By which legal issue is it classified?

Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ bhajati? Katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ upanissitaṃ? Katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ pariyāpannaṃ? Katamena adhikaraṇena saṅgahitaṃ?

A legal issue arising from accusations—among the four legal issues, to which legal issue does it belong? Which legal issue is it dependent on? In which legal issue is it included? By which legal issue is it classified?

Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ bhajati? Katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ upanissitaṃ? Katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ pariyāpannaṃ? Katamena adhikaraṇena saṅgahitaṃ?

A legal issue arising from offenses—among the four legal issues, to which legal issue does it belong? Which legal issue is it dependent on? In which legal issue is it included? By which legal issue is it classified?

Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ bhajati? Katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ upanissitaṃ? Katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ pariyāpannaṃ? Katamena adhikaraṇena [T 0.0287] saṅgahitaṃ?

A legal issue concerning duties—among the four legal issues, to which legal issue does it belong? Which legal issue is it dependent on? In which legal issue is it included? By which legal issue is it classified?

Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ vivādādhikaraṇaṃ bhajati, vivādādhikaraṇaṃ upanissitaṃ, vivādādhikaraṇaṃ pariyāpannaṃ, vivādādhikaraṇena saṅgahitaṃ.

A legal issue arising from disputes—among the four legal issues—belongs to a legal issue arising from disputes, is dependent on a legal issue arising from disputes, is included in a legal issue arising from disputes, and is classified by a legal issue arising from disputes.

Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ [M 0.0205] catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ bhajati, anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ upanissitaṃ, anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ pariyāpannaṃ, anuvādādhikaraṇena saṅgahitaṃ.

A legal issue arising from accusations—among the four legal issues—belongs to a legal issue arising from accusations, is dependent on a legal issue arising from accusations, is included in a legal issue arising from accusations, and is classified by a legal issue arising from accusations.

Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ āpattādhikaraṇaṃ bhajati, āpattādhikaraṇaṃ upanissitaṃ, āpattādhikaraṇaṃ pariyāpannaṃ, āpattādhikaraṇena saṅgahitaṃ.

A legal issue arising from offenses—among the four legal issues—belongs to a legal issue arising from offenses, is dependent on a legal issue arising from offenses, is included in a legal issue arising from offenses, and is classified by a legal issue arising from offenses.

Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ kiccādhikaraṇaṃ bhajati, kiccādhikaraṇaṃ upanissitaṃ, kiccādhikaraṇaṃ pariyāpannaṃ, kiccādhikaraṇena saṅgahitaṃ.

A legal issue concerning duties—among the four legal issues—pertains to a legal issue concerning duties, is dependent on a legal issue concerning duties, is included in a legal issue concerning duties, and is classified by a legal issue concerning duties.

319. Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ [V 0.0228] sattannaṃ samathānaṃ kati samathe bhajati, kati samathe upanissitaṃ, kati samathe pariyāpannaṃ, katihi samathehi saṅgahitaṃ, katihi samathehi sammati?

319. A legal issue arising from disputes—among the seven settlements, to how many settlements does it pertain? On how many settlements is it dependent? In how many settlements is it included? By how many settlements is it classified? By how many settlements is it settled?

Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ sattannaṃ samathānaṃ kati samathe bhajati, kati samathe upanissitaṃ, kati samathe pariyāpannaṃ, katihi samathehi saṅgahitaṃ, katihi samathehi sammati?

A legal issue arising from accusations—among the seven settlements, to how many settlements does it pertain? On how many settlements is it dependent? In how many settlements is it included? By how many settlements is it classified? By how many settlements is it settled?

Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ sattannaṃ samathānaṃ kati samathe bhajati, kati samathe upanissitaṃ, kati samathe pariyāpannaṃ, katihi samathehi saṅgahitaṃ, katihi samathehi sammati?

A legal issue arising from an offense—among the seven settlements, to how many settlements does it pertain? On how many settlements is it dependent? In how many settlements is it included? By how many settlements is it classified? By how many settlements is it settled?

Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ sattannaṃ samathānaṃ kati samathe bhajati, kati samathe upanissitaṃ, kati samathe pariyāpannaṃ, katihi samathehi saṅgahitaṃ, katihi samathehi sammati?

A legal issue concerning duties—among the seven settlements, to how many settlements does it pertain? On how many settlements is it dependent? In how many settlements is it included? By how many settlements is it classified? By how many settlements is it settled?

Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ sattannaṃ samathānaṃ dve samathe bhajati, dve samathe upanissitaṃ, dve samathe pariyāpannaṃ, dvīhi samathehi saṅgahitaṃ, dvīhi samathehi sammati – sammukhāvinayena ca yebhuyyasikāya ca.

A legal issue arising from disputes, among the seven settlements, pertains to two settlements, is dependent on two settlements, is included in two settlements, is classified by two settlements, and is settled by two settlements: by the procedure in the presence and by the decision by majority.

Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ sattannaṃ samathānaṃ cattāro samathe bhajati, cattāro samathe upanissitaṃ, cattāro samathe pariyāpannaṃ, catūhi samathehi saṅgahitaṃ, catūhi samathehi sammati – sammukhāvinayena ca sativinayena [T 0.0288] ca amūḷhavinayena ca tassapāpiyasikāya ca.

A legal issue arising from accusations, among the seven settlements, pertains to four settlements, is dependent on four settlements, is included in four settlements, is classified by four settlements, and is settled by four settlements: by the procedure in the presence, by the procedure of mindfulness, by the procedure for one who is no longer confused, and by the procedure for his bad character.

Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ [M 0.0206] sattannaṃ samathānaṃ tayo samathe bhajati, tayo samathe upanissitaṃ, tayo samathe pariyāpannaṃ, tīhi samathehi saṅgahitaṃ tīhi samathehi sammati – sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena [P 5.0113] tiṇavatthārakena ca.

A legal issue arising from an offense, among the seven settlements, pertains to three settlements, is dependent on three settlements, is included in three settlements, is classified by three settlements, and is settled by three settlements: by the procedure in the presence, by the procedure of acting on an admission, and by the procedure of covering with grass.

Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ sattannaṃ samathānaṃ ekaṃ samathaṃ bhajati, ekaṃ samathaṃ upanissitaṃ, ekaṃ samathaṃ pariyāpannaṃ, ekena samathena saṅgahitaṃ, ekena samathena sammati – sammukhāvinayenāti.

A legal issue concerning duties, among the seven settlements, pertains to one settlement, is dependent on one settlement, is included in one settlement, is classified by one settlement, and is settled by one settlement: by the procedure in the presence.

Bhajativāro niṭṭhito ekavīsatimo.

The Bhajativāra, the twenty-first section, is finished.

Samathabhedo niṭṭhito.

The Analysis of Settlements is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Adhikaraṇaṃ [V 0.0229] pariyāyaṃ, sādhāraṇā ca bhāgiyā;

Samathā sādhāraṇikā, samathassa tabbhāgiyā.

The Categories of Issues section, the Common section, and the Specific section; the Common to Settlements section, and the Specific to a Settlement section.

Samathā sammukhā ceva, vinayena kusalena ca;

Yattha samathasaṃsaṭṭhā, sammanti na sammanti ca.

The Settlements and Proceeding in Presence section, the Vinaya section, and the Skillful section; the 'Where', 'Settlement', and 'Associated' sections; the 'Is Settled' section, and the 'Is Not Settled' section.

Samathādhikaraṇañceva, samuṭṭhānaṃ bhajanti cāti.

The Settlements and Issues section, the Arising section, and the Association section. Thus ends the summary.

Khandhakapucchāvāro

The Section of Questions on the Khandhakas

320.

320.

Upasampadaṃ [T 0.0289][P 5.0114][M 0.0207][V 0.0230] pucchissaṃ sanidānaṃ saniddesaṃ;

Samukkaṭṭhapadānaṃ kati āpattiyo;

Upasampadaṃ vissajjissaṃ sanidānaṃ saniddesaṃ;

Samukkaṭṭhapadānaṃ dve āpattiyo.

I will ask about the Upasampadākkhandhaka, with its origin story and explanation: how many offenses are there for the terms set forth therein? I will answer concerning the Upasampadākkhandhaka, with its origin story and explanation: there are two offenses for the terms set forth therein.

Uposathaṃ pucchissaṃ sanidānaṃ saniddesaṃ;

Samukkaṭṭhapadānaṃ kati āpattiyo;

Uposathaṃ vissajjissaṃ sanidānaṃ saniddesaṃ;

Samukkaṭṭhapadānaṃ tisso āpattiyo.

I will ask about the Uposathakkhandhaka, with its origin story and explanation: of the terms set forth therein, how many offenses are there? I will answer concerning the Uposathakkhandhaka, with its origin story and explanation: of the terms set forth therein, there are three offenses.

Vassūpanāyikaṃ pucchissaṃ sanidānaṃ saniddesaṃ;

Samukkaṭṭhapadānaṃ kati āpattiyo;

Vassūpanāyikaṃ vissajjissaṃ sanidānaṃ saniddesaṃ;

Samukkaṭṭhapadānaṃ ekā āpatti.

I will ask about the Vassūpanāyikakkhandhaka, with its origin story and explanation: of the terms set forth therein, how many offenses are there? I will answer concerning the Vassūpanāyikakkhandhaka, with its origin story and explanation: of the terms set forth therein, there is one offense.

Pavāraṇaṃ pucchissaṃ sanidānaṃ saniddesaṃ;

Samukkaṭṭhapadānaṃ kati āpattiyo;

Pavāraṇaṃ vissajjissaṃ sanidānaṃ saniddesaṃ;

Samukkaṭṭhapadānaṃ tisso āpattiyo.

I will ask about the Pavāraṇākkhandhaka, with its origin story and explanation: of the terms set forth therein, how many offenses are there? I will answer concerning the Pavāraṇākkhandhaka, with its origin story and explanation: of the terms set forth therein, there are three offenses.

Cammasaññuttaṃ pucchissaṃ sanidānaṃ saniddesaṃ;

Samukkaṭṭhapadānaṃ kati āpattiyo;

Cammasaññuttaṃ [T 0.0290][V 0.0231] vissajjissaṃ sanidānaṃ saniddesaṃ;

Samukkaṭṭhapadānaṃ tisso āpattiyo.

I will ask about the Cammakkhandhaka, with its origin story and explanation: of the terms set forth therein, how many offenses are there? I will answer concerning the Cammakkhandhaka, with its origin story and explanation: of the terms set forth therein, there are three offenses.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Upasampadūposatho[V 0.0234], vassūpanāyikapavāraṇā;

Cammabhesajjakathinā, cīvaraṃ campeyyakena ca.

Higher Ordination and Uposatha, Entering the Rains and Invitation; Leather, Medicines, and Kaṭhina, Robes, and also Campeyya.

Kosambakkhandhakaṃ kammaṃ, pārivāsisamuccayā;

Samathakhuddakā senā, saṅghabhedaṃ samācāro;

Ṭhapanaṃ bhikkhunikkhandhaṃ, pañcasattasatena cāti.

The Kosambaka Chapter, the Chapter on Formal Acts, Probation and Accumulation; Settlement and Minor Matters, Lodgings, Schism, and Conduct; Suspension, the Chapter on Bhikkhunīs, and also the Five Hundred and the Seven Hundred.

Ekuttarikanayo

The Gradual Method

1. Ekakavāro

1. The Section of Ones

321. Āpattikarā [T 0.0294][P 5.0115][M 0.0211][V 0.0235] dhammā jānitabbā. Anāpattikarā dhammā jānitabbā. Āpatti jānitabbā. Anāpatti jānitabbā. Lahukā āpatti jānitabbā. Garukā āpatti jānitabbā. Sāvasesā āpatti jānitabbā. Anavasesā āpatti jānitabbā. Duṭṭhullā āpatti jānitabbā. Aduṭṭhullā āpatti jānitabbā. Sappaṭikammā āpatti jānitabbā. Appaṭikammā āpatti jānitabbā. Desanāgāminī āpatti jānitabbā. Adesanāgāminī āpatti jānitabbā. Antarāyikā āpatti jānitabbā. Anantarāyikā āpatti jānitabbā. Sāvajjapaññatti āpatti jānitabbā. Anavajjapaññatti āpatti jānitabbā. Kiriyato samuṭṭhitā āpatti jānitabbā. Akiriyato samuṭṭhitā āpatti jānitabbā. Kiriyākiriyato samuṭṭhitā āpatti jānitabbā. Pubbāpatti jānitabbā. Aparāpatti jānitabbā. Pubbāpattīnaṃ antarāpatti jānitabbā. Aparāpattīnaṃ antarāpatti jānitabbā. Desitā gaṇanūpagā āpatti jānitabbā. Desitā na gaṇanūpagā āpatti jānitabbā. Paññatti jānitabbā. Anupaññatti jānitabbā. Anuppannapaññatti jānitabbā. Sabbatthapaññatti jānitabbā. Padesapaññatti jānitabbā. Sādhāraṇapaññatti jānitabbā[T 0.0295]. Asādhāraṇapaññatti jānitabbā. Ekatopaññatti jānitabbā. Ubhatopaññatti jānitabbā. Thullavajjā āpatti jānitabbā. Athullavajjā āpatti jānitabbā. Gihipaṭisaṃyuttā āpatti jānitabbā. Na gihipaṭisaṃyuttā āpatti jānitabbā. Niyatā āpatti jānitabbā. Aniyatā āpatti jānitabbā. Ādikaro puggalo jānitabbo. Anādikaro puggalo jānitabbo. Adhiccāpattiko puggalo jānitabbo. Abhiṇhāpattiko puggalo jānitabbo. Codako puggalo jānitabbo. Cuditako puggalo jānitabbo. Adhammacodako puggalo jānitabbo. Adhammacuditako puggalo jānitabbo. Dhammacodako puggalo jānitabbo. Dhammacuditako puggalo jānitabbo[V 0.0236]. Niyato puggalo jānitabbo. Aniyato puggalo jānitabbo. Abhabbāpattiko puggalo jānitabbo. Bhabbāpattiko puggalo jānitabbo. Ukkhittako puggalo jānitabbo. Anukkhittako puggalo jānitabbo. Nāsitako puggalo [M 0.0212] jānitabbo. Anāsitako puggalo jānitabbo. Samānasaṃvāsako puggalo jānitabbo. Asamānasaṃvāsako puggalo jānitabbo. Ṭhapanaṃ jānitabbanti.

321. Things that cause an offense should be known. Things that do not cause an offense should be known. An offense should be known. A non-offense should be known. A light offense should be known. A heavy offense should be known. An offense with a remainder should be known. An offense without a remainder should be known. A gross offense should be known. A non-gross offense should be known. An offense that has a remedy should be known. An offense that has no remedy should be known. An offense resolved by confession should be known. An offense not resolved by confession should be known. An obstructive offense should be known. A non-obstructive offense should be known. An offense of a blameworthy formulation should be known. An offense of a blameless formulation should be known. An offense arising from an action should be known. An offense arising from inaction should be known. An offense arising from both action and inaction should be known. A prior offense should be known. A subsequent offense should be known. An intermediate offense among prior offenses should be known. An intermediate offense among subsequent offenses should be known. An offense confessed and included in the count should be known. An offense confessed but not included in the count should be known. The original formulation should be known. The supplementary formulation should be known. The formulation for the unarisen should be known. The formulation applicable everywhere should be known. The formulation for a specific region should be known. The common formulation should be known. The uncommon formulation should be known. The formulation for one side should be known. The formulation for both sides should be known. An offense concerning a gross fault should be known. An offense concerning a non-gross fault should be known. An offense connected with laypersons should be known. An offense not connected with laypersons should be known. A fixed offense should be known. An unfixed offense should be known. An originator should be known. A person who causes a supplementary formulation should be known. An occasional offender should be known. A frequent offender should be known. An accuser should be known. An accused person should be known. An unlawful accuser should be known. An unlawfully accused person should be known. A lawful accuser should be known. A lawfully accused person should be known. A fixed person should be known. An unfixed person should be known. A person incapable of incurring an offense should be known. A person capable of incurring an offense should be known. A suspended person should be known. A non-suspended person should be known. An expelled person should be known. A non-expelled person should be known. A person in communion should be known. A person not in communion should be known. The setting aside of the Pātimokkha should be known.

Ekakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Single Section is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of that is:

Karā āpatti lahukā, sāvasesā ca duṭṭhullā;

Paṭikammadesanā [T 0.0296] ca, antarā vajjakiriyaṃ.

Causing an offense, offense, light, with a remainder, and gross; with a remedy and by confession, obstructive, blameworthy, and from an action.

Kiriyākiriyaṃ pubbā, antarā gaṇanūpagā;

Paññatti anānuppanna, sabbasādhāraṇā ca ekato paññattānuppannā sabbā, sādhāraṇā ca ekato (syā.).

From action and inaction, prior, intermediate, included in the count; formulation, supplementary, unarisen, universal, common, and for one side.

Thullagihiniyatā [P 5.0116] ca, ādi adhiccacodako;

Adhammadhammaniyato, abhabbokkhittanāsitā;

Samānaṃ ṭhapanañceva, uddānaṃ ekake idanti.

Gross fault, connected with laypersons, and fixed; the initiator, the occasional offender, the accuser; the unlawful, the lawful, the fixed person; the incapable, suspended, and expelled; those in communion, and the setting aside—this is the summary in the Single Section.

2. Dukavāro

2. The Section on Pairs

322. Atthāpatti saññā vimokkhā, atthāpatti no saññāvimokkhā. Atthāpatti laddhasamāpattikassa, atthāpatti na laddhasamāpattikassa. Atthāpatti saddhammapaṭisaññuttā, atthāpatti asaddhammapaṭisaññuttā. Atthāpatti saparikkhārapaṭisaññuttā, atthāpatti paraparikkhārapaṭisaññuttā. Atthāpatti sapuggalapaṭisaññuttā, atthāpatti parapuggalapaṭisaññuttā. Atthi saccaṃ bhaṇanto garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati, musā bhaṇanto lahukaṃ. Atthi musā bhaṇanto garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati, saccaṃ bhaṇanto lahukaṃ. Atthāpatti bhūmigato āpajjati, no vehāsagato. Atthāpatti vehāsagato āpajjati, no bhūmigato. Atthāpatti nikkhamanto āpajjati, no pavisanto. Atthāpatti pavisanto āpajjati, no nikkhamanto. Atthāpatti ādiyanto āpajjati, atthāpatti anādiyanto [T 0.0297] āpajjati. Atthāpatti [M 0.0213] samādiyanto āpajjati[V 0.0237], atthāpatti na samādiyanto āpajjati. Atthāpatti karonto āpajjati, atthāpatti na karonto āpajjati. Atthāpatti dento āpajjati, atthāpatti na dento āpajjati. (Atthāpatti desento āpajjati, atthāpatti na desento āpajjati.) ( ) (natthi katthaci) Atthāpatti paṭiggaṇhanto āpajjati, atthāpatti na paṭiggaṇhanto āpajjati. Atthāpatti paribhogena āpajjati, atthāpatti na paribhogena āpajjati. Atthāpatti rattiṃ āpajjati, no divā. Atthāpatti divā āpajjati, no rattiṃ. Atthāpatti aruṇugge āpajjati, atthāpatti na aruṇugge āpajjati. Atthāpatti chindanto āpajjati, atthāpatti na chindanto āpajjati. Atthāpatti chādento āpajjati, atthāpatti na chādento āpajjati. Atthāpatti dhārento āpajjati, atthāpatti na dhārento āpajjati.

322. There is an intentional offense; there is an unintentional offense. There is an offense for one who has attained meditative absorption; there is an offense for one who has not attained meditative absorption. There is an offense connected with the true Dhamma; there is an offense connected with what is not the true Dhamma. There is an offense connected with one's own requisites; there is an offense connected with others' requisites. There is an offense connected with oneself; there is an offense connected with another person. There is a case where speaking the truth incurs a heavy offense, while speaking falsely incurs a light one. There is a case where speaking falsely incurs a heavy offense, while speaking the truth incurs a light one. There is an offense incurred while on the ground, not while in the air. There is an offense incurred while in the air, not while on the ground. There is an offense incurred while going out, not while entering. There is an offense incurred while entering, not while going out. There is an offense incurred while taking; there is an offense incurred while not taking. There is an offense incurred while undertaking; there is an offense incurred while not undertaking. There is an offense incurred while doing; there is an offense incurred while not doing. There is an offense incurred while giving; there is an offense incurred while not giving. (There is an offense incurred while confessing; there is an offense incurred while not confessing.) There is an offense incurred while receiving; there is an offense incurred while not receiving. There is an offense incurred through use; there is an offense incurred without use. There is an offense incurred at night, not during the day. There is an offense incurred during the day, not at night. There is an offense incurred at dawn; there is an offense incurred not at dawn. There is an offense incurred while cutting; there is an offense incurred while not cutting. There is an offense incurred while concealing; there is an offense incurred while not concealing. There is an offense incurred while wearing; there is an offense incurred while not wearing.

Dve uposathā – cātuddasiko ca pannarasiko ca. Dve pavāraṇā – cātuddasikā ca pannarasikā ca. Dve kammāni – apalokanakammaṃ, ñattikammaṃ. Aparānipi dve kammāni – ñattidutiyakammaṃ, ñatticatutthakammaṃ. Dve kammavatthūni – apalokanakammassa vatthu, ñattikammassa vatthu. Aparānipi dve kammavatthūni – ñattidutiyakammassa vatthu, ñatticatutthakammassa vatthu. Dve kammadosā – apalokanakammassa doso, ñattikammassa doso. Aparepi [T 0.0298] dve kammadosā – ñattidutiyakammassa doso, ñatticatutthakammassa doso. Dve kammasampattiyo – apalokanakammassa sampatti, ñattikammassa sampatti. Aparāpi dve kammasampattiyo – ñattidutiyakammassa sampatti, ñatticatutthakammassa sampatti. Dve nānāsaṃvāsakabhūmiyo – attanā vā attānaṃ nānāsaṃvāsakaṃ karoti, samaggo vā naṃ saṅgho ukkhipati adassane vā appaṭikamme vā appaṭinissagge vā. Dve samānasaṃvāsakabhūmiyo – attanā vā attānaṃ [P 5.0117] samānasaṃvāsakaṃ karoti, samaggo vā naṃ saṅgho ukkhittaṃ osāreti dassane vā paṭikamme vā paṭinissagge vā. Dve pārājikā – bhikkhūnañca bhikkhunīnañca. Dve saṅghādisesā, dve thullaccayā, dve pācittiyā, dve pāṭidesanīyā, dve dukkaṭā, dve dubbhāsitā – bhikkhūnañca bhikkhunīnañca. Satta āpattiyo, satta āpattikkhandhā. Dvīhākārehi saṅgho bhijjati – kammena vā salākaggāhena vā.

There are two Uposathas: the fourteenth-day and the fifteenth-day. There are two Pavāraṇās: the fourteenth-day and the fifteenth-day. There are two formal acts: the act by consent and the act by motion. There are also two other formal acts: the act with a motion and one proclamation, and the act with a motion and three proclamations. There are two grounds for formal acts: the ground for the act by consent and the ground for the act by motion. There are also two other grounds for formal acts: the ground for an act with a motion and one proclamation, and the ground for an act with a motion and three proclamations. There are two faults of formal acts: the fault of the act by consent and the fault of the act by motion. There are also two other faults of formal acts: the fault of an act with a motion and one proclamation, and the fault of an act with a motion and three proclamations. There are two accomplishments of formal acts: the accomplishment of the act by consent and the accomplishment of the act by motion. There are also two other accomplishments of formal acts: the accomplishment of an act with a motion and one proclamation, and the accomplishment of an act with a motion and three proclamations. There are two grounds for separate communion: either one makes oneself of separate communion, or a united Saṅgha suspends one for not acknowledging an offense, for not making amends, or for not relinquishing a view. There are two grounds for common communion: either one makes oneself of common communion, or a united Saṅgha reinstates one who was suspended upon acknowledging the offense, making amends, or relinquishing the view. There are two Pārājikas: for monks and for nuns. There are two Saṅghādisesas, two Thullaccayas, two Pācittiyas, two Pāṭidesanīyas, two Dukkaṭas, and two Dubbhāsitas: for monks and for nuns. There are seven offenses and seven aggregates of offenses. The Saṅgha is split in two ways: by a formal act or by the taking of ballots.

Dve [M 0.0214] puggalā na upasampādetabbā – addhānahīno, aṅgahīno. Aparepi dve puggalā na upasampādetabbā – vatthuvipanno, karaṇadukkaṭako. Aparepi dve puggalā na upasampādetabbā – aparipūro paripūro no ca yācati. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ nissāya na vatthabbaṃ – alajjissa ca bālassa ca. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ nissayo [T 0.0299] na dātabbo – alajjissa ca lajjino ca na yācati. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ nissayo dātabbo – bālassa ca lajjissa ca yācati. Dve puggalā abhabbā āpattiṃ āpajjituṃ – buddhā ca paccekabuddhā ca. Dve puggalā bhabbā, āpattiṃ [V 0.0238] āpajjituṃ – bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca. Dve puggalā abhabbā sañcicca āpattiṃ āpajjituṃ – bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca ariyapuggalā. Dve puggalā bhabbā sañcicca āpattiṃ āpajjituṃ – bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca puthujjanā. Dve puggalā abhabbā sañcicca sātisāraṃ vatthuṃ ajjhācarituṃ – bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca ariyapuggalā. Dve puggalā bhabbā sañcicca sātisāraṃ vatthuṃ ajjhācarituṃ – bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca puthujjanā.

Two individuals should not be given full ordination: one deficient in age and one deficient in limbs. Also, two other individuals should not be given full ordination: one whose basis is defective and one who has committed a wrongdoing. Also, two other individuals should not be given full ordination: one who is incomplete with bowl and robes and one who is complete but does not request it. One should not live in dependence on two individuals: the shameless one and the one unskilled in the Vinaya. Dependence should not be given to two individuals: to the shameless one and to the conscientious one who does not request it. Dependence should be given to two individuals: to the one unskilled in the Vinaya and to the conscientious one who requests it. Two individuals are incapable of committing an offense: Buddhas and Paccekabuddhas. Two individuals are capable of committing an offense: monks and nuns. Two individuals are incapable of intentionally committing an offense: monks and nuns who are noble individuals. Two individuals are capable of intentionally committing an offense: monks and nuns who are worldlings. Two individuals are incapable of intentionally transgressing a blameworthy matter: monks and nuns who are noble individuals. Two individuals are capable of intentionally transgressing a blameworthy matter: monks and nuns who are worldlings.

Dve paṭikkosā – kāyena vā paṭikkosati vācāya vā paṭikkosati. Dve nissāraṇā – atthi puggalo appatto nissāraṇaṃ taṃ ce saṅgho nissāreti ekacco sunissārito, ekacco dunnissārito. Dve osāraṇā – atthi puggalo appatto osāraṇaṃ taṃ ce saṅgho osāreti ekacco sosārito, ekacco dosārito. Dve paṭiññā – kāyena vā paṭijānāti vācāya vā paṭijānāti. Dve paṭiggahā – kāyena vā paṭiggaṇhāti kāyapaṭibaddhena vā paṭiggaṇhāti. Dve paṭikkhepā – kāyena vā paṭikkhipati vācāya vā paṭikkhipati. Dve [T 0.0300] upaghātikā – sikkhūpaghātikā ca bhogūpaghātikā ca. Dve codanā – kāyena vā codeti vācāya vā codeti. Dve kathinassa palibodhā – āvāsapalibodho ca cīvarapalibodho ca. Dve kathinassa apalibodhā – āvāsaapalibodho ca cīvaraapalibodho ca. Dve cīvarāni – gahapatikañca paṃsukūlañca. Dve pattā – ayopatto mattikāpatto. Dve maṇḍalāni – tipumayaṃ, sīsamayaṃ. Dve pattassa adhiṭṭhānā – kāyena vā adhiṭṭheti vācāya vā adhiṭṭheti. Dve cīvarassa [P 5.0118] adhiṭṭhānā – kāyena vā adhiṭṭheti vācāya vā adhiṭṭheti. Dve vikappanā – sammukhāvikappanā ca parammukhāvikappanā ca. Dve vinayā – bhikkhūnañca bhikkhunīnañca. Dve [M 0.0215] venayikā – paññattañca paññattānulomañca. Dve vinayassa sallekhā – akappiye setughāto, kappiye mattakāritā. Dvīhākārehi āpattiṃ āpajjati – kāyena vā āpajjati vācāya vā āpajjati. Dvīhākārehi āpattiyā vuṭṭhāti – kāyena vā vuṭṭhāti vācāya vā vuṭṭhāti. Dve parivāsā – paṭicchannaparivāso, appaṭicchannaparivāso. Aparepi dve parivāsā – suddhantaparivāso samodhānaparivāso. Dve mānattā – paṭicchannamānattaṃ, appaṭicchannamānattaṃ. Aparepi dve mānattā – pakkhamānattaṃ, samodhānamānattaṃ. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ ratticchedo [T 0.0301] – pārivāsikassa ca mānattacārikassa ca. Dve anādariyāni – puggalānādariyañca dhammānādariyañca. Dve loṇāni – jātimañca kārimañca jātimayañca khārimayañca (syā.). Aparānipi dve loṇāni – sāmuddaṃ kāḷaloṇaṃ. Aparānipi dve loṇāni – sindhavaṃ, ubbhidaṃ ubbhiraṃ (itipi). Aparānipi dve loṇāni – romakaṃ, pakkālakaṃ. Dve paribhogā – abbhantaraparibhogo ca bāhiraparibhogo ca. Dve akkosā – hīno ca akkoso ukkaṭṭho ca akkoso. Dvīhākārehi pesuññaṃ hoti – piyakamyassa vā bhedādhippāyassa [V 0.0239] vā. Dvīhākārehi gaṇabhojanaṃ pasavati – nimantanato vā viññattito vā. Dve vassūpanāyikā – purimikā, pacchimikā. Dve adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni. Dve dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni.

There are two prohibitions: prohibiting by body or prohibiting by speech. There are two expulsions: there is a person not liable for expulsion; if the Saṅgha expels that person, one is well-expelled, another is badly expelled. There are two reinstatements: there is a person not liable for reinstatement; if the Saṅgha reinstates that person, one is well-reinstated, another is badly reinstated. There are two acknowledgements: acknowledging by body or acknowledging by speech. There are two acceptances: accepting by body or accepting by what is connected with the body. There are two refusals: refusing by body or refusing by speech. There are two kinds of damaging: damaging the training and damaging requisites. There are two accusations: accusing by body or accusing by speech. There are two impediments to the Kathina: the impediment of the residence and the impediment of the robe. There are two non-impediments to the Kathina: the non-impediment of the residence and the non-impediment of the robe. There are two kinds of robes: the householder's robe and the rag-robe. There are two kinds of bowls: the iron bowl and the clay bowl. There are two bowl-stands: one made of tin, and one made of lead. There are two determinations of a bowl: determining by body or determining by speech. There are two determinations of a robe: determining by body or determining by speech. There are two kinds of assignment: assignment in one's presence and assignment in one's absence. There are two Vinayas: that of monks and that of nuns. There are two matters of Vinaya: that which is laid down and that which is in conformity with what is laid down. There are two kinds of austerity in the Vinaya: cutting off the cause in what is improper, and moderation in what is proper. One commits an offense in two ways: by body or by speech. One emerges from an offense in two ways: by body or by speech. There are two kinds of probation: concealed probation and unconcealed probation. There are two other kinds of probation: probation until purification and combined probation. There are two kinds of penance: concealed penance and unconcealed penance. There are two other kinds of penance: penance for a fortnight and combined penance. There is an interruption of nights for two persons: for one on probation and for one undergoing penance. There are two kinds of disrespect: disrespect for a person and disrespect for the Dhamma. There are two kinds of salt: natural salt and manufactured salt. There are two other kinds of salt: sea salt and black salt. There are two other kinds of salt: Sindhava salt and rock salt. There are two other kinds of salt: Romaka salt and Pakkālaka salt. There are two kinds of use: internal use and external use. There are two kinds of abuse: inferior abuse and superior abuse. Slander occurs in two ways: from a desire to be dear, or with the intention of causing division. A group meal arises in two ways: through invitation or through requesting. There are two Rains-retreats: the earlier and the later. There are two unlawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha. There are two lawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha.

a. ni. 2.99 ādayo Dve puggalā bālā – yo ca anāgataṃ bhāraṃ vahati, yo ca āgataṃ bhāraṃ na vahati. Dve puggalā paṇḍitā – yo ca anāgataṃ bhāraṃ na vahati, yo ca āgataṃ bhāraṃ vahati. Aparepi dve puggalā bālā – yo ca akappiye kappiyasaññī, yo ca kappiye akappiyasaññī. Dve puggalā paṇḍitā – yo ca akappiye akappiyasaññī, yo ca kappiye kappiyasaññī. Aparepi dve puggalā bālā – yo ca anāpattiyā āpattisaññī, yo ca āpattiyā anāpattisaññī. Dve puggalā paṇḍitā – yo [T 0.0302] ca āpattiyā āpattisaññī, yo ca anāpattiyā anāpattisaññī. Aparepi dve puggalā bālā – yo ca adhamme dhammasaññī, yo ca dhamme adhammasaññī. Dve puggalā paṇḍitā – yo ca adhamme adhammasaññī, yo ca dhamme dhammasaññī. Aparepi dve puggalā bālā – yo ca avinaye vinayasaññī, yo [M 0.0216] ca vinaye avinayasaññī. Dve puggalā paṇḍitā – yo ca avinaye avinayasaññī, yo ca vinaye vinayasaññī.

Two persons are foolish: one who carries a burden that has not yet come, and one who does not carry a burden that has come. Two persons are wise: one who does not carry a burden that has not yet come, and one who carries a burden that has come. Furthermore, two persons are foolish: one who perceives the unallowable as allowable, and one who perceives the allowable as unallowable. Two persons are wise: one who perceives the unallowable as unallowable, and one who perceives the allowable as allowable. Furthermore, two persons are foolish: one who perceives a non-offense as an offense, and one who perceives an offense as a non-offense. Two persons are wise: one who perceives an offense as an offense, and one who perceives a non-offense as a non-offense. Furthermore, two persons are foolish: one who perceives what is not the Dhamma as the Dhamma, and one who perceives the Dhamma as not the Dhamma. Two persons are wise: one who perceives what is not the Dhamma as not the Dhamma, and one who perceives the Dhamma as the Dhamma. Furthermore, two persons are foolish: one who perceives what is not the Vinaya as the Vinaya, and one who perceives the Vinaya as not the Vinaya. Two persons are wise: one who perceives what is not the Vinaya as not the Vinaya, and one who perceives the Vinaya as the Vinaya.

a. ni. 2.109 Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ āsavā vaḍḍhanti – yo ca na kukkuccāyitabbaṃ kukkuccāyati, yo ca kukkuccāyitabbaṃ [P 5.0119] kukkuccāyati. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ āsavā na vaḍḍhanti – yo ca kukkuccāyitabbaṃ na kukkuccāyati, yo ca kukkuccāyitabbaṃ kukkuccāyati. Aparesampi dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ āsavā vaḍḍhanti – yo ca akappiye kappiyasaññī, yo ca kappiye akappiyasaññī. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ āsavā na vaḍḍhanti – yo ca akappiye akappiyasaññī, yo ca kappiye kappiyasaññī. Aparesampi dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ āsavā vaḍḍhanti – yo ca anāpattiyā āpattisaññī, yo ca āpattiyā anāpattisaññī. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ āsavā na vaḍḍhanti – yo ca anāpattiyā anāpattisaññī, yo ca āpattiyā āpattisaññī. Aparesampi dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ āsavā vaḍḍhanti – yo ca adhamme dhammasaññī, yo ca dhamme adhammasaññī. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ āsavā na vaḍḍhanti [T 0.0303] – yo ca adhamme adhammasaññī, yo ca dhamme dhammasaññī. Aparesampi dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ āsavā vaḍḍhanti – yo ca avinaye vinayasaññī, yo ca vinaye avinayasaññī. Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ āsavā na vaḍḍhanti – yo ca avinaye avinayasaññī, yo ca vinaye vinayasaññī.

For two persons, the taints increase: one who feels remorse over what should not be felt remorse for, and one who feels no remorse over what should be felt remorse for. For two persons, the taints do not increase: one who feels no remorse over what should not be felt remorse for, and one who feels remorse over what should be felt remorse for. For another two persons, the taints increase: one who perceives what is impermissible as permissible, and one who perceives what is permissible as impermissible. For two persons, the taints do not increase: one who perceives what is impermissible as impermissible, and one who perceives what is permissible as permissible. For another two persons, the taints increase: one who perceives a non-offense as an offense, and one who perceives an offense as a non-offense. For two persons, the taints do not increase: one who perceives a non-offense as a non-offense, and one who perceives an offense as an offense. For another two persons, the taints increase: one who perceives what is not the Dhamma as the Dhamma, and one who perceives the Dhamma as not the Dhamma. For two persons, the taints do not increase: one who perceives what is not the Dhamma as not the Dhamma, and one who perceives the Dhamma as the Dhamma. For another two persons, the taints increase: one who perceives what is not the Vinaya as the Vinaya, and one who perceives the Vinaya as not the Vinaya. For two persons, the taints do not increase: one who perceives what is not the Vinaya as not the Vinaya, and one who perceives the Vinaya as the Vinaya.

Dukā niṭṭhitā.

The Couplets are concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Saññā [V 0.0240] laddhā ca saddhammā, parikkhārā ca puggalā;

Saccaṃ bhūmi nikkhamanto, ādiyanto samādiyaṃ.

Perception, attainment, and the true Dhamma; requisites and persons; truth, ground, departing, taking, and undertaking.

Karonto dento gaṇhanto, paribhogena ratti ca;

Aruṇāchindaṃ chādento, dhārento ca uposathā.

Doing, giving, receiving; using, and night; dawn, cutting, concealing, wearing, and the Uposatha.

Pavāraṇā kammāparā, vatthu aparā dosā ca;

Aparā dve ca sampatti, nānā samānameva ca.

The Pavāraṇā, a formal act and another; the basis, another, and faults; another, two accomplishments; diverse and the same.

Pārājisaṅghathullaccaya, pācitti pāṭidesanā;

Dukkaṭā dubbhāsitā ceva, satta āpattikkhandhā ca.

Pārājika, Saṅghādisesa, Thullaccaya, Pācittiya, Pāṭidesanīya, Dukkaṭa, and Dubbhāsita, and the seven classes of offenses.

Bhijjati [M 0.0217] upasampadā, tatheva apare duve;

Na vatthabbaṃ na dātabbaṃ, abhabbābhabbameva ca.

Schism, higher ordination, likewise two others; not to be lived with, not to be given, the incapable, and the capable.

Sañcicca sātisārā ca, paṭikkosā nissāraṇā;

Osāraṇā [T 0.0304] paṭiññā ca, paṭiggahā paṭikkhipā.

Intentional and with transgression; censure, expulsion; rehabilitation, acknowledgment, acceptance, rejection.

Upaghāti codanā ca, kathinā ca duve tathā;

Cīvarā pattamaṇḍalā, adhiṭṭhānā tatheva dve.

Destruction and accusation; likewise, the two on the Kathina; robes, bowls, and boundary stones; likewise, the two on determination.

Vikappanā ca vinayā, venayikā ca sallekhā;

Āpajjati ca vuṭṭhāti, parivāsāpare duve.

Alienation and Vinaya; one to be trained and austerity; incurring and emerging; probation and two others.

Dve mānattā apare ca, ratticchedo anādari;

Dve loṇā tayo apare, paribhogakkosena ca.

Two on penance and another; interruption of nights, disrespect; two on salt, three others; and by use and reviling.

Pesuñño ca gaṇāvassa, ṭhapanā bhārakappiyaṃ;

Anāpatti adhammadhammā, vinaye āsave tathāti.

Slander, group meals, and the rains-residence; suspension, a burden, what is unallowable; no offense, not-Dhamma and Dhamma; likewise on Vinaya and taints. Thus it should be known.

3. Tikavāro

3. The Section on Triads

323. Atthāpatti [V 0.0241] tiṭṭhante bhagavati āpajjati, no parinibbute; atthāpatti parinibbute bhagavati āpajjati, no tiṭṭhante; atthāpatti [P 5.0120] tiṭṭhantepi bhagavati āpajjati parinibbutepi. Atthāpatti kāle āpajjati, no vikāle; atthāpatti vikāle āpajjati, no kāle; atthāpatti kāle ceva āpajjati vikāle ca. Atthāpatti rattiṃ āpajjati, no divā; atthāpatti divā āpajjati, no rattiṃ; atthāpatti rattiñceva āpajjati divā ca. Atthāpatti dasavasso āpajjati, no ūnadasavasso; atthāpatti ūnadasavasso āpajjati, no [T 0.0305] dasavasso; atthāpatti dasavasso ceva āpajjati ūnadasavasso ca. Atthāpatti pañcavasso āpajjati, no ūnapañcavasso; atthāpatti ūnapañcavasso āpajjati, no pañcavasso; atthāpatti pañcavasso ceva āpajjati ūnapañcavasso ca. Atthāpatti kusalacitto āpajjati; atthāpatti akusalacitto āpajjati; atthāpatti abyākatacitto āpajjati. Atthāpatti sukhavedanāsamaṅgī āpajjati; atthāpatti dukkhavedanāsamaṅgī āpajjati; atthāpatti adukkhamasukhavedanāsamaṅgī āpajjati. Tīṇi codanāvatthūni [M 0.0218] – diṭṭhena, sutena, parisaṅkāya. Tayo salākaggāhā – guḷhako, vivaṭako vivaṭṭako (ka.), sakaṇṇajappako. Tayo paṭikkhepā – mahicchatā, asantuṭṭhitā asantuṭṭhatā (syā.), asallekhatā. Tayo anuññātā – appicchatā, santuṭṭhitā, sallekhatā. Aparepi tayo paṭikkhepā – mahicchatā, asantuṭṭhitā, amattaññutā. Tayo anuññātā – appicchatā, santuṭṭhitā, mattaññutā. Tisso paññattiyo – paññatti, anupaññatti, anuppannapaññatti. Aparāpi tisso paññattiyo – sabbatthapaññatti, padesapaññatti, sādhāraṇapaññatti. Aparāpi tisso paññattiyo – asādhāraṇapaññatti, ekatopaññatti, ubhatopaññatti.

323. There is an offense one commits while the Blessed One is present, but not after his final passing; there is an offense one commits after the Blessed One's final passing, but not while he is present; there is an offense one commits both while the Blessed One is present and after his final passing. There is an offense one commits at the proper time, but not at the wrong time; there is an offense one commits at the wrong time, but not at the proper time; there is an offense one commits both at the proper time and at the wrong time. There is an offense one commits at night, but not during the day; there is an offense one commits during the day, but not at night; there is an offense one commits both at night and during the day. There is an offense a monk of ten rains commits, but not one of less than ten rains; there is an offense a monk of less than ten rains commits, but not one of ten rains; there is an offense both a monk of ten rains and one of less than ten rains commit. There is an offense a monk of five rains commits, but not one of less than five rains; there is an offense a monk of less than five rains commits, but not one of five rains; there is an offense both a monk of five rains and one of less than five rains commit. There is an offense one commits with a wholesome mind; there is an offense one commits with an unwholesome mind; there is an offense one commits with an indeterminate mind. There is an offense one commits while endowed with pleasant feeling; there is an offense one commits while endowed with painful feeling; there is an offense one commits while endowed with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. There are three grounds for accusation: by what is seen, by what is heard, by suspicion. There are three ways of taking voting tickets: secretly, openly, and by whispering in the ear. There are three things to be rejected: great desire, discontent, and lack of effacement. There are three things to be allowed: fewness of desires, contentment, and effacement. There are another three things to be rejected: great desire, discontent, and not knowing moderation. There are three things to be allowed: fewness of desires, contentment, and knowing moderation. There are three regulations: the original regulation, the supplementary regulation, and the preventative regulation. There are another three regulations: the universal regulation, the local regulation, and the common regulation. There are yet another three regulations: the uncommon regulation, the one-sided regulation, and the two-sided regulation.

Atthāpatti bālo āpajjati, no paṇḍito; atthāpatti paṇḍito āpajjati, no bālo; atthāpatti bālo ceva āpajjati paṇḍito [T 0.0306] ca. Atthāpatti kāḷe āpajjati, no juṇhe; atthāpatti juṇhe āpajjati, no kāḷe; atthāpatti kāḷe ceva āpajjati juṇhe ca. Atthi kāḷe kappati, no juṇhe; atthi juṇhe kappati, no kāḷe; atthi kāḷe ceva kappati juṇhe ca. Atthāpatti hemante āpajjati, no gimhe no vasse; atthāpatti gimhe āpajjati, no hemante no vasse; atthāpatti vasse āpajjati, no hemante no gimhe. Atthāpatti saṅgho āpajjati, na gaṇo na puggalo; atthāpatti gaṇo āpajjati, na saṅgho na puggalo; atthāpatti puggalo āpajjati, na saṅgho na gaṇo. Atthi saṅghassa kappati, na gaṇassa [V 0.0242] na puggalassa; atthi gaṇassa kappati, na saṅghassa na puggalassa; atthi puggalassa kappati, na saṅghassa na gaṇassa. Tisso chādanā vatthuṃ chādeti, no āpattiṃ; āpattiṃ chādeti, no vatthuṃ; vatthuñceva chādeti āpattiñca. Tisso paṭicchādiyo – jantāgharapaṭicchādi, udakapaṭicchādi, vatthapaṭicchādi. a. ni. 3.132 Tīṇi paṭicchannāni vahanti, no vivaṭāni – mātugāmo paṭicchanno vahati, no vivaṭo; brāhmaṇānaṃ mantā paṭicchannā vahanti, no vivaṭā; micchādiṭṭhi paṭicchannā [P 5.0121] vahati, no vivaṭā. Tīṇi vivaṭāni virocanti, no paṭicchannāni – candamaṇḍalaṃ vivaṭaṃ virocati, no paṭicchannaṃ; sūriyamaṇḍalaṃ vivaṭaṃ virocati, no paṭicchannaṃ; tathāgatappavedito [T 0.0307] dhammavinayo vivaṭo virocati, no paṭicchanno. Tayo senāsanaggāhā – purimako[M 0.0219], pacchimako, antarāmuttako. Atthāpatti gilāno āpajjati, no agilāno; atthāpatti agilāno āpajjati, no gilāno; atthāpatti gilāno ceva āpajjati agilāno ca.

There is an offense a fool commits, not a wise one; there is an offense a wise one commits, not a fool; there is an offense both a fool and a wise one commit. There is an offense committed in the dark fortnight, not in the bright fortnight; there is an offense committed in the bright fortnight, not in the dark fortnight; there is an offense committed in both the dark fortnight and the bright fortnight. There is something allowable in the dark fortnight, not in the bright fortnight; there is something allowable in the bright fortnight, not in the dark fortnight; there is something allowable in both the dark fortnight and the bright fortnight. There is an offense committed in the cold season, not in the hot season or the rainy season; there is an offense committed in the hot season, not in the cold season or the rainy season; there is an offense committed in the rainy season, not in the cold season or the hot season. There is an offense the Saṅgha commits, not a group or an individual; there is an offense a group commits, not the Saṅgha or an individual; there is an offense an individual commits, not the Saṅgha or a group. There is something allowable for the Saṅgha, not for a group or an individual; there is something allowable for a group, not for the Saṅgha or an individual; there is something allowable for an individual, not for the Saṅgha or a group. Three coverings: they cover the basis, not the offense; they cover the offense, not the basis; they cover both the basis and the offense. Three concealments: concealment by a steam-bath house, concealment by water, concealment by cloth. Three things are esteemed when concealed, not when revealed: a woman is esteemed when concealed, not when revealed; the counsels of the brahmins are esteemed when concealed, not when revealed; wrong view is esteemed when concealed, not when revealed. Three things shine when revealed, not when concealed: the orb of the moon shines when revealed, not when concealed; the orb of the sun shines when revealed, not when concealed; the Dhamma-Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata shines when revealed, not when concealed. Three acceptances of lodgings: the first, the last, the intermediate. There is an offense a sick person commits, not a healthy one; there is an offense a healthy one commits, not a sick one; there is an offense both a sick and a healthy person commit.

Tīṇi adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni. Tīṇi dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni. Tayo parivāsā – paṭicchannaparivāso, appaṭicchannaparivāso, suddhantaparivāso. Tayo mānattā – paṭicchannamānattaṃ, appaṭicchannamānattaṃ, pakkhamānattaṃ. Tayo pārivāsikassa bhikkhuno ratticchedā – sahavāso, vippavāso, anārocanā. Atthāpatti anto āpajjati, no bahi; atthāpatti bahi āpajjati, no anto; atthāpatti anto ceva āpajjati bahi ca. Atthāpatti antosīmāya āpajjati, no bahisīmāya; atthāpatti bahisīmāya āpajjati, no antosīmāya; atthāpatti antosīmāya ceva āpajjati bahisīmāya ca. Tīhākārehi āpattiṃ āpajjati – kāyena āpajjati, vācāya āpajjati, kāyena vācāya āpajjati. Aparehipi tīhākārehi āpattiṃ āpajjati – saṅghamajjhe, gaṇamajjhe, puggalassa santike. Tīhākārehi āpattiyā vuṭṭhāti – kāyena vuṭṭhāti, vācāya vuṭṭhāti, kāyena vācāya vuṭṭhāti. Aparehipi tīhākārehi [T 0.0308] āpattiyā vuṭṭhāti – saṅghamajjhe, gaṇamajjhe, puggalassa santike. Tīṇi adhammikāni amūḷhavinayassa dānāni. Tīṇi dhammikāni amūḷhavinayassa dānāni.

Three unlawful postponements of the Pātimokkha. Three lawful postponements of the Pātimokkha. Three probations: concealed probation, unconcealed probation, and probation until purification. Three penances: concealed penance, unconcealed penance, and fortnight penance. Three interruptions of the nights for a bhikkhu observing probation: dwelling together, dwelling apart, and non-announcement. There is an offense committed inside, not outside; there is an offense committed outside, not inside; there is an offense committed both inside and outside. There is an offense committed within the sīmā, not outside the sīmā; there is an offense committed outside the sīmā, not within the sīmā; there is an offense committed both within and outside the sīmā. One commits an offense in three ways: by body, by speech, by body and speech. One also commits an offense in three other ways: in the midst of the Saṅgha, in the midst of a group, and in the presence of an individual. One is cleared of an offense in three ways: by body, by speech, by body and speech. One is also cleared of an offense in three other ways: in the midst of the Saṅgha, in the midst of a group, and in the presence of an individual. Three unlawful grantings of the amūḷha-vinaya. Three lawful grantings of the amūḷha-vinaya.

cūḷava. 6 Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho tajjanīyakammaṃ kareyya – bhaṇḍanakārako hoti kalahakārako vivādakārako bhassakārako saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako, bālo hoti abyatto, āpattibahulo anapadāno gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi. cūḷava. 15 Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho niyassakammaṃ kareyya – bhaṇḍanakārako [V 0.0243] hoti…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako, bālo hoti abyatto, āpattibahulo anapadāno gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi. cūḷava. 27 Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyya – bhaṇḍanakārako hoti…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako, bālo hoti abyatto, āpattibahulo anapadāno kuladūkako hoti pāpasamācāro pāpasamācārā dissanti [M 0.0220] ceva suyyanti ca. Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ kareyya – bhaṇḍanakārako hoti…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako, bālo hoti abyatto, āpatti bahulo anapadāno gihī akkosati paribhāsati. cūḷava. 50 Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya [P 5.0122] – bhaṇḍanakārako hoti…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako, bālo hoti abyatto, āpattibahulo anapadāno āpattiṃ āpajjitvā na icchati āpattiṃ passituṃ. cūḷava. 59 Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno [T 0.0309] ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya – bhaṇḍanakārako hoti…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako, bālo hoti abyatto, āpattibahulo anapadāno āpattiṃ āpajjitvā na icchati āpattiṃ paṭikātuṃ. cūḷava. 69 Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kareyya – bhaṇḍanakārako hoti…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako, bālo hoti abyatto, āpattibahulo anapadāno na icchati pāpikaṃ diṭṭhiṃ paṭinissajjituṃ.

If it so wishes, the Saṅgha should carry out an act of censure towards a monk endowed with three factors: he is quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, loquacious, and a creator of legal issues in the Saṅgha; he is foolish and incompetent; he has many offenses, they are without limit, and he dwells associated with householders through unsuitable associations with householders. If it so wishes, the Saṅgha should carry out an act of subordination towards a monk endowed with three factors: he is quarrelsome… a creator of legal issues in the Saṅgha; he is foolish and incompetent; he has many offenses, they are without limit, and he dwells associated with householders through unsuitable associations with householders. If it so wishes, the Saṅgha should carry out an act of banishment towards a monk endowed with three factors: he is quarrelsome… a creator of legal issues in the Saṅgha; he is foolish and incompetent, has many offenses, and they are without limit; he is a corrupter of families and of evil conduct, and his evil conducts are both seen and heard. If it so wishes, the Saṅgha should carry out an act of reconciliation towards a monk endowed with three factors: he is quarrelsome… a creator of legal issues in the Saṅgha; he is foolish and incompetent, has many offenses, and they are without limit; he insults and reviles householders. If it so wishes, the Saṅgha should carry out an act of suspension for not seeing an offense towards a monk endowed with three factors: he is quarrelsome… a creator of legal issues in the Saṅgha; he is foolish and incompetent, has many offenses, and they are without limit; having committed an offense, he does not wish to see the offense. If it so wishes, the Saṅgha should carry out an act of suspension for not making amends for an offense towards a monk endowed with three factors: he is quarrelsome… a creator of legal issues in the Saṅgha; he is foolish and incompetent, has many offenses, and they are without limit; having committed an offense, he does not wish to make amends for the offense. If it so wishes, the Saṅgha should carry out an act of suspension for not relinquishing an evil view towards a monk endowed with three factors: he is quarrelsome… a creator of legal issues in the Saṅgha; he is foolish and incompetent, has many offenses, and they are without limit; he does not wish to relinquish an evil view.

Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho āgāḷhāya ceteyya – bhaṇḍanakārako hoti kalahakārako vivādakārako bhassakārako saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako, bālo hoti abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno, gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi. Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ – alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto ca. Aparehipi tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ – adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno [T 0.0310] hoti. Aparehipi tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ – kāyikena davena samannāgato hoti, vācasikena davena samannāgato hoti, kāyikavācasikena davena samannāgato hoti. Aparehipi tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno [V 0.0244] kammaṃ kātabbaṃ – kāyikena anācārena samannāgato hoti, vācasikena anācārena samannāgato hoti, kāyikavācasikena anācārena samannāgato hoti. Aparehipi tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno [M 0.0221] kammaṃ kātabbaṃ – kāyikena upaghātikena samannāgato hoti, vācasikena upaghātikena samannāgato hoti, kāyikavācasikena upaghātikena samannāgato hoti. Aparehipi tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ – kāyikena micchājīvena samannāgato hoti, vācasikena micchājīvena samannāgato hoti, kāyikavācasikena micchājīvena samannāgato hoti. Aparehipi tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ – āpattiṃ āpanno kammakato upasampādeti, nissayaṃ deti, sāmaṇeraṃ upaṭṭhāpeti. Aparehipi tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ – yāya āpattiyā saṅghena kammaṃ kataṃ hoti taṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati, aññaṃ vā tādisikaṃ, tato vā pāpiṭṭhataraṃ. Aparehipi tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ – buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati.

If it so wishes, the Saṅgha should firmly admonish a bhikkhu endowed with three factors: he is quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, loquacious, and a creator of legal issues in the Saṅgha; he is foolish, incompetent, has many offenses, and they are without limit; he dwells associated with householders through unsuitable associations with householders. An act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with three factors: he is shameless, foolish, and unreformed. An act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with another three factors: he is corrupt in virtue with regard to higher morality, corrupt in conduct with regard to higher conduct, and corrupt in view with regard to excessive view. An act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with another three factors: he is endowed with bodily wantonness, verbal wantonness, and bodily and verbal wantonness. An act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with another three factors: he is endowed with bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, and bodily and verbal misconduct. An act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with another three factors: he is endowed with bodily destructiveness of the training rules, verbal destructiveness of the training rules, and bodily and verbal destructiveness of the training rules. An act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with another three factors: he is endowed with bodily wrong livelihood, verbal wrong livelihood, and bodily and verbal wrong livelihood. An act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with another three factors: having committed an offense and being one against whom an act has been carried out, he gives the higher ordination, gives dependence, or has a novice attend on him. An act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with another three factors: he commits the offense for which an act has been carried out by the Saṅgha, or another similar to it, or one that is worse than that. An act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with another three factors: he speaks in disparagement of the Buddha, speaks in disparagement of the Dhamma, and speaks in disparagement of the Saṅgha.

Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno [T 0.0311] saṅghamajjhe uposathaṃ ṭhapentassa – “alaṃ, bhikkhu, mā bhaṇḍanaṃ mā kalahaṃ mā viggahaṃ mā vivāda”nti omadditvā saṅghena uposatho kātabbo – alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto ca. Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno saṅghamajjhe pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapentassa – “alaṃ, bhikkhu, mā bhaṇḍanaṃ mā kalahaṃ mā viggahaṃ mā vivāda”nti omadditvā saṅghena pavāretabbaṃ – alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto ca. Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno na kāci saṅghasammuti dātabbā – alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto ca. Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ saṃgho na voharitabbo (syā.) – alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto ca. Tīhaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu na kismiṃ ci paccekaṭṭhāne ṭhapetabbo – alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto ca. Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno [P 5.0123] nissāya na vatthabbaṃ – alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto ca. Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno nissayo na dātabbo – alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto ca. Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno okāsakammaṃ kārāpentassa nālaṃ okāsakammaṃ kātuṃ – alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto ca. Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno savacanīyaṃ nādātabbaṃ – alajjī ca hoti, bālo [M 0.0222] ca, apakatatto ca. Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno vinayo [T 0.0312] na pucchitabbo – alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto ca. Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā vinayo na pucchitabbo – alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto ca. Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno vinayo na vissajjetabbo – alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto ca. Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā vinayo na vissajjetabbo – alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto [V 0.0245] ca. Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno anuyogo na dātabbo – alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto ca. Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ vinayo na sākacchitabbo sākacchātabbo (ka.) – alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto ca. Tīhaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ na nissayo dātabbo na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo – alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto ca.

When a monk endowed with three factors is obstructing the Uposatha in the midst of the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the Uposatha after having overruled him, saying: ‘Enough, monk, do not quarrel, do not create conflict, do not speak contentiously, do not dispute’; he is shameless, foolish, and not a monk in good standing. When a monk endowed with three factors is obstructing the Pavāraṇā in the midst of the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the Pavāraṇā after having overruled him, saying: ‘Enough, monk, do not quarrel, do not create conflict, do not speak contentiously, do not dispute’; he is shameless, foolish, and not a monk in good standing.
