No Saṅgha authorization should be given to a monk endowed with three factors; he is shameless, foolish, and not a monk in good standing. A monk endowed with three factors should not speak on any matter in the Saṅgha; he is shameless, foolish, and not a monk in good standing. A monk endowed with three factors should not be placed in any individual position of authority; he is shameless, foolish, and not a monk in good standing. One should not live in dependence on a monk endowed with three factors; he is shameless, foolish, and not a monk in good standing. Dependence should not be given to a monk endowed with three factors; he is shameless, foolish, and not a monk in good standing. It is not proper to grant permission to a monk endowed with three factors who is requesting it; he is shameless, foolish, and not a monk in good standing. The admonition of a monk endowed with three factors should not be accepted; he is shameless, foolish, and not a monk in good standing. A monk endowed with three factors should not be asked about the Vinaya; he is shameless, foolish, and not a monk in good standing. A monk endowed with three factors should not ask about the Vinaya; he is shameless, foolish, and not a monk in good standing. The Vinaya should not be explained to a monk endowed with three factors; he is shameless, foolish, and not a monk in good standing. A monk endowed with three factors should not explain the Vinaya; he is shameless, foolish, and not a monk in good standing. An opportunity for questioning should not be given to a monk endowed with three factors; he is shameless, foolish, and not a monk in good standing. The Vinaya should not be discussed with a monk endowed with three factors; he is shameless, foolish, and not a monk in good standing. A monk endowed with three factors should not give higher ordination, nor give dependence, nor have a novice attend on him; he is shameless, foolish, and not a monk in good standing.

Tayo uposathā – cātuddasiko, pannarasiko, sāmaggiuposatho. Aparepi tayo uposathā – saṅgheuposatho, gaṇeuposatho, puggaleuposatho. Aparepi tayo uposathā – suttuddesouposatho, pārisuddhiuposatho, adhiṭṭhānuposatho. Tisso pavāraṇā – cātuddasikā, pannarasikā, sāmaggipavāraṇā. Aparāpi tisso pavāraṇā – saṅghepavāraṇā, gaṇepavāraṇā, puggalepavāraṇā. Aparāpi tisso pavāraṇā – tevācikāpavāraṇā[T 0.0313], dvevācikāpavāraṇā, samānavassikāpavāraṇā.

There are three Uposathas: the Cātuddasika, the Pannarasika, and the Sāmaggī Uposatha. There are another three Uposathas: the Saṅgha Uposatha, the Gaṇa Uposatha, and the Puggala Uposatha. There are yet another three Uposathas: the Suttuddesa Uposatha, the Pārisuddhi Uposatha, and the Adhiṭṭhāna Uposatha. There are three Pavāraṇās: the Cātuddasikā, the Pannarasikā, and the Sāmaggī Pavāraṇā. There are another three Pavāraṇās: the Saṅgha Pavāraṇā, the Gaṇa Pavāraṇā, and the Puggala Pavāraṇā. There are yet another three Pavāraṇās: the Tevācikā Pavāraṇā, the Dvevācikā Pavāraṇā, and the Samānavassikā Pavāraṇā.

Tayo āpāyikā nerayikā – idamappahāya, yo ca abrahmacārī brahmacāripaṭiñño, yo ca suddhaṃ brahmacāriṃ parisuddhabrahmacariyaṃ carantaṃ amūlakena abrahmacariyena anuddhaṃseti, yo cāyaṃ evaṃvādī evaṃdiṭṭhi evaṃdiṭṭhī (sī.) – “natthi kāmesu doso”ti so kāmesu pātabyataṃ āpajjati. a. ni. 3.70 Tīṇi akusalamūlāni – lobho akusalamūlaṃ, doso akusalamūlaṃ, moho akusalamūlaṃ. a. ni. 3.70 Tīṇi kusalamūlāni – alobho kusalamūlaṃ, adoso kusalamūlaṃ, amoho kusalamūlaṃ. Tīṇi duccaritāni – kāyaduccaritaṃ, vacīduccaritaṃ, manoduccaritaṃ. Tīṇi sucaritāni – kāyasucaritaṃ, vacīsucaritaṃ, manosucaritaṃ. Tayo atthavase paṭicca bhagavatā kulesu tikabhojanaṃ paññattaṃ – dummaṅkūnaṃ puggalānaṃ niggahāya, pesalānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ [M 0.0223] phāsuvihārāya, “mā pāpicchā pakkhaṃ nissāya saṅghaṃ bhindeyyu”nti [P 5.0124] kulānuddayatāya ca. cūḷava. 350 Tīhi asaddhammehi abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto devadatto āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho pāpicchatā pāpamittatā oramattakena visesādhigamena antarā vosānaṃ āpādi. Tisso sammutiyo – daṇḍasammuti, sikkāsammuti, daṇḍasikkāsammuti. Tisso pādukā dhuvaṭṭhānikā asaṅkamanīyā – vaccapādukā, passāvapādukā, ācamanapādukā. Tisso pādaghaṃsaniyo – sakkharaṃ, kathalā, samuddapheṇakoti.

These three persons, without abandoning this, are destined for the plane of misery, for hell: one who, not practicing the noble practice, claims to practice the noble practice; one who, without basis, accuses a monk practicing the pure and noble practice of the ignoble practice; and one who is of such speech and such a view, saying, 'There is no fault in sensual pleasures,' and thus falls into indulgence in sensual pleasures. Three unwholesome roots: greed is an unwholesome root, hatred is an unwholesome root, delusion is an unwholesome root. Three wholesome roots: non-greed is a wholesome root, non-hatred is a wholesome root, non-delusion is a wholesome root. Three kinds of misconduct: bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct. Three kinds of good conduct: bodily good conduct, verbal good conduct, mental good conduct. On account of three benefits, the Blessed One laid down the rule of taking food in threes in families: for the restraint of persons without virtue, for the comfortable abiding of monks with amiable virtue, and out of concern for the lay supporters, so that 'monks with evil desires, relying on a faction, may not split the Saṅgha.' Overcome by three unrighteous qualities, with his wholesome mind exhausted, Devadatta is destined for the plane of misery, for hell, to remain for an aeon, incurable; due to having evil desires, having evil friends, and by attaining a superior human state that was only minor, he came to the cessation of his training in the middle. Three authorizations: authorization to carry a staff, authorization to carry a bowl in a sling, authorization to carry both a staff and a sling. Three kinds of permanent, unmovable footwear: footwear for the latrine, footwear for the urinal, footwear for cleansing. Three foot-scrubbers: gravel, a potsherd, sea-foam.

Tikaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section of Triads is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Tiṭṭhante [T 0.0314] kāle rattiñca, dasa pañca kusalena;

Vedanā codanā vatthu, salākā dve paṭikkhipā.

The Tiṭṭhanta Tika, the Kāla Tika, and the Ratti Tika; the Dasavassa Tika, the Pañcavassa Tika, and the Kusala Tika; the Vedanā Tika, the Codanāvatthu Tika, the Salākā Tika, and the two Paṭikkhepa Tikas.

Paññatti [V 0.0246] apare dve ca, bālo kāḷe ca kappati;

Hemante saṅgho saṅghassa, chādanā ca paṭicchādi.

The Paññatti Tika and the two other Paññatti Tikas; the Bāla Tika, the Kāḷa Tika, and the Kappati Tika; the Hemanta Tika, the Saṅgha Tika, and the Saṅghassa Tika; the Chādana Tika and the Paṭicchādi Tika.

Paṭicchannā vivaṭā ca, senāsanagilāyanā;

Pātimokkhaṃ parivāsaṃ, mānattā pārivāsikā.

The Paṭicchanna Tika and the Vivaṭa Tika; the Senāsana Tika and the Gilāna Tika; the Pātimokkhaṭṭhapana Tikas, the Parivāsa Tika, the Mānatta Tika, and the Pārivāsika Tika.

Anto anto ca sīmāya, āpajjati punāpare;

Vuṭṭhāti apare ceva, amūḷhavinayā duve.

The triad on 'within'; and the triad on 'within the boundary'; the triad on falling into an offense; again, the triad on another falling into an offense; the triad on emerging from an offense; and the triad on another emerging from an offense; and the two on the verdict of past insanity (unlawful and lawful).

Tajjanīyā niyassā ca, pabbājapaṭisāraṇī;

Adassanā paṭikamme, anissagge ca diṭṭhiyā.

The triad on the act of censure (tajjanīyakamma) and the act of subordination (niyassakamma); the act of banishment (pabbājanīyakamma) and the act of reconciliation (paṭisāraṇīyakamma); the act of suspension for not seeing an offense; the act of suspension for not making amends; and the act of suspension for not renouncing a wrong view.

Āgāḷhakammādhisīle, davānācāra ghātikā;

Ājīvāpannā tādisikā, avaṇṇuposathena ca.

The triad on āgāḷha; the triad on a formal act; the triad on a formal act concerning higher virtue; the triads on a formal act of mischief, a formal act of misconduct, and a formal act of destructiveness; the triads on a formal act concerning wrong livelihood and a formal act concerning one who has fallen into an offense; the triad on a formal act against such a one; and the triads on dispraise and the Uposatha.

Pavāraṇā sammuti ca, vohārapaccekena ca;

Na vatthabbaṃ na dātabbaṃ, okāsaṃ na kare tathā.

The triad on Pavāraṇā; the triad on Community authorization; the triad on 'should not be addressed'; the triad on a separate place; the triad on 'should not dwell'; the triad on 'should not be given'; likewise, the triad on 'not granting an opportunity'.

Na kare savacanīyaṃ, na pucchitabbakā duve;

Na vissajje duve ceva, anuyogampi no dade.

The triad on 'admonition should not be given'; the two triads on 'should not be questioned'; the two triads on 'should not be answered'; and the triad on 'interrogation should not be given'.

Sākacchā [T 0.0315][M 0.0224] upasampadā, nissayasāmaṇerā ca;

Uposathatikā tīṇi, pavāraṇatikā tayo.

The triad on 'should not discuss'; the triad on 'should not ordain'; the triad on 'dependence should not be given'; the triad on 'a novice should not be attended to'; the three triads on Uposatha; and the three triads on Pavāraṇā.

Āpāyikā akusalā, kusalā caritā duve;

Tikabhojanasaddhamme, sammuti pādukena ca;

Pādaghaṃsanikā ceva, uddānaṃ tikake idanti.

The triad on what leads to states of woe; the triad on unwholesome roots; the triad on wholesome roots; the two triads on conduct (misconduct and good conduct); the triads on the threefold meal and the false Dhamma; the triad on authorization; the triad on footwear; and the triad on the foot-scraper. This is the summary in the section on triads.

4. Catukkavāro

4. The Section of Fours

324. Atthāpatti [V 0.0247] sakavācāya āpajjati, paravācāya vuṭṭhāti; atthāpatti paravācāya āpajjati, sakavācāya vuṭṭhāti; atthāpatti sakavācāya āpajjati, sakavācāya vuṭṭhāti; atthāpatti paravācāya āpajjati, paravācāya vuṭṭhāti. Atthāpatti kāyena āpajjati, vācāya vuṭṭhāti; atthāpatti vācāya āpajjati, kāyena vuṭṭhāti; atthāpatti kāyena āpajjati, kāyena vuṭṭhāti; atthāpatti vācāya āpajjati, vācāya vuṭṭhāti. Atthāpatti pasutto āpajjati, paṭibuddho vuṭṭhāti; atthāpatti paṭibuddho [P 5.0125] āpajjati, pasutto vuṭṭhāti; atthāpatti pasutto āpajjati, pasutto vuṭṭhāti; atthāpatti paṭibuddho āpajjati, paṭibuddho vuṭṭhāti. Atthāpatti acittako āpajjati, sacittako vuṭṭhāti; atthāpatti sacittako āpajjati, acittako vuṭṭhāti; atthāpatti acittako āpajjati, acittako vuṭṭhāti; atthāpatti sacittako āpajjati, sacittako vuṭṭhāti. Atthāpatti āpajjanto deseti; desento āpajjati; atthāpatti [T 0.0316] āpajjanto vuṭṭhāti; vuṭṭhahanto āpajjati. Atthāpatti kammena āpajjati, akammena vuṭṭhāti; atthāpatti akammena āpajjati, kammena vuṭṭhāti; atthāpatti kammena āpajjati, kammena vuṭṭhāti; atthāpatti akammena āpajjati, akammena vuṭṭhāti.

324. There is an offense incurred by one's own speech and emerged from by another's speech; there is an offense incurred by another's speech and emerged from by one's own speech; there is an offense incurred by one's own speech and emerged from by one's own speech; there is an offense incurred by another's speech and emerged from by another's speech. There is an offense incurred by body and emerged from by speech; there is an offense incurred by speech and emerged from by body; there is an offense incurred by body and emerged from by body; there is an offense incurred by speech and emerged from by speech. There is an offense incurred while asleep and emerged from while awake; there is an offense incurred while awake and emerged from while asleep; there is an offense incurred while asleep and emerged from while asleep; there is an offense incurred while awake and emerged from while awake. There is an offense incurred without intention and emerged from with intention; there is an offense incurred with intention and emerged from without intention; there is an offense incurred without intention and emerged from without intention; there is an offense incurred with intention and emerged from with intention. There is an offense: while incurring it, one confesses; while confessing, one incurs an offense. There is an offense: while incurring it, one emerges; while emerging, one incurs an offense. There is an offense incurred by a formal act and emerged from without a formal act; there is an offense incurred without a formal act and emerged from by a formal act; there is an offense incurred by a formal act and emerged from by a formal act; there is an offense incurred without a formal act and emerged from without a formal act.

a. ni. 4.250; dī. ni. 3.313; vibha. 939 Cattāro anariyavohārā – adiṭṭhe diṭṭhavāditā, assute sutavāditā, amute mutavāditā, aviññāte viññātavāditā. Cattāro ariyavohārā – adiṭṭhe adiṭṭhavāditā, assute assutavāditā, amute amutavāditā, aviññāte aviññātavāditā. Aparepi cattāro anariyavohārā – diṭṭhe adiṭṭhavāditā, sute assutavāditā, mute amutavāditā, viññāte aviññātavāditā. Cattāro [M 0.0225] ariyavohārā – diṭṭhe diṭṭhavāditā, sute sutavāditā, mute mutavāditā, viññāte viññātavāditā.

Four ignoble expressions: speaking of the unseen as seen, of the unheard as heard, of the unsensed as sensed, of the unknown as known. Four noble expressions: speaking of the unseen as unseen, of the unheard as unheard, of the unsensed as unsensed, of the unknown as unknown. Another four ignoble expressions: speaking of the seen as unseen, of the heard as unheard, of the sensed as unsensed, of the known as unknown. Four noble expressions: speaking of the seen as seen, of the heard as heard, of the sensed as sensed, of the known as known.

Cattāro pārājikā bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīhi sādhāraṇā; cattāro pārājikā bhikkhunīnaṃ bhikkhūhi asādhāraṇā. Cattāro parikkhārā – atthi parikkhāro rakkhitabbo gopetabbo mamāyitabbo paribhuñjitabbo; atthi parikkhāro rakkhitabbo gopetabbo mamāyitabbo, na paribhuñjitabbo; atthi parikkhāro rakkhitabbo gopetabbo, na mamāyitabbo na paribhuñjitabbo; atthi parikkhāro na rakkhitabbo na gopetabbo, na mamāyitabbo na paribhuñjitabbo. Atthāpatti [T 0.0317] sammukhā āpajjati, parammukhā vuṭṭhāti; atthāpatti parammukhā āpajjati[V 0.0248], sammukhā vuṭṭhāti; atthāpatti sammukhā āpajjati, sammukhā vuṭṭhāti; atthāpatti parammukhā āpajjati, parammukhā vuṭṭhāti. Atthāpatti ajānanto āpajjati, jānanto vuṭṭhāti; atthāpatti jānanto āpajjati, ajānanto vuṭṭhāti; atthāpatti ajānanto āpajjati, ajānanto vuṭṭhāti; atthāpatti jānanto āpajjati, jānanto vuṭṭhāti.

Four pārājika offenses are common to monks and nuns; four pārājika offenses are not common to nuns with monks. Four requisites: there is a requisite to be guarded, to be protected, to be cherished, and to be used; there is a requisite to be guarded, to be protected, and to be cherished, but not to be used; there is a requisite to be guarded and to be protected, but not to be cherished and not to be used; there is a requisite not to be guarded, not to be protected, not to be cherished, and not to be used. There is an offense that one incurs in the presence and emerges from in the absence; there is an offense that one incurs in the absence and emerges from in the presence; there is an offense that one incurs in the presence and emerges from in the presence; there is an offense that one incurs in the absence and emerges from in the absence. There is an offense that one incurs unknowingly and emerges from knowingly; there is an offense that one incurs knowingly and emerges from unknowingly; there is an offense that one incurs unknowingly and emerges from unknowingly; there is an offense that one incurs knowingly and emerges from knowingly.

Catūhākārehi āpattiṃ āpajjati – kāyena āpajjati, vācāya āpajjati, kāyena vācāya āpajjati, kammavācāya āpajjati. Aparehipi catūhākārehi āpattiṃ āpajjati – saṅghamajjhe, gaṇamajjhe, puggalassa santike, liṅgapātubhāvena. Catūhākārehi āpattiyā vuṭṭhāti – kāyena vuṭṭhāti, vācāya vuṭṭhāti, kāyena vācāya vuṭṭhāti, kammavācāya vuṭṭhāti. Aparehipi catūhākārehi āpattiyā vuṭṭhāti – saṅghamajjhe, gaṇamajjhe, puggalassa santike, liṅgapātubhāvena. Saha paṭilābhena purimaṃ jahati, pacchime patiṭṭhāti, viññattiyo paṭippassambhanti, paṇṇattiyo nirujjhanti. Saha paṭilābhena pacchimaṃ jahati, purime patiṭṭhāti, viññattiyo paṭippassambhanti, paṇṇattiyo nirujjhanti. Catasso codanā – sīlavipattiyā codeti[P 5.0126], ācāravipattiyā codeti, diṭṭhivipattiyā codeti, ājīvavipattiyā codeti. Cattāro parivāsā – paṭicchannaparivāso[T 0.0318], appaṭicchannaparivāso, suddhantaparivāso, samodhānaparivāso. Cattāro mānattā – paṭicchannamānattaṃ, appaṭicchannamānattaṃ, pakkhamānattaṃ, samodhānamānattaṃ. Cattāro mānattacārikassa bhikkhuno ratticchedā – sahavāso, vippavāso, anārocanā, ūne gaṇe carati. Cattāro sāmukkaṃsā[M 0.0226]. Cattāro paṭiggahitaparibhogā – yāvakālikaṃ, yāmakālikaṃ, sattāhakālikaṃ, yāvajīvikaṃ. Cattāri mahāvikaṭāni – gūtho, muttaṃ, chārikā, mattikā. Cattāri kammāni – apalokanakammaṃ, ñattikammaṃ, ñattidutiyakammaṃ, ñatticatutthakammaṃ. Aparānipi cattāri kammāni – adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ, dhammena samaggakammaṃ. Catasso vipattiyo – sīlavipatti, ācāravipatti, diṭṭhivipatti, ājīvavipatti. Cattāri adhikaraṇāni – vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, kiccādhikaraṇaṃ. a. ni. 4.211 Cattāro parisadūsanā – bhikkhu dussīlo pāpadhammo parisadūsano, bhikkhunī dussīlā pāpadhammā parisadūsanā, upāsako dussīlo pāpadhammo parisadūsano, upāsikā dussīlā pāpadhammā parisadūsanā. Cattāro parisasobhanā parisasobhaṇā (syā. ka.) – bhikkhu sīlavā kalyāṇadhammo parisasobhano, bhikkhunī sīlavatī kalyāṇadhammā parisasobhanā, upāsako sīlavā kalyāṇadhammo parisasobhano, upāsikā sīlavatī kalyāṇadhammā parisasobhanā.

One incurs an offense in four ways: by body, by speech, by both body and speech, or by a formal act. One also incurs an offense in four other ways: in the midst of the Saṅgha, in the midst of a group, in the presence of an individual, or through the manifestation of sex. One emerges from an offense in four ways: by body, by speech, by both body and speech, or by a formal act. One also emerges from an offense in four other ways: in the midst of the Saṅgha, in the midst of a group, in the presence of an individual, or through the manifestation of sex. Upon acquisition, one abandons the former and establishes the latter; the intimations subside, and the designations cease. Upon acquisition, one abandons the latter and establishes the former; the intimations subside, and the designations cease. There are four accusations: one accuses regarding a corruption of virtue, a corruption of conduct, a corruption of view, or a corruption of livelihood. There are four probationary periods: concealed probation, unconcealed probation, probation until cleared, and compounding probation. There are four periods of penance: concealed penance, unconcealed penance, half-month penance, and compounding penance. There are four interruptions of the nights for a monk observing penance: cohabitation, separation, non-reporting, or practicing with an incomplete quorum. There are four great standards. There are four accepted uses of requisites: for a limited time, for a day and a night, for seven days, or for life. There are four great medicines: excrement, urine, ashes, and clay. There are four kinds of formal acts: the act of information, the act by motion, the act with a motion and one proclamation, and the act with a motion and three proclamations. There are also four other kinds of formal acts: an unlawful act by a divided assembly, an unlawful act by a complete assembly, a lawful act by a divided assembly, and a lawful act by a complete assembly. There are four corruptions: corruption of virtue, corruption of conduct, corruption of view, and corruption of livelihood. There are four kinds of legal issues: disputes, accusations, offenses, and issues of procedure. There are four defilers of assemblies: a bhikkhu who is immoral and of bad character, a bhikkhunī who is immoral and of bad character, a male lay follower who is immoral and of bad character, and a female lay follower who is immoral and of bad character. There are four embellishers of assemblies: a bhikkhu who is virtuous and of good qualities, a bhikkhunī who is virtuous and of good qualities, a male lay follower who is virtuous and of good qualities, and a female lay follower who is virtuous and of good qualities.

Atthāpatti [V 0.0249] āgantuko āpajjati, no āvāsiko; atthāpatti [T 0.0319] āvāsiko āpajjati, no āgantuko; atthāpatti āgantuko ceva āpajjati āvāsiko ca atthāpatti neva āgantuko āpajjati, no āvāsiko. Atthāpatti gamiko āpajjati, no āvāsiko; atthāpatti āvāsiko āpajjati, no gamiko; atthāpatti gamiko ceva āpajjati āvāsiko ca; atthāpatti neva gamiko āpajjati no āvāsiko. Atthi vatthunānattatā no āpattinānattatā, atthi āpattinānattatā no vatthunānattatā, atthi vatthunānattatā ceva āpattinānattatā ca, atthi neva vatthunānattatā no āpattinānattatā. Atthi vatthusabhāgatā no āpattisabhāgatā, atthi āpattisabhāgatā no vatthusabhāgatā, atthi vatthusabhāgatā ceva āpattisabhāgatā ca atthi neva vatthusabhāgatā no āpattisabhāgatā. Atthāpatti upajjhāyo āpajjati no saddhivihāriko, atthāpatti saddhivihāriko āpajjati no upajjhāyo, atthāpatti upajjhāyo ceva āpajjati saddhivihāriko ca, atthāpatti neva upajjhāyo āpajjati no saddhivihāriko. Atthāpatti ācariyo āpajjati [M 0.0227] no antevāsiko, atthāpatti antevāsiko āpajjati no ācariyo, atthāpatti ācariyo ceva āpajjati antevāsiko ca, atthāpatti neva ācariyo āpajjati no antevāsiko. Cattāro paccayā anāpatti vassacchedassa – saṅgho vā bhinno [T 0.0320] hoti, saṅghaṃ vā bhinditukāmā honti, jīvitantarāyo vā hoti, brahmacariyantarāyo vā hoti. Cattāri vacīduccaritāni – musāvādo, pisuṇā vācā, pharusā vācā, samphappalāpo. Cattāri vacīsucaritāni – saccavācā, apisuṇā vācā, saṇhā vācā, mantā bhāsā. Atthi [P 5.0127] ādiyanto garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati, payojento lahukaṃ; atthi ādiyanto lahukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati, payojento garukaṃ, atthi ādiyantopi payojentopi garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati; atthi ādiyantopi payojentopi lahukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati.

There is an offense that a visiting monk commits, but a resident monk does not; there is an offense that a resident monk commits, but a visiting monk does not; there is an offense that both a visiting monk and a resident monk commit; there is an offense that neither a visiting monk nor a resident monk commits. There is an offense that a traveling monk commits, but a resident monk does not; there is an offense that a resident monk commits, but a traveling monk does not; there is an offense that both a traveling monk and a resident monk commit; there is an offense that neither a traveling monk nor a resident monk commits. There is diversity of object but not diversity of offense; there is diversity of offense but not diversity of object; there is diversity of both object and offense; there is neither diversity of object nor diversity of offense. There is similarity of object but not similarity of offense; there is similarity of offense but not similarity of object; there is similarity of both object and offense; there is neither similarity of object nor similarity of offense. There is an offense that a preceptor commits, but a co-resident pupil does not; there is an offense that a co-resident pupil commits, but a preceptor does not; there is an offense that both a preceptor and a co-resident pupil commit; there is an offense that neither a preceptor nor a co-resident pupil commits. There is an offense that a teacher commits, but a student does not; there is an offense that a student commits, but a teacher does not; there is an offense that both a teacher and a student commit; there is an offense that neither a teacher nor a student commits. There are four conditions for no-offense in breaking the rains-residence: the Saṅgha is split, or they desire to split the Saṅgha, or there is danger to life, or there is danger to the holy life. There are four kinds of verbal misconduct: false speech, malicious speech, harsh speech, and idle chatter. There are four kinds of good verbal conduct: truthful speech, non-malicious speech, gentle speech, and considered speech. There is a case where one who takes commits a grave offense, and one who instigates a minor offense; there is a case where one who takes commits a minor offense, and one who instigates a grave offense; there is a case where both one who takes and one who instigates commit a grave offense; there is a case where both one who takes and one who instigates commit a minor offense.

Atthi puggalo abhivādanāraho, no paccuṭṭhānāraho; atthi puggalo paccuṭṭhānāraho, no abhivādanāraho; atthi puggalo abhivādanāraho ceva paccuṭṭhānāraho ca; atthi puggalo neva abhivādanāraho no paccuṭṭhānāraho. Atthi puggalo āsanāraho, no abhivādanāraho; atthi puggalo abhivādanāraho, no āsanāraho; atthi puggalo āsanāraho ceva abhivādanāraho ca; atthi puggalo neva āsanāraho no abhivādanāraho. Atthāpatti kāle āpajjati, no vikāle; atthāpatti vikāle āpajjati, no kāle; atthāpatti kāle ceva āpajjati vikāle ca; atthāpatti neva kāle āpajjati no vikāle. Atthi paṭiggahitaṃ kāle kappati, no vikāle; atthi paṭiggahitaṃ vikāle kappati, no kāle; atthi paṭiggahitaṃ kāle [V 0.0250] ceva kappati [T 0.0321] vikāle ca; atthi paṭiggahitaṃ neva kāle kappati no vikāle. Atthāpatti paccantimesu janapadesu āpajjati, no majjhimesu; atthāpatti majjhimesu janapadesu āpajjati, no paccantimesu; atthāpatti paccantimesu ceva janapadesu āpajjati majjhimesu ca; atthāpatti neva paccantimesu janapadesu āpajjati no majjhimesu. Atthi paccantimesu janapadesu kappati, no majjhimesu; atthi majjhimesu janapadesu kappati, no paccantimesu; atthi paccantimesu ceva janapadesu kappati majjhimesu ca; atthi neva paccantimesu janapadesu kappati no [M 0.0228] majjhimesu. Atthāpatti anto āpajjati, no bahi; atthāpatti bahi āpajjati, no anto; atthāpatti anto ceva āpajjati bahi ca; atthāpatti neva anto āpajjati no bahi. Atthāpatti antosīmāya āpajjati, no bahisīmāya; atthāpatti bahisīmāya āpajjati, no antosīmāya; atthāpatti antosīmāya ceva āpajjati bahisīmāya ca; atthāpatti neva antosīmāya āpajjati no bahisīmāya. Atthāpatti gāme āpajjati, no araññe; atthāpatti araññe āpajjati, no gāme; atthāpatti gāme ceva āpajjati araññe ca; atthāpatti neva gāme āpajjati no araññe.

There is a person worthy of veneration, but not of rising up for; there is a person worthy of rising up for, but not of veneration; there is a person worthy of both veneration and of rising up for; there is a person worthy of neither veneration nor of rising up for. There is a person worthy of a seat, but not of veneration; there is a person worthy of veneration, but not of a seat; there is a person worthy of both a seat and of veneration; there is a person worthy of neither a seat nor of veneration. There is an offense that is committed at the proper time, not at the improper time; there is an offense that is committed at the improper time, not at the proper time; there is an offense that is committed at both the proper time and the improper time; there is an offense that is committed at neither the proper time nor the improper time. There is something received that is permissible at the proper time, not at the improper time; there is something received that is permissible at the improper time, not at the proper time; there is something received that is permissible at both the proper time and the improper time; there is something received that is permissible at neither the proper time nor the improper time. There is an offense that is committed in the border districts, not in the central districts; there is an offense that is committed in the central districts, not in the border districts; there is an offense that is committed in both the border districts and the central districts; there is an offense that is committed in neither the border districts nor the central districts. There is an act that is permissible in the border districts, not in the central districts; there is an act that is permissible in the central districts, not in the border districts; there is an act that is permissible in both the border districts and the central districts; there is an act that is permissible in neither the border districts nor the central districts. There is an offense that is committed inside, not outside; there is an offense that is committed outside, not inside; there is an offense that is committed both inside and outside; there is an offense that is committed neither inside nor outside. There is an offense that is committed within the boundary, not outside the boundary; there is an offense that is committed outside the boundary, not within the boundary; there is an offense that is committed both within the boundary and outside the boundary; there is an offense that is committed neither within the boundary nor outside the boundary. There is an offense that is committed in a village, not in a forest; there is an offense that is committed in a forest, not in a village; there is an offense that is committed in both a village and a forest; there is an offense that is committed neither in a village nor in a forest.

Catasso codanā – vatthusandassanā, āpattisandassanā, saṃvāsapaṭikkhepo[T 0.0322], sāmīcipaṭikkhepo. Cattāro pubbakiccā. Cattāro pattakallā. Cattāri anaññapācittiyāni. Catasso bhikkhusammutiyo. a. ni. 4.17; vibha. 939; dī. ni. 3.311 Cattāri agatigamanāni – chandāgatiṃ gacchati, dosāgatiṃ gacchati, mohāgatiṃ gacchati, bhayāgatiṃ gacchati. Cattāri nāgatigamanāni – na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, na dosāgatiṃ gacchati, na mohāgatiṃ gacchati, na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati. Catūhaṅgehi samannāgato alajjī bhikkhu saṅghaṃ bhindati – chandāgatiṃ gacchanto, dosāgatiṃ gacchanto, mohāgatiṃ gacchanto, bhayāgatiṃ gacchanto. Catūhaṅgehi samannāgato pesalo bhikkhu bhinnaṃ saṅghaṃ samaggaṃ karoti – na chandāgatiṃ gacchanto, na dosāgatiṃ gacchanto, na mohāgatiṃ gacchanto, na bhayāgatiṃ gacchanto. Catūhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno vinayo na pucchitabbo – chandāgatiṃ gacchati, dosāgatiṃ gacchati, mohāgatiṃ gacchati[V 0.0251], bhayāgatiṃ gacchati. Catūhaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā vinayo na pucchitabbo – chandāgatiṃ gacchati, dosāgatiṃ gacchati, mohāgatiṃ gacchati, bhayāgatiṃ gacchati. Catūhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno vinayo na vissajjetabbo – chandāgatiṃ gacchati, dosāgatiṃ gacchati, mohāgatiṃ gacchati, bhayāgatiṃ gacchati. Catūhaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā vinayo na vissajjetabbo – chandāgatiṃ gacchati, dosāgatiṃ gacchati, mohāgatiṃ gacchati, bhayāgatiṃ gacchati. Catūhaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno anuyogo na dātabbo – chandāgatiṃ gacchati[T 0.0323], dosāgatiṃ gacchati, mohāgatiṃ gacchati, bhayāgatiṃ gacchati. Catūhaṅgehi [M 0.0229] samannāgate [P 5.0128] bhikkhunā saddhiṃ vinayo na sākacchitabbo – chandāgatiṃ gacchati, dosāgatiṃ gacchati, mohāgatiṃ gacchati, bhayāgatiṃ gacchati. Atthāpatti gilāno āpajjati, no agilāno; atthāpatti agilāno āpajjati, no gilāno; atthāpatti gilāno ceva āpajjati agilāno ca; atthāpatti neva gilāno āpajjati no agilāno. Cattāri adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni. Cattāri dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni.

There are four kinds of accusations: pointing out the basis, pointing out the offense, rejection of communion, and rejection of proper conduct. There are four preliminary duties. There are four conditions for fitness. There are four pācittiya offenses not involving another factor. There are four authorizations for bhikkhus. There are four wrong courses: one goes astray through desire, one goes astray through hatred, one goes astray through delusion, and one goes astray through fear. There are four right courses: one does not go astray through desire, one does not go astray through hatred, one does not go astray through delusion, and one does not go astray through fear. A shameless bhikkhu endowed with four factors splits the Saṅgha: one who goes astray through desire, goes astray through hatred, goes astray through delusion, and goes astray through fear. A conscientious bhikkhu endowed with four factors reconciles a divided Saṅgha: one who does not go astray through desire, does not go astray through hatred, does not go astray through delusion, and does not go astray through fear. The Vinaya should not be asked of a bhikkhu endowed with four factors: one who goes astray through desire, goes astray through hatred, goes astray through delusion, and goes astray through fear. The Vinaya should not be asked by a bhikkhu endowed with four factors: one who goes astray through desire, goes astray through hatred, goes astray through delusion, and goes astray through fear. The Vinaya should not be explained to a bhikkhu endowed with four factors: one who goes astray through desire, goes astray through hatred, goes astray through delusion, and goes astray through fear. The Vinaya should not be explained by a bhikkhu endowed with four factors: one who goes astray through desire, goes astray through hatred, goes astray through delusion, and goes astray through fear. Leave to question should not be given to a bhikkhu endowed with four factors: one who goes astray through desire, goes astray through hatred, goes astray through delusion, and goes astray through fear. The Vinaya should not be discussed with a bhikkhu endowed with four factors: one who goes astray through desire, goes astray through hatred, goes astray through delusion, and goes astray through fear. There is an offense that a sick bhikkhu incurs, but not one who is not sick; there is an offense that a bhikkhu who is not sick incurs, but not one who is sick; there is an offense that both a sick bhikkhu and one who is not sick incur; there is an offense that neither a sick bhikkhu nor one who is not sick incurs. There are four unlawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha. There are four lawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha.

Catukkaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Chapter of Fours is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Sakavācāya kāyena, pasutto ca acittako;

Āpajjanto ca kammena, vohārā caturo tathā.

By one's own speech, by the body, one who is asleep, and one without intention; one who is incurring, and by an action, and likewise the four expressions.

Bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnañca, parikkhāro ca sammukhā;

Ajānakāye majjhe ca, vuṭṭhāti duvidhā tathā.

For bhikkhus and for bhikkhunīs, requisites, and in the presence; not knowing, by the body, and in the midst, and likewise the two kinds of rehabilitation.

Paṭilābhena codanā, parivāsā ca vuccati;

Mānattacārikā cāpi, sāmukkaṃsā paṭiggahi.

By acquisition, accusation, and probation are mentioned; also the Mānatta and Mānattacārika, the Sāmukkaṃsa, and what is received.

Mahāvikaṭakammāni, puna kamme vipattiyo;

Adhikaraṇā [T 0.0324] dussīlā ca, sobhanāgantukena ca.

The Mahāvikaṭa and Kamma, again Kamma, and failures; disputes, and the immoral, the adorning, and by the newcomer.

Gamiko vatthunānattā, sabhāgupajjhāyena ca;

Ācariyo paccayā vā, duccaritaṃ sucaritaṃ.

The tetrad of the traveler, the tetrad of the diversity of the basis, the tetrad of the similarity of the basis, and the tetrad of the preceptor; the tetrad of the teacher, or the tetrad of conditions, the tetrad of misconduct in speech, and the tetrad of good conduct in speech.

Ādiyanto puggalo ca, araho āsanena ca;

Kāle ca kappati ceva, paccantimesu kappati.

The tetrad of one who takes, the tetrad of the person for veneration, and the tetrad of one worthy of a seat; and the tetrad of time, the tetrad of the time of receiving, the first tetrad of border regions, and the second tetrad of border regions.

Anto anto ca sīmāya, gāme ca codanāya ca;

Pubbakiccaṃ pattakallaṃ, anaññā sammutiyo ca.

The tetrad of what is within, and what is within the boundary, and the village, and accusation; the tetrad of preliminary duties, the tetrad of the fitness of the bowl, the tetrad of the Pācittiya concerning what is not for another, and the tetrad of authorizations for a bhikkhu.

Agati [V 0.0252] nāgati ceva, alajjī pesalena ca;

Pucchitabbā duve ceva, vissajjeyyā tathā duve;

Anuyogo ca sākacchā, gilāno ṭhapanena cāti.

The tetrad of going the wrong course and not going the wrong course, the tetrad of the shameless and the tetrad of the virtuous; and the two tetrads of what is not to be asked, and likewise the two tetrads of what is not to be answered; the tetrad of inquiry not to be undertaken, the tetrad of what is not to be discussed, the tetrad of the sick, and the tetrads of the unrighteous and righteous suspension of the Pātimokkha.

5. Pañcakavāro

5. The Section on Fives

325. Pañca [M 0.0230] āpattiyo. Pañca āpattikkhandhā. Pañca vinītavatthūni. Pañca kammāni ānantarikāni. Pañca puggalā niyatā. Pañca chedanakā āpattiyo. Pañcahākārehi āpattiṃ āpajjati. Pañca āpattiyo. Musāvādapaccayā pañcahākārehi kammaṃ na upeti – sayaṃ vā kammaṃ na karoti, paraṃ vā na ajjhesati, chandaṃ vā pārisuddhiṃ vā na deti, kayiramāne kamme paṭikkosati, kate vā pana kamme adhammadiṭṭhi hoti. Pañcahākārehi kammaṃ upeti [T 0.0325] – sayaṃ vā kammaṃ karoti, paraṃ vā ajjhesati, chandaṃ vā pārisuddhiṃ vā deti, kayiramāne kamme nappaṭikkosati, kate vā pana kamme dhammadiṭṭhi hoti. Pañca piṇḍapātikassa bhikkhuno kappanti – anāmantacāro, gaṇabhojanaṃ, paramparabhojanaṃ, anadhiṭṭhānaṃ, avikappanā. a. ni. 5.102 Pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ussaṅkitaparisaṅkito [P 5.0129] hoti – pāpabhikkhupi akuppadhammopi vesiyāgocaro vā hoti, vidhavāgocaro vā hoti, thullakumārigocaro vā hoti, paṇḍakagocaro vā hoti, bhikkhunigocaro vā hoti. Pañca telāni – tilatelaṃ, sāsapatelaṃ, madhukatelaṃ, eraṇḍakatelaṃ, vasātelaṃ. Pañca vasāni – acchavasaṃ, macchavasaṃ, susukāvasaṃ, sūkaravasaṃ, gadrabhavasaṃ. a. ni. 5.130; dī. ni. 3.316 Pañca byasanāni – ñātibyasanaṃ, bhogabyasanaṃ, rogabyasanaṃ, sīlabyasanaṃ, diṭṭhibyasanaṃ. a. ni. 5.130; dī. ni. 3.316 Pañca sampadā – ñātisampadā, bhogasampadā, arogasampadā, sīlasampadā, diṭṭhisampadā. Pañca nissayapaṭippassaddhiyo upajjhāyamhā – upajjhāyo pakkanto vā hoti, vibbhanto vā, kālaṅkato vā, pakkhasaṅkanto vā, āṇattiyeva pañcamī. Pañca puggalā na upasampādetabbā – addhānahīno, aṅgahīno, vatthuvipanno, karaṇadukkaṭako, aparipūro. Pañca paṃsukūlāni – sosānikaṃ, pāpaṇikaṃ, undūrakkhāyikaṃ, upacikakkhāyikaṃ, aggidaḍḍhaṃ. Aparānipi pañca paṃsukūlāni – gokhāyikaṃ, ajakkhāyikaṃ, thūpacīvaraṃ, ābhisekikaṃ, gatapaṭiyāgataṃ bhatapaṭiyābhataṃ (ka.). Pañca avahārā – theyyāvahāro, pasayhāvahāro, parikappāvahāro[T 0.0326], paṭicchannāvahāro, kusāvahāro. Pañca mahācorā santo saṃvijjamānā lokasmiṃ. Pañca avissajjaniyāni. Pañca avebhaṅgiyāni. Pañcāpattiyo kāyato samuṭṭhanti, na vācato na cittato. Pañcāpattiyo kāyato ca vācato ca samuṭṭhanti, [M 0.0231] cittato. Pañcāpattiyo desanāgāminiyo. Pañca saṅghā[V 0.0253]. Pañca pātimokkhuddesā. Sabbapaccantimesu janapadesu vinayadharapañcamena gaṇena upasampādetabbaṃ. Pañcānisaṃsā kathinatthāre. Pañca kammāni. Yāvatatiyake pañca āpattiyo. Pañcahākārehi adinnaṃ ādiyantassa āpatti pārājikassa. Pañcahākārehi adinnaṃ ādiyantassa āpatti thullaccayassa. Pañcahākārehi adinnaṃ ādiyantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa. Pañca akappiyāni na paribhuñjitabbāni – adinnañca hoti, aviditañca hoti, akappiyañca hoti, appaṭiggahitañca hoti, akatātirittañca hoti. Pañca kappiyāni paribhuñjitabbāni – dinnañca hoti, viditañca hoti, kappiyañca hoti, paṭiggahitañca hoti, katātirittañca hoti. Pañca dānāni apuññāni puññasammatāni lokasmiṃ lokassa (syā.) – majjadānaṃ, samajjadānaṃ, itthidānaṃ, usabhadānaṃ, cittakammadānaṃ. Pañca uppannā duppaṭivinodayā vinodiyā (syā.) – uppanno rāgo duppaṭivinodayo, uppanno doso duppaṭivinodayo, uppanno moho duppaṭivinodayo, uppannaṃ paṭibhānaṃ duppaṭivinodayaṃ, uppannaṃ gamiyacittaṃ duppaṭivinodayaṃ[T 0.0327]. Pañcānisaṃsā sammajjaniyā – sakacittaṃ pasīdati, paracittaṃ pasīdati, devatā attamanā honti, pāsādikasaṃvattanikakammaṃ [P 5.0130] upacinati, kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. Aparepi pañcānisaṃsā sammajjaniyā – sakacittaṃ pasīdati, paracittaṃ pasīdati, devatā attamanā honti, satthusāsanaṃ kataṃ hoti, pacchimā janatā diṭṭhānugatiṃ āpajjati.

325. There are five offenses. There are five aggregates of offenses. There are five settled cases. There are five actions with immediate results. There are five persons fixed in their destiny. There are five offenses entailing cutting off. In five ways, one incurs an offense. On account of false speech, one falls into five offenses. In five ways, a formal act is not complete: one does not perform the act oneself, does not request another to do it, does not give consent or a declaration of purity, objects while the act is being performed, or holds an unrighteous view regarding the act when it is done. In five ways, a formal act is complete: one performs the act oneself, requests another to do it, gives consent or a declaration of purity, does not object while the act is being performed, or holds a righteous view regarding the act when it is done. Five things are allowable for a monk who undertakes the alms-food-eater's practice: going without asking a present monk, a group meal, a consecutive meal, not making a determination of the time, and not making a formal disposal of expected food. A monk endowed with five factors is to be suspected and doubted: whether he is a bad monk or an Arahant of unshakeable nature, he resorts to a place frequented by prostitutes, or widows, or spinsters, or eunuchs, or nuns. There are five kinds of oil: sesame oil, mustard-seed oil, madhuka oil, castor oil, and tallow. There are five kinds of fat: bear fat, fish fat, crocodile fat, pig fat, and donkey fat. There are five losses: loss of relatives, loss of wealth, loss through illness, loss of virtue, and loss of right view. There are five accomplishments: accomplishment in relatives, accomplishment in wealth, accomplishment in health, accomplishment in virtue, and accomplishment in right view. There are five cessations of dependence on a preceptor: the preceptor has gone away, or has disrobed, or has died, or has gone over to another side, and the fifth is by command. Five persons are not to be given higher ordination: one deficient in age, one deficient in limbs, one whose 'basis' is ruined, one who has committed a heinous act, or one who is incomplete in requisites. There are five kinds of rag-robes: from a charnel ground, from a shop, gnawed by rats, gnawed by termites, or burnt by fire. And another five kinds of rag-robes: gnawed by a cow, gnawed by a goat, a stūpa-robe, a consecration-robe, or one brought to a charnel ground and returned. There are five kinds of appropriation: appropriation by stealth, appropriation by force, appropriation by planning, appropriation by concealment, and appropriation by a kusa-grass lot. There are five great thieves existing in the world. There are five things not to be given away. There are five things not to be divided. Five offenses arise from the body, not from speech, not from mind. Five offenses arise from the body and from speech, not from the mind. Five offenses are to be confessed. There are five kinds of Sangha. There are five recitations of the Pātimokkha. In all border districts, higher ordination should be conferred by a chapter with a Vinaya expert as the fifth. There are five benefits in the spreading of the Kaṭhina. There are five formal acts. In the procedure up to the third announcement, there are five offenses. For one who takes what is not given with five factors, there is an offense of pārājika. For one who takes what is not given with five factors, there is an offense of thullaccaya. For one who takes what is not given with five factors, there is an offense of dukkaṭa. Five unallowable things are not to be consumed: it is not formally offered, it is not known to be offered, it is not made allowable, it is not received, or it is not made leftover. Five allowable things are to be consumed: it is formally offered, it is known to be offered, it is made allowable, it is received, and it is made leftover. Five gifts, though considered meritorious in the world, are demeritorious: a gift of intoxicants, a gift for a festival, a gift of a woman, a gift of releasing a bull, and a gift of a painting depicting a man and woman in union. Five arisen things are hard to dispel: arisen lust is hard to dispel; arisen hate is hard to dispel; arisen delusion is hard to dispel; arisen inspiration is hard to dispel; an arisen thought of going on a journey is hard to dispel. There are five benefits of sweeping: one's own mind becomes clear, another's mind becomes clear, the deities are pleased, one accumulates kamma that leads to serenity, and with the breakup of the body, after death, one is reborn in a good destination, the heavenly world. And another five benefits of sweeping: one's own mind becomes clear, another's mind becomes clear, the deities are pleased, the Teacher's instruction is carried out, and a later generation follows the example.

Pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo “bālo” tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – attano bhāsapariyantaṃ na uggaṇhāti, parassa bhāsapariyantaṃ na uggaṇhāti, attano bhāsapariyantaṃ na uggahetvā parassa bhāsapariyantaṃ na uggahetvā adhammena kāreti appaṭiññāya. Pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo “paṇḍito” tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – attano bhāsapariyantaṃ uggaṇhāti, parassa bhāsapariyantaṃ uggaṇhāti, attano bhāsapariyantaṃ uggahetvā parassa bhāsapariyantaṃ uggahetvā dhammena kāreti paṭiññāya. Aparehipi pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo bālo tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – āpattiṃ na jānāti, āpattiyā mūlaṃ na jānāti, āpattisamudayaṃ [M 0.0232] na jānāti, āpattinirodhaṃ na jānāti, āpattinirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ na jānāti. Pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo paṇḍito tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – āpattiṃ jānāti, āpattiyā mūlaṃ jānāti, āpattisamudayaṃ jānāti, āpattinirodhaṃ jānāti[T 0.0328], āpattinirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ jānāti. Aparehipi pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo bālo tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – adhikaraṇaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇasamudayaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇanirodhaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ na jānāti. Pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo paṇḍito tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – adhikaraṇaṃ jānāti[V 0.0254], adhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇasamudayaṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇanirodhaṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ jānāti. Aparehipi pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo bālo tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – vatthuṃ na jānāti, nidānaṃ na jānāti, paññattiṃ na jānāti, anupaññattiṃ na jānāti, anusandhivacanapathaṃ na jānāti. Pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo paṇḍito tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – vatthuṃ jānāti, nidānaṃ jānāti, paññattiṃ jānāti, anupaññattiṃ jānāti, anusandhivacanapathaṃ jānāti. Aparehipi pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo bālo tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – ñattiṃ na jānāti, ñattiyā karaṇaṃ na jānāti, na pubbakusalo hoti, na aparakusalo hoti, akālaññū ca hoti. Pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo paṇḍito tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – ñattiṃ jānāti, ñattiyā karaṇaṃ jānāti, pubbakusalo hoti, aparakusalo hoti, kālaññū ca hoti. Aparehipi pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo bālo tveva saṅkhaṃ [T 0.0329] gacchati – āpattānāpattiṃ na jānāti, lahukagarukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, sāvasesānavasesaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, ācariyaparamparā kho panassa na suggahitā hoti na sumanasikatā na sūpadhāritā. Pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo paṇḍitotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – āpattānāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukagarukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, sāvasesānavasesaṃ āpattiṃ jānati, duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, ācariyaparamparā kho panassa suggahitā hoti sumanasikatā sūpadhāritā. Aparehipi pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo bālo tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – āpattānāpattiṃ na jānāti, lahukagarukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, sāvasesānavasesaṃ [M 0.0233] āpattiṃ na jānāti, duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ [P 5.0131] jānāti, ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni na vitthārena svāgatāni honti na suvibhattāni na suppavattīni na suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso. Pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo paṇḍito tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – āpattānāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukagarukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, sāvasesānavasesaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni honti suvibhattāni suppavattīni suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso. Aparehipi pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo bālo tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – āpattānāpattiṃ na jānāti, lahukagarukaṃ āpattiṃ [T 0.0330] na jānāti, sāvasesānavasesaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇe ca na vinicchayakusalo hoti. Pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo paṇḍito tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – āpattānāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukagarukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, sāvasesānavasesaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇe ca vinicchayakusalo hoti.

A Vinaya-expert endowed with five factors is reckoned only as a “fool”: they do not grasp the extent of their own discourse, they do not grasp the extent of another's discourse, and not having grasped the extent of their own discourse or the extent of another's discourse, they make a decision unrighteously, without admission. A Vinaya-expert endowed with five factors is reckoned only as “wise”: they grasp the extent of their own discourse, they grasp the extent of another's discourse, and having grasped the extent of their own discourse and the extent of another's discourse, they make a decision righteously, with admission. A Vinaya-expert endowed with another five factors is reckoned only as a “fool”: they do not know an offense, they do not know the root of an offense, they do not know the origin of an offense, they do not know the cessation of an offense, they do not know the practice leading to the cessation of an offense. A Vinaya-expert endowed with five factors is reckoned only as “wise”: they know an offense, they know the root of an offense, they know the origin of an offense, they know the cessation of an offense, they know the practice leading to the cessation of an offense. A Vinaya-expert endowed with another five factors is reckoned only as a “fool”: they do not know a legal issue, they do not know the root of a legal issue, they do not know the origin of a legal issue, they do not know the cessation of a legal issue, they do not know the practice leading to the cessation of a legal issue. A Vinaya-expert endowed with five factors is reckoned only as “wise”: they know a legal issue, they know the root of a legal issue, they know the origin of a legal issue, they know the cessation of a legal issue, they know the practice leading to the cessation of a legal issue. A Vinaya-expert endowed with another five factors is reckoned only as a “fool”: they do not know the matter, they do not know the occasion, they do not know the original formulation, they do not know the subsequent formulation, they do not know the sequence of connection and the path of speech. A Vinaya-expert endowed with five factors is reckoned only as “wise”: they know the matter, they know the occasion, they know the original formulation, they know the subsequent formulation, they know the sequence of connection and the path of speech. A Vinaya-expert endowed with another five factors is reckoned only as a “fool”: they do not know the motion, they do not know the function of the motion, they are not skilled in the preceding speech, they are not skilled in the subsequent speech, and they do not know the proper time. A Vinaya-expert endowed with five factors is reckoned only as “wise”: they know the motion, they know the function of the motion, they are skilled in the preceding speech, they are skilled in the subsequent speech, and they know the proper time. A Vinaya-expert endowed with another five factors is reckoned only as a “fool”: they do not know what is an offense and what is not an offense, they do not know a light and a serious offense, they do not know an offense with a remainder and without a remainder, they do not know a gross and a non-gross offense, and for them, the succession of teachers is not well-grasped, not well-attended to, and not well-retained. A Vinaya-expert endowed with five factors is reckoned only as “wise”: they know what is an offense and what is not an offense, they know a light and a serious offense, they know an offense with a remainder and without a remainder, they know a gross and a non-gross offense, and for them, the succession of teachers is well-grasped, well-attended to, and well-retained. A Vinaya-expert endowed with another five factors is reckoned only as a “fool”: they do not know what is an offense and what is not an offense, they do not know a light and a serious offense, they do not know an offense with a remainder and without a remainder, they do not know a gross and a non-gross offense, and for them, the two Pātimokkhas are not well-mastered in detail, not well-analyzed, not well-recited, and not well-decided upon by rule and by detailed explanation. A Vinaya-expert endowed with five factors is reckoned only as “wise”: they know what is an offense and what is not an offense, they know a light and a serious offense, they know an offense with a remainder and without a remainder, they know a gross and a non-gross offense, and for them, the two Pātimokkhas are well-mastered in detail, well-analyzed, well-recited, and well-decided upon by rule and by detailed explanation. A Vinaya-expert endowed with another five factors is reckoned only as a “fool”: they do not know what is an offense and what is not an offense, they do not know a light and a serious offense, they do not know an offense with a remainder and without a remainder, they do not know a gross and a non-gross offense, and they are not skilled in making decisions in legal issues. A Vinaya-expert endowed with five factors is reckoned only as “wise”: they know what is an offense and what is not an offense, they know a light and a serious offense, they know an offense with a remainder and without a remainder, they know a gross and a non-gross offense, and they are skilled in making decisions in legal issues.

a. ni. 5.181; pari. 443 Pañca [V 0.0255] āraññikā – mandattā momūhattā āraññiko hoti, pāpiccho icchāpakato āraññiko hoti, ummādā cittakkhepā āraññiko hoti, vaṇṇitaṃ buddhehi buddhasāvakehīti āraññiko hoti, api ca appicchaññeva nissāya santuṭṭhiññeva nissāya sallekhaññeva nissāya pavivekaññeva nissāya idamatthitaññeva idamaṭṭhitaññeva (sī. syā.) nissāya āraññiko hoti. Pañca piṇḍapātikā…pe… pañca paṃsukūlikā…pe… pañca rukkhamūlikā…pe… pañca sosānikā…pe… pañca abbhokāsikā…pe… pañca tecīvarikā…pe… pañca sapadānacārikā…pe… pañca nesajjikā…pe… pañca yathāsanthatikā…pe… pañca ekāsanikā…pe… pañca khalupacchābhattikā…pe… pañca pattapiṇḍikā – mandattā momūhattā pattapiṇḍiko hoti, pāpiccho icchāpakato pattapiṇḍiko hoti, ummādā cittakkhepā pattapiṇḍiko hoti, vaṇṇitaṃ buddhehi buddhasāvakehīti pattapiṇḍiko hoti, api ca appicchaññeva [T 0.0331] nissāya santuṭṭhiññeva nissāya sallekhaññeva nissāya pavivekaññeva nissāya idamatthitaññeva nissāya pattapiṇḍiko hoti.

There are five kinds of forest-dwellers: one becomes a forest-dweller due to dullness and delusion; one becomes a forest-dweller due to evil desires and being overcome by desire; one becomes a forest-dweller due to madness and mental distraction; one becomes a forest-dweller thinking, 'It is praised by the Buddhas and the disciples of the Buddhas'; and furthermore, one becomes a forest-dweller relying solely on fewness of wishes, contentment, effacement, seclusion, and this very purpose. There are five kinds of alms-food eaters… and so on… five kinds of rag-robe wearers… five kinds of tree-root dwellers… five kinds of charnel-ground dwellers… five kinds of open-air dwellers… five kinds of triple-robe wearers… five kinds of house-to-house alms-goers… five kinds of sitters… five kinds of any-bed users… five kinds of one-session eaters… five kinds of refusers of subsequent food… There are five kinds of bowl-food eaters: one becomes a bowl-food eater due to dullness and delusion; one becomes a bowl-food eater due to evil desires and being overcome by desire; one becomes a bowl-food eater due to madness and mental distraction; one becomes a bowl-food eater thinking, 'It is praised by the Buddhas and the disciples of the Buddhas'; and furthermore, one becomes a bowl-food eater relying solely on fewness of wishes, contentment, effacement, seclusion, and this very purpose.

pari. 417 Pañcahaṅgehi [M 0.0234] samannāgatena bhikkhunā nānissitena vatthabbaṃ – uposathaṃ na jānāti, uposathakammaṃ na jānāti, pātimokkhaṃ na jānāti, pātimokkhuddesaṃ na jānāti, ūnapañcavasso hoti. Pañcahaṅgehi [P 5.0132] samannāgatena bhikkhunā anissitena vatthabbaṃ – uposathaṃ jānāti, uposathakammaṃ jānāti, pātimokkhaṃ jānāti, pātimokkhuddesaṃ jānāti, pañcavasso vā hoti atirekapañcavasso vā. Aparehipi pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā nānissitena vatthabbaṃ – pavāraṇaṃ na jānāti, pavāraṇākammaṃ na jānāti, pātimokkhaṃ na jānāti, pātimokkhuddesaṃ na jānāti, ūnapañcavasso hoti. Pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anissitena vatthabbaṃ – pavāraṇaṃ jānāti, pavāraṇākammaṃ jānāti, pātimokkhaṃ jānāti, pātimokkhuddesaṃ jānāti, pañcavasso vā hoti atirekapañcavasso vā. Aparehipi pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā nānissitena vatthabbaṃ – āpattānāpattiṃ na jānāti, lahukagarukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, sāvasesānavasesaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, ūnapañcavasso hoti. Pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anissitena vatthabbaṃ – āpattānāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukagarukaṃ āpattiṃ [T 0.0332] jānāti, sāvasesānavasesaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, pañcavasso vā hoti atirekapañcavasso vā. Pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatāya bhikkhuniyā nānissitāya vatthabbaṃ – uposathaṃ na jānāti, uposathakammaṃ na jānāti, pātimokkhaṃ na jānāti, pātimokkhuddesaṃ na jānāti, ūnapañcavassā hoti. Pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatāya bhikkhuniyā anissitāya vatthabbaṃ [V 0.0256] – uposathaṃ jānāti, uposathakammaṃ jānāti, pātimokkhaṃ jānāti, pātimokkhuddesaṃ jānāti, pañcavassā vā hoti atirekapañcavassā vā. Aparehipi pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatāya bhikkhuniyā nānissitāya vatthabbaṃ – pavāraṇaṃ na jānāti, pavāraṇākammaṃ na jānāti, pātimokkhaṃ na jānāti, pātimokkhuddesaṃ na jānāti, ūnapañcavassā hoti. Pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatāya bhikkhuniyā anissitāya vatthabbaṃ – pavāraṇaṃ jānāti, pavāraṇākammaṃ jānāti, pātimokkhaṃ jānāti, pātimokkhuddesaṃ jānāti, pañcavassā vā hoti atirekapañcavassā vā. Aparehipi pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatāya bhikkhuniyā nānissitāya vatthabbaṃ [M 0.0235] – āpattānāpattiṃ na jānāti, lahukagarukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, sāvasesānavasesaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, ūnapañcavassā hoti. Pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatāya bhikkhuniyā anissitāya vatthabbaṃ – āpattānāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukagarukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, sāvasesānavasesaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ [T 0.0333] jānāti, pañcavassā vā hoti atirekapañcavassā vā.

A bhikkhu endowed with five factors is not to live without dependence: he does not know the Uposatha, does not know the Uposatha ceremony, does not know the Pātimokkha, does not know the recitation of the Pātimokkha, and has less than five years of seniority. A bhikkhu endowed with five factors is to live without dependence: he knows the Uposatha, knows the Uposatha ceremony, knows the Pātimokkha, knows the recitation of the Pātimokkha, and has five years or more of seniority. Furthermore, a bhikkhu endowed with another five factors is not to live without dependence: he does not know the Pavāraṇā, does not know the Pavāraṇā ceremony, does not know the Pātimokkha, does not know the recitation of the Pātimokkha, and has less than five years of seniority. A bhikkhu endowed with five factors is to live without dependence: he knows the Pavāraṇā, knows the Pavāraṇā ceremony, knows the Pātimokkha, knows the recitation of the Pātimokkha, and has five years or more of seniority. Furthermore, a bhikkhu endowed with another five factors is not to live without dependence: he does not know what is an offense and what is not an offense, does not know minor and grave offenses, does not know offenses with remainder and without remainder, does not know gross and non-gross offenses, and has less than five years of seniority. A bhikkhu endowed with five factors is to live without dependence: he knows what is an offense and what is not an offense, knows minor and grave offenses, knows offenses with remainder and without remainder, knows gross and non-gross offenses, and has five years or more of seniority. A bhikkhunī endowed with five factors is not to live without dependence: she does not know the Uposatha, does not know the Uposatha ceremony, does not know the Pātimokkha, does not know the recitation of the Pātimokkha, and has less than five years of seniority. A bhikkhunī endowed with five factors is to live without dependence: she knows the Uposatha, knows the Uposatha ceremony, knows the Pātimokkha, knows the recitation of the Pātimokkha, and has five years or more of seniority. Furthermore, a bhikkhunī endowed with another five factors is not to live without dependence: she does not know the Pavāraṇā, does not know the Pavāraṇā ceremony, does not know the Pātimokkha, does not know the recitation of the Pātimokkha, and has less than five years of seniority. A bhikkhunī endowed with five factors is to live without dependence: she knows the Pavāraṇā, knows the Pavāraṇā ceremony, knows the Pātimokkha, knows the recitation of the Pātimokkha, and has five years or more of seniority. Furthermore, a bhikkhunī endowed with another five factors is not to live without dependence: she does not know what is an offense and what is not an offense, does not know minor and grave offenses, does not know offenses with remainder and without remainder, does not know gross and non-gross offenses, and has less than five years of seniority. A bhikkhunī endowed with five factors is to live without dependence: she knows what is an offense and what is not an offense, knows minor and grave offenses, knows offenses with remainder and without remainder, knows gross and non-gross offenses, and has five years or more of seniority.

Pañca ādīnavā apāsādike – attāpi attānaṃ upavadati, anuviccapi viññū garahanti, pāpako kittisaddo abbhuggacchati, sammūḷho kālaṃ karoti, kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati. Pañcānisaṃsā pāsādike – attāpi attānaṃ na upavadati, anuviccapi viññū pasaṃsanti, kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggacchati, asammūḷho kālaṃ karoti, kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. Aparepi pañca ādīnavā apāsādike – appasannā na pasīdanti, pasannānaṃ ekaccānaṃ aññathattaṃ hoti, satthusāsanaṃ akataṃ hoti, pacchimā janatā diṭṭhānugatiṃ nāpajjati, cittamassa na pasīdati. Pañcānisaṃsā pāsādike – appasannā pasīdanti, pasannānaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya hoti, satthusāsanaṃ kataṃ hoti, pacchimā janatā diṭṭhānugatiṃ āpajjati, cittamassa pasīdati. Pañca ādīnavā kulūpake – anāmantacāre āpajjati, raho nisajjāya āpajjati, paṭicchanne āsane āpajjati, mātugāmassa uttarichappañcavācāhi dhammaṃ desento āpajjati, kāmasaṅkappabahulo ca viharati. Pañca ādīnavā kulūpakassa bhikkhuno – ativelaṃ kulesu saṃsaṭṭhassa viharato mātugāmassa abhiṇhadassanaṃ, dassane sati saṃsaggo, saṃsagge sati vissāso, vissāse sati otāro, otiṇṇacittassetaṃ [T 0.0334] bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ anabhirato vā brahmacariyaṃ carissati aññataraṃ vā saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjissati sikkhaṃ vā paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissati.

There are five drawbacks in that which does not inspire confidence: one blames oneself; having investigated, the wise also criticize one; an evil reputation spreads; one dies confused; and with the breaking up of the body, after death, one is reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell. There are five benefits in that which is inspiring of confidence: one does not blame oneself; having investigated, the wise also praise one; a good reputation spreads; one dies unconfused; and with the breaking up of the body, after death, one is reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world. There are another five drawbacks in that which does not inspire confidence: those who are not confident do not gain confidence; for some of those who have confidence, it is lost; the Teacher’s dispensation is not fulfilled; the later generation does not follow the example; and his mind is not serene. There are five benefits in that which is inspiring of confidence: those who are not confident gain confidence; for those who have confidence, their confidence increases; the Teacher’s dispensation is fulfilled; the later generation follows the example; and his mind becomes serene. There are five drawbacks for a bhikkhu who frequents families: he incurs the offense of entering uninvited; he incurs the offense of sitting in a secluded place; he incurs the offense of sitting on a concealed seat; he incurs an offense by teaching the Dhamma to a woman with more than five or six sentences; and he dwells with many sensual thoughts. There are five drawbacks for a bhikkhu who frequents families and dwells associating with them excessively: frequent seeing of women occurs; seeing leads to association; association leads to familiarity; familiarity leads to a descent into defilements; and for a bhikkhu whose mind has so descended, it is to be expected that he will either practice the holy life while dissatisfied, or he will incur some defiled offense, or, having renounced the training, he will return to the lower life.

pāci. 92 Pañca [V 0.0257] bījajātāni – mūlabījaṃ, khandhabījaṃ, phaḷubījaṃ, aggabījaṃ, bījabījaññeva bījabījameva (ka.) pañcamaṃ. Pañcahi samaṇakappehi phalaṃ paribhuñjitabbaṃ – aggiparijitaṃ, satthaparijitaṃ, nakhaparijitaṃ, abījaṃ, nibbattabījaññeva nibbaṭṭabījaññeva (sī.), nibbaṭabījaññeva (syā.), nippaṭṭabījaññeva (ka.) pañcamaṃ. Pañca visuddhiyo – nidānaṃ uddisitvā avasesaṃ [M 0.0236] sutena sāvetabbaṃ, ayaṃ paṭhamā visuddhi; nidānaṃ uddisitvā cattāri pārājikāni uddisitvā avasesaṃ sutena sāvetabbaṃ, ayaṃ dutiyā visuddhi; nidānaṃ uddisitvā cattāri pārājikāni uddisitvā terasa saṅghādisese uddisitvā avasesaṃ sutena sāvetabbaṃ, ayaṃ tatiyā visuddhi; nidānaṃ uddisitvā cattāri pārājikāni uddisitvā terasa saṅghādisese uddisitvā dve aniyate [P 5.0133] uddisitvā avasesaṃ sutena sāvetabbaṃ, ayaṃ catutthā visuddhi; vitthāreneva pañcamī. Aparāpi pañca visuddhiyo – suttuddeso, pārisuddhiuposatho, adhiṭṭhānuposatho, pavāraṇā, sāmaggīuposathoyeva pañcamo. Pañcānisaṃsā vinayadhare – attano sīlakkhandho sugutto hoti surakkhito, kukkuccapakatānaṃ paṭisaraṇaṃ hoti, visārado saṅghamajjhe voharati, paccatthike sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggaṇhāti, saddhammaṭṭhitiyā paṭipanno hoti. Pañca adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni[T 0.0335]. Pañca dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanānīti.

There are five kinds of seeds: root-seed, stem-seed, joint-seed, shoot-seed, and seed-seed itself is the fifth. Fruit is to be consumed by means of five ways of making it allowable for a monk: made allowable by fire, made allowable by a knife, made allowable by a fingernail, fruit with immature seeds, and fruit from which the seed has been removed is the fifth. There are five purifications: after reciting the introduction, the remainder should be made heard with the word 'suta'—this is the first purification; after reciting the introduction and the four Pārājikas, the remainder should be made heard with the word 'suta'—this is the second purification; after reciting the introduction, the four Pārājikas, and the thirteen Saṅghādisesas, the remainder should be made heard with the word 'suta'—this is the third purification; after reciting the introduction, the four Pārājikas, the thirteen Saṅghādisesas, and the two Aniyatas, the remainder should be made heard with the word 'suta'—this is the fourth purification; the recitation in full is the fifth. There are another five purifications: the Suttuddesa Uposatha, the Pārisuddhi Uposatha, the Adhiṭṭhāna Uposatha, the Pavāraṇā, and the Sāmaggī Uposatha itself is the fifth. There are five benefits in one who upholds the Vinaya: one's own aggregate of virtue is well-guarded and well-protected; one is a refuge for those afflicted by remorse; one speaks confidently in the midst of the Saṅgha; one rightly and well restrains adversaries with the Dhamma; one practices for the stability of the true Dhamma. There are five unlawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha. There are five lawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha.

Pañcakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Pentad is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Āpatti āpattikkhandhā, vinītānantarena ca;

Puggalā chedanā ceva, āpajjati ca paccayā.

The pentad of Offenses, the pentad of Aggregates of Offenses, the pentad of Disciplined Cases and the pentad of Actions with Immediate Results; the pentad of Individuals, the pentad of Cutting, the pentad of 'Committing an Offense', and the pentad of Conditions.

Na upeti upeti ca, kappantusaṅkitelañca;

Vasaṃ byasanā sampadā, passaddhi puggalena ca.

The pentad of 'Does Not Amount To' and 'Amounts To', the pentad of 'Is Allowable', the pentad of 'Is Suspected', and the pentad of Oil; the pentad of Fat, the pentad of Misfortunes, the pentad of Accomplishments, the pentad of Cessation of Dependence, and the pentad of Individuals (not to be ordained).

Sosānikaṃ khāyitañca, theyyaṃ coro ca vuccati;

Avissajji avebhaṅgi, kāyato kāyavācato.

The pentad of the Charnel-Ground-Dweller and 'Eaten by a Cow', Theft and the Thief are mentioned; the pentad of Not Given Up, the pentad of Not Distributed, from the Body, and from Body and Speech.

Desanā [V 0.0258] saṅghaṃ uddesaṃ, paccantikathinena ca;

Kammāni yāvatatiyaṃ, pārājithulladukkaṭaṃ.

The pentad of offenses to be confessed, the pentad on the Saṅgha, the pentad on the recitation of the Pātimokkha, the pentad on the border region, and the pentad on the benefits of spreading the kathina cloth; the pentad on formal acts, the pentad on up to the third time, the pentad on Pārājika, the pentad on Thullaccaya, and the pentad on Dukkaṭa.

Akappiyaṃ kappiyañca, apuññaduvinodayā;

Sammajjanī apare ca, bhāsaṃ āpattimeva ca.

The pentad on the improper and the pentad on the proper, the pentad on demerit and the pentad on what is difficult to dispel; the pentad on the benefits of sweeping and the other pentad on the benefits of sweeping, the pentad on the limit of speech, and the pentad on offenses.

Adhikaraṇaṃ vatthu ñatti, āpattā ubhayāni ca;

Lahukaṭṭhamakā ete, kaṇhasukkā vijānatha.

The pentad on legal questions, the pentad on the ground, the pentad on the motion, the pentad on offense and non-offense, and the pentad on both; and the eighth, the pentad on the light. You should know these eight pentads as the dark side and the bright side.

Araññaṃ piṇḍapātañca, paṃsurukkhasusānikā;

Abbhokāso cīvarañca, sapadāno nisajjiko.

The forest-dweller's ascetic practice, the alms-food-eater's ascetic practice, the refuse-rag-wearer's ascetic practice, the tree-root-dweller's ascetic practice, the charnel-ground-dweller's ascetic practice, the open-air-dweller's ascetic practice, the triple-robe-wearer's ascetic practice, the house-to-house-goer's ascetic practice, and the sitter's ascetic practice.

Santhati [M 0.0237] khalu pacchāpi, pattapiṇḍikameva ca;

Uposathaṃ [T 0.0336] pavāraṇaṃ, āpattānāpattipi ca.

The any-bed-user's ascetic practice, the after-food-refuser's ascetic practice, and the bowl-food-eater's ascetic practice; the pentad on the Uposatha, the pentad on the Pavāraṇā, and the pentad on offense and non-offense.

Kaṇhasukkapadā ete, bhikkhunīnampi te tathā;

Apāsādikapāsādi, tatheva apare duve.

These three pentads are the dark side and the bright side. For the bhikkhunīs, too, those three pentads are likewise. In the pentad on the displeasing and the pentad on the pleasing, it is likewise; and also the other two: the other pentad on the displeasing and the other pentad on the pleasing.

Kulūpake ativelaṃ, bījaṃ samaṇakappi ca;

Visuddhi apare ceva, vinayādhammikena ca;

Dhammikā ca tathā vuttā, niṭṭhitā suddhipañcakāti.

The pentad on frequenting families, the pentad on an inappropriate time, the pentad on what is born from seeds, and the pentad on what is befitting an ascetic; the pentad on purity and the other pentad on purity; and the pentad on the Vinaya-expert, the pentad on the unlawful suspension of the Pātimokkha, and the pentad on the lawful suspension of the Pātimokkha. Thus spoken, the pentads on purity are concluded.

6. Chakkavāro

6. The Section on Sixes

326. dī. ni. 3.324 Cha agāravā. Cha gāravā. Cha vinītavatthūni. Cha sāmīciyo. Cha āpattisamuṭṭhānā. Chacchedanakā āpattiyo. Chahākārehi āpattiṃ āpajjati. Chānisaṃsā vinayadhare. Cha paramāni. Chārattaṃ ticīvarena vippavasitabbaṃ. Cha cīvarāni[P 5.0134]. Cha rajanāni. Cha āpattiyo kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti na vācato. Cha āpattiyo vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti na kāyato. Cha āpattiyo kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti. Cha kammāni. Cha vivādamūlāni. Cha anuvādamūlāni. Cha sāraṇīyā dhammā dīghaso. Cha vidatthiyo, sugatavidatthiyā, tiriyaṃ cha vidatthiyo. Cha nissayapaṭippassaddhiyo ācariyamhā. Cha nahāne anupaññattiyo – vippakatacīvaraṃ [T 0.0337] ādāya pakkamati, vippakatacīvaraṃ samādāya pakkamati.

326. Six are the instances of disrespect. Six are the instances of respect. Six are the matters of training. Six are the proper conducts. Six are the origins of offenses. Six are the offenses preceded by cutting. One falls into an offense through six causes. Six are the benefits for a Vinaya-expert. Six are the maximums. One may dwell apart from the three robes for six nights. Six are the robes. Six are the dyes. Six offenses arise from the body and from the mind, not from speech. Six offenses arise from speech and from the mind, not from the body. Six offenses arise from the body, from speech, and from the mind. Six are the formal acts. Six are the roots of dispute. Six are the roots of accusation. Six are the conditions for cordiality. In length, six spans by the Sugata's span; in width, six spans. Six are the cessations of dependence on a teacher. Six are the supplementary allowances concerning bathing: he departs taking an unfinished robe; he departs having properly taken an unfinished robe.

mahāva. 85 ādayo Chahaṅgehi [V 0.0259] samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ nissayo dātabbo sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo – asekkhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena samādhikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena paññakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena vimuttikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, dasavasso vā hoti atirekadasavasso vā.

A bhikkhu endowed with six qualities should give the higher ordination, give dependence, and have a novice attend on him: he is endowed with the aggregate of virtue of one beyond training, endowed with the aggregate of concentration of one beyond training, endowed with the aggregate of wisdom of one beyond training, endowed with the aggregate of liberation of one beyond training, endowed with the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training, and he is of ten years' standing or more than ten years' standing.

Aparehipi chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ nissayo dātabbo sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo – attanā asekkhena sīlakkhandhe [M 0.0238] samannāgato hoti, paraṃ asekkhe sīlakkhandhe samādapetā; attanā asekkhena samādhikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, paraṃ asekkhe samādhikkhandhe samādapetā; attanā asekkhena paññakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, paraṃ asekkhe paññakkhandhe samādapetā; attanā asekkhena vimuttikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, paraṃ asekkhe vimuttikkhandhe samādapetā; attanā asekkhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, paraṃ asekkhe vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhe samādapetā; dasavasso vā hoti atirekadasavasso vā.

A bhikkhu endowed with six other qualities may give the higher ordination, give dependence, and have a novice attend on him: he himself is endowed with the aggregate of virtue of one beyond training, and he establishes another in the aggregate of virtue of one beyond training; he himself is endowed with the aggregate of concentration of one beyond training, and he establishes another in the aggregate of concentration of one beyond training; he himself is endowed with the aggregate of wisdom of one beyond training, and he establishes another in the aggregate of wisdom of one beyond training; he himself is endowed with the aggregate of liberation of one beyond training, and he establishes another in the aggregate of liberation of one beyond training; he himself is endowed with the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training, and he establishes another in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training; and he is of ten years' standing or more than ten years' standing.

Aparehipi chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ nissayo dātabbo sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo – saddho hoti, hirimā hoti, ottappī hoti, āraddhavīriyo hoti[T 0.0338], upaṭṭhitassati hoti, dasavasso vā hoti atirekadasavasso vā.

A bhikkhu endowed with six other qualities may give the higher ordination, give dependence, and have a novice attend on him: he is faithful, he has a sense of moral shame, he has a sense of moral dread, he is energetic, his mindfulness is established, and he is of ten years' standing or more than ten years' standing.

Aparehipi chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ nissayo dātabbo sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo – na adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, na ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, na atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti, bahussuto hoti, paññavā hoti, dasavasso vā hoti atirekadasavasso vā.

A bhikkhu endowed with six other qualities may give the higher ordination, give dependence, and have a novice attend on him: he is not corrupt in higher virtue, he is not corrupt in conduct through transgression, he is not corrupt in view through holding extreme views, he is learned, he is wise, and he is of ten years' standing or more than ten years' standing.

Aparehipi chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ nissayo dātabbo sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo – paṭibalo hoti antevāsiṃ vā saddhivihāriṃ vā gilānaṃ upaṭṭhātuṃ vā upaṭṭhāpetuṃ vā, anabhirataṃ vūpakāsetuṃ vā vūpakāsāpetuṃ vā anabhiratiṃ (ka.), uppannaṃ kukkuccaṃ dhammato vinodetuṃ vinodetuṃ vā vinodāpetuṃ vā (syā.) mahāva. 85, āpattiṃ jānāti, āpattivuṭṭhānaṃ jānāti, dasavasso vā hoti atirekadasavasso vā.

A bhikkhu endowed with six other qualities may give the higher ordination, give dependence, and have a novice attend on him: he is capable of attending to or having attended to a sick pupil or co-resident; he is capable of leading away or having led away one who is discontented; he is capable of dispelling arisen remorse according to the Dhamma; he knows an offense; he knows the emergence from an offense; and he is of ten years' standing or more than ten years' standing.

Aparehipi [V 0.0260] chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ nissayo dātabbo sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo – paṭibalo hoti antevāsiṃ vā saddhivihāriṃ vā ābhisamācārikāya sikkhāya sikkhāpetuṃ, ādibrahmacāriyakāya sikkhāya vinetuṃ, abhidhamme vinetuṃ, abhivinaye vinetuṃ, uppannaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ dhammato vivecetuṃ, dasavasso vā hoti atirekadasavasso vā.

A bhikkhu endowed with six other qualities may give the higher ordination, give dependence, and have a novice attend on him: he is capable of training a pupil or co-resident in the training in proper conduct; he is capable of guiding them in the training in the fundamentals of the holy life; he is capable of guiding them in the Abhidhamma; he is capable of guiding them in the Abhivinaya; he is capable of dispelling an arisen wrong view according to the Dhamma; and he is of ten years' standing or more than ten years' standing.
