Aparehipi [M 0.0239] chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ nissayo dātabbo sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo – āpattiṃ jānāti, anāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukaṃ [T 0.0339] āpattiṃ jānāti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni honti suvibhattāni suppavattīni suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso, dasavasso vā hoti atirekadasavasso vā.

A bhikkhu endowed with six other qualities may give the higher ordination, give dependence, and have a novice attend on him: he knows an offense; he knows what is not an offense; he knows a light offense; he knows a grave offense; both Pātimokkhas are well-mastered by him in detail, well-analyzed, well-established, and well-judged, according to the rules and their detailed analysis; and he is of ten years' standing or more than ten years' standing.

Cha adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni, cha dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanānīti.

There are six unrighteous postponements of the Pātimokkha, and six righteous postponements of the Pātimokkha.

Chakkaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section of Sixes is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Agāravā gāravā ca, vinītā sāmīcipi ca;

Samuṭṭhānā chedanā ceva, ākārānisaṃsena ca.

Disrespect and respect, training matters and proper conduct; origins and cutting off, ways and benefits.

Paramāni ca chārattaṃ, cīvaraṃ rajanāni ca;

Kāyato cittato cāpi, vācato cittatopi ca.

Maximum limits and six nights, robes and dyes; from body and mind, and also from speech and mind.

Kāyavācācittato ca, kammavivādameva ca;

Anuvādā dīghaso ca, tiriyaṃ nissayena ca.

From body, speech, and mind, formal acts and disputes; accusations, length, width, and dependence.

Anupaññatti ādāya, samādāya tatheva ca;

Asekkhe samādapetā, saddho adhisīlena ca;

Gilānābhisamācārī, āpattādhammadhammikāti.

The group of six on supplementary allowances, the group of six on taking, and likewise the group of six on undertaking; the group of six on the one beyond training, the group of six on establishing, the group of six on faith, and the group of six on higher virtue; the group of six on the sick, the group of six on proper conduct, the group of six on offenses, the group of six on the unrighteous suspension of the Pātimokkha, and the group of six on the righteous suspension of the Pātimokkha.

7. Sattakavāro

7. The Chapter of Sevens

327. Sattāpattiyo[V 0.0261]. Sattāpattikkhandhā. Satta vinītavatthūni. Satta sāmīciyo. Satta adhammikā paṭiññātakaraṇā. Satta dhammikā paṭiññātakaraṇā. Sattannaṃ anāpatti sattāhakaraṇīyena [T 0.0340] gantuṃ. Sattānisaṃsā vinayadhare. Satta paramāni[P 5.0135]. Sattame aruṇuggamane nissaggiyaṃ hoti. Satta samathā. Satta kammāni. Satta āmakadhaññāni. Tiriyaṃ sattantarā. Gaṇabhojane [M 0.0240] satta anupaññattiyo. Bhesajjāni paṭiggahetvā sattāhaparamaṃ sannidhikārakaṃ paribhuñjitabbāni. Katacīvaraṃ ādāya pakkamati. Katacīvaraṃ samādāya pakkamati. Bhikkhussa na hoti āpatti daṭṭhabbā. Bhikkhussa hoti āpatti daṭṭhabbā. Bhikkhussa hoti āpatti daṭṭhabbā paṭikātabbā (sabbattha) aṭṭhakathā ca campeyyakkhandhake adhammakammādikathā ca oloketabbā. Satta adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni. Satta dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni.

327. There are seven offenses. There are seven aggregates of offenses. There are seven settled cases. There are seven proper courtesies. There are seven unrighteous acts of confession. There are seven righteous acts of confession. For the seven kinds of persons, there is no offense in going on business to be done within seven days. There are seven benefits for a Vinaya-expert. There are seven supreme things. At the seventh sunrise, it becomes subject to forfeiture. There are seven means of settling legal questions. There are seven formal acts. There are seven kinds of raw grain. Seven cubits across. Regarding group meals, there are seven supplementary allowances. Having received medicines, they are to be consumed after having been stored for a maximum period of seven days. Taking a completed robe, he departs. Having well undertaken a completed robe, he departs. For a bhikkhu, there is no offense to be seen. For a bhikkhu, there is an offense to be seen. For a bhikkhu, there is an offense to be seen. There are seven unrighteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha. There are seven righteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha.

a. ni. 7.75 Sattahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu vinayadharo hoti – āpattiṃ jānāti, anāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu, catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ ābhicetasikānaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī, āsavānañca khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.

A bhikkhu endowed with seven qualities is a master of the discipline: he knows an offense, he knows what is not an offense, he knows a light offense, he knows a heavy offense; he is virtuous, he dwells restrained by the restraint of the Pātimokkha, endowed with good conduct and resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults, undertaking and training himself in the training rules; he is one who obtains at will, without trouble or difficulty, the four jhānas that are of the higher mind, pleasant dwellings in this very life; and through the destruction of the taints, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge in this very life, he enters upon and dwells in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom.

Aparehipi sattahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu vinayadharo hoti – āpattiṃ jānāti, anāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā [T 0.0341] majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ abhivadanti tathārūpassa dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā dhatā (sī. syā.) vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā, catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ ābhicetasikānaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī, āsavānañca khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.

A bhikkhu endowed with seven other qualities is an expert in the discipline: he knows an offense, he knows what is not an offense, he knows a light offense, he knows a heavy offense; he is very learned, a bearer of the teachings, a repository of learning; those teachings that are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing, which proclaim the wholly fulfilled and purified spiritual life—he has heard many such teachings, retained them, recited them verbally, reflected upon them in his mind, and penetrated them well by wisdom; he is one who obtains at will, without trouble or difficulty, the four jhānas that are of the higher mind, pleasant dwellings in this very life; and through the destruction of the taints, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge in this very life, he enters upon and dwells in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom.

Aparehipi sattahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu vinayadharo hoti – āpattiṃ jānāti, anāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, ubhayāni kho panassa [V 0.0262] pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni honti suvibhattāni suppavattīni suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso, catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ ābhicetasikānaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī, āsavānañca [M 0.0241] khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.

A bhikkhu endowed with seven other qualities is a bearer of the Discipline: he knows an offense, he knows what is not an offense, he knows a light offense, he knows a heavy offense; furthermore, both Pātimokkhas are well-mastered by him in detail, well-analyzed, well-recited, and well-determined according to the rules and their detailed phrasing; he obtains at will, without trouble or difficulty, the four jhānas that are of the higher mind, pleasant dwellings in this very life; and through the destruction of the taints, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge in this very life, he enters upon and dwells in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom.

Aparehipi sattahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu vinayadharo hoti – āpattiṃ jānāti; anāpattiṃ jānāti; lahukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti; garukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti; anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo dasapi jātiyo vīsampi jātiyo tiṃsampi jātiyo cattālīsampi jātiyo paññāsampi jātiyo jātisatampi [T 0.0342] jātisahassampi jātisatasahassampi anekepi saṃvaṭṭakappe anekepi vivaṭṭakappe anekepi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe – “amutrāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto amutra udapādiṃ; tatrāpāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto idhūpapanno”ti iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati; dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena atikkantamānussakena (ka.) satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe, sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāti – “ime vata bhonto sattā kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā vacīduccaritena samannāgatā manoduccaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ upavādakā micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapannā, ime vā pana bhonto sattā kāyasucaritena samannāgatā vacīsucaritena samannāgatā manosucaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ anupavādakā sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannā”ti iti dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāti; āsavānañca khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā [T 0.0343] sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.

A bhikkhu endowed with seven other qualities is a bearer of the discipline: he knows an offense; he knows what is not an offense; he knows a light offense; he knows a heavy offense; he recollects his manifold past lives, that is to say—one birth, two births, three births, four births, five births, ten births, twenty births, thirty births, forty births, fifty births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births, many eons of cosmic contraction, many eons of cosmic expansion, many eons of cosmic contraction and expansion: “There I was, so named, of such a clan, with such an appearance, such food, such an experience of pleasure and pain, such a lifespan. Passing away from there, I was reborn elsewhere. There too I was so named, of such a clan, with such an appearance, such food, such an experience of pleasure and pain, such a lifespan. Passing away from there, I was reborn here.” Thus he recollects his manifold past lives with their aspects and details; with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, he sees beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate—and he understands how beings fare according to their kamma: “Indeed, these beings, endowed with misconduct of body, speech, and mind, revilers of the noble ones, holding wrong view, undertaking actions under the influence of wrong view—with the breakup of the body, after death, have reappeared in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell. Or indeed, these beings, endowed with good conduct of body, speech, and mind, not revilers of the noble ones, holding right view, undertaking actions under the influence of right view—with the breakup of the body, after death, have reappeared in a good destination, in a heavenly world.” Thus, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, he sees beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate—and he understands how beings fare according to their kamma; and through the destruction of the taints, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge in this very life, he enters upon and dwells in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom.

Sattahaṅgehi [M 0.0242] samannāgato vinayadharo sobhati – āpattiṃ jānāti, anāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, garukaṃ [P 5.0136] āpattiṃ jānāti, sīlavā hoti…pe… samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu, catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ ābhicetasikānaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī hoti [V 0.0263] akicchalābhī akasiralābhī, āsavānañca khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.

A keeper of the Discipline endowed with seven qualities shines: he knows an offense, he knows a non-offense, he knows a light offense, he knows a heavy offense; he is virtuous… he trains himself in the training rules, having undertaken them; he obtains at will, without trouble, without difficulty, the four jhānas, which are of the higher mind, pleasant dwellings in this very life; and through the destruction of the taints, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge in this very life, he enters upon and dwells in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom.

Aparehipi sattahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo. Sobhati – āpattiṃ jānāti, anāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, bahussuto hoti…pe… diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdho catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ ābhicetasikānaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī, āsavānañca khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.

A keeper of the Discipline endowed with another seven factors shines: he knows an offense, he knows a non-offense, he knows a light offense, he knows a heavy offense; he is learned… he is well-penetrated in view; he attains at will, without trouble or difficulty, the four jhānas that are of the higher mind, pleasant dwellings in this very life; and through the destruction of the taints, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge in this very life, he enters upon and dwells in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom.

Aparehipi sattahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo sobhati – āpattiṃ jānāti, anāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni honti suvibhattāni suppavattīni suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso, catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ ābhicetasikānaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī, āsavānañca khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ [T 0.0344] abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.

A keeper of the Discipline endowed with yet another seven factors shines: he knows an offense, he knows a non-offense, he knows a light offense, he knows a heavy offense; both Pātimokkhas are well-mastered by him in detail, well-analyzed, well-recited, and well-determined, rule by rule and detail by detail; he attains at will, without difficulty or trouble, the four jhānas that are of the higher mind, pleasant dwellings in this very life; and through the destruction of the taints, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge in this very life, he enters upon and dwells in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom.

Aparehipi sattahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo sobhati – āpattiṃ jānāti; anāpattiṃ jānāti; lahukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti; garukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti; anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāti…pe… iti dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage [M 0.0243] satte pajānāti; āsavānañca khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.

A Vinaya-holder endowed with another seven factors is resplendent: he knows an offense; he knows what is not an offense; he knows a light offense; he knows a grave offense; he recollects his manifold past existences, that is, one birth, two births… thus he recollects his manifold past existences with their aspects and particulars; with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in good destinations and in bad destinations—and he understands beings who fare according to their kamma… thus with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in good destinations and in bad destinations—and he understands beings who fare according to their kamma; and, through the destruction of the taints, he in this very life enters and dwells in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, having realized it for himself with higher knowledge.

dī. ni. 3.330 Satta asaddhammā – assaddho hoti, ahiriko hoti, anottappī hoti, appassuto hoti, kusīto hoti, muṭṭhassati hoti, duppañño hoti.

Seven qualities of the unvirtuous: he is without faith, he is shameless, he lacks moral dread, he has little learning, he is lazy, he has lapsed mindfulness, and he is without wisdom.

dī. ni. 3.330 Satta [V 0.0264] saddhammā – saddho hoti, hirimā hoti, ottappī hoti, bahussuto hoti, āraddhavīriyo hoti, upaṭṭhitassati hoti, paññavā hotīti.

Seven qualities of the virtuous: he has faith, he has a sense of shame, he has moral dread, he is very learned, he has aroused effort, he has established mindfulness, and he has wisdom.

Sattakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Septad is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Āpatti āpattikkhandhā, vinītā sāmīcipi ca;

Adhammikā dhammikā ca, anāpatti ca sattāhaṃ.

Offenses, aggregates of offenses, resolved cases, and proper conduct; Unrighteous and righteous, and non-offense for seven days.

Ānisaṃsā paramāni, aruṇasamathena ca;

Kammā āmakadhaññā ca, tiriyaṃ gaṇabhojane.

Benefits, supreme things, and settlement at sunrise; Actions, raw grain, animals, and group meals.

Sattāhaparamaṃ [T 0.0345] ādāya, samādāya tatheva ca;

Na hoti hoti hoti ca, adhammā dhammikāni ca.

A maximum of seven days, taking, and likewise undertaking; There is not, there is, and there is; and unrighteous and righteous things.

Caturo vinayadharā, catubhikkhū ca sobhane;

Satta ceva asaddhammā, satta saddhammā desitāti.

Four Vinaya-holders, and four resplendent monks; And seven qualities of the unvirtuous, seven qualities of the virtuous were taught.

8. Aṭṭhakavāro

8. The Chapter on Eights

328. Aṭṭhānisaṃse sampassamānena na so bhikkhu āpattiyā adassane ukkhipitabbo. Aṭṭhānisaṃse sampassamānena paresampi saddhāya sā āpatti desetabbā. Aṭṭha yāvatatiyakā. Aṭṭhahākārehi kulāni dūseti. Aṭṭha mātikā cīvarassa uppādāya. Aṭṭha mātikā kathinassa ubbhārāya. Aṭṭha pānāni. cūḷava. 348; a. ni. 8.7 Aṭṭhahi asaddhammehi abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto devadatto āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho[M 0.0244]. Aṭṭha lokadhammā. Aṭṭha garudhammā. Aṭṭha pāṭidesanīyā. Aṭṭhaṅgiko musāvādo[P 5.0137]. Aṭṭha uposathaṅgāni. Aṭṭha dūteyyaṅgāni. Aṭṭha titthiyavattāni. Aṭṭha acchariyā abbhutadhammā mahāsamudde. Aṭṭha acchariyā abbhutadhammā imasmiṃ dhammavinaye. Aṭṭha anatirittā. Aṭṭha atirittā. Aṭṭhame aruṇuggamane nissaggiyaṃ hoti. Aṭṭha pārājikā. Aṭṭhamaṃ vatthuṃ paripūrentī nāsetabbā. Aṭṭhamaṃ vatthuṃ paripūrentiyā desitāpi adesitā hoti. Aṭṭhavācikā [T 0.0346] upasampadā. Aṭṭhannaṃ paccuṭṭhātabbaṃ. Aṭṭhannaṃ [V 0.0265] āsanaṃ dātabbaṃ. Upāsikā aṭṭha varāni yācati. Aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhikkhunovādako sammannitabbo sammanitabbo (ka.). Aṭṭhānisaṃsā vinayadhare. Aṭṭha paramāni. Tassapāpiyasikakammakatena bhikkhunā aṭṭhasu dhammesu sammā vattitabbaṃ. Aṭṭha adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni aṭṭha dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanānīti.

328. Seeing the eight benefits, that monk should not be suspended for not seeing an offense. Seeing the eight benefits, and also through faith in others, that offense should be confessed. There are eight yāvatatiyaka offenses. He corrupts families in eight ways. There are eight grounds for the arising of robes. There are eight grounds for the removal of the Kathina. There are eight drinks. Overcome by eight unwholesome qualities, with his mind consumed, Devadatta is destined for the plane of misery, for hell, to remain for the aeon, incurable. There are eight worldly conditions. There are eight weighty rules. There are eight Pāṭidesanīya offenses. False speech has eight factors. There are eight factors of the Uposatha. There are eight factors of an envoy. There are eight practices of sectarians. There are eight wonderful and amazing things in the great ocean. There are eight wonderful and amazing things in this Dhamma and Discipline. There are eight that are not surplus. There are eight that are surplus. At the eighth dawn, it becomes an offense requiring forfeiture. There are eight Pārājika offenses. A bhikkhunī who fulfills the eighth item is to be expelled. For a bhikkhunī who fulfills the eighth item, even if confessed, it is as if not confessed. The higher ordination with eight proclamations. One should rise up for eight. A seat should be given to eight. The female lay follower asks for eight boons. A monk endowed with eight factors should be appointed as an instructor of bhikkhunīs. There are eight benefits for a Vinaya-holder. There are eight supreme things. A monk upon whom the Tassapāpiyasikakamma has been carried out must conduct himself rightly in eight matters. There are eight unlawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha and eight lawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha.

Aṭṭhakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The section on eights is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Na so bhikkhu paresampi, yāvatatiyadūsanā;

Mātikā kathinubbhārā, pānā abhibhūtena ca.

'Not that monk,' 'Also for others,' 'Up to the third time' and 'Corrupting'; 'Grounds,' 'Removal of the Kathina,' 'Drinks,' and 'Overcome.'

Lokadhammā garudhammā, pāṭidesanīyā musā;

Uposathā ca dūtaṅgā, titthiyā samuddepi ca.

The octad on worldly conditions, the octad on weighty rules, the octad on matters to be confessed, the octad on false speech; the octad on the factors of the Uposatha, the octad on the factors of an envoy, the octad on the practices of sectarians, and the octad on the great ocean.

Abbhutā anatirittaṃ, atirittaṃ nissaggiyaṃ;

Pārājikaṭṭhamaṃ vatthu, adesitūpasampadā.

The octad on wonderful things, the octad on what is not surplus, the octad on what is surplus, the octad on matters requiring forfeiture; the octad on Pārājika offenses, the octad on the eighth matter, the octad on what is not pointed out, and the octad on higher ordination.

Paccuṭṭhānāsanañceva, varaṃ ovādakena ca;

Ānisaṃsā paramāni, aṭṭhadhammesu vattanā;

Adhammikā dhammikā ca, aṭṭhakā suppakāsitāti.

The octad on those for whom one should rise and the octad on seats, the octad on boons, and the octad on the exhorter of nuns; the octad on benefits, the octad on supreme things, the octad on conduct in the eight matters; the unrighteous and the righteous octads on the suspension of the Pātimokkha: thus, these octads are well explained.

9. Navakavāro

9. The Chapter of Nines

329. Nava āghātavatthūni. Nava āghātapaṭivinayā. Nava vinītavatthūni. Nava paṭhamāpattikā. Navahi saṅgho bhijjati. Nava paṇītabhojanāni[T 0.0347]. Navamaṃsehi [M 0.0245] dukkaṭaṃ. Nava pātimokkhuddesā. Nava paramāni. Nava taṇhāmūlakā dhammā. Nava vidhamānā. Nava cīvarāni adhiṭṭhātabbāni. Nava cīvarāni na vikappetabbāni. Dīghaso nava vidatthiyo sugatavidatthiyā. Nava adhammikāni dānāni. Nava adhammikā paṭiggahā. Nava adhammikā paribhogā – tīṇi dhammikāni dānāni, tayo dhammikā paṭiggahā, tayo dhammikā paribhogā. Nava adhammikā saññattiyo [V 0.0266] paññattiyo (sabbattha) aṭṭhakathā ca samathakkhandhake kaṇhapakkhanavakañca oloketabbaṃ. Nava dhammikā saññattiyo. Adhammakamme dve navakāni. Dhammakamme dve [P 5.0138] navakāni. Nava adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni. Nava dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanānīti.

329. There are nine grounds for resentment. There are nine removals of resentment. There are nine settled matters. There are nine first offenses. The Saṅgha is split by nine persons. There are nine exquisite foods. A dukkaṭa offense is incurred through nine kinds of meat. There are nine recitations of the Pātimokkha. There are nine supreme things. There are nine things rooted in craving. There are nine kinds of arrogance. Nine robes are to be determined. Nine robes are not to be assigned to another. In length, there are nine spans by the Sugata's span. There are nine unrighteous gifts. There are nine unrighteous acceptances. There are nine unrighteous usages—there are three righteous gifts, three righteous acceptances, and three righteous usages. There are nine unrighteous announcements. There are nine righteous announcements. In an unrighteous formal act, there are two sets of nine. In a righteous formal act, there are two sets of nine. There are nine unrighteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha. There are nine righteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha.

Navakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Chapter of Nines is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this:

Āghātavatthuvinayā, vinītā paṭhamena ca;

Bhijjati ca paṇītañca, maṃsuddesaparamāni ca.

Grounds for resentment, their removal, settled matters, and first offenses; splitting, exquisite foods, meat, recitations, and supreme things.

Taṇhā mānā adhiṭṭhānā, vikappe ca vidatthiyo;

Dānā paṭiggahā bhogā, tividhā puna dhammikā.

Craving, arrogance, and determinations; assigning to another and spans; gifts, acceptances, and usages; and again, the three righteous kinds.

Adhammadhammasaññatti, duve dve navakāni ca;

Pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni, adhammadhammikāni cāti.

Unrighteous and righteous announcements, the two pairs of nines concerning formal acts, and the unrighteous and righteous suspensions of the Pātimokkha.

10. Dasakavāro

10. The Chapter of Tens

330. Dasa āghātavatthūni. Dasa āghātapaṭivinayā. Dasa vinītavatthūni. Dasavatthukā micchādiṭṭhi. Dasavatthukā sammādiṭṭhi. Dasa antaggāhikā diṭṭhi. Dasa micchattā. Dasa sammattā. Dasa [T 0.0348] akusalakammapathā. Dasa kusalakammapathā. Dasa adhammikā salākaggāhā. Dasa dhammikā salākaggāhā. Sāmaṇerānaṃ dasa sikkhāpadāni. Dasahaṅgehi samannāgato sāmaṇero nāsetabbo.

330. There are ten grounds for resentment. There are ten removals of resentment. There are ten settled matters. Wrong view has ten bases. Right view has ten bases. There are ten views that grasp at extremes. There are ten wrongnesses. There are ten rightnesses. There are ten unwholesome courses of action. There are ten wholesome courses of action. There are ten unrighteous takings of voting tickets. There are ten righteous takings of voting tickets. There are ten training rules for novices. A novice endowed with ten factors should be expelled.

Dasahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo bālo tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – attano bhāsapariyantaṃ na uggaṇhāti, parassa bhāsapariyantaṃ na uggaṇhāti[M 0.0246], attano bhāsapariyantaṃ anuggahetvā parassa bhāsapariyantaṃ anuggahetvā adhammena kāreti, appaṭiññāya āpattiṃ na jānāti, āpattiyā mūlaṃ na jānāti, āpattisamudayaṃ na jānāti, āpattinirodhaṃ na jānāti, āpattinirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ na jānāti.

A Vinaya-expert endowed with ten factors is reckoned only as a fool: he does not grasp the extent of his own speech; he does not grasp the extent of another's speech; not having grasped the extent of his own speech and not having grasped the extent of another's speech, he makes a decision unrighteously and based on non-admission; he does not know an offense; he does not know the root of an offense; he does not know the origin of an offense; he does not know the cessation of an offense; he does not know the practice leading to the cessation of an offense.

Dasahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo paṇḍito tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – attano bhāsapariyantaṃ uggaṇhāti, parassa bhāsapariyantaṃ uggaṇhāti, attano bhāsapariyantaṃ uggahetvā parassa bhāsapariyantaṃ [V 0.0267] uggahetvā dhammena kāreti, paṭiññāya āpattiṃ jānāti, āpattiyā mūlaṃ jānāti, āpattisamudayaṃ jānāti, āpattinirodhaṃ jānāti, āpattinirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ jānāti.

A Vinaya-expert endowed with ten factors is reckoned only as wise: he grasps the extent of his own speech; he grasps the extent of another's speech; having grasped the extent of his own speech and having grasped the extent of another's speech, he makes a decision righteously and based on admission; he knows an offense; he knows the root of an offense; he knows the origin of an offense; he knows the cessation of an offense; he knows the practice leading to the cessation of an offense.

Aparehipi dasahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo bālo tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – adhikaraṇaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇasamudayaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇanirodhaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ na jānāti, vatthuṃ na jānāti, nidānaṃ uddānaṃ (ka.) na jānāti, paññattiṃ na jānāti, anupaññattiṃ na jānāti[T 0.0349], anusandhivacanapathaṃ na jānāti.

A Vinaya-expert endowed with another ten factors is reckoned only as a fool: he does not know the legal issue; he does not know the root of the legal issue; he does not know the origin of the legal issue; he does not know the cessation of the legal issue; he does not know the practice leading to the cessation of the legal issue; he does not know the subject matter; he does not know the occasion; he does not know the original regulation; he does not know the supplementary regulation; he does not know the sequence of the text and its interpretation.

Dasahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo paṇḍito tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – adhikaraṇaṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇassa mūlaṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇasamudayaṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇanirodhaṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ jānāti, vatthuṃ jānāti, nidānaṃ jānāti, paññattiṃ jānāti, anupaññattiṃ jānāti, anusandhivacanapathaṃ jānāti.

A Vinaya-expert endowed with ten factors is reckoned only as wise: he knows the legal issue; he knows the root of the legal issue; he knows the origin of the legal issue; he knows the cessation of the legal issue; he knows the practice leading to the cessation of the legal issue; he knows the subject matter; he knows the occasion; he knows the original regulation; he knows the supplementary regulation; he knows the sequence of the text and its interpretation.

Aparehipi dasahaṅgehi samannāgato [P 5.0139] vinayadharo bālo tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – ñattiṃ na jānāti, ñattiyā karaṇaṃ na jānāti, na pubbakusalo hoti, na aparakusalo hoti, akālaññū ca hoti, āpattānāpattiṃ na jānāti, lahukagarukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, sāvasesānavasesaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, ācariyaparamparā kho panassa na suggahitā hoti na sumanasikatā na sūpadhāritā.

A Vinaya-expert endowed with another ten factors is reckoned only as a fool: he does not know the motion; he does not know the function of the motion; he is not skilled in the preceding speech; he is not skilled in the succeeding speech; and he does not know the proper time; he does not know what is an offense and what is not an offense; he does not know a light or a heavy offense; he does not know an offense with a remainder or without a remainder; he does not know a coarse or a non-coarse offense; and indeed, for him the succession of teachers is not well-learned, not well-attended to, and not well-retained.

Dasahaṅgehi [M 0.0247] samannāgato vinayadharo paṇḍito tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – ñattiṃ jānāti, ñattiyā karaṇaṃ jānāti, pubbakusalo hoti, aparakusalo hoti, kālaññū ca hoti, āpattānāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukagarukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, sāvasesānavasesaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, ācariyaparamparā kho panassa suggahitā hoti sumanasikatā sūpadhāritā.

A Vinaya-expert endowed with ten factors is reckoned only as wise: he knows the motion; he knows the function of the motion; he is skilled in the preceding speech; he is skilled in the succeeding speech; and he knows the proper time; he knows what is an offense and what is not an offense; he knows a light or a heavy offense; he knows an offense with a remainder or without a remainder; he knows a coarse or a non-coarse offense; and indeed, for him the succession of teachers is well-learned, well-attended to, and well-retained.

Aparehipi dasahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo bālo tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – āpattānāpattiṃ na jānāti, lahukagarukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, sāvasesānavasesaṃ āpattiṃ na [T 0.0350] jānāti, duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni vitthārena na svāgatāni honti na suvibhattāni na suppavattīni na suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso[V 0.0268], āpattānāpattiṃ na jānāti, lahukagarukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, sāvasesānavasesaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇe ca na vinicchayakusalo hoti.

A keeper of the discipline endowed with another ten factors is reckoned only as a fool: he does not know what is an offense and what is not an offense; he does not know a light or a heavy offense; he does not know an offense with a remainder or without a remainder; he does not know a coarse or a non-coarse offense; and indeed, for him the two Pātimokkhas are not well-learned in detail, not well-analyzed, not well-mastered, not well-decided by way of the rules and by way of the details; he does not know what is an offense and what is not an offense; he does not know a light or a heavy offense; he does not know an offense with a remainder or without a remainder; he does not know a coarse or a non-coarse offense; and he is not skilled in deciding legal issues.

Dasahaṅgehi samannāgato vinayadharo paṇḍito tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati – āpattānāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukagarukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, sāvasesānavasesaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni honti suvibhattāni suppavattīni suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso, āpattānāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukagarukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, sāvasesānavasesaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇe ca vinicchayakusalo hoti.

A master of the Vinaya endowed with ten factors is reckoned as wise: he knows what is an offense and what is not an offense, he knows a light and a heavy offense, he knows an offense with a remainder and without a remainder, he knows a coarse and a non-coarse offense, and both Pātimokkhas are well-learned by him in detail, well-analyzed, well-mastered, and well-determined both by way of the rules and by way of the detailed analysis; he knows what is an offense and what is not an offense, he knows a light and a heavy offense, he knows an offense with a remainder and without a remainder, he knows a coarse and a non-coarse offense, and he is skilled in judging legal issues.

a. ni. 10.33 Dasahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya sammannitabbo. Dasa atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ. Dasa ādīnavā rājantepurappavesane. Dasa dānavatthūni. Dasa ratanāni. Dasavaggo bhikkhusaṅgho. Dasavaggena gaṇena upasampādetabbaṃ. Dasa paṃsukūlāni. Dasa cīvaradhāraṇā cīvaradhāraṇāni (syā.). Dasāhaparamaṃ atirekacīvaraṃ dhāretabbaṃ[M 0.0248]. Dasa sukkāni. Dasa itthiyo. Dasa [T 0.0351] bhariyāyo. Vesāliyā dasa vatthūni dīpenti. Dasa puggalā avandiyā. Dasa akkosavatthūni. Dasahākārehi pesuññaṃ upasaṃharati. Dasa senāsanāni. Dasa varāni yāciṃsu. Dasa adhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni. Dasa dhammikāni pātimokkhaṭṭhapanāni. Dasānisaṃsā yāguyā. Dasa maṃsā akappiyā. Dasa paramāni. Dasavassena bhikkhunā byattena paṭibalena pabbājetabbaṃ upasampādetabbaṃ nissayo dātabbo sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Dasavassāya bhikkhuniyā byattāya paṭibalāya pabbājetabbaṃ upasampādetabbaṃ nissayo dātabbo sāmaṇerī upaṭṭhāpetabbā. Dasavassāya bhikkhuniyā byattāya paṭibalāya vuṭṭhāpanasammuti sāditabbā. Dasavassāya gihigatāya sikkhā dātabbāti.

A monk endowed with ten factors should be appointed by a formal act of inquiry. On account of ten benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the training rule for the disciples. There are ten dangers in entering the royal inner palace. There are ten grounds for giving. There are ten treasures. The community of monks is a group of ten. One should be given higher ordination by a group of ten. There are ten kinds of rag-robes. There are ten ways of wearing a robe. An extra robe may be kept for at most ten days. There are ten kinds of semen. There are ten kinds of women. There are ten kinds of wives. In Vesālī, they set forth ten points. Ten individuals are unworthy of veneration. There are ten grounds for abuse. One brings forth slanderous speech in ten ways. There are ten kinds of lodgings. They asked for ten boons. There are ten unlawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha. There are ten lawful suspensions of the Pātimokkha. There are ten benefits of rice gruel. Ten kinds of meat are unallowable. There are ten supreme things. A competent and capable monk of ten years' standing may give the going forth, give the higher ordination, should give dependence, and may have a novice attend on him. A competent and capable nun of ten years' standing may give the going forth, give the higher ordination, should give dependence, and may have a female novice attend on her. A competent and capable nun of ten years' standing should be granted the authorization to ordain. The training should be given to a married girl who is ten years old.

Dasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Chapter of Tens is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Āghātaṃ [P 5.0140] vinayaṃ vatthu, micchā sammā ca antagā;

Micchattā ceva sammattā, akusalā kusalāpi ca.

Resentment, removal, grounds, wrong and right, and extremes; wrongness and rightness, unwholesome and wholesome as well.

Salākā [V 0.0269] adhammā dhammā, sāmaṇerā ca nāsanā;

Bhāsādhikaraṇañceva, ñattilahukameva ca.

Unlawful and lawful voting tickets, and novices, expulsion; speech, and legal questions, motions, and minor matters as well.

Lahukā garukā ete, kaṇhasukkā vijānatha;

Ubbāhikā ca sikkhā ca, antepure ca vatthūni.

These light and heavy sets, you should know as the dark and the bright; and the formal act of inquiry, and training rules, and the royal inner quarters, and grounds for giving.

Ratanaṃ [T 0.0352] dasavaggo ca, tatheva upasampadā;

Paṃsukūladhāraṇā ca, dasāhasukkaitthiyo.

Treasures and the group of ten, and likewise ordination; rag-robes and the wearing of robes, the ten-day limit, semen, and women.

Bhariyā dasa vatthūni, avandiyakkosena ca;

Pesuññañceva senāni, varāni ca adhammikā.

Wives, the ten points, and the unworthy of veneration and abuse; and slander, lodgings, and boons, and the unlawful.

Dhammikā yāgumaṃsā ca, paramā bhikkhu bhikkhunī;

Vuṭṭhāpanā gihigatā, dasakā suppakāsitāti.

The lawful, and rice gruel and meat, the supreme, a monk, a nun; authorization to ordain, the married girl—thus these sets of ten are well proclaimed.

11. Ekādasakavāro

11. The Chapter of Elevens

331. Ekāda [M 0.0249] puggalā anupasampannā na upasampādetabbā, upasampannā nāsetabbā. Ekādasa pādukā akappiyā. Ekādasa pattā akappiyā. Ekādasa cīvarāni akappiyāni. Ekādasa yāvatatiyakā. Bhikkhunīnaṃ ekādasa antarāyikā dhammā pucchitabbā. Ekādasa cīvarāni adhiṭṭhātabbāni. Ekādasa cīvarāni na vikappetabbāni. Ekādase aruṇuggamane nissaggiyaṃ hoti. Ekādasa gaṇṭhikā kappiyā. Ekādasa vidhā vīthā (syā.) kappiyā. Ekādasa pathavī akappiyā. Ekādasa pathavī kappiyā. Ekādasa nissayapaṭippassaddhiyo. Ekādasa puggalā avandiyā. Ekādasa paramāni. Ekādasa varāni yāciṃsu. Ekādasa sīmādosā. Akkosakaparibhāsake puggale ekādasādīnavā pāṭikaṅkhā. a. ni. 11.15; mi. pa. 4.4.6 Mettāya cetovimuttiyā āsevitāya bhāvitāya bahulīkatāya yānīkatāya vatthukatāya anuṭṭhitāya paricitāya susamāraddhāya ekādasānisaṃsā pāṭikaṅkhā[T 0.0353]. Sukhaṃ supati, sukhaṃ paṭibujjhati, na pāpakaṃ supinaṃ passati, manussānaṃ piyo hoti, amanussānaṃ piyo hoti, devatā rakkhanti, nāssa aggi vā visaṃ vā satthaṃ vā kamati, tuvaṭṭaṃ cittaṃ samādhiyati, mukhavaṇṇo vippasīdati, asammūḷho kālaṅkaroti, uttari appaṭivijjhanto brahmalokūpago hoti – mettāya cetovimuttiyā [V 0.0270] āsevitāya bhāvitāya bahulīkatāya yānīkatāya vatthukatāya anuṭṭhitāya paricitāya susamāraddhāya ime ekādasānisaṃsā pāṭikaṅkhāti.

331. Eleven individuals who are not fully ordained should not be given full ordination; if they are fully ordained, they should be expelled. Eleven kinds of sandals are not allowable. Eleven kinds of bowls are not allowable. Eleven kinds of robes are not allowable. There are eleven offenses requiring a third warning. For bhikkhunīs, eleven obstructive conditions should be asked. Eleven robes should be determined. Eleven robes should not be alienated. At the eleventh sunrise, it becomes subject to forfeiture. Eleven kinds of knots are allowable. Eleven kinds of belt-toggles are allowable. Eleven kinds of earth are not allowable. Eleven kinds of earth are allowable. There are eleven cessations of dependence. Eleven individuals are not to be venerated. There are eleven supreme things. They requested eleven boons. There are eleven boundary defects. In an abusive and reviling person, eleven disadvantages are to be expected. When the mind-deliverance by loving-kindness is cultivated, developed, practiced much, made a vehicle, made a basis, established, made familiar, and well undertaken, eleven benefits are to be expected: one sleeps happily, one awakes happily, one sees no evil dreams, one is dear to human beings, one is dear to non-human beings, deities protect one, fire or poison or weapons do not affect one, one's mind quickly becomes concentrated, one's facial complexion is serene, one dies unconfused, and if one penetrates no further, one goes to the Brahma world—these eleven benefits are to be expected when the mind-deliverance by loving-kindness is cultivated, developed, practiced much, made a vehicle, made a basis, established, made familiar, and well undertaken.

Ekādasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Chapter of Elevens is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Nāsetabbā pādukā ca, pattā ca cīvarāni ca;

Tatiyā pucchitabbā ca, adhiṭṭhānavikappanā.

Those to be expelled, and sandals, bowls, and robes; the third, things to be asked, determination, and alienation.

Aruṇā [P 5.0141] gaṇṭhikā vidhā, akappiyā ca kappiyaṃ;

Nissayāvandiyā ceva, paramāni varāni ca;

Sīmādosā ca akkosā, mettāyekādasā katāti.

Sunrise, knots, belt-toggles, unallowable and allowable; dependence and not to be venerated, supreme things and boons; boundary defects and abuse, and loving-kindness; thus the elevens are taught.

Ekuttarikanayo.

The Method of Numerical Progression.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Ekakā [M 0.0250] ca dukā ceva, tikā ca catupañcakā;

Chasattaṭṭhanavakā ca, dasa ekādasāni ca.

Ones and twos, threes, fours and fives; sixes, sevens, eights and nines, tens and elevens.

Hitāya sabbasattānaṃ, ñātadhammena tādinā;

Ekuttarikā vimalā, mahāvīrena desitāti.

For the welfare of all beings, the stainless Numerical Collection was taught by the one who has known the Dhamma, the Such One, the Great Hero.

Ekuttarikanayo niṭṭhito.

The Method of the Numerical Collection is concluded.

Uposathādipucchāvissajjanā

Questions and Answers on the Uposatha and Related Matters

Ādimajjhantapucchanaṃ

The Questioning of the Beginning, Middle, and End

332. Uposathakammassa [T 0.0354][P 5.0142][M 0.0251][V 0.0271] ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Pavāraṇākammassa ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Tajjanīyakammassa ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Niyassakammassa…pe… pabbājanīyakammassa…pe… paṭisāraṇīyakammassa…pe… ukkhepanīyakammassa…pe… parivāsadānassa…pe… mūlāyapaṭikassanāya…pe… mānattadānassa…pe… abbhānassa…pe… upasampadākammassa ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Tajjanīyakammassa paṭippassaddhiyā ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Niyassakammassa paṭippassaddhiyā ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Pabbājanīyakammassa paṭippassaddhiyā ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Paṭisāraṇīyakammassa paṭippassaddhiyā ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Ukkhepanīyakammassa paṭippassaddhiyā ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Sativinayassa ko ādi, kiṃ majje, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Amūḷhavinayassa ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Tassapāpiyasikāya ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Tiṇavatthārakassa ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Bhikkhunovādakasammutiyā ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Ticīvarena avippavāsasammutiyā ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Santhatasammutiyā ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Rūpiyachaḍḍakasammutiyā ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Sāṭiyaggāhāpakasammutiyo ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Pattaggāhāpakasammutiyā ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Daṇḍasammutiyā ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Sikkāsammutiyā ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Daṇḍasikkāsammutiyā ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ?

332. What is the beginning, middle, and end of the Uposatha act; of the Pavāraṇā act; of the Tajjanīya act; of the Niyassa act… and so on…; of the Pabbājanīya act… and so on…; of the Paṭisāraṇīya act… and so on…; of the Ukkhepanīya act… and so on…; of the giving of probation… and so on…; of sending back to the root… and so on…; of the giving of penance… and so on…; of rehabilitation… and so on…; of the higher ordination act; of the revocation of the Tajjanīya act; of the revocation of the Niyassa act; of the revocation of the Pabbājanīya act; of the revocation of the Paṭisāraṇīya act; of the revocation of the Ukkhepanīya act; of the verdict of mindfulness; of the verdict of past insanity; of the Tassapāpiyasikā act; of the act of covering over with grass; of the authorization of an exhorter of bhikkhunīs; of the authorization for not being separated from the three robes; of the authorization for a felt rug; of the authorization of a discarder of money; of the authorization of a receiver of cloth; of the authorization of a receiver of bowls; of the authorization for a staff; of the authorization for a carrying sling; of the authorization for a staff and carrying sling?

Ādimajjhantavissajjanā

Exposition on the Beginning, Middle, and End

333. Uposathakammassa [T 0.0355][V 0.0272] ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānanti? Uposathakammassa sāmaggī ādi, kiriyā majjhe, niṭṭhānaṃ pariyosānaṃ.

333. What is the beginning, what is the middle, and what is the end of the Uposatha act? For the Uposatha act, physical unanimity is the beginning, the act of reciting the Pātimokkha is the middle, and its completion is the end.

Pavāraṇākammassa [M 0.0252] ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānanti? Pavāraṇākammassa sāmaggī ādi, kiriyā majjhe, niṭṭhānaṃ pariyosānaṃ.

What is the beginning, what is the middle, and what is the end of the Pavāraṇā act? For the Pavāraṇā act, physical unanimity is the beginning, the act of reciting the Pavāraṇā motion is the middle, and its completion is the end.

Tajjanīyakammassa ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānanti? Tajjanīyakammassa vatthu ca puggalo ca ādi, ñatti majjhe, kammavācā pariyosānaṃ.

What is the beginning, what is the middle, and what is the end of the Tajjanīya act? For the Tajjanīya act, both the matter and the person are the beginning, the motion is the middle, and the formal act announcement is the end.

Niyassakammassa…pe… pabbājanīyakammassa…pe… paṭisāraṇīyakammassa…pe… ukkhepanīyakammassa…pe… parivāsadānassa…pe… mūlāyapaṭikassanāya…pe… mānattadānassa…pe… abbhānassa ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānanti? Abbhānassa vatthu ca puggalo ca ādi, ñatti majjhe, kammavācā pariyosānaṃ.

For the Niyassa act… for the Pabbājanīya act… for the Paṭisāraṇīya act… for the Ukkhepanīya act… for the granting of probation… for sending back to the root… for the granting of penance… for rehabilitation, what is the beginning, what is the middle, and what is the end? For rehabilitation, both the matter and the person are the beginning, the motion is the middle, and the formal act announcement is the end.

Upasampadākammassa ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānanti? Upasampadākammassa puggalo ādi, ñatti majjhe, kammavācā pariyosānaṃ.

What is the beginning, what is the middle, and what is the end of the higher ordination act? For the higher ordination act, the person is the beginning, the motion is the middle, and the formal act announcement is the end.

Tajjanīyakammassa paṭippassaddhiyā ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānanti? Tajjanīyakammassa paṭippassaddhiyā sammāvattanā ādi, ñatti majjhe, kammavācā pariyosānaṃ.

What is the beginning, what is the middle, and what is the end of the revocation of the Tajjanīya act? For the revocation of the Tajjanīya act, proper conduct is the beginning, the motion is the middle, and the formal act announcement is the end.

Niyassakammassa…pe… pabbājanīyakammassa…pe… paṭisāraṇīyakammassa…pe… ukkhepanīyakammassa paṭippassaddhiyā ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānanti? Ukkhepanīyakammassa paṭippassaddhiyā sammāvattanā ādi, ñatti majjhe, kammavācā pariyosānaṃ.

For the revocation of the Niyassa act… for the revocation of the Pabbājanīya act… for the revocation of the Paṭisāraṇīya act… for the revocation of the Ukkhepanīya act, what is the beginning, what is the middle, and what is the end? For the revocation of the Ukkhepanīya act, proper conduct is the beginning, the motion is the middle, and the formal act announcement is the end.

Sativinayassa ko ādi[P 5.0143], kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānanti? Sativinayassa vatthu [T 0.0356] ca puggalo ca ādi, ñatti majjhe, kammavācā pariyosānaṃ.

What is the beginning, what is the middle, and what is the end of the verdict of mindfulness? For the verdict of mindfulness, both the matter and the person are the beginning, the motion is the middle, and the formal act announcement is the end.

Amūḷhavinayassa [V 0.0273] …pe… tassapāpiyasikāya…pe… tiṇavatthārakassa…pe… bhikkhunovādakasammutiyā…pe… ticīvarena avippavāsasammutiyā…pe… santhatasammutiyā…pe… rūpiyachaḍḍakasammutiyā…pe… sāṭiyaggāhāpakasammutiyā…pe… pattaggāhāpakasammutiyā…pe… daṇḍasammutiyā…pe… sikkāsammutiyā…pe… daṇḍasikkāsammutiyā ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānanti? Daṇḍasikkāsammutiyā vatthu ca puggalo ca ādi, ñatti majjhe, kammavācā pariyosānaṃ.

For the verdict of past insanity… for the Tassapāpiyasikā act… for the act of covering over with grass… for the authorization to advise nuns… for the authorization for non-separation from the three robes… for the authorization for a felt rug… for the authorization for discarding money… for the authorization for accepting a cloth… for the authorization for accepting a bowl… for the authorization for a staff… for the authorization for a carrying sling… for the authorization for a staff and carrying sling, what is the beginning, what is the middle, and what is the end? For the authorization for a staff and carrying sling, both the matter and the person are the beginning, the motion is the middle, and the formal act announcement is the end.

Uposathādipucchāvissajjanā niṭṭhitā.

The Questions and Answers beginning with the Uposatha are concluded.

Atthavasapakaraṇaṃ

The Treatise on the Grounds

334. a. ni. 10.334; pari. 22 Dasa [T 0.0357][M 0.0253] atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ – saṅghasuṭṭhutāya, saṅghaphāsutāya, dummaṅkūnaṃ puggalānaṃ niggahāya, pesalānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ phāsuvihārāya, diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ āsavānaṃ saṃvarāya, samparāyikānaṃ āsavānaṃ paṭighātāya, appasannānaṃ pasādāya, pasannānaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya, saddhammaṭṭhitiyā vinayānuggahāya.

334. In consideration of ten benefits, the Tathāgata has laid down the training rule for the disciples: for the well-being of the Saṅgha, for the comfort of the Saṅgha, for the restraint of immoral individuals, for the comfortable abiding of virtuous bhikkhus, for the prevention of taints in the present life, for the warding off of taints in the future, for inspiring faith in the faithless, for the increase of faith in the faithful, for the stability of the good Dhamma, and for the support of the Vinaya.

Yaṃ saṅghasuṭṭhu taṃ saṅghaphāsu. Yaṃ saṅghaphāsu taṃ dummaṅkūnaṃ puggalānaṃ niggahāya. Yaṃ dummaṅkūnaṃ puggalānaṃ niggahāya taṃ pesalānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ phāsuvihārāya. Yaṃ pesalānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ phāsuvihārāya taṃ diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ āsavānaṃ saṃvarāya. Yaṃ diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ āsavānaṃ saṃvarāya taṃ samparāyikānaṃ āsavānaṃ paṭighātāya. Yaṃ samparāyikānaṃ āsavānaṃ paṭighātāya taṃ appasannānaṃ pasādāya. Yaṃ appasannānaṃ pasādāya taṃ pasannānaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya. Yaṃ pasannānaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya taṃ saddhammaṭṭhitiyā. Yaṃ saddhammaṭṭhitiyā taṃ vinayānuggahāya.

That which is for the well-being of the Saṅgha is for the comfort of the Saṅgha. That which is for the comfort of the Saṅgha is for the restraint of immoral individuals. That which is for the restraint of immoral individuals is for the comfortable abiding of virtuous bhikkhus. That which is for the comfortable abiding of virtuous bhikkhus is for the restraint of taints in the present life. That which is for the restraint of taints in the present life is for the warding off of taints in the future. That which is for the warding off of taints in the future is for inspiring faith in the faithless. That which is for inspiring faith in the faithless is for the increase of faith in the faithful. That which is for the increase of faith in the faithful is for the stability of the good Dhamma. That which is for the stability of the good Dhamma is for the support of the Vinaya.

Yaṃ saṅghasuṭṭhu taṃ saṅghaphāsu. Yaṃ saṅghasuṭṭhu taṃ dummaṅkūnaṃ puggalānaṃ niggahāya. Yaṃ saṅghasuṭṭhu taṃ pesalānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ phāsuvihārāya. Yaṃ saṅghasuṭṭhu taṃ diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ āsavānaṃ saṃvarāya. Yaṃ saṅghasuṭṭhu taṃ samparāyikānaṃ āsavānaṃ paṭighātāya. Yaṃ saṅghasuṭṭhu taṃ [T 0.0358] appasannānaṃ pasādāya. Yaṃ saṅghasuṭṭhu taṃ pasannānaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya. Yaṃ saṅghasuṭṭhu taṃ saddhammaṭṭhitiyā. Yaṃ saṅghasuṭṭhu taṃ vinayānuggahāya.

Whatever is the well-being of the Sangha, that is for the comfort of the Sangha. Whatever is the well-being of the Sangha, that is for the restraint of immoral individuals. Whatever is the well-being of the Sangha, that is for the comfortable abiding of monks of amiable virtue. Whatever is the well-being of the Sangha, that is for the restraint of taints in the present life. Whatever is the well-being of the Sangha, that is for the dispelling of taints in the future life. Whatever is the well-being of the Sangha, that is for inspiring faith in the unfaithful. Whatever is the well-being of the Sangha, that is for the increase of faith in the faithful. Whatever is the well-being of the Sangha, that is for the establishment of the good Dhamma. Whatever is the well-being of the Sangha, that is for the support of the discipline.

Yaṃ saṅghaphāsu taṃ dummaṅkūnaṃ puggalānaṃ niggahāya. Yaṃ saṅghaphāsu taṃ pesalānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ phāsuvihārāya[V 0.0274]. Yaṃ saṅghaphāsu taṃ diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ āsavānaṃ saṃvarāya. Yaṃ saṅghaphāsu taṃ samparāyikānaṃ āsavānaṃ paṭighātāya. Yaṃ saṅghaphāsu taṃ appasannānaṃ pasādāya. Yaṃ saṅghaphāsu taṃ pasannānaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya. Yaṃ saṅghaphāsu taṃ saddhammaṭṭhitiyā. Yaṃ saṅghaphāsu taṃ vinayānuggahāya. Yaṃ saṅghaphāsu taṃ saṅghasuṭṭhu.

Whatever is the comfort of the Sangha, that is for the restraint of immoral individuals. Whatever is the comfort of the Sangha, that is for the comfortable abiding of monks of amiable virtue. Whatever is the comfort of the Sangha, that is for the restraint of taints in the present life. Whatever is the comfort of the Sangha, that is for the dispelling of taints in the future life. Whatever is the comfort of the Sangha, that is for inspiring faith in the unfaithful. Whatever is the comfort of the Sangha, that is for the increase of faith in the faithful. Whatever is the comfort of the Sangha, that is for the establishment of the good Dhamma. Whatever is the comfort of the Sangha, that is for the support of the discipline. Whatever is the comfort of the Sangha, that is for the well-being of the Sangha.

Yaṃ dummaṅkūnaṃ puggalānaṃ niggahāya…pe… yaṃ pesalānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ phāsuvihārāya… yaṃ diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ āsavānaṃ saṃvarāya… yaṃ samparāyikānaṃ āsavānaṃ [M 0.0254] paṭighātāya… yaṃ appasannānaṃ pasādāya… yaṃ pasannānaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya… yaṃ saddhammaṭṭhitiyā… yaṃ vinayānuggahāya taṃ saṅghasuṭṭhu. Yaṃ vinayānuggahāya taṃ saṅghaphāsu. Yaṃ vinayānuggahāya taṃ dummaṅkūnaṃ puggalānaṃ niggahāya. Yaṃ vinayānuggahāya taṃ pesalānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ phāsuvihārāya. Yaṃ vinayānuggahāya taṃ diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ āsavānaṃ saṃvarāya. Yaṃ vinayānuggahāya taṃ samparāyikānaṃ āsavānaṃ paṭighātāya. Yaṃ vinayānuggahāya taṃ appasannānaṃ pasādāya. Yaṃ vinayānuggahāya taṃ pasannānaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya. Yaṃ vinayānuggahāya taṃ [T 0.0359] saddhammaṭṭhitiyāti.

What is for the subduing of persons without virtue... what is for the comfortable abiding of virtuous monks... what is for the restraint of taints in this present life... what is for the dispelling of future taints... what is for inspiring faith in the faithless... what is for the increase of faith in the faithful... what is for the establishment of the good Dhamma... what is for the upholding of the Vinaya is for the well-being of the Saṅgha. What is for the upholding of the Vinaya is for the comfort of the Saṅgha. What is for the upholding of the Vinaya is for the subduing of persons without virtue. What is for the upholding of the Vinaya is for the comfortable abiding of virtuous monks. What is for the upholding of the Vinaya is for the restraint of taints in this present life. What is for the upholding of the Vinaya is for the dispelling of future taints. What is for the upholding of the Vinaya is for inspiring faith in the faithless. What is for the upholding of the Vinaya is for the increase of faith in the faithful. What is for the upholding of the Vinaya is for the establishment of the good Dhamma.

Atthasataṃ dhammasataṃ, dve ca niruttisatāni;

Cattāri ñāṇasatāni, atthavase pakaraṇeti.

One hundred meanings, one hundred teachings, and two hundred derivations; four hundred knowledges, in the treatise on the grounds.

Atthavasapakaraṇaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Treatise on the Grounds is concluded.

Mahāvaggo niṭṭhito.

The Great Section is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Paṭhamaṃ aṭṭhapucchāyaṃ, paccayesu punaṭṭha ca;

Bhikkhūnaṃ soḷasa ete, bhikkhunīnañca soḷasa.

In the first inquiry there are eight sections, and again eight on conditions; these sixteen are in the analysis for monks, and sixteen for the nuns.

Peyyālaantarā bhedā, ekuttarikameva ca;

Pavāraṇatthavasikā, mahāvaggassa saṅgahoti.

The various intermediate repetitions, and the numerical progression by one; the questions and answers on the ten benefits of the Invitation and so on—this is the summary of the Great Section.

Atthavasapakaraṇaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Treatise on the Benefits is concluded.

Gāthāsaṅgaṇikaṃ

A Collection of Verses

1. Sattanagaresu paññattasikkhāpadaṃ

The Training Rule Laid Down in Seven Cities

335.

335.

Ekaṃsaṃ [T 0.0360][P 5.0144][M 0.0255][V 0.0275] cīvaraṃ katvā, paggaṇhitvāna añjaliṃ;

Āsīsamānarūpova āsiṃsamānarūpova (sī. syā.), kissa tvaṃ idha māgato.

1. Having arranged your robe over one shoulder, having raised your joined palms, as if with an expectation—for what reason have you come here?

Dvīsu vinayesu ye paññattā;

Uddesaṃ āgacchanti uposathesu;

Kati te sikkhāpadā honti;

Katisu nagaresu paññattā.

Those training rules that were laid down in the two Vinayas, which come up for recitation during the Uposatha days—how many are those training rules? In how many cities were they laid down?

Bhaddako te ummaṅgo, yoniso paripucchasi;

Taggha te ahamakkhissaṃ, yathāsi kusalo tathā.

Excellent is your inquiry; you ask thoughtfully. Indeed, I will explain it to you, so that you may become proficient.

Dvīsu vinayesu ye paññattā;

Uddesaṃ āgacchanti uposathesu;

Aḍḍhuḍḍhasatāni te honti;

Sattasu nagaresu paññattā.

Those training rules that were laid down in the two Vinayas, which come up for recitation during the Uposatha days—they are three hundred and fifty, laid down in seven cities.

Katamesu sattasu nagaresu paññattā;

Iṅgha me tvaṃ byākara naṃ iṅgha me taṃ byākara (ka.);

Taṃ vacanapathaṃ tava vacanapathaṃ (syā.) nisāmayitvā;

Paṭipajjema hitāya no siyā.

In which seven cities were they laid down? Pray, do you explain this to me. Having hearkened to that course of speech, we shall practice; it would be for our welfare.

Vesāliyaṃ [V 0.0276] rājagahe, sāvatthiyañca āḷaviyaṃ;

Kosambiyañca sakkesu, bhaggesu ceva paññattā.

In Vesālī, Rājagaha, Sāvatthī, and Āḷavī; in Kosambī, among the Sakyans, and among the Bhaggas, they were laid down.

Kati [T 0.0361] vesāliyaṃ paññattā, kati rājagahe katā;

Sāvatthiyaṃ kati honti, kati āḷaviyaṃ katā.

How many were laid down in Vesālī, how many were made in Rājagaha? How many are there in Sāvatthī, how many were made in Āḷavī?

Kati kosambiyaṃ paññattā, kati sakkesu vuccanti;

Kati bhaggesu paññattā, taṃ me akkhāhi pucchito.

How many were laid down in Kosambī, how many are spoken of among the Sakyans? How many were laid down among the Bhaggas? Being asked, please declare this to me.

Dasa [M 0.0256] vesāliyaṃ paññattā, ekavīsa rājagahe katā;

Chaūna tīṇisatāni, sabbe sāvatthiyaṃ katā.

Ten were laid down in Vesālī, twenty-one were made in Rājagaha; three hundred less six, all were made in Sāvatthī.

Cha āḷaviyaṃ paññattā, aṭṭha kosambiyaṃ katā;

Aṭṭha sakkesu vuccanti, tayo bhaggesu paññattā.

Six were laid down in Āḷavī, eight were made in Kosambī; eight are spoken of among the Sakyans, three were laid down among the Bhaggas.

Ye vesāliyaṃ paññattā, te suṇohi yathātathaṃ yathākathaṃ (sī. syā. evamuparipi);

Methunaviggahuttari, atirekañca kāḷakaṃ.

Those that were laid down in Vesālī, listen to them in accordance with reality: the rule on sexual intercourse, on a human corpse, on superhuman states, on an extra robe, and on black wool.

Bhūtaṃ paramparabhattaṃ, dantaponena dantapoṇena (ka.) acelako;

Bhikkhunīsu ca akkoso, dasete vesāliyaṃ katā.

The rule on informing of a true attainment, on eating food in succession, the rule on a tooth-cleaner, on a naked ascetic, and the rule on reviling—these ten were made in Vesālī.

Ye rājagahe paññattā, te suṇohi yathātathaṃ;

Adinnādānaṃ rājagahe, dve anuddhaṃsanā dvepi ca bhedā.

Those that were laid down in Rājagaha, listen to them in accordance with reality: the rule on taking what is not given, two on harassing, and also two on schisms.

Antaravāsakaṃ rūpiyaṃ suttaṃ, ujjhāpanena ca pācitapiṇḍaṃ[T 0.0362][P 5.0145];

Gaṇabhojanaṃ vikāle ca, cārittaṃ nahānaṃ ūnavīsati.

The rule on accepting a robe from an unrelated bhikkhunī, on silver, on thread, on complaining, on almsfood prepared by a bhikkhunī, on eating in a group, on eating at the wrong time, on wandering for alms, on bathing, and on ordaining one under twenty years of age.

Cīvaraṃ datvā vosāsanti, ete rājagahe katā;

Giraggacariyā tattheva, chandadānena ekavīsati.

The rule on complaining after giving a robe, on dismissing from a dwelling, on the Giragga festival, on wandering during the rains-residence, on departing after the rains-residence, and on giving consent to one on probation. These twenty-one were made in Rājagaha.

Ye [V 0.0277] sāvatthiyaṃ paññattā, te suṇohi yathātathaṃ;

Pārājikāni cattāri, saṅghādisesā bhavanti soḷasa.

Those that were laid down in Sāvatthī, listen to them as they truly are: there are four Pārājikas, and sixteen Saṅghādisesas.

Aniyatā ca dve honti, nissaggiyā catuvīsati;

Chapaññāsasatañceva, khuddakāni pavuccanti.

There are also two Aniyatas and twenty-four Nissaggiyas; and one hundred and fifty-six minor rules are spoken of.

Dasayeva ca gārayhā, dvesattati ca sekhiyā;

Chaūna tīṇisatāni, sabbe sāvatthiyaṃ katā.

And ten reprehensible rules are spoken of, and seventy-two training rules; thus all these two hundred and ninety-four were laid down in Sāvatthī.

Ye āḷaviyaṃ paññattā, te suṇohi yathātathaṃ;

Kuṭikosiyaseyyā ca, khaṇane gaccha devate;

Sappāṇakañca siñcanti, cha ete āḷaviyaṃ katā.

Those that were laid down in Āḷavī, listen to them as they truly are: the rules on a hut, on silk, and on lying down; on digging, on plant life, and on sprinkling water with living beings—these six were laid down in Āḷavī.

Ye kosambiyaṃ paññattā, te suṇohi yathātathaṃ;

Mahāvihāro dovacassaṃ, aññaṃ dvāraṃ surāya ca;

Anādariyaṃ sahadhammo, payopānena aṭṭhamaṃ.

Those that were laid down in Kosambī, listen to them as they truly are: the Mahalla-vihāra rule, the Dovacassa rule, the Aññavādaka rule, the Yāva-dvara-kosa rule, the Surāpāna rule, the Anādariya rule, the Sahadhammika rule, and the Surusuru-kāraka rule as the eighth.

Ye [M 0.0257] sakkesu paññattā, te suṇohi yathātathaṃ;

Eḷakalomāni patto ca, ovādo ceva bhesajjaṃ.

Those that were laid down among the Sakyans, listen to them as they truly are: the Eḷakaloma-dhovāpana rule, the rule on a bowl, the Bhikkhunupassaya-ovāda rule, and the Tatuttari-bhesajja-viññāpana rule.

Sūci āraññiko ceva, aṭṭhete cha ete (sabbattha) kāpilavatthave;

Udakasuddhiyā [T 0.0363] ovādo, bhikkhunīsu pavuccanti.

The Sūcighara rule and the Āraññaka rule, as well as the Udakasuddhi rule and the Ovādūpagamana rule concerning bhikkhunīs, are declared. These eight were laid down in Kapilavatthu.

Ye bhaggesu paññattā, te suṇohi yathātathaṃ;

Samādahitvā visibbenti, sāmisena sasitthakaṃ.

Those that were laid down among the Bhaggas, listen to them as they truly are: the Samādahitvā-visibbana rule, the Sāmisa-hattha rule, and the Sasitthaka rule.

Pārājikāni cattāri, saṅghādisesāni bhavanti;

Satta ca nissaggiyāni, aṭṭha dvattiṃsa khuddakā.

There are four Pārājikas, seven Saṅghādisesas, eight Nissaggiyas, and thirty-two minor rules.

Dve [V 0.0278] gārayhā tayo sekkhā, chappaññāsa sikkhāpadā;

Chasu nagaresu paññattā, buddhenādiccabandhunā.

There are two reprehensible rules and three training rules. Thus, fifty-six training rules were laid down in six cities by the Buddha, the kinsman of the sun.

Chaūna tīṇisatāni, sabbe sāvatthiyaṃ katā;

Kāruṇikena buddhena, gotamena yasassinā.

Two hundred and ninety-four—all these training rules were laid down in Sāvatthī by the compassionate and glorious Buddha Gotama.

2. Catuvipattiṃ

2. The Four Corruptions

336.

336.

Yaṃ taṃ yaṃ yaṃ (ka.) pucchimha akittayi no;

Taṃ taṃ byākataṃ anaññathā;

Aññaṃ taṃ pucchāmi tadiṅgha brūhi;

Garuka lahukañcāpi sāvasesaṃ;

Anavasesaṃ duṭṭhullañca aduṭṭhullaṃ;

Ye ca yāvatatiyakā.

Whatever we asked you, that you have declared to us; that has been explained without deviation. I will ask you another question; come, please speak on it. Concerning the grave offense and the light offense; the offense with a remainder and the offense without a remainder; the coarse offense and the non-coarse offense; and those which are offenses 'up to the third time'.

Sādhāraṇaṃ asādhāraṇaṃ;

Vibhattiyo ca vipattiyo ca (sī. syā.) yehi samathehi sammanti;

Sabbānipetāni viyākarohi;

Handa vākyaṃ suṇoma te.

The common offense and the uncommon offense; the classifications, and by which legal procedures they are settled—please make all of these clear. Now, let us hear your words.

Ekatiṃsā [P 5.0146] ye garukā, aṭṭhettha anavasesā;

Ye [T 0.0364] garukā te duṭṭhullā, ye duṭṭhullā sā sīlavipatti;

Pārājikaṃ saṅghādiseso, “sīlavipattī”ti vuccati.

There are thirty-one grave offenses; among these, eight are 'without a remainder'. Those that are grave offenses are coarse offenses. Those that are coarse offenses are a corruption of virtue. Pārājika and Saṅghādisesa are called 'a corruption of virtue'.

Thullaccayaṃ [M 0.0258] pācittiyā, pāṭidesanīyaṃ dukkaṭaṃ;

Dubbhāsitaṃ yo cāyaṃ, akkosati hasādhippāyo;

Ayaṃ sā ācāravipattisammatā.

The Thullaccaya offense, the Pācittiya offense, the Pāṭidesanīya offense, the Dukkaṭa offense, and the Dubbhāsita offense of one who reviles with playful intent—this is considered a corruption of conduct.

Viparītadiṭṭhiṃ [V 0.0279] gaṇhanti, asaddhammehi purakkhatā;

Abbhācikkhanti sambuddhaṃ, duppaññā mohapārutā;

Ayaṃ sā diṭṭhivipattisammatā.

Those who, surrounded by false doctrines, of little wisdom and enveloped in delusion, take up a perverse view and slander the Fully Awakened One—this is considered a corruption of view.

Ājīvahetu ājīvakāraṇā pāpiccho icchāpakato asantaṃ abhūtaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ ullapati, ājīvahetu ājīvakāraṇā sañcarittaṃ samāpajjati, ājīvahetu ājīvakāraṇā – “yo te vihāre vasati, so bhikkhu arahā”ti bhaṇati, ājīvahetu ājīvakāraṇā bhikkhu paṇītabhojanāni attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjati, ājīvahetu ājīvakāraṇā bhikkhunī paṇītabhojanāni attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjati, ājīvahetu ājīvakāraṇā sūpaṃ vā odanaṃ vā agilāno attano atthāya viññāpetvā bhuñjati. Ayaṃ sā ājīvavipatti sammatā.

For the sake of livelihood, due to the cause of livelihood, being of evil desires and overcome by such desire, one proclaims a state superior to that of humans which is non-existent and untrue. For the sake of livelihood, due to the cause of livelihood, one engages in matchmaking. For the sake of livelihood, due to the cause of livelihood, one says, 'The monk who lives in your monastery is an Arahant.' For the sake of livelihood, due to the cause of livelihood, a monk, having requested choice foods for his own benefit, eats them. For the sake of livelihood, due to the cause of livelihood, a nun, having requested choice foods for her own benefit, eats them. For the sake of livelihood, due to the cause of livelihood, not being ill, one, having requested curry or rice for one's own benefit, eats it. This is designated as a corruption of livelihood.

Ekādasa yāvatatiyakā, te suṇohi yathātathaṃ;

Ukkhittānuvattikā, aṭṭha yāvatatiyakā;

Ariṭṭho caṇḍakāḷī ca, ime te yāvatatiyakā.

There are eleven 'up to the third time' offenses; listen to them as they truly are. The training rule on following a suspended monk, the eight Saṅghādisesa offenses that are 'up to the third time', the training rule concerning Ariṭṭha, and that concerning Caṇḍakāḷī—these are the 'up to the third time' offenses.

3. Chedanakādi

3. Beginning with Cutting

337. Kati [T 0.0365] chedanakāni? Kati bhedanakāni? Kati uddālanakāni? Kati anaññapācittiyāni? Kati bhikkhusammutiyo? Kati sāmīciyo? Kati paramāni?

337. How many are the cutting rules? How many are the splitting rules? How many are the uprooting rules? How many are the Anañña Pācittiya offenses? How many are the monastic authorizations? How many are the proper practices? How many are the maximums?

Kati jānanti paññattā, buddhenādiccabandhunā.

How many training rules were laid down with the word 'knowing' by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun?

Cha chedanakāni. Ekaṃ bhedanakaṃ. Ekaṃ uddālanakaṃ. Cattāri anaññapācittiyāni. Catasso bhikkhusammutiyo. Satta sāmīciyo. Cuddasa paramāni.

There are six cutting rules. There is one splitting rule. There is one uprooting rule. There are four Anañña Pācittiya offenses. There are four monastic authorizations. There are seven proper practices. There are fourteen maximums.

Sodasa soḷasa (sī. syā.) aṭṭhakathā oloketabbā jānanti paññattā, buddhenādiccabandhunā.

Sixteen training rules were laid down with the word 'knowing' by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun.

4. Asādhāraṇādi

4. Beginning with the Uncommon

338.

338.

Vīsaṃ [M 0.0259][V 0.0280] dve satāni bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadāni;

Uddesaṃ āgacchanti uposathesu;

Tīṇi satāni cattāri bhikkhunīnaṃ sikkhāpadāni;

Uddesaṃ āgacchanti uposathesu.

Two hundred and twenty training rules for monks come up for recitation on Uposatha days; three hundred and four training rules for nuns come up for recitation on Uposatha days.

Chacattārīsā bhikkhūnaṃ, bhikkhunīhi asādhāraṇā;

Sataṃ tiṃsā ca bhikkhunīnaṃ, bhikkhūhi asādhāraṇā.

Forty-six of the monks' rules are not shared with the nuns; one hundred and thirty of the nuns' rules are not shared with the monks.

Sataṃ sattati chacceva, ubhinnaṃ asādhāraṇā;

Sataṃ sattati cattāri, ubhinnaṃ samasikkhatā.

One hundred and seventy-six are the rules not shared between the two communities; one hundred and seventy-four are trained in common by both.

Vīsaṃ [P 5.0147] dve satāni bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadāni;

Uddesaṃ āgacchanti uposathesu;

Te suṇohi yathātathaṃ.

Two hundred and twenty training rules for monks come up for recitation on Uposatha days; listen to them as they truly are.

Pārājikāni cattāri, saṅghādisesāni bhavanti terasa;

Aniyatā dve honti.

There are four Pārājikas, thirteen Saṅghādisesas, and two Aniyatas.

Nissaggiyāni tiṃseva, dvenavuti ca khuddakā;

Cattāro [T 0.0366] pāṭidesanīyā, pañcasattati sekhiyā.

There are thirty Nissaggiya rules, ninety-two minor rules, four Pāṭidesanīya rules, and seventy-five Sekhiya rules.

Vīsaṃ dve satāni cime honti bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadāni;

Uddesaṃ āgacchanti uposathesu.

These are the two hundred and twenty training rules for the monks; they come up for recitation on the Uposatha days.

Tīṇi satāni cattāri, bhikkhunīnaṃ sikkhāpadāni;

Uddesaṃ āgacchanti uposathesu, te suṇohi yathātathaṃ.

There are three hundred and four training rules for the nuns; they come up for recitation on the Uposatha days. Listen to them as they truly are.

Pārājikāni [V 0.0281] aṭṭha, saṅghādisesāni bhavanti sattarasa;

Nissaggiyāni tiṃseva, sataṃ saṭṭhi cha ceva khuddakāni pavuccanti.

There are eight Pārājika rules and seventeen Saṅghādisesa rules. Thirty are called Nissaggiya rules, and one hundred and sixty-six are called minor rules.

Aṭṭha pāṭidesanīyā, pañcasattati sekhiyā;

Tīṇi satāni cattāri cime honti bhikkhunīnaṃ sikkhāpadāni;

Uddesaṃ āgacchanti uposathesu.

There are eight Pāṭidesanīya rules and seventy-five Sekhiya rules. These are the three hundred and four training rules for the nuns; they come up for recitation on the Uposatha days.

Chacattārīsā bhikkhūnaṃ, bhikkhunīhi asādhāraṇā;

Te suṇohi yathātathaṃ.

Forty-six training rules of the monks are not shared with the nuns; listen to them as they truly are.

[M 0.0260] Saṅghādisesā, dve aniyatehi aṭṭha;

Nissaggiyāni [T 0.0367] dvādasa, tehi te honti vīsati.

Six are Saṅghādisesas; with the two Aniyatas, they are eight. Twelve are Nissaggiya rules; with those, they become twenty.

Dvevīsati khuddakā, caturo pāṭidesanīyā;

Chacattārīsā cime honti, bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīhi asādhāraṇā.

Twenty-two are the Khuddaka rules, and four are the Pāṭidesanīya. These forty-six training rules of the monks are not shared with the nuns.

Sataṃ tiṃsā ca bhikkhunīnaṃ, bhikkhūhi asādhāraṇā;

Te suṇohi yathātathaṃ.

One hundred and thirty are the training rules of the nuns not shared with the monks; listen to them as they truly are.

Pārājikāni [V 0.0282] cattāri, saṅghamhā dasa nissare;

Nissaggiyāni dvādasa, channavuti ca khuddakā;

Aṭṭha pāṭidesanīyā.

Four are the Pārājika rules; ten are those that lead to removal from the Saṅgha; twelve are the Nissaggiya rules; ninety-six are the Khuddaka rules; and eight are the Pāṭidesanīya.

Sataṃ tiṃsā cime honti bhikkhunīnaṃ, bhikkhūhi asādhāraṇā;

Sataṃ sattati chacceva, ubhinnaṃ asādhāraṇā;

Te suṇohi yathātathaṃ.

These one hundred and thirty are the training rules of the nuns not shared with the monks. One hundred and seventy-six are the rules not held in common by the two groups; listen to them as they truly are.

Pārājikāni cattāri, saṅghādisesāni bhavanti soḷasa;

Aniyatā dve honti, nissaggiyāni catuvīsati;

Sataṃ aṭṭhārasā ceva, khuddakāni pavuccanti;

Dvādasa pāṭidesanīyā.

There are four Pārājika rules and sixteen Saṅghādisesa rules. There are two Aniyata rules and twenty-four Nissaggiya rules. One hundred and eighteen are called Khuddaka rules, and twelve are the Pāṭidesanīya rules.

Sataṃ sattati chaccevime honti, ubhinnaṃ asādhāraṇā;

Sataṃ sattati cattāri, ubhinnaṃ samasikkhatā;

Te suṇohi yathātathaṃ.

These one hundred and seventy-six are the rules not held in common by the two groups. One hundred and seventy-four are rules of shared training for both; listen to them as they truly are.

Pārājikāni cattāri, saṅghādisesāni bhavanti satta;

Nissaggiyāni aṭṭhārasa, samasattati khuddakā;

Pañcasattati sekhiyāni.

There are four Pārājika rules and seven Saṅghādisesa rules. There are eighteen Nissaggiya rules, seventy Khuddaka rules, and seventy-five Sekhiya rules.

Sataṃ sattati cattāri cime honti, ubhinnaṃ samasikkhatā;

Aṭṭhe [P 5.0148] pārājikā ye durāsadā, tālavatthusamūpamā.

These one hundred and seventy-four are rules of shared training for both. The eight Pārājikas that exist are difficult to approach, like the mere stump of an uprooted palm tree.

Paṇḍupalāso puthusilā, sīsacchinnova so naro;

Tālova matthakacchinno, aviruḷhī bhavanti te.

Like a withered leaf, like a great stone slab split in two, like that man whose head has been cut off, and like a palm tree whose crown has been cut off, they are of a nature that does not grow again.

Tevīsati [M 0.0261] saṅghādisesā, dve aniyatā;

Dve [T 0.0368] cattārīsa nissaggiyā;

Aṭṭhāsītisataṃ pācittiyā, dvādasa pāṭidesanīyā.

Twenty-three are the Saṅghādisesas, and two are the Aniyatas; forty-two are the Nissaggiyas; one hundred and eighty-eight are the Pācittiyas, and twelve are the Pāṭidesanīyas.

Pañcasattati sekhiyā, tīhi samathehi sammanti;

Sammukhā ca paṭiññāya, tiṇavatthārakena ca.

Seventy-five are the Sekhiyas; they are settled by three settlements: that carried out in the presence, that based on an admission, and that of covering over with grass.

Dve uposathā dve pavāraṇā;

Cattāri kammāni jinena desitā;

Pañceva uddesā caturo bhavanti;

Anaññathā āpattikkhandhā ca bhavanti satta.

Two Uposathas, two Pavāraṇās, and four kinds of formal acts were taught by the Conqueror. The recitations are five and four respectively, not otherwise. And the groups of offenses are seven.

Adhikaraṇāni [V 0.0283] cattāri sattahi samathehi sammanti;

Dvīhi catūhi tīhi kiccaṃ ekena sammati.

There are four legal issues, which are settled by seven settlements. A legal issue arising from a dispute is settled by two; one arising from an accusation, by four; one arising from an offense, by three; and one concerning duties is settled by one.

5. Pārājikādiāpatti

5. Offenses Beginning with Pārājika

339.

339.

‘Pārājika’nti yaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ suṇohi yathātathaṃ;

Cuto paraddho bhaṭṭho ca, saddhammā hi niraṅkato;

Saṃvāsopi tahiṃ natthi, tenetaṃ iti vuccati.

That which is called ‘Pārājika,’ listen to it as it truly is. Because one has fallen away, failed, and is ruined, cast out from the good Dhamma; there is no communion with such a one. Therefore, it is so called.

‘Saṅghādiseso’ti yaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ suṇohi yathātathaṃ;

Saṅghova deti parivāsaṃ, mūlāya paṭikassati;

Mānattaṃ deti abbheti, tenetaṃ iti vuccati.

That which is called ‘Saṅghādisesa,’ listen to it as it truly is. The Saṅgha alone gives probation, sends one back to the beginning, gives penance, and rehabilitates; therefore, it is so called.

‘Aniyato’ti yaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ suṇohi yathātathaṃ;

Aniyato na niyato, anekaṃsikataṃ padaṃ;

Tiṇṇamaññataraṃ ṭhānaṃ, ‘aniyato’ti pavuccati.

That which is called ‘Aniyata,’ listen to it as it truly is. Because it is not fixed, the rule is made to be of uncertain application, being one or another of three cases; therefore, it is called ‘Aniyata.’

‘Thullaccaya’nti yaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ suṇohi yathātathaṃ;

Ekassa [T 0.0369] mūle yo deseti, yo ca taṃ paṭigaṇhati;

Accayo tena samo natthi, tenetaṃ iti vuccati.

That which is called ‘Thullaccaya,’ listen to it as it truly is. He who confesses it in the presence of one monk, and he who receives that confession; there is no transgression equal to it. Therefore, it is so called.

‘Nissaggiya’nti yaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ suṇohi yathātathaṃ;

Saṅghamajjhe gaṇamajjhe, ekasseva ca ekato;

Nissajjitvāna deseti, tenetaṃ iti vuccati.
