That which is called ‘Nissaggiya,’ listen to it as it truly is. Because one confesses after having forfeited the item in the midst of the Saṅgha, in the midst of a group, or in the presence of just one individual, therefore, it is so called.

‘Pācittiya’nti [M 0.0262] yaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ suṇohi yathātathaṃ;

Pāteti kusalaṃ dhammaṃ, ariyamaggaṃ aparajjhati;

Cittasaṃmohanaṭṭhānaṃ, tenetaṃ iti vuccati.

That which is called ‘Pācittiya,’ listen to it as it truly is. It causes wholesome states to fall, it makes one miss the noble path, and it is a cause for confusion of mind; therefore, it is so called.

‘Pāṭidesanīya’nti [V 0.0284] yaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ suṇohi yathātathaṃ;

Bhikkhu aññātako santo, kicchā laddhāya bhojanaṃ;

Sāmaṃ gahetvā bhuñjeyya, ‘gārayha’nti pavuccati.

That which is called 'Pāṭidesanīya,' listen to it as it truly is: Should a bhikkhu, being unrelated, personally accept and eat food from a bhikkhunī who obtained it with difficulty, this is called 'reprehensible'.

Nimantanāsu bhuñjantā chandāya, vosāsati tattha bhikkhuniṃ;

Anivāretvā tahiṃ bhuñje, gārayhanti pavuccati.

While eating at invited meals, should a bhikkhunī there give instructions according to her wish, and should one eat in that household without having prevented her, this is called 'reprehensible'.

Saddhācittaṃ [P 5.0149] kulaṃ gantvā, appabhogaṃ anāḷiyaṃ anāḷhiyaṃ (sī. syā.);

Agilāno tahiṃ bhuñje, gārayhanti pavuccati.

Having gone to a family designated as 'in training' that has a faithful mind, but is of little wealth and poor, should one, not being ill, eat there, this is called 'reprehensible'.

Yo ce araññe viharanto, sāsaṅke sabhayānake;

Aviditaṃ tahiṃ bhuñje, gārayhanti pavuccati.

Whatever bhikkhu, dwelling in a forest monastery that is questionable and fearful, should eat there something that has not been made known, this is called 'reprehensible'.

Bhikkhunī aññātikā santā, yaṃ paresaṃ mamāyitaṃ;

Sappi telaṃ madhuṃ phāṇitaṃ, macchamaṃsaṃ atho khīraṃ;

Dadhiṃ sayaṃ [T 0.0370] viññāpeyya bhikkhunī, gārayhapattā sugatassa sāsane.

Whatever bhikkhunī, being unrelated, should personally request that which is cherished by others—ghee, oil, honey, molasses, fish, meat, and also milk or curd—that bhikkhunī has committed a reprehensible offense in the Dispensation of the Sugata.

‘Dukkaṭa’nti yaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ suṇohi yathātathaṃ;

Aparaddhaṃ viraddhañca, khalitaṃ yañca dukkaṭaṃ.

That which is called 'Dukkaṭa,' listen to it as it truly is: That which is faulty, contrary, and a slip is a 'wrongdoing' (dukkaṭa).

Yaṃ manusso kare pāpaṃ, āvi vā yadi vā raho;

‘Dukkaṭa’nti pavedenti, tenetaṃ iti vuccati.

Whatever evil a person does, whether openly or in secret, just as they declare that evil to be a 'wrongdoing' (dukkaṭa), for that reason this is so called.

‘Dubbhāsita’nti yaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ suṇohi yathātathaṃ;

Dubbhāsitaṃ durābhaṭṭhaṃ, saṃkiliṭṭhañca yaṃ padaṃ;

Yañca viññū garahanti, tenetaṃ iti vuccati.

That which is called 'Dubbhāsita,' listen to it as it truly is: 'Wrong speech' (dubbhāsita) is that which is badly uttered, and any phrase that is defiled. And because the wise censure it, for that reason this is so called.

‘Sekhiya’nti yaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ suṇohi yathātathaṃ;

Sekkhassa sikkhamānassa, ujumaggānusārino.

That which is called 'Sekhiya,' listen to it as it truly is.

Ādi [V 0.0285] cetaṃ caraṇañca, mukhaṃ saññamasaṃvaro;

Sikkhā etādisī natthi, tenetaṃ iti vuccati.

For the trainee who is practicing and following the straight path, this is the beginning and the conduct; restraint and control are the foremost part. There is no training such as this; for that reason this is so called.

udā. 45 udānepi Channamativassati[M 0.0263], vivaṭaṃ nātivassati;

Tasmā channaṃ vivaretha, evaṃ taṃ nātivassati.

What is concealed leaks; what is uncovered does not leak. Therefore, uncover what is concealed; in this way, it will not leak.

Gati migānaṃ pavanaṃ, ākāso pakkhinaṃ gati;

Vibhavo gati dhammānaṃ, nibbānaṃ arahato gatīti.

The resort of deer is the forest; the sky is the resort of birds. Cessation is the resort of conditioned things; Nibbāna is the resort of the Arahant.

Gāthāsaṅgaṇikaṃ.

The Collection in Verses.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Sattanagaresu paññattā, vipatti caturopi ca;

Bhikkhūnaṃ [T 0.0371] bhikkhunīnañca, sādhāraṇā asādhāraṇā;

Sāsanaṃ anuggahāya, gāthāsaṅgaṇikaṃ idanti.

The rules laid down in the seven cities, and also the four kinds of failure; those common and uncommon to both bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs; for the support of the Dispensation, this Collection in Verses has been spoken.

Gāthāsaṅgaṇikaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Collection in Verses is concluded.

Adhikaraṇabhedo

The Classification of Legal Issues

1. Ukkoṭanabhedādi

1. Classification of Annulment, etc.

340. cūḷava. 215; pari. 275 Cattāri [T 0.0372][P 5.0150][M 0.0264][V 0.0286] adhikaraṇāni. Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, kiccādhikaraṇaṃ – imāni cattāri adhikaraṇāni.

340. There are four legal issues: the legal issue of disputes, the legal issue of accusations, the legal issue of offenses, and the legal issue of duties. These are the four legal issues.

Imesaṃ catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ kati ukkoṭā? Imesaṃ catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ dasa ukkoṭā. Vivādādhikaraṇassa dve ukkoṭā, anuvādādhikaraṇassa cattāro ukkoṭā, āpattādhikaraṇassa tayo ukkoṭā, kiccādhikaraṇassa eko ukkoṭo – imesaṃ catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ ime dasa ukkoṭā.

How many annulments are there for these four legal issues? There are ten annulments for these four legal issues. For a legal issue of disputes, there are two annulments; for a legal issue of accusations, there are four annulments; for a legal issue of offenses, there are three annulments; for a legal issue of duties, there is one annulment. These are the ten annulments for these four legal issues.

Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭento kati samathe ukkoṭeti? Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭento kati samathe ukkoṭeti? Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭento kati samathe ukkoṭeti? Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭento kati samathe ukkoṭeti?

When annulling a legal issue of disputes, how many settlements does one annul? When annulling a legal issue of accusations, how many settlements does one annul? When annulling a legal issue of offenses, how many settlements does one annul? When annulling a legal issue of duties, how many settlements does one annul?

Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭento dve samathe ukkoṭeti. Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭento cattāro samathe ukkoṭeti. Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭento tayo samathe ukkoṭeti. Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭento ekaṃ samathaṃ ukkoṭeti.

When annulling a legal issue of disputes, one annuls two settlements. When annulling a legal issue of accusations, one annuls four settlements. When annulling a legal issue of offenses, one annuls three settlements. When annulling a legal issue of duties, one annuls one settlement.

341. Kati ukkoṭā? Katihākārehi ukkoṭanaṃ pasavati? Katihaṅgehi samannāgato puggalo adhikaraṇaṃ [T 0.0373] ukkoṭeti? Kati puggalā adhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭentā āpattiṃ āpajjanti?

341. How many are the annulments? By how many modes does annulment arise? Endowed with how many factors does a person annul a legal issue? How many persons, while annulling a legal issue, incur an offense?

Dvādasa [V 0.0287] ukkoṭā. Dasahākārehi ukkoṭanaṃ pasavati. Catūhaṅgehi samannāgato puggalo adhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭeti. Cattāro puggalā adhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭentā āpattiṃ āpajjanti?

There are twelve annulments. Annulment arises by ten modes. A person endowed with four factors annuls a legal issue. Four persons, while annulling a legal issue, incur an offense.

Katame dvādasa ukkoṭā? Akataṃ kammaṃ, dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ, puna kātabbaṃ kammaṃ, anihataṃ, dunnihataṃ, puna nihanitabbaṃ, avinicchitaṃ, duvinicchitaṃ, puna vinicchitabbaṃ, avūpasantaṃ, duvūpasantaṃ, puna vūpasametabbanti – ime dvādasa ukkoṭā.

What are the twelve annulments? A formal act not performed, a formal act wrongly performed, a formal act to be performed again; a matter not brought forward, a matter wrongly brought forward, a matter to be brought forward again; a matter not decided, a matter wrongly decided, a matter to be decided again; a matter not settled, a matter wrongly settled, a matter to be settled again—these are the twelve annulments.

Katamehi [M 0.0265] dasahākārehi ukkoṭanaṃ pasavati? Tattha jātakaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭeti, tattha jātakaṃ vūpasantaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭeti, antarāmagge adhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭeti, antarāmagge vūpasantaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭeti, tattha gataṃ adhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭeti, tattha gataṃ vūpasantaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭeti, sativinayaṃ ukkoṭeti, amūḷhavinayaṃ ukkoṭeti, tassapāpiyasikaṃ [P 5.0151] ukkoṭeti, tiṇavatthārakaṃ ukkoṭeti – imehi dasahākārehi ukkoṭanaṃ pasavati.

By what ten modes does re-opening arise? One re-opens a legal issue that has arisen there; one re-opens a legal issue that has arisen there and has been settled; one re-opens a legal issue on the way; one re-opens a legal issue that has been settled on the way; one re-opens a legal issue that has gone there; one re-opens a legal issue that has gone there and has been settled; one re-opens a verdict of mindfulness; one re-opens a verdict of past insanity; one re-opens a verdict for one's bad character; one re-opens a covering over with grass—by these ten modes re-opening arises.

Katamehi catūhaṅgehi samannāgato puggalo adhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭeti? Chandāgatiṃ gacchanto adhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭeti, dosāgatiṃ gacchanto adhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭeti, mohāgatiṃ gacchanto adhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭeti, bhayāgatiṃ gacchanto adhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭeti – imehi catūhaṅgehi samannāgato puggalo adhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭeti.

Endowed with which four factors does a person re-open a legal issue? Going the wrong way through desire, one re-opens a legal issue; going the wrong way through aversion, one re-opens a legal issue; going the wrong way through delusion, one re-opens a legal issue; going the wrong way through fear, one re-opens a legal issue—endowed with these four factors, a person re-opens a legal issue.

Katame cattāro puggalā adhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭentā āpattiṃ āpajjanti? Tadahupasampanno ukkoṭeti ukkoṭanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ, āgantuko ukkoṭeti ukkoṭanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ, kārako ukkoṭeti ukkoṭanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ, chandadāyako ukkoṭeti ukkoṭanakaṃ pācittiyaṃ – ime cattāro puggalā adhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭentā āpattiṃ āpajjanti.

Which four persons, in re-opening a legal issue, incur an offense? If one ordained on that day re-opens it, there is a pācittiya offense of re-opening. If a visiting monk re-opens it, there is a pācittiya offense of re-opening. If the one who carried out the formal act re-opens it, there is a pācittiya offense of re-opening. If the one who gave consent re-opens it, there is a pācittiya offense of re-opening. These four persons, in re-opening a legal issue, incur an offense.

2. Adhikaraṇanidānādi

2. The Source, etc., of Legal Issues

342. Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ [T 0.0374] kiṃnidānaṃ, kiṃsamudayaṃ, kiṃjātikaṃ, kiṃpabhavaṃ, kiṃsambhāraṃ, kiṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ? Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ kiṃnidānaṃ, kiṃsamudayaṃ, kiṃjātikaṃ, kiṃpabhavaṃ, kiṃsambhāraṃ, kiṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ? Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ kiṃnidānaṃ, kiṃsamudayaṃ, kiṃjātikaṃ, kiṃpabhavaṃ, kiṃsambhāraṃ, kiṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ[V 0.0288]? Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ kiṃnidānaṃ, kiṃsamudayaṃ, kiṃjātikaṃ, kiṃpabhavaṃ, kiṃsambhāraṃ, kiṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ?

342. A legal issue of disputes—what is its source, what is its origin, what is its genesis, what is its provenance, what are its components, what is its arising? A legal issue of accusations—what is its source, what is its origin, what is its genesis, what is its provenance, what are its components, what is its arising? A legal issue of an offense—what is its source, what is its origin, what is its genesis, what is its provenance, what are its components, what is its arising? A legal issue of duties—what is its source, what is its origin, what is its genesis, what is its provenance, what are its components, what is its arising?

Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ vivādanidānaṃ vivādasamudayaṃ vivādajātikaṃ vivādapabhavaṃ vivādasambhāraṃ vivādasamuṭṭhānaṃ. Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ anuvādanidānaṃ anuvādasamudayaṃ anuvādajātikaṃ anuvādapabhavaṃ anuvādasambhāraṃ anuvādasamuṭṭhānaṃ. Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ āpattinidānaṃ āpattisamudayaṃ āpattijātikaṃ āpattipabhavaṃ āpattisambhāraṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānaṃ. Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ kiccayanidānaṃ kiccayasamudayaṃ kiccayajātikaṃ kiccayapabhavaṃ kiccayasambhāraṃ kiccayasamuṭṭhānaṃ.

A legal issue of disputes has dispute as its source, dispute as its origin, dispute as its genesis, dispute as its provenance, dispute as its components, and dispute as its arising. A legal issue of accusations has accusation as its source, accusation as its origin, accusation as its genesis, accusation as its provenance, accusation as its components, and accusation as its arising. A legal issue of offenses has an offense as its source, an offense as its origin, an offense as its genesis, an offense as its provenance, an offense as its components, and an offense as its arising. A legal issue of duties has duty as its source, duty as its origin, duty as its genesis, duty as its provenance, duty as its components, and duty as its arising.

Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ [M 0.0266] kiṃnidānaṃ, kiṃsamudayaṃ, kiṃjātikaṃ, kiṃpabhavaṃ, kiṃsambhāraṃ, kiṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ? Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ…pe… āpattādhikaraṇaṃ…pe… kiccādhikaraṇaṃ kiṃnidānaṃ, kiṃsamudayaṃ, kiṃjātikaṃ, kiṃpabhavaṃ, kiṃsambhāraṃ, kiṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ?

A legal issue of disputes—what is its source, what is its origin, what is its genesis, what is its provenance, what are its components, what is its arising? A legal issue of accusations… and so on… a legal issue of offenses… and so on… a legal issue of duties—what is its source, what is its origin, what is its genesis, what is its provenance, what are its components, what is its arising?

Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ hetunidānaṃ, hetusamudayaṃ, hetujātikaṃ, hetupabhavaṃ, hetusambhāraṃ, hetusamuṭṭhānaṃ. Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ…pe… āpattādhikaraṇaṃ…pe… kiccādhikaraṇaṃ hetunidānaṃ, hetusamudayaṃ, hetujātikaṃ, hetupabhavaṃ, hetusambhāraṃ, hetusamuṭṭhānaṃ.

A legal issue of disputes has a cause as its source, a cause as its origin, a cause as its genesis, a cause as its provenance, a cause as its components, and a cause as its arising. A legal issue of accusations… and so on… a legal issue of offenses… and so on… a legal issue of duties has a cause as its source, a cause as its origin, a cause as its genesis, a cause as its provenance, a cause as its components, and a cause as its arising.

Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ kiṃnidānaṃ, kiṃsamudayaṃ, kiṃjātikaṃ, kiṃpabhavaṃ, kiṃsambhāraṃ, kiṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ? Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ [T 0.0375] …pe… āpattādhikaraṇaṃ…pe… kiccādhikaraṇaṃ kiṃnidānaṃ, kiṃsamudayaṃ, kiṃjātikaṃ, kiṃpabhavaṃ, kiṃsambhāraṃ, kiṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ?

A legal issue of disputes—what is its source, what is its origin, what is its genesis, what is its provenance, what are its components, what is its arising? A legal issue of accusations… and so on… a legal issue of offenses… and so on… a legal issue of duties—what is its source, what is its origin, what is its genesis, what is its provenance, what are its components, what is its arising?

Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ paccayanidānaṃ, paccayasamudayaṃ, paccayajātikaṃ, paccayapabhavaṃ, paccayasambhāraṃ, paccayasamuṭṭhānaṃ. Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ…pe… āpattādhikaraṇaṃ…pe… kiccādhikaraṇaṃ paccayanidānaṃ, paccayasamudayaṃ, paccayajātikaṃ, paccayapabhavaṃ, paccayasambhāraṃ, paccayasamuṭṭhānaṃ.

A legal matter concerning disputes has a condition as its cause, a condition as its origin, a condition as its nature, a condition as its source, a condition as its requisite, and a condition as its origination. A legal matter concerning accusations… and so on… A legal matter concerning offenses… and so on… A legal matter concerning duties has a condition as its cause, a condition as its origin, a condition as its nature, a condition as its source, a condition as its requisite, and a condition as its origination.

3. Adhikaraṇamūlādi

3. The Roots of Legal Matters, etc.

343. Catunnaṃ [V 0.0289] adhikaraṇānaṃ kati mūlāni, kati samuṭṭhānā? Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ tettiṃsa mūlāni, tettiṃsa samuṭṭhānā.

343. How many roots and how many origins are there for the four legal matters? There are thirty-three roots and thirty-three origins for the four legal matters.

Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamāni tettiṃsa mūlāni? Vivādādhikaraṇassa dvādasa mūlāni, anuvādādhikaraṇassa cuddasa mūlāni, āpattādhikaraṇassa cha mūlāni, kiccādhikaraṇassa ekaṃ mūlaṃ, saṅgho – catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ imāni tettiṃsa mūlāni.

What are the thirty-three roots of the four legal matters? For a legal matter concerning disputes, there are twelve roots; for a legal matter concerning accusations, there are fourteen roots; for a legal matter concerning offenses, there are six roots; for a legal matter concerning duties, there is one root, the Saṅgha. These are the thirty-three roots of the four legal matters.

Catunnaṃ [P 5.0152] adhikaraṇānaṃ katame tettiṃsa samuṭṭhānā? Vivādādhikaraṇassa aṭṭhārasabhedakaravatthūni samuṭṭhānā, anuvādādhikaraṇassa catasso vipattiyo samuṭṭhānā, āpattādhikaraṇassa sattāpattikkhandhā samuṭṭhānā, kiccādhikaraṇassa cattāri kammāni samuṭṭhānā – catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ ime tettiṃsa samuṭṭhānā.

What are the thirty-three origins of the four legal matters? For a legal matter concerning disputes, the eighteen grounds for causing schism are the origins; for a legal matter concerning accusations, the four failures are the origins; for a legal matter concerning offenses, the seven classes of offenses are the origins; for a legal matter concerning duties, the four formal acts are the origins. These are the thirty-three origins of the four legal matters.

4. Adhikaraṇapaccayāpatti

4. Offenses on Account of Legal Matters

344. Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ [M 0.0267] āpattānāpattīti? Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ na āpatti. Kiṃ pana vivādādhikaraṇapaccayā āpattiṃ āpajjeyyāti? Āma, vivādādhikaraṇapaccayā āpattiṃ āpajjeyya. Vivādādhikaraṇapaccayā [T 0.0376] kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Vivādādhikaraṇapaccayā dve āpattiyo āpajjati. Upasampannaṃ omasati, āpatti pācittiyassa; anupasampannaṃ omasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa – vivādādhikaraṇapaccayā imā dve āpattiyo āpajjati.

344. Is a legal matter concerning a dispute an offense or not an offense? A legal matter concerning a dispute is not an offense. But can one incur an offense on account of a legal matter concerning a dispute? Yes, one can incur an offense on account of a legal matter concerning a dispute. How many offenses does one incur on account of a legal matter concerning a dispute? One incurs two offenses on account of a legal matter concerning a dispute. If one reviles an ordained person, it is an offense of pācittiya; if one reviles an unordained person, it is an offense of dukkaṭa. One incurs these two offenses on account of a legal matter concerning a dispute.

Tā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ kati vipattiyo bhajanti? Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ? Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katihi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā? Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti? Katihi adhikaraṇehi katisu ṭhānesu katihi samathehi sammanti?

To how many of the four failures do those offenses belong? Among the four legal matters, which legal matter is it? By how many of the seven classes of offenses are they included? From how many of the six origins of offenses do they arise? By how many legal matters, in how many places, and by how many settlements are they settled?

Tā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ ekaṃ vipattiṃ bhajanti – ācāravipattiṃ. Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ[P 5.0153], āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ dvīhi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā – siyā pācittiyāpattikkhandhena, siyā dukkaṭāpattikkhandhena. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi [V 0.0290] samuṭṭhanti. Ekena adhikaraṇena – kiccādhikaraṇena; tīsu ṭhānesu – saṅghamajjhe, gaṇamajjhe, puggalassa santike; tīhi samathehi sammanti – siyā sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca, siyā sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca.

Those offenses pertain to one of the four failures—the failure in conduct. Among the four legal matters, it is a legal matter concerning an offense. They are included under two of the seven classes of offenses—sometimes by the class of pācittiya offenses, sometimes by the class of dukkaṭa offenses. They arise from three of the six origins of offenses. They are settled by one legal matter—a legal matter concerning duties; in three places—in the midst of the Saṅgha, in the midst of a group, or in the presence of an individual; by three settlements—sometimes by the procedure in the presence and by the act of acknowledgment, and sometimes by the procedure in the presence and by the covering over as with grass.

345. Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ āpattānāpattīti? Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ na āpatti. Kiṃ pana anuvādādhikaraṇapaccayā āpattiṃ āpajjeyyāti? Āma, anuvādādhikaraṇapaccayā āpattiṃ āpajjeyya. Anuvādādhikaraṇapaccayā, kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Anuvādādhikaraṇapaccayā tisso [T 0.0377] āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhikkhuṃ amūlakena pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṃseti, āpatti saṅghādisesassa; amūlakena saṅghādisesena anuddhaṃseti, āpatti pācittiyassa; amūlikāya ācāravipattiyā anuddhaṃseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa – anuvādādhikaraṇapaccayā imā tisso āpattiyo āpajjati.

345. Is a legal matter concerning accusation an offense or not an offense? A legal matter concerning accusation is not an offense. But might one incur an offense on account of a legal matter concerning accusation? Yes, one might incur an offense on account of a legal matter concerning accusation. On account of a legal matter concerning accusation, how many offenses does one incur? On account of a legal matter concerning accusation, one incurs three offenses. If one groundlessly accuses a bhikkhu of an offense entailing expulsion, it is an offense entailing a formal meeting of the Saṅgha; if one groundlessly accuses him of an offense entailing a formal meeting of the Saṅgha, it is an offense entailing expiation; if one groundlessly accuses him of a failure in conduct, it is an offense of wrong-doing. On account of a legal matter concerning accusation, one incurs these three offenses.

Tā [M 0.0268] āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ kati vipattiyo bhajanti? Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ? Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katihi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā? Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti? Katihi adhikaraṇehi katisu ṭhānesu katihi samathehi sammanti?

To how many of the four failures do those offenses pertain? Among the four legal matters, which legal matter is it? By how many of the seven classes of offenses are they included? From how many of the six origins of offenses do they arise? By how many legal matters, in how many places, and by how many settlements are they settled?

Tā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ dve vipattiyo bhajanti – siyā sīlavipattiṃ, siyā ācāravipattiṃ. Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ, āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ tīhi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā – siyā saṅghādisesāpattikkhandhena, siyā pācittiyāpattikkhandhena, siyā dukkaṭāpattikkhandhena. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti. Yā tā āpattiyo garukā tā āpattiyo ekena adhikaraṇena – kiccādhikaraṇena; ekamhi ṭhāne – saṅghamajjhe; dvīhi samathehi sammanti – sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca. Yā tā āpattiyo lahukā tā āpattiyo ekena adhikaraṇena – kiccādhikaraṇena; tīsu ṭhānesu – saṅghamajjhe gaṇamajjhe puggalassa santike; tīhi samathehi sammanti – siyā sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca[T 0.0378], siyā sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca.

Those offenses pertain to two of the four failures—sometimes a failure in virtue, sometimes a failure in conduct. Among the four legal matters, it is a legal matter concerning an offense. They are included under three of the seven classes of offenses—sometimes by the class of offenses entailing a formal meeting of the Saṅgha, sometimes by the class of offenses entailing expiation, and sometimes by the class of offenses of wrong-doing. They arise from three of the six origins of offenses. Those offenses that are serious are settled by one legal matter—a legal matter concerning duties; in one place—in the midst of the Saṅgha; by two settlements—by the procedure in the presence and by the act of acknowledgment. Those offenses that are minor are settled by one legal matter—a legal matter concerning duties; in three places—in the midst of the Saṅgha, in the midst of a group, or in the presence of an individual; by three settlements—sometimes by the procedure in the presence and by the act of acknowledgment, and sometimes by the procedure in the presence and by the covering over as with grass.

346. Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ āpattānāpattīti? Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ āpatti. Kiṃ pana āpattādhikaraṇapaccayā āpattiṃ āpajjeyyāti? Āma, āpattādhikaraṇapaccayā āpattiṃ āpajjeyya. Āpattādhikaraṇapaccayā kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Āpattādhikaraṇapaccayā catasso [V 0.0291] āpattiyo āpajjati. Bhikkhunī jānaṃ pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ pārājikaṃ dhammaṃ ajjhāpannaṃ (syā.) paṭicchādeti, āpatti pārājikassa; vematikā paṭicchādeti, āpatti thullaccayassa; bhikkhu saṅghādisesaṃ paṭicchādeti, āpatti pācittiyassa; ācāravipattiṃ paṭicchādeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa – āpattādhikaraṇapaccayā imā catasso āpattiyo āpajjati.

346. Is a legal issue concerning an offense an offense or not an offense? A legal issue concerning an offense is an offense. But could one incur an offense because of a legal issue concerning an offense? Yes, one could incur an offense because of a legal issue concerning an offense. Because of a legal issue concerning an offense, how many offenses does one incur? Because of a legal issue concerning an offense, one incurs four offenses. If a nun knowingly conceals an offense entailing expulsion, she incurs an offense entailing expulsion; if, being doubtful, she conceals it, she incurs an offense of grave matter; if a monk conceals an offense entailing a formal meeting of the Saṅgha, he incurs an offense entailing confession; if he conceals a failure in conduct, he incurs an offense of wrong-doing—because of a legal issue concerning an offense, one incurs these four offenses.

Tā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ kati vipattiyo bhajanti? Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ? Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katihi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā? Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti[M 0.0269]? Katihi adhikaraṇehi katisu ṭhānesu katihi samathehi sammanti?

To how many of the four failures do these offenses pertain? Among the four legal issues, which legal issue is it? By how many of the seven aggregates of offenses are they included? From how many of the six origins of offenses do they arise? By how many legal issues, in how many places, and by how many means of settlement are they settled?

Tā āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ dve vipattiyo bhajanti – siyā sīlavipattiṃ siyā ācāravipattiṃ. Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ – āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ catūhi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā – siyā pārājikāpattikkhandhena, siyā thullaccayāpattikkhandhena, siyā pācittiyāpattikkhandhena, siyā dukkaṭāpattikkhandhena. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhanti [T 0.0379] – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti. Yā sā āpatti anavasesā sā āpatti na katamena adhikaraṇena, na katamamhi ṭhāne, na katamena samathena sammati. Yā tā āpattiyo lahukā tā āpattiyo ekena adhikaraṇena – kiccādhikaraṇena; tīsu ṭhānesu – saṅghamajjhe, gaṇamajjhe, puggalassa santike; tīhi samathehi sammanti – siyā sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca, siyā sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca.

Those offenses pertain to two of the four failures: either a failure in virtue or a failure in conduct. Among the four legal issues, it is a legal issue concerning an offense. They are included under four of the seven aggregates of offenses: either by the aggregate of offenses entailing expulsion, or by the aggregate of offenses of grave matter, or by the aggregate of offenses entailing confession, or by the aggregate of offenses of wrong-doing. They arise from one of the six origins of offenses: they arise from body, speech, and mind. That offense which is without remainder is not settled by any legal issue, not in any place, not by any means of settlement. Those offenses that are minor are settled by one legal issue—a legal issue concerning a duty; in three places—in the midst of the Saṅgha, in the midst of a group, or in the presence of an individual; and by three means of settlement—either by the procedure in the presence and by the act of acknowledgment, or by the procedure in the presence and by the covering over with grass.

347. Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ āpattānāpattīti? Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ na āpatti. Kiṃ pana kiccādhikaraṇapaccayā āpattiṃ āpajjeyyāti? Āma, kiccādhikaraṇapaccayā āpattiṃ āpajjeyya. Kiccādhikaraṇapaccayā kati āpattiyo āpajjati? Kiccādhikaraṇapaccayā pañca āpattiyo āpajjati. Ukkhittānuvattikā bhikkhunī yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjati, ñattiyā dukkaṭaṃ; dvīhi kammavācāhi thullaccayā; kammavācāpariyosāne āpatti pārājikassa; bhedakānuvattakā bhikkhū yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanti, āpatti saṅghādisesassa; pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjanti, āpatti pācittiyassa – kiccādhikaraṇapaccayā imā pañca āpattiyo āpajjati.

347. Is a legal issue concerning a duty an offense or not an offense? A legal issue concerning a duty is not an offense. But then, might one incur an offense on account of a legal issue concerning a duty? Yes, on account of a legal issue concerning a duty, one might incur an offense. On account of a legal issue concerning a duty, how many offenses does one incur? On account of a legal issue concerning a duty, one incurs five offenses. A nun who follows one who has been suspended and does not relinquish this after being admonished up to the third time, incurs an offense of wrong-doing with the motion; offenses of grave matter with the two formal acts; at the conclusion of the formal act, an offense entailing expulsion. Monks who follow a schismatic and do not relinquish this after being admonished up to the third time, incur an offense entailing a formal meeting of the Saṅgha. Those who, holding a wrong view, do not relinquish it after being admonished up to the third time, incur an offense entailing confession. On account of a legal issue concerning a duty, one incurs these five offenses.

Tā [V 0.0292] āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ kati vipattiyo bhajanti? Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ? Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ katihi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā? Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ [T 0.0380] katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti? Katihi adhikaraṇehi katisu ṭhānesu katihi samathehi sammanti?

To how many of the four failures do these offenses pertain? Among the four legal issues, which legal issue is it? By how many of the seven aggregates of offenses are they included? From how many of the six origins of offenses do they arise? By how many legal issues, in how many places, and by how many means of settlement are they settled?

Tā [P 5.0154][M 0.0270] āpattiyo catunnaṃ vipattīnaṃ dve vipattiyo bhajanti – siyā sīlavipattiṃ siyā ācāravipattiṃ. Catunnaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ – āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ pañcahi āpattikkhandhehi saṅgahitā – siyā pārājikāpattikkhandhena, siyā saṅghādisesāpattikkhandhena, siyā thullaccayāpattikkhandhena, siyā pācittiyāpattikkhandhena, siyā dukkaṭāpattikkhandhena. Channaṃ āpattisamuṭṭhānānaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhanti – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti. Yā sā āpatti anavasesā sā āpatti na katamena adhikaraṇena, na katamamhi ṭhāne, na katamena samathena sammati. Yā sā āpatti garukā sā āpatti ekena adhikaraṇena – kiccādhikaraṇena; ekamhi ṭhāne – saṅghamajjhe; dvīhi samathehi sammati – sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca. Yā tā āpattiyo lahukā tā āpattiyo ekena adhikaraṇena – kiccādhikaraṇena; tīsu ṭhānesu – saṅghamajjhe, gaṇamajjhe, puggalassa santike; tīhi samathehi sammanti – siyā sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca, siyā sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca.

Those offenses pertain to two of the four failures: either a failure in virtue or a failure in conduct. Among the four legal issues, it is a legal issue concerning an offense. They are included under five of the seven aggregates of offenses: either by the aggregate of offenses entailing expulsion, or by the aggregate of offenses entailing a formal meeting of the Saṅgha, or by the aggregate of offenses of grave matter, or by the aggregate of offenses entailing confession, or by the aggregate of offenses of wrong-doing. They arise from one of the six origins of offenses: they arise from body, speech, and mind. That offense which is without remainder is not settled by any legal issue, nor in any place, nor by any means of settlement. That offense which is grave is settled by one legal issue—a legal issue concerning a duty; in one place—in the midst of the Saṅgha; by two means of settlement—by the procedure in the presence and by the act of acknowledgment. Those offenses which are minor are settled by one legal issue—a legal issue concerning a duty; in three places—in the midst of the Saṅgha, in the midst of a group, or in the presence of an individual; by three means of settlement—either by the procedure in the presence and by the act of acknowledgment, or by the procedure in the presence and by the covering over with grass.

5. Adhikaraṇādhippāyo

5. The Meaning of the Legal Issues

348. Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ hoti anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti kiccādhikaraṇaṃ. Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ na hoti anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, na hoti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, na hoti kiccādhikaraṇaṃ; api [T 0.0381] ca, vivādādhikaraṇapaccayā hoti anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti kiccādhikaraṇaṃ. Yathā kathaṃ viya? cūḷava. 215; pari. 314 Idha bhikkhū vivadanti – dhammoti vā adhammoti vā duṭṭhullāpattīti vā aduṭṭhullāpattīti vā. Yaṃ tattha bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo nānāvādo aññathāvādo vipaccatāya vohāro medhakaṃ, idaṃ vuccati vivādādhikaraṇaṃ. Vivādādhikaraṇe saṅgho vivadati vivādādhikaraṇaṃ. Vivadamāno anuvadati anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ. Anuvadamāno āpattiṃ āpajjati āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Tāya āpattiyā saṅgho kammaṃ karoti kiccādhikaraṇaṃ. Evaṃ vivādādhikaraṇapaccayā hoti anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti kiccādhikaraṇaṃ.

348. Is a legal issue of dispute a legal issue of accusation, a legal issue of offense, and a legal issue of duties? A legal issue of dispute is not a legal issue of accusation, is not a legal issue of offense, and is not a legal issue of duties; and yet, conditioned by a legal issue of dispute, there arises a legal issue of accusation, a legal issue of offense, and a legal issue of duties. How so? Here, monks dispute—whether it is Dhamma or not-Dhamma ... or a grave offense or not a grave offense. Whatever quarreling, contention, strife, dispute, differing opinions, contrary statements, speech for the sake of mental distress, or escalated quarreling there is—this is called a legal issue of dispute. Regarding a legal issue of dispute, the Saṅgha disputes, which becomes a legal issue of dispute. While disputing, one accuses, which becomes a legal issue of accusation. While accusing, one incurs an offense, which becomes a legal issue of offense. For that offense, the Saṅgha performs a formal act, which becomes a legal issue of duties. Thus, conditioned by a legal issue of dispute, there arises a legal issue of accusation, a legal issue of offense, and a legal issue of duties.

Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ [M 0.0271][V 0.0293] hoti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti kiccādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti vivādādhikaraṇaṃ. Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ na hoti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, na hoti kiccādhikaraṇaṃ, na hoti vivādādhikaraṇaṃ; api ca, anuvādādhikaraṇapaccayā hoti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti kiccādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti vivādādhikaraṇaṃ. Yathā kathaṃ viya? Idha bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ anuvadanti sīlavipattiyā vā ācāravipattiyā vā diṭṭhivipattiyā vā ājīvavipattiyā vā. Yo tattha anuvādo anuvadanā anullapanā anubhaṇanā anusampavaṅkatā abbhussahanatā anubalappadānaṃ, idaṃ vuccati anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ. Anuvādādhikaraṇe saṅgho vivadati, vivādādhikaraṇaṃ. Vivadamāno anuvadati, anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ. Anuvadamāno āpattiṃ āpajjati, āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Tāya āpattiyā saṅgho kammaṃ karoti, kiccādhikaraṇaṃ. Evaṃ anuvādādhikaraṇapaccayā hoti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti kiccādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti vivādādhikaraṇaṃ.

Is a legal issue of accusation a legal issue of offense, a legal issue of duties, and a legal issue of dispute? A legal issue of accusation is not a legal issue of offense, is not a legal issue of duties, and is not a legal issue of dispute; and yet, conditioned by a legal issue of accusation, there arises a legal issue of offense, a legal issue of duties, and a legal issue of dispute. How so? Here, monks accuse a monk of a lapse in virtue, a lapse in conduct, a lapse in view, or a lapse in livelihood. Whatever accusation, act of accusing, speaking disparagingly, faultfinding, persistence, making a charge, or giving of support there is—this is called a legal issue of accusation. Regarding a legal issue of accusation, the Saṅgha disputes, which becomes a legal issue of dispute. While disputing, one accuses, which becomes a legal issue of accusation. While accusing, one incurs an offense, which becomes a legal issue of offense. For that offense, the Saṅgha performs a formal act, which becomes a legal issue of duties. Thus, conditioned by a legal issue of accusation, there arises a legal issue of offense, a legal issue of duties, and a legal issue of dispute.

Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ hoti kiccādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ. Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ na hoti kiccādhikaraṇaṃ, na hoti vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, na hoti anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ; api ca, āpattādhikaraṇapaccayā hoti kiccādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ. Yathā kathaṃ viya? cūḷava. 215; pari. 348 Pañcapi āpattikkhandhā āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, sattapi āpattikkhandhā āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, idaṃ vuccati āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Āpattādhikaraṇe saṅgho vivadati vivādādhikaraṇaṃ. Vivadamāno anuvadati anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ. Anuvadamāno āpattiṃ āpajjati āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Tāya āpattiyā saṅgho kammaṃ karoti kiccādhikaraṇaṃ. Evaṃ āpattādhikaraṇapaccayā hoti kiccādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ.

Is a legal issue of offense a legal issue of duties, a legal issue of dispute, and a legal issue of accusation? A legal issue of offense is not a legal issue of duties, is not a legal issue of dispute, and is not a legal issue of accusation; and yet, conditioned by a legal issue of offense, there arises a legal issue of duties, a legal issue of dispute, and a legal issue of accusation. How so? The five groups of offenses are a legal issue of offense, and the seven groups of offenses are a legal issue of offense; this is called a legal issue of offense. Regarding a legal issue of offense, the Saṅgha disputes, which becomes a legal issue of dispute. While disputing, one accuses, which becomes a legal issue of accusation. While accusing, one incurs an offense, which becomes a legal issue of offense. For that offense, the Saṅgha performs a formal act, which becomes a legal issue of duties. Thus, conditioned by a legal issue of offense, there arises a legal issue of duties, a legal issue of dispute, and a legal issue of accusation.

Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ hoti vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ na hoti vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, na hoti anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, na hoti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ; api ca, kiccādhikaraṇapaccayā hoti vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti [T 0.0383] āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Yathā kathaṃ viya? Yā saṅghassa kiccayatā karaṇīyatā apalokanakammaṃ ñattikammaṃ ñattidutiyakammaṃ ñatticatutthakammaṃ, idaṃ [M 0.0272] vuccati kiccādhikaraṇaṃ. Kiccādhikaraṇe saṅgho vivadati vivādādhikaraṇaṃ. Vivadamāno anuvadati anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ. Anuvadamāno āpattiṃ āpajjati āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Tāya āpattiyā saṅgho kammaṃ karoti kiccādhikaraṇaṃ. Evaṃ kiccādhikaraṇapaccayā hoti vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, hoti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ.

Is a legal issue of duties a legal issue of dispute, a legal issue of accusation, and a legal issue of offense? A legal issue of duties is not a legal issue of dispute, is not a legal issue of accusation, and is not a legal issue of offense; and yet, conditioned by a legal issue of duties, there arises a legal issue of dispute, a legal issue of accusation, and a legal issue of offense. How so? Whatever is the Saṅgha’s duty, what ought to be done—a formal act by announcement, a formal act by motion, a formal act by motion and one proclamation, or a formal act by motion and three proclamations—this is called a legal issue of duties. Regarding a legal issue of duties, the Saṅgha disputes, which becomes a legal issue of dispute. While disputing, one accuses, which becomes a legal issue of accusation. While accusing, one incurs an offense, which becomes a legal issue of offense. For that offense, the Saṅgha performs a formal act, which becomes a legal issue of duties. Thus, conditioned by a legal issue of duties, there arises a legal issue of dispute, a legal issue of accusation, and a legal issue of offense.

6. Pucchāvāro

6. The Section on Questions

349. Yattha [V 0.0294] sativinayo tattha sammukhāvinayo? Yattha sammukhāvinayo [P 5.0155] tattha sativinayo? Yattha amūḷhavinayo tattha sammukhāvinayo? Yattha sammukhāvinayo tattha amūḷhavinayo? Yattha paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ tattha sammukhāvinayo? Yattha sammukhāvinayo tattha paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ? Yattha yebhuyyasikā tattha sammukhāvinayo? Yattha sammukhāvinayo tattha yebhuyyasikā? Yattha tassapāpiyasikā tattha sammukhāvinayo? Yattha sammukhāvinayo tattha tassapāpiyasikā? Yattha tiṇavatthārako tattha sammukhāvinayo? Yattha sammukhāvinayo tattha tiṇavatthārako?

349. Where there is the settlement by mindfulness, is there the settlement in the presence of? Where there is the settlement in the presence of, is there the settlement by mindfulness? Where there is the settlement for one of sound mind, is there the settlement in the presence of? Where there is the settlement in the presence of, is there the settlement for one of sound mind? Where there is the settlement by acknowledgement, is there the settlement in the presence of? Where there is the settlement in the presence of, is there the settlement by acknowledgement? Where there is the settlement by majority vote, is there the settlement in the presence of? Where there is the settlement in the presence of, is there the settlement by majority vote? Where there is the settlement for a particularly wicked person, is there the settlement in the presence of? Where there is the settlement in the presence of, is there the settlement for a particularly wicked person? Where there is the settlement of covering over with grass, is there the settlement in the presence of? Where there is the settlement in the presence of, is there the settlement of covering over with grass?

7. Vissajjanāvāro

7. The Section on Elucidation

350. Yasmiṃ samaye sammukhāvinayena ca sativinayena ca adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati – yattha sativinayo tattha sammukhāvinayo, yattha sammukhāvinayo tattha sativinayo, na tattha amūḷhavinayo, na tattha [T 0.0384] paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ, na tattha yebhuyyasikā, na tattha tassapāpiyasikā, na tattha tiṇavatthārako. Yasmiṃ samaye sammukhāvinayena ca amūḷhavinayena ca…pe… sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca…pe… sammukhāvinayena ca yebhuyyasikāya ca…pe… sammukhāvinayena ca tassapāpiyasikāya ca…pe… sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati – yattha tiṇavatthārako tattha sammukhāvinayo, yattha sammukhāvinayo tattha tiṇavatthārako, na tattha sativinayo, na tattha amūḷhavinayo, na tattha paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ, na tattha yebhuyyasikā, na tattha tassapāpiyasikā.

350. At a time when a legal case is settled by the settlement in the presence and by the settlement by mindfulness—where there is the settlement by mindfulness, there is the settlement in the presence; where there is the settlement in the presence, there is the settlement by mindfulness; there is not the settlement for one of sound mind, nor the settlement by acknowledgement, nor the settlement by majority vote, nor the settlement for a particularly wicked person, nor the settlement of covering over with grass. At a time when a legal case is settled by the settlement in the presence and by the settlement for one of sound mind… by the settlement in the presence and by the settlement by acknowledgement… by the settlement in the presence and by the settlement by majority vote… by the settlement in the presence and by the settlement for a particularly wicked person… by the settlement in the presence and by the settlement of covering over with grass—where there is the settlement of covering over with grass, there is the settlement in the presence; where there is the settlement in the presence, there is the settlement of covering over with grass; there is not the settlement by mindfulness, nor the settlement for one of sound mind, nor the settlement by acknowledgement, nor the settlement by majority vote, nor the settlement for a particularly wicked person.

8. Saṃsaṭṭhavāro

8. The Section on Association

351. Sammukhāvinayoti vā sativinayoti vā – ime dhammā saṃsaṭṭhā udāhu visaṃsaṭṭhā? Labbhā ca panimesaṃ dhammānaṃ vinibbhujitvā vinibbhujitvā nānākaraṇaṃ [M 0.0273] paññāpetuṃ? Sammukhāvinayoti vā amūḷhavinayoti vā…pe… sammukhāvinayoti vā paṭiññātakaraṇanti vā… sammukhāvinayoti vā yebhuyyasikāti vā… sammukhāvinayoti vā tassapāpiyasikāti vā… sammukhāvinayoti vā tiṇavatthārakoti – ime dhammā saṃsaṭṭhā udāhu visaṃsaṭṭhā[V 0.0295]? Labbhā ca panimesaṃ dhammānaṃ vinibbhujitvā vinibbhujitvā nānākaraṇaṃ paññāpetuṃ?

351. The settlement in the presence, or the settlement by mindfulness—are these phenomena associated or dissociated? And is it possible, having repeatedly separated these phenomena, to declare a distinction between them? The settlement in the presence, or the settlement for one of sound mind… The settlement in the presence, or the settlement by acknowledgement… The settlement in the presence, or the settlement by majority vote… The settlement in the presence, or the settlement for a particularly wicked person… The settlement in the presence, or the settlement of covering over with grass—are these phenomena associated or dissociated? And is it possible, having repeatedly separated these phenomena, to declare a distinction between them?

Sammukhāvinayoti vā sativinayoti vā – ime dhammā saṃsaṭṭhā, no visaṃsaṭṭhā; na ca labbhā imesaṃ dhammānaṃ vinibbhujitvā vinibbhujitvā nānākaraṇaṃ paññāpetuṃ. Sammukhāvinayoti vā amūḷhavinayoti [T 0.0385] vā…pe… sammukhāvinayoti vā paṭiññātakaraṇanti vā… sammukhāvinayoti vā yebhuyyasikāti vā… sammukhāvinayoti vā tassapāpiyasikāti vā… sammukhāvinayoti vā tiṇavatthārakoti vā – ime dhammā saṃsaṭṭhā, no visaṃsaṭṭhā; na ca labbhā imesaṃ dhammānaṃ vinibbhujitvā vinibbhujitvā nānākaraṇaṃ paññāpetuṃ.

The settlement in the presence, or the settlement by mindfulness—these phenomena are associated, not dissociated; and it is not possible, having repeatedly separated these phenomena, to declare a distinction between them. The settlement in the presence, or the settlement for one of sound mind… The settlement in the presence, or the settlement by acknowledgement… The settlement in the presence, or the settlement by majority vote… The settlement in the presence, or the settlement for a particularly wicked person… The settlement in the presence, or the settlement of covering over with grass—these phenomena are associated, not dissociated; and it is not possible, having repeatedly separated these phenomena, to declare a distinction between them.

9. Sattasamathanidānaṃ

9. The Origin of the Seven Settlements

352. Sammukhāvinayo kiṃnidāno, kiṃsamudayo, kiṃjātiko, kiṃpabhavo, kiṃsambhāro kiṃsamuṭṭhāno? Sativinayo kiṃnidāno, kiṃsamudayo, kiṃjātiko, kiṃpabhavo, kiṃsambhāro, kiṃsamuṭṭhāno? Amūḷhavinayo kiṃnidāno, kiṃsamudayo, kiṃjātiko, kiṃpabhavo, kiṃsambhāro, kiṃsamuṭṭhāno? Paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ kiṃnidānaṃ, kiṃsamudayaṃ, kiṃjātikaṃ, kiṃpabhavaṃ, kiṃsambhāraṃ, kiṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ? Yebhuyyasikā kiṃnidānā, kiṃsamudayā, kiṃjātikā, kiṃpabhavā, kiṃsambhārā, kiṃsamuṭṭhānā? Tassapāpiyasikā kiṃnidānā, kiṃsamudayā, kiṃjātikā, kiṃpabhavā, kiṃsambhārā, kiṃsamuṭṭhānā tiṇavatthārako kiṃnidāno, kiṃsamudayo, kiṃjātiko, kiṃpabhavo, kiṃsambhāro, kiṃsamuṭṭhāno?

352. The settlement in the presence: what is its source, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its provenance, what are its requisites, what is its arising? The settlement by mindfulness: what is its source, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its provenance, what are its requisites, what is its arising? The settlement for one of sound mind: what is its source, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its provenance, what are its requisites, what is its arising? The settlement by acknowledgement: what is its source, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its provenance, what are its requisites, what is its arising? The settlement by majority vote: what is its source, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its provenance, what are its requisites, what is its arising? The settlement for a particularly wicked person: what is its source, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its provenance, what are its requisites, what is its arising? The settlement of covering over with grass: what is its source, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its provenance, what are its requisites, what is its arising?

Sammukhāvinayo nidānanidāno, nidānasamudayo, nidānajātiko, nidānapabhavo, nidānasambhāro, nidānasamuṭṭhāno. Sativinayo…pe… amūḷhavinayo…pe… paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ nidānanidānaṃ, nidānasamudayaṃ, nidānajātikaṃ, nidānapabhavaṃ, nidānasambhāraṃ, nidānasamuṭṭhānaṃ. Yebhuyyasikā…pe… tassapāpiyasikā nidānanidānā, nidānasamudayā, nidānajātikā, nidānapabhavā, nidānasambhārā[M 0.0274], nidānasamuṭṭhānā. Tiṇavatthārako nidānanidāno, nidānasamudayo, nidānajātiko, nidānapabhavo, nidānasambhāro, nidānasamuṭṭhāno.

The settlement in the presence has a source as its source, has a source as its origin, has a source as its birth, has a source as its provenance, has a source as its requisites, and has a source as its arising. The settlement by mindfulness… and so on… the settlement for one of sound mind… and so on… The settlement by acknowledgement has a source as its source, has a source as its origin, has a source as its birth, has a source as its provenance, has a source as its requisites, and has a source as its arising. The settlement by majority vote… and so on… the settlement for a particularly wicked person has a source as its source, has a source as its origin, has a source as its birth, has a source as its provenance, has a source as its requisites, and has a source as its arising. The settlement of covering over with grass has a source as its source, has a source as its origin, has a source as its birth, has a source as its provenance, has a source as its requisites, and has a source as its arising.

Sammukhāvinayo [P 5.0156] kiṃnidāno, kiṃsamudayo, kiṃjātiko, kiṃpabhavo, kiṃsambhāro, kiṃsamuṭṭhāno[V 0.0296]? Sativinayo…pe… amūḷhavinayo…pe… paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ…pe… yebhuyyasikā…pe… tassapāpiyasikā…pe… tiṇavatthārako kiṃnidāno, kiṃsamudayo, kiṃjātiko, kiṃpabhavo, kiṃsambhāro, kiṃsamuṭṭhāno?

The settlement in the presence: what is its source, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its provenance, what are its requisites, what is its arising? The settlement by mindfulness… and so on… the settlement for one of sound mind… and so on… the settlement by acknowledgement… and so on… the settlement by majority vote… and so on… the settlement for a particularly wicked person… and so on… The settlement of covering over with grass: what is its source, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its provenance, what are its requisites, what is its arising?

Sammukhāvinayo hetunidāno, hetusamudayo, hetujātiko, hetupabhavo, hetusambhāro, hetusamuṭṭhāno[T 0.0386]. Sativinayo…pe… amūḷhavinayo…pe… paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ hetunidānaṃ, hetusamudayaṃ, hetujātikaṃ, hetupabhavaṃ, hetusambhāraṃ, hetusamuṭṭhānaṃ. Yebhuyyasikā…pe… tassapāpiyasikā hetunidānā, hetusamudayā, hetujātikā, hetupabhavā, hetusambhārā, hetusamuṭṭhānā. Tiṇavatthārako hetunidāno, hetusamudayo, hetujātiko, hetupabhavo, hetusambhāro, hetusamuṭṭhāno.

The settlement in the presence has a cause as its source, a cause as its origin, a cause as its birth, a cause as its provenance, a cause as its requisites, and a cause as its arising. The settlement by mindfulness… and so on… the settlement for one of sound mind… and so on… The settlement by acknowledgement has a cause as its source, a cause as its origin, a cause as its birth, a cause as its provenance, a cause as its requisites, and a cause as its arising. The settlement by majority vote… and so on… the settlement for a particularly wicked person has a cause as its source, a cause as its origin, a cause as its birth, a cause as its provenance, a cause as its requisites, and a cause as its arising. The settlement of covering over with grass has a cause as its source, a cause as its origin, a cause as its birth, a cause as its provenance, a cause as its requisites, and a cause as its arising.

Sammukhāvinayo kiṃnidāno, kiṃsamudayo, kiṃjātiko, kiṃpabhavo, kiṃsambhāro, kiṃsamuṭṭhāno? Sativinayo…pe… amūḷhavinayo…pe… paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ…pe… yebhuyyasikā…pe… tassapāpiyasikā…pe… tiṇavatthārako kiṃnidāno, kiṃsamudayo, kiṃjātiko, kiṃpabhavo, kiṃsambhāro, kiṃsamuṭṭhāno? Sammukhāvinayo paccayanidāno, paccayasamudayo, paccayajātiko, paccayapabhavo, paccayasambhāro, paccayasamuṭṭhāno. Sativinayo…pe… amūḷhavinayo…pe… paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ paccayanidānaṃ, paccayasamudayaṃ, paccayajātikaṃ, paccayapabhavaṃ, paccayasambhāraṃ, paccayasamuṭṭhānaṃ. Yebhuyyasikā…pe… tassapāpiyasikā paccayanidānā, paccayasamudayā, paccayajātikā, paccayapabhavā, paccayasambhārā, paccayasamuṭṭhānā. Tiṇavatthārako paccayanidāno, paccayasamudayo, paccayajātiko, paccayapabhavo, paccayasambhāro, paccayasamuṭṭhāno.

The settlement of adjudication in the presence: what is its source, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its provenance, what are its constituents, what is its emergence? The settlement of adjudication by mindfulness… and so on… the settlement of adjudication for non-delusion… and so on… the settlement of adjudication by acknowledgement… and so on… the settlement of adjudication by majority… and so on… the settlement of adjudication for bad character… and so on… The settlement of adjudication by covering over with grass: what is its source, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its provenance, what are its constituents, what is its emergence? The settlement of adjudication in the presence has a condition as its source, a condition as its origin, a condition as its birth, a condition as its provenance, a condition as its constituents, and a condition as its emergence. The settlement of adjudication by mindfulness… and so on… the settlement of adjudication for non-delusion… and so on… the settlement of adjudication by acknowledgement has a condition as its source, a condition as its origin, a condition as its birth, a condition as its provenance, a condition as its constituents, and a condition as its emergence. The settlement of adjudication by majority… and so on… the settlement of adjudication for bad character has a condition as its source, a condition as its origin, a condition as its birth, a condition as its provenance, a condition as its constituents, and a condition as its emergence. The settlement of adjudication by covering over with grass has a condition as its source, a condition as its origin, a condition as its birth, a condition as its provenance, a condition as its constituents, and a condition as its emergence.

353. Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ kati mūlāni, kati samuṭṭhānā? Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ chabbīsa mūlāni, chattiṃsa samuṭṭhānā. Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katamāni chabbī [M 0.0275] mūlāni? Sammukhāvinayassa cattāri mūlāni. Saṅghasammukhatā, dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā, puggalasammukhatā; sativinayassa cattāri mūlāni; amūḷhavinayassa cattāri mūlāni; paṭiññātakaraṇassa dve mūlāni – yo ca deseti yassa ca deseti; yebhuyyasikāya cattāri mūlāni; tassapāpiyasikāya cattāri [T 0.0387] mūlāni; tiṇavatthārakassa cattāri mūlāni – saṅghasammukhatā, dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā, puggalasammukhatā – sattannaṃ samathānaṃ imāni chabbīsa mūlāni.

353. Of the seven settlements of adjudication, how many roots and how many origins are there? The seven settlements of adjudication have twenty-six roots and thirty-six origins. Of the seven settlements of adjudication, what are the twenty-six roots? The settlement of adjudication in the presence has four roots: the presence of the Saṅgha, the presence of the Dhamma, the presence of the Vinaya, and the presence of the individual. The settlement of adjudication by mindfulness has four roots. The settlement of adjudication for non-delusion has four roots. The settlement of adjudication by acknowledgement has two roots: the one who confesses and the one to whom confession is made. The settlement of adjudication by majority has four roots. The settlement of adjudication for bad character has four roots. The settlement of adjudication by covering over with grass has four roots: the presence of the Saṅgha, the presence of the Dhamma, the presence of the Vinaya, and the presence of the individual. These are the twenty-six roots of the seven settlements of adjudication.

Sattannaṃ [V 0.0297] samathānaṃ katame chattiṃsa samuṭṭhānā? Sativinayassa kammassa kiriyā, karaṇaṃ, upagamanaṃ, ajjhupagamanaṃ, adhivāsanā, appaṭikkosanā. Amūḷhavinayassa kammassa…pe… paṭiññātakaraṇassa kammassa… yebhuyyasikāya kammassa… tassapāpiyasikāya kammassa… tiṇavatthārakassa kammassa kiriyā, karaṇaṃ, upagamanaṃ, ajjhupagamanaṃ, adhivāsanā, appaṭikkosanā – sattannaṃ samathānaṃ ime chattiṃsa samuṭṭhānā.

Of the seven settlements of adjudication, what are the thirty-six origins? For the formal act of the settlement of adjudication by mindfulness: performance, execution, undertaking, consenting, acceptance, and non-rejection. For the formal act of the settlement of adjudication for non-delusion… and so on… for the formal act of the settlement of adjudication by acknowledgement… for the formal act of the settlement of adjudication by majority… for the formal act of the settlement of adjudication for bad character… for the formal act of the settlement of adjudication by covering over with grass: performance, execution, undertaking, consenting, acceptance, and non-rejection. These are the thirty-six origins of the seven settlements of adjudication.

10. Sattasamathanānatthādi

10. The Diversity of the Seven Settlements, etc.

354. Sammukhāvinayoti vā sativinayoti vā – ime dhammā nānatthā nānābyañjanā udāhu ekatthā byañjanameva nānaṃ? Sammukhāvinayoti vā amūḷhavinayoti vā…pe… sammukhāvinayoti vā paṭiññātakaraṇanti vā… sammukhāvinayoti vā yebhuyyasikāti vā… sammukhāvinayoti vā tassapāpiyasikāti vā… sammukhāvinayoti vā tiṇavatthārakoti vā – ime dhammā nānatthā nānābyañjanā udāhu ekatthā byañjanameva nānaṃ? Sammukhāvinayoti vā sativinayoti vā – ime dhammā nānatthā ceva nānābyañjanā ca. Sammukhāvinayoti vā amūḷhavinayoti vā…pe… sammukhāvinayoti vā paṭiññātakaraṇanti vā… sammukhāvinayoti vā yebhuyyasikāti vā… sammukhāvinayoti vā tassapāpiyasikāti vā… sammukhāvinayoti vā [T 0.0388] tiṇavatthārakoti vā – ime dhammā nānatthā ceva nānā byañjanā ca.

354. ‘Settlement of adjudication in the presence’ or ‘settlement of adjudication by mindfulness’—are these terms different in meaning and different in phrasing, or are they the same in meaning and only different in phrasing? ‘Settlement of adjudication in the presence’ or ‘settlement of adjudication for non-delusion’… and so on… ‘Settlement of adjudication in the presence’ or ‘settlement of adjudication by acknowledgement’… ‘Settlement of adjudication in the presence’ or ‘settlement of adjudication by majority’… ‘Settlement of adjudication in the presence’ or ‘settlement of adjudication for bad character’… ‘Settlement of adjudication in the presence’ or ‘settlement of adjudication by covering over with grass’—are these terms different in meaning and different in phrasing, or are they the same in meaning and only different in phrasing? ‘Settlement of adjudication in the presence’ or ‘settlement of adjudication by mindfulness’—these terms are both different in meaning and different in phrasing. ‘Settlement of adjudication in the presence’ or ‘settlement of adjudication for non-delusion’… and so on… ‘Settlement of adjudication in the presence’ or ‘settlement of adjudication by acknowledgement’… ‘Settlement of adjudication in the presence’ or ‘settlement of adjudication by majority’… ‘Settlement of adjudication in the presence’ or ‘settlement of adjudication for bad character’… ‘Settlement of adjudication in the presence’ or ‘settlement of adjudication by covering over with grass’—these terms are both different in meaning and different in phrasing.

355. cūḷava. 224 Vivādo [P 5.0157] vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, vivādo no adhikaraṇaṃ, adhikaraṇaṃ no vivādo, adhikaraṇañceva vivādo ca? Siyā vivādo vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, siyā vivādo no adhikaraṇaṃ, siyā adhikaraṇaṃ no vivādo, siyā adhikaraṇañceva vivādo ca.

355. Is a dispute a legal issue concerning a dispute? Is a dispute not a legal issue? Is a legal issue not a dispute? Is it both a legal issue and a dispute? It may be that a dispute is a legal issue concerning a dispute; it may be that a dispute is not a legal issue; it may be that a legal issue is not a dispute; it may be that it is both a legal issue and a dispute.

Tattha [M 0.0276] katamo vivādo vivādādhikaraṇaṃ? Idha bhikkhū vivadanti dhammoti vā adhammoti vā…pe… duṭṭhullā āpattīti vā aduṭṭhullā āpattīti vā. Yaṃ tattha bhaṇḍanaṃ, kalaho, viggaho, vivādo, nānāvādo, aññathāvādo, vipaccatāya vohāro, medhakaṃ – ayaṃ vivādo vivādādhikaraṇaṃ.

Herein, what dispute is a legal issue concerning a dispute? Here, monks dispute: ‘This is Dhamma,’ or ‘This is not Dhamma’… and so on… ‘This is a grave offense,’ or ‘This is not a grave offense.’ Whatever quarreling, contention, strife, dispute, differing opinions, opposing views, vexatious speech, or brawling there is—this dispute is a legal issue concerning a dispute.

Tattha katamo vivādo no adhikaraṇaṃ? Mātāpi puttena vivadati, puttopi mātarā vivadati, pitāpi puttena vivadati, puttopi pitarā vivadati, bhātāpi bhātarā vivadati, bhātāpi [V 0.0298] bhaginiyā vivadati, bhaginīpi bhātarā vivadati, sahāyopi sahāyena vivadati – ayaṃ vivādo no adhikaraṇaṃ.

Herein, what dispute is not a legal issue? A mother disputes with her son, and a son disputes with his mother; a father disputes with his son, and a son disputes with his father; a brother disputes with his brother; a brother disputes with his sister, and a sister disputes with her brother; a friend disputes with a friend—this dispute is not a legal issue.

Tattha katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ no vivādo? Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, kiccādhikaraṇaṃ – idaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ no vivādo.

Herein, what legal issue is not a dispute? A legal issue concerning an accusation, a legal issue concerning an offense, and a legal issue concerning a formal act—this is a legal issue that is not a dispute.

Tattha katamaṃ adhikaraṇañceva vivādo ca? Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ adhikaraṇañceva vivādo ca.

Herein, what is both a legal issue and a dispute? A legal issue concerning a dispute is both a legal issue and a dispute.

356. cūḷava. 224 ādayo Anuvādo anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, anuvādo no adhikaraṇaṃ, adhikaraṇaṃ no anuvādo, adhikaraṇañceva anuvādo ca? Siyā anuvādo [T 0.0389] anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, siyā anuvādo no adhikaraṇaṃ, siyā adhikaraṇaṃ no anuvādo, siyā adhikaraṇañceva anuvādo ca.

356. Is an accusation a legal issue concerning an accusation? Is an accusation not a legal issue? Is a legal issue not an accusation? Is it both a legal issue and an accusation? It may be that an accusation is a legal issue concerning an accusation; it may be that an accusation is not a legal issue; it may be that a legal issue is not an accusation; it may be that it is both a legal issue and an accusation.

Tattha katamo anuvādo anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ? Idha bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ anuvadanti sīlavipattiyā vā ācāravipattiyā vā diṭṭhivipattiyā vā ājīvavipattiyā vā. Yo tattha anuvādo, anuvadanā anullapanā anubhaṇanā anusampavaṅkatā abbhussahanatā anubalappadānaṃ – ayaṃ anuvādo anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ.

Herein, what accusation is a legal issue concerning an accusation? Here, monks accuse a monk of a failure in virtue, or a failure in conduct, or a failure in view, or a failure in livelihood. Whatever therein is an accusation, a speaking against, a repeated telling, a recounting, a devious insinuation, an undertaking, or a giving of support—this accusation is a legal issue concerning an accusation.

Tattha katamo anuvādo no adhikaraṇaṃ? Mātāpi puttaṃ anuvadati, puttopi mātaraṃ anuvadati, pitāpi puttaṃ anuvadati, puttopi pitaraṃ anuvadati, bhātāpi bhātaraṃ anuvadati, bhātāpi bhaginiṃ anuvadati, bhaginīpi bhātaraṃ anuvadati, sahāyopi sahāyaṃ anuvadati – ayaṃ anuvādo no adhikaraṇaṃ.

Herein, which accusation is not a legal issue? A mother accuses her son, and a son accuses his mother; a father accuses his son, and a son accuses his father; a brother accuses his brother, a brother accuses his sister, and a sister accuses her brother; a friend accuses a friend. This accusation is not a legal issue.

Tattha katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ no anuvādo? Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ kiccādhikaraṇaṃ vivādādhikaraṇaṃ – idaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ no anuvādo.

Herein, which legal issue is not an accusation? The legal issue concerning an offense, the legal issue concerning a duty, and the legal issue concerning a dispute. This is a legal issue that is not an accusation.

Tattha [M 0.0277] katamaṃ adhikaraṇañceva anuvādo ca? Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ adhikaraṇañceva anuvādo ca.

Herein, which is both a legal issue and an accusation? The legal issue concerning an accusation is both a legal issue and an accusation.

357. Āpatti [V 0.0299] āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, āpatti no adhikaraṇaṃ, adhikaraṇaṃ no āpatti, adhikaraṇañceva āpatti ca? Siyā āpatti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, siyā āpatti no adhikaraṇaṃ, siyā adhikaraṇaṃ no āpatti, siyā adhikaraṇañceva āpatti ca.

357. Is an offense a legal issue concerning an offense? Is an offense not a legal issue? Is a legal issue not an offense? Is it both a legal issue and an offense? In some cases, an offense is a legal issue concerning an offense. In some cases, an offense is not a legal issue. In some cases, a legal issue is not an offense. In some cases, it is both a legal issue and an offense.

Tattha katamā āpatti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ? Pañcapi āpattikkhandhā āpattādhikaraṇaṃ[T 0.0390]. Sattapi āpattikkhandhā āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Ayaṃ āpatti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ.

Among these, which offense is a legal issue concerning an offense? The five groups of offenses are a legal issue concerning an offense. The seven groups of offenses are a legal issue concerning an offense. This offense is a legal issue concerning an offense.

Tattha katamā āpatti no adhikaraṇaṃ? Sotāpatti samāpatti – ayaṃ āpatti no adhikaraṇaṃ.

Among these, which offense is not a legal issue? The attainment of stream-entry—this attainment is not a legal issue.

Tattha katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ no āpatti? Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ vivādādhikaraṇaṃ anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ – idaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ no āpatti.

Among these, which legal issue is not an offense? A legal issue concerning duties, a legal issue concerning disputes, and a legal issue concerning accusations—this is a legal issue that is not an offense.

Tattha katamaṃ adhikaraṇañceva āpatti ca? Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ adhikaraṇañceva āpatti ca.

Among these, what is both a legal issue and an offense? A legal issue concerning an offense is both a legal issue and an offense.

358. cūḷava. 223 Kiccaṃ kiccādhikaraṇaṃ, kiccaṃ no adhikaraṇaṃ, adhikaraṇaṃ no kiccaṃ, adhikaraṇañceva kiccañca? Siyā kiccaṃ kiccādhikaraṇaṃ, siyā kiccaṃ no adhikaraṇaṃ, siyā adhikaraṇaṃ no kiccaṃ, siyā adhikaraṇañceva kiccañca.

358. Is a duty a legal issue concerning a duty? Is a duty not a legal issue? Is a legal issue not a duty? Is it both a legal issue and a duty? In some cases, a duty is a legal issue concerning a duty. In some cases, a duty is not a legal issue. In some cases, a legal issue is not a duty. In some cases, it is both a legal issue and a duty.

Tattha katamaṃ kiccaṃ kiccādhikaraṇaṃ? Yā saṅghassa kiccayatā karaṇīyatā apalokanakammaṃ ñattikammaṃ ñattidutiyakammaṃ ñatticatutthakammaṃ – idaṃ kiccaṃ kiccādhikaraṇaṃ.

Among these, which duty is a legal issue concerning a duty? Whatever is the duty of the Sangha, what is to be done—the act of seeking approval, a motion, a motion with one announcement, a motion with three announcements—this duty is a legal issue concerning a duty.

Tattha katamaṃ kiccaṃ no adhikaraṇaṃ? Ācariyakiccaṃ upajjhāyakiccaṃ upajjhāyakiccaṃ sakiccaṃ (ka.) samānupajjhāyakiccaṃ samānācariyakiccaṃ – idaṃ kiccaṃ no adhikaraṇaṃ.

Among these, which duty is not a legal issue? The duty of a teacher, the duty of a preceptor, the duty of one who has the same preceptor, the duty of one who has the same teacher—this duty is not a legal issue.

Tattha katamaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ no kiccaṃ? Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ āpattādhikaraṇaṃ – idaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ no kiccaṃ.

Among these, which legal issue is not a duty? A legal issue concerning disputes, a legal issue concerning accusations, and a legal issue concerning offenses—this legal issue is not a duty.

Tattha [M 0.0278][V 0.0300] katamaṃ adhikaraṇañceva kiccañca? Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ adhikaraṇañceva kiccaṃ cāti.

Among these, what is both a legal issue and a duty? A legal issue concerning a duty is both a legal issue and a duty.

Adhikaraṇabhedo niṭṭhito.

The Analysis of Legal Issues is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Adhikaraṇaṃ [T 0.0391] ukkoṭā, ākārā puggalena ca;

Nidānahetupaccayā, mūlaṃ samuṭṭhānena ca.

Legal issue, overturning, manners, and persons; source, cause, and condition; root and origin.

Āpatti hoti yattha ca, saṃsaṭṭhā nidānena ca saṃsaṭṭhā nidānapabhavā (sī.);

Hetupaccayamūlāni, samuṭṭhānena byañjanā;

Vivādo adhikaraṇanti, bhedādhikaraṇe idanti.

Offense, whether it is a legal issue, and where; mixed, and with its source; causes, conditions, roots, origin, and phrasing; whether a dispute is a legal issue—this is the analysis of legal issues.

Aparagāthāsaṅgaṇikaṃ

The Collection of Subsequent Verses

1. Codanādipucchāvissajjanā

1. Questions and Answers on Accusation, etc.

359.

359.

Codanā [T 0.0392][P 5.0158][M 0.0279][V 0.0301] kimatthāya, sāraṇā kissa kāraṇā;

Saṅgho kimatthāya, matikammaṃ pana kissa kāraṇā.

For what purpose is accusation? For what reason is reminding? For what purpose is the assembly of the Saṅgha? And for what reason is deliberation?

Codanā sāraṇatthāya, niggahatthāya sāraṇā;

Saṅgho pariggahatthāya, matikammaṃ pana pāṭiyekkaṃ.

Accusation is for the purpose of reminding; reminding is for the purpose of restraint; the assembly of the Saṅgha is for the purpose of taking up the matter; and deliberation is for individual consideration.

Mā kho turito abhaṇi, mā kho caṇḍikato bhaṇi;

Mā kho paṭighaṃ janayi, sace anuvijjako tuvaṃ.

If you are an investigator, do not speak hastily, do not speak angrily, do not arouse animosity.

Mā kho sahasā abhaṇi, kathaṃ viggāhikaṃ anatthasaṃhitaṃ;

Sutte vinaye anulome, paññatte anulomike.

Do not speak rashly speech that is contentious and unbeneficial; in accordance with the Sutta, the Vinaya, the Anuloma, what has been laid down, and what is conformable.

Anuyogavattaṃ nisāmaya, kusalena buddhimatā kataṃ;

Suvuttaṃ sikkhāpadānulomikaṃ, gatiṃ na nāsento samparāyikaṃ;

Hitesī anuyuñjassu, kālenatthūpasaṃhitaṃ.

Heed the procedure for inquiry, established by the skillful and wise one; it is well-spoken and conforms to the training rules. Not destroying your future destination, heed the procedure for inquiry. Wishing for welfare, you should inquire at the proper time into what is connected with benefit.

Cuditassa ca codakassa ca;

Sahasā vohāraṃ mā padhāresi;

Codako āha āpannoti;

Cuditako āha anāpannoti.

Of both the accused and the accuser, do not rashly accept the statement. The accuser might say, 'You have committed an offense'; the accused might say, 'I have not committed an offense'.

Ubho [V 0.0302] anukkhipanto, paṭiññānusandhitena [T 0.0393] kāraye;

Paṭiññā lajjīsu katā, alajjīsu evaṃ na vijjati;

Bahumpi alajjī bhāseyya, vattānusandhitena vuttānusandhitena (sī. syā. ka.) kāraye.

Without siding with either, one should settle the matter through the sequence of admission. Among the conscientious, a decision is made by admission; among the shameless, it is not so. Since a shameless person might say many things, one should settle the matter by the sequence of their conduct.

Alajjī kīdiso hoti, paṭiññā yassa na rūhati;

Etañca evañca (ka.) tāhaṃ pucchāmi, kīdiso vuccati alajjī puggalo.

What is a shameless person like, whose admission does not take root? This I also ask you: what kind of person is called a shameless individual?

Sañcicca āpattiṃ āpajjati, āpattiṃ parigūhati;

Agatigamanañca gacchati, ediso vuccati alajjīpuggalo.

A person who intentionally commits an offense, conceals the offense, and goes on a wrong course—such a one is called a shameless individual.

Saccaṃ ahampi jānāmi, ediso vuccati alajjīpuggalo;

Aññañca tāhaṃ pucchāmi, kīdiso vuccati lajjīpuggalo.

Truly, I too know that such a one is called a shameless individual. And I ask you another question: what kind of person is called a conscientious individual?

Sañcicca āpattiṃ nāpajjati, āpattiṃ na parigūhati;

Agatigamanaṃ [T 0.0394] na gacchati, ediso vuccati lajjīpuggalo.

A person who does not intentionally commit an offense, does not conceal an offense, and does not go on a wrong course—such a one is called a conscientious individual.

Saccaṃ [M 0.0280] ahampi jānāmi, ediso vuccati lajjīpuggalo;

Aññañca tāhaṃ pucchāmi, kīdiso vuccati adhammacodako.

Truly, I too know that such a one is called a conscientious individual. And I ask you another question: what kind of person is called an unrighteous accuser?

Akāle [P 5.0159] codeti abhūtena;

Pharusena anatthasaṃhitena;

Dosantaro codeti no mettācitto;

Ediso vuccati adhammacodako.

One who accuses at an improper time, with what is untrue, harshly, with what is unbeneficial; who accuses with a mind of hatred, not with a mind of loving-kindness—such a one is called an unrighteous accuser.

Saccaṃ ahampi jānāmi, ediso vuccati adhammacodako;

Aññañca tāhaṃ pucchāmi, kīdiso vuccati dhammacodako.

Truly, I too know that such a one is called an unrighteous accuser. And I ask you another question: what kind of person is called a righteous accuser?

Kālena codeti bhūtena, saṇhena atthasaṃhitena;

Mettācitto codeti no dosantaro;

Ediso vuccati dhammacodako.

One who accuses at a suitable time, with what is true, gently, with what is connected to benefit; who accuses with a mind of loving-kindness, not with a mind of hatred—such a one is called a righteous accuser.

Saccaṃ [V 0.0303] ahampi jānāmi, ediso vuccati dhammacodako;

Aññañca tāhaṃ pucchāmi, kīdiso vuccati bālacodako.

Truly, I too know that such a one is called a righteous accuser. And I ask you another question: what kind of person is called a foolish accuser?

Pubbāparaṃ na jānāti, pubbāparassa akovido;

Anusandhivacanapathaṃ na jānāti;

Anusandhivacanapathassa akovido;

Ediso vuccati bālacodako.

One who does not know the preceding and subsequent speech and is unskilled in the preceding and subsequent speech; who does not know the way of connected speech and is unskilled in the way of connected speech—such a one is called a foolish accuser.

Saccaṃ ahampi jānāmi, ediso vuccati bālacodako;

Aññañca [T 0.0395] tāhaṃ pucchāmi, kīdiso vuccati paṇḍitacodako.

It is true, and I also know it, that such a person is called a foolish reprover. And I will ask you another matter: what kind of person is called a wise reprover?

Pubbāparampi jānāti, pubbāparassa kovido;

Anusandhivacanapathaṃ jānāti, anusandhivacanapathassa kovido;

Ediso vuccati paṇḍitacodako.

Upāli, a person who knows the preceding and subsequent speech and is skilled in the preceding and subsequent speech; who knows the way of connected speech and is skilled in the way of connected speech—such a person is called a wise reprover.

Saccaṃ ahampi jānāmi, ediso vuccati paṇḍitacodako;

Aññañca tāhaṃ pucchāmi, codanā kinti vuccati.

It is true, and I also know it, that such a person is called a wise reprover. And I will ask you another matter: why is it called 'reproof'?

Sīlavipattiyā codeti, atho ācāradiṭṭhiyā;

Ājīvenapi codeti, codanā tena vuccatīti.

Upāli, one reproves by a corruption of virtue; furthermore, by a corruption of conduct and view; one also reproves by a corruption of livelihood. For that reason, it is called 'reproof'.

Aparaṃ gāthāsaṅgaṇikaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The subsequent Gāthāsaṅgaṇika is concluded.

Codanākaṇḍaṃ

The Section on Reproof

1. Anuvijjakaanuyogo

1. The Investigator's Inquiry

360. Anuvijjake [T 0.0396][P 5.0160][M 0.0281][V 0.0304] codako pucchitabbo – “yaṃ kho tvaṃ, āvuso, imaṃ bhikkhuṃ codesi, kimhi naṃ codesi, sīlavipattiyā vā codesi, ācāravipattiyā vā codesi, diṭṭhivipattiyā vā codesī”ti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – “sīlavipattiyā vā codemi, ācāravipattiyā vā codemi, diṭṭhivipattiyā vā codemī”ti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “jānāsi panāyasmā sīlavipattiṃ, jānāsi ācāravipattiṃ, jānāsi diṭṭhivipatti”nti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – “jānāmi kho ahaṃ, āvuso, sīlavipattiṃ, jānāmi ācāravipattiṃ, jānāmi diṭṭhivipatti”nti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “katamā panāvuso, sīlavipatti? Katamā ācāravipatti? Katamā diṭṭhivipattī”ti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – “cattāri ca pārājikāni, terasa ca saṅghādisesā – ayaṃ sīlavipatti. Thullaccayaṃ, pācittiyaṃ, pāṭidesanīyaṃ, dukkaṭaṃ, dubbhāsitaṃ, ayaṃ ācāravipatti. Micchādiṭṭhi, antaggāhikā diṭṭhi – ayaṃ diṭṭhivipattī”ti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “yaṃ kho tvaṃ, āvuso, imaṃ bhikkhuṃ codesi, diṭṭhena vā codesi sutena vā codesi parisaṅkāya vā codesī”ti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – “diṭṭhena vā codemi sutena vā codemi parisaṅkāya vā codemī”ti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “yaṃ kho tvaṃ, āvuso, imaṃ bhikkhuṃ diṭṭhena codesi, kiṃ te diṭṭhaṃ kinti te diṭṭhaṃ, kadā [T 0.0397] te diṭṭhaṃ, kattha te diṭṭhaṃ pārājikaṃ ajjhāpajjanto diṭṭho, saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpajjanto diṭṭho, thullaccayaṃ… pācittiyaṃ… pāṭidesanīyaṃ… dukkaṭaṃ… dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpajjanto diṭṭho, kattha ca tvaṃ ahosi, kattha cāyaṃ bhikkhu ahosi, kiñca tvaṃ karosi, kiṃ cāyaṃ bhikkhu karotī”ti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – “na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, imaṃ bhikkhuṃ diṭṭhena codemi, api ca sutena codemī”ti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “yaṃ kho tvaṃ, āvuso, imaṃ bhikkhuṃ sutena codesi, kiṃ te sutaṃ, kinti te sutaṃ, kadā te sutaṃ[V 0.0305], kattha te sutaṃ, pārājikaṃ ajjhāpannoti sutaṃ, saṅghādisesaṃ… thullaccayaṃ… pācittiyaṃ… pāṭidesanīyaṃ… dukkaṭaṃ… dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpannoti sutaṃ, bhikkhussa sutaṃ, bhikkhuniyā sutaṃ, sikkhamānāya sutaṃ[M 0.0282], sāmaṇerassa sutaṃ, sāmaṇeriyā sutaṃ, upāsakassa sutaṃ, upāsikāya sutaṃ, rājūnaṃ sutaṃ, rājamahāmattānaṃ sutaṃ, titthiyānaṃ sutaṃ, titthiyasāvakānaṃ suta”nti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – “na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, imaṃ bhikkhuṃ sutena codemi, api ca parisaṅkāya codemī”ti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “yaṃ kho tvaṃ, āvuso, imaṃ bhikkhuṃ parisaṅkāya codesi, kiṃ parisaṅkasi, kinti parisaṅkasi, kadā parisaṅkasi, kattha parisaṅkasi, pārājikaṃ ajjhāpannoti [T 0.0398] parisaṅkasi, saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpannoti parisaṅkasi, thullaccayaṃ… pācittiyaṃ… pāṭidesanīyaṃ… dukkaṭaṃ… dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpannoti parisaṅkasi, bhikkhussa sutvā parisaṅkasi, bhikkhuniyā sutvā parisaṅkasi, sikkhamānāya sutvā parisaṅkasi, sāmaṇerassa sutvā parisaṅkasi, sāmaṇeriyā sutvā parisaṅkasi, upāsakassa sutvā parisaṅkasi, upāsikāya sutvā parisaṅkasi, rājūnaṃ sutvā parisaṅkasi, rājamahāmattānaṃ sutvā parisaṅkasi, titthiyānaṃ sutvā parisaṅkasi, titthiyasāvakānaṃ sutvā parisaṅkasī”ti?
