360. The accuser should be questioned by the investigator: “Friend, when you accuse this bhikkhu, for what fault do you accuse him? Do you accuse him of a corruption of virtue, or a corruption of conduct, or a corruption of view?” If he replies: “I accuse him of a corruption of virtue, or a corruption of conduct, or a corruption of view,” he should be told: “Venerable sir, do you know what a corruption of virtue is, what a corruption of conduct is, what a corruption of view is?” If he replies: “I know, friend, what a corruption of virtue is, what a corruption of conduct is, what a corruption of view is,” he should be told: “What, friend, is the corruption of virtue? What is the corruption of conduct? What is the corruption of view?” If he replies: “The four Pārājikas and the thirteen Saṅghādisesas—this is the corruption of virtue. The Thullaccaya, Pācittiya, Pāṭidesanīya, Dukkaṭa, and Dubbhāsita—this is the corruption of conduct. Wrong view and view holding to extremes—this is the corruption of view,” he should be told: “Friend, when you accuse this bhikkhu, do you accuse him based on what is seen, or on what is heard, or on suspicion?” If he replies: “I accuse him based on what is seen, or on what is heard, or on suspicion,” he should be told: “Friend, when you accuse this bhikkhu based on what is seen, what did you see? In what way did you see it? When did you see it? Where did you see it? Was he seen committing a Pārājika? Was he seen committing a Saṅghādisesa, a Thullaccaya… a Pācittiya… a Pāṭidesanīya… a Dukkaṭa… a Dubbhāsita? And where were you, and where was this bhikkhu? And what were you doing, and what was this bhikkhu doing?” If he replies: “Friend, I do not indeed accuse this bhikkhu based on what is seen, but rather on what is heard,” he should be told: “Friend, when you accuse this bhikkhu based on what is heard, what did you hear? In what way did you hear it? When did you hear it? Where did you hear it? Did you hear, ‘He has committed a Pārājika’? Did you hear, ‘He has committed a Saṅghādisesa… a Thullaccaya… a Pācittiya… a Pāṭidesanīya… a Dukkaṭa… a Dubbhāsita’? Did you hear it from a bhikkhu, a bhikkhunī, a probationer, a male novice, a female novice, a male lay follower, a female lay follower, from kings, from royal ministers, from sectarians, or from disciples of sectarians?” If he replies: “Friend, I do not indeed accuse this bhikkhu based on what is heard, but rather on suspicion,” he should be told: “Friend, when you accuse this bhikkhu based on suspicion, what do you suspect? In what way do you suspect it? When did you suspect it? Where do you suspect it? Do you suspect, ‘He has committed a Pārājika’? Do you suspect, ‘He has committed a Saṅghādisesa… a Thullaccaya… a Pācittiya… a Pāṭidesanīya… a Dukkaṭa… a Dubbhāsita’? Do you suspect it after hearing from a bhikkhu, a bhikkhunī, a probationer, a male novice, a female novice, a male lay follower, a female lay follower, from kings, from royal ministers, from sectarians, or from disciples of sectarians?”

361.

361.

Diṭṭhaṃ diṭṭhena sameti diṭṭhena saṃsandate diṭṭhaṃ;

Diṭṭhaṃ paṭicca na upeti asuddhaparisaṅkito;

So puggalo paṭiññāya kātabbo tenuposatho.

What was seen accords with what was seen; what was seen corresponds with what was seen. Based on what was seen, he does not incur an offense; he is suspected without basis. The Uposatha should be performed with that person upon his acknowledgement.

Sutaṃ sutena sameti sutena saṃsandate sutaṃ;

Sutaṃ paṭicca na upeti asuddhaparisaṅkito;

So puggalo paṭiññāya kātabbo tenuposatho.

What was heard accords with what was heard; what was heard corresponds with what was heard. Based on what was heard, he does not incur an offense; he is suspected without basis. The Uposatha should be performed with that person upon his acknowledgement.

Mutaṃ mutena sameti mutena saṃsandate mutaṃ;

Mutaṃ paṭicca na upeti asuddhaparisaṅkito;

So puggalo paṭiññāya kātabbo tenuposatho.

What was perceived accords with what was perceived; what was perceived corresponds with what was perceived. Based on what was perceived, he does not incur an offense; he is suspected without basis. The Uposatha should be performed with that person upon his acknowledgement.

362. Codanāya ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Codanāya okāsakammaṃ ādi, kiriyā majjhe, samatho pariyosānaṃ. Codanāya [T 0.0399] kati mūlāni, kati vatthūni, kati bhūmiyo, katihākārehi codeti? Codanāya dve mūlāni, tīṇi vatthūni, pañca bhūmiyo, dvīhākārehi codeti. Codanāya katamāni dve mūlāni? Samūlikā vā amūlikā vā – codanāya [V 0.0306] imāni dve mūlāni. Codanāya katamāni tīṇi vatthūni? Diṭṭhena [M 0.0283] sutena parisaṅkāya – codanāya imāni tīṇi vatthūni. Codanā [P 5.0161] katamā pañca bhūmiyo? Kālena vakkhāmi no akālena, bhūtena vakkhāmi no abhūtena, saṇhena vakkhāmi no pharusena, atthasaṃhitena vakkhāmi no anatthasaṃhitena, mettācitto vakkhāmi no dosantaroti – codanāya imā pañca bhūmiyo.

362. What is the beginning of an accusation, what is its middle, and what is its end? The act of asking for an opportunity is the beginning of an accusation, the act of accusing is its middle, and the settlement is its end. How many roots does an accusation have, how many grounds, how many foundations, and in how many ways does one accuse? An accusation has two roots, three grounds, five foundations, and one accuses in two ways. What are the two roots of an accusation? Either with a basis or without a basis—these are the two roots of an accusation. What are the three grounds of an accusation? By what is seen, by what is heard, and by suspicion—these are the three grounds of an accusation. What are the five foundations of an accusation? 'I will speak at the proper time, not at an improper time; I will speak truthfully, not untruthfully; I will speak gently, not harshly; I will speak with what is connected to benefit, not with what is not connected to benefit; I will speak with a mind of loving-kindness, not with inner hate'—these are the five foundations of an accusation.

Katamehi dvīhākārehi codeti? Kāyena vā codeti vācāya vā codeti – imehi dvīhākārehi codeti.

By what two ways does one accuse? One accuses either by body or by speech—by these two ways one accuses.

2. Codakādipaṭipatti

2. The Conduct of the Accuser and Others

363. Codakena kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbaṃ? Cuditakena kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbaṃ? Saṅghena kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbaṃ? Anuvijjakena kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbaṃ? Codakena kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbanti? Codakena pañcasu dhammesu patiṭṭhāya paro codetabbo. Kālena vakkhāmi no akālena, bhūtena vakkhāmi no abhūtena, saṇhena vakkhāmi no pharusena, atthasaṃhitena vakkhāmi no anatthasaṃhitena, mettācitto vakkhāmi no dosantaroti – codakena evaṃ paṭipajjitabbaṃ. Cuditakena kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbanti? Cuditakena dvīsu dhammesu paṭipajjitabbaṃ. Sacce ca akuppe ca – cuditakena evaṃ paṭipajjitabbaṃ. Saṅghena kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbanti? Saṅghena [T 0.0400] otiṇṇānotiṇṇaṃ jānitabbaṃ. Saṅghena evaṃ paṭipajjitabbaṃ. Anuvijjakena kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbanti? Anuvijjakena yena dhammena yena vinayena yena satthusāsanena taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati tathā taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametabbaṃ. Anuvijjakena evaṃ paṭipajjitabbaṃ.

363. How should an accuser conduct himself? How should the accused conduct himself? How should the Saṅgha conduct itself? How should an investigator conduct himself? As to ‘How should an accuser conduct himself?’: An accuser should accuse another, having established himself in five qualities: “I will speak at a suitable time, not at an unsuitable time; I will speak truthfully, not falsely; I will speak gently, not harshly; I will speak beneficially, not unbeneficially; I will speak with a mind of loving-kindness, not with inner hatred.” Thus should an accuser conduct himself. As to ‘How should the accused conduct himself?’: The accused should conduct himself in two qualities: in truth and in non-anger. Thus should the accused conduct himself. As to ‘How should the Saṅgha conduct itself?’: The Saṅgha should know what is relevant and what is irrelevant. Thus should the Saṅgha conduct itself. As to ‘How should an investigator conduct himself?’: An investigator should settle that legal issue in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher's teaching by which that legal issue is settled. Thus should an investigator conduct himself.

364.

364.

Uposatho kimatthāya, pavāraṇā kissa kāraṇā;

Parivāso kimatthāya, mūlāyapaṭikassanā kissa kāraṇā;

Mānattaṃ kimatthāya, abbhānaṃ kissa kāraṇā.

What is the purpose of the Uposatha? For what reason is the Pavāraṇā? What is the purpose of probation? For what reason is the sending back to the beginning? What is the purpose of penance? For what reason is rehabilitation?

Uposatho sāmaggatthāya, visuddhatthāya pavāraṇā;

Parivāso mānattatthāya, mūlāyapaṭikassanā niggahatthāya;

Mānattaṃ abbhānatthāya, visuddhatthāya abbhānaṃ.

The Uposatha is for the sake of concord; the Pavāraṇā is for the sake of purity. Probation is for the sake of penance; the sending back to the beginning is for the sake of censure. Penance is for the sake of rehabilitation; rehabilitation is for the sake of purity.

Chandā [M 0.0284][V 0.0307] dosā bhayā mohā, there ca paribhāsati;

Kāyassa bhedā duppañño, khato upahatindriyo;

Nirayaṃ gacchati dummedho, na ca sikkhāya gāravo.

He who, through desire, hatred, fear, or delusion, reviles the elders—that unwise, self-ruined one with impaired faculties, that dull-witted one with no reverence for the training—goes to hell upon the breakup of the body.

Na ca āmisaṃ nissāya;

Na ca nissāya puggalaṃ;

Ubho ete vivajjetvā;

Yathādhammo tathā kare.

Not relying on material gain, nor relying on a person, having avoided both of these, one should decide in accordance with the Dhamma.

3. Codakassaattajhāpanaṃ

3. The Accuser's Self-Burning

Kodhano upanāhī ca;

Caṇḍo ca paribhāsako;

Anāpattiyā āpattīti ropeti;

Tādiso codako jhāpeti attānaṃ.

An angry and rancorous person, fierce and reviling, who imputes an offense where there is no offense—such an accuser burns himself.

Upakaṇṇakaṃ jappati jimhaṃ pekkhati;

Vītiharati [T 0.0401] kummaggaṃ paṭisevati;

Anāpattiyā [P 5.0162] āpattīti ropeti;

Tādiso codako jhāpeti attānaṃ.

He whispers near the ear, looks for faults; he subverts the judgment, follows a crooked path; he imputes an offense where there is no offense—such an accuser burns himself.

Akālena codeti abhūtena;

Pharusena anatthasaṃhitena;

Dosantaro codeti no mettācitto;

Anāpattiyā āpattīti ropeti;

Tādiso codako jhāpeti attānaṃ.

He accuses at an improper time and falsely, with harsh words, not connected with benefit, accusing with inner hatred, not with a mind of loving-kindness; he imputes an offense where there is no offense—such an accuser burns himself.

Dhammādhammaṃ na jānāti;

Dhammādhammassa akovido;

Anāpattiyā [V 0.0308] āpattīti ropeti;

Tādiso codako jhāpeti attānaṃ.

He does not know Dhamma from non-Dhamma; he is unskilled in Dhamma and non-Dhamma; he imputes an offense where there is no offense; such an accuser burns himself.

Vinayāvinayaṃ na jānāti;

Vinayāvinayassa akovido;

Anāpattiyā āpattīti ropeti;

Tādiso codako jhāpeti attānaṃ.

He does not know Vinaya from non-Vinaya; he is unskilled in Vinaya and non-Vinaya; he imputes an offense where there is no offense; such an accuser burns himself.

Bhāsitābhāsitaṃ [M 0.0285] na jānāti;

Bhāsitābhāsitassa akovido;

Anāpattiyā āpattīti ropeti;

Tādiso codako jhāpeti attānaṃ.

He does not know what has been taught from what has not been taught; he is unskilled in what has been taught and what has not been taught; he imputes an offense where there is no offense; such an accuser burns himself.

Āciṇṇānāciṇṇaṃ [T 0.0402] na jānāti;

Āciṇṇānāciṇṇassa akovido;

Anāpattiyā āpattīti ropeti;

Tādiso codako jhāpeti attānaṃ.

He does not know what is practiced from what is not practiced; he is unskilled in what is practiced and what is not practiced; he imputes an offense where there is no offense; such an accuser burns himself.

Paññattāpaññattaṃ na jānāti;

Paññattāpaññattassa akovido;

Anāpattiyā āpattīti ropeti;

Tādiso codako jhāpeti attānaṃ.

He does not know what is laid down from what is not laid down; he is unskilled in what is laid down and what is not laid down; he imputes an offense where there is no offense; such an accuser burns himself.

Āpattānāpattiṃ na jānāti;

Āpattānāpattiyā akovido;

Anāpattiyā āpattīti ropeti;

Tādiso codako jhāpeti attānaṃ.

He does not know an offense from a non-offense; he is unskilled in offense and non-offense; he imputes an offense where there is no offense; such an accuser burns himself.

Lahukagarukaṃ na jānāti;

Lahukagarukassa akovido;

Anāpattiyā [V 0.0309] āpattīti ropeti;

Tādiso codako jhāpeti attānaṃ.

He does not know a light offense from a heavy one; he is unskilled in light and heavy offenses; he imputes an offense where there is no offense; such an accuser burns himself.

Sāvasesānavasesaṃ na jānāti;

Sāvasesānavasesassa akovido;

Anāpattiyā āpattīti ropeti;

Tādiso codako jhāpeti attānaṃ.

He does not know an offense with a remainder from one without a remainder; he is unskilled in offenses with a remainder and those without a remainder; he imputes an offense where there is no offense; such an accuser burns himself.

Duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ [T 0.0403] na jānāti;

Duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullassa akovido;

Anāpattiyā āpattīti ropeti;

Tādiso codako jhāpeti attānaṃ.

He does not know a grave offense from one that is not grave; he is unskilled in grave and non-grave offenses; he imputes an offense where there is no offense; such an accuser burns himself.

Pubbāparaṃ [M 0.0286] na jānāti;

Pubbāparassa akovido;

Anāpattiyā āpattīti ropeti;

Tādiso codako jhāpeti attānaṃ.

He does not know what is prior from what is subsequent; he is unskilled in what is prior and what is subsequent; he imputes an offense where there is no offense; such an accuser burns himself.

Anusandhivacanapathaṃ na jānāti;

Anusandhivacanapathassa akovido;

Anāpattiyā āpattīti ropeti;

Tādiso codako jhāpeti attānanti.

He does not know the context of what is said; he is unskilled in the context of what is said; he imputes an offense where there is no offense; such an accuser burns himself.

Codanākaṇḍaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section on Accusation is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Codanā anuvijjā ca, ādi mūlenuposatho;

Gati codanakaṇḍamhi, sāsanaṃ patiṭṭhāpayanti.

Accusation and investigation, the beginning, the root, the Uposatha, and the course: this, in the section on accusation, is the summary that establishes the Dispensation.

Cūḷasaṅgāmo

The Minor Dispute

1. Anuvijjakassapaṭipatti

1. The Practice of the Investigator

365. pari. 421 Saṅgāmāvacare [T 0.0404][P 5.0163][M 0.0287][V 0.0310] bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamantena nīcacittena saṅgho upasaṅkamitabbo rajoharaṇasamena cittena; āsanakusalena bhavitabbaṃ nisajjakusalena; there bhikkhū anupakhajjantena, nave bhikkhū āsanena appaṭibāhantena, yathāpatirūpe āsane nisīditabbaṃ; anānākathikena bhavitabbaṃ atiracchānakathikena; sāmaṃ vā dhammo bhāsitabbo paro vā ajjhesitabbo ariyo vā tuṇhībhāvo nātimaññitabbo.

365. A monk who enters upon a legal dispute, when approaching the Sangha, should approach the Sangha with a humble mind, with a mind like a dust-cloth. One should be skilled in seating and skilled in sitting. Without pushing against the elder monks, and without barring the junior monks from a seat, one should sit in a suitable place. One should not be a speaker of various kinds of talk, nor a speaker of talk that is contrary to the path. Either the Dhamma should be spoken by oneself, or another should be invited to speak; and noble silence should not be despised.

Saṅghena anumatena puggalena anuvijjakena anuvijjitukāmena na upajjhāyo pucchitabbo, na ācariyo pucchitabbo, na saddhivihāriko pucchitabbo, na antevāsiko pucchitabbo, na samānupajjhāyako pucchitabbo, na samānācariyako pucchitabbo, na jāti pucchitabbā, na nāmaṃ pucchitabbaṃ, na gottaṃ pucchitabbaṃ, na āgamo pucchitabbo, na kulapadeso pucchitabbo, na jātibhūmi pucchitabbā. Taṃ kiṃ kāraṇā? Atrassa pemaṃ vā doso vā. Peme vā sati dose vā, chandāpi gaccheyya dosāpi gaccheyya mohāpi gaccheyya bhayāpi gaccheyya.

An investigator, authorized by the Sangha and wishing to investigate, should not question the preceptor, should not question the teacher, should not question the co-resident, should not question the resident pupil, should not question one with a common preceptor, should not question one with a common teacher. Birth should not be asked, the name should not be asked, the clan should not be asked, the scriptural tradition should not be asked, the family lineage should not be asked, the birthplace should not be asked. For what reason? Towards that person, there might be affection or aversion. If there is affection or aversion, one might go astray through desire, go astray through hatred, go astray through delusion, or go astray through fear.

Saṅghena anumatena puggalena anuvijjakena anuvijjitukāmena saṅghagarukena bhavitabbaṃ no puggalagarukena, saddhammagarukena bhavitabbaṃ no āmisagarukena, atthavasikena bhavitabbaṃ no parisakappikena, kālena anuvijjitabbaṃ no akālena, bhūtena anuvijjitabbaṃ [T 0.0405] no abhūtena, saṇhena anuvijjitabbaṃ no pharusena, atthasaṃhitena anuvijjitabbaṃ no anatthasaṃhitena, mettācittena anuvijjitabbaṃ no dosantarena, na upakaṇṇakajappinā bhavitabbaṃ, na [V 0.0311] jimhaṃ pekkhitabbaṃ, na akkhi nikhaṇitabbaṃ, na bhamukaṃ ukkhipitabbaṃ, na sīsaṃ ukkhipitabbaṃ, na hatthavikāro kātabbo, na hatthamuddā dassetabbā.

An investigator, permitted by the Sangha and wishing to investigate, should be respectful of the Sangha, not of persons; respectful of the good Dhamma, not of material things; one who decides by the meaning, not one who speaks to please the assembly. One should investigate at a suitable time, not at an unsuitable time; with truth, not with falsehood; gently, not harshly; with what is beneficial, not with what is unbeneficial; with a mind of loving-kindness, not with a mind of aversion. One should not be a whisperer in the ear; one should not look crookedly; one should not wink the eye; one should not raise the eyebrows; one should not raise the head; no hand gesture should be made; no fist should be shown.

Āsanakusalena bhavitabbaṃ nisajjakusalena, yugamattaṃ pekkhantena atthaṃ anuvidhiyantena sake āsane nisīditabbaṃ, na ca āsanā vuṭṭhātabbaṃ[M 0.0288], na vītihātabbaṃ, na kummaggo sevitabbo, na bāhāvikkhepakaṃ na vācā vikkhepakaṃ (syā.) bhaṇitabbaṃ, aturitena bhavitabbaṃ asāhasikena, acaṇḍikatena bhavitabbaṃ vacanakkhame[P 5.0164], mettācittena bhavitabbaṃ hitānukampinā, kāruṇikena bhavitabbaṃ hitaparisakkinā, asamphappalāpinā bhavitabbaṃ pariyantabhāṇinā, averavasikena bhavitabbaṃ anasuruttena, attā pariggahetabbo, paro pariggahetabbo, codako pariggahetabbo, cuditako pariggahetabbo, adhammacodako pariggahetabbo, adhammacuditako pariggahetabbo, dhammacodako pariggahetabbo, dhammacuditako pariggahetabbo, vuttaṃ ahāpentena avuttaṃ apakāsentena otiṇṇāni padabyañjanāni sādhukaṃ pariggahetvā paro paṭipucchitvā yathā paṭiññāya kāretabbo, mando hāsetabbo vepo pahāsetabbo (syā.), bhīrū [T 0.0406] assāsetabbo, caṇḍo nisedhetabbo, asuci vibhāvetabbo, ujumaddavena na chandāgatiṃ gantabbaṃ, na dosāgatiṃ gantabbaṃ, na mohāgatiṃ gantabbaṃ, na bhayāgatiṃ gantabbaṃ, majjhattena bhavitabbaṃ dhammesu ca puggalesu ca. Evañca pana anuvijjako anuvijjamāno satthu ceva sāsanakaro hoti, viññūnañca sabrahmacārīnaṃ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo ca.

One should be skilled in one's seat and skilled in sitting. Looking at the distance of a yoke's length, noting the meaning that is to be decided, one should sit in the seat that has been assigned to one. One should not rise from one's seat, the verdict should not be diminished, a crooked path should not be followed, and one should not speak while shaking one's arms. One should be unhurried and not rash. One should not be harsh and should be patient with speech. One should have a mind of loving-kindness, be one who guards what is beneficial, be compassionate, and be one who seeks what is beneficial. One should not speak frivolous talk and should speak conclusively. One should not be under the sway of those who are hostile and should have speech that is not contentious. Oneself should be examined, the other should be examined, the accuser should be examined, the accused should be examined, the one who accuses unrighteously should be examined, the one unrighteously accused should be examined, the one who accuses righteously should be examined, and the one righteously accused should be examined. Not diminishing what has been said, not revealing what has not been said, having carefully grasped the words and phrases that have been brought forth, and having questioned the other, the decision should be made according to the admission. The dull person should be gladdened, the timid person should be reassured, the harsh person should be restrained, and the impure person should be exposed. The upright should be treated with gentleness. One should not follow a wrong course through desire, one should not follow a wrong course through hatred, one should not follow a wrong course through delusion, and one should not follow a wrong course through fear. In matters of Dhamma and in individuals, one should be impartial. And thus, the investigator, while investigating, is one who carries out the Teacher's Dispensation, and to his wise companions in the holy life, he is dear, agreeable, respected, and esteemed.

366. Suttaṃ saṃsandanatthāya, opammaṃ nidassanatthāya, attho viññāpanatthāya, paṭipucchā ṭhapanatthāya, okāsakammaṃ codanatthāya, codanā sāraṇatthāya, sāraṇā savacanīyatthāya, savacanīyaṃ palibodhatthāya, palibodho vinicchayatthāya, vinicchayo santīraṇatthāya, santīraṇaṃ ṭhānāṭhānagamanatthāya, ṭhānāṭhānagamanaṃ dummaṅkūnaṃ puggalānaṃ niggahatthāya, pesalānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ sampaggahatthāya, saṅgho sampariggahasampaṭicchanatthāya, saṅghena anumatā puggalā paccekaṭṭhāyino avisaṃvādakaṭṭhāyino.

366. The Pāḷi text is for the purpose of comparison; the simile is for the purpose of illustration; the meaning is for the purpose of making it known; questioning is for the purpose of establishing the matter; the act of asking for leave is for the purpose of accusation; accusation is for the purpose of causing one to remember; causing one to remember is for the purpose of making one open to admonition; making one open to admonition is for the purpose of obstruction; obstruction is for the purpose of reaching a decision; reaching a decision is for the purpose of investigation; investigation is for the purpose of knowing what is and is not the case; knowing what is and is not the case is for the purpose of restraining immoral individuals and for uplifting virtuous monks; the Sangha is for the purpose of fully grasping and accepting the decision; individuals approved by the Sangha stand as leaders, as speakers of unerring truth.

Vinayo saṃvaratthāya, saṃvaro avippaṭisāratthāya, avippaṭisāro pāmujjatthāya, pāmujjaṃ pītatthāya, pīti passaddhatthāya, passaddhi sukhatthāya, sukhaṃ samādhatthāya, samādhi yathābhūtañāṇadassanatthāya, yathābhūtañāṇadassanaṃ nibbidatthāya, nibbidā virāgatthāya, virāgo vimuttatthāya, vimutti vimuttiñāṇadassanatthāya, vimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ anupādāparinibbānatthāya. Etadatthā [M 0.0289][V 0.0312] kathā, etadatthā mantanā, etadatthā upanisā, etadatthaṃ sotāvadhānaṃ – yadidaṃ [T 0.0407] anupādācittassa vimokkhoti.

The discipline is for the purpose of restraint; restraint is for the purpose of non-remorse; non-remorse is for the purpose of joy; joy is for the purpose of rapture; rapture is for the purpose of tranquility; tranquility is for the purpose of happiness; happiness is for the purpose of concentration; concentration is for the purpose of the knowledge and vision of things as they really are; the knowledge and vision of things as they really are is for the purpose of powerful insight; powerful insight is for the purpose of the noble path; the noble path is for the purpose of the fruit of Arahantship; the fruit of Arahantship is for the purpose of the reviewing knowledge; the reviewing knowledge is for the purpose of final Nibbāna without clinging. For this purpose is the discourse, for this purpose is the consultation, for this purpose is the causal connection, for this purpose is attentive listening—that is, the liberation of the mind without clinging.

367.

367.

Anuyogavattaṃ nisāmaya, kusalena buddhimatā kataṃ;

Suvuttaṃ sikkhāpadānulomikaṃ, gatiṃ na nāsento samparāyikaṃ.

Pay heed to the practice of investigation, established by the skillful and wise One; it is well-expounded and in accordance with the training rules, so that one does not destroy one's future destination.

Vatthuṃ [P 5.0165] vipattiṃ āpattiṃ, nidānaṃ ākāraakovido;

Pubbāparaṃ na jānāti, katākataṃ samena ca.

One who does not know the basis, the failure, the offense, or the cause, and is unskilled in the proper reason; who does not know what comes before and after, nor, with impartiality, what has been done and what has not been done.

Kammañca adhikaraṇañca, samathe cāpi akovido;

Ratto duṭṭho ca mūḷho ca, bhayā mohā ca gacchati.

Who does not know the formal act and the legal question, and is also unskilled in the methods of settlement; who is lustful, hateful, and deluded, and proceeds from fear and delusion.

Na ca saññattikusalo, nijjhattiyā ca akovido;

Laddhapakkho ahiriko, kaṇhakammo anādaro;

Sa ve sace (ka.) tādisako bhikkhu, appaṭikkhoti vuccati.

He is not skilled in making things understood, and is unskilled in judgment; he obtains a faction, is shameless, of dark deeds, and disrespectful. Indeed, such a monk is called 'unworthy of esteem'.

Vatthuṃ vipattiṃ āpattiṃ, nidānaṃ ākārakovido;

Pubbāparañca jānāti, katākataṃ samena ca.

He knows the basis, the failure, the offense, and the origin; he is skilled in the proper manner, knows what comes before and after, and knows impartially what is done and not done.

Kammañca adhikaraṇañca, samathe cāpi kovido;

Aratto aduṭṭho amūḷho, bhayā mohā na gacchati.

He knows the formal act and the legal issue, and is also skilled in the settlement procedures; he is not attached, not hateful, not deluded, and does not follow the wrong course through fear or delusion.

Saññattiyā ca kusalo, nijjhattiyā ca kovido;

Laddhapakkho hirimano, sukkakammo sagāravo;

Sa ve tādisako bhikkhu, sappaṭikkhoti vuccatīti.

He is skilled in making things understood and skilled in judging; he has gained a following, is conscientious, of pure deeds, and respectful. Indeed, such a bhikkhu is called 'worthy of esteem'.

Cūḷasaṅgāmo niṭṭhito.

The Minor Dispute is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Nīcacittena [T 0.0408][V 0.0313] puccheyya, garu saṅghe na puggale;

Suttaṃ saṃsandanatthāya, vinayānuggahena ca;

Uddānaṃ cūḷasaṅgāme, ekuddeso ekuddesaṃ (sī. syā.) idaṃ katanti.

With a humble mind one should approach; respect for the Saṅgha, not for the individual; the Sutta for the purpose of comparison and for the upholding of the Vinaya; this summary, a single recitation, is made in the Minor Dispute.

Mahāsaṅgāmo

The Great Dispute

1. Voharantena jānitabbādi

1. What Should Be Known by One Who Judges, etc.

368. Saṅgāmāvacare [T 0.0409][P 5.0166][M 0.0290] bhikkhunā saṅghe voharantena vatthu jānitabbaṃ, vipatti jānitabbā, āpatti jānitabbā, nidānaṃ jānitabbaṃ, ākāro jānitabbo, pubbāparaṃ jānitabbaṃ, katākataṃ jānitabbaṃ, kammaṃ jānitabbaṃ, adhikaraṇaṃ jānitabbaṃ, samatho jānitabbo, na chandāgati gantabbā, na dosāgati gantabbā, na mohāgati gantabbā, na bhayāgati gantabbā, saññāpanīye ṭhāne saññāpetabbaṃ, nijjhāpanīye ṭhāne nijjhāpetabbaṃ, pekkhanīye ṭhāne pekkhitabbaṃ, pasādanīye ṭhāne pasādetabbaṃ, laddhapakkhomhīti parapakkho nāvajānitabbo, bahussutomhīti appassuto nāvajānitabbo, therataromhīti navakataro nāvajānitabbo, asampattaṃ na byāhātabbaṃ, sampattaṃ dhammato vinayato na parihāpetabbaṃ, yena dhammena yena vinayena yena satthusāsanena taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati, tathā taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametabbaṃ.

368. By a bhikkhu who engages in disputes, who judges in the Saṅgha, the matter should be known, the deviation should be known, the offense should be known, the origin should be known, the manner should be known, the preceding and subsequent should be known, what has been done and not done should be known, the formal act should be known, the legal issue should be known, the settlement should be known. One should not follow the wrong course through desire, one should not follow the wrong course through aversion, one should not follow the wrong course through delusion, one should not follow the wrong course through fear. In a situation requiring that something be made known, it should be made known; in a situation requiring investigation, it should be investigated; in a situation requiring consideration, it should be considered; in a situation requiring that confidence be inspired, confidence should be inspired. Thinking, ‘I have gained a following,’ one should not despise the other side. Thinking, ‘I am very learned,’ one should not despise one who is less learned. Thinking, ‘I am a senior elder,’ one should not despise a more junior one. What has not yet come up should not be spoken of; what has come up should not be allowed to lapse from the Dhamma and the Vinaya. By whatever Dhamma, by whatever Vinaya, by whatever teaching of the Master that legal issue is settled, in that way should that legal issue be settled.

369. Vatthu jānitabbanti aṭṭhapārājikānaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ pārājikānaṃ (sī. ka.) vatthu jānitabbaṃ, tevīsasaṅghādisesānaṃ vatthu jānitabbaṃ, dveaniyatānaṃ vatthu jānitabbaṃ, dvecattārīsanissaggiyānaṃ vatthu jānitabbaṃ, aṭṭhāsītisatapācittiyānaṃ vatthu jānitabbaṃ, dvādasapāṭidesanīyānaṃ vatthu jānitabbaṃ, dukkaṭānaṃ vatthu [T 0.0410] jānitabbaṃ, dubbhāsitānaṃ vatthu jānitabbaṃ.

369. 'The basis should be known' means that the basis of the eight Pārājika offenses should be known, the basis of the twenty-three Saṅghādisesa offenses should be known, the basis of the two Aniyata offenses should be known, the basis of the forty-two Nissaggiya offenses should be known, the basis of the one hundred and eighty-eight Pācittiya offenses should be known, the basis of the twelve Pāṭidesanīya offenses should be known, the basis of the Dukkaṭa offenses should be known, and the basis of the Dubbhāsita offenses should be known.

370. Vipatti jānitabbāti sīlavipatti jānitabbā, ācāravipatti jānitabbā, diṭṭhivipatti jānitabbā, ājīvavipatti jānitabbā.

370. 'Failure should be known' means that failure in morality should be known, failure in conduct should be known, failure in view should be known, and failure in livelihood should be known.

371. Āpatti jānitabbāti pārājikāpatti jānitabbā, saṅghādisesāpatti jānitabbā, thullaccayāpatti [V 0.0315] jānitabbā, pācittiyāpatti jānitabbā, pāṭidesanīyāpatti jānitabbā, dukkaṭāpatti jānitabbā, dubbhāsitāpatti jānitabbā.

371. 'An offense should be known' means that a Pārājika offense should be known, a Saṅghādisesa offense should be known, a Thullaccaya offense should be known, a Pācittiya offense should be known, a Pāṭidesanīya offense should be known, a Dukkaṭa offense should be known, and a Dubbhāsita offense should be known.

372. Nidānaṃ [M 0.0291] jānitabbanti aṭṭhapārājikānaṃ nidānaṃ jānitabbaṃ, tevīsasaṅghādisesānaṃ nidānaṃ jānitabbaṃ, dveaniyatānaṃ nidānaṃ jānitabbaṃ, dvecattārīsanissaggiyānaṃ nidānaṃ jānitabbaṃ, aṭṭhāsītisatapācittiyānaṃ nidānaṃ jānitabbaṃ, dvādasapāṭidesanīyānaṃ nidānaṃ jānitabbaṃ, dukkaṭānaṃ nidānaṃ jānitabbaṃ, dubbhāsitānaṃ nidānaṃ jānitabbaṃ.

372. 'The origin should be known' means that the origin of the eight Pārājika offenses should be known, the origin of the twenty-three Saṅghādisesa offenses should be known, the origin of the two Aniyata offenses should be known, the origin of the forty-two Nissaggiya offenses should be known, the origin of the one hundred and eighty-eight Pācittiya offenses should be known, the origin of the twelve Pāṭidesanīya offenses should be known, the origin of the Dukkaṭa offenses should be known, and the origin of the Dubbhāsita offenses should be known.

373. Ākāro jānitabboti saṅgho ākārato jānitabbo, gaṇo ākārato jānitabbo, puggalo ākārato jānitabbo, codako ākārato jānitabbo, cuditako ākārato jānitabbo[P 5.0167]. Saṅgho ākārato jānitabboti paṭibalo nu kho ayaṃ saṅgho imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena udāhu noti, evaṃ saṅgho ākārato jānitabbo. Gaṇo ākārato jānitabboti paṭibalo nu kho ayaṃ gaṇo imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena udāhu noti, evaṃ gaṇo ākārato jānitabbo[T 0.0411]. Puggalo ākārato jānitabboti paṭibalo nu kho ayaṃ puggalo imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena udāhu noti, evaṃ puggalo ākārato jānitabbo. Codako ākārato jānitabboti kacci nu kho ayamāyasmā pañcasu dhammesu patiṭṭhāya paraṃ codeti udāhu noti, evaṃ codako ākārato jānitabbo. Cuditako ākārato jānitabboti kacci nu kho ayamāyasmā dvīsu dhammesu patiṭṭhito sacce ca akuppe ca udāhu noti, evaṃ cuditako ākārato jānitabbo.

373. 'The manner should be known' means that the Saṅgha should be known by its manner, the group should be known by its manner, the individual should be known by their manner, the accuser should be known by their manner, and the accused should be known by their manner. 'The Saṅgha should be known by its manner' means: “Is this Saṅgha capable of settling this legal issue according to the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction, or not?” Thus, the Saṅgha should be known by its manner. 'The group should be known by its manner' means: “Is this group capable of settling this legal issue according to the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction, or not?” Thus, the group should be known by its manner. 'The individual should be known by their manner' means: “Is this individual capable of settling this legal issue according to the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction, or not?” Thus, the individual should be known by their manner. 'The accuser should be known by their manner' means: “Does this venerable one, having established themselves in five qualities, accuse another, or not?” Thus, the accuser should be known by their manner. 'The accused should be known by their manner' means: “Is this venerable one established in two qualities—truth and imperturbability—or not?” Thus, the accused should be known by their manner.

374. Pubbāparaṃ jānitabbanti kacci nu kho ayamāyasmā vatthuto vā vatthuṃ saṅkamati, vipattito vā vipattiṃ saṅkamati, āpattito vā āpattiṃ saṅkamati, avajānitvā vā paṭijānāti, paṭijānitvā vā avajānāti, aññena vā aññaṃ paṭicarati, udāhu noti, evaṃ pubbāparaṃ jānitabbaṃ.

374. 'The sequence of speech should be known' means: “Does this venerable one shift from one basis to another basis, or from one deviation to another deviation, or from one offense to another offense; or having denied, do they then acknowledge; or having acknowledged, do they then deny; or do they conceal one matter with another, or not?” Thus, the sequence of speech should be known.

375. Katākataṃ jānitabbanti methunadhammo jānitabbo, methunadhammassa anulomaṃ jānitabbaṃ, methunadhammassa pubbabhāgo jānitabbo. Methunadhammo jānitabboti dvayaṃdvayasamāpatti jānitabbā. Methunadhammassa anulomaṃ [M 0.0292] jānitabbanti bhikkhu attano mukhena parassa aṅgajātaṃ gaṇhāti[V 0.0316]. Methunadhammassa pubbabhāgo jānitabboti vaṇṇāvaṇṇo vaṇṇo avaṇṇo (syā.), kāyasaṃsaggo, duṭṭhullavācā, attakāmapāricariyā, vacanamanuppadānaṃ [T 0.0412] dhanamanuppadānaṃ (ka.).

375. 'What has been done and not done should be known' means that sexual intercourse should be known, what is in conformity with sexual intercourse should be known, and the preliminary part of sexual intercourse should be known. 'Sexual intercourse should be known' means that the joining in pairs should be known. 'What is in conformity with sexual intercourse should be known' means that a bhikkhu takes the genital organ of another with his own mouth. 'The preliminary part of sexual intercourse should be known' means that emission and non-emission of semen, bodily contact, coarse speech, service for one's own sensual pleasure, and giving possessions and acting as a go-between should be known.

376. Kammaṃ jānitabbanti soḷasakammāni jānitabbāni – cattāri apalokanakammāni jānitabbāni, cattāri ñattikammāni jānitabbāni, cattāri ñattidutiyakammāni jānitabbāni, cattāri ñatticatutthakammāni jānitabbāni.

376. The legal procedure should be known: sixteen acts of procedure should be known—four acts of announcement should be known, four acts of motion should be known, four acts of motion with one announcement should be known, four acts of motion with three announcements should be known.

377. Adhikaraṇaṃ jānitabbanti cattāri adhikaraṇāni jānitabbāni – vivādādhikaraṇaṃ jānitabbaṃ, anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ jānitabbaṃ, āpattādhikaraṇaṃ jānitabbaṃ, kiccādhikaraṇaṃ jānitabbaṃ.

377. The legal issue should be known: four legal issues should be known—a legal issue arising from disputes should be known, a legal issue arising from accusations should be known, a legal issue arising from offenses should be known, a legal issue arising from duties should be known.

378. Samatho jānitabboti satta samathā jānitabbā – sammukhāvinayo jānitabbo, sativinayo jānitabbo, amūḷhavinayo jānitabbo, paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ jānitabbaṃ, yebhuyyasikā jānitabbā, tassapāpiyasikā jānitabbā, tiṇavatthārako jānitabbo.

378. The settlement should be known: seven settlements should be known—the settlement in the presence of, the settlement by recollection, the settlement on account of past insanity, the settlement by acknowledgement, the settlement by majority decision, the settlement for specific depravity, and the settlement of covering over with grass.

2. Agatiagantabbo

2. The Wrong Course Not to Be Followed

379. Na chandāgati gantabbāti chandāgatiṃ gacchanto kathaṃ chandāgatiṃ gacchati? Idhekacco – “ayaṃ me upajjhāyo vā ācariyo vā saddhivihāriko vā antevāsiko vā samānupajjhāyako vā samānācariyako vā sandiṭṭho vā sambhatto vā ñātisālohito vā”ti, tassānukampāya tassānurakkhāya adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti, avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpeti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpeti, abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatena bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatenāti [T 0.0413] dīpeti, bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatena abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, apaññattaṃ tathāgatena paññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, paññattaṃ tathāgatena apaññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, anāpattiṃ [M 0.0293] āpattīti dīpeti, āpattiṃ anāpattīti dīpeti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ garukā āpattīti dīpeti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ lahukā āpattīti dīpeti, sāvasesaṃ āpattiṃ anavasesā āpattīti dīpeti, anavasesaṃ āpattiṃ sāvasesā āpattīti dīpeti, duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti, aduṭṭhullaṃ [P 5.0168] āpattiṃ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti. Imehi aṭṭhārasahi vatthūhi chandāgatiṃ gacchanto bahujanāhitāya [V 0.0317] paṭipanno hoti bahujanāsukhāya bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṃ. Imehi aṭṭhārasahi vatthūhi chandāgatiṃ gacchanto khataṃ upahataṃ attānaṃ pariharati, sāvajjo ca hoti sānuvajjo ca viññūnaṃ, bahuñca apuññaṃ pasavati. Chandāgatiṃ gacchanto evaṃ chandāgatiṃ gacchati.

379. One should not go by the course of partiality due to desire. How does one who goes by the course of partiality due to desire go by the course of partiality due to desire? Here, a certain person thinks: 'This is my preceptor, or teacher, or co-resident disciple, or pupil, or a disciple with the same preceptor, or a disciple with the same teacher, or an acquaintance, or a companion, or a kinsman by blood.' Out of compassion for that person, in order to protect that person, he explains what is not-Dhamma as Dhamma, and the Dhamma as not-Dhamma. He explains what is not-Vinaya as Vinaya, and the Vinaya as not-Vinaya. He explains what was not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata, and what was spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata. He explains what was not practiced by the Tathāgata as practiced by the Tathāgata, and what was practiced by the Tathāgata as not practiced by the Tathāgata. He explains what was not laid down by the Tathāgata as laid down by the Tathāgata, and what was laid down by the Tathāgata as not laid down by the Tathāgata. He explains a non-offense as an offense, and an offense as a non-offense. He explains a light offense as a grave offense, and a grave offense as a light offense. He explains an offense with a remainder as an offense without a remainder, and an offense without a remainder as an offense with a remainder. He explains a coarse offense as a non-coarse offense, and a non-coarse offense as a coarse offense. By these eighteen grounds, one who goes by the course of partiality due to desire practices for the non-welfare of many people, for the unhappiness of many people, for the harm of the multitude, for the non-welfare and suffering of devas and humans. By these eighteen grounds, one who goes by the course of partiality due to desire carries himself as undermined and impaired, is blameworthy and is censurable by the wise, and generates much demerit. Thus, one who goes by the course of partiality due to desire goes by the course of partiality due to desire.

380. Na dosāgati gantabbāti dosāgatiṃ gacchanto kathaṃ dosāgatiṃ gacchati? Idhekacco anatthaṃ me acarīti āghātaṃ bandhati, anatthaṃ me caratīti āghātaṃ bandhati, anatthaṃ me carissatīti [T 0.0414] āghātaṃ bandhati, piyassa me manāpassa anatthaṃ acari… anatthaṃ carati… anatthaṃ carissatīti āghātaṃ bandhati, appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṃ acari… atthaṃ carati… atthaṃ carissatīti āghātaṃ bandhati. Imehi navahi āghātavatthūhi āghāto paṭighāto kuddho kodhābhibhūto adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti…pe… duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti, aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti. Imehi aṭṭhārasahi vatthūhi dosāgatiṃ gacchanto bahujanāhitāya paṭipanno hoti bahujanāsukhāya bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṃ. Imehi aṭṭhārasahi vatthūhi dosāgatiṃ gacchanto khataṃ upahataṃ attānaṃ pariharati, sāvajjo ca hoti sānuvajjo ca viññūnaṃ bahuñca apuññaṃ pasavati. Dosāgatiṃ gacchanto evaṃ dosāgatiṃ gacchati.

380. One should not go the wrong course through hatred. How does one who goes the wrong course through hatred go the wrong course through hatred? Here, a certain person harbors resentment, thinking: 'He has done me harm,' 'He is doing me harm,' or 'He will do me harm.' He harbors resentment, thinking: 'He has done harm to my beloved and dear one... is doing harm... will do harm.' He harbors resentment, thinking: 'He has done good to my unloved and disagreeable one... is doing good... will do good.' By these nine grounds for resentment, being resentful, hostile, angry, and overcome by anger, he declares what is not the Dhamma as the Dhamma, and what is the Dhamma as not the Dhamma... he declares a coarse offense as a non-coarse offense, and a non-coarse offense as a coarse offense. By these eighteen grounds, one who goes the wrong course through hatred acts for the non-welfare of many people, for the unhappiness of many people, for the harm of the multitude, and for the non-welfare and suffering of devas and humans. By these eighteen grounds, one who goes the wrong course through hatred carries himself as undermined and impaired, is blameworthy and is censurable by the wise, and he generates much demerit. Thus, one who goes the wrong course through hatred goes the wrong course through hatred.

381. Na mohāgati gantabbāti mohāgatiṃ gacchanto kathaṃ mohāgatiṃ gacchati? Ratto rāgavasena gacchati, duṭṭho dosavasena gacchati, mūḷho mohavasena gacchati, parāmaṭṭho diṭṭhivasena gacchati, mūḷho saṃmūḷho mohābhibhūto adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti [M 0.0294] dīpeti…pe… duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti, aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti. Imehi aṭṭhārasahi vatthūhi mohāgatiṃ gacchanto bahujanāhitāya paṭipanno hoti bahujanāsukhāya bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya [T 0.0415] dukkhāya devamanussānaṃ. Imehi aṭṭhārasahi vatthūhi mohāgatiṃ gacchanto khataṃ upahataṃ attānaṃ pariharati, sāvajjo ca hoti sānuvajjo ca viññūnaṃ, bahuñca apuññaṃ pasavati. Mohāgatiṃ gacchanto evaṃ mohāgatiṃ gacchati.

381. One should not go the wrong course through delusion. How does one who goes the wrong course through delusion go the wrong course through delusion? One who is lustful proceeds by the power of lust. One who is hostile proceeds by the power of hatred. One who is deluded proceeds by the power of delusion. One who wrongly grasps proceeds by the power of wrong view. Being deluded, utterly deluded, and overcome by delusion, he declares what is not the Dhamma as the Dhamma, and the Dhamma as not the Dhamma... he declares a coarse offense as a non-coarse offense, and a non-coarse offense as a coarse offense. By these eighteen grounds, one who goes the wrong course through delusion practices for the non-welfare of many people, for the unhappiness of many people, for the harm of the multitude, and for the non-welfare and suffering of devas and humans. By these eighteen grounds, one who goes the wrong course through delusion carries himself as undermined and impaired, is blameworthy and is censured by the wise, and he generates much demerit. Thus, one who goes the wrong course through delusion goes the wrong course through delusion.

382. Na bhayāgati gantabbāti bhayāgatiṃ gacchanto kathaṃ bhayāgatiṃ gacchati? Idhekacco – “ayaṃ visamanissito vā gahananissito vā balavanissito vā kakkhaḷo pharuso jīvitantarāyaṃ vā brahmacariyantarāyaṃ vā karissatī”ti, tassa bhayā bhīto adhammaṃ dhammoti [V 0.0318] dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti, avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpeti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpeti, abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatena bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatena abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, apaññattaṃ tathāgatena paññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, paññattaṃ tathāgatena apaññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, anāpattiṃ āpattīti dīpeti, āpattiṃ anāpattīti dīpeti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ garukā āpattīti dīpeti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ lahukā āpattīti dīpeti, sāvasesaṃ āpattiṃ anavasesā āpattīti dīpeti, anavasesaṃ āpattiṃ sāvasesā āpattīti dīpeti, duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti, aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti. Imehi aṭṭhārasahi vatthūhi bhayāgatiṃ gacchanto bahujanāhitāya paṭipanno hoti bahujanāsukhāya bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṃ. Imehi aṭṭhārasahi vatthūhi bhayāgatiṃ gacchanto khataṃ upahataṃ attānaṃ pariharati, sāvajjo ca hoti sānuvajjo ca viññūnaṃ, bahuñca apuññaṃ pasavati. Bhayāgatiṃ gacchanto evaṃ bhayāgatiṃ gacchati.

382. One should not go the wrong course through fear. How does one who goes the wrong course through fear do so? Here, a certain person thinks: 'This person relies on what is unsuitable, or relies on the thicket of wrong views, or relies on the powerful, or is harsh and rough—he might cause danger to my life or danger to my holy life.' Through fear, being afraid of that person, he declares what is not the Dhamma as the Dhamma, and the Dhamma as not the Dhamma; he declares what is not the Vinaya as the Vinaya, and the Vinaya as not the Vinaya; he declares what was not spoken and uttered by the Tathāgata as spoken and uttered by the Tathāgata, and what was spoken and uttered by the Tathāgata as not spoken and uttered by the Tathāgata; he declares what was not practiced by the Tathāgata as practiced by the Tathāgata, and what was practiced by the Tathāgata as not practiced by the Tathāgata; he declares what was not laid down by the Tathāgata as laid down by the Tathāgata, and what was laid down by the Tathāgata as not laid down by the Tathāgata; he declares a non-offense as an offense, and an offense as a non-offense; he declares a light offense as a grave offense, and a grave offense as a light offense; he declares an offense with residue as an offense without residue, and an offense without residue as an offense with residue; he declares a gross offense as a non-gross offense, and a non-gross offense as a gross offense. By these eighteen grounds, one who goes the wrong course through fear acts for the detriment of many people, for the unhappiness of many people, for the disadvantage, harm, and suffering of devas and humans. By these eighteen grounds, one who goes the wrong course through fear maintains himself as injured and damaged; he becomes blameworthy and subject to reproach by the wise, and he generates much demerit. In this way, one who goes the wrong course through fear goes the wrong course through fear.

Chandā dosā bhayā mohā, yo dhammaṃ ativattati;

Nihīyati tassa yaso, kāḷapakkheva candimāti.

Through desire, hatred, fear, or delusion, whoever violates the Dhamma—their glory diminishes like the moon in the dark fortnight.

3. Agatiagamanaṃ

3. Not Going on Wrong Courses

383. Kathaṃ [M 0.0295] na chandāgatiṃ gacchati? Adhammaṃ adhammoti dīpento na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, dhammaṃ dhammoti dīpento [P 5.0169] na chandāgatiṃ [T 0.0416] gacchati, avinayaṃ avinayoti dīpento na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, vinayaṃ vinayoti dīpento na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatena abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpento na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatena bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpento na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpento na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpento na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, apaññattaṃ tathāgatena apaññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpento na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, paññattaṃ tathāgatena paññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpento na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, anāpattiṃ anāpattīti dīpento na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, āpattiṃ āpattīti dīpento na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ lahukā āpattīti dīpento na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, garukaṃ āpattiṃ garukā āpattīti dīpento na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, sāvasesaṃ āpattiṃ sāvasesā āpattīti dīpento na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, anavasesaṃ [V 0.0319] āpattiṃ anavasesā āpattīti dīpento na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpento na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpento na chandāgatiṃ gacchati. Evaṃ na chandāgatiṃ gacchati.

383. How does one not go on a wrong course through desire? One who declares what is not Dhamma as not Dhamma does not go on a wrong course through desire; one who declares what is Dhamma as Dhamma does not go on a wrong course through desire; one who declares what is not Vinaya as not Vinaya does not go on a wrong course through desire; one who declares what is Vinaya as Vinaya does not go on a wrong course through desire; one who declares what was not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata does not go on a wrong course through desire; one who declares what was spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata does not go on a wrong course through desire; one who declares what was not habitually practiced by the Tathāgata as not habitually practiced by the Tathāgata does not go on a wrong course through desire; one who declares what was habitually practiced by the Tathāgata as habitually practiced by the Tathāgata does not go on a wrong course through desire; one who declares what was not laid down by the Tathāgata as not laid down by the Tathāgata does not go on a wrong course through desire; one who declares what was laid down by the Tathāgata as laid down by the Tathāgata does not go on a wrong course through desire; one who declares a non-offense as a non-offense does not go on a wrong course through desire; one who declares an offense as an offense does not go on a wrong course through desire; one who declares a light offense as a light offense does not go on a wrong course through desire; one who declares a grave offense as a grave offense does not go on a wrong course through desire; one who declares an offense with remainder as an offense with remainder does not go on a wrong course through desire; one who declares an offense without remainder as an offense without remainder does not go on a wrong course through desire; one who declares a gross offense as a gross offense does not go on a wrong course through desire; one who declares a non-gross offense as a non-gross offense does not go on a wrong course through desire. Thus, one does not go on a wrong course through desire.

384. Kathaṃ na dosāgatiṃ gacchati? Adhammaṃ adhammoti dīpento [T 0.0417] na dosāgatiṃ gacchati, dhammaṃ dhammoti dīpento na dosāgatiṃ gacchati…pe… duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpento na dosāgatiṃ gacchati, aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpento na dosāgatiṃ gacchati. Evaṃ na dosāgatiṃ gacchati.

384. How does one not go on a wrong course through hatred? One who declares what is not the Dhamma as not the Dhamma does not go on a wrong course through hatred. One who declares the Dhamma as the Dhamma does not go on a wrong course through hatred... One who declares a gross offense as a gross offense does not go on a wrong course through hatred. One who declares a non-gross offense as a non-gross offense does not go on a wrong course through hatred. In this way, one does not go on a wrong course through hatred.

385. Kathaṃ na mohāgatiṃ gacchati? Adhammaṃ adhammoti dīpento na mohāgatiṃ gacchati, dhammaṃ dhammoti dīpento na mohāgatiṃ gacchati…pe… duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpento na mohāgatiṃ [M 0.0296] gacchati, aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpento na mohāgatiṃ gacchati. Evaṃ na mohāgatiṃ gacchati.

385. How does one not go on a wrong course through delusion? One who declares what is not the Dhamma as not the Dhamma does not go on a wrong course through delusion. One who declares the Dhamma as the Dhamma does not go on a wrong course through delusion... One who declares a gross offense as a gross offense does not go on a wrong course through delusion. One who declares a non-gross offense as a non-gross offense does not go on a wrong course through delusion. In this way, one does not go on a wrong course through delusion.

386. Kathaṃ na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati? Adhammaṃ adhammoti dīpento na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, dhammaṃ dhammoti dīpento na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, avinayaṃ avinayoti dīpento na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, vinayaṃ vinayoti dīpento na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatena abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpento na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatena bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpento na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpento na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpento na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, apaññattaṃ tathāgatena apaññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpento na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, paññattaṃ tathāgatena paññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpento na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, anāpattiṃ anāpattīti dīpento na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, āpattiṃ āpattīti dīpento na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ lahukā āpattīti dīpento na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, garukaṃ āpattiṃ garukā āpattīti dīpento na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, sāvasesaṃ āpattiṃ sāvasesā āpattīti dīpento na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, anavasesaṃ āpattiṃ anavasesā āpattīti dīpento na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpento na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpento na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati. Evaṃ na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati.

386. How does one not go on a wrong course through fear? One who declares what is not Dhamma as 'not Dhamma' does not go on a wrong course through fear. One who declares what is Dhamma as 'Dhamma' does not go on a wrong course through fear. One who declares what is not Vinaya as 'not Vinaya' does not go on a wrong course through fear. One who declares what is Vinaya as 'Vinaya' does not go on a wrong course through fear. One who declares what was not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as 'not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata' does not go on a wrong course through fear. One who declares what was spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as 'spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata' does not go on a wrong course through fear. One who declares what was not habitually practiced by the Tathāgata as 'not habitually practiced by the Tathāgata' does not go on a wrong course through fear. One who declares what was habitually practiced by the Tathāgata as 'habitually practiced by the Tathāgata' does not go on a wrong course through fear. One who declares what was not laid down by the Tathāgata as 'not laid down by the Tathāgata' does not go on a wrong course through fear. One who declares what was laid down by the Tathāgata as 'laid down by the Tathāgata' does not go on a wrong course through fear. One who declares a non-offense as 'a non-offense' does not go on a wrong course through fear. One who declares an offense as 'an offense' does not go on a wrong course through fear. One who declares a light offense as 'a light offense' does not go on a wrong course through fear. One who declares a heavy offense as 'a heavy offense' does not go on a wrong course through fear. One who declares an offense with a remainder as 'an offense with a remainder' does not go on a wrong course through fear. One who declares an offense without a remainder as 'an offense without a remainder' does not go on a wrong course through fear. One who declares a gross offense as 'a gross offense' does not go on a wrong course through fear. One who declares a non-gross offense as 'a non-gross offense' does not go on a wrong course through fear. In this way, one does not go on a wrong course through fear.

Chandā [V 0.0320] dosā bhayā mohā, yo dhammaṃ nātivattati;

Āpūrati tassa yaso, sukkapakkheva candimāti.

Whoever, through desire, hatred, fear, or delusion, does not transgress the Dhamma, their fame increases, like the moon in the waxing fortnight.

4. Saññāpanīyādi

4. 4. Making Known, etc.

387. Kathaṃ saññāpanīye ṭhāne saññāpeti? Adhammaṃ adhammoti dīpento saññāpanīye ṭhāne saññāpeti, dhammaṃ dhammoti dīpento [T 0.0418] saññāpanīye ṭhāne saññāpeti…pe… duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpento saññāpanīye ṭhāne saññāpeti, aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhullā [M 0.0297] āpattīti dīpento saññāpanīye ṭhāne saññāpeti. Evaṃ saññāpanīye ṭhāne saññāpeti.

387. How does one make known in a situation where something should be made known? By declaring what is not Dhamma as 'not Dhamma,' one makes known in a situation where something should be made known. By declaring what is Dhamma as 'Dhamma,' one makes known in a situation where something should be made known... By declaring a gross offense as 'a gross offense,' one makes known in a situation where something should be made known. By declaring a non-gross offense as 'a non-gross offense,' one makes known in a situation where something should be made known. Thus, one makes known in a situation where something should be made known.

388. Kathaṃ nijjhāpanīye ṭhāne nijjhāpeti? Adhammaṃ adhammoti dīpento nijjhāpanīye ṭhāne nijjhāpeti, dhammaṃ dhammoti dīpento nijjhāpanīye ṭhāne nijjhāpeti…pe… duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpento nijjhāpanīye ṭhāne nijjhāpeti, aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpento nijjhāpanīye ṭhāne nijjhāpeti. Evaṃ nijjhāpanīye ṭhāne nijjhāpeti.

388. How does one cause to reflect in a situation where one should cause to reflect? By declaring what is not Dhamma as 'not Dhamma,' one causes to reflect in a situation where one should cause to reflect. By declaring what is Dhamma as 'Dhamma,' one causes to reflect in a situation where one should cause to reflect... By declaring a gross offense as 'a gross offense,' one causes to reflect in a situation where one should cause to reflect. By declaring a non-gross offense as 'a non-gross offense,' one causes to reflect in a situation where one should cause to reflect. Thus, one causes to reflect in a situation where one should cause to reflect.

389. Kathaṃ pekkhanīye ṭhāne pekkhati? Adhammaṃ adhammoti dīpento pekkhanīye ṭhāne pekkhati, dhammaṃ dhammoti dīpento pekkhanīye ṭhāne pekkhati…pe… duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpento pekkhanīye ṭhāne pekkhati, aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpento pekkhanīye ṭhāne pekkhati. Evaṃ pekkhanīye ṭhāne pekkhati.

389. How does one consider in a situation where one should consider? By declaring what is not Dhamma as 'not Dhamma,' one considers in a situation where one should consider. By declaring what is Dhamma as 'Dhamma,' one considers in a situation where one should consider... By declaring a gross offense as 'a gross offense,' one considers in a situation where one should consider. By declaring a non-gross offense as 'a non-gross offense,' one considers in a situation where one should consider. Thus, one considers in a situation where one should consider.

390. Kathaṃ pasādanīye ṭhāne pasādeti? Adhammaṃ adhammoti dīpento pasādanīye ṭhāne pasādeti, dhammaṃ dhammoti dīpento pasādanīye ṭhāne pasādeti…pe… duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpento pasādanīye ṭhāne pasādeti, aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ [T 0.0419] aduṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpento pasādanīye ṭhāne pasādeti. Evaṃ pasādanīye ṭhāne pasādeti.

390. How does one inspire confidence in a situation where one should inspire confidence? By declaring what is not Dhamma as 'not Dhamma,' one inspires confidence in a situation where one should inspire confidence. By declaring what is Dhamma as 'Dhamma,' one inspires confidence in a situation where one should inspire confidence... By declaring a gross offense as 'a gross offense,' one inspires confidence in a situation where one should inspire confidence. By declaring a non-gross offense as 'a non-gross offense,' one inspires confidence in a situation where one should inspire confidence. Thus, one inspires confidence in a situation where one should inspire confidence.

5. Parapakkhādiavajānanaṃ

5. 5. Disparaging the Other Faction, etc.

391. Kathaṃ laddhapakkhomhīti parapakkhaṃ avajānāti? Idhekacco laddhapakkho hoti laddhaparivāro [V 0.0321] pakkhavā ñātimā. “Ayaṃ aladdhapakkho aladdhaparivāro na pakkhavā na ñātimā”ti tassa avajānanto adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti…pe… duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti, aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti. Evaṃ laddhapakkhomhīti parapakkhaṃ avajānāti.

391. How does one, thinking, “I have gained a faction,” disparage another’s faction? Here, a certain one has gained a faction, has gained a retinue, has a faction, and has relatives. Thinking, “This one has not gained a faction, has not gained a retinue, has no faction, and has no relatives,” and disparaging him, one explains what is not-Dhamma as Dhamma, and what is Dhamma as not-Dhamma… one explains a gross offense as a not-gross offense, and a not-gross offense as a gross offense. In this way, thinking, “I have gained a faction,” one disparages another’s faction.

392. Kathaṃ bahussutomhīti appassutaṃ avajānāti? Idhekacco bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo. “Ayaṃ appassuto appāgamo [M 0.0298] appadharo”ti tassa avajānanto adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti…pe… duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti, aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti. Evaṃ bahussutomhīti appassutaṃ avajānāti.

392. How does one, thinking, “I am very learned,” disparage one who is less learned? Here, a certain one is very learned, a bearer of the teachings, an accumulator of the teachings. Thinking, “This one is less learned, has little textual knowledge, and is a poor bearer of the teachings,” and disparaging him, one explains what is not-Dhamma as Dhamma, and what is Dhamma as not-Dhamma… one explains a gross offense as a not-gross offense, and a not-gross offense as a gross offense. In this way, thinking, “I am very learned,” one disparages one who is less learned.

393. Kathaṃ therataromhīti navakataraṃ avajānāti? Idhekacco thero hoti rattaññū cirapabbajito ayaṃ navako appaññāto appakataññū imassa vacanaṃ akataṃ bhavissatī”ti tassa avajānanto adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti [T 0.0420] …pe… duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti, aduṭṭhullaṃ [P 5.0170] āpattiṃ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti. Evaṃ therataromhīti navakataraṃ avajānāti.

393. How does one, thinking, “I am a senior,” disparage a junior? Here, a certain one is a senior, of long standing, and long ordained. Thinking, “This one is a junior, little-known, and inexperienced; his words will not be acted upon,” and disparaging him, one explains what is not-Dhamma as Dhamma, and what is Dhamma as not-Dhamma… one explains a gross offense as a not-gross offense, and a not-gross offense as a gross offense. In this way, thinking, “I am a senior,” one disparages a junior.

394. Asampattaṃ na byāharitabbanti anotiṇṇaṃ bhāraṃ bhāsaṃ (syā.) na otāretabbaṃ. Sampattaṃ dhammato vinayato na parihāpetabbanti yaṃatthāya saṅgho sannipatito hoti taṃ atthaṃ dhammato vinayato na parihāpetabbaṃ.

394. As for the saying, 'What has not been arrived at should not be spoken of,' it means a burden that has not come before the Saṅgha should not be put down. As for the saying, 'What has been arrived at should not be caused to fail in accordance with the Dhamma and the Vinaya,' it means the purpose for which the Saṅgha has assembled should not be caused to fail in accordance with the Dhamma and the Vinaya.

395. Yena dhammenāti bhūtena vatthunā. Yena vinayenāti codetvā sāretvā. Yena satthusāsanenāti ñattisampadāya anussāvanasampadāya, yena dhammena yena vinayena yena satthusāsanena taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati, tathā taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametabbanti.

395. “By which Dhamma” means by a true matter. “By which Vinaya” means having accused and having reminded. “By which Teacher’s instruction” means by the accomplishment of the motion and by the accomplishment of the proclamation. By whichever Dhamma, by whichever Vinaya, by whichever Teacher's instruction a legal issue is settled, in that way should that legal issue be settled.

6. Anuvijjakassa anuyogaṃ

6. The Inquiry of the Investigator

396. Anuvijjakena codako pucchitabbo – “yaṃ kho tvaṃ, āvuso, imassa bhikkhuno pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapesi, kimhi naṃ ṭhapesi, sīlavipattiyā vā ṭhapesi, ācāravipattiyā vā ṭhapesi, diṭṭhivipattiyā vā ṭhapesī”ti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – “sīlavipattiyā vā ṭhapemi [V 0.0322] ācāravipattiyā vā ṭhapemi diṭṭhivipattiyā vā ṭhapemī”ti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “jānāti panāyasmā sīlavipattiṃ, jānāti ācāravipattiṃ, jānāti diṭṭhivipatti”nti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – “jānāmi kho ahaṃ, āvuso, sīlavipattiṃ, jānāmi ācāravipattiṃ, jānāmi diṭṭhivipatti”nti[T 0.0421], so evamassa vacanīyo – “katamā [M 0.0299] panāvuso, sīlavipatti katamā ācāravipatti katamā diṭṭhivipattī”ti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – “cattāri pārājikāni terasa saṅghādisesā – ayaṃ sīlavipatti. Thullaccayaṃ pācittiyaṃ pāṭidesanīyaṃ dukkaṭaṃ dubbhāsitaṃ – ayaṃ ācāravipatti. Micchādiṭṭhi antaggāhikādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ diṭṭhivipattī”ti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “yaṃ kho tvaṃ, āvuso, imassa bhikkhuno pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapesi, diṭṭhena vā ṭhapesi, sutena vā ṭhapesi, parisaṅkāya vā ṭhapesī”ti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – “diṭṭhena vā ṭhapemi, sutena vā ṭhapemi, parisaṅkāya vā ṭhapemī”ti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “yaṃ kho tvaṃ, āvuso, imassa bhikkhuno diṭṭhena pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapesi, kiṃ te diṭṭhaṃ, kinti te diṭṭhaṃ, kadā te diṭṭhaṃ, kattha te diṭṭhaṃ, pārājikaṃ ajjhāpajjanto diṭṭho, saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpajjanto diṭṭho, thullaccayaṃ… pācittiyaṃ… pāṭidesanīyaṃ… dukkaṭaṃ… dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpajjanto diṭṭho, kattha ca tvaṃ ahosi, kattha cāyaṃ bhikkhu ahosi, kiñca tvaṃ karosi, kiṃ cāyaṃ bhikkhu karotī”ti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – “na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, imassa bhikkhuno diṭṭhena pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapemi, api ca sutena pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapemī”ti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “yaṃ kho tvaṃ, āvuso, imassa bhikkhuno sutena pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapesi [T 0.0422] kiṃ te sutaṃ, kinti te sutaṃ, kadā te sutaṃ, kattha te sutaṃ, pārājikaṃ ajjhāpannoti sutaṃ, saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpannoti sutaṃ, thullaccayaṃ… pācittiyaṃ… pāṭidesanīyaṃ… dukkaṭaṃ… dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpannoti sutaṃ, bhikkhussa sutaṃ, bhikkhuniyā sutaṃ, sikkhamānāya sutaṃ, sāmaṇerassa sutaṃ, sāmaṇeriyā sutaṃ, upāsakassa sutaṃ, upāsikāya sutaṃ, rājūnaṃ sutaṃ, rājamahāmattānaṃ sutaṃ, titthiyānaṃ sutaṃ, titthiyasāvakānaṃ suta”nti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – “na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, imassa bhikkhuno sutena pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapemi, api ca parisaṅkāya pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapemī”ti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “yaṃ kho tvaṃ, āvuso, imassa bhikkhuno parisaṅkāya pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapesi, kiṃ parisaṅkasi, kinti parisaṅkasi, kadā parisaṅkasi, kattha parisaṅkasi, pārājikaṃ ajjhāpannoti parisaṅkasi, saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpannoti parisaṅkasi, thullaccayaṃ… pācittiyaṃ… pāṭidesanīyaṃ… dukkaṭaṃ… dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpannoti parisaṅkasi, bhikkhussa sutvā parisaṅkasi, bhikkhuniyā sutvā parisaṅkasi, sikkhamānāya sutvā parisaṅkasi, sāmaṇerassa sutvā parisaṅkasi, sāmaṇeriyā sutvā parisaṅkasi, upāsakassa sutvā parisaṅkasi, upāsikāya sutvā [M 0.0300] parisaṅkasi, rājūnaṃ sutvā [V 0.0323] parisaṅkasi rājamahāmattānaṃ [T 0.0423] sutvā parisaṅkasi, titthiyānaṃ sutvā parisaṅkasi, titthiyasāvakānaṃ sutvā parisaṅkasī”ti?

396. An investigator should question the accuser: “Friend, regarding the Pavāraṇā of this monk that you suspended, for what reason did you suspend it? Did you suspend it because of a corruption of virtue, a corruption of conduct, or a corruption of view?” If he should reply: “I suspend it because of a corruption of virtue, or a corruption of conduct, or a corruption of view,” he should be spoken to thus: “But does Your Reverence know what a corruption of virtue is, know what a corruption of conduct is, and know what a corruption of view is?” If he should reply: “Indeed, friend, I know what a corruption of virtue is, I know what a corruption of conduct is, and I know what a corruption of view is,” he should be spoken to thus: “What, friend, is a corruption of virtue? What is a corruption of conduct? What is a corruption of view?” If he should reply: “The four Pārājika offenses and the thirteen Saṅghādisesa offenses—this is a corruption of virtue. The Thullaccaya, Pācittiya, Pāṭidesanīya, Dukkaṭa, and Dubbhāsita offenses—this is a corruption of conduct. Wrong view and a view of holding to an extreme—this is a corruption of view,” he should be spoken to thus: “Friend, regarding the Pavāraṇā of this monk that you suspended, did you suspend it based on what was seen, based on what was heard, or based on suspicion?” If he should reply: “I suspend it based on what was seen, or based on what was heard, or based on suspicion,” he should be spoken to thus: “Friend, regarding the Pavāraṇā of this monk that you suspended based on what was seen, what did you see? In what manner did you see it? When did you see it? Where did you see it? Was he seen committing a Pārājika offense? Was he seen committing a Saṅghādisesa offense? …a Thullaccaya offense… a Pācittiya offense… a Pāṭidesanīya offense… a Dukkaṭa offense… a Dubbhāsita offense? And where were you, and where was this monk? And what were you doing, and what was this monk doing?” If he should reply: “Indeed, friend, I do not suspend this monk's Pavāraṇā based on what was seen, but rather I suspend it based on what was heard,” he should be spoken to thus: “Friend, regarding the Pavāraṇā of this monk that you suspend based on what was heard, what did you hear? In what manner did you hear it? When did you hear it? Where did you hear it? Was it heard that he had committed a Pārājika offense? Was it heard that he had committed a Saṅghādisesa offense? Was it heard that he had committed a Thullaccaya offense… a Pācittiya offense… a Pāṭidesanīya offense… a Dukkaṭa offense… a Dubbhāsita offense? Was it heard from a bhikkhu? From a bhikkhunī? From a probationer? From a male novice? From a female novice? From a male lay follower? From a female lay follower? From kings? From royal ministers? From sectarians? From disciples of sectarians?” If he should reply: “Indeed, friend, I do not suspend this monk's Pavāraṇā based on what was heard, but rather I suspend it based on suspicion,” he should be spoken to thus: “Friend, regarding the Pavāraṇā of this monk that you suspend based on suspicion, what do you suspect? In what manner do you suspect it? When do you suspect it? Where do you suspect it? Do you suspect that he has committed a Pārājika offense? Do you suspect that he has committed a Saṅghādisesa offense? Do you suspect that he has committed a Thullaccaya offense… a Pācittiya offense… a Pāṭidesanīya offense… a Dukkaṭa offense… a Dubbhāsita offense? Do you suspect after hearing from a bhikkhu? From a bhikkhunī? From a probationer? From a male novice? From a female novice? From a male lay follower? From a female lay follower? From kings? From royal ministers? From sectarians? From disciples of sectarians?”

397.

397.

Diṭṭhaṃ diṭṭhena sameti, diṭṭhena saṃsandate diṭṭhaṃ;

Diṭṭhaṃ paṭicca na upeti, asuddhaparisaṅkito;

So puggalo paṭiññāya, kātabbā tena pavāraṇā.

What is seen agrees with 'seen'; what is seen corresponds with 'seen'. Depending on what is seen, he does not incur an offense; he is suspected of being impure. For that person, by his admission, the Invitation should be performed with him.

Sutaṃ sutena sameti, sutena saṃsandate sutaṃ;

Sutaṃ paṭicca na upeti, asuddhaparisaṅkito;

So puggalo paṭiññāya, kātabbā tena pavāraṇā.

What is heard agrees with 'heard'; with 'heard' corresponds what is heard. Depending on what is heard, he does not incur an offense; he is suspected of impurity. For that person, by his admission, the Pavāraṇā should be performed with him.

Mutaṃ mutena sameti, mutena saṃsandate mutaṃ;

Mutaṃ paṭicca na upeti, asuddhaparisaṅkito;

So puggalo paṭiññāya, kātabbā tena pavāraṇāti.

What is sensed agrees with 'sensed'; with 'sensed' corresponds what is sensed. Depending on what is sensed, he does not incur an offense; he is suspected of impurity. For that person, by his admission, the Pavāraṇā should be performed with him.

7. Pucchāvibhāgo

7. The Division of Questions

398. Kiṃ te diṭṭhanti katamā pucchā? Kinti te diṭṭhanti katamā pucchā? Kadā te diṭṭhanti katamā pucchā? Kattha te diṭṭhanti katamā pucchā?

398. The question, 'What was seen by you?'—which question is it? The question, 'How was it seen by you?'—which question is it? The question, 'When was it seen by you?'—which question is it? The question, 'Where was it seen by you?'—which question is it?

399. Kiṃ te diṭṭhanti vatthupucchā, vipattipucchā, āpattipucchā, ajjhācārapucchā. Vatthupucchāti – aṭṭhapārājikānaṃ vatthupucchā, tevīsasaṅghādisesānaṃ vatthupucchā, dveaniyatānaṃ vatthupucchā, dvecattārīsanissaggiyānaṃ vatthupucchā, aṭṭhāsītisatapācittiyānaṃ vatthupucchā, dvādasapāṭidesanīyānaṃ vatthupucchā, dukkaṭānaṃ vatthupucchā, dubbhāsitānaṃ vatthupucchā. Vipattipucchāti – sīlavipattipucchā, ācāravipattipucchā, diṭṭhivipattipucchā[T 0.0424], ājīvavipattipucchā. Āpattipucchāti – pārājikāpattipucchā, saṅghādisesāpattipucchā, thullaccayāpattipucchā, pācittiyāpattipucchā, pāṭidesanīyāpattipucchā, dukkaṭāpattipucchā, dubbhāsitāpattipucchā. Ajjhācārapucchāti – dvayaṃdvayasamāpattipucchā.

399. The question, 'What was seen by you?' is a question about the basis, a question about failure, a question about an offense, and a question about misconduct. A question about the basis refers to: a question about the basis of the eight Pārājika offenses, the twenty-three Saṅghādisesa offenses, the two Aniyata offenses, the forty-two Nissaggiya offenses, the one hundred and eighty-eight Pācittiya offenses, the twelve Pāṭidesanīya offenses, the Dukkaṭa offenses, and the Dubbhāsita offenses. A question about failure refers to: a question about failure in virtue, failure in conduct, failure in view, and failure in livelihood. A question about an offense refers to: a question about a Pārājika offense, a Saṅghādisesa offense, a Thullaccaya offense, a Pācittiya offense, a Pāṭidesanīya offense, a Dukkaṭa offense, and a Dubbhāsita offense. A question about misconduct refers to: a question concerning an offense committed by a pair.

400. Kinti te diṭṭhanti liṅgapucchā, iriyāpathapucchā, ākārapucchā, vippakārapucchā. Liṅgapucchāti – dīghaṃ vā rassaṃ vā kaṇhaṃ vā odātaṃ vā. Iriyāpathapucchāti gacchantaṃ vā ṭhitaṃ [V 0.0324] vā nisinnaṃ vā nipannaṃ vā. Ākārapucchāti gihiliṅge [M 0.0301] vā titthiyaliṅge vā pabbajitaliṅge vā. Vippakārapucchāti gacchantaṃ vā ṭhitaṃ vā nisinnaṃ vā nipannaṃ vā.

400. The question, 'In what way was it seen by you?' is a question about appearance, a question about posture, a question about manner, and a question about deviation. A question about appearance is: 'Was it seen as long or short, black or white?' A question about posture is: 'Was it seen going, standing, sitting, or lying down?' A question about manner is: 'Was it seen in the appearance of a householder, in the appearance of a heretic, or in the appearance of a renunciate?' A question about deviation is: 'Was it seen going, standing, sitting, or lying down?'

401. Kadā [P 5.0171] te diṭṭhanti kālapucchā, samayapucchā, divasapucchā, utupucchā. Kālapucchāti pubbaṇhakāle vā majjhanhikakāle vā sāyanhakāle vā. Samayapucchāti pubbaṇhasamaye vā majjhanhikasamaye vā sāyanhasamaye vā. Divasapucchāti purebhattaṃ vā pacchābhattaṃ vā rattiṃ vā divā vā kāḷe vā juṇhe vā. Utupucchāti hemante vā gimhe vā vasse vā vassāne vā (sī.).

401. The question, 'When was it seen by you?' is a question about time, a question about occasion, a question about the day, and a question about the season. A question about time is: 'Was it seen in the morning time, at midday time, or in the evening time?' A question about occasion is: 'Was it seen in the morning, at midday, or in the evening?' A question about the day is: 'Was it seen before the meal or after the meal, at night or in the day, in the dark fortnight or in the bright fortnight?' A question about the season is: 'Was it seen in the cold season, the hot season, or the rainy season?'

402. Kattha te diṭṭhanti ṭhānapucchā, bhūmipucchā, okāsapucchā, padesapucchā. Ṭhānapucchāti bhūmiyā vā pathaviyā vā dharaṇiyā vā jagatiyā vā. Bhūmipucchāti bhūmiyā vā pathaviyā vā pabbate vā pāsāṇe vā pāsāde vā. Okāsapucchāti puratthime vā okāse pacchime [T 0.0425] vā okāse uttare vā okāse dakkhiṇe vā okāse. Padesapucchāti puratthime vā padese pacchime vā padese uttare vā padese dakkhiṇe vā padeseti.

402. The question, 'Where was it seen by you?' is a question about place, a question about ground, a question about space, and a question about region. A question about place is: 'Was it seen on the earth, on the ground, on the land, or on the world?' A question about ground is: 'Was it seen on the earth, on the ground, on a mountain, on a rock, or in a mansion?' A question about space is: 'Was it seen in the eastern space, the western space, the northern space, or the southern space?' A question about region is: 'Was it seen in the eastern region, the western region, the northern region, or the southern region?'

Mahāsaṅgāmo niṭṭhito.

The Great Conflict is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Vatthu nidānaṃ ākāro, pubbāparaṃ katākataṃ;

Kammādhikaraṇañceva, samatho chandagāmi ca.

The basis, the origin, the manner, the sequence, the done and the undone; the act and the legal question, the settlement, and not going the wrong way through desire.

Dosā mohā bhayā ceva, saññā nijjhāpanena ca;

Pekkhā pasāde pakkhomhi, sutatheratarena ca.

Not going the wrong way through hatred, delusion, and fear; making understood and making reflect; considering, inspiring confidence, 'I have gained a faction,' 'I am very learned,' and 'I am the more senior elder.'

Asampattañca sampattaṃ, dhammena vinayena ca;

Satthussa sāsanenāpi, mahāsaṅgāmañāpanāti.
