The unarisen and the arisen; by the Dhamma and the Vinaya, and also by the Teacher's Dispensation. This is what makes the Great Conflict known.

Kathinabhedo

The Division on the Kathina

1. Kathinaatthatādi

1. The Spreading of the Kathina, etc.

403. Kassa [T 0.0426][P 5.0172][M 0.0302][V 0.0325] kathinaṃ kaṭhinaṃ (sī. syā.) anatthataṃ? Kassa kathinaṃ atthataṃ? Kinti kathinaṃ anatthataṃ? Kinti kathinaṃ atthataṃ?

403. For whom is the Kathina not spread? For whom is the Kathina spread? In what manner is the Kathina not spread? In what manner is the Kathina spread?

Kassa kathinaṃ anatthatanti? Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ anatthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ – anatthārakassa ca ananumodakassa ca. Imesaṃ dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ anatthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ.

For whom is the Kathina not spread? The Kathina is not spread for two individuals: for one who does not spread it and for one who does not give approval. For these two individuals, the Kathina is not spread.

Kassa kathinaṃ atthatanti? Dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ – atthārakassa ca anumodakassa ca. Imesaṃ dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ.

For whom is the Kathina spread? The Kathina is spread for two individuals: for one who spreads it and for one who gives approval. For these two individuals, the Kathina is spread.

Kinti kathinaṃ anatthatanti? Catuvīsatiyā ākārehi anatthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na ullikhitamattena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na dhovanamattena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na cīvaravicāraṇamattena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na chedanamattena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na bandhanamattena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na ovaṭṭiyakaraṇamattena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na kaṇḍusakaraṇamattena na gaṇḍusakaraṇamattena (ka.) atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na daḷhīkammakaraṇamattena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na anuvātakaraṇamattena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na paribhaṇḍakaraṇamattena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na ovaddheyyakaraṇamattena na ovaṭṭeyyakaraṇamattena (sī. syā.), na ovadeyyakaraṇamattena (ka.) atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na kambalamaddanamattena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na nimittakatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na [T 0.0427] parikathākatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na kukkukatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na sannidhikatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na nissaggiyena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na akappakatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na aññatra saṅghāṭiyā atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na aññatra uttarāsaṅgena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na aññatra antaravāsakena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ[V 0.0326], na aññatra pañcakena vā atirekapañcakena vā tadaheva sañchinnena samaṇḍalīkatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na aññatra puggalassa atthārā atthataṃ [M 0.0303] hoti kathinaṃ, sammā ce atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ taṃ ce nissīmaṭṭho anumodati. Evampi anatthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ.

In what manner is the Kathina not spread? The Kathina is not spread in twenty-four ways: it is not spread merely by marking out the measurements, not spread merely by washing, not spread merely by preparing the robe-cloth, not spread merely by cutting, not spread merely by tacking it together, not spread merely by sewing the long seam, not spread merely by sewing the short seam, not spread merely by joining the two layers, not spread merely by applying the long border strip, not spread merely by applying the short border strip, not spread merely by applying the upper layer, not spread merely by dyeing it the color of ivory with one dip, not spread with a robe-cloth obtained by making a sign, not spread with a robe-cloth obtained through allusive talk, not spread with a robe-cloth that is temporarily borrowed, not spread with a robe-cloth that is not finished on the same day it was received, not spread with a robe-cloth that has become subject to forfeiture, not spread with a robe that has not had the kappabindu mark applied, not spread apart from the double-layered outer robe (saṅghāṭī), not spread apart from the upper robe (uttarāsaṅga), not spread apart from the lower robe (antaravāsaka), not spread apart from a robe of five panels or more than five panels, which has been well-cut on that very day and made complete with its long and short sections, not spread apart from the spreading by an individual. If the Kathina is properly spread, and a monk standing outside the boundary gives his approval for it, even so, the Kathina is not spread.

Nimittakammaṃ nāma nimittaṃ karoti – “iminā dussena kathinaṃ attharissāmī”ti. Parikathā nāma parikathaṃ karoti – “imāya parikathāya kathinadussaṃ nibbattessāmī”ti. Kukkukataṃ nāma anādiyadānaṃ vuccati. Sannidhi nāma dve sannidhiyo – karaṇasannidhi vā nicayasannidhi vā. Nissaggiyaṃ nāma kayiramāne aruṇaṃ uṭṭhahati udriyati (sī. syā.). Imehi catuvīsatiyā ākārehi anatthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ.

The act of making a sign (`nimittakamma`) is making a sign, thus: 'With this cloth, I will spread the Kathina.' Roundabout talk (`parikathā`) is making roundabout talk, thus: 'Through this roundabout talk, I will produce the Kathina cloth.' What is called `kukkukata` is improper giving. Storing (`sannidhi`) is of two kinds: storing by keeping to make (`karaṇasannidhi`) or storing by having kept overnight (`nicayasannidhi`). Forfeitable (`nissaggiya`) is when dawn breaks while it is being made. By these twenty-four modes, the Kathina is not spread.

Kinti kathinaṃ atthatanti? Sattarasahi ākārehi atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ. Ahatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, ahatakappena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, pilotikāya atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, paṃsukūlena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, pāpaṇikena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, animittakatena atthataṃ [T 0.0428] hoti kathinaṃ, aparikathākatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, akukkukatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, asannidhikatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, anissaggiyena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, kappakatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, saṅghāṭiyā atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, uttarāsaṅgena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, antaravāsakena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, pañcakena vā atirekapañcakena vā tadaheva sañchinnena samaṇḍalīkatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, puggalassa atthārā atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, sammā ce atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, taṃ ce sīmaṭṭho anumodati, evampi atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ. Imehi sattarasahi ākārehi atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ.

How is the Kathina spread? The Kathina is spread in seventeen modes. The Kathina is spread with new cloth; it is spread with cloth like new; it is spread with worn-out cloth; it is spread with rags-from-the-dust-heap; it is spread with cloth found at a shop door; it is spread with cloth obtained without making a sign; it is spread with cloth not produced by roundabout talk; it is spread with cloth not borrowed; it is spread with cloth not stored; it is spread with a robe that is not forfeitable; it is spread with a robe marked with a `kappabindu`; it is spread with the double-layered robe; it is spread with the upper robe; it is spread with the lower garment; it is spread with a robe of five or more than five sections, well cut and made with panels on that very day; it is spread by the spreading of an individual. And if the Kathina is well spread, and if a monk standing within the boundary rejoices in it, even so is the Kathina spread. In these seventeen modes, the Kathina is spread.

Saha kathinassa atthārā kati dhammā jāyanti? Saha kathinassa atthārā pannarasa dhammā jāyanti – aṭṭha mātikā, dve palibodhā, pañcānisaṃsā. Saha kathinassa atthārā ime pannarasa dhammā jāyanti.

Together with the spreading of the Kathina, how many phenomena arise? Together with the spreading of the Kathina, fifteen phenomena arise: eight headings (`mātikā`), two impediments (`palibodhā`), and five benefits (`ānisaṃsā`). Together with the spreading of the Kathina, these fifteen phenomena arise.

2. Kathinaanantarapaccayādi

2. The Kathina: The Immediacy Condition and so forth

404. Payogassa [P 5.0173] katame dhammā anantarapaccayena paccayo, samanantarapaccayena paccayo, nissayapaccayena paccayo, upanissayapaccayena paccayo[M 0.0304], purejātapaccayena paccayo, pacchājātapaccayena paccayo, sahajātapaccayena paccayo? Pubbakaraṇassa katame dhammā anantarapaccayena [V 0.0327] paccayo…pe… paccuddhārassa katame dhammā… adhiṭṭhānassa katame dhammā… atthārassa katame dhammā… mātikānañca palibodhānañca katame dhammā… vatthussa katame dhammā anantarapaccayena paccayo, samanantarapaccayena paccayo, nissayapaccayena paccayo, upanissayapaccayena [T 0.0429] paccayo, purejātapaccayena paccayo, pacchājātapaccayena paccayo, sahajātapaccayena paccayo?

404. Which phenomena are a condition for effort by way of immediacy condition, by way of contiguity condition, by way of dependence condition, by way of strong dependence condition, by way of pre-nascence condition, by way of post-nascence condition, by way of conascence condition? Which phenomena are a condition for the preliminary action by way of immediacy condition… and so on… which phenomena for withdrawal… which phenomena for determination… which phenomena for spreading… which phenomena for the mātikās and impediments… which phenomena are a condition for the cloth by way of immediacy condition, by way of contiguity condition, by way of dependence condition, by way of strong dependence condition, by way of pre-nascence condition, by way of post-nascence condition, by way of conascence condition?

Pubbakaraṇaṃ payogassa anantarapaccayena paccayo, samanantarapaccayena paccayo, nissayapaccayena paccayo, upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Payogo pubbakaraṇassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. Pubbakaraṇaṃ payogassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. Pannarasa dhammā sahajātapaccayena paccayo. Paccuddhāro pubbakaraṇassa anantarapaccayena paccayo, samanantarapaccayena paccayo, nissayapaccayena paccayo, upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Pubbakaraṇaṃ paccuddhārassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. Paccuddhāro pubbakaraṇassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. Pannarasa dhammā sahajātapaccayena paccayo. Adhiṭṭhānaṃ paccuddhārassa anantarapaccayena paccayo, samanantarapaccayena paccayo, nissayapaccayena paccayo, upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Paccuddhāro adhiṭṭhānassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. Adhiṭṭhānaṃ paccuddhārassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. Pannarasa dhammā sahajātapaccayena paccayo. Atthāro adhiṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo, samanantarapaccayena paccayo, nissayapaccayena paccayo, upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Adhiṭṭhānaṃ atthārassa purejātapaccayena [T 0.0430] paccayo. Atthāro adhiṭṭhānassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. Pannarasa dhammā sahajātapaccayena paccayo. Mātikā ca palibodhā ca atthārassa anantarapaccayena paccayo, samanantarapaccayena paccayo, nissayapaccayena paccayo, upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Atthāro mātikānañca palibodhānañca purejātapaccayena paccayo. Mātikā ca palibodhā ca atthārassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. Pannarasa dhammā sahajātapaccayena paccayo. Āsā [P 5.0174] ca anāsā ca vatthussa anantarapaccayena paccayo, samanantarapaccayena paccayo, nissayapaccayena paccayo[M 0.0305], upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Vatthu āsānañca anāsānañca purejātapaccayena paccayo. Āsā ca anāsā ca vatthussa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. Pannarasa dhammā sahajātapaccayena paccayo.

Preliminary action is a condition for effort by way of immediacy condition, by way of contiguity condition, by way of dependence condition, and by way of strong dependence condition. Effort is a condition for preliminary action by way of pre-nascence condition. Preliminary action is a condition for effort by way of post-nascence condition. Fifteen phenomena are a condition by way of conascence condition. Withdrawal is a condition for preliminary action by way of immediacy condition, by way of contiguity condition, by way of dependence condition, and by way of strong dependence condition. Preliminary action is a condition for withdrawal by way of pre-nascence condition. Withdrawal is a condition for preliminary action by way of post-nascence condition. Fifteen phenomena are a condition by way of conascence condition. Determination is a condition for withdrawal by way of immediacy condition, by way of contiguity condition, by way of dependence condition, and by way of strong dependence condition. Withdrawal is a condition for determination by way of pre-nascence condition. Determination is a condition for withdrawal by way of post-nascence condition. Fifteen phenomena are a condition by way of conascence condition. The spreading of the Kathina is a condition for determination by way of immediacy condition, by way of contiguity condition, by way of dependence condition, and by way of strong dependence condition. Determination is a condition for the spreading of the Kathina by way of pre-nascence condition. The spreading of the Kathina is a condition for determination by way of post-nascence condition. Fifteen phenomena are a condition by way of conascence condition. The mātikās and impediments are conditions for the spreading of the Kathina by way of immediacy condition, by way of contiguity condition, by way of dependence condition, and by way of strong dependence condition. The spreading of the Kathina is a condition for the mātikās and impediments by way of pre-nascence condition. The mātikās and impediments are conditions for the spreading of the Kathina by way of post-nascence condition. Fifteen phenomena are a condition by way of conascence condition. Hope and absence of hope are conditions for the cloth by way of immediacy condition, by way of contiguity condition, by way of dependence condition, and by way of strong dependence condition. The cloth is a condition for hope and for absence of hope by way of pre-nascence condition. Hope and absence of hope are conditions for the cloth by way of post-nascence condition. Fifteen phenomena are a condition by way of conascence condition.

3. Pubbakaraṇanidānādivibhāgo

3. The Division on Preliminary Action, Cause, and so forth

405. Pubbakaraṇaṃ kiṃnidānaṃ, kiṃsamudayaṃ, kiṃjātikaṃ, kiṃpabhavaṃ, kiṃsambhāraṃ, kiṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ[V 0.0328]? Paccuddhāro kiṃnidāno, kiṃsamudayo, kiṃjātiko, kiṃpabhavo, kiṃsambhāro, kiṃsamuṭṭhāno? Adhiṭṭhānaṃ kiṃnidānaṃ, kiṃsamudayaṃ, kiṃjātikaṃ, kiṃpabhavaṃ, kiṃsambhāraṃ, kiṃsamuṭṭhānaṃ? Atthāro kiṃnidāno, kiṃsamudayo, kiṃjātiko, kiṃpabhavo, kiṃsambhāro, kiṃsamuṭṭhāno? Mātikā ca palibodhā ca kiṃnidānā, kiṃsamudayā, kiṃjātikā, kiṃpabhavā, kiṃsambhārā kiṃsamuṭṭhānā? Āsā ca anāsā [T 0.0431] ca kiṃnidānā, kiṃsamudayā, kiṃjātikā, kiṃpabhavā, kiṃsambhārā, kiṃsamuṭṭhānā?

405. Preliminary action: what is its cause, what is its arising, what is its nature, what is its source, what are its components, what is its origination? Revocation: what is its cause, what is its arising, what is its nature, what is its source, what are its components, what is its origination? Determination: what is its cause, what is its arising, what is its nature, what is its source, what are its components, what is its origination? The spreading: what is its cause, what is its arising, what is its nature, what is its source, what are its components, what is its origination? The mātikā and the impediments: what are their causes, what are their arisings, what are their natures, what are their sources, what are their components, what are their originations? Hope and non-hope: what are their causes, what are their arisings, what are their natures, what are their sources, what are their components, what are their originations?

Pubbakaraṇaṃ payoganidānaṃ, payogasamudayaṃ, payogajātikaṃ, payogapabhavaṃ, payogasambhāraṃ, payogasamuṭṭhānaṃ. Paccuddhāro pubbakaraṇanidāno, pubbakaraṇasamudayo, pubbakaraṇajātiko, pubbakaraṇapabhavo, pubbakaraṇasambhāro, pubbakaraṇasamuṭṭhāno. Adhiṭṭhānaṃ paccuddhāranidānaṃ, paccuddhārasamudayaṃ, paccuddhārajātikaṃ, paccuddhārapabhavaṃ, paccuddhārasambhāraṃ, paccuddhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ. Atthāro adhiṭṭhānanidāno, adhiṭṭhānasamudayo, adhiṭṭhānajātiko, adhiṭṭhānapabhavo, adhiṭṭhānasambhāro, adhiṭṭhānasamuṭṭhāno. Mātikā ca palibodhā ca atthāranidānā, atthārasamudayā, atthārajātikā, atthārapabhavā, atthārasambhārā, atthārasamuṭṭhānā. Āsā ca anāsā ca vatthunidānā, vatthusamudayā, vatthujātikā, vatthupabhavā, vatthusambhārā, vatthusamuṭṭhānā.

Preliminary action has effort as its cause, effort as its arising, effort as its nature, effort as its source, effort as its components, and effort as its origination. Revocation has preliminary action as its cause, preliminary action as its arising, preliminary action as its nature, preliminary action as its source, preliminary action as its components, and preliminary action as its origination. Determination has revocation as its cause, revocation as its arising, revocation as its nature, revocation as its source, revocation as its components, and revocation as its origination. The spreading has determination as its cause, determination as its arising, determination as its nature, determination as its source, determination as its components, and determination as its origination. The mātikā and the impediments have the spreading as their cause, the spreading as their arising, the spreading as their nature, the spreading as their source, the spreading as their components, and the spreading as their origination. Hope and non-hope have the cloth as their cause, the cloth as their arising, the cloth as their nature, the cloth as their source, the cloth as their components, and the cloth as their origination.

406. Payogo kiṃnidāno, kiṃsamudayo, kiṃjātiko, kiṃpabhavo, kiṃsambhāro, kiṃsamuṭṭhāno, pubbakaraṇaṃ…pe… paccuddhāro… adhiṭṭhānaṃ… atthāro… mātikā ca palibodhā ca… vatthu… āsā ca anāsā ca kiṃnidānā, kiṃsamudayā, kiṃjātikā, kiṃpabhavā, kiṃsambhārā, kiṃsamuṭṭhānā?

406. Effort: what is its cause, its arising, its nature, its source, its components, and its origination? And for preliminary action… and so on… revocation… determination… the spreading… the mātikā and the impediments… the cloth… hope and non-hope—what are their causes, their arisings, their natures, their sources, their components, and their originations?

Payogo [M 0.0306] hetunidāno, hetusamudayo, hetujātiko, hetupabhavo, hetusambhāro, hetusamuṭṭhāno. Pubbakaraṇaṃ…pe… paccuddhāro… adhiṭṭhānaṃ… atthāro [T 0.0432]… mātikā ca palibodhā ca… vatthu… āsā ca anāsā ca hetunidānā, hetusamudayā, hetujātikā, hetupabhavā, hetusambhārā, hetusamuṭṭhānā.

Effort has cause as its cause, cause as its arising, cause as its nature, cause as its source, cause as its components, and cause as its origination. Preliminary action… and so on… revocation… determination… the spreading… the mātikā and the impediments… the cloth… hope and non-hope have cause as their cause, cause as their arising, cause as their nature, cause as their source, cause as their components, and cause as their origination.

407. Payogo kiṃnidāno, kiṃsamudayo, kiṃjātiko, kiṃpabhavo, kiṃsambhāro, kiṃsamuṭṭhāno? Pubbakaraṇaṃ…pe… paccuddhāro… adhiṭṭhānaṃ… atthāro… mātikā ca palibodhā ca… vatthu… āsā ca anāsā ca kiṃnidānā, kiṃsamudayā, kiṃjātikā, kiṃpabhavā, kiṃsambhārā, kiṃsamuṭṭhānā?

407. Effort: what is its cause, its arising, its nature, its source, its components, and its origination? And for preliminary action… and so on… revocation… determination… the spreading… the mātikā and the impediments… the cloth… hope and non-hope—what are their causes, their arisings, their natures, their sources, their components, and their originations?

Payogo [V 0.0329] paccayanidāno, paccayasamudayo, paccayajātiko, paccayapabhavo, paccayasambhāro, paccayasamuṭṭhāno. Pubbakaraṇaṃ…pe… paccuddhāro… adhiṭṭhānaṃ… atthāro… mātikā ca palibodhā ca… vatthu… āsā ca anāsā ca paccayanidānā, paccayasamudayā, paccayajātikā, paccayapabhavā, paccayasambhārā, paccayasamuṭṭhānā.

Effort has condition as its cause, condition as its arising, condition as its nature, condition as its source, condition as its components, and condition as its origination. Preliminary action… and so on… revocation… determination… the spreading… the mātikā and the impediments… the cloth… hope and non-hope have condition as their cause, condition as their arising, condition as their nature, condition as their source, condition as their components, and condition as their origination.

408. Pubbakaraṇaṃ katihi dhammehi saṅgahitaṃ? Pubbakaraṇaṃ sattahi dhammehi saṅgahitaṃ. Dhovanena, vicāraṇena, chedanena, bandhanena, sibbanena, rajanena, kappakaraṇena – pubbakaraṇaṃ imehi sattahi dhammehi saṅgahitaṃ.

408. By how many factors is the preliminary action comprised? The preliminary action is comprised of seven factors: washing, preparing, cutting, tacking, sewing, dyeing, and applying the determination mark. The preliminary action is comprised of these seven factors.

Paccuddhāro katihi dhammehi saṅgahito? Paccuddhāro tīhi dhammehi saṅgahito – saṅghāṭiyā, uttarāsaṅgena, antaravāsakena.

By how many factors is the revocation comprised? The revocation is comprised of three factors: the double-layered robe, the upper robe, and the lower robe.

Adhiṭṭhānaṃ katihi dhammehi saṅgahitaṃ? Adhiṭṭhānaṃ tīhi dhammehi saṅgahitaṃ – saṅghāṭiyā, uttarāsaṅgena, antaravāsakena.

By how many factors is the determination comprised? The determination is comprised of three factors: the double-layered robe, the upper robe, and the lower robe.

Atthāro katihi dhammehi saṅgahito? Atthāro ekena [T 0.0433] dhammena saṅgahito – vacībhedena.

By how many factors is the spreading comprised? The spreading is comprised of one factor: by verbal declaration.

Kathinassa kati mūlāni, kati vatthūni, kati bhūmiyo? Kathinassa [P 5.0175] ekaṃ mūlaṃ – saṅgho; tīṇi vatthūni – saṅghāṭi, uttarāsaṅgo, antaravāsako, cha bhūmiyo – khomaṃ, kappāsikaṃ, koseyyaṃ, kambalaṃ, sāṇaṃ, bhaṅgaṃ.

How many roots does the Kathina have, how many objects, how many grounds? The Kathina has one root: the Saṅgha; three objects: the double-layered robe, the upper robe, and the lower robe; six grounds: linen, cotton, silk, wool, hemp, and mixed-fiber cloth.

Kathinassa [M 0.0307] ko ādi, kiṃ majjhe, kiṃ pariyosānaṃ? Kathinassa pubbakaraṇaṃ ādi, kriyā majjhe, atthāro pariyosānaṃ.

What is the beginning of the Kathina, what is the middle, what is the conclusion? The preliminary acts are the beginning of the Kathina, the procedure of relinquishing and determining is the middle, and the spreading is the conclusion.

409. Katihaṅgehi samannāgato puggalo abhabbo kathinaṃ attharituṃ? Katihaṅgehi samannāgato puggalo bhabbo kathinaṃ attharituṃ? Aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgato puggalo abhabbo kathinaṃ attharituṃ. Aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgato puggalo bhabbo kathinaṃ attharituṃ. Katamehi aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgato puggalo abhabbo kathinaṃ attharituṃ? Pubbakaraṇaṃ na jānāti, paccuddhāraṃ na jānāti, adhiṭṭhānaṃ na jānāti, atthāraṃ na jānāti, mātikaṃ na jānāti, palibodhaṃ na jānāti, uddhāraṃ na jānāti, ānisaṃsaṃ na jānāti – imehi aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgato puggalo [V 0.0330] abhabbo kathinaṃ attharituṃ. Katamehi aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgato puggalo bhabbo kathinaṃ attharituṃ? Pubbakaraṇaṃ jānāti, paccuddhāraṃ jānāti, adhiṭṭhānaṃ jānāti, atthāraṃ jānāti, mātikaṃ jānāti, palibodhaṃ jānāti, uddhāraṃ jānāti, ānisaṃsaṃ jānāti – imehi aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgato puggalo bhabbo kathinaṃ attharituṃ.

409. Endowed with how many factors is a person unfit to spread the Kathina? Endowed with how many factors is a person fit to spread the Kathina? A person endowed with eight factors is unfit to spread the Kathina. A person endowed with eight factors is fit to spread the Kathina. Endowed with which eight factors is a person unfit to spread the Kathina? One does not know the preliminary acts, one does not know the relinquishing, one does not know the determination, one does not know the spreading, one does not know the matrix, one does not know the impediments, one does not know the withdrawal, one does not know the benefits—a person endowed with these eight factors is unfit to spread the Kathina. Endowed with which eight factors is a person fit to spread the Kathina? One knows the preliminary acts, one knows the relinquishing, one knows the determination, one knows the spreading, one knows the matrix, one knows the impediments, one knows the withdrawal, one knows the benefits—a person endowed with these eight factors is fit to spread the Kathina.

410. Katinaṃ [T 0.0434] puggalānaṃ kathinatthārā na ruhanti? Katinaṃ puggalānaṃ kathinatthārā ruhanti? Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ kathinatthārā na ruhanti. Tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ kathinatthārā ruhanti. Katamesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ kathinatthārā na ruhanti? Nissīmaṭṭho anumodati, anumodento na vācaṃ bhindati, vācaṃ bhindanto na paraṃ viññāpeti – imesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ kathinatthārā na ruhanti. Katamesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ kathinatthārā ruhanti? Sīmaṭṭho anumodati, anumodento vācaṃ bhindati, vācaṃ bhindanto paraṃ viññāpeti – imesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ kathinatthārā ruhanti.

410. For how many individuals does the spreading of the Kathina not take effect? For how many individuals does the spreading of the Kathina take effect? For three individuals, the spreading of the Kathina does not take effect. For three individuals, the spreading of the Kathina takes effect. For which three individuals does the spreading of the Kathina not take effect? One who gives approval while standing outside the boundary; one who, while giving approval, does not make a verbal declaration; and one who, while making a verbal declaration, does not inform another—for these three individuals, the spreading of the Kathina does not take effect. For which three individuals does the spreading of the Kathina take effect? One who gives approval while standing within the boundary; one who, while giving approval, makes a verbal declaration; and one who, while making a verbal declaration, informs another—for these three individuals, the spreading of the Kathina takes effect.

411. Kati kathinatthārā na ruhanti? Kati kathinatthārā ruhanti? Tayo kathinatthārā na ruhanti. Tayo kathinatthārā ruhanti. Katame tayo kathinatthārā na ruhanti? Vatthuvipannañceva hoti, kālavipannañca, karaṇavipannañca – ime tayo kathinatthārā na ruhanti. Katame tayo kathinatthārā ruhanti? Vatthusampannañceva hoti, kālasampannañca, karaṇasampannañca – ime tayo kathinatthārā ruhanti.

411. How many spreadings of the Kathina do not take effect? How many spreadings of the Kathina take effect? Three spreadings of the Kathina do not take effect. Three spreadings of the Kathina take effect. Which three spreadings of the Kathina do not take effect? When the material is defective, the time is defective, and the procedure is defective—these three spreadings of the Kathina do not take effect. Which three spreadings of the Kathina take effect? When the material is complete, the time is complete, and the procedure is complete—these three spreadings of the Kathina take effect.

4. Kathinādijānitabbavibhāgo

4. Analysis of What Should Be Known Regarding the Kathina, etc.

412. Kathinaṃ [M 0.0308] jānitabbaṃ, kathinatthāro jānitabbo, kathinassa atthāramāso jānitabbo, kathinassa atthāravipatti jānitabbā, kathinassa atthārasampatti jānitabbā, nimittakammaṃ jānitabbaṃ, parikathā jānitabbā, kukkukataṃ jānitabbaṃ, sannidhi jānitabbā, nissaggiyaṃ [T 0.0435] jānitabbaṃ.

412. The Kathina should be known; the spreading of the Kathina should be known; the month for spreading the Kathina should be known; the failure of the spreading of the Kathina should be known; the completion of the spreading of the Kathina should be known; the act of making a sign should be known; allusive speech should be known; giving disrespectfully should be known; storing up should be known; forfeiture should be known.

Kathinaṃ [P 5.0176] jānitabbanti tesaññeva dhammānaṃ saṅgaho samavāyo nāmaṃ nāmakammaṃ nāmadheyyaṃ nirutti byañjanaṃ abhilāpo yadidaṃ kathinanti.

As for 'The Kathina should be known': that which is called 'Kathina' is the collection, the combination, the name, the act of naming, the designation, the expression, the manifestation, and the term for those very same phenomena.

Kathinassa [V 0.0331] atthāramāso jānitabboti vassānassa pacchimo māso jānitabbo.

As for 'The month for spreading the Kathina should be known': the last month of the rainy season should be known.

Kathinassa atthāravipatti jānitabbāti catuvīsatiyā ākārehi kathinassa atthāravipatti jānitabbā.

As for 'The failure of the spreading of the Kathina should be known': the failure of the spreading of the Kathina should be known by twenty-four modes.

Kathinassa atthārasampatti jānitabbāti sattarasahi ākārehi kathinassa atthārasampatti jānitabbā.

As for 'The completion of the spreading of the Kathina should be known': the completion of the spreading of the Kathina should be known by seventeen modes.

Nimittakammaṃ jānitabbanti nimittaṃ karoti iminā dussena kathinaṃ attharissāmīti.

As for 'The act of making a sign should be known': one makes a sign thus, 'With this cloth, I will spread the Kathina.'

Parikathā jānitabbāti parikathaṃ karoti imāya parikathāya kathinadussaṃ nibbattessāmīti.

As for 'Allusive speech should be known': one makes allusive speech thus, 'By this allusive speech, I will cause a Kathina-cloth to arise.'

Kukkukataṃ jānitabbanti anādiyadānaṃ jānitabbaṃ.

As for 'Giving disrespectfully should be known': disrespectful giving should be known.

Sannidhi jānitabbāti dve sannidhiyo jānitabbā – karaṇasannidhi vā nicayasannidhi vā.

As for 'Storing should be known': two kinds of storing should be known—storing for making or storing by accumulation.

Nissaggiyaṃ jānitabbanti kariyamāne aruṇaṃ uṭṭhahati.

As for 'What is to be forfeited should be known': dawn rises while it is being made.

Kathinatthāro jānitabboti sace saṅghassa kathinadussaṃ uppannaṃ hoti, saṅghena kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbaṃ, atthārakena kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbaṃ, anumodakena kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbaṃ.

As for 'The spreading of the Kathina should be known': if a Kathina-cloth has arisen for the Sangha, how should the Sangha proceed? How should the one who spreads it proceed? How should the one who gives approval proceed?

413. Saṅghena ñattidutiyena kammena kathinatthārakassa bhikkhuno dātabbaṃ, tena kathinatthārakena bhikkhunā tadaheva dhovitvā vimajjitvā vicāretvā chinditvā sibbetvā rajitvā kappaṃ katvā kathinaṃ attharitabbaṃ. Sace [M 0.0309] saṅghāṭiyā kathinaṃ attharitukāmo hoti, porāṇikā saṅghāṭi paccuddharitabbā[T 0.0436], navā saṅghāṭi adhiṭṭhātabbā. Imāya saṅghāṭiyā kathinaṃ attharāmīti vācā bhinditabbā. Sace uttarāsaṅgena kathinaṃ attharitukāmo hoti, porāṇako uttarāsaṅgo paccuddharitabbo, navo uttarāsaṅgo adhiṭṭhātabbo. Iminā uttarāsaṅgena kathinaṃ attharāmīti vācā bhinditabbā. Sace antaravāsakena kathinaṃ attharitukāmo hoti, porāṇako antaravāsako paccuddharitabbo, navo antaravāsako adhiṭṭhātabbo. Iminā antaravāsakena kathinaṃ attharāmīti vācā bhinditabbā. Tena kathinatthārakena bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ [V 0.0332] karitvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – “atthataṃ, bhante, saṅghassa kathinaṃ, dhammiko kathinatthāro, anumodathā”ti. Tehi anumodakehi bhikkhūhi ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā añjaliṃ [P 5.0177] paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – “atthataṃ, āvuso, saṅghassa kathinaṃ, dhammiko kathinatthāro, anumodāmā”ti. Tena kathinatthārakena bhikkhunā sambahule bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā añjaliṃ [T 0.0437] paggahetvā evamassu vacanīyā – “atthataṃ, bhante, saṅghassa kathinaṃ, dhammiko kathinatthāro, anumodathā”ti. Tehi anumodakehi bhikkhūhi ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – “atthataṃ, āvuso, saṅghassa kathinaṃ, dhammiko kathinatthāro anumodāmā”ti. Tena kathinatthārakena bhikkhunā ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – “atthataṃ, āvuso, saṅghassa kathinaṃ, dhammiko kathinatthāro, anumodāhī”ti. Tena anumodakena bhikkhunā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – “atthataṃ, āvuso, saṅghassa kathinaṃ, dhammiko kathinatthāro, anumodāmī”ti.

413. The Saṅgha, by a formal act preceded by a motion, should give it to the bhikkhu who is to spread the kathina. That bhikkhu who is to spread the kathina, on that very day, having washed, scrubbed, prepared, cut, sewn, dyed, and made the kappa-mark on it, should spread the kathina. If he wishes to spread the kathina with the outer robe, the old outer robe should be relinquished, and the new outer robe should be determined upon. The words, 'I spread the kathina with this outer robe,' should be uttered. If he wishes to spread the kathina with the upper robe, the old upper robe should be relinquished, and the new upper robe should be determined upon. The words, 'I spread the kathina with this upper robe,' should be uttered. If he wishes to spread the kathina with the lower robe, the old lower robe should be relinquished, and the new lower robe should be determined upon. The words, 'I spread the kathina with this lower robe,' should be uttered. That bhikkhu who spreads the kathina should approach the Saṅgha, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, raise his joined palms, and say: 'Venerable sirs, the Saṅgha's kathina has been spread. The spreading of the kathina is lawful. Please rejoice.' Those bhikkhus who rejoice should arrange their upper robes over one shoulder, raise their joined palms, and say: 'Friends, the Saṅgha's kathina has been spread. The spreading of the kathina is lawful. We rejoice.' That bhikkhu who spreads the kathina should approach many bhikkhus, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, raise his joined palms, and say: 'Venerable sirs, the Saṅgha's kathina has been spread. The spreading of the kathina is lawful. Please rejoice.' Those bhikkhus who rejoice should arrange their upper robes over one shoulder, raise their joined palms, and say: 'Friends, the Saṅgha's kathina has been spread. The spreading of the kathina is lawful. We rejoice.' That bhikkhu who spreads the kathina should approach a single bhikkhu, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, raise his joined palms, and say: 'Friend, the Saṅgha's kathina has been spread. The spreading of the kathina is lawful. Please rejoice.' That bhikkhu who rejoices should arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, raise his joined palms, and say: 'Friend, the Saṅgha's kathina has been spread. The spreading of the kathina is lawful. I rejoice.'

5. Puggalassevakathinatthāro

5. The Spreading of the Kathina by an Individual Only

414. Saṅgho kathinaṃ attharati, gaṇo kathinaṃ attharati, puggalo kathinaṃ attharatīti. Na saṅgho kathinaṃ attharati, na gaṇo kathinaṃ attharati, puggalo kathinaṃ attharatīti. Hañci na saṅgho kathinaṃ attharati, na gaṇo kathinaṃ attharati, puggalo kathinaṃ attharati. Saṅghassa anatthataṃ [M 0.0310] hoti kathinaṃ, gaṇassa anatthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, puggalassa atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ. Saṅgho pātimokkhaṃ uddisati gaṇo pātimokkhaṃ uddisati puggalo pātimokkhaṃ uddisatīti na saṅgho pātimokkhaṃ uddisati, na gaṇo pātimokkhaṃ uddisati, puggalo pātimokkhaṃ uddisatīti. Hañci na saṅgho pātimokkhaṃ uddisati, na gaṇo pātimokkhaṃ uddisati, puggalo pātimokkhaṃ uddisati. Saṅghassa anuddiṭṭhaṃ hoti pātimokkhaṃ, gaṇassa anuddiṭṭhaṃ hoti pātimokkhaṃ, puggalassa uddiṭṭhaṃ hoti pātimokkhaṃ. Saṅghassa sāmaggiyā gaṇassa sāmaggiyā puggalassa uddesā saṅghassa uddiṭṭhaṃ hoti pātimokkhaṃ, gaṇassa uddiṭṭhaṃ hoti pātimokkhaṃ, puggalassa uddiṭṭhaṃ hoti pātimokkhaṃ. Evameva na saṅgho kathinaṃ attharati, na [T 0.0438] gaṇo kathinaṃ attharati, puggalo kathinaṃ attharati. Saṅghassa anumodanāya gaṇassa anumodanāya puggalassa atthārā saṅghassa atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, gaṇassa atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, puggalassa atthataṃ hoti kathinanti.

414. Does the Saṅgha spread the kathina? Does a group spread the kathina? Does an individual spread the kathina? The Saṅgha does not spread the kathina; a group does not spread the kathina; an individual spreads the kathina. If the Saṅgha does not spread the kathina, and a group does not spread the kathina, but an individual spreads the kathina, then for the Saṅgha the kathina is not spread, for a group the kathina is not spread, but for the individual the kathina is spread. Does the Saṅgha recite the Pātimokkha? Does a group recite the Pātimokkha? Does an individual recite the Pātimokkha? The Saṅgha does not recite the Pātimokkha; a group does not recite the Pātimokkha; an individual recites the Pātimokkha. If the Saṅgha does not recite the Pātimokkha, and a group does not recite the Pātimokkha, but an individual recites the Pātimokkha, then for the Saṅgha the Pātimokkha is unrecited, for a group the Pātimokkha is unrecited, but for the individual the Pātimokkha is recited. Through the harmony of the Saṅgha, through the harmony of a group, and due to the individual’s recitation, the Pātimokkha is recited for the Saṅgha, is recited for a group, and is recited for the individual. In this very same way, the Saṅgha does not spread the kathina; a group does not spread the kathina; an individual spreads the kathina. Through the approval of the Saṅgha, through the approval of a group, and due to the individual’s spreading, the kathina is spread for the Saṅgha, is spread for a group, and is spread for the individual.

6. Palibodhapañhābyākaraṇaṃ

6. Questions and Answers on the Impediments

415.

415.

Pakkamanantiko [V 0.0333] kathinuddhāro, vutto ādiccabandhunā;

Etañca tāhaṃ pucchāmi, katamo palibodho paṭhamaṃ chijjati.

The removal of the kathina which has departure as its end was declared by the Kinsman of the Sun. And this I ask you: which impediment is severed first?

Pakkamanantiko [P 5.0178] kathinuddhāro, vutto ādiccabandhunā;

Etañca tāhaṃ vissajjissaṃ, cīvarapalibodho paṭhamaṃ chijjati;

Tassa saha bahisīmagamanā, āvāsapalibodho chijjati.

The removal of the kathina which has departure as its end was declared by the Kinsman of the Sun. And this I will answer: the robe-impediment is severed first. Together with his going outside the boundary, the dwelling-impediment is severed.

Niṭṭhānantiko kathinuddhāro, vutto ādiccabandhunā;

Etañca tāhaṃ pucchāmi, katamo palibodho paṭhamaṃ chijjati.

The removal of the kathina which has completion as its end was declared by the Kinsman of the Sun. And this I ask you: which impediment is severed first?

Niṭṭhānantiko kathinuddhāro, vutto ādiccabandhunā;

Etañca tāhaṃ vissajjissaṃ, āvāsapalibodho [T 0.0439] paṭhamaṃ chijjati;

Cīvare niṭṭhite cīvarapalibodho chijjati.

The removal of the kathina which has completion as its end was declared by the Kinsman of the Sun. And this I will answer: the dwelling-impediment is severed first. When the robe is completed, the robe-impediment is severed.

Sanniṭṭhānantiko kathinuddhāro, vutto ādiccabandhunā;

Etañca tāhaṃ pucchāmi, katamo palibodho paṭhamaṃ chijjati.

The removal of the kathina which has determination as its end was declared by the Kinsman of the Sun. And this I ask you: which impediment is severed first?

Sanniṭṭhānantiko kathinuddhāro, vutto ādiccabandhunā;

Etañca tāhaṃ vissajjissaṃ, dve palibodhā apubbaṃ acarimaṃ chijjanti.

The removal of the kathina which has determination as its end was declared by the Kinsman of the Sun. And this I will answer: the two impediments are severed simultaneously.

Nāsanantiko [M 0.0311] kathinuddhāro, vutto ādiccabandhunā;

Etañca tāhaṃ pucchāmi, katamo palibodho paṭhamaṃ chijjati.

The removal of the kathina which has loss as its end was declared by the Kinsman of the Sun. And this I ask you: which impediment is severed first?

Nāsanantiko kathinuddhāro, vutto ādiccabandhunā;

Etañca tāhaṃ vissajjissaṃ, āvāsapalibodho paṭhamaṃ chijjati;

Cīvare naṭṭhe cīvarapalibodho chijjati.

The withdrawal of the Kathina with loss as its end was declared by the Kinsman of the Sun. And this I will answer you: the dwelling-impediment is severed first. When the robe is lost, the robe-impediment is severed.

Savanantiko [T 0.0440][V 0.0334] kathinuddhāro, vutto ādiccabandhunā;

Etañca tāhaṃ pucchāmi, katamo palibodho paṭhamaṃ chijjati.

The withdrawal of the Kathina with hearing as its end was declared by the Kinsman of the Sun. And this I ask you: which impediment is severed first?

Savanantiko kathinuddhāro, vutto ādiccabandhunā;

Etañca tāhaṃ vissajjissaṃ, cīvarapalibodho paṭhamaṃ chijjati;

Tassa saha savanena, āvāsapalibodho chijjati.

The withdrawal of the Kathina with hearing as its end was declared by the Kinsman of the Sun. And this I will answer you: the robe-impediment is severed first. Together with the hearing of it, the dwelling-impediment is severed.

Āsāvacchediko kathinuddhāro, vutto ādiccabandhunā;

Etañca tāhaṃ pucchāmi, katamo palibodho paṭhamaṃ chijjati.

The withdrawal of the Kathina with the cutting off of hope as its end was declared by the Kinsman of the Sun. And this I ask you: which impediment is severed first?

Āsāvacchediko kathinuddhāro, vutto ādiccabandhunā;

Etañca tāhaṃ vissajjissaṃ, āvāsapalibodho paṭhamaṃ chijjati;

Cīvarāsāya upacchinnāya cīvarapalibodho chijjati.

The withdrawal of the Kathina with the cutting off of hope as its end was declared by the Kinsman of the Sun. And this I will answer you: the dwelling-impediment is severed first. When the hope for a robe is cut off, the robe-impediment is severed.

Sīmātikkamanantiko kathinuddhāro, vutto ādiccabandhunā;

Etañca tāhaṃ pucchāmi, katamo [T 0.0441] palibodho paṭhamaṃ chijjati.

The withdrawal of the Kathina with transgression of the boundary as its end was declared by the Kinsman of the Sun. And this I ask you: which impediment is severed first?

Sīmātikkamanantiko kathinuddhāro, vutto ādiccabandhunā;

Etañca tāhaṃ vissajjissaṃ, cīvarapalibodho paṭhamaṃ chijjati;

Tassa bahisīme bahisīmagatassa (sī. syā.) āvāsapalibodho chijjati.

The withdrawal of the Kathina with transgression of the boundary as its end was declared by the Kinsman of the Sun. And this I will answer you: the robe-impediment is severed first. For this withdrawal, the dwelling-impediment is severed outside the boundary.

Sahubbhāro kathinuddhāro saubbhāro (ka.), vutto ādiccabandhunā;

Etañca tāhaṃ pucchāmi, katamo palibodho paṭhamaṃ chijjati.

The withdrawal of the Kathina by concurrence was declared by the Kinsman of the Sun. And this I ask you: which impediment is severed first?

Sahubbhāro kathinuddhāro, vutto ādiccabandhunā;

Etañca tāhaṃ vissajjissaṃ, dve palibodhā apubbaṃ acarimaṃ chijjantīti.

The withdrawal of the Kathina by concurrence was declared by the Kinsman of the Sun. And this I will answer you: the two impediments are severed simultaneously.

416. Kati kathinuddhārā saṅghādhīnā? Kati kathinuddhārā puggalādhīnā? Kati kathinuddhārā neva saṅghādhīnā na puggalādhīnā? Eko kathinuddhāro saṅghādhīno [M 0.0312] – antarubbhāro. Cattāro kathinuddhārā puggalādhīnā – pakkamanantiko, niṭṭhānantiko, sanniṭṭhānantiko, sīmātikkamanantiko[V 0.0335]. Cattāro kathinuddhārā neva saṅghādhīnā na puggalādhīnā – nāsanantiko, savanantiko, āsāvacchediko, sahubbhāro. Kati [T 0.0442][P 5.0179] kathinuddhārā antosīmāya uddhariyyanti? Kati kathinuddhārā bahisīmāya uddhariyyanti? Kati kathinuddhārā siyā antosīmāya uddhariyyanti siyā bahisīmāya uddhariyyanti? Dve kathinuddhārā antosīmāya uddhariyyanti – antarubbhāro, sahubbhāro. Tayo kathinuddhārā bahisīmāya uddhariyyanti – pakkamanantiko, savanantiko, sīmātikkamanantiko. Cattāro kathinuddhārā siyā antosīmāya uddhariyyanti siyā bahisīmāya uddhariyyanti – niṭṭhānantiko, sanniṭṭhānantiko, nāsanantiko, āsāvacchediko.

416. How many Kathina withdrawals are dependent on the Sangha? How many Kathina withdrawals are dependent on an individual? How many are neither dependent on the Sangha nor on an individual? One Kathina withdrawal is dependent on the Sangha—the interim withdrawal. Four Kathina withdrawals are dependent on an individual—the withdrawal with departure as its end, the withdrawal with completion as its end, the withdrawal with resolution as its end, and the withdrawal with transgression of the boundary as its end. Four Kathina withdrawals are neither dependent on the Sangha nor on an individual—the withdrawal with loss as its end, the withdrawal with hearing as its end, the withdrawal with the cutting off of hope as its end, and the withdrawal by concurrence. How many Kathina withdrawals are effected within the boundary? How many Kathina withdrawals are effected outside the boundary? How many Kathina withdrawals may be effected either within the boundary or outside the boundary? Two Kathina withdrawals are effected within the boundary—the interim withdrawal and the withdrawal by concurrence. Three Kathina withdrawals are effected outside the boundary—the withdrawal with departure as its end, the withdrawal with hearing as its end, and the withdrawal with transgression of the boundary as its end. Four Kathina withdrawals may be effected either within the boundary or outside the boundary—the withdrawal with completion as its end, the withdrawal with resolution as its end, the withdrawal with loss as its end, and the withdrawal with the cutting off of hope as its end.

Kati kathinuddhārā ekuppādā ekanirodhā? Kati kathinuddhārā ekuppādā nānānirodhā? Dve kathinuddhārā ekuppādā ekanirodhā – antarubbhāro, sahubbhāro. Avasesā kathinuddhārā ekuppādā nānānirodhāti.

How many Kathina withdrawals arise at the same time and cease at the same time? How many Kathina withdrawals arise at the same time but cease at different times? Two Kathina withdrawals arise at the same time and cease at the same time: the interim withdrawal and the withdrawal by concurrence. The remaining Kathina withdrawals arise at the same time but cease at different times.

Kathinabhedo niṭṭhito.

The Analysis of the Kathina is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of this is:

Kassa kinti pannarasa, dhammā nidānahetu ca;

Paccayasaṅgahamūlā, ādi ca atthārapuggalā aṭṭhapuggalā (sī.).

The question ‘by whom?’, the question ‘what?’, the fifteen factors, the occasion and the cause; conditions, inclusion, roots, and the beginning, and the persons who spread the Kathina.

Tiṇṇaṃ bhedato tiṇṇaṃ (ka.) tayo jānitabbaṃ, atthāraṃ uddesena ca;

Palibodhādhinā, sīmāya uppādanirodhena cāti ito paraṃ “parivāraṃ niṭṭhitaṃ” itipāṭho kesuci potthakesu dissati.

The three persons, the three ways of spreading, what should be known, the spreading, and the recitation; the impediments, dependency, the boundary, and arising and ceasing.

Upālipañcakaṃ

The Pentad of Upāli

1. Anissitavaggo

1. The Chapter on Non-reliance

417. Tena [T 0.0443][P 5.0180][M 0.0313][V 0.0336] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho āyasmā upāli yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā upāli bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “katihi nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā yāvajīvaṃ nānissitena vatthabba”nti?

417. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park. Then the Venerable Upāli went to where the Blessed One was; having gone, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Having sat down to one side, the Venerable Upāli said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, endowed with how many factors is a bhikkhu not to live without dependence for his whole life?”

“Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā yāvajīvaṃ nānissitena vatthabbaṃ. pari. 325 Katamehi pañcahi? Uposathaṃ na jānāti, uposathakammaṃ na jānāti, pātimokkhaṃ na jānāti, pātimokkhuddesaṃ na jānāti, ūnapañcavasso hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā yāvajīvaṃ nānissitena vatthabbaṃ. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā yāvajīvaṃ anissitena vatthabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Uposathaṃ jānāti, uposathakammaṃ jānāti, pātimokkhaṃ jānāti, pātimokkhuddesaṃ jānāti, pañcavasso vā hoti atirekapañcavasso vā – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā yāvajīvaṃ anissitena vatthabbaṃ.

“Upāli, endowed with five factors, a bhikkhu is not to live without dependence for his whole life. With what five? He does not know the Uposatha, he does not know the Uposatha ceremony, he does not know the Pātimokkha, he does not know the recitation of the Pātimokkha, and he has less than five vassas. Upāli, endowed with these five factors, a bhikkhu is not to live without dependence for his whole life. Upāli, endowed with five factors, a bhikkhu may live without dependence for his whole life. With what five? He knows the Uposatha, he knows the Uposatha ceremony, he knows the Pātimokkha, he knows the recitation of the Pātimokkha, and he has five vassas or more than five vassas. Upāli, endowed with these five factors, a bhikkhu may live without dependence for his whole life.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā yāvajīvaṃ nānissitena vatthabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Pavāraṇaṃ na jānāti, pavāraṇākammaṃ na jānāti, pātimokkhaṃ [T 0.0444] na jānāti, pātimokkhuddesaṃ na jānāti, ūnapañcavasso hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā yāvajīvaṃ nānissitena vatthabbaṃ. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā yāvajīvaṃ anissitena vatthabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Pavāraṇaṃ jānāti[V 0.0337], pavāraṇākammaṃ jānāti, pātimokkhaṃ jānāti, pātimokkhuddesaṃ jānāti, pañcavasso vā hoti atirekapañcavasso vā – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā yāvajīvaṃ anissitena vatthabbaṃ.

Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors should not live without dependence for as long as life lasts. With what five? He does not know the Pavāraṇā, he does not know the Pavāraṇā ceremony, he does not know the Pātimokkha, he does not know the recitation of the Pātimokkha, and he is of less than five vassas. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not live without dependence for as long as life lasts. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors may live without dependence for as long as life lasts. With what five? He knows the Pavāraṇā, he knows the Pavāraṇā ceremony, he knows the Pātimokkha, he knows the recitation of the Pātimokkha, and he is of five vassas or of more than five vassas. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors may live without dependence for as long as life lasts.

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā yāvajīvaṃ nānissitena vatthabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Āpattānāpattiṃ na jānāti, lahukagarukaṃ [M 0.0314] āpattiṃ na jānāti, sāvasesānavasesaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, ūnapañcavasso hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā yāvajīvaṃ nānissitena vatthabbaṃ. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā yāvajīvaṃ anissitena vatthabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Āpattānāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukagarukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, sāvasesānavasesaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, pañcavasso vā hoti atirekapañcavasso vā – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā yāvajīvaṃ anissitena vatthabbaṃ”.

Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors should not live without dependence for as long as life lasts. With what five? He does not know what is an offense and what is not an offense, he does not know light and heavy offenses, he does not know offenses that can be remedied and those that cannot, he does not know gross and non-gross offenses, and he is of less than five vassas. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not live without dependence for as long as life lasts. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors may live without dependence for as long as life lasts. With what five? He knows what is an offense and what is not an offense, he knows light and heavy offenses, he knows offenses that can be remedied and those that cannot, he knows gross and non-gross offenses, and he is of five vassas or of more than five vassas. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors may live without dependence for as long as life lasts.

418. “Katihi [P 5.0181] nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na [T 0.0445] upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo”ti?

418. Venerable Sir, endowed with how many factors should a bhikkhu not give the higher ordination, not give dependence, and not have a novice attend upon him?

mahāva. 84 “Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Na paṭibalo hoti antevāsiṃ vā saddhivihāriṃ vā gilānaṃ upaṭṭhātuṃ vā upaṭṭhāpetuṃ vā, anabhirataṃ vūpakāsetuṃ vā vūpakāsāpetuṃ vā, uppannaṃ kukkuccaṃ dhammato vinodetuṃ imasmiṃ ṭhāne sabbattha “vinodetuṃ vā vinodāpetuṃ vā”ti pāṭho dissati, vimativinodanīṭīkāya mahāvaggavaṇṇanā oloketabbā, abhidhamme vinetuṃ, abhivinaye vinetuṃ – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Paṭibalo hoti antevāsiṃ vā saddhivihāriṃ vā gilānaṃ upaṭṭhātuṃ vā upaṭṭhāpetuṃ vā, anabhirataṃ vūpakāsetuṃ vā vūpakāsāpetuṃ vā, uppannaṃ kukkuccaṃ dhammato vinodetuṃ, abhidhamme vinetuṃ, abhivinaye vinetuṃ – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should not give higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend upon him. What five? He is incapable of nursing or arranging for the nursing of a pupil or co-resident who is sick; he is incapable of leading away or causing to be led away one who is discontented; he is incapable of dispelling arisen remorse in accordance with the Dhamma; he is incapable of training in the higher Dhamma; and he is incapable of training in the higher Vinaya. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not give higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend upon him. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors may give higher ordination, may give dependence, and may have a novice attend upon him. What five? He is capable of nursing or arranging for the nursing of a pupil or co-resident who is sick; he is capable of leading away or causing to be led away one who is discontented; he is capable of dispelling arisen remorse in accordance with the Dhamma; he is capable of training in the higher Dhamma; and he is capable of training in the higher Vinaya. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors may give higher ordination, may give dependence, and may have a novice attend upon him.

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo [V 0.0338] dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Katamehi pañcahi[M 0.0315]? Na paṭibalo hoti [T 0.0446] antevāsiṃ vā saddhivihāriṃ vā abhisamācārikāya sikkhāya sikkhāpetuṃ, ādibrahmacāriyakāya sikkhāya vinetuṃ, adhisīle vinetuṃ, adhicitte vinetuṃ, adhipaññāya vinetuṃ – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Paṭibalo hoti antevāsiṃ vā saddhivihāriṃ vā abhisamācārikāya sikkhāya sikkhāpetuṃ, ādibrahmacāriyakāya sikkhāya vinetuṃ, adhisīle vinetuṃ, adhicitte vinetuṃ, adhipaññāya vinetuṃ – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo”ti.

Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors should not give higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend upon him. With what five? He is not capable of instructing a pupil or a co-resident in the training in proper conduct, of training them in the training that is the beginning of the holy life, of training them in the higher virtue, of training them in the higher mind, and of training them in the higher wisdom. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not give higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend upon him. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors may give higher ordination, may give dependence, and may have a novice attend upon him. With what five? He is capable of instructing a pupil or a co-resident in the training in proper conduct, of training them in the training that is the beginning of the holy life, of training them in the higher virtue, of training them in the higher mind, and of training them in the higher wisdom. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors may give higher ordination, may give dependence, and may have a novice attend upon him.

419. “Katihi nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabba”nti?

419. Venerable Sir, endowed with how many factors should a formal act be carried out against a bhikkhu?

Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto ca, micchādiṭṭhiko ca hoti, ājīvavipanno ca – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ.

Upāli, a formal act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with five factors. With what five? He is shameless, foolish, not of normal character, holds wrong view, and has a corrupt livelihood. Upāli, a formal act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors.

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti[T 0.0447], micchādiṭṭhiko ca hoti, ājīvavipanno ca – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ.

Furthermore, Upāli, a formal act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors. With what five? He is corrupt in the higher virtue, he is corrupt in conduct, he is corrupt in view due to holding extreme views, he holds wrong view, and he has a corrupt livelihood. Upāli, a formal act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors.

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Kāyikena davena samannāgato hoti, vācasikena davena samannāgato hoti, kāyikavācasikena davena samannāgato hoti, micchādiṭṭhiko [P 5.0182] ca hoti, ājīvavipanno ca – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ.

Furthermore, Upāli, a formal act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors. With which five? He is endowed with bodily frivolity, he is endowed with verbal frivolity, he is endowed with bodily and verbal frivolity, he holds wrong view, and he is corrupt in livelihood. Indeed, Upāli, a formal act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors.

“Aparehipi[M 0.0316], upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Kāyikena anācārena samannāgato hoti[V 0.0339], vācasikena anācārena samannāgato hoti, kāyikavācasikena anācārena samannāgato hoti, micchādiṭṭhiko ca hoti, ājīvavipanno ca – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ.

Furthermore, Upāli, a formal act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors. With which five? He is endowed with bodily misconduct, he is endowed with verbal misconduct, he is endowed with bodily and verbal misconduct, he holds wrong view, and he is corrupt in livelihood. Indeed, Upāli, a formal act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors.

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Kāyikena upaghātikena samannāgato hoti, vācasikena upaghātikena samannāgato hoti, kāyikavācasikena upaghātikena samannāgato hoti, micchādiṭṭhiko ca hoti, ājīvavipanno ca – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ.

Furthermore, Upāli, a formal act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors. With which five? He is endowed with destructive bodily conduct, he is endowed with destructive verbal conduct, he is endowed with destructive bodily and verbal conduct, he holds wrong view, and he is corrupt in livelihood. Indeed, Upāli, a formal act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors.

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Kāyikena micchājīvena samannāgato [T 0.0448] hoti, vācasikena micchājīvena samannāgato hoti, kāyikavācasikena micchājīvena samannāgato hoti, micchādiṭṭhiko ca hoti, ājīvavipanno ca – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ.

Furthermore, Upāli, a formal act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors. With which five? He is endowed with wrong livelihood by body, he is endowed with wrong livelihood by speech, he is endowed with wrong livelihood by body and speech, he holds wrong view, and he is corrupt in livelihood. Indeed, Upāli, a formal act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors.

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Āpattiṃ āpanno kammakato upasampādeti, nissayaṃ deti, sāmaṇeraṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, bhikkhunovādakasammutiṃ sādiyati, sammatopi bhikkhuniyo ovadati – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ.

Furthermore, Upāli, a formal act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors. With which five? A bhikkhu against whom a formal act has been carried out for having committed an offense gives full ordination; he gives dependence; he has a novice attend on him; he consents to the appointment as an instructor of bhikkhunīs; and though appointed, he instructs bhikkhunīs. Indeed, Upāli, a formal act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors.

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena kammaṃ kataṃ hoti taṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati, aññaṃ vā tādisikaṃ, tato vā pāpiṭṭhataraṃ, kammaṃ garahati, kammike garahati – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ.

Furthermore, Upāli, a formal act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors. With which five? He commits the offense for which a formal act has been carried out by the Saṅgha, or another similar to it, or one more blameworthy than it; he disparages the formal act; he disparages those who carried out the formal act. Indeed, Upāli, a formal act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors.

“Aparehipi[M 0.0317], upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, micchādiṭṭhiko ca hoti, ājīvavipanno ca – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ kātabba”nti.

Furthermore, Upāli, a formal act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors. With which five? He speaks dispraise of the Buddha; he speaks dispraise of the Dhamma; he speaks dispraise of the Saṅgha; he holds wrong view; and he is corrupt in livelihood. Indeed, Upāli, a formal act should be carried out against a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors.

Anissitavaggo niṭṭhito paṭhamo.

The Anissita Vagga, the first chapter, is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Uposathaṃ [T 0.0449][V 0.0340] pavāraṇaṃ, āpatti ca gilānakaṃ;

Abhisamācāralajjī ca, adhisīle davena ca.

Uposatha, Pavāraṇā, offense, and the sick one; proper conduct, the shameless one, higher morality, and frivolity.

Anācāraṃ upaghāti, micchā āpattimeva ca;

Yāyāpattiyā buddhassa, paṭhamo vaggasaṅgahoti.

Misconduct, destructive, wrong livelihood, and committing an offense; the offense for which, and dispraise of the Buddha: this is the collection of the first chapter.

2. Nappaṭippassambhanavaggo

2. The Chapter on Not Rescinding

420. “Katihi nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabba”nti?

420. “Venerable sir, with how many factors should a bhikkhu be endowed so that a formal act against him should not be rescinded?”

“Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi[P 5.0183]? Āpattiṃ āpanno kammakato upasampādeti, nissayaṃ deti, sāmaṇeraṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, bhikkhunovādakasammutiṃ sādiyati, sammatopi bhikkhuniyo ovadati – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

“Upāli, a formal act against a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should not be rescinded. With which five? A bhikkhu against whom a formal act has been carried out for having committed an offense gives full ordination; he gives dependence; he has a novice attend on him; he consents to the appointment as an instructor of bhikkhunīs; and even when appointed, he instructs bhikkhunīs. Indeed, Upāli, a formal act against a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not be rescinded.

cūḷava. 8-9, 18, 30-31, 43, 53, 62, 72 “Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Yāya āpattiyā saṅghena kammaṃ kataṃ hoti taṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati, aññaṃ vā tādisikaṃ, tato vā pāpiṭṭhataraṃ, kammaṃ garahati, kammike garahati – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, Upāli, a formal act against a bhikkhu endowed with another five factors should not be rescinded. With which five? He commits the offense for which a formal act has been carried out by the Saṅgha, or another of a similar nature, or one that is more blameworthy than it; he disparages the formal act; he disparages those who carried out the formal act. Indeed, Upāli, a formal act against a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not be rescinded.

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, micchādiṭṭhiko ca [T 0.0450] hoti, ājīvavipanno [M 0.0318] ca – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, Upāli, a formal act against a bhikkhu endowed with another five factors should not be rescinded. With which five? He speaks in dispraise of the Buddha; he speaks in dispraise of the Dhamma; he speaks in dispraise of the Saṅgha; he holds wrong view; and he is corrupt in livelihood. Indeed, Upāli, a formal act against a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not be rescinded.

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto ca, omaddakārako ca hoti, vattesu [V 0.0341] sikkhāya ca na paripūrakārī – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno kammaṃ nappaṭippassambhetabba”nti.

Furthermore, Upāli, a formal act against a bhikkhu endowed with another five factors should not be rescinded. With which five? He is shameless, foolish, not of normal status, and acts oppressively; and he is not one who fulfills the duties and the training. Indeed, Upāli, a formal act against a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not be rescinded.”

421. “Saṅgāmāvacarena, bhante, bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamantena kati dhamme ajjhattaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā saṅgho upasaṅkamitabbo”ti?

421. “Venerable sir, how many principles should a bhikkhu who enters the Saṅgha assembly to settle a legal issue establish internally before approaching the Saṅgha?”

pari. 365 “Saṅgāmāvacarena, upāli, bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamantena pañca dhamme ajjhattaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā saṅgho upasaṅkamitabbo. Katame pañca? Saṅgāmāvacarena, upāli, bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamantena nīcacittena saṅgho upasaṅkamitabbo, rajoharaṇasamena cittena, āsanakusalena bhavitabbaṃ nissajjakusalena, there bhikkhū anupakhajjantena, nave bhikkhū āsanena appaṭibāhantena yathāpatirūpe āsane nisīditabbaṃ, anānākathikena bhavitabbaṃ atiracchānakathikena, sāmaṃ vā dhammo bhāsitabbo, paro vā ajjhesitabbo, ariyo vā tuṇhibhāvo nātimaññitabbo, sace, upāli, saṅgho samaggakaraṇīyāni kammāni karoti tatra ce, upāli, bhikkhuno nakkhamati, api diṭṭhāvikammaṃ katvā ñāpetabbā sāmaggī. Taṃ kissahetu? Māhaṃ saṅghena nānatto assanti. Saṅgāmāvacarenupāli[T 0.0451], bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamantena ime pañca dhamme ajjhattaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā saṅgho upasaṅkamitabbo”ti.

“Upāli, a bhikkhu who engages in settling a dispute, when approaching the Saṅgha, should establish five qualities within himself before approaching the Saṅgha. What five? Upāli, a bhikkhu who engages in settling a dispute, when approaching the Saṅgha, should approach the Saṅgha with a humble mind, with a mind like a dust-cloth. He should be skilled in seating and skilled in sitting. Not pushing past the senior bhikkhus, not obstructing the junior bhikkhus from a seat, he should sit in a seat suitable for himself. He should not be one who speaks various kinds of talk, nor one who speaks unbecoming talk. He should either speak the Dhamma himself or invite another to speak; and the noble silence should not be despised. If, Upāli, the Saṅgha is performing acts that are to be done in harmony, and if, Upāli, it does not please that bhikkhu, then even after having made his view known, he should enter into that harmony. For what reason? Thinking, ‘May I not be divided from the Saṅgha.’ Upāli, a bhikkhu who engages in settling a dispute, when approaching the Saṅgha, should establish these five qualities within himself before approaching the Saṅgha.”

422. “Katihi nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu saṅghe voharanto bahujanaakanto ca hoti bahujanaamanāpo ca bahujanaarucito cā”ti?

422. “Venerable sir, endowed with how many factors is a bhikkhu who, when settling a matter in the Saṅgha, is disliked by many, unpleasing to many, and disagreeable to many?”

“Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu saṅghe voharanto bahujanaakanto ca hoti bahujanaamanāpo ca bahujanaarucito ca. Katamehi pañcahi? Ussitamantī ca hoti, nissitajappī ca, na ca bhāsānusandhikusalo [M 0.0319] hoti, na yathādhamme yathāvinaye yathāpattiyā codetā hoti, na yathādhamme yathāvinaye yathāpattiyā kāretā hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu saṅghe voharanto bahujanaakanto ca hoti bahujanaamanāpo ca bahujanaarucito ca. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu saṅghe voharanto bahujanakanto ca hoti bahujanamanāpo ca bahujanaarucito ca. Katamehi pañcahi? Na ussitamantī ca hoti, na nissitajappī ca, bhāsānusandhikusalo ca hoti, yathādhamme yathāvinaye yathāpattiyā codetā hoti, yathādhamme yathāvinaye yathāpattiyā kāretā hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi [V 0.0342] samannāgato bhikkhu saṅghe voharanto bahujanakanto ca hoti bahujanamanāpo ca bahujanarucito ca.

“Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors, when settling a legal issue in the Saṅgha, is disliked by many people, unpleasing to many people, and disagreeable to many people. With which five? He has arrogant speech; he speaks relying on a prominent person; he is not skilled in the connection of discourse and legal decisions; he is not one who accuses in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the offense; and he is not one who makes a decision in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the offense. Indeed, Upāli, endowed with these five factors, a bhikkhu, when settling a legal issue in the Saṅgha, is disliked by many people, unpleasing to many people, and disagreeable to many people. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors, when settling a legal issue in the Saṅgha, is liked by many people, pleasing to many people, and agreeable to many people. With which five? He does not have arrogant speech; he does not speak relying on a prominent person; he is skilled in the connection of discourse and legal decisions; he is one who accuses in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the offense; and he is one who makes a decision in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the offense. Indeed, Upāli, endowed with these five factors, a bhikkhu, when settling a legal issue in the Saṅgha, is liked by many people, pleasing to many people, and agreeable to many people.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu saṅghe voharanto bahujanaakanto ca hoti bahujanaamanāpo ca [T 0.0452] bahujanaarucito ca. Katamehi pañcahi? Ussādetā ca hoti, apasādetā ca, adhammaṃ gaṇhāti, dhammaṃ paṭibāhati, samphañca bahuṃ bhāsati – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu saṅghe voharanto bahujanaakanto ca hoti bahujanaamanāpo ca bahujanaarucito ca. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu saṅghe voharanto bahujanakanto ca hoti bahujanamanāpo ca bahujanarucito [P 5.0184] ca. Katamehi pañcahi? Na ussādetā ca hoti, na apasādetā ca, dhammaṃ gaṇhāti, adhammaṃ paṭibāhati, samphañca na bahuṃ bhāsati – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu saṅghe voharanto bahujanakanto ca hoti bahujanamanāpo ca bahujanarucito ca.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors, when transacting business in the Saṅgha, is disliked by many, unpleasing to many, and disagreeable to many. What are the five? He is one who exalts and one who disparages; he takes up what is not the Dhamma; he obstructs the Dhamma; and he speaks much idle chatter. Indeed, Upāli, endowed with these five factors, a bhikkhu, when transacting business in the Saṅgha, is disliked by many, unpleasing to many, and disagreeable to many. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors, when transacting business in the Saṅgha, is liked by many, pleasing to many, and agreeable to many. What are the five? He is not one who exalts and not one who disparages; he takes up the Dhamma; he obstructs what is not the Dhamma; and he does not speak much idle chatter. Indeed, Upāli, endowed with these five factors, a bhikkhu, when transacting business in the Saṅgha, is liked by many, pleasing to many, and agreeable to many.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu saṅghe voharanto bahujanaakanto ca hoti bahujanaamanāpo ca bahujanaarucito ca. Katamehi pañcahi? Pasayhapavattā hoti, anokāsakammaṃ kāretvā pavattā hoti, na yathādhamme yathāvinaye yathāpattiyā codetā hoti, na yathādhamme yathāvinaye yathāpattiyā kāretā hoti, na yathādiṭṭhiyā byākatā hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu saṅghe voharanto bahujanaakanto ca hoti bahujanaamanāpo [M 0.0320] ca bahujanaarucito ca. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu saṅghe voharanto bahujanakanto ca hoti bahujanamanāpo ca bahujanarucito ca. Katamehi pañcahi? Na [T 0.0453] pasayhapavattā hoti, okāsakammaṃ kāretvā pavattā hoti, yathādhamme yathāvinaye yathāpattiyā codetā hoti, yathādhamme yathāvinaye yathāpattiyā kāretā hoti, yathādiṭṭhiyā byākatā hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu saṅghe voharanto bahujanakanto ca hoti bahujanamanāpo ca bahujanarucito cā”ti.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five other qualities, when adjudicating in the Saṅgha, is disliked by many, displeasing to many, and unappealing to many. With which five? He speaks forcefully; he speaks without having granted an opportunity; he does not accuse in accordance with the Dhamma, in accordance with the Vinaya, and in accordance with the offense; he does not make a decision in accordance with the Dhamma, in accordance with the Vinaya, and in accordance with the offense; he does not speak in accordance with his own view. Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five qualities, when adjudicating in the Saṅgha, is disliked by many, displeasing to many, and unappealing to many. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five qualities, when adjudicating in the Saṅgha, is liked by many, pleasing to many, and appealing to many. With which five? He does not speak forcefully; he speaks after having granted an opportunity; he accuses in accordance with the Dhamma, in accordance with the Vinaya, and in accordance with the offense; he makes a decision in accordance with the Dhamma, in accordance with the Vinaya, and in accordance with the offense; he speaks in accordance with his own view. Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five qualities, when adjudicating in the Saṅgha, is liked by many, pleasing to many, and appealing to many.”

423. “Kati nu kho, bhante, ānisaṃsā vinayapariyattiyā”ti?

423. “Venerable sir, how many benefits are there in learning the Vinaya?”

“Pañcime, upāli, ānisaṃsā vinayapariyattiyā. Katame pañca? Attano sīlakkhandho sugutto hoti surakkhito, kukkuccapakatānaṃ paṭisaraṇaṃ hoti, visārado saṅghamajjhe [V 0.0343] voharati, paccatthike sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggaṇhāti, saddhammaṭṭhitiyā paṭipanno hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcānisaṃsā vinayapariyattiyā”.

“Upāli, there are these five benefits of learning the Vinaya. Which five? One's own aggregate of virtue is well-guarded and well-protected; one becomes a refuge for those afflicted by remorse; one speaks confidently in the midst of the Saṅgha; one rightly and thoroughly restrains opponents in accordance with the Dhamma; one is practicing for the stability of the true Dhamma. These, Upāli, are the five benefits of learning the Vinaya.”

Nappaṭippassambhanavaggo niṭṭhito dutiyo.

The Second Chapter, on Not Calming, is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Āpanno yāyavaṇṇañca, alajjī saṅgāmena ca;

Ussitā ussādetā ca, pasayha pariyattiyāti.

Having committed an offense, by which offense, and dispraise; the shameless one, and the battle; the conceited one, and the extoller; by force, and the learning of Vinaya.

Paṭhamayamakapaññatti.

The First Formulation of Pairs.

3. Vohāravaggo

3. The Chapter on Adjudication

424. “Katihi [P 5.0185] nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabba”nti?

424. “Venerable sir, with how many factors must a bhikkhu be endowed that he should not adjudicate in the Saṅgha?”

“Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Āpattiṃ na jānāti, āpattisamuṭṭhānaṃ na jānāti, āpattiyā payogaṃ na [T 0.0454] jānāti, āpattiyā vūpasamaṃ na jānāti, āpattiyā na vinicchayakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi [M 0.0321] samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe voharitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Āpattiṃ jānāti, āpattisamuṭṭhānaṃ jānāti, āpattiyā payogaṃ jānāti, āpattiyā vūpasamaṃ jānāti, āpattiyā vinicchayakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe voharitabbaṃ.

“Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should not adjudicate in the Saṅgha. With which five? He does not know an offense; he does not know the origin of an offense; he does not know the application in regard to an offense; he does not know the cessation of an offense; he is not skilled in the adjudication of an offense. Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not adjudicate in the Saṅgha. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should adjudicate in the Saṅgha. With which five? He knows an offense; he knows the origin of an offense; he knows the application in regard to an offense; he knows the cessation of an offense; he is skilled in the adjudication of an offense. Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should adjudicate in the Saṅgha.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Adhikaraṇaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇasamuṭṭhānaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇassa payogaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇassa vūpasamaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇassa na vinicchayakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe voharitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Adhikaraṇaṃ jānāti[V 0.0344], adhikaraṇasamuṭṭhānaṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇassa payogaṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇassa vūpasamaṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇassa vinicchayakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe voharitabbaṃ.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors should not adjudicate in the Saṅgha. With which five? He does not know a legal question; he does not know the origin of a legal question; he does not know the application in regard to a legal question; he does not know the settlement of a legal question; he is not skilled in the adjudication of a legal question.
