Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not adjudicate in the Saṅgha. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should adjudicate in the Saṅgha. With which five? He knows a legal question; he knows the origin of a legal question; he knows the application in regard to a legal question; he knows the settlement of a legal question; he is skilled in the adjudication of a legal question. Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should adjudicate in the Saṅgha.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena [T 0.0455] bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Pasayhapavattā hoti, anokāsakammaṃ kāretvā pavattā hoti, na yathādhamme yathāvinaye yathāpattiyā codetā hoti, na yathādhamme yathāvinaye yathāpattiyā kāretā hoti, na yathādiṭṭhiyā byākatā hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe voharitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Na pasayhapavattā hoti, okāsakammaṃ kāretvā pavattā hoti, yathādhamme yathāvinaye yathāpattiyā codetā hoti, yathādhamme yathāvinaye yathāpattiyā kāretā hoti, yathādiṭṭhiyā byākatā hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe voharitabbaṃ.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors should not adjudicate in the Saṅgha. With what five? He speaks coercively; he speaks without having granted permission; he does not accuse in accordance with the Dhamma, in accordance with the Vinaya, in accordance with the offense; he does not pass judgment in accordance with the Dhamma, in accordance with the Vinaya, in accordance with the offense; he does not explain in accordance with his view. Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not adjudicate in the Saṅgha. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should adjudicate in the Saṅgha. With what five? He does not speak coercively; he speaks after having granted permission; he accuses in accordance with the Dhamma, in accordance with the Vinaya, and in accordance with the offense; he passes judgment in accordance with the Dhamma, in accordance with the Vinaya, and in accordance with the offense; he explains in accordance with his view. Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should adjudicate in the Saṅgha.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Āpattānāpattiṃ na jānāti, lahukagarukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, sāvasesānavasesaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ [M 0.0322] āpattiṃ na jānāti, sappaṭikammaṃ appaṭikammaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti – imehi [T 0.0456] kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe voharitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Āpattānāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukagarukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, sāvasesānavasesaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, sappaṭikammaṃ appaṭikammaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe voharitabbaṃ.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors should not adjudicate in the Saṅgha. With what five? He does not know what is an offense and what is not an offense; he does not know what is a light or a serious offense; he does not know what is an offense with a remainder or without a remainder; he does not know what is a grave or a non-grave offense; he does not know what is an offense that can be remedied or that cannot be remedied. Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not adjudicate in the Saṅgha. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should adjudicate in the Saṅgha. With what five? He knows what is an offense and what is not an offense; he knows what is a light or a serious offense; he knows what is an offense with a remainder or without a remainder; he knows what is a grave or a non-grave offense; he knows what is an offense that can be remedied or that cannot be remedied. Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should adjudicate in the Saṅgha.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Kammaṃ na jānāti, kammassa karaṇaṃ na jānāti, kammassa vatthuṃ na jānāti, kammassa vattaṃ na jānāti, kammassa vūpasamaṃ na jānāti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ. Pañcahupāli[P 5.0186], aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe voharitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Kammaṃ jānāti, kammassa karaṇaṃ jānāti, kammassa vatthuṃ jānāti, kammassa vattaṃ jānāti, kammassa vūpasamaṃ jānāti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe voharitabbaṃ.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors should not adjudicate in the Saṅgha. With what five? He does not know the formal act; he does not know the performance of the formal act; he does not know the basis of the formal act; he does not know the procedure for the formal act; he does not know the settling of the formal act. Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not adjudicate in the Saṅgha. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should adjudicate in the Saṅgha. With what five? He knows the formal act; he knows the performance of the formal act; he knows the basis of the formal act; he knows the procedure for the formal act; he knows the settling of the formal act. Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should adjudicate in the Saṅgha.”

“Aparehipi[V 0.0345], upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Vatthuṃ na jānāti, nidānaṃ na jānāti, paññattiṃ na jānāti, padapaccābhaṭṭhaṃ na jānāti, anusandhivacanapathaṃ na jānāti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe voharitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Vatthuṃ jānāti, nidānaṃ jānāti, paññattiṃ jānāti, padapaccābhaṭṭhaṃ jānāti, anusandhivacanapathaṃ jānāti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe voharitabbaṃ.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors should not adjudicate in the Saṅgha. With what five? He does not know the basis; he does not know the origin; he does not know the regulation; he does not know the sequence of words; he does not know the connection in the phrasing. Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not adjudicate in the Saṅgha. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should adjudicate in the Saṅgha. With what five? He knows the basis; he knows the origin; he knows the regulation; he knows the sequence of words; he knows the connection in the phrasing. Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should adjudicate in the Saṅgha.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ[T 0.0457]. Katamehi pañcahi? Chandāgatiṃ gacchati, dosāgatiṃ gacchati, mohāgatiṃ gacchati, bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, alajjī ca hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe voharitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, na dosāgatiṃ gacchati, na mohāgatiṃ [M 0.0323] gacchati, na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, lajjī ca hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe voharitabbaṃ.

Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors should not adjudicate in the Saṅgha. With what five? He follows a wrong course through desire, he follows a wrong course through hatred, he follows a wrong course through delusion, he follows a wrong course through fear, and he is shameless. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not adjudicate in the Saṅgha. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should adjudicate in the Saṅgha. With what five? He does not follow a wrong course through desire, he does not follow a wrong course through hatred, he does not follow a wrong course through delusion, he does not follow a wrong course through fear, and he has a sense of shame. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should adjudicate in the Saṅgha.

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Chandāgatiṃ gacchati, dosāgatiṃ gacchati, mohāgatiṃ gacchati, bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, akusalo ca hoti vinaye – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe voharitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, na dosāgatiṃ gacchati, na mohāgatiṃ gacchati, na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, kusalo ca hoti vinaye – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe voharitabbaṃ.

Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors should not adjudicate in the Saṅgha. With what five? He follows a wrong course through desire, he follows a wrong course through hatred, he follows a wrong course through delusion, he follows a wrong course through fear, and he is unskilled in the Vinaya. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not adjudicate in the Saṅgha. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should adjudicate in the Saṅgha. With what five? He does not follow a wrong course through desire, he does not follow a wrong course through hatred, he does not follow a wrong course through delusion, he does not follow a wrong course through fear, and he is skilled in the Vinaya. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should adjudicate in the Saṅgha.

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Ñattiṃ na jānāti, ñattiyā karaṇaṃ na jānāti, ñattiyā anussāvanaṃ na jānāti, ñattiyā samathaṃ na jānāti, ñattiyā vūpasamaṃ na jānāti – imehi kho, upāli[T 0.0458], pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe voharitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Ñattiṃ jānāti, ñattiyā karaṇaṃ [V 0.0346] jānāti, ñattiyā anussāvanaṃ jānāti, ñattiyā samathaṃ jānāti, ñattiyā vūpasamaṃ jānāti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe voharitabbaṃ.

Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors should not settle a legal case in the Saṅgha. With what five? He does not know the motion; he does not know the procedure by means of the motion; he does not know the proclamation with the motion; he does not know the settlement by means of the motion; he does not know the pacification by means of the motion. Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not settle a legal case in the Saṅgha. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should settle a legal case in the Saṅgha. With what five? He knows the motion; he knows the procedure by means of the motion; he knows the proclamation with the motion; he knows the settlement by means of the motion; he knows the pacification by means of the motion. Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should settle a legal case in the Saṅgha.

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Suttaṃ na jānāti, suttānulomaṃ na jānāti, vinayaṃ na jānāti, vinayānulomaṃ na jānāti, na ca ṭhānāṭhānakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe voharitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Suttaṃ jānāti, suttānulomaṃ jānāti, vinayaṃ jānāti, vinayānulomaṃ jānāti, ṭhānāṭhānakusalo ca hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe voharitabbaṃ.

Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors should not settle a legal case in the Saṅgha. With what five? He does not know the two Vibhaṅgas; he does not know what is in conformity with the two Vibhaṅgas; he does not know the Khandhakas and the Parivāra; he does not know what is in conformity with the Khandhakas and the Parivāra; and he is not skilled in what is a valid reason and what is not. Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not settle a legal case in the Saṅgha. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should settle a legal case in the Saṅgha. With what five? He knows the two Vibhaṅgas; he knows what is in conformity with the two Vibhaṅgas; he knows the Khandhakas and the Parivāra; he knows what is in conformity with the Khandhakas and the Parivāra; and he is skilled in what is a valid reason and what is not. Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should settle a legal case in the Saṅgha.

“Aparehipi[M 0.0324], upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Dhammaṃ na jānāti, dhammānulomaṃ na jānāti, vinayaṃ na jānāti, vinayānulomaṃ na jānāti, na ca pubbāparakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe na voharitabbaṃ. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe voharitabbaṃ. Katamehi [T 0.0459] pañcahi? Dhammaṃ jānāti, dhammānulomaṃ jānāti, vinayaṃ jānāti, vinayānulomaṃ jānāti, pubbāparakusalo ca hoti – imehi [P 5.0187] kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saṅghe voharitabba”nti.

Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors should not adjudicate in the Saṅgha. With what five? He does not know the Dhamma, he does not know what is in conformity with the Dhamma, he does not know the Vinaya, he does not know what is in conformity with the Vinaya, and he is not skilled in the preceding and subsequent matters. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not adjudicate in the Saṅgha. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should adjudicate in the Saṅgha. With what five? He knows the Dhamma, he knows what is in conformity with the Dhamma, he knows the Vinaya, he knows what is in conformity with the Vinaya, and he is skilled in the preceding and subsequent matters. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should adjudicate in the Saṅgha.

Vohāravaggo niṭṭhito tatiyo.

The third chapter, the Chapter on Adjudication, is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Here is the summary:

Āpatti adhikaraṇaṃ, pasayhāpatti jānanā;

Kammaṃ vatthuṃ alajjī ca, akusalo ca ñattiyā;

Suttaṃ na jānāti dhammaṃ, tatiyo vaggasaṅgahoti.

Offense, legal question, acting with force, and knowing offenses; the formal act, the basis, the shameless one, the unskilled one, and the motion; ‘He does not know the Sutta,’ and ‘He does not know the Dhamma’—this is the collection of the third chapter.

4. Diṭṭhāvikammavaggo

4. The Chapter on Making a View Manifest

425. “Kati nu kho, bhante, adhammikā diṭṭhāvikammā”ti? “Pañcime, upāli, adhammikā diṭṭhāvikammā. Katame pañca? Anāpattiyā diṭṭhiṃ āvi karoti, adesanāgāminiyā [V 0.0347] āpattiyā diṭṭhiṃ āvi karoti, desitāya āpattiyā diṭṭhiṃ āvi karoti, catūhi pañcahi diṭṭhiṃ āvi karoti, mano mānasena diṭṭhiṃ āvi karoti – ime kho, upāli, pañca adhammikā diṭṭhāvikammā.

425. “Venerable sir, how many unlawful ways of making a view manifest are there?” “Upāli, there are these five unlawful ways of making a view manifest. Which five? One makes a view manifest regarding a non-offense; one makes a view manifest regarding an offense that is not confessable; one makes a view manifest regarding an offense that has been confessed; one makes a view manifest in the presence of four or five bhikkhus; one makes a view manifest by mind alone. These, Upāli, are the five unlawful ways of making a view manifest.

“Pañcime, upāli, dhammikā diṭṭhāvikammā. Katame pañca? Āpattiyā diṭṭhiṃ āvi karoti, desanāgāminiyā āpattiyā diṭṭhiṃ āvi karoti, adesitāya āpattiyā diṭṭhiṃ āvi karoti, na catūhi pañcahi diṭṭhiṃ āvi karoti, na mano mānasena diṭṭhiṃ āvi karoti – ime kho, upāli, pañca dhammikā diṭṭhāvikammā.

Upāli, there are these five lawful ways of making a view manifest. Which five? One makes a view manifest regarding an offense; one makes a view manifest regarding a confessable offense; one makes a view manifest regarding an offense that has not been confessed; one does not make a view manifest in the presence of four or five bhikkhus; one does not make a view manifest by mind alone. These, Upāli, are the five lawful ways of making a view manifest.

“Aparepi[M 0.0325], upāli, pañca adhammikā diṭṭhāvikammā. Katame [T 0.0460] pañca? Nānāsaṃvāsakassa santike diṭṭhiṃ āvi karoti, nānāsīmāya ṭhitassa santike diṭṭhiṃ āvi karoti, apakatattassa santike diṭṭhiṃ āvi karoti, catūhi pañcahi diṭṭhiṃ āvi karoti, mano mānasena diṭṭhiṃ āvi karoti – ime kho, upāli, pañca adhammikā diṭṭhāvikammā.

Furthermore, Upāli, there are five other unlawful ways of making a view manifest. Which five? One makes a view manifest in the presence of a bhikkhu of a different communion; one makes a view manifest in the presence of a bhikkhu standing in a different boundary; one makes a view manifest in the presence of a bhikkhu not in good standing; one makes a view manifest in the presence of four or five bhikkhus; one makes a view manifest by mind alone. These, Upāli, are the five unlawful ways of making a view manifest.

“Pañcime, upāli, dhammikā diṭṭhāvikammā. Katame pañca? Samānasaṃvāsakassa santike diṭṭhiṃ āvi karoti, samānasīmāya ṭhitassa santike diṭṭhiṃ āvi karoti, pakatattassa santike diṭṭhiṃ āvi karoti, na catūhi pañcahi diṭṭhiṃ āvi karoti, na mano mānasena diṭṭhiṃ āvi karoti – ime kho, upāli, pañca dhammikā diṭṭhāvikammāti.

Upāli, there are these five lawful acts of disclosing a view. Which five? One discloses a view in the presence of a monk of the same communion; one discloses a view in the presence of a monk standing in the same boundary; one discloses a view in the presence of a monk in good standing; one does not disclose a view to four or five monks; one does not disclose a view by mind alone. These, Upāli, are the five lawful acts of disclosing a view.

426. “Kati nu kho, bhante, adhammikā paṭiggahā”ti? “Pañcime, upāli, adhammikā paṭiggahā. Katame pañca? Kāyena diyyamānaṃ kāyena appaṭiggahitaṃ, kāyena diyyamānaṃ kāyappaṭibaddhena appaṭiggahitaṃ, kāyappaṭibaddhena diyyamānaṃ kāyena appaṭiggahitaṃ, kāyappaṭibaddhena diyyamānaṃ kāyappaṭibaddhena appaṭiggahitaṃ, nissaggiyena diyyamānaṃ kāyena vā kāyappaṭibaddhena vā appaṭiggahitaṃ – ime kho, upāli, pañca adhammikā paṭiggahā.

426. “Venerable sir, how many unlawful receptions are there?” “Upāli, there are these five unlawful receptions. Which five? What is given by hand is not received by hand; what is given by hand is not received with something connected to the body; what is given with something connected to the body is not received by hand; what is given with something connected to the body is not received with something connected to the body; what is given by releasing it is not received either by hand or with something connected to the body. These, Upāli, are the five unlawful receptions.”

“Pañcime, upāli, dhammikā paṭiggahā. Katame pañca? Kāyena diyyamānaṃ kāyena paṭiggahitaṃ, kāyena diyyamānaṃ kāyappaṭibaddhena paṭiggahitaṃ, kāyappaṭibaddhena diyyamānaṃ kāyena paṭiggahitaṃ, kāyappaṭibaddhena diyyamānaṃ kāyappaṭibaddhena paṭiggahitaṃ, nissaggiyena diyyamānaṃ kāyena vā kāyappaṭibaddhena vā paṭiggahitaṃ – ime [T 0.0461] kho, upāli, pañca dhammikā paṭiggahā”ti.

“Upāli, there are these five lawful receptions. Which five? What is given by hand is received by hand; what is given by hand is received with something connected to the body; what is given with something connected to the body is received by hand; what is given with something connected to the body is received with something connected to the body; what is given by releasing it is received either by hand or with something connected to the body. These, Upāli, are the five lawful receptions.”

427. “Kati [P 5.0188][V 0.0348] nu kho, bhante, anatirittā”ti? “Pañcime, upāli, anatirittā. Katame pañca? pāci. 239 Akappiyakataṃ hoti, appaṭiggahitakataṃ hoti anuccāritakataṃ hoti, ahatthapāse kataṃ hoti, alametaṃ sabbanti avuttaṃ hoti – ime kho, upāli, pañca anatirittā.

427. “Venerable sir, how many non-surpluses are there?” “Upāli, there are these five non-surpluses. Which five? It is made surplus from what is unallowable; it is made surplus from what has not been accepted; it is made surplus from what cannot be lifted; it is made surplus when not within hand's reach; and it is not said, ‘This is sufficient for all.’ These, Upāli, are the five non-surpluses.”

“Pañcime, upāli, atirittā. Katame pañca? pāci. 239 Kappiyakataṃ hoti, paṭiggahitakataṃ hoti, uccāritakataṃ hoti, hatthapāse kataṃ hoti, alametaṃ sabbanti vuttaṃ hoti – ime kho, upāli, pañca atirittā”ti.

“Upāli, there are these five surpluses. Which five? It is made surplus from what is allowable; it is made surplus from what has been accepted; it is made surplus from what can be lifted; it is made surplus when within hand's reach; and it is said, ‘This is sufficient for all.’ These, Upāli, are the five surpluses.”

428. “Katihi [M 0.0326] nu kho, bhante, ākārehi pavāraṇā paññāyatī”ti? “Pañcahupāli, ākārehi pavāraṇā paññāyati. Katamehi pañcahi? pāci. 239 Asanaṃ paññāyati, bhojanaṃ paññāyati, hatthapāse ṭhito abhiharati, paṭikkhepo paññāyati – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahākārehi pavāraṇā paññāyatī”ti.

428. “Venerable sir, by how many signs is satisfaction known?” “Upāli, satisfaction is known by five signs. By which five? The act of eating is apparent; food is apparent; one is standing within hand's reach; one brings it forward; a refusal is apparent. By these five signs, Upāli, satisfaction is known.”

429. “Kati nu kho, bhante, adhammikā paṭiññātakaraṇā”ti? “Pañcime, upāli, adhammikā paṭiññātakaraṇā. Katame pañca? Bhikkhu pārājikaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti, pārājikena codiyamāno saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpanno paṭijānāti, taṃ saṅgho saṅghādisesena kāreti, adhammikaṃ paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ[T 0.0462]. Bhikkhu pārājikaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti, pārājikena codiyamāno pācittiyaṃ…pe… pāṭidesanīyaṃ… dukkaṭaṃ ajjhāpanno paṭijānāti, taṃ saṅgho dukkaṭena kāreti, adhammikaṃ paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ. Bhikkhu saṅghādisesaṃ…pe… pācittiyaṃ… pāṭidesanīyaṃ… dukkaṭaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti. Dukkaṭena codiyamāno pārājikaṃ ajjhāpanno paṭijānāti, taṃ saṅgho pārājikena kāreti, adhammikaṃ paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ. Bhikkhu dukkaṭaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti, dukkaṭena codiyamāno saṅghādisesaṃ…pe… pācittiyaṃ… pāṭidesanīyaṃ ajjhāpanno paṭijānāti, taṃ saṅgho pāṭidesanīyena kāreti – adhammikaṃ paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ. Ime kho, upāli, pañca adhammikā paṭiññātakaraṇā.

429. “Venerable sir, how many unlawful acts of confession are there?” “Upāli, there are these five unlawful acts of confession. Which five? A monk has committed a Pārājika offense; when accused of a Pārājika, he confesses to having committed a Saṅghādisesa. The Saṅgha deals with him for the Saṅghādisesa. This is an unlawful act of confession. A monk has committed a Pārājika offense; when accused of a Pārājika, he confesses to having committed a Pācittiya… a Pāṭidesanīya… or a Dukkaṭa offense. The Saṅgha deals with him for the Dukkaṭa. This is an unlawful act of confession. A monk has committed a Saṅghādisesa… a Pācittiya… a Pāṭidesanīya… or a Dukkaṭa offense; when accused of a Dukkaṭa, he confesses to having committed a Pārājika offense. The Saṅgha deals with him for the Pārājika. This is an unlawful act of confession. A monk has committed a Dukkaṭa offense; when accused of a Dukkaṭa, he confesses to having committed a Saṅghādisesa… a Pācittiya… or a Pāṭidesanīya offense. The Saṅgha deals with him for the Pāṭidesanīya. This is an unlawful act of confession. These, Upāli, are the five unlawful acts of confession.”

“Pañcime, upāli, dhammikā paṭiññātakaraṇā. Katame pañca? Bhikkhu pārājikaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti, pārājikena codiyamāno pārājikaṃ ajjhāpanno paṭijānāti, taṃ saṅgho pārājikena kāreti, dhammikaṃ paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ. Bhikkhu saṅghādisesaṃ…pe… pācittiyaṃ… pāṭidesanīyaṃ… dukkaṭaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti, dukkaṭena codiyamāno dukkaṭaṃ ajjhāpanno paṭijānāti[V 0.0349], taṃ saṅgho dukkaṭena kāreti, dhammikaṃ paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ. Ime kho, upāli, pañca dhammikā paṭiññātakaraṇā”ti.

“Upāli, there are these five lawful acts of confession. Which five? A monk has committed a Pārājika offense; when accused of a Pārājika, he confesses to having committed a Pārājika offense. The Saṅgha deals with him for the Pārājika. This is a lawful act of confession. A monk has committed a Saṅghādisesa… a Pācittiya… a Pāṭidesanīya… or a Dukkaṭa offense; when accused of a Dukkaṭa, he confesses to having committed a Dukkaṭa offense. The Saṅgha deals with him for the Dukkaṭa. This is a lawful act of confession. These, Upāli, are the five lawful acts of confession.”

430. “Katihi [P 5.0189] nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno okāsakammaṃ kārāpentassa nālaṃ okāsakammaṃ kātu”nti? “Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno okāsakammaṃ kārāpentassa nālaṃ okāsakammaṃ [M 0.0327] kātuṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto ca, cāvanādhippāyo vattā hoti, no vuṭṭhānādhippāyo – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno [T 0.0463] okāsakammaṃ kārāpentassa nālaṃ okāsakammaṃ kātuṃ.

430. “Venerable sir, with how many factors is a bhikkhu endowed, for whom it is unsuitable to perform the act of granting leave when he requests it?” “Upāli, for a bhikkhu endowed with five factors, it is unsuitable to perform the act of granting leave when he requests it. With which five? He is shameless; he is foolish; he is not a monk in good standing; he speaks with the intention of causing one to fall away from the Dispensation; he does not speak with the intention of rehabilitating one from an offense. Upāli, for a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors, it is unsuitable to perform the act of granting leave when he requests it.”

“Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno okāsakammaṃ kārāpentassa alaṃ okāsakammaṃ kātuṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Lajjī ca hoti, paṇḍito ca, pakatatto ca, vuṭṭhānādhippāyo vattā hoti, no cāvanādhippāyo – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno okāsakammaṃ kārāpentassa alaṃ okāsakammaṃ kātu”nti.

“Upāli, for a bhikkhu endowed with five factors, it is suitable to perform the act of granting leave when he requests it. With which five? He is conscientious; he is wise; he is a monk in good standing; he speaks with the intention of rehabilitating one from an offense; he does not speak with the intention of causing one to fall away from the Dispensation. Upāli, for a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors, it is suitable to perform the act of granting leave when he requests it.”

431. “Katihi nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ vinayo na sākacchitabbo”ti? “Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ vinayo na sākacchitabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Vatthuṃ na jānāti, nidānaṃ na jānāti, paññattiṃ na jānāti, padapaccābhaṭṭhaṃ na jānāti, anusandhivacanapathaṃ na jānāti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ vinayo na sākacchitabbo.

431. “Venerable sir, with how many factors must a bhikkhu be endowed such that the Vinaya should not be discussed with him?” “Upāli, the Vinaya should not be discussed with a bhikkhu who is endowed with five factors. With which five? He does not know the subject matter; he does not know the origin; he does not know the regulation; he does not know the key phrase; he does not know the sequence of words and their connection. Upāli, the Vinaya should not be discussed with a bhikkhu who is endowed with these five factors.”

“Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ vinayo sākacchitabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Vatthuṃ jānāti, nidānaṃ jānāti, paññattiṃ jānāti, padapaccābhaṭṭhaṃ jānāti, anusandhivacanapathaṃ jānāti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ vinayo sākacchitabbo”ti.

“Upāli, the Vinaya should be discussed with a bhikkhu who is endowed with five factors. With which five? He knows the subject matter; he knows the origin; he knows the regulation; he knows the key phrase; he knows the sequence of words and their connection. Upāli, the Vinaya should be discussed with a bhikkhu who is endowed with these five factors.”

432. “Kati nu kho, bhante, pañhāpucchā”ti? “Pañcimā, upāli, pañhāpucchā. Katamā pañca? Mandattā momūhattā pañhaṃ pucchati, pāpiccho icchāpakato pañhaṃ pucchati, paribhavā pañhaṃ pucchati[T 0.0464], aññātukāmo pañhaṃ pucchati, sace me pañhaṃ puṭṭho sammadeva byākarissati [V 0.0350] iccetaṃ kusalaṃ no ce pañhaṃ puṭṭho sammadeva byākarissati ahamassa sammadeva byākarissāmīti pañhaṃ pucchati – imā kho, upāli, pañca pañhāpucchā”ti.

432. “Venerable Sir, how many kinds of questioning are there?” “Upāli, there are these five kinds of questioning. What five? One asks a question out of dullness and delusion; one asks a question with evil desires, being overcome by desire; one asks a question out of contempt; one asks a question wishing to know; one asks a question thinking: ‘If, when I have asked the question, he answers correctly, that is good; but if he does not answer correctly, I will answer it correctly for him’—these, Upāli, are the five kinds of questioning.”

433. “Kati nu kho, bhante, aññabyākaraṇā”ti? “Pañcime, upāli, aññabyākaraṇā. Katame pañca? Mandattā momūhattā aññaṃ byākaroti, pāpiccho icchāpakato aññaṃ byākaroti, ummādā cittakkhepā aññaṃ byākaroti[M 0.0328], adhimānena aññaṃ byākaroti, bhūtaṃ aññaṃ byākaroti – ime kho, upāli, pañca aññabyākaraṇā”ti.

433. “Venerable Sir, how many declarations of final knowledge are there?” “Upāli, there are these five declarations of final knowledge. What five? One declares final knowledge out of dullness and delusion; one declares final knowledge out of evil desires, being overcome by desire; one declares final knowledge out of madness and mental distraction; one declares final knowledge out of conceit; one declares final knowledge of what is actual—these, Upāli, are the five declarations of final knowledge.”

434. “Kati nu kho, bhante, visuddhiyo”ti? “Pañcimā, upāli, visuddhiyo. Katamā pañca? Nidānaṃ uddisitvā avasesaṃ sutena sāvetabbaṃ ayaṃ paṭhamā visuddhi, nidānaṃ uddisitvā cattāri pārājikāni uddisitvā avasesaṃ sutena sāvetabbaṃ ayaṃ dutiyā visuddhi, nidānaṃ uddisitvā cattāri pārājikāni uddisitvā terasa saṅghādisese uddisitvā avasesaṃ sutena sāvetabbaṃ ayaṃ tatiyā visuddhi, nidānaṃ uddisitvā cattāri pārājikāni uddisitvā terasa saṅghādisese uddisitvā dve aniyate uddisitvā avasesaṃ sutena sāvetabbaṃ ayaṃ catutthā visuddhi, vitthāreneva pañcamī – imā kho, upāli, pañca visuddhiyo”ti.

434. “Venerable Sir, how many purifications are there?” “Upāli, there are these five purifications. What five? After reciting the preamble, the remainder should be announced by the word ‘heard’—this is the first purification. After reciting the preamble and the four Pārājikas, the remainder should be announced by the word ‘heard’—this is the second purification. After reciting the preamble, the four Pārājikas, and the thirteen Saṅghādisesas, the remainder should be announced by the word ‘heard’—this is the third purification. After reciting the preamble, the four Pārājikas, the thirteen Saṅghādisesas, and the two Aniyatas, the remainder should be announced by the word ‘heard’—this is the fourth purification. The fifth is the recitation in full—these, Upāli, are the five purifications.”

435. “Kati [P 5.0190] nu kho, bhante, bhojanā”ti? “Pañcime, upāli, bhojanā[T 0.0465]. Katame pañca? Odano, kummāso, sattu, maccho, maṃsaṃ – ime kho, upāli, pañca bhojanā”ti.

435. “Venerable Sir, how many staple foods are there?” “Upāli, there are these five staple foods. What five? Cooked rice, barley-meal, roasted grain flour, fish, and meat—these, Upāli, are the five staple foods.”

Diṭṭhāvikammavaggo niṭṭhito catuttho.

The Fourth Chapter, on Making Seen, is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary for this is:

Diṭṭhāvikammā apare, paṭiggahānatirittā;

Pavāraṇā paṭiññātaṃ, okāsaṃ sākacchena ca;

Pañhaṃ aññabyākaraṇā, visuddhi cāpi bhojanāti.

Making seen, the other, acceptance, not in excess; invitation, undertaking, permission, and with discussion; questioning, declaration of final knowledge, purification, and also food.

5. Attādānavaggo

5. The Chapter on Admonishment

436. cūḷava. 399; a. ni. 10.44 “Codakena, bhante, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena kati dhamme ajjhattaṃ paccavekkhitvā paro codetabbo”ti? “Codakenupāli, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena pañca dhamme ajjhattaṃ [V 0.0351] paccavekkhitvā paro codetabbo. Katame pañca? Codakenupāli, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – parisuddhakāyasamācāro nu khomhi, parisuddhenamhi kāyasamācārena samannāgato acchiddena appaṭimaṃsena, saṃvijjati nu kho me [M 0.0329] eso dhammo udāhu no”ti. No ce, upāli, bhikkhu parisuddhakāyasamācāro hoti, parisuddhena kāyasamācārena samannāgato acchiddena appaṭimaṃsena, tassa bhavanti vattāro – ‘iṅgha, tāva āyasmā kāyikaṃ sikkhassū’ti itissa bhavanti vattāro.

436. “Venerable sir, having reflected inwardly on how many qualities should a bhikkhu who wishes to admonish another do so?” “Upāli, a bhikkhu who wishes to admonish another should do so after having reflected inwardly on five qualities. What are the five? Upāli, a bhikkhu who wishes to admonish another should reflect thus: ‘Am I of pure bodily conduct? Am I endowed with bodily conduct that is pure, unbroken, and irreproachable? Does this quality exist in me, or not?’ If, Upāli, a bhikkhu is not of pure bodily conduct, not endowed with bodily conduct that is pure, unbroken, and irreproachable, there will be those who will say to him: ‘Come, venerable one, first you should train in what pertains to the body.’ Thus there will be those who will say this to him.”

“Puna caparaṃ, upāli, codakena bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘parisuddhavacīsamācāro nu khomhi, parisuddhenamhi vacīsamācārena [T 0.0466] samannāgato acchiddena appaṭimaṃsena, saṃvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no’ti. No ce, upāli, bhikkhu parisuddhavacīsamācāro hoti, parisuddhena vacīsamācārena samannāgato acchiddena appaṭimaṃsena, tassa bhavanti vattāro – ‘iṅgha, tāva āyasmā vācasikaṃ sikkhassū’ti itissa bhavanti vattāro.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu who wishes to admonish another should reflect thus: ‘Am I of pure verbal conduct? Am I endowed with verbal conduct that is pure, unbroken, and irreproachable? Does this quality exist in me, or not?’ If, Upāli, a bhikkhu is not of pure verbal conduct, not endowed with verbal conduct that is pure, unbroken, and irreproachable, there will be those who say to him: ‘Come, venerable one, first you should train in what pertains to speech.’ Thus there will be those who will say this to him.”

“Puna caparaṃ, upāli, codakena bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘mettaṃ nu kho me cittaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ sabrahmacārīsu anāghātaṃ, saṃvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no’ti. No ce, upāli, bhikkhuno mettaṃ cittaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ hoti sabrahmacārīsu anāghātaṃ, tassa bhavanti vattāro – ‘iṅgha, tāva āyasmā sabrahmacārīsu mettaṃ cittaṃ upaṭṭhāpehī’ti itissa bhavanti vattāro.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu who wishes to admonish another should reflect thus: ‘Is my mind of loving-kindness, free from animosity, established towards my fellows in the holy life? Does this quality exist in me, or does it not?’ If, Upāli, a bhikkhu's mind of loving-kindness, free from animosity, is not established towards his fellows in the holy life, there will be those who say to him: ‘Come, venerable one, first establish a mind of loving-kindness towards your fellows in the holy life.’ Thus there will be those who will say this to him.”

“Puna caparaṃ, upāli, codakena bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘bahussuto nu khomhi sutadharo sutasannicayo, ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ abhivadanti, tathārūpā me dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā, saṃvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no’ti. No ce, upāli, bhikkhu bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo, ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṃ [T 0.0467] sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ abhivadanti, tathārūpassa dhammā na bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā, tassa bhavanti vattāro – ‘iṅgha, tāva āyasmā āgamaṃ pariyāpuṇassū’ti itissa bhavanti vattāro.

Furthermore, Upāli, a monk desiring to admonish another should reflect thus: ‘Am I of great learning, a bearer of the teachings, an accumulator of the teachings? Those teachings that are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with meaning and with expression, proclaiming the holy life that is wholly complete and perfectly pure—have such teachings been greatly learned by me, borne in mind, familiarized by word, contemplated by mind, and well penetrated by wisdom? Does this quality exist in me, or does it not?’ If, Upāli, a monk is not of great learning, a bearer of the teachings, an accumulator of the teachings; and if those teachings that are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with meaning and with expression, proclaiming the holy life that is wholly complete and perfectly pure, have not been greatly learned by him, borne in mind, familiarized by word, contemplated by mind, and well penetrated by wisdom, there will be those who say to him: ‘Come, venerable one, first learn the scriptures.’ Thus, there will be those who speak to him.

“Puna [M 0.0330][V 0.0352] caparaṃ, upāli, codakena bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘ubhayāni kho me pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni honti suvibhattāni suppavattīni suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso, saṃvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no’ti. No ce, upāli, bhikkhuno ubhayāni pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni honti suvibhattāni suppavattīni suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso, ‘idaṃ panāvuso kattha vuttaṃ bhagavatā’ti iti puṭṭho na sampāyati na sampādayati (ka.), na sampādeti (syā.), tassa bhavanti vattāro – ‘iṅgha, tāva āyasmā vinayaṃ pariyāpuṇassū’ti itissa bhavanti vattāro. Codakenupāli, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena ime pañca dhamme ajjhattaṃ paccavekkhitvā paro codetabbo”ti.

Furthermore, Upāli, a monk who is an admonisher, desiring to admonish another, should reflect thus: ‘Are both Pātimokkhas well-mastered by me in detail, well-analyzed, well-recited, and well-decided upon, according to the rule and according to the detailed analysis? Does this quality exist in me, or does it not?’ If, Upāli, both Pātimokkhas are not well-mastered by the monk in detail, well-analyzed, well-recited, and well-decided upon, according to the rule and according to the detailed analysis, and when asked, ‘Friend, where was this spoken by the Blessed One?’ he is unable to answer fully, then there will be those who say to him: ‘Come now, venerable one, first you should master the Vinaya.’ Thus there will be those who speak to him. Upāli, a monk who is an admonisher, desiring to admonish another, having reflected on these five qualities within himself, should admonish another.

437. “Codakena, bhante, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena kati dhamme ajjhattaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā paro codetabbo”ti? “Codakenupāli, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena pañca dhamme ajjhattaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā paro codetabbo. Katame pañca? Kālena vakkhāmi no akālena[T 0.0468], bhūtena vakkhāmi no abhūtena, saṇhena vakkhāmi no pharusena, atthasaṃhitena vakkhāmi no anatthasaṃhitena, mettācitto vakkhāmi no dosantaroti – codakenupāli, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena ime pañca dhamme ajjhattaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā paro codetabbo”ti.

437. “Venerable sir, a monk desiring to admonish another should establish how many qualities within himself before admonishing that other?” “Upāli, a monk desiring to admonish another should establish five qualities within himself before admonishing that other. What five? ‘I will speak at the proper time, not at the improper time; I will speak what is true, not what is untrue; I will speak gently, not harshly; I will speak what is beneficial, not what is unbeneficial; I will speak with a mind of loving-kindness, not with a mind of inner hatred.’ Upāli, a monk desiring to admonish another, having established these five qualities within himself, should then admonish that other.”

438. cūḷava. 400 “Codakena, bhante, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena kati dhamme ajjhattaṃ manasi karitvā paro codetabbo”ti? “Codakenupāli, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena pañca dhamme ajjhattaṃ manasi karitvā paro codetabbo. Katame pañca? Kāruññatā, hitesitā, anukampatā, āpattivuṭṭhānatā, vinayapurekkhāratā – codakenupāli, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena ime pañca dhamme ajjhattaṃ manasi karitvā paro codetabbo”ti.

438. “Venerable sir, a monk desiring to admonish another should bear how many qualities in mind before admonishing that other person?” “Upāli, a monk desiring to admonish another should bear five qualities in mind before admonishing that other person. What five? Compassion, seeking their welfare, sympathy, desiring their rehabilitation from an offense, and holding the Vinaya foremost. Upāli, a monk desiring to admonish another should bear these five qualities in mind before admonishing that other person.”

439. “Katihi nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno okāsakammaṃ kārāpentassa nālaṃ okāsakammaṃ kātu”nti? “Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno okāsakammaṃ kārāpentassa nālaṃ okāsakammaṃ kātuṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Aparisuddhakāyasamācāro hoti[M 0.0331], aparisuddhavacīsamācāro hoti, aparisuddhājīvo hoti, bālo hoti abyatto, na paṭibalo anuyuñjiyamāno anuyogaṃ dātuṃ – imehi [P 5.0191] kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno okāsakammaṃ kārāpentassa nālaṃ okāsakammaṃ kātuṃ.

439. “Venerable sir, endowed with how many factors is a monk unsuitable to perform the act of giving leave?” “Upāli, a monk endowed with five factors is unsuitable to perform the act of giving leave. With what five? He is of impure bodily conduct, he is of impure verbal conduct, he is of impure livelihood, he is foolish and unskilful, and when questioned, is not competent to give a response. Upāli, a monk endowed with these five factors is unsuitable to perform the act of giving leave.”

“Pañcahupāli[V 0.0353], aṅgehi [T 0.0469] samannāgatassa bhikkhuno okāsakammaṃ kārāpentassa alaṃ okāsakammaṃ kātuṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Parisuddhakāyasamācāro hoti, parisuddhavacīsamācāro hoti, parisuddhājīvo hoti, paṇḍito hoti byatto paṭibalo anuyuñjiyamāno anuyogaṃ dātuṃ – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno okāsakammaṃ kārāpentassa alaṃ okāsakammaṃ kātu”nti.

“Upāli, a monk endowed with five factors is suitable to perform the act of giving leave. With what five? He is of pure bodily conduct, he is of pure verbal conduct, he is of pure livelihood, he is wise and skilful, and when questioned, is competent to give a response. Upāli, a monk endowed with these five factors is suitable to perform the act of giving leave.”

440. cūḷava. 398 “Attādānaṃ ādātukāmena, bhante, bhikkhunā katihaṅgehi samannāgataṃ attādānaṃ ādātabba”nti? “Attādānaṃ ādātukāmenupāli, bhikkhunā pañcaṅgasamannāgataṃ pañcahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ (sī. syā.) attādānaṃ ādātabbaṃ. Katame pañca katamehi pañcahi (syā.)? Attādānaṃ ādātukāmena, upāli, bhikkhunā evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ imaṃ attādānaṃ ādātukāmo, kālo nu kho imaṃ attādānaṃ ādātuṃ udāhu no’ti. Sace, upāli, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘akālo imaṃ attādānaṃ ādātuṃ no kālo’ti, na taṃ, upāli, attādānaṃ ādātabbaṃ.

440. “Venerable sir, when a bhikkhu wishes to take up a legal issue for himself, how many factors must that issue possess for it to be taken up?” “Upāli, when a bhikkhu wishes to take up a legal issue for himself, it should possess five factors for it to be taken up. What are the five? A bhikkhu who wishes to take up a legal issue for himself, Upāli, should reflect thus: ‘Regarding this legal issue I wish to take up for myself, is it the right time to take it up, or is it not?’ If, Upāli, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, knows thus: ‘It is the wrong time to take up this legal issue for oneself, not the right time,’ then, Upāli, that legal issue for oneself must not be taken up.

“Sace panupāli, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘kālo imaṃ attādānaṃ ādātuṃ no akālo’ti, tenupāli bhikkhunā uttari paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ imaṃ attādānaṃ ādātukāmo bhūtaṃ nu kho idaṃ attādānaṃ udāhu no’ti. Sace, upāli, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘abhūtaṃ idaṃ attādānaṃ no bhūta’nti, na taṃ, upāli, attādānaṃ ādātabbaṃ.

“But if, Upāli, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, knows thus: ‘It is the right time to take up this legal issue for oneself, not the wrong time,’ then, Upāli, that bhikkhu must reflect further: ‘Regarding this legal issue I wish to take up for myself, is it factual, or is it not?’ If, Upāli, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, knows thus: ‘This legal issue for oneself is not factual; it is not true,’ then, Upāli, that legal issue for oneself must not be taken up.

“Sace panupāli bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno [T 0.0470] evaṃ jānāti – ‘bhūtaṃ idaṃ attādānaṃ no abhūta’nti, tenupāli bhikkhunā uttari paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘yaṃ kho ahaṃ imaṃ attādānaṃ ādātukāmo, atthasaṃhitaṃ nu kho idaṃ attādānaṃ udāhu no’ti. Sace, upāli, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti [M 0.0332] –’ anatthasaṃhitaṃ idaṃ attādānaṃ no atthasaṃhita’nti, na taṃ, upāli, attādānaṃ ādātabbaṃ.

But if, Upāli, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, knows thus: ‘This matter to be taken up by oneself is factual, not unfactual,’ then, Upāli, that bhikkhu must reflect further: ‘Regarding this matter I wish to take up for myself, is it connected with benefit, or is it not?’ If, Upāli, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, knows thus: ‘This matter to be taken up by oneself is unbeneficial, not beneficial,’ then, Upāli, that matter to be taken up by oneself must not be taken up.

“Sace panupāli bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘atthasaṃhitaṃ idaṃ attādānaṃ no anatthasaṃhita’nti, tenupāli bhikkhunā uttari paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘imaṃ kho ahaṃ attādānaṃ ādiyamāno labhissāmi sandiṭṭhe sambhatte bhikkhū dhammato vinayato pakkhe udāhu no’ti. Sace, upāli, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘imaṃ kho ahaṃ attādānaṃ ādiyamāno [V 0.0354] na labhissāmi sandiṭṭhe sambhatte bhikkhū dhammato vinayato pakkhe’ti, na taṃ, upāli, attādānaṃ ādātabbaṃ.

But if, Upāli, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, knows thus: ‘This matter to be taken up by oneself is beneficial, not unbeneficial,’ then, Upāli, that bhikkhu should reflect further: ‘By taking up this matter for myself, shall I gain bhikkhus who are acquaintances and companions as allies in accordance with the Dhamma and the Vinaya, or not?’ If, Upāli, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, knows thus: ‘By taking up this matter for myself, I shall not gain bhikkhus who are acquaintances and companions as allies in accordance with the Dhamma and the Vinaya,’ then, Upāli, that matter to be taken up by oneself should not be taken up.

“Sace panupāli bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘idaṃ kho ahaṃ attādānaṃ ādiyamāno labhissāmi sandiṭṭhe sambhatte bhikkhū dhammato vinayato pakkhe’ti, tenupāli bhikkhunā uttari paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘imaṃ kho me attādānaṃ ādiyato bhavissati saṅghassa tatonidānaṃ bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo saṅghabhedo saṅgharāji saṅghavavatthānaṃ saṅghanānākaraṇaṃ udāhu no’ti. Sace, upāli, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘imaṃ kho me attādānaṃ ādiyato bhavissati saṅghassa tatonidānaṃ bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo [T 0.0471] saṅghabhedo saṅgharāji saṅghavavatthānaṃ saṅghanānākaraṇa’nti, na taṃ, upāli, attādānaṃ ādātabbaṃ.

But if, Upāli, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, knows thus: ‘By taking up this matter for myself, I shall gain bhikkhus who are acquaintances and companions as allies in accordance with the Dhamma and the Vinaya,’ then, Upāli, that bhikkhu should reflect further: ‘As a result of my taking up this matter, will there arise for the Saṅgha quarreling, disputes, contention, controversy, schism in the Saṅgha, a rift in the Saṅgha, a division in the Saṅgha, and separate observances in the Saṅgha, or not?’ If, Upāli, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, knows thus: ‘As a result of my taking up this matter, there will arise for the Saṅgha quarreling, disputes, contention, controversy, schism in the Saṅgha, a rift in the Saṅgha, a division in the Saṅgha, and separate observances in the Saṅgha,’ then, Upāli, that matter to be taken up by oneself should not be taken up.

“Sace panupāli bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘imaṃ kho me attādānaṃ ādiyato na bhavissati saṅghassa tatonidānaṃ bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo saṅghabhedo saṅgharāji saṅghavavatthānaṃ saṅghanānākaraṇa’nti, taṃ ādātabbaṃ, upāli, attādānaṃ. Evaṃ pañcaṅgasamannāgataṃ kho, upāli, attādānaṃ ādinnaṃ pacchāpi avippaṭisārakaraṃ bhavissatī”ti.

But if, Upāli, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, knows thus: ‘As a result of my taking up this matter, there will not arise for the Saṅgha quarreling, disputes, contention, controversy, schism in the Saṅgha, a rift in the Saṅgha, a division in the Saṅgha, or separate observances in the Saṅgha,’ then, Upāli, that matter to be taken up by oneself should be taken up. Thus, Upāli, the taking up of a matter endowed with five factors, when it is taken up, will also afterwards be a cause for non-regret.

441. “Katihi nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu adhikaraṇajātānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bahūpakāro hotī”ti? “Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu adhikaraṇajātānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bahūpakāro hoti. Katamehi pañcahi? Sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati [M 0.0333] sikkhāpadesu; bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo; ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ abhivadanti tathārūpassa dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā, ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni honti suvibhattāni suppavattīni suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso; vinaye kho pana ṭhito hoti asaṃhīro; paṭibalo hoti [T 0.0472] ubho atthapaccatthike assāsetuṃ saññāpetuṃ nijjhāpetuṃ pekkhetuṃ pasādetuṃ – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu adhikaraṇajātānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bahūpakāro hoti.

441. “Venerable sir, with how many qualities must a bhikkhu be endowed to be of great help to bhikkhus involved in disputes?” “Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five qualities is of great help to bhikkhus involved in disputes. Which five? He is virtuous; he dwells restrained by the Pātimokkha restraint, accomplished in conduct and resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults, and trains himself by undertaking the training rules. He is learned, a preserver of what he has heard, a storer of what he has heard. Those teachings that are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing, proclaiming the perfectly complete and pure holy life—such teachings he has heard much, retained, recited verbally, mentally investigated, and penetrated well by view. Both Pātimokkhas are well learned by him in detail, well analyzed, well mastered, and well determined according to the rules and their detailed analysis. He is firm in the Vinaya and unshakeable. He is competent to reassure, persuade, convince, clarify, and please both parties in the dispute. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five qualities is of great help to bhikkhus involved in disputes.

“Aparehipi[V 0.0355], upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu adhikaraṇajātānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bahūpakāro hoti. Katamehi pañcahi? Parisuddhakāyasamācāro hoti, parisuddhavacīsamācāro hoti, parisuddhājīvo hoti, paṇḍito hoti byatto, paṭibalo anuyuñjiyamāno anuyogaṃ dātuṃ – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu adhikaraṇajātānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bahūpakāro hoti.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five other qualities is of great help to bhikkhus involved in disputes. Which five? He is pure in bodily conduct, pure in verbal conduct, and pure in livelihood; he is wise and clever, and competent to give an answer when questioned. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five qualities is of great help to bhikkhus involved in disputes.

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu adhikaraṇajātānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bahūpakāro hoti. Katamehi pañcahi? Vatthuṃ jānāti, nidānaṃ jānāti, paññattiṃ jānāti[P 5.0192], padapaccābhaṭṭhaṃ jānāti, anusandhivacanapathaṃ jānāti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu adhikaraṇajātānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bahūpakāro hotī”ti.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five other qualities is of great help to bhikkhus involved in disputes. Which five? He knows the subject matter, he knows the origin, he knows the regulation, he knows the initial word, and he knows the sequence of connected speech. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five qualities is of great help to bhikkhus involved in disputes.”

442. “Katihi nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā nānuyuñjitabba”nti? “Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā nānuyuñjitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Suttaṃ na jānāti, suttānulomaṃ na jānāti, vinayaṃ na jānāti, vinayānulomaṃ na jānāti, na ca ṭhānāṭhānakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā nānuyuñjitabbaṃ.

442. “Venerable sir, endowed with how many qualities should a bhikkhu not be questioned?” “Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five qualities should not be questioned. With which five? He does not know the Sutta, he does not know what is in conformity with the Sutta, he does not know the Vinaya, he does not know what is in conformity with the Vinaya, and he is not skilled in what is a valid reason and what is not. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five qualities should not be questioned.

“Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena [T 0.0473] bhikkhunā anuyuñjitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Suttaṃ jānāti, suttānulomaṃ jānāti, vinayaṃ jānāti, vinayānulomaṃ [M 0.0334] jānāti, ṭhānāṭhānakusalo ca hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anuyuñjitabbaṃ.

“Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five qualities should be questioned. With which five? He knows the Sutta, he knows what is in conformity with the Sutta, he knows the Vinaya, he knows what is in conformity with the Vinaya, and he is skilled in what is a valid reason and what is not. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five qualities should be questioned.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā nānuyuñjitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Dhammaṃ na jānāti, dhammānulomaṃ na jānāti, vinayaṃ na jānāti, vinayānulomaṃ na jānāti, na ca pubbāparakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā nānuyuñjitabbaṃ.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with another five qualities should not be questioned. With which five? He does not know the Dhamma, he does not know what is in conformity with the Dhamma, he does not know the Vinaya, he does not know what is in conformity with the Vinaya, and he is not skilled in what comes before and after. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five qualities should not be questioned.”

“Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anuyuñjitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Dhammaṃ jānāti, dhammānulomaṃ jānāti, vinayaṃ jānāti, vinayānulomaṃ jānāti, pubbāparakusalo [V 0.0356] ca hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anuyuñjitabbaṃ.

“Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five qualities should be questioned. With which five? He knows the Dhamma, he knows what is in conformity with the Dhamma, he knows the Vinaya, he knows what is in conformity with the Vinaya, and he is skilled in what comes before and after. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five qualities should be questioned.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā nānuyuñjitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Vatthuṃ na jānāti, nidānaṃ na jānāti, paññattiṃ na jānāti, padapaccābhaṭṭhaṃ na jānāti, anusandhivacanapathaṃ na jānāti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā nānuyuñjitabbaṃ.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with another five qualities should not be questioned. With which five? He does not know the subject matter, he does not know the origin, he does not know the regulation, he does not know the word presented, and he does not know the connection of the discourse. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five qualities should not be questioned.”

“Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anuyuñjitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Vatthuṃ jānāti, nidānaṃ jānāti, paññattiṃ jānāti, padapaccābhaṭṭhaṃ jānāti, anusandhivacanapathaṃ jānāti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā [T 0.0474] anuyuñjitabbaṃ.

“Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five qualities should be questioned. With which five? He knows the subject matter, he knows the origin, he knows the regulation, he knows the word presented, and he knows the connection of the discourse. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five qualities should be questioned.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā nānuyuñjitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Āpattiṃ na jānāti, āpattisamuṭṭhānaṃ na jānāti, āpattiyā payogaṃ na jānāti, āpattiyā vūpasamaṃ na jānāti, āpattiyā na vinicchayakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā nānuyuñjitabbaṃ.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with another five qualities should not be questioned. With which five? He does not know the offense, he does not know the origin of the offense, he does not know the application of the offense, he does not know the settlement of the offense, and he is not skilled in deciding upon the offense. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five qualities should not be questioned.”

“Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anuyuñjitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Āpattiṃ jānāti, āpattisamuṭṭhānaṃ jānāti, āpattiyā payogaṃ jānāti, āpattiyā vūpasamaṃ jānāti, āpattiyā vinicchayakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anuyuñjitabbaṃ.

“Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five qualities should be questioned. With which five? He knows the offense, he knows the origin of the offense, he knows the application of the offense, he knows the settlement of the offense, and he is skilled in deciding upon the offense. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five qualities should be questioned.”

“Aparehipi[M 0.0335], upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā nānuyuñjitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Adhikaraṇaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇasamuṭṭhānaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇassa payogaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇassa vūpasamaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇassa na vinicchayakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā nānuyuñjitabbaṃ.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with another five qualities should not be questioned. With which five? He does not know the legal issue, he does not know the origin of the legal issue, he does not know the application of the legal issue, he does not know the settlement of the legal issue, and he is not skilled in deciding upon the legal issue. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five qualities should not be questioned.”

“Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anuyuñjitabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Adhikaraṇaṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇasamuṭṭhānaṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇassa payogaṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇassa [V 0.0357] vūpasamaṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇassa vinicchayakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anuyuñjitabba”nti.

“Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five qualities should be questioned. With which five? He knows the legal issue, he knows the origin of the legal issue, he knows the application of the legal issue, he knows the settlement of the legal issue, and he is skilled in deciding the legal issue. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five qualities should be questioned.”

Attādānavaggo niṭṭhito pañcamo.

The fifth chapter, the Attādāna Vagga, is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Parisuddhañca [T 0.0475] kālena, kāruññaṃ okāsena ca;

Attādānaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ, aparehipi vatthuñca;

Suttaṃ dhammaṃ puna vatthuñca, āpatti adhikaraṇena cāti.

Purity and Time, Compassion and Permission; Taking up a Case, the Legal Issue, and the other on the Legal Issue; Subject Matter, Sutta, Dhamma, and again Subject Matter; Offense and the Legal Issue.

6. Dhutaṅgavaggo

6. The Dhutaṅga Chapter

443. “Kati [P 5.0193] nu kho, bhante, āraññikā”ti? “Pañcime, upāli, āraññikā a. ni. 5.181; pari. 325. Katame pañca? Mandattā momūhattā āraññiko hoti, pāpiccho icchāpakato āraññiko hoti, ummādā cittakkhepā āraññiko hoti, vaṇṇitaṃ buddhehi buddhasāvakehīti āraññiko hoti, api ca appicchaññeva nissāya santuṭṭhiññeva nissāya – sallekhaññeva nissāya pavivekaññeva nissāya [V 0.0358] idamatthitaññeva nissāya āraññiko hoti – ime kho, upāli, pañca āraññikā”ti.

443. “Venerable sir, how many kinds of forest-dwellers are there?” “Upāli, there are these five kinds of forest-dwellers. What five? One becomes a forest-dweller due to dullness and delusion; one becomes a forest-dweller due to evil desires and being overcome by wishes; one becomes a forest-dweller due to madness and mental distraction; one becomes a forest-dweller thinking, ‘It is praised by the Buddhas and the Buddha’s disciples’; and one becomes a forest-dweller relying only on fewness of desires, relying only on contentment, relying only on effacement, relying only on seclusion, and relying only on this being the purpose. These, Upāli, are the five kinds of forest-dwellers.”

“Kati nu kho, bhante, piṇḍapātikāti…pe… kati nu kho, bhante, paṃsukūlikāti…pe… kati nu kho, bhante, rukkhamūlikāti…pe… kati nu kho, bhante, sosānikāti…pe… kati nu kho, bhante, abbhokāsikāti…pe… kati [M 0.0336] nu kho, bhante, tecīvarikāti…pe… kati nu kho, bhante, sapadānacārikāti…pe… kati nu kho, bhante, nesajjikāti…pe… kati nu kho, bhante, yathāsanthatikāti…pe… kati nu kho, bhante, ekāsanikāti…pe… kati nu kho, bhante, khalupacchābhattikāti…pe… kati [T 0.0476] nu kho, bhante, pattapiṇḍikāti? Pañcime, upāli, pattapiṇḍikā. Katame pañca? Mandattā momūhattā pattapiṇḍiko hoti, pāpiccho icchāpakato pattapiṇḍiko hoti, ummādā cittakkhepā pattapiṇḍiko hoti, vaṇṇitaṃ buddhehi buddhasāvakehīti pattapiṇḍiko hoti, api ca appicchaññeva nissāya santuṭṭhiññeva nissāya sallekhaññeva nissāya pavivekaññeva nissāya idamatthitaññeva nissāya pattapiṇḍiko hoti – ime kho, upāli, pañca pattapiṇḍikā”ti.

“Venerable sir, how many kinds of alms-food-eaters are there? …and so on… Venerable sir, how many kinds of rag-robe-wearers are there? …and so on… Venerable sir, how many kinds of tree-root-dwellers are there? …and so on… Venerable sir, how many kinds of charnel-ground-dwellers are there? …and so on… Venerable sir, how many kinds of open-air-dwellers are there? …and so on… Venerable sir, how many kinds of triple-robe-wearers are there? …and so on… Venerable sir, how many kinds of continuous-alms-round practitioners are there? …and so on… Venerable sir, how many kinds of sitters are there? …and so on… Venerable sir, how many kinds of any-bed-users are there? …and so on… Venerable sir, how many kinds of one-session-eaters are there? …and so on… Venerable sir, how many kinds of those who refuse later food are there? …and so on… Venerable sir, how many kinds of bowl-food-eaters are there? Upāli, there are these five kinds of bowl-food-eaters. What five? One is a bowl-food-eater due to dullness and delusion; one is a bowl-food-eater due to evil desires and being overcome by wishes; one is a bowl-food-eater due to madness and mental distraction; one is a bowl-food-eater thinking, ‘It is praised by the Buddhas and the Buddha’s disciples’; and moreover, one is a bowl-food-eater relying only on fewness of wishes, relying only on contentment, relying only on effacement, relying only on seclusion, and relying only on this very purpose. These, Upāli, are the five kinds of bowl-food-eaters.”

Dhutaṅgavaggo niṭṭhito chaṭṭho.

The sixth chapter, the Chapter on the Ascetic Practices, is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of its contents:

Āraññiko piṇḍipaṃsu, rukkhasusānapañcamaṃ;

Abbho tecīvarañceva, sapadānanesajjikā;

Santhatekāsanañceva, khalupacchā pattapiṇḍikāti.

The forest-dweller, the alms-food-eater, and the rag-robe-wearer; the tree-root-dweller, and fifth, the charnel-ground-dweller; the open-air-dweller and the triple-robe-wearer; the continuous-alms-round practitioner and the sitter; the any-bed-user and the one-session-eater; the one who refuses later food, and the bowl-food-eater.

7. Musāvādavaggo

7. The Chapter on False Speech

444. “Kati nu kho, bhante, musāvādā”ti? “Pañcime, upāli, musāvādā. Katame pañca? Atthi musāvādo pārājikagāmī, atthi musāvādo saṅghādisesagāmī, atthi musāvādo thullaccayagāmī, atthi musāvādo pācittiyagāmī, atthi musāvādo dukkaṭagāmī – ime kho, upāli, pañca musāvādā”ti.

444. “Venerable sir, how many kinds of false speech are there?” “Upāli, there are these five kinds of false speech. What five? There is false speech that leads to a pārājika offense, there is false speech that leads to a saṅghādisesa offense, there is false speech that leads to a thullaccaya offense, there is false speech that leads to a pācittiya offense, and there is false speech that leads to a dukkaṭa offense. These, Upāli, are the five kinds of false speech.”

445. “Katihi nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno saṅghamajjhe uposathaṃ vā pavāraṇaṃ vā ṭhapentassa – ‘alaṃ, bhikkhu, mā [T 0.0477] bhaṇḍanaṃ, mā kalahaṃ, mā viggahaṃ, mā vivāda’nti [V 0.0359] omadditvā saṅghena uposatho vā pavāraṇā vā kātabbā”ti? “Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno saṅghamajjhe [M 0.0337] uposathaṃ vā pavāraṇaṃ vā ṭhapentassa – ‘alaṃ, bhikkhu, mā bhaṇḍanaṃ, mā kalahaṃ, mā viggahaṃ, mā vivāda’nti omadditvā saṅghena uposatho vā pavāraṇā vā kātabbā. Katamehi pañcahi? Alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto ca, cāvanādhippāyo vattā hoti, no vuṭṭhānādhippāyo – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno saṅghamajjhe uposathaṃ vā pavāraṇaṃ vā ṭhapentassa – ‘alaṃ, bhikkhu, mā bhaṇḍanaṃ, mā kalahaṃ, mā viggahaṃ, mā vivāda’nti omadditvā saṅghena uposatho vā pavāraṇā vā kātabbā.

445. “Venerable sir, with how many factors must a bhikkhu be endowed such that when he suspends the Uposatha or the Pavāraṇā in the midst of the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the Uposatha or the Pavāraṇā after suppressing him, saying: ‘Enough, bhikkhu, do not quarrel, do not dispute, do not contend, do not argue’?” “Upāli, a bhikkhu is endowed with five factors such that when he suspends the Uposatha or the Pavāraṇā in the midst of the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the Uposatha or the Pavāraṇā after suppressing him, saying: ‘Enough, bhikkhu, do not quarrel, do not dispute, do not contend, do not argue.’ With which five? He is shameless, foolish, not of normal character, speaks with the intention of expulsion, and not with the intention of rehabilitation. Upāli, a bhikkhu is endowed with these five factors such that when he suspends the Uposatha or the Pavāraṇā in the midst of the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the Uposatha or the Pavāraṇā after suppressing him, saying: ‘Enough, bhikkhu, do not quarrel, do not dispute, do not contend, do not argue.’”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno saṅghamajjhe uposathaṃ vā pavāraṇaṃ vā ṭhapentassa – ‘alaṃ, bhikkhu, mā bhaṇḍanaṃ, mā kalahaṃ, mā viggahaṃ, mā vivāda’nti omadditvā saṅghena uposatho vā pavāraṇā vā kātabbā. Katamehi pañcahi? Aparisuddhakāyasamācāro hoti, aparisuddhavacīsamācāro [P 5.0194] hoti, aparisuddhājīvo hoti, bālo hoti abyatto, bhaṇḍanakārako hoti kalahakārako – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno saṅghamajjhe uposathaṃ vā pavāraṇaṃ vā ṭhapentassa – ‘alaṃ, bhikkhu, mā bhaṇḍanaṃ, mā kalahaṃ, mā viggahaṃ, mā vivāda’nti omadditvā saṅghena uposatho [T 0.0478] vā pavāraṇā vā kātabbā”ti.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu is endowed with five other factors such that when he suspends the Uposatha or the Pavāraṇā in the midst of the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the Uposatha or the Pavāraṇā after suppressing him, saying: ‘Enough, bhikkhu, do not quarrel, do not dispute, do not contend, do not argue.’ With which five? He has impure bodily conduct, impure verbal conduct, and impure livelihood; he is foolish and inept; and he is a maker of quarrels and a maker of disputes. Upāli, a bhikkhu is endowed with these five factors such that when he suspends the Uposatha or the Pavāraṇā in the midst of the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the Uposatha or the Pavāraṇā after suppressing him, saying: ‘Enough, bhikkhu, do not quarrel, do not dispute, do not contend, do not argue.’”

446. “Katihi nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno anuyogo na dātabbo”ti? “Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno anuyogo na dātabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Āpattānāpattiṃ na jānāti, lahukagarukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, sāvasesānavasesaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, sappaṭikammāpaṭikammaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno anuyogo na dātabbo.

446. “Venerable sir, of a bhikkhu endowed with how many factors should an inquiry not be undertaken?” “Upāli, of a bhikkhu endowed with five factors, an inquiry should not be undertaken. With what five? He does not know offense and non-offense; he does not know a light and a serious offense; he does not know an offense with a remainder and without a remainder; he does not know a gross and a non-gross offense; he does not know an offense that can be remedied and one that cannot be remedied. Upāli, of a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors, an inquiry should not be undertaken.”

“Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno anuyogo dātabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Āpattānāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukagarukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, sāvasesānavasesaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, duṭṭhullāduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, sappaṭikammāpaṭikammaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno anuyogo dātabbo”ti.

“Upāli, of a bhikkhu endowed with five factors, an inquiry should be undertaken. With what five? He knows offense and non-offense; he knows a light and a serious offense; he knows an offense with a remainder and without a remainder; he knows a gross and a non-gross offense; he knows an offense that can be remedied and one that cannot be remedied. Upāli, of a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors, an inquiry should be undertaken.”

447. “Katihi [M 0.0338] nu kho, bhante, ākārehi bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpajjatī”ti? “Pañcahupāli, ākārehi bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpajjati. Katamehi pañcahi? Alajjitā, aññāṇatā, kukkuccapakatatā, akappiye kappiyasaññitā, kappiye akappiyasaññitā – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahākārehi bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpajjati.

447. “Venerable sir, in how many ways does a bhikkhu commit an offense?” “Upāli, a bhikkhu commits an offense in five ways. In what five? Through shamelessness, through ignorance, through being prone to scrupulousness, through perceiving the unallowable as allowable, and through perceiving the allowable as unallowable. Upāli, it is in these five ways that a bhikkhu commits an offense.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahākārehi bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpajjati. Katamehi pañcahi[T 0.0479]? Adassanena, assavanena, pasuttakatā, tathāsaññī, satisammosā – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahākārehi bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpajjatī”ti.

“Upāli, a bhikkhu also commits an offense in five other ways. In what five? Through not seeing, through not hearing, through being asleep, through a mistaken perception, and through a lapse of mindfulness. Upāli, it is in these five ways that a bhikkhu commits an offense.”

448. “Kati nu kho, bhante, verā”ti? “Pañcime, upāli, verā. Katame pañca? Pāṇātipāto[V 0.0360], adinnādānaṃ, kāmesumicchācāro, musāvādo, surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānaṃ – ime kho, upāli, pañca verā”ti.

448. “Venerable sir, how many enmities are there?” “Upāli, there are these five enmities. What five? The destruction of life, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and indulgence in distilled and fermented intoxicants which are the basis for heedlessness. These, Upāli, are the five enmities.”

“Kati nu kho, bhante, veramaṇiyo”ti? “Pañcimā, upāli, veramaṇiyo. Katamā pañca? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī veramaṇi (ka.), adinnādānā veramaṇī, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī, musāvādā veramaṇī, surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī – imā kho, upāli, pañca veramaṇiyo”ti.

“Venerable sir, how many abstinences are there?” “Upāli, there are these five abstinences. What five? Abstaining from the destruction of life, abstaining from taking what is not given, abstaining from sexual misconduct, abstaining from false speech, and abstaining from consuming intoxicating drink and drugs which are the basis for heedlessness. These, Upāli, are the five abstinences.”

449. “Kati nu kho, bhante, byasanānī”ti? “Pañcimāni, upāli, byasanāni. pari. 325; a. ni. 5.130 Katamāni pañca? Ñātibyasanaṃ, bhogabyasanaṃ, rogabyasanaṃ, sīlabyasanaṃ, diṭṭhibyasanaṃ – imāni kho, upāli, pañca byasanānī”ti.

449. “Venerable sir, how many misfortunes are there?” “Upāli, there are these five misfortunes. What five? The misfortune of relatives, the misfortune of wealth, the misfortune of disease, the misfortune of virtue, and the misfortune of view. These, Upāli, are the five misfortunes.”

“Kati nu kho, bhante, sampadā”ti? “Pañcimā, upāli, sampadā. pari. 325; a. ni. 5.130 Katamā pañca? Ñātisampadā, bhogasampadā, ārogyasampadā, sīlasampadā, diṭṭhisampadā – imā kho, upāli, pañca sampadā”ti.

“Venerable sir, how many accomplishments are there?” “Upāli, there are these five accomplishments. What five? The accomplishment of relatives, the accomplishment of wealth, the accomplishment of health, the accomplishment of virtue, and the accomplishment of view. These, Upāli, are the five accomplishments.”

Musāvādavaggo niṭṭhito sattamo.

The Seventh Chapter on False Speech is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Musāvādo [T 0.0480][P 5.0195] ca omaddi, aparehi anuyogo;

Āpattiñca aparehi, verā veramaṇīpi ca;

Byasanaṃ sampadā ceva, sattamo vaggasaṅgahoti.

False Speech, Suppression, another on Suppression, Inquiry; Offense, another on Offense, Enmities and Abstinences too; Misfortunes and Accomplishments as well. This is the collection of the seventh chapter.

8. Bhikkhunovādavaggo

8. The Chapter on Admonition to Bhikkhunīs

450. “Katihi [M 0.0339] nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno bhikkhunisaṅgheneva kammaṃ kātabba”nti? “Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno bhikkhunisaṅgheneva kammaṃ kātabbaṃ, avandiyo so bhikkhu bhikkhunisaṅghena. Katamehi pañcahi? Vivaritvā kāyaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ dasseti, ūruṃ dasseti, aṅgajātaṃ dasseti, ubho aṃsakūṭe dasseti, obhāsati, gihī [V 0.0361] sampayojeti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno bhikkhunisaṅgheneva kammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Avandiyo so bhikkhu bhikkhunisaṅghena.

450. “Venerable sir, endowed with how many factors is a bhikkhu against whom a formal act should be undertaken by the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha alone?” “Upāli, endowed with five factors, a formal act should be undertaken against a bhikkhu by the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha alone; that bhikkhu is not to be venerated by the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha. With which five? He exposes his body to bhikkhunīs; he exposes his thigh; he exposes his genitals; he exposes both his shoulder-tops; he reviles; he arranges for a layperson to have sexual intercourse. Upāli, endowed with these five factors, a formal act should be undertaken against a bhikkhu by the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha alone. That bhikkhu is not to be venerated by the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno bhikkhunisaṅgheneva kammaṃ kātabbaṃ, avandiyo so bhikkhu bhikkhunisaṅghena. Katamehi pañcahi? Bhikkhunīnaṃ alābhāya parisakkati, bhikkhunīnaṃ anatthāya parisakkati, bhikkhunīnaṃ avāsāya parisakkati, bhikkhuniyo akkosati paribhāsati, bhikkhū bhikkhunīhi bhedeti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno bhikkhunisaṅgheneva kammaṃ kātabbaṃ, avandiyo so bhikkhu bhikkhunisaṅghena.

“Furthermore, Upāli, for a monk endowed with five other factors, an act should be done by the Saṅgha of nuns alone. That monk is not to be venerated by the Saṅgha of nuns. With which five? He strives for the nuns’ loss of gains, he strives for the nuns’ non-benefit, he strives so that the nuns cannot stay in their residence, he insults and reviles the nuns, and he causes division between the monks and the nuns. Indeed, Upāli, for a monk endowed with these five factors, an act should be done by the Saṅgha of nuns alone. That monk is not to be venerated by the Saṅgha of nuns.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno bhikkhunisaṅgheneva kammaṃ kātabbaṃ, avandiyo so [T 0.0481] bhikkhu bhikkhunisaṅghena. Katamehi pañcahi? Bhikkhunīnaṃ alābhāya parisakkati, bhikkhunīnaṃ anatthāya parisakkati, bhikkhunīnaṃ avāsāya parisakkati, bhikkhuniyo akkosati paribhāsati, bhikkhū bhikkhunīhi sampayojeti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa bhikkhuno bhikkhunisaṅgheneva kammaṃ kātabbaṃ, avandiyo so bhikkhu bhikkhunisaṅghenā”ti.

“Furthermore, Upāli, for a monk endowed with five other factors, an act should be done by the Saṅgha of nuns alone. That monk is not to be venerated by the Saṅgha of nuns. With which five? He strives for the nuns’ loss of gains, he strives for the nuns’ non-benefit, he strives so that the nuns cannot stay in their residence, he insults and reviles the nuns, and he joins monks with nuns for sexual intercourse. Indeed, Upāli, for a monk endowed with these five factors, an act should be done by the Saṅgha of nuns alone. That monk is not to be venerated by the Saṅgha of nuns.”

451. “Katihi nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgatāya bhikkhuniyā kammaṃ kātabba”nti? Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatāya bhikkhuniyā kammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Vivaritvā kāyaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dasseti, ūruṃ dasseti, aṅgajātaṃ dasseti, ubho aṃsakūṭe dasseti, obhāsati, gihī sampayojeti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatāya bhikkhuniyā kammaṃ kātabbaṃ.

451. “Venerable sir, for a nun endowed with how many factors should an act be done?” “Upāli, for a nun endowed with five factors, an act should be done. With which five? Having uncovered her body, she shows it to the monks; she shows her thigh; she shows her sexual organ; she shows both her collarbones; she reviles; she joins a layperson in sexual intercourse. Indeed, Upāli, for a nun endowed with these five factors, an act should be done.”

“Aparehipi[M 0.0340], upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatāya bhikkhuniyā kammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Bhikkhūnaṃ alābhāya parisakkati, bhikkhūnaṃ anatthāya parisakkati, bhikkhūnaṃ avāsāya parisakkati, bhikkhū akkosati paribhāsati, bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūhi bhedeti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatāya bhikkhuniyā kammaṃ kātabbaṃ.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a formal act should be carried out against a bhikkhunī who is endowed with five other factors. With which five? She strives for the bhikkhus' lack of gain, she strives for the bhikkhus' harm, she strives for the bhikkhus' non-residence, she insults and reviles bhikkhus, and she causes division between the bhikkhunīs and the bhikkhus. Indeed, Upāli, a formal act should be carried out against a bhikkhunī who is endowed with these five factors.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatāya bhikkhuniyā kammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Bhikkhūnaṃ alābhāya parisakkati, bhikkhūnaṃ anatthāya parisakkati, bhikkhūnaṃ avāsāya [V 0.0362] parisakkati, bhikkhū akkosati [T 0.0482] paribhāsati, bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūhi sampayojeti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi [P 5.0196] samannāgatāya bhikkhuniyā kammaṃ kātabba”nti.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a formal act should be carried out against a bhikkhunī who is endowed with five other factors. With which five? She strives for the bhikkhus' lack of gain, she strives for the bhikkhus' harm, she strives for the bhikkhus' non-residence, she insults and reviles bhikkhus, and she brings bhikkhunīs together with bhikkhus for the purpose of sexual intercourse. Indeed, Upāli, a formal act should be carried out against a bhikkhunī who is endowed with these five factors.”
