452. “Katihi nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā bhikkhunīnaṃ ovādo na ṭhapetabbo”ti? “Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā bhikkhunīnaṃ ovādo na ṭhapetabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto ca, cāvanādhippāyo vattā hoti, no vuṭṭhānādhippāyo – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā bhikkhunīnaṃ ovādo na ṭhapetabbo.

452. “Venerable sir, endowed with how many factors should a bhikkhu not be appointed for the exhortation of bhikkhunīs?” “Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should not be appointed for the exhortation of bhikkhunīs. With which five? He is shameless, foolish, and not of normal standing; he speaks with the intention of causing a falling away, not with the intention of raising from an offense. Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not be appointed for the exhortation of bhikkhunīs.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā bhikkhunīnaṃ ovādo na ṭhapetabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Aparisuddhakāyasamācāro hoti, aparisuddhavacīsamācāro hoti, aparisuddhājīvo hoti, bālo hoti, abyatto, na paṭibalo anuyuñjiyamāno anuyogaṃ dātuṃ – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā bhikkhunīnaṃ ovādo na ṭhapetabbo.

Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors should not be appointed for the exhortation of bhikkhunīs. With which five? He is of impure bodily conduct, of impure verbal conduct, and of impure livelihood; he is foolish and incompetent, unable to respond to an inquiry when questioned. Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not be appointed for the exhortation of bhikkhunīs.

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā bhikkhunīnaṃ ovādo na ṭhapetabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Kāyikena anācārena samannāgato hoti, vācasikena anācārena samannāgato hoti, kāyikavācasikena anācārena samannāgato hoti, bhikkhunīnaṃ akkosakaparibhāsako hoti, bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ saṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikena saṃsaggena – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena [T 0.0483] bhikkhunā bhikkhunīnaṃ ovādo na ṭhapetabbo.

Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors should not be appointed to admonish the bhikkhunīs. With which five? He is endowed with bodily misconduct, he is endowed with verbal misconduct, he is endowed with bodily and verbal misconduct, he is one who reviles and insults the bhikkhunīs, and he dwells in association with bhikkhunīs through an improper association. Endowed with these five factors, Upāli, a bhikkhu should not be appointed to admonish the bhikkhunīs.

“Aparehipi[M 0.0341], upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā bhikkhunīnaṃ ovādo na ṭhapetabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto ca, bhaṇḍanakārako ca hoti kalahakārako, sikkhāya ca na paripūrikārī – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā bhikkhunīnaṃ ovādo na ṭhapetabbo”ti.

Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors should not be appointed to admonish the bhikkhunīs. With which five? He is shameless, foolish, not of normal character, a maker of quarrels and a maker of disputes, and is not a fulfiller of the training. Endowed with these five factors, Upāli, a bhikkhu should not be appointed to admonish the bhikkhunīs.

453. “Katihi nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā bhikkhunīnaṃ ovādo na gahetabbo”ti? “Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā bhikkhunīnaṃ ovādo na gahetabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Kāyikena anācārena samannāgato hoti, vācasikena anācārena samannāgato hoti, kāyikavācasikena anācārena samannāgato hoti, bhikkhunīnaṃ akkosakaparibhāsako [V 0.0363] hoti, bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ saṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikena saṃsaggena – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā bhikkhunīnaṃ ovādo na gahetabbo.

453. “Venerable sir, endowed with how many factors should a bhikkhu not undertake the admonition of the bhikkhunīs?” “Upāli, endowed with five factors, a bhikkhu should not undertake the admonition of the bhikkhunīs. With which five? He is endowed with bodily misconduct, he is endowed with verbal misconduct, he is endowed with bodily and verbal misconduct, he is one who reviles and insults the bhikkhunīs, and he dwells in association with bhikkhunīs through an improper association. Endowed with these five factors, Upāli, a bhikkhu should not undertake the admonition of the bhikkhunīs.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā bhikkhunīnaṃ ovādo na gahetabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Alajjī ca hoti, bālo ca, apakatatto ca, gamiko vā hoti, gilāno vā – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā bhikkhunīnaṃ ovādo na gahetabbo”ti.

Furthermore, Upāli, the exhortation to the bhikkhunīs should not be undertaken by a bhikkhu who is endowed with five other factors. With which five? He is shameless, and he is foolish, and he is not of normal character, or he is a bhikkhu setting out on a journey, or he is sick. Indeed, Upāli, the exhortation to the bhikkhunīs should not be undertaken by a bhikkhu who is endowed with these five factors.

454. “Katihi [T 0.0484] nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ na sākacchitabbo”ti? “Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ na sākacchitabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Na asekkhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na asekkhena samādhikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na asekkhena paññākkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na asekkhena vimuttikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na asekkhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena samannāgato hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ na sākacchitabbo. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ sākacchitabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Asekkhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena samādhikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena paññākkhandhena samannāgato hoti[M 0.0342], asekkhena vimuttikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena [P 5.0197] samannāgato hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ sākacchitabbo.

454. “Venerable sir, with a bhikkhu endowed with how many factors should one not hold a discussion?” “Upāli, one should not hold a discussion with a bhikkhu endowed with five factors. With which five? He is not endowed with the aggregate of virtue of one beyond training, he is not endowed with the aggregate of concentration of one beyond training, he is not endowed with the aggregate of wisdom of one beyond training, he is not endowed with the aggregate of liberation of one beyond training, and he is not endowed with the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training. Indeed, Upāli, one should not hold a discussion with a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors. Upāli, one should hold a discussion with a bhikkhu endowed with five factors. With which five? He is endowed with the aggregate of virtue of one beyond training, he is endowed with the aggregate of concentration of one beyond training, he is endowed with the aggregate of wisdom of one beyond training, he is endowed with the aggregate of liberation of one beyond training, and he is endowed with the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training. Indeed, Upāli, one should hold a discussion with a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ na sākacchitabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Na atthapaṭisambhidāpatto hoti, na dhammapaṭisambhidāpatto hoti, na niruttipaṭisambhidāpatto hoti, na paṭibhānapaṭisambhidāpatto hoti, yathāvimuttaṃ cittaṃ na paccavekkhitā – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ na sākacchitabbo. Pañcahupāli[T 0.0485], aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ sākacchitabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Atthapaṭisambhidāpatto hoti, dhammapaṭisambhidāpatto hoti, niruttipaṭisambhidāpatto hoti, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidāpatto hoti, yathāvimuttaṃ cittaṃ paccavekkhitā – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ sākacchitabbo”ti.

Furthermore, Upāli, one should not engage in discussion with a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors. With what five? He has not attained the analytical knowledge of meaning, he has not attained the analytical knowledge of the Dhamma, he has not attained the analytical knowledge of language, he has not attained the analytical knowledge of eloquence, and he is not one who reviews the mind as it is liberated. Indeed, Upāli, one should not engage in discussion with a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors. Upāli, one should engage in discussion with a bhikkhu endowed with five factors. With what five? He has attained the analytical knowledge of meaning, he has attained the analytical knowledge of the Dhamma, he has attained the analytical knowledge of language, he has attained the analytical knowledge of eloquence, and he is one who reviews the mind as it is liberated. Indeed, Upāli, one should engage in discussion with a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors.

Bhikkhunovādavaggo niṭṭhito aṭṭhamo.

The eighth chapter, the Chapter on the Exhortation of Bhikkhunīs, is completed.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Bhikkhunīheva [V 0.0364] kātabbaṃ, aparehi tathā duve;

Bhikkhunīnaṃ tayo kammā, na ṭhapetabbā dve dukā;

Na gahetabbā dve vuttā, sākacchāsu ca dve dukāti.

The pentad on acts to be done by nuns alone, and likewise two others; three pentads on acts for nuns, two dyads on 'not to be suspended'; two pentads stated on 'not to be taken', and in the discussion pentads, two dyads.

9. Ubbāhikavaggo

9. The Chapter on Arbitration

455. “Katihi nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya na sammannitabbo”ti? “Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya na sammannitabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Na atthakusalo hoti, na dhammakusalo hoti, na niruttikusalo hoti, na byañjanakusalo hoti, na pubbāparakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya na sammannitabbo. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya sammannitabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Atthakusalo hoti, dhammakusalo hoti, niruttikusalo [M 0.0343] hoti, byañjanakusalo hoti, pubbāparakusalo hoti [T 0.0486] – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya sammannitabbo.

455. “Venerable sir, endowed with how many factors should a bhikkhu not be appointed by a formal act?” “Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should not be appointed by a formal act. With which five? He is not skilled in the meaning, he is not skilled in the Dhamma, he is not skilled in etymology, he is not skilled in phrasing, and he is not skilled in what precedes and what follows. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not be appointed by a formal act. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should be appointed by a formal act. With which five? He is skilled in the meaning, he is skilled in the Dhamma, he is skilled in etymology, he is skilled in phrasing, and he is skilled in what precedes and what follows. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should be appointed by a formal act.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya na sammannitabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Kodhano hoti kodhābhibhūto, makkhī hoti makkhābhibhūto, paḷāsī hoti paḷāsābhibhūto, issukī hoti issābhibhūto, sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya na sammannitabbo. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya sammannitabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Na kodhano hoti na kodhābhibhūto, na makkhī hoti na makkhābhibhūto, na paḷāsī hoti na paḷāsābhibhūto, na issukī hoti na issābhibhūto, asandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti anādhānaggāhī suppaṭinissaggī – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya sammannitabbo.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with another five factors should not be appointed by a formal act. With which five? He is irascible and overcome by irascibility; he is disparaging and overcome by disparagement; he is rivalrous and overcome by rivalry; he is envious and overcome by envy; he clings to his own views, holds to them tenaciously, and relinquishes them with difficulty. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not be appointed by a formal act. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should be appointed by a formal act. With which five? He is not irascible nor overcome by irascibility; he is not disparaging nor overcome by disparagement; he is not rivalrous nor overcome by rivalry; he is not envious nor overcome by envy; he does not cling to his own views, does not hold to them tenaciously, and relinquishes them with ease. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should be appointed by a formal act.”

“Aparehipi[P 5.0198], upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya na sammannitabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Kuppati, byāpajjati, patiṭṭhiyati, kopaṃ janeti, akhamo hoti apadakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsaniṃ – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya na sammannitabbo. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya sammannitabbo[V 0.0365]. Katamehi pañcahi? Na kuppati, na byāpajjati, na patiṭṭhiyati, na kopaṃ janeti, khamo hoti padakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsaniṃ – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi [T 0.0487] samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya sammannitabbo.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with another five factors should not be appointed by a formal act. With which five? He gets angry, is malicious, is obstinate, generates anger, and is intolerant of instruction, not accepting it in a good way. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not be appointed by a formal act. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should be appointed by a formal act. With which five? He does not get angry, is not malicious, is not obstinate, does not generate anger, and is tolerant of instruction, accepting it in a good way. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should be appointed by a formal act.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya na sammannitabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Pasāretā hoti no sāretā, anokāsakammaṃ kāretvā pavattā hoti, na yathādhamme yathāvinaye yathāpattiyā codetā hoti, na yathādhamme yathāvinaye yathāpattiyā kāretā hoti, na yathādiṭṭhiyā byākatā hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya na sammannitabbo. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya sammannitabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Sāretā hoti no pasāretā, okāsakammaṃ [M 0.0344] kāretvā pavattā hoti, yathādhammaṃ yathāvinaye yathāpattiyā codetā hoti, yathādhamme yathāvinaye yathāpattiyā kāretā hoti, yathādiṭṭhiyā byākatā hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya sammannitabbo.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with another five factors should not be appointed by a formal act. With which five? He is one who obstructs, not one who reminds; he speaks, having initiated proceedings without granting an opportunity; he is not one who accuses in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the offense; he is not one who decides in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the offense; he is not one who declares in accordance with his own view. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not be appointed by a formal act. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should be appointed by a formal act. With which five? He is one who reminds, not one who obstructs; he speaks, having initiated proceedings after granting an opportunity; he is one who accuses in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the offense; he is one who decides in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the offense; he is one who declares in accordance with his own view. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should be appointed by a formal act.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya na sammannitabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Chandāgatiṃ gacchati, dosāgatiṃ gacchati, mohāgatiṃ gacchati, bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, alajjī ca hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya na sammannitabbo. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya sammannitabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, na dosāgatiṃ gacchati, na mohāgatiṃ gacchati, na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, lajjī [T 0.0488] ca hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya sammannitabbo.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with another five factors should not be appointed by a formal act. With which five? He follows a wrong course through desire, he follows a wrong course through hatred, he follows a wrong course through delusion, he follows a wrong course through fear, and he is shameless. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not be appointed by a formal act. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should be appointed by a formal act. With which five? He does not follow a wrong course through desire, he does not follow a wrong course through hatred, he does not follow a wrong course through delusion, he does not follow a wrong course through fear, and he has a sense of shame. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should be appointed by a formal act.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya na sammannitabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Chandāgatiṃ gacchati, dosāgatiṃ gacchati, mohāgatiṃ gacchati, bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, akusalo ca hoti vinaye – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya na sammannitabbo. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya sammannitabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, na dosāgatiṃ gacchati, na mohāgatiṃ gacchati, na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, kusalo ca hoti vinaye – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu ubbāhikāya sammannitabbo”ti.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with another five factors should not be appointed by a formal act. With which five? He follows a wrong course through desire, he follows a wrong course through hatred, he follows a wrong course through delusion, he follows a wrong course through fear, and he is unskilled in the Vinaya. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not be appointed by a formal act. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should be appointed by a formal act. With which five? He does not follow a wrong course through desire, he does not follow a wrong course through hatred, he does not follow a wrong course through delusion, he does not follow a wrong course through fear, and he is skilled in the Vinaya. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should be appointed by a formal act.”

456. “Katihi [V 0.0366] nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu bālotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchatī”ti? “Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu bālotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Katamehi pañcahi? Suttaṃ na jānāti, suttānulomaṃ na jānāti, vinayaṃ na jānāti, vinayānulomaṃ na jānāti, na ca ṭhānaṭhānakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu bālotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu paṇḍitotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Katamehi pañcahi? Suttaṃ jānāti, suttānulomaṃ jānāti, vinayaṃ jānāti, vinayānulomaṃ [M 0.0345] jānāti, ṭhānāṭhānakusalo ca [T 0.0489] hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu paṇḍitotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati.

456. “Venerable Sir, by how many factors is a bhikkhu reckoned only as a fool?” “Upāli, by five factors a bhikkhu is reckoned only as a fool. Which five? He does not know the Sutta; he does not know what is in conformity with the Sutta; he does not know the Vinaya; he does not know what is in conformity with the Vinaya; and he is not skilled in cause and non-cause. By these five factors, Upāli, a bhikkhu is reckoned only as a fool. Upāli, by five factors a bhikkhu is reckoned only as wise. Which five? He knows the Sutta; he knows what is in conformity with the Sutta; he knows the Vinaya; he knows what is in conformity with the Vinaya; and he is skilled in cause and non-cause. By these five factors, Upāli, a bhikkhu is reckoned only as wise.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu bālotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Katamehi pañcahi? Dhammaṃ na jānāti, dhammānulomaṃ [P 5.0199] jānāti, vinayaṃ na jānāti, vinayānulomaṃ na jānāti, na ca pubbāparakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu bālotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu paṇḍitotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Katamehi pañcahi? Dhammaṃ jānāti, dhammānulomaṃ jānāti, vinayaṃ jānāti, vinayānulomaṃ jānāti, pubbāparakusalo ca hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu paṇḍitotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati.

“Furthermore, Upāli, by another five factors a bhikkhu is reckoned only as a fool. Which five? He does not know the Dhamma; he does not know what is in conformity with the Dhamma; he does not know the Vinaya; he does not know what is in conformity with the Vinaya; and he is not skilled in the sequence of discourse. By these five factors, Upāli, a bhikkhu is reckoned only as a fool. Upāli, by five factors a bhikkhu is reckoned only as wise. Which five? He knows the Dhamma; he knows what is in conformity with the Dhamma; he knows the Vinaya; he knows what is in conformity with the Vinaya; and he is skilled in the sequence of discourse. By these five factors, Upāli, a bhikkhu is reckoned only as wise.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu bālotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Katamehi pañcahi? Vatthuṃ na jānāti, nidānaṃ na jānāti, paññattiṃ na jānāti, padapaccābhaṭṭhaṃ na jānāti, anusandhivacanapathaṃ na jānāti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu bālotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu paṇḍitotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Katamehi pañcahi? Vatthuṃ jānāti, nidānaṃ jānāti, paññattiṃ jānāti, padapaccābhaṭṭhaṃ jānāti, anusandhivacanapathaṃ jānāti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu paṇḍitotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati.

“Furthermore, Upāli, by another five factors a bhikkhu is reckoned only as a fool. Which five? He does not know the subject matter; he does not know the origin; he does not know the regulation; he does not know the word under discussion; and he does not know the connected sequence of statements. By these five factors, Upāli, a bhikkhu is reckoned only as a fool. Upāli, by five factors a bhikkhu is reckoned only as wise. Which five? He knows the subject matter; he knows the origin; he knows the regulation; he knows the word under discussion; and he knows the connected sequence of statements. By these five factors, Upāli, a bhikkhu is reckoned only as wise.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato [T 0.0490] bhikkhu bālotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Katamehi pañcahi? Āpattiṃ na jānāti, āpattisamuṭṭhānaṃ na jānāti, āpattiyā payogaṃ na jānāti, āpattiyā vūpasamaṃ na jānāti, āpattiyā na vinicchayakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu bālotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu paṇḍitotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Katamehi pañcahi? Āpattiṃ jānāti[V 0.0367], āpattisamuṭṭhānaṃ jānāti, āpattiyā payogaṃ jānāti, āpattiyā vūpasamaṃ jānāti, āpattiyā vinicchayakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu paṇḍitotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati.

“Furthermore, Upāli, by another five factors a bhikkhu is reckoned only as a fool. Which five? He does not know an offense; he does not know the origin of an offense; he does not know the commission of an offense; he does not know the settlement of an offense; and he is not skilled in the adjudication of an offense. By these five factors, Upāli, a bhikkhu is reckoned only as a fool. Upāli, by five factors a bhikkhu is reckoned only as wise. Which five? He knows an offense; he knows the origin of an offense; he knows the commission of an offense; he knows the settlement of an offense; and he is skilled in the adjudication of an offense. By these five factors, Upāli, a bhikkhu is reckoned only as wise.”

“Aparehipi[M 0.0346], upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu bālotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Katamehi pañcahi? Adhikaraṇaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇasamuṭṭhānaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇassa payogaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇassa vūpasamaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇassa na vinicchayakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu bālotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu paṇḍitotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Katamehi pañcahi? Adhikaraṇaṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇasamuṭṭhānaṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇassa payogaṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇassa vūpasamaṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇassa vinicchayakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu paṇḍitotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchatī”ti.

“Furthermore, Upāli, by another five factors a bhikkhu is reckoned only as a fool. Which five? He does not know a legal issue; he does not know the origin of a legal issue; he does not know the procedure for a legal issue; he does not know the settlement of a legal issue; and he is not skilled in the adjudication of a legal issue. By these five factors, Upāli, a bhikkhu is reckoned only as a fool. Upāli, by five factors a bhikkhu is reckoned only as wise. Which five? He knows a legal issue; he knows the origin of a legal issue; he knows the procedure for a legal issue; he knows the settlement of a legal issue; and he is skilled in the adjudication of a legal issue. By these five factors, Upāli, a bhikkhu is reckoned only as wise.”

Ubbāhikavaggo niṭṭhito navamo.

The ninth Ubbāhika Vagga is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The Summary:

Na [T 0.0491] atthakusalo ceva, kodhano kuppatī ca yo;

Pasāretā chandāgatiṃ, akusalo tatheva ca.

Not skilled in the meaning, the angry one, and one who is agitated; The one who stretches out, going astray through desire, and likewise the unskilled.

Suttaṃ dhammañca vatthuñca, āpatti adhikaraṇaṃ;

Dve dve pakāsitā sabbe, kaṇhasukkaṃ vijānathāti.

The Sutta, the Dhamma, the subject matter, the offense, the legal issue; all have been explained in pairs; one should know the dark and the bright.

10. Adhikaraṇavūpasamavaggo

10. The Chapter on the Settlement of Legal Issues

457. “Katihi nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu nālaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametu”nti? “Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu nālaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Āpattiṃ [P 5.0200] na jānāti, āpattisamuṭṭhānaṃ na jānāti, āpattiyā payogaṃ na jānāti, āpattiyā vūpasamaṃ na jānāti, āpattiyā na vinicchayakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu nālaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Āpattiṃ [V 0.0368] jānāti, āpattisamuṭṭhānaṃ jānāti, āpattiyā payogaṃ jānāti, āpattiyā vūpasamaṃ jānāti, āpattiyā [M 0.0347] vinicchayakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ.

457. “Venerable sir, with how many factors is a monk endowed who is not capable of settling a dispute?” “Upāli, a monk endowed with five factors is not capable of settling a dispute. With which five? He does not know an offense, he does not know the arising of an offense, he does not know the application of an offense, he does not know the subsiding of an offense, and he is not skilled in deciding on an offense. Upāli, a monk endowed with these five factors is not capable of settling a dispute. Upāli, a monk endowed with five factors is capable of settling a dispute. With which five? He knows an offense, he knows the arising of an offense, he knows the application of an offense, he knows the subsiding of an offense, and he is skilled in deciding on an offense. Upāli, a monk endowed with these five factors is capable of settling a dispute.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu nālaṃ [T 0.0492] adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Adhikaraṇaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇasamuṭṭhānaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇassa payogaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇassa vūpasamaṃ na jānāti, adhikaraṇassa na vinicchayakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu nālaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a monk endowed with five other factors is not capable of settling a dispute. With which five? He does not know a dispute, he does not know the arising of a dispute, he does not know the application of a dispute, he does not know the subsiding of a dispute, and he is not skilled in deciding on a dispute. Upāli, a monk endowed with these five factors is not capable of settling a dispute.”

“Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Adhikaraṇaṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇasamuṭṭhānaṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇassa payogaṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇassa vūpasamaṃ jānāti, adhikaraṇassa vinicchayakusalo hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ.

“Upāli, a monk endowed with five factors is capable of settling a dispute. With which five? He knows a dispute, he knows the arising of a dispute, he knows the application of a dispute, he knows the subsiding of a dispute, and he is skilled in deciding on a dispute. Upāli, a monk endowed with these five factors is capable of settling a dispute.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu nālaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Chandāgatiṃ gacchati, dosāgatiṃ gacchati, mohāgatiṃ gacchati, bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, alajjī ca hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu nālaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, na dosāgatiṃ gacchati, na mohāgatiṃ gacchati, na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, lajjī ca hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a monk endowed with five other factors is not capable of settling a dispute. With which five? He follows a wrong course through desire, he follows a wrong course through aversion, he follows a wrong course through delusion, he follows a wrong course through fear, and he is shameless. Upāli, a monk endowed with these five factors is not capable of settling a dispute. Upāli, a monk endowed with five factors is capable of settling a dispute. With which five? He does not follow a wrong course through desire, he does not follow a wrong course through aversion, he does not follow a wrong course through delusion, he does not follow a wrong course through fear, and he is conscientious. Upāli, a monk endowed with these five factors is capable of settling a dispute.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu nālaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Chandāgatiṃ gacchati, dosāgatiṃ gacchati, mohāgatiṃ gacchati, bhayāgatiṃ gacchati[T 0.0493], appassuto ca hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu nālaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, na dosāgatiṃ gacchati, na mohāgatiṃ gacchati, na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, bahussuto ca hoti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a monk endowed with five other factors is not capable of settling a dispute. With which five? He follows a wrong course through desire, he follows a wrong course through aversion, he follows a wrong course through delusion, he follows a wrong course through fear, and he is of little learning. Upāli, a monk endowed with these five factors is not capable of settling a dispute. Upāli, a monk endowed with five factors is capable of settling a dispute. With which five? He does not follow a wrong course through desire, he does not follow a wrong course through aversion, he does not follow a wrong course through delusion, he does not follow a wrong course through fear, and he is very learned. Upāli, a monk endowed with these five factors is capable of settling a dispute.”

“Aparehipi[M 0.0348][V 0.0369], upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu nālaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Vatthuṃ na jānāti, nidānaṃ na jānāti, paññattiṃ na jānāti, padapaccābhaṭṭhaṃ na jānāti, anusandhivacanapathaṃ na jānāti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu nālaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Vatthuṃ jānāti, nidānaṃ jānāti, paññattiṃ jānāti, padapaccābhaṭṭhaṃ jānāti, anusandhivacanapathaṃ jānāti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a monk endowed with five other factors is not capable of settling a dispute. With which five? He does not know the subject matter, he does not know the origin, he does not know the regulation, he does not know the initial phrase, and he does not know the connected train of reasoning. Upāli, a monk endowed with these five factors is not capable of settling a dispute. Upāli, a monk endowed with five factors is capable of settling a dispute. With which five? He knows the subject matter, he knows the origin, he knows the regulation, he knows the initial phrase, and he knows the connected train of reasoning. Upāli, a monk endowed with these five factors is capable of settling a dispute.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu nālaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Chandāgatiṃ gacchati, dosāgatiṃ gacchati, mohāgatiṃ gacchati, bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, akusalo ca hoti vinaye – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu nālaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, na dosāgatiṃ gacchati, na mohāgatiṃ gacchati, na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, kusalo ca hoti vinaye – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a monk endowed with five other factors is not capable of settling a dispute. With which five? He follows a wrong course through desire, he follows a wrong course through aversion, he follows a wrong course through delusion, he follows a wrong course through fear, and he is unskilled in the Discipline. Upāli, a monk endowed with these five factors is not capable of settling a dispute. Upāli, a monk endowed with five factors is capable of settling a dispute. With which five? He does not follow a wrong course through desire, he does not follow a wrong course through aversion, he does not follow a wrong course through delusion, he does not follow a wrong course through fear, and he is skilled in the Discipline. Upāli, a monk endowed with these five factors is capable of settling a dispute.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu nālaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Chandāgatiṃ gacchati, dosāgatiṃ gacchati, mohāgatiṃ gacchati, bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, puggalagaru hoti no saṅghagaru – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu nālaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Pañcahupāli[P 5.0201], aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ[T 0.0494]. Katamehi pañcahi? Na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, na dosāgatiṃ gacchati, na mohāgatiṃ gacchati, na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, saṅghagaru hoti no puggalagaru – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ.

Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors is not capable of settling a dispute. With which five? He goes the wrong way through desire, he goes the wrong way through aversion, he goes the wrong way through delusion, he goes the wrong way through fear, and he respects individuals but does not respect the Saṅgha. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors is not capable of settling a dispute. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors is capable of settling a dispute. With which five? He does not go the wrong way through desire, he does not go the wrong way through aversion, he does not go the wrong way through delusion, he does not go the wrong way through fear, and he respects the Saṅgha but does not respect individuals. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors is capable of settling a dispute.

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu nālaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Chandāgatiṃ gacchati, dosāgatiṃ gacchati, mohāgatiṃ gacchati, bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, āmisagaru hoti no saddhammagaru – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu nālaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ [M 0.0349] vūpasametuṃ. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Katamehi pañcahi? Na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, na dosāgatiṃ gacchati, na [V 0.0370] mohāgatiṃ gacchati, na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, saddhammagaru hoti no [T 0.0495] āmisagaru – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametu”nti.

Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five other factors is not capable of settling a dispute. With which five? He goes the wrong way through desire, he goes the wrong way through aversion, he goes the wrong way through delusion, he goes the wrong way through fear, and he respects material gain but does not respect the good Dhamma. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors is not capable of settling a dispute. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors is capable of settling a dispute. With which five? He does not go the wrong way through desire, he does not go the wrong way through aversion, he does not go the wrong way through delusion, he does not go the wrong way through fear, and he respects the good Dhamma but does not respect material gain. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors is capable of settling a dispute.

458. “Katihi nu kho, bhante, ākārehi saṅgho bhijjatī”ti? “Pañcahupāli, ākārehi saṅgho bhijjati. Katamehi pañcahi? Kammena, uddesena, voharanto, anussāvanena, salākaggāhena – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahākārehi saṅgho bhijjatī”ti.

458. “Venerable sir, in how many ways does the Saṅgha split?” “Upāli, the Saṅgha splits in five ways. In which five? By a separate formal act, by a separate recitation of the Pātimokkha, by declaration, by announcement, and by the taking of voting tickets. Upāli, the Saṅgha splits in these five ways.”

“Saṅgharāji saṅgharājīti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, saṅgharāji hoti no ca saṅghabhedo? Kittāvatā ca pana saṅgharāji ceva hoti saṅghabhedo cā”ti? “Paññattetaṃ, upāli, mayā āgantukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ āgantukavattaṃ. Evaṃ supaññatte kho, upāli, mayā sikkhāpade āgantukā bhikkhū āgantukavatte na vattanti. Evampi kho, upāli, saṅgharāji hoti no ca saṅghabhedo. Paññattetaṃ, upāli, mayā āvāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ āvāsikavattaṃ. Evaṃ supaññatte kho, upāli, mayā sikkhāpade āvāsikā bhikkhū āvāsikavatte na vattanti. Evampi kho, upāli, saṅgharāji hoti no ca saṅghabhedo. Paññattetaṃ upāli mayā bhikkhūnaṃ bhattagge bhattaggavattaṃ – yathāvuḍḍhaṃ yathārattaṃ yathāpatirūpaṃ aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggapiṇḍaṃ. Evaṃ supaññatte kho, upāli, mayā sikkhāpade navā bhikkhū bhattagge therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ āsanaṃ paṭibāhanti. Evampi kho, upāli, saṅgharāji hoti no ca saṅghabhedo. Paññattetaṃ, upāli, mayā bhikkhūnaṃ senāsane [T 0.0496] senāsanavattaṃ – yathāvuḍḍhaṃ yathārattaṃ yathāpatirūpaṃ. Evaṃ supaññatte kho, upāli, mayā sikkhāpade navā bhikkhū therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ senāsanaṃ paṭibāhanti. Evampi kho, upāli, saṅgharāji hoti no ca saṅghabhedo. Paññattetaṃ, upāli, mayā bhikkhūnaṃ antosīmāya ekaṃ uposathaṃ ekaṃ pavāraṇaṃ ekaṃ saṅghakammaṃ ekaṃ kammākammaṃ. Evaṃ supaññatte kho, upāli, mayā sikkhāpade tattheva antosīmāya āvenibhāvaṃ āveṇibhāvaṃ (sī. syā.) karitvā gaṇaṃ bandhitvā [M 0.0350] āveniṃ āveṇi (sī. syā.) uposathaṃ karonti āveniṃ pavāraṇaṃ [P 5.0202] karonti āveniṃ saṅghakammaṃ karonti āveniṃ kammākammāni karonti. Evaṃ kho, upāli, saṅgharāji ceva hoti saṅghabhedo cā”ti.

“Venerable sir, it is said, ‘a rift in the Saṅgha, a rift in the Saṅgha.’ To what extent, venerable sir, is there a rift in the Saṅgha but not a schism of the Saṅgha? And to what extent is there both a rift in the Saṅgha and a schism of the Saṅgha?” “Upāli, I have laid down for incoming bhikkhus the duty for incoming bhikkhus. When, Upāli, the training rule has been well laid down by me, incoming bhikkhus do not practice the duty for incoming bhikkhus. In this way, Upāli, there is a rift in the Saṅgha but not a schism of the Saṅgha. I have laid down for resident bhikkhus, Upāli, the duty for resident bhikkhus. When, Upāli, the training rule has been well laid down by me, resident bhikkhus do not practice the duty for resident bhikkhus. In this way also, Upāli, there is a rift in the Saṅgha but not a schism of the Saṅgha. I have laid down for the bhikkhus, Upāli, the duty in the refectory: the chief seat, the chief water, and the chief almsfood, according to seniority, according to the time of their ordination, and according to what is suitable. When, Upāli, the training rule has been well laid down by me, junior bhikkhus in the refectory prevent the senior bhikkhus from their seats. In this way also, Upāli, there is a rift in the Saṅgha but not a schism of the Saṅgha. I have laid down for the bhikkhus, Upāli, the duty regarding lodgings: according to seniority, according to the time of their ordination, and according to what is suitable. When, Upāli, the training rule has been well laid down by me, junior bhikkhus prevent the senior bhikkhus from their lodgings. In this way also, Upāli, there is a rift in the Saṅgha but not a schism of the Saṅgha. I have laid down for the bhikkhus, Upāli, that within a single boundary there should be one Uposatha, one Pavāraṇā, one Saṅghakamma, and the same minor and major acts. When, Upāli, the training rule has been well laid down by me, within that very same boundary they create a separate state, form a faction, and perform a separate Uposatha, a separate Pavāraṇā, a separate Saṅghakamma, and separate minor and major acts. In this way, Upāli, there is both a rift in the Saṅgha and a schism of the Saṅgha.”

Adhikaraṇavūpasamavaggo niṭṭhito dasamo.

The tenth, the Chapter on the Settlement of Disputes, is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Āpattiṃ [V 0.0371] adhikaraṇaṃ, chandā appassutena ca;

Vatthuñca akusalo ca, puggalo āmisena ca;

Bhijjati saṅgharāji ca, saṅghabhedo tatheva cāti.

Offenses, disputes, biased conduct, and one who has heard little; the basis, the unskillful, the person, and material gain; ‘it splits,’ a rift in the Saṅgha, and likewise a schism in the Saṅgha.

11. Saṅghabhedakavaggo

11. The Chapter on the Schismatic

459. cūḷava. 354-355; a. ni. 10.38 ādayo “Katihi nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho”ti? “Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho. Katamehi pañcahi? Idhupāli, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti, avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpeti, vinayaṃ avinayoti [T 0.0497] dīpeti, vinidhāya diṭṭhiṃ kammena – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho.

459. “Venerable sir, with how many factors is a schismatic endowed, such that he is destined for a state of woe, destined for hell, remaining for the eon, and incurable?” “Upāli, a schismatic is endowed with five factors, such that he is destined for a state of woe, destined for hell, remaining for the eon, and incurable. With which five? Here, Upāli, a bhikkhu declares what is not the Dhamma to be the Dhamma; he declares the Dhamma to be what is not the Dhamma; he declares what is not the Vinaya to be the Vinaya; he declares the Vinaya to be what is not the Vinaya; having established his view, by means of a formal act. Indeed, Upāli, a schismatic endowed with these five factors is destined for a state of woe, destined for hell, remaining for the eon, and incurable.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho. Katamehi pañcahi? Idhupāli, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti, avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpeti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpeti, vinidhāya diṭṭhiṃ uddesena – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho.

“Upāli, a schismatic endowed with five other factors is destined for a state of woe, destined for hell, remaining for the eon, and incurable. With which five? Here, Upāli, a bhikkhu declares what is not the Dhamma to be the Dhamma; he declares the Dhamma to be what is not the Dhamma; he declares what is not the Vinaya to be the Vinaya; he declares the Vinaya to be what is not the Vinaya; having established his view, by means of a separate recitation of the Pātimokkha. Indeed, Upāli, a schismatic endowed with these five factors is destined for a state of woe, destined for hell, remaining for the eon, and incurable.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho. Katamehi pañcahi? Idhupāli, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti, avinayaṃ [M 0.0351] vinayoti dīpeti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpeti, vinidhāya diṭṭhi voharanto – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho.

Furthermore, Upāli, endowed with five other factors, a schismatic is destined for a state of woe, destined for hell, remaining for the eon, and incurable. With which five? Here, Upāli, a bhikkhu declares what is not the Dhamma to be the Dhamma; he declares the Dhamma to be what is not the Dhamma; he declares what is not the Vinaya to be the Vinaya; he declares the Vinaya to be what is not the Vinaya; and he speaks, having established his view. Indeed, Upāli, a schismatic endowed with these five factors is destined for a state of woe, destined for hell, remaining for the eon, and incurable.

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho. Katamehi pañcahi? Idhupāli, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti, avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpeti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpeti, vinidhāya diṭṭhiṃ [V 0.0372] anussāvanena – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho.

Furthermore, Upāli, endowed with five other factors, a schismatic is destined for a state of woe, destined for hell, remaining for the eon, and incurable. With which five? Here, Upāli, a bhikkhu declares what is not the Dhamma to be the Dhamma; he declares the Dhamma to be what is not the Dhamma; he declares what is not the Vinaya to be the Vinaya; he declares the Vinaya to be what is not the Vinaya; and he makes a proclamation, having established his view. Indeed, Upāli, a schismatic endowed with these five factors is destined for a state of woe, destined for hell, remaining for the eon, and incurable.

“Aparehipi, upāli[T 0.0498], pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho. Katamehi pañcahi? Idhupāli, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti, avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpeti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpeti, vinidhāya diṭṭhiṃ salākaggāhena – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho.

Furthermore, Upāli, endowed with five other factors, a schismatic is destined for a state of woe, destined for hell, remaining for the eon, and incurable. With which five? Here, Upāli, a bhikkhu declares what is not the Dhamma to be the Dhamma; he declares the Dhamma to be what is not the Dhamma; he declares what is not the Vinaya to be the Vinaya; he declares the Vinaya to be what is not the Vinaya; and he takes a vote using tickets, having established his view. Indeed, Upāli, a schismatic endowed with these five factors is destined for a state of woe, destined for hell, remaining for the eon, and incurable.

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho. Katamehi pañcahi? Idhupāli, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti, avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpeti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpeti, vinidhāya khantiṃ kammena…pe… vinidhāya khantiṃ uddesena…pe… vinidhāya khantiṃ voharanto…pe… vinidhāya khantiṃ anussāvanena…pe… vinidhāya khantiṃ salākaggāhena – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho.

Furthermore, Upāli, endowed with five other factors, a schismatic is destined for a state of woe, destined for hell, remaining for the eon, and incurable. With which five? Here, Upāli, a bhikkhu declares what is not the Dhamma to be the Dhamma; he declares the Dhamma to be what is not the Dhamma; he declares what is not the Vinaya to be the Vinaya; he declares the Vinaya to be what is not the Vinaya; and having established a preference, he acts by a formal act… by the recitation of the Pātimokkha… by speaking… by proclamation… by the taking of voting tickets. Indeed, Upāli, a schismatic endowed with these five factors is destined for a state of woe, destined for hell, remaining for the eon, and incurable.

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho. Katamehi pañcahi? Idhupāli, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpeti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpeti, vinidhāya ruciṃ kammena…pe… vinidhāya ruciṃ uddesena…pe… vinidhāya ruciṃ voharanto…pe… vinidhāya ruciṃ anussāvanena…pe… vinidhāya ruciṃ salākaggāhena – imehi kho[T 0.0499], upāli, pañcahaṅgehi [M 0.0352] samannāgato saṅghabhedako āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho.

Furthermore, Upāli, endowed with five other factors, a schismatic is destined for a state of woe, destined for hell, remaining for the eon, and incurable. With which five? Here, Upāli, a bhikkhu declares what is not the Dhamma to be the Dhamma; he declares the Dhamma to be what is not the Dhamma; he declares what is not the Vinaya to be the Vinaya; he declares the Vinaya to be what is not the Vinaya; and having established a strong preference, he acts by a separate formal act… by a separate recitation of the Pātimokkha… by speaking… by proclamation… by the taking of voting tickets. Indeed, Upāli, a schismatic endowed with these five factors is destined for a state of woe, destined for hell, remaining for the eon, and incurable.

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho. Katamehi pañcahi? Idhupāli[P 5.0203], bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti, avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpeti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpeti, vinidhāya saññaṃ kammena…pe… vinidhāya saññaṃ uddesena…pe… vinidhāya saññaṃ voharanto…pe… vinidhāya saññaṃ anussāvanena…pe… vinidhāya saññaṃ salākaggāhena – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho”ti.

Furthermore, Upāli, endowed with five other factors, a schismatic is destined for a state of woe, destined for hell, remaining for the eon, and incurable. With which five? Here, Upāli, a bhikkhu declares what is not the Dhamma to be the Dhamma; he declares the Dhamma to be what is not the Dhamma; he declares what is not the Vinaya to be the Vinaya; he declares the Vinaya to be what is not the Vinaya; and having established a perception, he acts by a separate formal act… by a separate recitation of the Pātimokkha… by speaking… by proclamation… by the taking of voting tickets. Indeed, Upāli, a schismatic endowed with these five factors is destined for a state of woe, destined for hell, remaining for the eon, and incurable.

Saṅghabhedakavaggo niṭṭhito ekādasamo.

The Eleventh Chapter on Schism is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Vinidhāya [V 0.0373] diṭṭhiṃ kammena, uddese voharena ca;

Anussāvane salākena, pañcete diṭṭhinissitā;

Khantiṃ ruciñca saññañca, tayo te pañcadhā nayāti.

Having established a view: by a formal act, by recitation, by speaking, by proclamation, and by taking voting tickets—these five are based on view. Preference, strong preference, and perception—these three methods are each fivefold.

12. Dutiyasaṅghabhedakavaggo

12. The Second Chapter on Schism in the Saṅgha

460. “Katihi nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako na āpāyiko na nerayiko na kappaṭṭho na atekiccho”ti? “Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako na āpāyiko na nerayiko na kappaṭṭho na atekiccho. Katamehi pañcahi? Idhupāli, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti[T 0.0500], avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpeti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpeti, avinidhāya diṭṭhiṃ kammena – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako na āpāyiko na nerayiko na kappaṭṭho na atekiccho.

460. “Venerable sir, endowed with how many factors is a schismatic not destined for a state of woe, not destined for hell, not remaining for the eon, and curable?” “Upāli, endowed with five factors, a schismatic is not destined for a state of woe, not destined for hell, not remaining for the eon, and is curable. With which five? Here, Upāli, a bhikkhu declares what is not the Dhamma to be the Dhamma; he declares the Dhamma to be what is not the Dhamma; he declares what is not the Vinaya to be the Vinaya; he declares the Vinaya to be what is not the Vinaya; and he performs a formal act without having established a view. Indeed, Upāli, a schismatic endowed with these five factors is not destined for a state of woe, not destined for hell, not remaining for the eon, and is curable.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako na āpāyiko na nerayiko na kappaṭṭho na atekiccho. Katamehi pañcahi? Idhupāli, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti, avinayaṃ [M 0.0353] vinayoti dīpeti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpeti, avinidhāya diṭṭhiṃ uddesena – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako na āpāyiko na nerayiko na kappaṭṭho na atekiccho.

“Furthermore, Upāli, endowed with five other factors, a schismatic is not destined for a state of woe, not destined for hell, not remaining for the eon, and is curable. With which five? Here, Upāli, a bhikkhu declares what is not the Dhamma to be the Dhamma; he declares the Dhamma to be what is not the Dhamma; he declares what is not the Vinaya to be the Vinaya; he declares the Vinaya to be what is not the Vinaya; and he recites the Pātimokkha separately without having established a view. Indeed, Upāli, a schismatic endowed with these five factors is not destined for a state of woe, not destined for hell, not remaining for the eon, and is curable.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako na āpāyiko na nerayiko na kappaṭṭho na atekiccho. Katamehi pañcahi? Idhupāli, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti, avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpeti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpeti, avinidhāya diṭṭhiṃ voharanto. Imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako na āpāyiko na nerayiko na kappaṭṭho na atekiccho.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a schismatic endowed with five other factors is not destined for the states of deprivation, not destined for hell, not to remain for an aeon, and is curable. What five? Here, Upāli, a bhikkhu declares what is not Dhamma to be Dhamma, declares Dhamma to be not Dhamma, declares what is not Vinaya to be Vinaya, declares Vinaya to be not Vinaya, and makes a pronouncement without having established a view. Endowed with these five factors, Upāli, a schismatic is not destined for the states of deprivation, not destined for hell, not to remain for an aeon, and is curable.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako na āpāyiko na nerayiko na kappaṭṭho na atekiccho. Katamehi pañcahi? Idhupāli, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti, avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpeti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpeti, avinidhāya [T 0.0501][V 0.0374] diṭṭhiṃ anussāvanena – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako na āpāyiko na nerayiko na kappaṭṭho na atekiccho.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a schismatic endowed with five other factors is not destined for the states of deprivation, not destined for hell, not to remain for an aeon, and is curable. With what five? Here, Upāli, a bhikkhu declares what is not Dhamma to be Dhamma, and Dhamma to be not Dhamma; he declares what is not Vinaya to be Vinaya, and Vinaya to be not Vinaya; and he does so by an announcement, without having established his view. A schismatic endowed with these five factors, Upāli, is not destined for the states of deprivation, not destined for hell, not to remain for an aeon, and is curable.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako na āpāyiko na nerayiko na kappaṭṭho na atekiccho. Katamehi pañcahi? Idhupāli, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti, avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpeti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpeti, avinidhāya diṭṭhiṃ salākaggāhena – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako na āpāyiko na nerayiko na kappaṭṭho na atekiccho.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a schismatic endowed with five other factors is not destined for the states of deprivation, not destined for hell, not to remain for an aeon, and is curable. With what five? Here, Upāli, a bhikkhu declares what is not Dhamma to be Dhamma, and Dhamma to be not Dhamma; he declares what is not Vinaya to be Vinaya, and Vinaya to be not Vinaya; and he does so by taking a ballot, without having established his view. A schismatic endowed with these five factors, Upāli, is not destined for the states of deprivation, not destined for hell, not to remain for an aeon, and is curable.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako na āpāyiko na nerayiko na kappaṭṭho na atekiccho. Katamehi pañcahi? Idhupāli, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti, avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpeti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpeti, avinidhāya khantiṃ kammena…pe… avinidhāya khantiṃ uddesena…pe… avinidhāya khantiṃ voharanto…pe… avinidhāya khantiṃ anussāvanena…pe… avinidhāya khantiṃ salākaggāhena – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako na āpāyiko na nerayiko na kappaṭṭho na atekiccho.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a schismatic endowed with five other factors is not destined for the states of deprivation, not destined for hell, not to remain for an aeon, and is curable. With what five? Here, Upāli, a bhikkhu declares what is not Dhamma to be Dhamma, and Dhamma to be not Dhamma; he declares what is not Vinaya to be Vinaya, and Vinaya to be not Vinaya; and he does so by a formal act, without having established his approval… by a recitation, without having established his approval… by a pronouncement, without having established his approval… by an announcement, without having established his approval… by taking a ballot, without having established his approval. A schismatic endowed with these five factors, Upāli, is not destined for the states of deprivation, not destined for hell, not to remain for an aeon, and is curable.”

“Aparehipi[M 0.0354], upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako na āpāyiko na nerayiko na kappaṭṭho na atekiccho. Katamehi pañcahi? Idhupāli, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti, avinayaṃ [T 0.0502] vinayoti dīpeti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpeti, avinidhāya ruciṃ kammena…pe… avinidhāya ruciṃ uddesena…pe… avinidhāya ruciṃ voharanto…pe… avinidhāya ruciṃ anussāvanena…pe… avinidhāya ruciṃ salākaggāhena – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako na āpāyiko na nerayiko na kappaṭṭho na atekiccho.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a schismatic endowed with five other factors is not destined for the states of deprivation, not destined for hell, not to remain for an aeon, and is curable. With which five? Here, Upāli, a bhikkhu declares what is not the Dhamma as the Dhamma, and the Dhamma as not the Dhamma; he declares what is not the Vinaya as the Vinaya, and the Vinaya as not the Vinaya; without having established a preference, by means of a formal act… without having established a preference, by means of a recitation… without having established a preference, while speaking… without having established a preference, by means of an announcement… without having established a preference, by means of taking a voting ticket. A schismatic endowed with these five factors, Upāli, is not destined for the states of deprivation, not destined for hell, not to remain for an aeon, and is curable.”

“Aparehipi, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako na āpāyiko na nerayiko na kappaṭṭho na atekiccho. Katamehi pañcahi? Idhupāli, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti, avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpeti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpeti, avinidhāya saññaṃ kammena…pe… avinidhāya saññaṃ uddesena…pe… avinidhāya saññaṃ voharanto…pe… avinidhāya saññaṃ anussāvanena…pe… avinidhāya saññaṃ salākaggāhena [V 0.0375] – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saṅghabhedako na āpāyiko na nerayiko na kappaṭṭho na atekiccho”ti.

“Furthermore, Upāli, a schismatic endowed with five other factors is not destined for the states of deprivation, not destined for hell, not to remain for an aeon, and is curable. With which five? Here, Upāli, a bhikkhu declares what is not the Dhamma as the Dhamma, and the Dhamma as not the Dhamma; he declares what is not the Vinaya as the Vinaya, and the Vinaya as not the Vinaya; without having established a perception, by means of a formal act… without having established a perception, by means of a recitation… without having established a perception, while speaking… without having established a perception, by means of an announcement… without having established a perception, by means of taking a voting ticket. A schismatic endowed with these five factors, Upāli, is not destined for the states of deprivation, not destined for hell, not to remain for an aeon, and is curable.”

Dutiyasaṅghabhedakavaggo niṭṭhito dvādasamo.

The Second Chapter on Schism, the twelfth, is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Avinidhāya diṭṭhiṃ kammena, uddese voharena ca;

Anussāvane salākena, pañcete diṭṭhinissitā.

Without having established a view: by a formal act, by a recitation, and by speaking; by an announcement, by a voting ticket—these five are based on view.

Khantiṃ ruciñca saññañca, tayo te pañcadhā nayā.

Approval, preference, and perception—those three methods are each fivefold.

Heṭṭhime kaṇhapakkhamhi, samavīsati vidhī yathā;

Tatheva sukkapakkhamhi, samavīsati jānathāti.

Just as in the lower dark side there are twenty methods, so too in the bright side, you should know there are twenty.

13. Āvāsikavaggo

13. The Chapter on Residents

461. “Katihi [T 0.0503] nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye”ti? “Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye[M 0.0355]. Katamehi pañcahi? Chandāgatiṃ gacchati, dosāgatiṃ [P 5.0204] gacchati, mohāgatiṃ gacchati, bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, saṅghikaṃ puggalikaparibhogena paribhuñjati – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye.

461. “Venerable sir, endowed with how many factors is a resident monk placed in hell just as if brought and put there?” “Upāli, a resident monk endowed with five factors is placed in hell just as if brought and put there. With which five? He goes on the wrong course through desire, goes on the wrong course through hatred, goes on the wrong course through delusion, goes on the wrong course through fear, and uses what belongs to the Saṅgha for his personal use. Upāli, a resident monk endowed with these five factors is placed in hell just as if brought and put there.”

“Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ sagge. Katamehi pañcahi? Na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, na dosāgatiṃ gacchati, na mohāgatiṃ gacchati, na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, saṅghikaṃ na puggalikaparibhogena paribhuñjati – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ sagge”ti.

“Upāli, a resident monk endowed with five factors is placed in heaven just as if brought and put there. With which five? He does not go on the wrong course through desire, does not go on the wrong course through hatred, does not go on the wrong course through delusion, does not go on the wrong course through fear, and he does not use what belongs to the Saṅgha for his personal use. Upāli, a resident monk endowed with these five factors is placed in heaven just as if brought and put there.”

462. “Kati nu kho, bhante, adhammikā vinayabyākaraṇā”ti? “Pañcime, upāli, adhammikā vinayabyākaraṇā. Katame pañca? Idhupāli, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti pariṇāmeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti pariṇāmeti, avinayaṃ vinayoti pariṇāmeti, vinayaṃ avinayoti pariṇāmeti[V 0.0376], apaññattaṃ paññāpeti, paññattaṃ samucchindati – ime kho, upāli, pañca adhammikā vinayabyākaraṇā. Pañcime, upāli, dhammikā vinayabyākaraṇā. Katame pañca? Idhupāli, bhikkhu adhammaṃ adhammoti pariṇāmeti, dhammaṃ dhammoti pariṇāmeti, avinayaṃ [T 0.0504] avinayoti pariṇāmeti, vinayaṃ vinayoti pariṇāmeti, apaññattaṃ na paññapeti, paññattaṃ na samucchindati – ime kho, upāli, pañca dhammikā vinayabyākaraṇā”ti.

462. “Venerable sir, how many unrighteous explanations of the Vinaya are there?” “Upāli, there are these five unrighteous explanations of the Vinaya. Which five? Here, Upāli, a monk causes what is not the Dhamma to be regarded as the Dhamma, causes the Dhamma to be regarded as not the Dhamma, causes what is not the Vinaya to be regarded as the Vinaya, causes the Vinaya to be regarded as not the Vinaya, lays down what has not been laid down, and abolishes what has been laid down. These, Upāli, are the five unrighteous explanations of the Vinaya. Upāli, there are these five righteous explanations of the Vinaya. Which five? Here, Upāli, a monk causes what is not the Dhamma to be regarded as not the Dhamma, causes the Dhamma to be regarded as the Dhamma, causes what is not the Vinaya to be regarded as not the Vinaya, causes the Vinaya to be regarded as the Vinaya, does not lay down what has not been laid down, and does not abolish what has been laid down. These, Upāli, are the five righteous explanations of the Vinaya.”

463. a. ni. 5.272-285 “Katihi nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgato bhattuddesako yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye”ti? “Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhattuddesako yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye. Katamehi pañcahi? Chandāgatiṃ gacchati, dosāgatiṃ gacchati, mohāgatiṃ gacchati, bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, uddiṭṭhānuddiṭṭhaṃ na jānāti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhattuddesako yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye.

463. “Venerable sir, endowed with how many factors is a meal distributor consigned to hell as if brought there?” “Upāli, a meal distributor endowed with five factors is consigned to hell as if brought there. With which five? He goes on the wrong course through desire, goes on the wrong course through hatred, goes on the wrong course through delusion, goes on the wrong course through fear, and does not know what has been assigned and what has not been assigned. Upāli, a meal distributor endowed with these five factors is consigned to hell as if brought there.”

a. ni. 5.272-285 “Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato bhattuddesako yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ sagge. Katamehi pañcahi? Na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, na dosāgatiṃ gacchati, na mohāgatiṃ gacchati, na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, uddiṭṭhānuddiṭṭhaṃ [M 0.0356] jānāti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato bhattuddesako yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ sagge”ti.

“Upāli, a meal distributor endowed with five factors is consigned to heaven as if brought there. With which five? He does not go on the wrong course through desire, does not go on the wrong course through hatred, does not go on the wrong course through delusion, does not go on the wrong course through fear, and knows what has been assigned and what has not been assigned. Upāli, a meal distributor endowed with these five factors is consigned to heaven as if brought there.”

464. “Katihi nu kho, bhante, aṅgehi samannāgato senāsanapaññāpako…pe… bhaṇḍāgāriko…pe… cīvarapaṭiggāhako…pe… cīvarabhājako…pe… yāgubhājako…pe… phalabhājako…pe… khajjabhājako…pe… appamattakavissajjako…pe… sāṭiyaggāhāpako…pe… pattaggāhāpako…pe… ārāmikapesako…pe… sāmaṇerapesako yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye”ti? “Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato sāmaṇerapesako yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye. Katamehi pañcahi? Chandāgatiṃ [T 0.0505] gacchati, dosāgatiṃ gacchati, mohāgatiṃ gacchati, bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, pesitāpesitaṃ na jānāti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato sāmaṇerapesako yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye. Pañcahupāli, aṅgehi samannāgato sāmaṇerapesako yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ sagge. Katamehi pañcahi? Na chandāgatiṃ gacchati, na dosāgatiṃ gacchati, na mohāgatiṃ gacchati, na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati, pesitāpesitaṃ jānāti – imehi kho, upāli, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato sāmaṇerapesako yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ sagge”ti.

464. “Venerable sir, endowed with how many factors is a lodging assigner… a storekeeper… a robe receiver… a robe distributor… a gruel distributor… a fruit distributor… a hard-food distributor… a distributor of minor items… one who arranges for robes to be accepted… one who arranges for bowls to be accepted… one who dispatches monastery attendants… or one who dispatches novices, consigned to hell as if brought there?” “Upāli, one who dispatches novices, endowed with five factors, is consigned to hell as if brought there. With which five? He goes on the wrong course through desire, he goes on the wrong course through hatred, he goes on the wrong course through delusion, he goes on the wrong course through fear, and he does not know what has been dispatched and what has not. Upāli, one who dispatches novices, endowed with these five factors, is consigned to hell as if brought there. Upāli, one who dispatches novices, endowed with five factors, is consigned to heaven as if brought there. With which five? He does not go on the wrong course through desire, he does not go on the wrong course through hatred, he does not go on the wrong course through delusion, he does not go on the wrong course through fear, and he knows what has been dispatched and what has not. Upāli, one who dispatches novices, endowed with these five factors, is consigned to heaven as if brought there.”

Āvāsikavaggo niṭṭhito terasamo.

The Thirteenth Chapter on Residents is finished.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of that is:

Āvāsikabyākaraṇā[P 5.0205][V 0.0377], bhattusenāsanāni ca;

Bhaṇḍacīvaraggāho ca, cīvarassa ca bhājako.

Residents, explanations, meals and lodgings; storekeepers, robe-receivers, and distributors of robes.

Yāgu phalaṃ khajjakañca, appasāṭiyagāhako;

Patto ārāmiko ceva, sāmaṇerena pesakoti.

Gruel, fruit, and hard-food; minor items, robes, and bowls; monastery attendants and dispatchers of novices.

14. Kathinatthāravaggo

14. The Chapter on the Spreading of the Kathina

465. “Kati nu kho, bhante, ānisaṃsā kathinatthāre”ti? “Pañcime, upāli, ānisaṃsā kathinatthāre. Katame pañca? Anāmantacāro, asamādānacāro, gaṇabhojanaṃ, yāvadatthacīvaraṃ, yo ca tattha cīvaruppādo [M 0.0357] so nesaṃ bhavissati – ime kho, upāli, pañca ānisaṃsā kathinatthāre”ti.

465. “Venerable sir, how many benefits are there in the spreading of the Kathina?” “Upāli, there are these five benefits in the spreading of the Kathina. Which five? Going without asking permission, going without the set of robes, group meals, as many robes as one wishes, and whatever robe-cloth arises there, it will belong to them. These, Upāli, are the five benefits in the spreading of the Kathina.”

466. “Kati nu kho, bhante, ādīnavā muṭṭhassatissa asampajānassa niddaṃ [T 0.0506] okkamato”ti? “Pañcime, upāli, ādīnavā muṭṭhassatissa asampajānassa niddaṃ okkamato. Katame pañca? Dukkhaṃ supati, dukkhaṃ paṭibujjhati, pāpakaṃ supinaṃ passati, devatā na rakkhanti, asuci muccati – ime kho, upāli, pañca ādīnavā muṭṭhassatissa asampajānassa niddaṃ okkamato. Pañcime, upāli, ānisaṃsā upaṭṭhitassatissa sampajānassa niddaṃ okkamato. Katame pañca? Sukhaṃ supati, sukhaṃ paṭibujjhati, na pāpakaṃ supinaṃ passati, devatā rakkhanti, asuci na muccati – ime kho, upāli, pañca ānisaṃsā upaṭṭhitassatissa sampajānassa niddaṃ okkamato”ti.

466. “Venerable sir, how many dangers are there for one with lapsed mindfulness and without clear comprehension who falls asleep?” “Upāli, there are these five dangers for one with lapsed mindfulness and without clear comprehension who falls asleep. Which five? One sleeps uncomfortably, one wakes uncomfortably, one sees a bad dream, the deities do not protect one, and semen is discharged. These, Upāli, are the five dangers for one with lapsed mindfulness and without clear comprehension who falls asleep. Upāli, there are these five benefits for one with established mindfulness and with clear comprehension who falls asleep. Which five? One sleeps comfortably, one wakes comfortably, one does not see a bad dream, the deities protect one, and semen is not discharged. These, Upāli, are the five benefits for one with established mindfulness and with clear comprehension who falls asleep.”

467. “Kati nu kho, bhante, avandiyā”ti? “Pañcime, upāli, avandiyā. Katame pañca? Antaragharaṃ paviṭṭho avandiyo, racchagato avandiyo, otamasiko avandiyo, asamannāharanto avandiyo, sutto avandiyo – ime kho, upāli, pañca avandiyā.

467. “Venerable sir, how many are not to be paid homage to?” “Upāli, there are these five who are not to be paid homage to. Which five? One who has entered within a village is not to be paid homage to; one who is on a street is not to be paid homage to; one who is in a dark place is not to be paid homage to; one who is not paying attention is not to be paid homage to; one who is asleep is not to be paid homage to. These, Upāli, are the five who are not to be paid homage to.”

“Aparepi, upāli, pañca avandiyā. Katame pañca? Yāgupāne avandiyo, bhattagge avandiyo, ekāvatto avandiyo, aññavihito avandiyo, naggo avandiyo – ime kho, upāli, pañca avandiyā.

“Furthermore, Upāli, there are another five who are not to be paid homage to. Which five? One who is drinking gruel is not to be paid homage to; one who is at a meal is not to be paid homage to; one who is on the opposing side is not to be paid homage to; one who is preoccupied is not to be paid homage to; one who is naked is not to be paid homage to. These, Upāli, are the five who are not to be paid homage to.”

“Aparepi[V 0.0378], upāli, pañca avandiyā. Katame pañca? Khādanto avandiyo, bhuñjanto avandiyo, uccāraṃ karonto avandiyo, passāvaṃ karonto avandiyo, ukkhittako avandiyo – ime kho, upāli, pañca avandiyā.

“Furthermore, Upāli, there are another five who are not to be paid homage to. Which five? One who is eating hard food is not to be paid homage to; one who is eating is not to be paid homage to; one who is defecating is not to be paid homage to; one who is urinating is not to be paid homage to; a monk who has been suspended is not to be paid homage to. These, Upāli, are the five who are not to be paid homage to.”

“Aparepi, upāli, pañca avandiyā[T 0.0507]. Katame pañca? Pure upasampannena pacchā upasampanno avandiyo, anupasampanno avandiyo, nānāsaṃvāsako vuḍḍhataro adhammavādī avandiyo, mātugāmo avandiyo, paṇḍako avandiyo – ime kho, upāli, pañca avandiyā.

“Furthermore, Upāli, there are another five who are not to be paid homage to. Which five? One who was fully ordained later is not to be paid homage to by one who was fully ordained earlier; a novice is not to be paid homage to; a senior monk of a different communion who speaks what is not the Dhamma is not to be paid homage to; a woman is not to be paid homage to; a paṇḍaka is not to be paid homage to. These, Upāli, are the five who are not to be paid homage to.”

“Aparepi, upāli, pañca avandiyā. Katame pañca? Pārivāsiko avandiyo, mūlāyapaṭikassanāraho avandiyo, mānattāraho avandiyo, mānattacāriko avandiyo, abbhānāraho avandiyo – ime kho, upāli, pañca avandiyā”ti.

“Furthermore, Upāli, there are another five who are not to be venerated. Which five? One undergoing parivāsa is not to be venerated, one deserving to be sent back to the beginning is not to be venerated, one deserving mānatta is not to be venerated, one undertaking mānatta is not to be venerated, and one deserving rehabilitation is not to be venerated—these, Upāli, are the five who are not to be venerated.”

468. “Kati [P 5.0206][M 0.0358] nu kho, bhante, vandiyā”ti? “Pañcime, upāli, vandiyā. Katame pañca? Pacchā upasampannena pure upasampanno vandiyo, nānāsaṃvāsako vuḍḍhataro dhammavādī vandiyo, ācariyo vandiyo, upajjhāyo vandiyo, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vandiyo – ime kho, upāli, pañca vandiyā”ti.

468. “How many, Venerable Sir, are to be venerated?” “Upāli, there are these five who are to be venerated. Which five? One who was fully ordained earlier is to be venerated by one who was fully ordained later; a senior of a different communion who speaks in accordance with the Dhamma is to be venerated; a teacher is to be venerated; a preceptor is to be venerated; and the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, is to be venerated in the world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans—these, Upāli, are the five who are to be venerated.”

469. “Navakatarena, bhante, bhikkhunā vuḍḍhatarassa bhikkhuno pāde vandantena kati dhamme ajjhattaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā pādā vanditabbā”ti? “Navakatarenupāli, bhikkhunā vuḍḍhatarassa bhikkhuno pāde vandantena pañca dhamme ajjhattaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā pādā vanditabbā. Katame pañca? Navakatarenupāli, bhikkhunā vuḍḍhatarassa bhikkhuno pāde vandantena ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā, añjaliṃ paggahetvā[T 0.0508], ubhohi pāṇitalehi pādāni parisambāhantena, pemañca gāravañca upaṭṭhāpetvā pādā vanditabbā – navakatarenupāli bhikkhunā vuḍḍhatarassa bhikkhuno pāde vandantena ime pañca dhamme ajjhattaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā pādā vanditabbā”ti.

469. “Venerable Sir, when a junior bhikkhu venerates the feet of a senior bhikkhu, how many things should he establish internally before venerating the feet?” “Upāli, when a junior bhikkhu venerates the feet of a senior bhikkhu, he should establish five things internally before venerating the feet. Which five? Upāli, when a junior bhikkhu venerates the feet of a senior bhikkhu, he should arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, raise his joined palms, massage the feet with both hands, and establish love and respect before venerating the feet—Upāli, when a junior bhikkhu venerates the feet of a senior bhikkhu, he should establish these five things internally before venerating the feet.”

Kathinatthāravaggo niṭṭhito cuddasamo.

The Fourteenth Chapter, on the Spreading of the Kathina, is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Kathinatthāraniddā [V 0.0379] ca, antarā yāgukhādane;

Pure ca pārivāsi ca, vandiyo vanditabbakanti.

Spreading the Kathina and sleep, within the house, gruel, and food; the one ordained earlier and the one on probation, the one to be venerated, and the act of venerating.

Upālipañcakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Upāli Pentad is concluded.

Tesaṃ vaggānaṃ uddānaṃ

The summary of these chapters:

Anissitena kammañca, vohārāvikammena ca;

Codanā ca dhutaṅgā ca, musā bhikkhunimeva ca.

Non-dependence and action, transactions and disclosure; accusation and ascetic practices, falsehood and the exhortation to nuns.

Ubbāhikādhikaraṇaṃ, bhedakā pañcamā pure;

Āvāsikā kathinañca, cuddasā suppakāsitāti.

The Ubbāhikā chapter, the Adhikaraṇa chapter, furthermore the two Bhedaka chapters, the Āvāsikā chapters, and the Kathina chapter—thus the fourteen chapters are well explained.

Atthāpattisamuṭṭhānaṃ

The Origin of Offenses

1. Pārājikaṃ

1. Pārājika

470. Atthāpatti [T 0.0509][P 5.0207][M 0.0359][V 0.0380] acittako āpajjati, sacittako vuṭṭhāti. Atthāpatti sacittako āpajjati, acittako vuṭṭhāti. Atthāpatti acittako āpajjati, acittako vuṭṭhāti. Atthāpatti sacittako āpajjati, sacittako vuṭṭhāti. Atthāpatti kusalacitto āpajjati, kusalacitto vuṭṭhāti. Atthāpatti kusalacitto āpajjati, akusalacitto vuṭṭhāti. Atthāpatti kusalacitto āpajjati, abyākatacitto vuṭṭhāti. Atthāpatti akusalacitto āpajjati, kusalacitto vuṭṭhāti. Atthāpatti akusalacitto āpajjati, akusalacitto vuṭṭhāti. Atthāpatti akusalacitto āpajjati, abyākatacitto vuṭṭhāti. Atthāpatti abyākatacitto āpajjati, kusalacitto vuṭṭhāti. Atthāpatti abyākatacitto āpajjati, akusalacitto vuṭṭhāti. Atthāpatti abyākatacitto āpajjati, abyākatacitto vuṭṭhāti.
