470. There is an offense which one without intention incurs, and from which one with intention rises. There is an offense which one with intention incurs, and from which one without intention rises. There is an offense which one without intention incurs, and from which one without intention rises. There is an offense which one with intention incurs, and from which one with intention rises. There is an offense which one with a wholesome mind incurs, and from which one with a wholesome mind rises. There is an offense which one with a wholesome mind incurs, and from which one with an unwholesome mind rises. There is an offense which one with a wholesome mind incurs, and from which one with an indeterminate mind rises. There is an offense which one with an unwholesome mind incurs, and from which one with a wholesome mind rises. There is an offense which one with an unwholesome mind incurs, and from which one with an unwholesome mind rises. There is an offense which one with an unwholesome mind incurs, and from which one with an indeterminate mind rises. There is an offense which one with an indeterminate mind incurs, and from which one with a wholesome mind rises. There is an offense which one with an indeterminate mind incurs, and from which one with an unwholesome mind rises. There is an offense which one with an indeterminate mind incurs, and from which one with an indeterminate mind rises.

Paṭhamaṃ pārājikaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Paṭhamaṃ pārājikaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti. Kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato.

From how many origins does the first pārājika offense arise? The first pārājika offense arises from one origin. It arises from body and mind, not from speech.

Dutiyaṃ pārājikaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Dutiyaṃ pārājikaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca [T 0.0510] vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti.

From how many origins does the second pārājika offense arise? The second pārājika offense arises from three origins: it may arise from body and mind, but not from speech; it may arise from speech and mind, but not from body; or it may arise from body, speech, and mind.

Tatiyaṃ pārājikaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Tatiyaṃ pārājikaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti.

From how many origins does the third pārājika offense arise? The third pārājika offense arises from three origins: it may arise from body and mind, but not from speech; it may arise from speech and mind, but not from body; or it may arise from body, speech, and mind.

Catutthaṃ [V 0.0381] pārājikaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Catutthaṃ pārājikaṃ tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti[M 0.0360], na vācato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti.

From how many origins does the fourth pārājika offense arise? The fourth pārājika offense arises from three origins: it may arise from body and mind, but not from speech; it may arise from speech and mind, but not from body; or it may arise from body, speech, and mind.

Cattāro pārājikā niṭṭhitā.

The four pārājikas are concluded.

2. Saṅghādisesaṃ

2. Saṅghādisesa

471. Upakkamitvā asuciṃ mocentassa saṅghādiseso katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Upakkamitvā asuciṃ mocentassa saṅghādiseso ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato.

471. For one who, having made an effort, emits semen, from how many origins does the saṅghādisesa offense arise? For one who, having made an effort, emits semen, the saṅghādisesa offense arises from one origin: it arises from body and mind, not from speech.

Mātugāmena saddhiṃ kāyasaṃsaggaṃ samāpajjantassa saṅghādiseso katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Mātugāmena saddhiṃ kāyasaṃsaggaṃ samāpajjantassa saṅghādiseso ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato.

For one who engages in bodily contact with a woman, from how many origins does the saṅghādisesa offense arise? For one who engages in bodily contact with a woman, the saṅghādisesa offense arises from one origin: it arises from body and mind, not from speech.

Mātugāmaṃ duṭṭhullāhi vācāhi obhāsentassa saṅghādiseso katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Mātugāmaṃ duṭṭhullāhi vācāhi obhāsentassa saṅghādiseso tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato ca [T 0.0511] cittato ca samuṭṭhāti na vācato; siyā vācato [P 5.0208] ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti.

For a monk who addresses a woman with coarse words, from how many origins does the saṅghādisesa offense arise? For a monk who addresses a woman with coarse words, the saṅghādisesa offense arises from three origins: sometimes it arises from body and mind, not from speech; sometimes it arises from speech and mind, not from body; sometimes it arises from body, speech, and mind.

Mātugāmassa santike attakāmapāricariyāya vaṇṇaṃ bhāsantassa saṅghādiseso katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Mātugāmassa santike attakāmapāricariyāya vaṇṇaṃ bhāsantassa saṅghādiseso tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

For a monk who, in the presence of a woman, speaks in praise of service for his own sake through sensual pleasures, from how many origins does the saṅghādisesa offense arise? For a monk who, in the presence of a woman, speaks in praise of service for his own sake through sensual pleasures, the saṅghādisesa offense arises from three origins…pe….

Sañcarittaṃ samāpajjantassa saṅghādiseso katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Sañcarittaṃ samāpajjantassa saṅghādiseso chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti – siyā kāyato samuṭṭhāti, na vācato na cittato; siyā vācato samuṭṭhāti, na kāyato na cittato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca samuṭṭhāti, na cittato; siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato; siyā [V 0.0382] vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti[M 0.0361], na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti.

For a monk who engages in acting as a go-between, from how many origins does the saṅghādisesa offense arise? For a monk who engages in acting as a go-between, the saṅghādisesa offense arises from six origins: sometimes it arises from body, not from speech, not from mind; sometimes it arises from speech, not from body, not from mind; sometimes it arises from body and speech, not from mind; sometimes it arises from body and mind, not from speech; sometimes it arises from speech and mind, not from body; sometimes it arises from body, speech, and mind.

Saññācikāya kuṭiṃ kārāpentassa saṅghādiseso katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Saññācikāya kuṭiṃ kārāpentassa saṅghādiseso chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

For a monk who has a hut built by means of solicitation, from how many origins does the saṅghādisesa offense arise? For a monk who has a hut built by means of solicitation, the saṅghādisesa offense arises from six origins…pe….

Mahallakaṃ vihāraṃ kārāpentassa saṅghādiseso katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Mahallakaṃ vihāraṃ kārāpentassa saṅghādiseso chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

For a monk who has a large dwelling built, from how many origins does the saṅghādisesa offense arise? For a monk who has a large dwelling built, the saṅghādisesa offense arises from six origins…pe….

Bhikkhuṃ amūlakena pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṃsentassa saṅghādiseso katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Bhikkhuṃ amūlakena pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṃsentassa saṅghādiseso tīhi samuṭṭhānehi [T 0.0512] samuṭṭhāti…pe….

For a monk who groundlessly accuses a bhikkhu of a pārājika offense, from how many origins does the saṅghādisesa offense arise? For a monk who groundlessly accuses a bhikkhu of a pārājika offense, the saṅghādisesa offense arises from three origins…pe….

Bhikkhuṃ aññabhāgiyassa adhikaraṇassa kiñci desaṃ lesamattaṃ upādāya pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṃsentassa saṅghādiseso katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Bhikkhuṃ aññabhāgiyassa adhikaraṇassa kiñci desaṃ lesamattaṃ upādāya pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṃsentassa saṅghādiseso tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti…pe….

For a monk who, taking up some part, a mere trifle, of a legal issue belonging to another party, accuses a bhikkhu of a pārājika offense, from how many origins does the saṅghādisesa offense arise? For a monk who, taking up some part, a mere trifle, of a legal issue belonging to another party, accuses a bhikkhu of a pārājika offense, the saṅghādisesa offense arises from three origins…pe….

Saṅghabhedakassa bhikkhuno yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjantassa saṅghādiseso katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Saṅghabhedakassa bhikkhuno yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjantassa saṅghādiseso ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti.

For a bhikkhu who is a schismatic of the Saṅgha and does not abandon his view after being admonished up to the third time, from how many origins does the saṅghādisesa offense arise? The saṅghādisesa offense for a bhikkhu who is a schismatic of the Saṅgha and does not abandon his view after being admonished up to the third time arises from one origin: it arises from body, speech, and mind.

Bhedakānuvattakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjantānaṃ saṅghādiseso katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Bhedakānuvattakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjantānaṃ saṅghādiseso ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti.

For bhikkhus who are followers of a schismatic and do not abandon their view after being admonished up to the third time, from how many origins does the saṅghādisesa offense arise? The saṅghādisesa offense for bhikkhus who are followers of a schismatic and do not abandon their view after being admonished up to the third time arises from one origin: it arises from body, speech, and mind.

Dubbacassa bhikkhuno yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjantassa saṅghādiseso katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Dubbacassa bhikkhuno yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjantassa [V 0.0383] saṅghādiseso ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti.

For a bhikkhu who is difficult to admonish and does not abandon his view after being admonished up to the third time, from how many origins does the saṅghādisesa offense arise? The saṅghādisesa offense for a bhikkhu who is difficult to admonish and does not abandon his view after being admonished up to the third time arises from one origin: it arises from body, speech, and mind.

Kuladūsakassa [M 0.0362] bhikkhuno yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjantassa saṅghādiseso katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Kuladūsakassa bhikkhuno yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya [T 0.0513] na paṭinissajjantassa saṅghādiseso ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti.

For a bhikkhu who is a corrupter of families and does not abandon his view after being admonished up to the third time, from how many origins does the saṅghādisesa offense arise? The saṅghādisesa offense for a bhikkhu who is a corrupter of families and does not abandon his view after being admonished up to the third time arises from one origin: it arises from body, speech, and mind.

Terasa saṅghādisesā niṭṭhitā.

The thirteen saṅghādisesa offenses are concluded.

472. …Pe… anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karontassa dukkaṭaṃ katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhāti? Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karontassa dukkaṭaṃ ekena samuṭṭhānena samuṭṭhāti – kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhāti, na vācato.

472. …pe… On account of disrespect, from how many origins does a dukkaṭa offense arise for a monk who passes excrement, urine, or sputum in water? On account of disrespect, a dukkaṭa offense for a monk who passes excrement, urine, or sputum in water arises from one origin: it arises from body and mind, not from speech.

Sekhiyā niṭṭhitā.

The Sekhiya training rules are concluded.

3. Pārājikādi

3. Pārājika and Other Offenses

473. Cattāro pārājikā katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti? Cattāro pārājikā tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti – siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti, na vācato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti, na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti.

473. From how many origins do the four pārājika offenses arise? The four pārājika offenses arise from three origins: sometimes they arise from body and mind, not from speech; sometimes they arise from speech and mind, not from body; sometimes they arise from body, speech, and mind.

Terasa [P 5.0209] saṅghādisesā katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti? Terasa saṅghādisesā chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti – siyā kāyato samuṭṭhanti, na vācato na cittato; siyā vācato samuṭṭhanti, na kāyato na cittato; siyā kāyato ca vācato na samuṭṭhanti, na cittato; siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti, na vācato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti, na kāyato; siyā [T 0.0514] kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti.

From how many origins do the thirteen saṅghādisesa offenses arise? The thirteen saṅghādisesa offenses arise from six origins: sometimes they arise from body, not from speech or mind; sometimes from speech, not from body or mind; sometimes from body and speech, not from mind; sometimes from body and mind, not from speech; sometimes from speech and mind, not from body; sometimes from body, speech, and mind.

Dve aniyatā katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti? Dve aniyatā tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti [V 0.0384] – siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti, na vācato; [M 0.0363] siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti, na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti.

From how many origins do the two aniyata offenses arise? The two aniyata offenses arise from three origins: sometimes they arise from body and mind, not from speech; sometimes they arise from speech and mind, not from body; sometimes they arise from body, speech, and mind.

Tiṃsa nissaggiyā pācittiyā katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti? Tiṃsa nissaggiyā pācittiyā chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti – siyā kāyato samuṭṭhanti, na vācato na cittato; siyā vācato samuṭṭhanti, na kāyato na cittato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca samuṭṭhanti, na cittato; siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti, na vācato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti, na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti.

From how many origins do the thirty nissaggiya pācittiya offenses arise? The thirty nissaggiya pācittiya offenses arise from six origins: sometimes they arise from body, not from speech or mind; sometimes from speech, not from body or mind; sometimes from body and speech, not from mind; sometimes from body and mind, not from speech; sometimes from speech and mind, not from body; sometimes from body, speech, and mind.

Dvenavuti pācittiyā katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti? Dvenavuti pācittiyā chahi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti – siyā kāyato samuṭṭhanti, na vācato na cittato; siyā vācato samuṭṭhanti, na kāyato na cittato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca samuṭṭhanti, na cittato; siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti na vācato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti, na kāyato; siyā [T 0.0515] kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti.

From how many origins do the ninety-two pācittiya offenses arise? The ninety-two pācittiya offenses arise from six origins: it may be that they arise from the body, but not from speech or mind; it may be that they arise from speech, but not from body or mind; it may be that they arise from body and speech, but not from mind; it may be that they arise from body and mind, but not from speech; it may be that they arise from speech and mind, but not from body; it may be that they arise from body, speech, and mind.

Cattāro pāṭidesanīyā katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti? Cattāro pāṭidesanīyā catūhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti – siyā kāyato samuṭṭhanti, na vācato na cittato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca samuṭṭhanti, na cittato; siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti, na vācato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti.

From how many origins do the four pāṭidesanīya offenses arise? The four pāṭidesanīya offenses arise from four origins: it may be that they arise from the body, but not from speech or mind; it may be that they arise from body and speech, but not from mind; it may be that they arise from body and mind, but not from speech; it may be that they arise from body, speech, and mind.

Pañcasattati sekhiyā katihi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti? Pañcasattati sekhiyā tīhi samuṭṭhānehi samuṭṭhanti – siyā kāyato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti, na vācato; siyā vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti, na kāyato; siyā kāyato ca vācato ca cittato ca samuṭṭhanti.

From how many origins do the seventy-five sekhiya rules arise? The seventy-five sekhiya rules arise from three origins: it may be that they arise from body and mind, but not from speech; it may be that they arise from speech and mind, but not from body; it may be that they arise from body, speech, and mind.

Samuṭṭhānaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The section on Origination is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Acittakusalā ceva, samuṭṭhānañca sabbathā;

Yathādhammena ñāyena, samuṭṭhānaṃ vijānathāti.

Unintentional and skillful offenses, and origination in all its aspects; one should understand origination according to the rule and the method.

Dutiyagāthāsaṅgaṇikaṃ

The Second Collection of Verses

1. Kāyikādiāpatti

1. Bodily Offenses and so forth

474. Kati [T 0.0516][P 5.0210][M 0.0364][V 0.0385] āpattiyo kāyikā, kati vācasikā katā.

474. How many offenses have been declared as bodily? How many have been declared as verbal?

Chādentassa kati āpattiyo, kati saṃsaggapaccayā.

For one who conceals, how many offenses? How many from the condition of association?

Chāpattiyo kāyikā, cha vācasikā katā;

Chādentassa tisso āpattiyo, pañca saṃsaggapaccayā.

Six offenses have been declared as bodily, and six as verbal; for one who conceals, three offenses; from the condition of association, five.

Aruṇugge kati āpattiyo, kati yāvatatiyakā;

Katettha aṭṭha vatthukā, katihi sabbasaṅgaho.

How many offenses are incurred at the rising of dawn? How many require a third announcement? How many herein have eight articles? By how many is the entire collection summarized?

Aruṇugge tisso āpattiyo, dve yāvatatiyakā;

Ekettha aṭṭha vatthukā, ekena sabbasaṅgaho.

Three offenses are incurred at the rising of dawn; two require a third announcement; one herein has eight articles; by one, the entire collection is summarized.

Vinayassa kati mūlāni, yāni buddhena paññattā;

Vinayagarukā kati vuttā, duṭṭhullacchādanā kati.

How many are the roots of the Vinaya that were laid down by the Buddha? How many grave offenses in the Vinaya were spoken of? How many are the offenses of concealing a gross offense?

Vinayassa dve mūlāni, yāni buddhena paññattā;

Vinayagarukā dve vuttā, dve duṭṭhullacchādanā.

Two are the roots of the Vinaya that were laid down by the Buddha; two grave offenses in the Vinaya were spoken of, and two are the offenses of concealing a gross offense.

Gāmantare kati āpattiyo, kati nadipārapaccayā;

Katimaṃsesu thullaccayaṃ, katimaṃsesu dukkaṭaṃ.

How many offenses were spoken of in regard to going to another village? How many on account of crossing a river? In regard to how many kinds of flesh was a grave offense spoken of? In regard to how many kinds of flesh, a minor offense?

Gāmantare [V 0.0386] catasso āpattiyo, catasso nadipārapaccayā;

Ekamaṃse thullaccayaṃ, navamaṃsesu dukkaṭaṃ.

In regard to going to another village, there are four offenses; four on account of crossing a river. In regard to one kind of flesh, there is a grave offense; in regard to nine kinds of flesh, a minor offense.

Kati vācasikā rattiṃ, kati vācasikā divā;

Dadamānassa kati āpattiyo, paṭiggaṇhantassa kittakā.

How many verbal offenses are there at night, and how many verbal offenses by day? For one who gives, how many offenses are there; for one who receives, how many?

Dve [T 0.0517] vācasikā rattiṃ, dve vācasikā divā;

Dadamānassa tisso āpattiyo, cattāro ca paṭiggahe.

There are two verbal offenses at night, and two verbal offenses by day; for one who gives, there are three offenses, and four in the case of receiving.

2. Desanāgāminiyādiāpatti

2. Offenses Beginning with Those Requiring Confession

475.

475.

Kati desanāgāminiyo, kati sappaṭikammā katā;

Katettha appaṭikammā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā.

How many offenses requiring confession were made known? How many remediable offenses were made known? Among these, how many irremediable offenses were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun?

Pañca [M 0.0365] desanāgāminiyo, cha sappaṭikammā katā;

Ekettha appaṭikammā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā.

Five offenses requiring confession were made known; six remediable offenses were made known. Among these, one irremediable offense was spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun.

Vinayagarukā kati vuttā, kāyavācasikāni ca;

Kati vikāle dhaññaraso, kati ñatticatutthena sammuti.

How many grave offenses in the Vinaya were spoken of, and how many rules are bodily and verbal? How many grain-juices are allowable at the wrong time? How many authorizations are there by a motion and three announcements?

Vinayagarukā dve vuttā, kāyavācasikāni ca;

Eko vikāle dhaññaraso, ekā ñatticatutthena sammuti.

Two grave offenses in the Vinaya were spoken of; and all training rules are bodily and verbal. One grain-juice is allowable at the wrong time; one authorization is by a motion and three announcements.

Pārājikā kāyikā kati, kati saṃvāsakabhūmiyo;

Katinaṃ [P 5.0211] ratticchedo, paññattā dvaṅgulā kati.

How many bodily Pārājika offenses are there? How many grounds for communion? For how many is there a break in the night's residence? How many two-finger-breadth regulations are there?

Pārājikā kāyikā dve, dve saṃvāsakabhūmiyo;

Dvinnaṃ ratticchedo, paññattā dvaṅgulā duve.

There are two bodily Pārājika offenses; two grounds for communion. For two persons, there is a break in the night's residence; there are two two-finger-breadth regulations.

Katattānaṃ [V 0.0387] vadhitvāna, katihi saṅgho bhijjati;

Katettha paṭhamāpattikā, ñattiyā karaṇā kati.

By tormenting oneself, into how many offenses does one fall? By how many causes is the Saṅgha split? Herein, how many first offenses are there? How many announcements of a motion are there?

Dve attānaṃ vadhitvāna, dvīhi saṅgho bhijjati;

Dvettha paṭhamāpattikā, ñattiyā karaṇā duve.

By tormenting oneself, one falls into two offenses; by two causes the Saṅgha is split. Herein, there are two first offenses; there are two announcements of a motion.

Pāṇātipāte kati āpattiyo, vācā pārājikā kati;

Obhāsanā [T 0.0518] kati vuttā, sañcarittena vā kati.

In the destruction of life, how many offenses are there? How many Pārājika offenses by speech were spoken of? How many were spoken of concerning hinting? Or by acting as a go-between, how many are there?

Pāṇātipāte tisso āpattiyo;

Vācā pārājikā tayo;

Obhāsanā tayo vuttā;

Sañcarittena vā tayo.

In the destruction of life, there are three offenses; three Pārājika offenses by speech; three were spoken of concerning hinting; or by acting as a go-between, there are three.

Kati puggalā na upasampādetabbā, kati kammānaṃ saṅgahā;

Nāsitakā kati vuttā, katinaṃ ekavācikā.

How many persons should not be given higher ordination? How many classifications of formal acts are spoken of? How many kinds of banishment are spoken of? For how many is a single recitation of the formal act allowable?

Tayo puggalā na upasampādetabbā, tayo kammānaṃ saṅgahā;

Nāsitakā tayo vuttā, tiṇṇannaṃ ekavācikā.

Three persons should not be given higher ordination; three classifications of formal acts are spoken of; three kinds of banishment are spoken of; for three, a single recitation of the formal act is allowable.

Adinnādāne kati āpattiyo, kati methunapaccayā;

Chindantassa kati āpattiyo, kati chaḍḍitapaccayā.

On account of theft, how many offenses are there? How many offenses are on account of sexual intercourse? For one who cuts, how many offenses are there? How many offenses are on account of discarding?

Adinnādāne tisso āpattiyo, catasso methunapaccayā;

Chindantassa tisso āpattiyo, pañca chaḍḍitapaccayā.

On account of theft, there are three offenses; on account of sexual intercourse, four; for one who cuts, there are three offenses; on account of discarding, five.

Bhikkhunovādakavaggasmiṃ[M 0.0366], pācittiyena dukkaṭā;

Katettha navakā vuttā, katinaṃ cīvarena ca.

In the Chapter on the Exhortation of Bhikkhunīs, are offenses of wrong-doing laid down together with an offense entailing expiation? How many groups of nine are spoken of here? And for how many is an offense spoken of on account of a robe?

Bhikkhunovādakavaggasmiṃ[V 0.0388], pācittiyena dukkaṭā katā;

Caturettha navakā vuttā, dvinnaṃ cīvarena ca.

In the Chapter on the Exhortation of Bhikkhunīs, offenses of wrong-doing are indeed laid down together with an offense entailing expiation. Four groups of nine are spoken of here, and for two, an offense is spoken of on account of a robe.

Bhikkhunīnañca akkhātā, pāṭidesaniyā kati;

Bhuñjantāmakadhaññena, pācittiyena dukkaṭā kati.

And for bhikkhunīs, how many offenses to be confessed are declared? For one who eats raw grain, how many offenses of wrong-doing are laid down together with an offense entailing expiation?

Bhikkhunīnañca akkhātā, aṭṭha pāṭidesanīyā katā;

Bhuñjantāmakadhaññena, pācittiyena dukkaṭā katā.

And for bhikkhunīs, eight offenses to be confessed are declared. For one who eats raw grain, offenses of wrong-doing are indeed laid down together with an offense entailing expiation.

Gacchantassa kati āpattiyo, ṭhitassa cāpi kittakā;

Nisinnassa [T 0.0519] kati āpattiyo, nipannassāpi kittakā.

How many offenses are there for one who is walking? And how many for one who is standing? How many offenses are there for one who is sitting? And how many for one who is lying down?

Gacchantassa catasso āpattiyo, ṭhitassa cāpi tattakā;

Nisinnassa catasso āpattiyo, nipannassāpi tattakā.

For one who is walking, there are four offenses; and for one who is standing, just as many. For one who is sitting, there are four offenses; and for one who is lying down, just as many.

3. Pācittiyaṃ

3. Offenses Entailing Expiation

476.

476.

Kati pācittiyāni, sabbāni nānāvatthukāni;

Apubbaṃ acarimaṃ, āpajjeyya ekato.

How many offenses entailing expiation, all having different grounds, might one fall into at once, simultaneously?

Pañca pācittiyāni, sabbāni nānāvatthukāni;

Apubbaṃ acarimaṃ, āpajjeyya ekato.

Five offenses entailing expiation, all having different grounds, one might fall into at once, simultaneously.

Kati pācittiyāni, sabbāni nānāvatthukāni;

Apubbaṃ acarimaṃ, āpajjeyya ekato.

How many offenses entailing expiation, all having different grounds, might one fall into at once, simultaneously?

Na [P 5.0212] pācittiyāni, sabbāni nānāvatthukāni;

Apubbaṃ acarimaṃ, āpajjeyya ekato.

Nine offenses entailing expiation, all having different grounds, one might fall into at once, simultaneously.

Kati [V 0.0389] pācittiyāni, sabbāni nānāvatthukāni;

Kati vācāya deseyya, vuttā ādiccabandhunā.

How many offenses entailing expiation, all having different grounds, have been spoken of by the Kinsman of the Sun to be confessed with how many utterances?

Pañca pācittiyāni, sabbāni nānāvatthukāni;

Ekavācāya deseyya, vuttā ādiccabandhunā.

Five offenses entailing expiation, all having different grounds, one should confess with a single utterance; so it was spoken by the Kinsman of the Sun.

Kati pācittiyāni, sabbāni nānāvatthukāni;

Kati vācāya deseyya, vuttā ādiccabandhunā.

How many offenses entailing expiation, all having different grounds, have been spoken of by the Kinsman of the Sun to be confessed with how many utterances?

Nava [M 0.0367] pācittiyāni, sabbāni nānāvatthukāni;

Ekavācāya deseyya, vuttā ādiccabandhunā.

Nine offenses entailing expiation, all having different grounds, one should confess with a single utterance; so it was spoken by the Kinsman of the Sun.

Kati pācittiyāni, sabbāni nānāvatthukāni;

Kiñca [T 0.0520] kittetvā deseyya, vuttā ādiccabandhunā.

How many offenses entailing expiation, all having different grounds, should one confess, and what should one recount when doing so, as spoken of by the Kinsman of the Sun?

Pañca pācittiyāni, sabbāni nānāvatthukāni;

Vatthuṃ kittetvā deseyya, vuttā ādiccabandhunā.

Five offenses entailing expiation, all having different grounds, one should confess, having recounted the ground; so it was spoken by the Kinsman of the Sun.

Kati pācittiyāni, sabbāni nānāvatthukāni;

Kiñca kittetvā deseyya, vuttā ādiccabandhunā.

How many offenses entailing expiation, all having different grounds, should one confess, and what should one recount when doing so, as spoken of by the Kinsman of the Sun?

Nava pācittiyāni, sabbāni nānāvatthukāni;

Vatthuṃ kittetvā deseyya, vuttā ādiccabandhunā.

Nine offenses entailing expiation, all having different grounds, one should confess, having recounted the ground; so it was spoken by the Kinsman of the Sun.

Yāvatatiyake kati āpattiyo, kati vohārapaccayā;

Khādantassa kati āpattiyo, kati bhojanapaccayā.

In the 'up to the third time' case, how many offenses are there? On account of an utterance, how many? For one eating solid food, how many offenses? On account of a meal, how many?

Yāvatatiyake tisso āpattiyo, cha vohārapaccayā;

Khādantassa tisso āpattiyo, pañca bhojanapaccayā.

In the 'up to the third time' case, there are three offenses; six on account of an utterance. For one eating solid food, there are three offenses; five on account of a meal.

Sabbā [V 0.0390] yāvatatiyakā, kati ṭhānāni gacchanti;

Katinañceva āpatti, katinaṃ adhikaraṇena ca.

All 'up to the third time' cases—to how many grounds do they lead? And for how many persons is there an offense? And for how many is there a legal issue?

Sabbā yāvatatiyakā, pañca ṭhānāni gacchanti;

Pañcannañceva āpatti, pañcannaṃ adhikaraṇena ca.

All 'up to the third time' cases lead to five grounds. And for five persons there is an offense, and for five there is a legal issue.

Katinaṃ vinicchayo hoti, katinaṃ vūpasamena ca;

Katinañceva anāpatti, katihi ṭhānehi sobhati.

For how many persons is there a judgment, and for how many a settlement? And for how many is there no offense? In how many respects does one shine?

Pañcannaṃ vinicchayo hoti, pañcannaṃ vūpasamena ca;

Pañcannañceva anāpatti, tīhi ṭhānehi sobhati.

For five persons there is a judgment, and for five a settlement. And for five there is no offense; one shines in three respects.

Kati [T 0.0521] kāyikā rattiṃ, kati kāyikā divā;

Nijjhāyantassa kati āpatti, kati piṇḍapātapaccayā.

How many bodily offenses are incurred at night, and how many bodily offenses by day? For one who is observing, how many offenses are there? On account of alms-food, how many?

Dve kāyikā rattiṃ, dve kāyikā divā;

Nijjhāyantassa ekā āpatti, ekā piṇḍapātapaccayā.

Two bodily offenses are incurred at night, and two bodily offenses by day. For one who is observing, there is one offense; on account of alms-food, there is one.

Katānisaṃse [M 0.0368] sampassaṃ, paresaṃ saddhāya desaye;

Ukkhittakā kati vuttā, kati sammāvattanā.

Seeing how many benefits should one confess to others with faith? How many are said to be 'suspended'? How many are duties of proper conduct?

Aṭṭhānisaṃse sampassaṃ, paresaṃ saddhāya desaye;

Ukkhittakā tayo vuttā, tecattālīsa sammāvattanā.

Seeing eight benefits, one should confess to others with faith. Three are said to be 'suspended'; forty-three are duties of proper conduct.

Kati ṭhāne musāvādo, kati paramanti vuccati;

Kati [P 5.0213] pāṭidesanīyā, katinaṃ desanāya ca.

In how many instances does false speech occur? How many are called 'supreme'? How many are the offenses to be confessed? And for how many is there confession?

Pañca ṭhāne musāvādo, cuddasa paramanti vuccati;

Dvādasa pāṭidesanīyā, catunnaṃ desanāya ca.

In five instances false speech occurs; fourteen are called 'supreme'. Twelve are the offenses to be confessed; and for four there is confession.

Kataṅgiko [V 0.0391] musāvādo, kati uposathaṅgāni;

Kati dūteyyaṅgāni, kati titthiyavattanā.

Of how many factors is false speech composed? How many are the Uposatha factors? How many are the factors of a messenger? How many are the practices for heretics?

Aṭṭhaṅgiko musāvādo, aṭṭha uposathaṅgāni;

Aṭṭha dūteyyaṅgāni, aṭṭha titthiyavattanā.

False speech is composed of eight factors; there are eight Uposatha factors. There are eight factors of a messenger; there are eight practices for heretics.

Kativācikā upasampadā, katinaṃ paccuṭṭhātabbaṃ;

Katinaṃ āsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, bhikkhunovādako katihi.

Of how many verbal announcements does the ordination of a bhikkhunī consist? For how many should one rise from one's seat? To how many should a seat be given? Possessed of how many factors should a bhikkhu be designated as an exhorter of bhikkhunīs?

Aṭṭhavācikā upasampadā, aṭṭhannaṃ paccuṭṭhātabbaṃ;

Aṭṭhannaṃ [T 0.0522] āsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, bhikkhunovādako aṭṭhahi.

The ordination of a bhikkhunī consists of eight verbal announcements; one should rise from one's seat for eight. A seat should be given to eight; a bhikkhu possessed of eight factors should be designated as an exhorter of bhikkhunīs.

Katinaṃ chejjaṃ hoti, katinaṃ thullaccayaṃ;

Katinañceva anāpatti, sabbesaṃ ekavatthukā.

For how many is there an offense of expulsion? For how many is there a grave offense? And for how many is there no offense? Do all of them have a single ground?

Ekassa chejjaṃ hoti, catunnaṃ thullaccayaṃ;

Catunnañceva anāpatti, sabbesaṃ ekavatthukā.

For one there is an offense of expulsion; for four there is a grave offense. And for four there is no offense; all of them have a single ground.

Kati āghātavatthūni, katihi saṅgho bhijjati;

Katettha paṭhamāpattikā, ñattiyā karaṇā kati.

How many are the grounds for resentment? By how many is the Saṅgha split? Among these, how many are initial offenses? How many are the acts done by a motion?

Nava āghātavatthūni, navahi saṅgho bhijjati;

Navettha paṭhamāpattikā, ñattiyā karaṇā nava.

There are nine grounds for resentment; by nine is the Saṅgha split. Among these, nine are initial offenses; nine are the acts done by a motion.

4. Avandanīyapuggalādi

4. Persons Not to Be Venerated, and so on

477.

477.

Kati puggalā nābhivādetabbā, añjalisāmicena ca;

Katinaṃ dukkaṭaṃ hoti, kati cīvaradhāraṇā.

How many persons should not be venerated, nor shown respect with the añjali gesture? For venerating how many does an offense of wrong-doing arise? For how many days is the keeping of an extra robe permitted?

Dasa [M 0.0369][V 0.0392] puggalā nābhivādetabbā, añjalisāmicena ca;

Dasannaṃ dukkaṭaṃ hoti, dasa cīvaradhāraṇā.

Ten persons should not be venerated, nor shown respect with the añjali gesture; for venerating ten persons there is an offense of wrong-doing. The keeping of an extra robe is permitted for ten days.

Katinaṃ vassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ, dātabbaṃ idha cīvaraṃ;

Katinaṃ bhante dātabbaṃ, katinañceva na dātabbaṃ.

To how many who have completed the rains-residence should a robe be given here in their presence? To how many should it be given in their absence, if there is a recipient? And to how many should it not be given?

Pañcannaṃ vassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ, dātabbaṃ idha cīvaraṃ;

Sattannaṃ sante dātabbaṃ, soḷasannaṃ na dātabbaṃ.

To five who have completed the rains-residence, a robe should be given here in their presence. To seven it should be given in their absence, if there is a recipient. To sixteen it should not be given.

Katisataṃ rattisataṃ, āpattiyo chādayitvāna;

Kati rattiyo vasitvāna, mucceyya pārivāsiko.

A bhikkhu on probation, having concealed how many hundred offenses for a hundred nights, after dwelling for how many nights would he be released?

Dasasataṃ rattisataṃ, āpattiyo chādayitvāna;

Dasa [T 0.0523] rattiyo vasitvāna, mucceyya pārivāsiko.

A bhikkhu on probation, having concealed a thousand offenses for a hundred nights, after dwelling for ten nights would be released.

Kati kammadosā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Campāyaṃ vinayavatthusmiṃ, sabbeva adhammikā sabbe adhammikā (sī. syā.) kati.

How many faulty acts were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun, in the Vinaya matter at Campā? Were all of them declared unlawful?

Dvādasa kammadosā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Campāyaṃ vinayavatthusmiṃ, sabbeva adhammikā sabbevādhammikā (sī.), sabbe adhammikā (syā.) katā.

Twelve faulty acts were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun; in the Vinaya matter at Campā, all were declared unlawful.

Kati kammasampattiyo vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Campāyaṃ vinayavatthusmiṃ, sabbeva dhammikā kati.

How many accomplished acts were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun, in the Vinaya matter at Campā? Were all of them declared lawful?

Catasso kammasampattiyo vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Campāyaṃ [P 5.0214] vinayavatthusmiṃ, sabbeva dhammikā katā.

Four accomplished acts were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun; in the Vinaya matter at Campā, all were declared lawful.

Kati kammāni vuttāni, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Campāyaṃ vinayavatthusmiṃ, dhammikā adhammikā kati.

How many acts were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun, in the Vinaya matter at Campā? How many were lawful, and how many were unlawful?

Cha [V 0.0393] kammāni vuttāni, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Campāyaṃ vinayavatthusmiṃ, ekettha dhammikā katā;

Pañca adhammikā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā.

Six acts were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun, in the Vinaya matter at Campā; among these, one was declared lawful. Five were declared unlawful by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun.

Kati kammāni vuttāni, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Campāyaṃ vinayavatthusmiṃ, dhammikā adhammikā kati.

How many acts were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun, in the Vinaya matter at Campā? How many were lawful, and how many were unlawful?

Cattāri [M 0.0370] kammāni vuttāni, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Campāyaṃ vinayavatthusmiṃ, ekettha dhammikā katā;

Tayo adhammikā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā.

Four acts were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun, in the Vinaya matter at Campā; among these, one was declared lawful. Three were declared unlawful by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun.

Yaṃ desitaṃnantajinena tādinā;

Āpattikkhandhāni [T 0.0524] vivekadassinā;

Katettha sammanti vinā samathehi;

Pucchāmi taṃ brūhi vibhaṅgakovida.

Regarding the groups of offenses taught by the limitless Conqueror, the Such-like One, the Seer of Seclusion: among these, how many are settled without the means of settlement? I ask you this; speak, O you who are skilled in the Vibhaṅgas.

Yaṃ desitaṃnantajinena tādinā;

Āpattikkhandhāni vivekadassinā;

Ekettha sammati vinā samathehi;

Etaṃ te akkhāmi vibhaṅgakovida.

Regarding the groups of offenses taught by the limitless Conqueror, the Such-like One, the Seer of Seclusion: among these, one is settled without the means of settlement. This I explain to you, O you who are skilled in the Vibhaṅgas.

Kati āpāyikā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni visayāni (sī. syā. evamuparipi) suṇoma te.

How many persons destined for the plane of misery were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun? From you, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, let us hear the Vinaya teachings.

Chaūnadiyaḍḍhasatā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Āpāyikā nerayikā, kappaṭṭhā saṅghabhedakā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇohi me.

One hundred and forty-four were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun: persons destined for the plane of misery, destined for hell, remaining for the aeon, who are schismatics. From me, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, listen to the Vinaya teachings.

Kati nāpāyikā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇoma te.

How many persons not destined for the plane of misery were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun? From you, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, let us hear the Vinaya teachings.

Aṭṭhārasa [V 0.0394] nāpāyikā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇohi me.

Eighteen persons not destined for the plane of misery were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun. From me, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, listen to the Vinaya teachings.

Kati aṭṭhakā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇoma te.

How many octads were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun? From you, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, let us hear the Vinaya teachings.

Aṭṭhārasa aṭṭhakā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇohi me.

Eighteen octads were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun. From me, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, listen to the Vinaya teachings.

478.

478.

Kati [T 0.0525] kammāni vuttāni, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇoma te.

How many acts were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun? From you, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, let us hear the Vinaya teachings.

Soḷasa [M 0.0371] kammāni vuttāni, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇohi me.

Sixteen acts were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun. From me, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, listen to the Vinaya teachings.

Kati kammadosā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ [P 5.0215] paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇoma te.

How many faulty acts were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun? From you, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, let us hear the Vinaya teachings.

Dvādasa kammadosā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇohi me.

Twelve faulty acts were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun. From me, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, listen to the Vinaya teachings.

Kati kammasampattiyo vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇoma te.

How many accomplished acts were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun? From you, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, let us hear the Vinaya teachings.

Catasso kammasampattiyo vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇohi me.

Four accomplished acts were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun. From me, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, listen to the Vinaya teachings.

Kati [V 0.0395] kammāni vuttāni, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇoma te.

How many acts were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun? From you, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, let us hear the Vinaya teachings.

Cha kammāni vuttāni, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇohi me.

Six acts were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun. From me, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, listen to the Vinaya teachings.

Kati kammāni vuttāni, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇoma te.

How many acts were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun? From you, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, let us hear the Vinaya teachings.

Cattāri kammāni vuttāni, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇohi me.

Four acts were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun. From me, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, listen to the Vinaya teachings.

Kati [T 0.0526] pārājikā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇoma te.

How many pārājikas were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun? From you, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, let us hear the Vinaya teachings.

Aṭṭha pārājikā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇohi me.

Eight pārājikas were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun. From me, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, listen to the Vinaya teachings.

Kati saṅghādisesā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇoma te.

How many saṅghādisesas were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun? From you, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, let us hear the Vinaya teachings.

Tevīsa saṅghādisesā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇohi me.

Twenty-three saṅghādisesas were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun. From me, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, listen to the Vinaya teachings.

Kati [M 0.0372] aniyatā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇoma te.

How many aniyatas were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun? From you, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, let us hear the Vinaya teachings.

Dve aniyatā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇohi me.

Two aniyatas were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun. From me, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, listen to the Vinaya teachings.

Kati [V 0.0396] nissaggiyā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇoma te.

How many nissaggiyas were spoken of by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun? From you, who professes knowledge of the Vinaya, let us hear the Vinaya teachings.

Dvecattālīsa nissaggiyā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇohi me.

Forty-two offenses of forfeiture were declared by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun. From me, who professes to know the Vinaya, listen to the Vinaya rules.

Kati pācittiyā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇoma te.

How many offenses entailing confession were declared by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun? From you, who professes to know the Vinaya, let us hear the Vinaya rules.

Aṭṭhāsītisataṃ pācittiyā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇohi me.

One hundred and eighty-eight offenses entailing confession were declared by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun. From me, who professes to know the Vinaya, listen to the Vinaya rules.

Kati [T 0.0527] pāṭidesanīyā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇoma te.

How many offenses to be acknowledged were declared by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun? From you, who professes to know the Vinaya, let us hear the Vinaya rules.

Dvādasa pāṭidesanīyā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇohi me.

Twelve offenses to be acknowledged were declared by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun. From me, who professes to know the Vinaya, listen to the Vinaya rules.

Kati sekhiyā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇoma te.

How many rules of training were declared by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun? From you, who professes to know the Vinaya, let us hear the Vinaya rules.

Pañcasattati sekhiyā vuttā, buddhenādiccabandhunā;

Vinayaṃ paṭijānantassa, vinayāni suṇohi me.

Seventy-five rules of training were declared by the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun. From me, who professes to know the Vinaya, listen to the Vinaya rules.

Yāva supucchitaṃ tayā, yāva suvissajjitaṃ mayā;

Pucchāvissajjanāya vā, natthi kiñci asuttakanti.

Inasmuch as was well asked by you, and inasmuch as was well answered by me, in either the questioning or the answering, there is nothing whatsoever that is not from the scriptures.

Dutiyagāthāsaṅgaṇikaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Second Collection of Verses is concluded.

Sedamocanagāthā

Sweat-Releasing Verses

1. Avippavāsapañhā

1. The Question on Non-Separation

479.

479.

Asaṃvāso [T 0.0528][P 5.0216][M 0.0373][V 0.0397] bhikkhūhi ca bhikkhunīhi ca;

Sambhogo ekacco tahiṃ na labbhati;

Avippavāsena anāpatti;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

There is no communion with bhikkhus and with bhikkhunīs; a certain intimate association is not permissible in that case. Through non-separation, there is no offense. This is a question considered by the skillful.

Avissajjiyaṃ avebhaṅgiyaṃ;

Pañca vuttā mahesinā;

Vissajjantassa paribhuñjantassa anāpatti;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

Not to be given away, not to be divided: five such things were declared by the Great Seer. For one who gives them away or uses them, there is no offense. This is a question considered by the skillful.

Dasa puggale na vadāmi, ekādasa vivajjiya;

Vuḍḍhaṃ vandantassa āpatti, pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

I do not speak of the ten persons, and I also exclude the eleven. For one who venerates an elder, there is an offense. This is a question considered by the skillful.

Na ukkhittako na ca pana pārivāsiko;

Na saṅghabhinno na ca pana pakkhasaṅkanto;

Samānasaṃvāsakabhūmiyā ṭhito;

Kathaṃ nu sikkhāya asādhāraṇo siyā;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

He is not a suspended monk, nor one on probation; not a schismatic, nor one who has gone over to another sect. He is established in the state of common communion; how then could he be subject to a training rule not shared with others? This is a question considered by the skillful.

Upeti [V 0.0398] dhammaṃ paripucchamāno, kusalaṃ atthūpasañhitaṃ;

Na [T 0.0529] jīvati na mato na nibbuto, taṃ puggalaṃ katamaṃ vadanti buddhā;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

He approaches, inquiring about the wholesome doctrine connected with benefit. He is not living, not dead, nor has he attained Parinibbāna. What person do the Buddhas say he is? This is a question considered by the skillful.

Ubbhakkhake na vadāmi, adho nābhiṃ vivajjiya;

Methunadhammapaccayā, kathaṃ pārājiko siyā;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

I do not speak with reference to the Pārājika offense incurred in the oral passage above the collarbone, and avoiding the passages below the navel; how, on account of the act of sexual intercourse in another part of the body, could one fall into a Pārājika offense? This is a question considered by the skillful.

Bhikkhu saññācikāya kuṭiṃ karoti;

Adesitavatthukaṃ pamāṇātikkantaṃ;

Sārambhaṃ aparikkamanaṃ anāpatti;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

A monk builds a hut with materials obtained by his own request; it has an unindicated site, exceeds the standard measurements, is subject to dangers, and lacks a surrounding open space. There is no offense. This is a question considered by the skillful.

Bhikkhu [M 0.0374] saññācikāya kuṭiṃ karoti;

Desitavatthukaṃ pamāṇikaṃ;

Anārambhaṃ saparikkamanaṃ āpatti;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

A monk builds a hut with materials obtained by his own request; it has an indicated site, is of the standard measurements, is not subject to dangers, and has a surrounding open space. There is an offense. This is a question considered by the skillful.

Na kāyikaṃ kiñci payogamācare;

Na cāpi vācāya pare bhaṇeyya;

Āpajjeyya garukaṃ chejjavatthuṃ;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

He would not commit any bodily transgression, nor would he speak to others with his voice; yet he would fall into a grave offense, a matter for expulsion. This is a question considered by the skillful.

Na kāyikaṃ vācasikañca kiñci;

Manasāpi santo na kareyya pāpaṃ;

So [T 0.0530] nāsito kinti sunāsito bhave;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

He would do no evil deed, bodily or verbal, nor any evil deed even with the mind; being so, if that person is destroyed, how could he be said to be well destroyed? This is a question considered by the skillful.

Anālapanto manujena kenaci;

Vācāgiraṃ no ca pare bhaṇeyya;

Āpajjeyya [P 5.0217][V 0.0399] vācasikaṃ na kāyikaṃ;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

Not speaking with any person, nor uttering a sound with reference to others, he would fall into an offense of speech, but not a bodily one. This is a question considered by the skillful.

Sikkhāpadā buddhavarena vaṇṇitā;

Saṅghādisesā caturo bhaveyyuṃ;

Āpajjeyya ekapayogena sabbe;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

There are four training rules called Saṅghādisesa, taught by the excellent Buddha. Could one fall into all of them with a single act? This is a question considered by the skillful.

Ubho ekato upasampannā;

Ubhinnaṃ hatthato cīvaraṃ paṭiggaṇheyya;

Siyā āpattiyo nānā;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

Two bhikkhunīs are each ordained from one Saṅgha only. If a monk were to receive a robe from the hands of both, would there be various offenses for him? This is a question considered by the skillful.

Caturo janā saṃvidhāya;

Garubhaṇḍaṃ avāharuṃ;

Tayo pārājikā eko na pārājiko;

Pañhā [T 0.0531] mesā kusalehi cintitā.

Four monks, having conspired together, stole a heavy item. Three of them fall into a Pārājika offense, but one does not. This is a question considered by the skillful.

2. Pārājikādipañhā

2. Questions Concerning Pārājika and Other Matters

480.

480.

Itthī [M 0.0375] ca abbhantare siyā,

Bhikkhu ca bahiddhā siyā;

Chiddaṃ tasmiṃ ghare natthi;

Methunadhammapaccayā;

Kathaṃ pārājiko siyā;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

A woman might be inside, and a bhikkhu might be outside; in that house, there is no opening. On account of sexual intercourse, how could he incur a pārājika offense? This is a question considered by the skillful.

Telaṃ madhuṃ phāṇitañcāpi sappiṃ;

Sāmaṃ gahetvāna nikkhipeyya;

Avītivatte [V 0.0400] sattāhe;

Sati paccaye paribhuñjantassa āpatti;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

Having received for oneself oil, honey, molasses, and also ghee, one might store it. Before seven days have passed, if there is a reason, an offense is incurred by the one who partakes of it. This is a question considered by the skillful.

Nissaggiyena āpatti;

Suddhakena pācittiyaṃ;

Āpajjantassa ekato;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

An offense of forfeiture together with an offense entailing confession; how could one incur them simultaneously? This is a question considered by the skillful.

Bhikkhū siyā vīsatiyā samāgatā;

Kammaṃ kareyyuṃ samaggasaññino;

Bhikkhu siyā dvādasayojane ṭhito;

Kammañca taṃ kuppeyya vaggapaccayā;

Pañhā [T 0.0532] mesā kusalehi cintitā.

Twenty bhikkhus might be gathered together; perceiving it as a complete assembly, they might perform a formal act. A bhikkhu might be standing twelve yojanas away; and would that formal act be invalid on account of being an incomplete quorum? This is a question considered by the skillful.

Padavītihāramattena vācāya bhaṇitena ca;

Sabbāni garukāni sappaṭikammāni;

Catusaṭṭhi āpattiyo āpajjeyya ekato;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

By the mere measure of a footstep and by a spoken utterance, could one incur at once all sixty-four grave, remediable offenses? This is a question considered by the skillful.

Nivattho antaravāsakena;

Diguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ pāruto;

Sabbāni tāni nissaggiyāni honti;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

Wearing the inner robe, and draped in the double-layered outer robe; do all of those robes become subject to forfeiture? This is a question considered by the skillful.

Na [M 0.0376] cāpi ñatti na ca pana kammavācā;

Na cehi bhikkhūti jino avoca;

Saraṇagamanampi na tassa atthi;

Upasampadā cassa akuppā;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

There is no motion, and no formal act; nor did the Conqueror say, 'Come, bhikkhu!' That person has not even gone for refuge, yet their ordination is unshakeable. This is a question considered by the skillful.

Itthiṃ [V 0.0401] hane na mātaraṃ, purisañca na pitaraṃ hane;

Haneyya anariyaṃ mando, tena cānantaraṃ phuse;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

One might kill a woman who is not one's mother, and a man who is not one's father. A foolish person might kill a non-noble one, and thereby commit an act with immediate result. This is a question considered by the skillful.

Itthiṃ hane ca mātaraṃ, purisañca pitaraṃ hane;

Mātaraṃ pitaraṃ hantvā, na tenānantaraṃ phuse;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

One might kill a woman who is one's mother, and a man who is one's father. Having killed mother and father, one does not thereby commit an act with immediate result. This is a question considered by the skillful.

Acodayitvā [P 5.0218] assārayitvā;

Asammukhībhūtassa kareyya kammaṃ;

Katañca kammaṃ sukataṃ bhaveyya;

Kārako [T 0.0533] ca saṅgho anāpattiko siyā;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

Without admonishing and without reminding, one might perform a formal act for someone who is not present; and the act performed would be well-performed, and the Saṅgha performing it would be without offense. This is a question considered by the skillful.

Codayitvā sārayitvā;

Sammukhībhūtassa kareyya kammaṃ;

Katañca kammaṃ akataṃ bhaveyya;

Kārako ca saṅgho sāpattiko siyā;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

Having admonished and having reminded, one might perform a formal act for someone who is present; and the act performed would be invalid, and the Saṅgha performing it would incur an offense. This is a question considered by the skillful.

Chindantassa āpatti, chindantassa anāpatti;

Chādentassa āpatti, chādentassa anāpatti;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

For one who cuts, there is an offense; for one who cuts, there is no offense. For one who covers, there is an offense; for one who covers, there is no offense. This question has been considered by the wise.

Saccaṃ bhaṇanto garukaṃ, musā ca lahu bhāsato;

Musā bhaṇanto garukaṃ, saccañca lahu bhāsato;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

Speaking the truth, one incurs a grave offense; and speaking falsehood, a light one. Speaking falsehood, one incurs a grave offense; and speaking the truth, a light one. This question has been considered by the wise.
