3. Questions on Pācittiya and so forth

481.

481.

Adhiṭṭhitaṃ [M 0.0377][V 0.0402] rajanāya rattaṃ;

Kappakatampi santaṃ;

Paribhuñjantassa āpatti;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

For one who uses a robe that has been determined, dyed with dye, and also marked with the kappa-bindu, there is an offense. This question has been considered by the wise.

Atthaṅgate sūriye bhikkhu maṃsāni khādati;

Na ummattako na ca pana khittacitto;

Na cāpi so vedanāṭṭo bhaveyya;

Na cassa hoti āpatti;

So ca dhammo sugatena desito;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

When the sun has set, a monk chews meat. He would not be insane, nor of distracted mind, nor would he be afflicted by pain. And for him there is no offense. And that principle was taught by the Sugata. This question has been considered by the wise.

Na rattacitto na ca pana theyyacitto;

Na cāpi so paraṃ maraṇāya cetayi;

Salākaṃ [T 0.0534] dentassa hoti chejjaṃ;

Paṭiggaṇhantassa thullaccayaṃ;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

He is not of lustful mind, nor is he of thievish mind, nor did he intend another's death. For the one giving the voting ticket, there is a cutting off; for the one receiving it, a grave offense. This question has been considered by the wise.

Na cāpi āraññakaṃ sāsaṅkasammataṃ;

Na cāpi saṅghena sammuti dinnā;

Na cassa kathinaṃ atthataṃ tattheva;

Cīvaraṃ nikkhipitvā gaccheyya aḍḍhayojanaṃ;

Tattheva aruṇaṃ uggacchantassa anāpatti;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

Nor is it a forest dwelling designated as dangerous, nor has permission been given by the Saṅgha, nor for him has the Kathina been spread. Having left the robe right there, he might go half a yojana; for him, as dawn rises right there, there is no offense. This question has been considered by the wise.

Kāyikāni na vācasikāni;

Sabbāni nānāvatthukāni;

Apubbaṃ [V 0.0403] acarimaṃ āpajjeyya ekato;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

Bodily, not verbal; all offenses of various grounds. One might incur them simultaneously, all together. This question has been considered by the wise.

Vācasikāni na kāyikāni;

Sabbāni nānāvatthukāni;

Apubbaṃ acarimaṃ āpajjeyya ekato;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

Verbal, not bodily; all offenses of various grounds. One might incur them simultaneously, all together. This question has been considered by the wise.

Tissitthiyo [M 0.0378] methunaṃ taṃ na seve;

Tayo purise tayo anariyapaṇḍake;

Na cācare methunaṃ byañjanasmiṃ;

Chejjaṃ [T 0.0535] siyā methunadhammapaccayā;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

He does not engage in sexual intercourse with three women, nor with three men, nor with three ignoble paṇḍakas. Nor does he practice sexual intercourse in his own organ. Yet a cutting off may occur on account of the act of sexual intercourse. This question has been considered by the wise.

Mātaraṃ cīvaraṃ yāce, no ca saṅghe no saṃghassa (ka.), no ca saṃghassa (syā.), no ce saṃghassa (sī.) pariṇataṃ;

Kenassa hoti āpatti, anāpatti ca ñātake;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

He asks his mother for a robe, and it is not dedicated to the Saṅgha. By what is there an offense for him, when in the case of a relative there is no offense? This question has been considered by the wise.

Kuddho [P 5.0219] ārādhako hoti, kuddho hoti garahiyo;

Atha ko nāma so dhammo, yena kuddho pasaṃsiyo;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

An angry person is one who pleases; an angry person is blameworthy. What then is that principle by which an angry person is praiseworthy? This question has been considered by the wise.

Tuṭṭho ārādhako hoti, tuṭṭho hoti garahiyo;

Atha ko nāma so dhammo, yena tuṭṭho garahiyo;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

A pleased person is one who pleases; a pleased person is blameworthy. What then is that principle by which a pleased person is blameworthy? This question has been considered by the wise.

Saṅghādisesaṃ thullaccayaṃ;

Pācittiyaṃ pāṭidesanīyaṃ;

Dukkaṭaṃ āpajjeyya ekato;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

A saṅghādisesa, a thullaccaya, a pācittiya, a pāṭidesanīya, and a dukkaṭa offense, one might incur at once. This question has been considered by the wise.

Ubho [V 0.0404] paripuṇṇavīsativassā;

Ubhinnaṃ ekupajjhāyo;

Ekācariyo ekā kammavācā;

Eko upasampanno eko anupasampanno;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

Both are of fully twenty years; for both there is one preceptor, one teacher, and one formal act. One is ordained, one is not ordained. This question has been considered by the wise.

Akappakataṃ nāpi rajanāya rattaṃ;

Tena [T 0.0536] nivattho yena kāmaṃ vajeyya;

Na cassa hoti āpatti;

So ca dhammo sugatena desito;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

Not made allowable, nor dyed with dye; having worn that, he may go wherever he wishes. And for him there is no offense; and that principle was taught by the Well-farer. This question has been considered by the wise.

Na [M 0.0379] deti na paṭiggaṇhāti, paṭiggaho tena na vijjati;

Āpajjati garukaṃ na lahukaṃ, tañca paribhogapaccayā;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

One does not give, one does not receive; thereby, receiving does not exist. One incurs a serious offense, not a minor one, and that on account of consumption. This question has been considered by the wise.

Na deti na paṭiggaṇhāti, paṭiggaho tena na vijjati;

Āpajjati lahukaṃ na garukaṃ, tañca paribhogapaccayā;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

One does not give, one does not receive; thereby, receiving does not exist. One incurs a minor offense, not a serious one, and that on account of consumption. This question has been considered by the wise.

Āpajjati garukaṃ sāvasesaṃ;

Chādeti anādariyaṃ paṭicca;

Na bhikkhunī no ca phuseyya vajjaṃ;

Pañhā mesā kusalehi cintitā.

One incurs a serious offense with a remainder; one conceals it on account of disrespect. Not a bhikkhunī, and one would not commit the fault. This question has been considered by the wise.

Sedamocanagāthā niṭṭhitā.

The Sweat-Releasing Verses are concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Asaṃvāso [T 0.0537] avissajji, dasa ca anukkhittako;

Upeti dhammaṃ ubbhakkhakaṃ, tato saññācikā ca dve.

Non-communion, not giving up, ten, and not suspended; approaching the Dhamma, ubbhakkhakaṃ, and then the two on requesting.

Na [V 0.0405] kāyikañca garukaṃ, na kāyikaṃ na vācasikaṃ na kāyikaṃ sunāsitaṃ (syā.);

Anālapanto sikkhā ca, ubho ca caturo janā.

Not bodily and serious, not bodily not verbal; not speaking, and the training rule, both, and four people.

Itthī telañca nissaggi, bhikkhu ca padavītiyo;

Nivattho ca na ca ñatti, na mātaraṃ pitaraṃ hane.

Woman, oil, and forfeiture; a bhikkhu and a footstep; clothed, and not a motion; not mother, killing father.

Acodayitvā codayitvā, chindantaṃ saccameva ca;

Adhiṭṭhitañcatthaṅgate, na rattaṃ na cāraññakaṃ.

Without admonishing, having admonished; cutting, and truth indeed; determined, and when the sun has set; not of lustful mind, and not a forest dwelling.

Kāyikā vācasikā ca, tissitthī cāpi mātaraṃ;

Kuddho ārādhako tuṭṭho, saṅghādisesā ca ubho.

Bodily, and verbal; three women, and also mother; an angry person who pleases, a pleased person; saṅghādisesa, and both.

Akappakataṃ na deti, na detāpajjatī garuṃ;

Sedamocanikā gāthā, pañhā viññūhi vibhāvitāti viññūvibhāvitā (sī. syā.).

The Akappakataṃ verse, the Na deti verse, the other Na deti verse, and the Āpajjati garuṃ verse; these sweat-inducing verses—the problems—have thus been made clear by the wise.

Pañcavaggo

The Fifth Chapter

1. Kammavaggo

1. The Chapter on Acts

482. Cattāri [T 0.0538][P 5.0220][M 0.0380][V 0.0406] kammāni. Apalokanakammaṃ, ñattikammaṃ, ñattidutiyakammaṃ, ñatticatutthakammaṃ – imāni cattāri kammāni. Katihākārehi vipajjanti? Imāni cattāri kammāni pañcahākārehi vipajjanti – vatthuto vā ñattito vā anussāvanato vā sīmato vā parisato vā.

482. There are four acts: the act of announcement, the act with a motion, the act with a motion and one proclamation, and the act with a motion and three proclamations—these are the four acts. In how many ways do they fail? These four acts fail in five ways: due to the object, due to the motion, due to the proclamation, due to the boundary, or due to the assembly.

483. Kathaṃ vatthuto kammāni vipajjanti? Sammukhākaraṇīyaṃ kammaṃ asammukhā karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ; paṭipucchākaraṇīyaṃ kammaṃ apaṭipucchā karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ; paṭiññāya karaṇīyaṃ kammaṃ apaṭiññāya karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ; sativinayārahassa amūḷhavinayaṃ deti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ; amūḷhavinayārahassa tassapāpiyasikākammaṃ karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ; tassapāpiyasikākammārahassa tajjanīyakammaṃ karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ; tajjanīyakammārahassa niyassakammaṃ karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ; niyassakammārahassa pabbājanīyakammaṃ karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ; pabbājanīyakammārahassa paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ; paṭisāraṇīyakammārahassa ukkhepanīyakammaṃ karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ; ukkhepanīyakammārahassa parivāsaṃ deti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ[T 0.0539]; parivāsārahaṃ mūlāya paṭikassati, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ; mūlāyapaṭikassanārahassa mānattaṃ deti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ; mānattārahaṃ abbheti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ; abbhānārahaṃ upasampādeti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ; anuposathe uposathaṃ karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ; apavāraṇāya pavāreti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Evaṃ vatthuto kammāni vipajjanti.

483. How do formal acts lapse due to the object? A formal act that should be performed face to face is performed not face to face: this is an invalid formal act regarding the object, an unlawful act. A formal act that should be performed after questioning is performed without questioning: this is an invalid formal act regarding the object, an unlawful act. A formal act that should be performed with acknowledgement is performed without acknowledgement: this is an invalid formal act regarding the object, an unlawful act. One gives the verdict of past insanity to one who deserves the verdict of mindfulness: this is an invalid formal act regarding the object, an unlawful act. One performs the act of further punishment for one who deserves the verdict of past insanity: this is an invalid formal act regarding the object, an unlawful act. One performs the act of rebuke for one who deserves the act of further punishment: this is an invalid formal act regarding the object, an unlawful act. One performs the act of subordination for one who deserves the act of rebuke: this is an invalid formal act regarding the object, an unlawful act. One performs the act of banishment for one who deserves the act of subordination: this is an invalid formal act regarding the object, an unlawful act. One performs the act of reconciliation for one who deserves the act of banishment: this is an invalid formal act regarding the object, an unlawful act. One performs the act of suspension for one who deserves the act of reconciliation: this is an invalid formal act regarding the object, an unlawful act. One gives probation to one who deserves the act of suspension: this is an invalid formal act regarding the object, an unlawful act. One sends back to the beginning one who deserves probation: this is an invalid formal act regarding the object, an unlawful act. One gives penance to one who deserves being sent back to the beginning: this is an invalid formal act regarding the object, an unlawful act. One rehabilitates one who deserves penance: this is an invalid formal act regarding the object, an unlawful act. One gives higher ordination to one who deserves rehabilitation: this is an invalid formal act regarding the object, an unlawful act. One performs the Uposatha on a non-Uposatha day: this is an invalid formal act regarding the object, an unlawful act. One performs the Pavāraṇā on a non-Pavāraṇā day: this is an invalid formal act regarding the object, an unlawful act. Thus, formal acts lapse due to the object.

484. Kathaṃ [V 0.0407] ñattito kammāni vipajjanti? Pañcahākārehi ñattito kammāni vipajjanti – vatthuṃ na parāmasati, saṅghaṃ na parāmasati, puggalaṃ na parāmasati, ñattiṃ na parāmasati, pacchā vā ñattiṃ ṭhapeti – imehi pañcahākārehi ñattito kammāni vipajjanti.

484. How do formal acts lapse due to the motion? Formal acts lapse due to the motion in five ways: one does not refer to the object, one does not refer to the Sangha, one does not refer to the individual, one does not refer to the motion, or one places the motion afterward—in these five ways, formal acts lapse due to the motion.

485. Kathaṃ [M 0.0381] anussāvanato kammāni vipajjanti? Pañcahākārehi [P 5.0221] anussāvanato kammāni vipajjanti – vatthuṃ na parāmasati, saṅghaṃ na parāmasati, puggalaṃ na parāmasati, sāvanaṃ hāpeti, akāle vā sāveti – imehi pañcahākārehi anussāvanato kammāni vipajjanti.

485. How do formal acts lapse due to the proclamation? Formal acts lapse due to the proclamation in five ways: one does not refer to the object, one does not refer to the Sangha, one does not refer to the individual, one omits the proclamation, or one proclaims at the wrong time—in these five ways, formal acts lapse due to the proclamation.

486. Kathaṃ sīmato kammāni vipajjanti? Ekādasahi ākārehi sīmato kammāni vipajjanti – atikhuddakaṃ sīmaṃ sammannati, atimahatiṃ sīmaṃ sammannati, khaṇḍanimittaṃ sīmaṃ sammannati, chāyānimittaṃ sīmaṃ [T 0.0540] sammannati, animittaṃ sīmaṃ sammannati, bahisīme ṭhito sīmaṃ sammannati, nadiyā sīmaṃ sammannati, samudde sīmaṃ sammannati, jātassare sīmaṃ sammannati, sīmāya sīmaṃ sambhindati, sīmāya sīmaṃ ajjhottharati – imehi ekādasahi ākārehi sīmato kammāni vipajjanti.

486. How do formal acts lapse because of the boundary? Formal acts lapse because of the boundary in eleven ways: by designating a boundary that is too small, by designating a boundary that is too large, by designating a boundary with broken markers, by designating a boundary with shadow markers, by designating a boundary without markers, by standing outside the boundary while designating it, by designating a boundary in a river, by designating a boundary in the ocean, by designating a boundary in a natural lake, by connecting a boundary with another boundary, by overlapping a boundary with another boundary—in these eleven ways, formal acts lapse because of the boundary.

487. Kathaṃ parisato kammāni vipajjanti? Dvādasahi ākārehi parisato kammāni vipajjanti – catuvaggakaraṇe kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammapattā te anāgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando anāhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti, catuvaggakaraṇe kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammapattā te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando anāhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti, catuvaggakaraṇe kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammapattā te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando āhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti. Pañcavaggakaraṇe kamme…pe… dasavaggakaraṇe kamme…pe… vīsativaggakaraṇe kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammapattā te anāgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando anāhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti, vīsativaggakaraṇe kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammapattā, te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando anāhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti, vīsativaggakaraṇe kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammapattā, te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ [T 0.0541] chando āhaṭo hoti sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti – imehi dvādasahi ākārehi parisato kammāni vipajjanti.

487. How do formal acts lapse on account of the assembly? Formal acts lapse on account of the assembly in twelve ways. In a formal act requiring a quorum of four: the bhikkhus qualified for the act are not present, the consent of those eligible to give consent has not been conveyed, and those present object; or the bhikkhus qualified for the act are present, the consent of those eligible to give consent has not been conveyed, and those present object; or the bhikkhus qualified for the act are present, the consent of those eligible to give consent has been conveyed, and those present object. The same applies to a formal act requiring a quorum of five... and to one requiring a quorum of ten... In a formal act requiring a quorum of twenty: the bhikkhus qualified for the act are not present, the consent of those eligible to give consent has not been conveyed, and those present object; or the bhikkhus qualified for the act are present, the consent of those eligible to give consent has not been conveyed, and those present object; or the bhikkhus qualified for the act are present, the consent of those eligible to give consent has been conveyed, and those present object. In these twelve ways, formal acts lapse on account of the assembly.

488. Catuvaggakaraṇe kamme cattāro bhikkhū pakatattā kammapattā, avasesā pakatattā chandārahā[V 0.0408]. Yassa saṅgho kammaṃ karoti so neva kammapatto nāpi chandāraho, api ca kammāraho. Pañcavaggakaraṇe [M 0.0382] kamme pañca bhikkhū pakatattā kammapattā, avasesā pakatattā chandārahā. Yassa saṅgho kammaṃ karoti so neva kammapatto nāpi chandāraho, api ca kammāraho. Dasavaggakaraṇe kamme dasa bhikkhū pakatattā kammapattā, avasesā pakatattā chandārahā. Yassa saṅgho kammaṃ karoti so neva kammapatto nāpi chandāraho, api ca kammāraho. Vīsativaggakaraṇe kamme vīsati bhikkhū pakatattā kammapattā, avasesā pakatattā chandārahā. Yassa saṅgho kammaṃ karoti so neva kammapatto nāpi chandāraho, api ca kammāraho.

488. In a formal act requiring a quorum of four, four bhikkhus of normal standing are qualified for the act; the remaining bhikkhus of normal standing are eligible to give consent. The bhikkhu upon whom the Saṅgha performs the act is neither qualified for the act nor eligible to give consent, but is indeed subject to the act. In a formal act requiring a quorum of five, five bhikkhus of normal standing are qualified for the act; the remaining bhikkhus of normal standing are eligible to give consent. The bhikkhu upon whom the Saṅgha performs the act is neither qualified for the act nor eligible to give consent, but is indeed subject to the act. In a formal act requiring a quorum of ten, ten bhikkhus of normal standing are qualified for the act; the remaining bhikkhus of normal standing are eligible to give consent. The bhikkhu upon whom the Saṅgha performs the act is neither qualified for the act nor eligible to give consent, but is indeed subject to the act. In a formal act requiring a quorum of twenty, twenty bhikkhus of normal standing are qualified for the act; the remaining bhikkhus of normal standing are eligible to give consent. The bhikkhu upon whom the Saṅgha performs the act is neither qualified for the act nor eligible to give consent, but is indeed subject to the act.

489. Cattāri [P 5.0222] kammāni – apalokanakammaṃ, ñattikammaṃ, ñattidutiyakammaṃ, ñatticatutthakammaṃ. Imāni cattāri kammāni katihākārehi vipajjanti? Imāni cattāri kammāni pañcahākārehi vipajjanti – vatthuto vā ñattito vā anussāvanato vā sīmato vā parisato vā.

489. There are four formal acts: the act of announcement, the act with a motion, the act with a motion and one proclamation, and the act with a motion and three proclamations. In how many ways do these four formal acts fail? These four formal acts fail in five ways: due to the basis, or due to the motion, or due to the proclamation, or due to the boundary, or due to the assembly.

490. Kathaṃ vatthuto kammāni vipajjanti? Paṇḍakaṃ upasampādeti[T 0.0542], vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Theyyasaṃvāsakaṃ upasampādeti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Titthiyapakkantakaṃ upasampādeti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Tiracchānagataṃ upasampādeti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Mātughātakaṃ upasampādeti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Pitughātakaṃ upasampādeti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Arahantaghātakaṃ upasampādeti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Bhikkhunidūsakaṃ upasampādeti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Saṅghabhedakaṃ upasampādeti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Lohituppādakaṃ upasampādeti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Ubhatobyañjanaṃ upasampādeti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Ūnavīsativassaṃ puggalaṃ upasampādeti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ. Evaṃ vatthuto kammāni vipajjanti.

490. How do formal acts fail on account of the basis? If one ordains a paṇḍaka, it is an unlawful act with a flawed basis. If one ordains one who lives in communion by theft, it is an unlawful act with a flawed basis. If one ordains one who has gone over to the heretics, it is an unlawful act with a flawed basis. If one ordains an animal, it is an unlawful act with a flawed basis. If one ordains a matricide, it is an unlawful act with a flawed basis. If one ordains a patricide, it is an unlawful act with a flawed basis. If one ordains a murderer of an Arahant, it is an unlawful act with a flawed basis. If one ordains a defiler of a bhikkhunī, it is an unlawful act with a flawed basis. If one ordains a schismatic, it is an unlawful act with a flawed basis. If one ordains one who has caused the Buddha's blood to flow, it is an unlawful act with a flawed basis. If one ordains one with both male and female characteristics, it is an unlawful act with a flawed basis. If one ordains a person under twenty years of age, it is an unlawful act with a flawed basis. Thus, formal acts fail on account of the basis.

491. Kathaṃ ñattito kammāni vipajjanti? Pañcahākārehi ñattito kammāni vipajjanti. Vatthuṃ na parāmasati, saṅghaṃ na parāmasati, puggalaṃ na parāmasati, ñattiṃ na parāmasati, pacchā vā ñattiṃ ṭhapeti – imehi pañcahākārehi ñattito kammāni vipajjanti.

491. How do formal acts fail on account of the motion? Formal acts fail on account of the motion in five ways: not referring to the basis, not referring to the Saṅgha, not referring to the individual, not referring to the motion, or proposing the motion afterward—in these five ways formal acts fail on account of the motion.

492. Kathaṃ anussāvanato kammāni vipajjanti? Pañcahākārehi anussāvanato kammāni vipajjanti – vatthuṃ na parāmasati, saṅghaṃ na parāmasati, puggalaṃ [M 0.0383] na parāmasati, sāvanaṃ [V 0.0409] hāpeti, akāle vā sāveti – imehi pañcahākārehi anussāvanato kammāni [T 0.0543] vipajjanti.

492. How do formal acts fail on account of the proclamation? Formal acts fail on account of the proclamation in five ways: not referring to the basis, not referring to the Saṅgha, not referring to the individual, omitting the proclamation, or proclaiming at the wrong time—in these five ways formal acts fail on account of the proclamation.

493. Kathaṃ sīmato kammāni vipajjanti? Ekādasahi ākārehi sīmato kammāni vipajjanti. Atikhuddakaṃ sīmaṃ sammannati, atimahatiṃ sīmaṃ sammannati, khaṇḍanimittaṃ sīmaṃ sammannati, chāyānimittaṃ sīmaṃ sammannati, animittaṃ sīmaṃ sammannati, bahisīme ṭhito sīmaṃ sammannati, nadiyā sīmaṃ sammannati, samudde sīmaṃ sammannati, jātassare sīmaṃ sammannati, sīmāya sīmaṃ sambhindati, sīmāya sīmaṃ ajjhottharati – imehi ekādasahi ākārehi sīmato kammāni vipajjanti.

493. How do formal acts fail on account of the boundary? Formal acts fail on account of the boundary in eleven ways: designating a boundary that is too small; designating a boundary that is too large; designating a boundary with broken markers; designating a boundary with shadow markers; designating a boundary without markers; designating a boundary while standing outside it; designating a boundary in a river; designating a boundary in the ocean; designating a boundary in a natural lake; connecting a boundary with another boundary; or encroaching upon a boundary with another boundary. In these eleven ways, formal acts fail on account of the boundary.

494. Kathaṃ parisato kammāni vipajjanti? Dvādasahi ākārehi parisato kammāni vipajjanti – catuvaggakaraṇe kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammapattā te anāgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando anāhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti, catuvaggakaraṇe kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammapattā te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando anāhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti. Catuvaggakaraṇe kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammapattā te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando āhaṭo hoti sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti. Pañcavaggakaraṇe kamme…pe… dasavaggakaraṇe kamme…pe… vīsativaggakaraṇe kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammapattā te [T 0.0544] anāgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando anāhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti. Vīsativaggakaraṇe kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammapattā te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando anāhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti. Vīsativaggakaraṇe kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammapattā te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando āhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti – imehi dvādasahi ākārehi parisato kammāni vipajjanti.

494. How do formal acts fail on account of the assembly? Formal acts fail on account of the assembly in twelve ways. In a formal act requiring a quorum of four: the bhikkhus fit for the act have not arrived, the consent of those entitled to give it has not been brought, and those who are present protest. In a formal act requiring a quorum of four: the bhikkhus fit for the act have arrived, the consent of those entitled to give it has not been brought, and those who are present protest. In a formal act requiring a quorum of four: the bhikkhus fit for the act have arrived, the consent of those entitled to give it has been brought, and those who are present protest. In a formal act requiring a quorum of five... and so on... in a formal act requiring a quorum of ten... and so on... In a formal act requiring a quorum of twenty: the bhikkhus fit for the act have not arrived, the consent of those entitled to give it has not been brought, and those who are present protest. In a formal act requiring a quorum of twenty: the bhikkhus fit for the act have arrived, the consent of those entitled to give it has not been brought, and those who are present protest. In a formal act requiring a quorum of twenty: the bhikkhus fit for the act have arrived, the consent of those entitled to give it has been brought, and those who are present protest. In these twelve ways, formal acts fail on account of the assembly.

495. Apalokanakammaṃ kati ṭhānāni gacchati? Ñattikammaṃ kati ṭhānāni gacchati? Ñattidutiyakammaṃ kati ṭhānāni gacchati? Ñatticatutthakammaṃ kati ṭhānāni gacchati? Apalokanakammaṃ pañca ṭhānāni gacchati. Ñattikammaṃ nava ṭhānāni gacchati. Ñattidutiyakammaṃ satta ṭhānāni gacchati. Ñatticatutthakammaṃ satta ṭhānāni gacchati.

495. How many instances does a formal act of announcement extend to? How many instances does a formal act with a motion extend to? How many instances does a formal act with a motion and one proclamation extend to? How many instances does a formal act with a motion and three proclamations extend to? A formal act of announcement extends to five instances. A formal act with a motion extends to nine instances. A formal act with a motion and one proclamation extends to seven instances. A formal act with a motion and three proclamations extends to seven instances.

496. Apalokanakammaṃ [M 0.0384] katamāni pañca ṭhānāni gacchati? Osāraṇaṃ, nissāraṇaṃ, bhaṇḍukammaṃ, brahmadaṇḍaṃ, kammalakkhaṇaññeva pañcamaṃ – apalokanakammaṃ imāni pañca ṭhānāni gacchati[V 0.0410]. Ñattikammaṃ katamāni nava ṭhānāni gacchati? Osāraṇaṃ, nissāraṇaṃ, uposathaṃ, pavāraṇaṃ, sammutiṃ, dānaṃ, paṭiggahaṃ, paccukkaḍḍhanaṃ, kammalakkhaṇaññeva navamaṃ – ñattikammaṃ imāni nava ṭhānāni gacchati. Ñattidutiyakammaṃ katamāni satta ṭhānāni gacchati? Osāraṇaṃ, nissāraṇaṃ, sammutiṃ, dānaṃ, uddharaṇaṃ, desanaṃ, kammalakkhaṇaññeva sattamaṃ – ñattidutiyakammaṃ imāni satta ṭhānāni gacchati. Ñatticatutthakammaṃ [T 0.0545] katamāni satta ṭhānāni gacchati? Osāraṇaṃ, nissāraṇaṃ, sammutiṃ, dānaṃ, niggahaṃ, samanubhāsanaṃ, kammalakkhaṇaññeva sattamaṃ – ñatticatutthakammaṃ imāni satta ṭhānāni gacchati.

496. To what five instances does an act by announcement extend? Reinstatement, expulsion, the act of shaving the head, the Brahma-penalty, and the characteristic of the act itself as the fifth—an act by announcement extends to these five instances. To what nine instances does an act by motion extend? Reinstatement, expulsion, the Uposatha, the Pavāraṇā, authorization, donation, confession of an offense, withdrawal of the Pavāraṇā, and the characteristic of the act itself as the ninth—an act by motion extends to these nine instances. To what seven instances does an act by motion and one proclamation extend? Reinstatement, expulsion, authorization, donation, withdrawal of the Kathina, announcement of a site, and the characteristic of the act itself as the seventh—an act by motion and one proclamation extends to these seven instances. To what seven instances does an act by motion and three proclamations extend? Reinstatement, expulsion, authorization, the granting of probation or penance, censure, formal admonition, and the characteristic of the act itself as the seventh—an act by motion and three proclamations extends to these seven instances.

497. Catuvaggakaraṇe kamme cattāro bhikkhū pakatattā kammapattā, avasesā pakatattā chandārahā. Yassa saṅgho kammaṃ karoti so neva kammapatto nāpi chandāraho, api ca kammāraho. Pañcavaggakaraṇe [P 5.0223] kamme pañca bhikkhū pakatattā kammapattā, avasesā pakatattā chandārahā. Yassa saṅgho kammaṃ karoti so neva kammapatto nāpi chandāraho, api ca kammāraho. Dasavaggakaraṇe kamme dasa bhikkhū pakatattā kammapattā, avasesā pakatattā chandārahā. Yassa saṅgho kammaṃ karoti so neva kammapatto nāpi chandāraho, api ca kammāraho. Vīsativaggakaraṇe kamme vīsati bhikkhū pakatattā kammapattā, avasesā pakatattā chandārahā. Yassa saṅgho kammaṃ karoti so neva kammapatto nāpi chandāraho, api ca kammāraho.

497. In an act to be performed by a chapter of four, four monks of normal standing are fit for the act; the remaining monks of normal standing are worthy of giving consent. The one for whom the Saṅgha performs the act is neither fit for the act nor worthy of giving consent, but indeed is the subject of the act. In an act to be performed by a chapter of five, five monks of normal standing are fit for the act; the remaining monks of normal standing are worthy of giving consent. The one for whom the Saṅgha performs the act is neither fit for the act nor worthy of giving consent, but indeed is the subject of the act. In an act to be performed by a chapter of ten, ten monks of normal standing are fit for the act; the remaining monks of normal standing are worthy of giving consent. The one for whom the Saṅgha performs the act is neither fit for the act nor worthy of giving consent, but indeed is the subject of the act. In an act to be performed by a chapter of twenty, twenty monks of normal standing are fit for the act; the remaining monks of normal standing are worthy of giving consent. The one for whom the Saṅgha performs the act is neither fit for the act nor worthy of giving consent, but indeed is the subject of the act.

Kammavaggo niṭṭhito paṭhamo.

The first Chapter on Acts is finished.

2. Atthavasavaggo

2. 2. The Chapter on Benefits

498. a. ni. 2.201-230 Dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ. Saṅghasuṭṭhutāya, saṅghaphāsutāya – ime dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ. Dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ. Dummaṅkūnaṃ puggalānaṃ niggahāya, pesalānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ phāsuvihārāya – ime dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgate [M 0.0385] sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ. Dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ. Diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ āsavānaṃ saṃvarāya, samparāyikānaṃ āsavānaṃ paṭighātāya – ime [T 0.0546] dve [V 0.0411] atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ. Dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ. Diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ verānaṃ saṃvarāya, samparāyikānaṃ verānaṃ paṭighātāya – ime dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ. Dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ. Diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ vajjānaṃ saṃvarāya, samparāyikānaṃ vajjānaṃ paṭighātāya – ime dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ. Dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ. Diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ bhayānaṃ saṃvarāya, samparāyikānaṃ bhayānaṃ paṭighātāya – ime dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ. Dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ. Diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ saṃvarāya, samparāyikānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ paṭighātāya – ime dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ. Dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ. Gihīnaṃ anukampāya, pāpicchānaṃ pakkhupacchedāya – ime dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ. Dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ. Appasannānaṃ pasādāya, pasannānaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya – ime dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ. Dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena [T 0.0547] sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ. Saddhammaṭṭhitiyā, vinayānuggahāya – ime dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ.

498. On account of two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the training rule for the disciples: for the excellence of the Saṅgha, for the comfort of the Saṅgha. On account of these two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the training rule for the disciples. On account of two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the training rule for the disciples: for the subduing of immoral individuals, for the comfortable abiding of virtuous bhikkhus. On account of these two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the training rule for the disciples. On account of two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the training rule for the disciples: for the restraint of taints in the present life, for the dispelling of taints in the future life. On account of these two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the training rule for the disciples. On account of two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the training rule for the disciples: for the restraint of enmities in the present life, for the dispelling of enmities in the future life. On account of these two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the training rule for the disciples. On account of two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the training rule for the disciples: for the restraint of faults in the present life, for the dispelling of faults in the future life. On account of these two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the training rule for the disciples. On account of two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the training rule for the disciples: for the restraint of dangers in the present life, for the dispelling of dangers in the future life. On account of these two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the training rule for the disciples. On account of two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the training rule for the disciples: for the restraint of unwholesome states in the present life, for the dispelling of unwholesome states in the future life. On account of these two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the training rule for the disciples. On account of two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the training rule for the disciples: for compassion for householders, for the cutting off of the faction of those with evil desires. On account of these two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the training rule for the disciples. On account of two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the training rule for the disciples: for inspiring faith in the uninspired, for the increase of faith in the inspired. On account of these two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the training rule for the disciples. On account of two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the training rule for the disciples: for the stability of the good Dhamma, for the support of the Vinaya. On account of these two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the training rule for the disciples.

Atthavasavaggo niṭṭhito dutiyo.

The second Chapter on Benefits is finished.

3. Paññattavaggo

3. 3. The Chapter on Formulations

499. Dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ pātimokkhaṃ paññattaṃ…pe… pātimokkhuddeso paññatto… pātimokkhaṭṭhapanaṃ paññattaṃ… pavāraṇā paññattā… pavāraṇāṭhapanaṃ paññattaṃ… tajjanīyakammaṃ paññattaṃ… niyassakammaṃ [M 0.0386] paññattaṃ… pabbājanīyakammaṃ paññattaṃ… paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ paññattaṃ… ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paññattaṃ… parivāsadānaṃ paññattaṃ… mūlāyapaṭikassanā paññattā… mānattadānaṃ paññattaṃ… abbhānaṃ paññattaṃ… osāraṇīyaṃ paññattaṃ… nissāraṇīyaṃ paññattaṃ… upasampadaṃ paññattaṃ… apalokanakammaṃ paññattaṃ… ñattikammaṃ paññattaṃ… ñattidutiyakammaṃ paññattaṃ… ñatticatutthakammaṃ paññattaṃ…pe….

499. On account of two purposes, the Tathāgata has laid down the Pātimokkha for the disciples… and so on… the recital of the Pātimokkha has been laid down… the suspension of the Pātimokkha has been laid down… the Pavāraṇā has been laid down… the suspension of the Pavāraṇā has been laid down… the act of censure has been laid down… the act of subordination has been laid down… the act of banishment has been laid down… the act of reconciliation has been laid down… the act of suspension has been laid down… the granting of probation has been laid down… the sending back to the beginning has been laid down… the granting of penance has been laid down… the rehabilitation has been laid down… the act of reinstatement has been laid down… the act of expulsion has been laid down… the higher ordination has been laid down… the act by announcement has been laid down… the act by motion has been laid down… the act with a motion and one announcement has been laid down… the act with a motion and three announcements has been laid down… and so on.

Paññattavaggo niṭṭhito tatiyo.

The third chapter, the Chapter on Enactments, is finished.

4. Apaññatte paññattavaggo

4. The Chapter on Enactments Regarding the Unenacted

500. …Pe… [V 0.0412] apaññatte paññattaṃ, paññatte anupaññattaṃ…pe… sammukhāvinayo paññatto…pe… sativinayo paññatto…pe… amūḷhavinayo paññatto…pe… paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ [P 5.0224] paññattaṃ…pe… yebhuyyasikā paññattā…pe… tassapāpiyasikā paññattā…pe… tiṇavatthārako paññatto saṅghasuṭṭhutāya, saṅghaphāsutāya – ime dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ [T 0.0548] tiṇavatthārako paññatto. Dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ tiṇavatthārako paññatto. Dummaṅkūnaṃ puggalānaṃ niggahāya, pesalānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ phāsuvihārāya – ime dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ tiṇavatthārako paññatto. Dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ tiṇavatthārako paññatto. Diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ āsavānaṃ saṃvarāya, samparāyikānaṃ āsavānaṃ paṭighātāya – ime dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ tiṇavatthārako paññatto. Dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ tiṇavatthārako paññatto. Diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ verānaṃ saṃvarāya, samparāyikānaṃ verānaṃ paṭighātāya – ime dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ tiṇavatthārako paññatto. Dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ tiṇavatthārako paññatto. Diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ vajjānaṃ saṃvarāya, samparāyikānaṃ vajjānaṃ paṭighātāya – ime dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ tiṇavatthārako paññatto. Dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ tiṇavatthārako paññatto. Diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ bhayānaṃ saṃvarāya, samparāyikānaṃ bhayānaṃ paṭighātāya – ime dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ tiṇavatthārako paññatto. Dve [M 0.0387] atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ tiṇavatthārako paññatto. Diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ saṃvarāya, samparāyikānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ paṭighātāya [T 0.0549] – ime dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ tiṇavatthārako paññatto. Dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ tiṇavatthārako paññatto. Gihīnaṃ anukampāya, pāpicchānaṃ pakkhupacchedāya – ime dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ tiṇavatthārako paññatto. Dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ tiṇavatthārako paññatto. Appasannānaṃ pasādāya, pasannānaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya – ime dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ tiṇavatthārako paññatto. Dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ tiṇavatthārako paññatto. Saddhammaṭṭhitiyā, vinayānuggahāya – ime dve atthavase paṭicca tathāgatena sāvakānaṃ tiṇavatthārako paññatto.

500. …and so on… An enactment was made where there was no enactment; a supplementary enactment was made where there was an enactment… and so on… the settlement in the presence was laid down… and so on… the settlement by mindfulness was laid down… and so on… the settlement for one not insane was laid down… and so on… the acting according to acknowledgement was laid down… and so on… the decision by majority was laid down… and so on… the procedure for one of bad character was laid down… and so on… the covering over with grass was laid down for the Saṅgha’s well-being, for the Saṅgha’s comfort. Depending on these two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the covering over with grass for his disciples. Depending on two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the covering over with grass for his disciples: for the restraint of immoral individuals and for the comfortable abiding of amiable monks. Depending on these two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the covering over with grass for his disciples. Depending on two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the covering over with grass for his disciples: for the restraint of taints in the present life and for the dispelling of taints relating to the future. Depending on these two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the covering over with grass for his disciples. Depending on two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the covering over with grass for his disciples: for the restraint of enmities in the present life and for the dispelling of enmities relating to the future. Depending on these two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the covering over with grass for his disciples. Depending on two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the covering over with grass for his disciples: for the restraint of faults in the present life and for the dispelling of faults relating to the future. Depending on these two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the covering over with grass for his disciples. Depending on two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the covering over with grass for his disciples: for the restraint of dangers in the present life and for the dispelling of dangers relating to the future. Depending on these two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the covering over with grass for his disciples. Depending on two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the covering over with grass for his disciples: for the restraint of unwholesome states in the present life and for the dispelling of unwholesome states relating to the future. Depending on these two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the covering over with grass for his disciples. Depending on two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the covering over with grass for his disciples: out of compassion for householders and for cutting off the faction of those with evil desires. Depending on these two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the covering over with grass for his disciples. Depending on two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the covering over with grass for his disciples: for inspiring confidence in those who are without confidence and for the increase of confidence in those who are confident. Depending on these two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the covering over with grass for his disciples. Depending on two benefits, the Tathāgata laid down the covering over with grass for his disciples: for the stability of the True Dhamma and for the support of the Discipline.

Apaññatte paññattavaggo niṭṭhito catuttho.

The fourth chapter, the Chapter on Enactments Regarding the Unenacted, is finished.

5. Navasaṅgahavaggo

5. The Chapter on the Nine Compendiums

501. Navasaṅgahā [V 0.0413] – vatthusaṅgaho, vipattisaṅgaho āpattisaṅgaho, nidānasaṅgaho, puggalasaṅgaho, khandhasaṅgaho, samuṭṭhānasaṅgaho, adhikaraṇasaṅgaho, samathasaṅgahoti.

501. The nine compendiums are: the compendium of the basis, the compendium of failures, the compendium of offenses, the compendium of origins, the compendium of persons, the compendium of aggregates, the compendium of arisings, the compendium of legal issues, and the compendium of settlements.

Adhikaraṇe samuppanne sace ubho atthapaccatthikā āgacchanti ubhinnampi vatthu ārocāpetabbaṃ. Ubhinnampi vatthu ārocāpetvā ubhinnampi paṭiññā sotabbā. Ubhinnampi paṭiññaṃ sutvā ubhopi vattabbā – “amhākaṃ imasmiṃ adhikaraṇe vūpasamite [T 0.0550] vūpasamepi (ka.) ubhopi tuṭṭhā bhavissathā”ti. Sace āhaṃsu – “ubhopi tuṭṭhā bhavissāmā”ti, saṅghena taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ sampaṭicchitabbaṃ. Sace alajjussannā hoti, parisā ubbāhikāya vūpasametabbaṃ. Sace bālussannā hoti, parisā vinayadharo pariyesitabbo yena dhammena yena vinayena yena satthusāsanena taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasammati. Tathā taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametabbaṃ.

When a legal issue has arisen, if both adversaries come, the matter should be announced to both. Having had the matter announced to both, the admission of both should be heard. Having heard the admission of both, both should be told: “When this legal issue is settled by us, will you both be satisfied?” If they say, “We will both be satisfied,” that legal issue should be accepted by the Saṅgha. If the assembly is full of shameless ones, it should be settled by the procedure of referral. If the assembly is full of foolish ones, an expert in the Vinaya should be sought. That legal issue should be settled in whatever way it is settled by the Dhamma, by the Vinaya, and by the Teacher’s teaching. In that way, that legal issue should be settled.

Vatthu jānitabbaṃ, gottaṃ jānitabbaṃ, nāmaṃ jānitabbaṃ, āpatti jānitabbā.

The basis should be known, the lineage should be known, the name should be known, the offense should be known.

Methunadhammoti [M 0.0388] vatthu ceva gottañca – pārājikanti nāmañceva āpatti ca.

‘Sexual intercourse’ is both the basis and the lineage; ‘pārājika’ is both the name and the offense.

Adinnādānanti vatthu ceva gottañca – pārājikanti nāmañceva āpatti ca.

‘Taking what is not given’ is both the basis and the lineage; ‘pārājika’ is both the name and the offense.

Manussaviggahoti vatthu ceva gottañca – pārājikanti nāmañceva āpatti ca.

‘A human being’ is both the basis and the lineage; ‘pārājika’ is both the name and the offense.

Uttarimanussadhammoti vatthu ceva gottañca – pārājikanti nāmañceva āpatti ca.

‘A superhuman state’ is both the basis and the lineage; ‘pārājika’ is both the name and the offense.

Sukkavissaṭṭhīti vatthu ceva gottañca – saṅghādisesoti nāmañceva āpatti ca.

‘Emission of semen’ is both the basis and the lineage; ‘saṅghādisesa’ is both the name and the offense.

Kāyasaṃsaggoti vatthu ceva gottañca – saṅghādisesoti nāmañceva āpatti ca.

‘Physical contact’ is both the basis and the lineage; ‘saṅghādisesa’ is both the name and the offense.

Duṭṭhullavācāti vatthu ceva gottañca – saṅghādisesoti nāmañceva āpatti ca.

‘Coarse speech’ is both the basis and the lineage; ‘saṅghādisesa’ is both the name and the offense.

Attakāmanti vatthu ceva gottañca – saṅghādisesoti nāmañceva āpatti ca.

‘Praise of service for one’s own sake’ is both the basis and the lineage; ‘saṅghādisesa’ is both the name and the offense.

Sañcarittanti [V 0.0414] vatthu ceva gottañca – saṅghādisesoti nāmañceva āpatti ca.

‘Being a go-between’ is both the basis and the lineage; ‘saṅghādisesa’ is both the name and the offense.

Saññācikāya kuṭiṃ kārāpananti vatthu ceva gottañca – saṅghādisesoti nāmañceva āpatti [T 0.0551] ca.

‘Having a hut built by soliciting’ is both the basis and the lineage; ‘saṅghādisesa’ is both the name and the offense.

Mahallakaṃ vihāraṃ kārāpananti vatthu ceva gottañca – saṅghādisesoti nāmañceva āpatti ca.

‘Having a large monastery built’ is both the basis and the lineage; ‘saṅghādisesa’ is both the name and the offense.

Bhikkhuṃ amūlakena pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṃsananti vatthu ceva gottañca – saṅghādisesoti nāmañceva āpatti ca.

‘Accusing a bhikkhu with a groundless Pārājika matter’ is both the basis and the lineage; ‘saṅghādisesa’ is both the name and the offense.

Bhikkhuṃ aññabhāgiyassa adhikaraṇassa kiñci desaṃ lesamattaṃ upādāya pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṃsananti [P 5.0225] vatthu ceva gottañca – saṅghādisesoti nāmañceva āpatti ca.

‘Accusing a bhikkhu with a Pārājika matter by taking up some part, a mere pretext, of a legal issue belonging to another category’ is both the basis and the lineage; ‘saṅghādisesa’ is both the name and the offense.

Saṅghabhedakassa bhikkhuno yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjananti vatthu ceva gottañca – saṅghādisesoti nāmañceva āpatti ca.

‘The non-relinquishing by a schismatic bhikkhu upon admonition up to the third time’ is both the basis and the lineage; ‘saṅghādisesa’ is both the name and the offense.

Bhedakānuvattakānaṃ [M 0.0389] bhikkhūnaṃ yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjananti vatthu ceva gottañca – saṅghādisesoti nāmañceva āpatti ca.

‘The non-relinquishing by bhikkhus who are followers of a schismatic upon admonition up to the third time’ is both the basis and the lineage; ‘saṅghādisesa’ is both the name and the offense.

Dubbacassa bhikkhuno yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjananti vatthu ceva gottañca – saṅghādisesoti nāmañceva āpatti ca.

‘The non-relinquishing by a bhikkhu who is difficult to speak to upon admonition up to the third time’ is both the basis and the lineage; ‘saṅghādisesa’ is both the name and the offense.

Kuladūsakassa bhikkhuno yāvatatiyaṃ samanubhāsanāya na paṭinissajjananti vatthu ceva gottañca – saṅghādisesoti nāmañceva āpatti ca…pe….

‘The non-relinquishing by a bhikkhu who is a corrupter of families upon admonition up to the third time’ is both the basis and the lineage; ‘saṅghādisesa’ is both the name and the offense…pe….

Anādariyaṃ paṭicca udake uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā karaṇanti vatthu ceva gottañca – dukkaṭanti nāmañceva āpatti cāti.

‘The act of defecating, urinating, or spitting in water on account of disrespect’ is both the basis and the lineage; ‘dukkaṭa’ is both the name and the offense.

Navasaṅgahavaggo niṭṭhito pañcamo.

The fifth Navasaṅgaha Chapter is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary verse:

Apalokanaṃ [T 0.0552][V 0.0415] ñatti ca, dutiyaṃ catutthena ca;

Vatthu ñatti anussāvanaṃ, sīmā parisameva ca.

Announcement and motion, the second and with the fourth; basis, motion, proclamation, boundary, and the assembly as well.

Sammukhā paṭipucchā ca, paṭiññā vinayāraho;

Vatthu saṅghapuggalañca, ñattiṃ na pacchā ñatti ca.

Being in the presence, and questioning, admission, one worthy of the Vinaya; the basis, the Saṅgha and the individual, not reconsidering the motion, and a subsequent motion.

Vatthuṃ saṅghapuggalañca, sāvanaṃ akālena ca;

Atikhuddakā mahantā ca, khaṇḍacchāyā nimittakā.

The ground, the Saṅgha, and the individual; the proclamation, and at the wrong time; the sīmā that is too small and too large; the one with a broken boundary marker, a shadow boundary marker, and no boundary marker.

Bahinadī samudde ca, jātassare ca bhindati;

Ajjhottharati sīmāya, catu pañca ca vaggikā.

The sīmā outside, the river sīmā, and the ocean sīmā; and the natural lake sīmā, the conjoined sīmā; the overlapping sīmā, and acts done by groups of four and five.

Dasa vīsativaggā ca, anāhaṭā ca āhaṭā;

Kammapattā chandārahā, kammārahā ca puggalā.

Acts done by groups of ten and twenty; the two cases of not bringing consent and the one case of bringing it; the monk present for the act, the one worthy of giving consent, and the individual worthy of the act.

Apalokanaṃ pañcaṭṭhānaṃ, ñatti ca navaṭhānikā;

Ñatti dutiyaṃ sattaṭṭhānaṃ, catutthā sattaṭhānikā.

The act of announcement applies in five instances, and the act by motion in nine instances; the act by motion and one announcement in seven instances, the act by motion and three announcements in seven instances.

Suṭṭhu phāsu ca dummaṅku, pesalā cāpi āsavā;

Veravajjabhayañceva, akusalaṃ gihīnañca.

For the good of the Saṅgha and for its comfort; for the control of unruly individuals and for well-behaved monks; for the taints, enmity, blame, and fear; for unwholesome states and for compassion for householders.

Pāpicchā [M 0.0390] appasannānaṃ, pasannā dhammaṭṭhapanā;

Vinayānuggahā ceva, pātimokkhuddesena ca.

For the control of those with evil wishes, for inspiring faith in the faithless, for the increase of faith in the faithful, for the establishment of the True Dhamma; and for the support of the Vinaya, and for the recitation of the Pātimokkha.

Pātimokkhañca [T 0.0553] ṭhapanā, pavāraṇañca ṭhapanaṃ;

Tajjanīyā niyassañca, pabbājanīya paṭisāraṇī;

The suspension of the Pātimokkha and the suspension of the Pavāraṇā; the act of censure, the act of subordination, the act of banishment, and the act of reconciliation.

Ukkhepana parivāsaṃ, mūlamānattaabbhānaṃ;

Osāraṇaṃ nissāraṇaṃ, tatheva upasampadā.

The act of suspension, the giving of probation, sending back to the beginning, the giving of penance, and rehabilitation; reinstatement, removal, and likewise, higher ordination.

Apalokanañatti [V 0.0416] ca, dutiyañca catutthakaṃ;

Apaññattenupaññattaṃ, sammukhāvinayo sati.

The act of announcement and the act by motion, the act by motion and one announcement, and the act by motion and three announcements; the original rule and the supplementary rule; the legal procedure of 'in the presence of', and the legal procedure of mindfulness.

Amūḷhapaṭiyebhuyya, pāpiya tiṇavatthārakaṃ;

Vatthu vipatti āpatti, nidānaṃ puggalena ca.

The legal procedure for the sane, acting on an admission, a majority decision, for one's bad character, and covering over with grass; the summary of the ground, of failures, of offenses, of origins, and of individuals.

Khandhā [P 5.0226] ceva samuṭṭhānā, adhikaraṇameva ca;

Samathā saṅgahā ceva, nāmaāpattikā tathāti.

And the summary of aggregates, the summary of origins, and the summary of legal questions; and the summary of settlements; likewise the names and offenses.

Parivāro niṭṭhito.

The Parivāra is concluded.

Parivārapāḷi niṭṭhitā.

The Parivāra Pāḷi is concluded.
